title: Outcomes Associated With Postoperative Dexamethasone Use After Adult Spinal Deformity Surgery
abstract: Objective: Dexamethasone is commonly prescribed following adult spinal deformity (ASD) surgery; however, dexamethasone’s immunosuppressive effects on clinical outcomes in ASD surgery remain unclear. This study sought to: assess the effects of postoperative dexamethasone after ASD surgery, and evaluate the potential association between postoperative dexamethasone and complications.Methods: This TriNetX study identified adults who underwent ASD surgery from 2009–2024. Outcomes were explored at 30-day, 90-day, and 1-year time points among patients with any systemic dexamethasone exposure within 7 days of surgery. Primary outcomes included wound infection, sepsis, and perioperative hematoma. Secondary outcomes included respiratory failure, delirium, new-onset diabetes, and in-hospital mortality. Propensity score matching (PSM) and logistic regression assessed associations.Results: After PSM, 42,472 patients were included in both the dexamethasone and control cohorts. At 30 days, dexamethasone exposure was associated with higher odds of wound infection. At 90 days, these associations included elevated risks for wound infection, respiratory failure, delirium, and sepsis. By 1 year, dexamethasone use remained significantly associated with wound infection, delirium, and respiratory failure, however, hospital-recorded mortality was lower in the dexamethasone cohort.Conclusion: In this l…

title: Inequality Metrics as Early Warning Indicators of Bitcoin Market Instability
abstract: Existing Bitcoin price prediction systems mainly rely on traditional statistical models or basic financial indicators, which often fail to capture complex market patterns and the highly volatile nature of cryptocurrency markets. Many machine learning models use only historical price values and do not integrate statistical inequality measures such as the Lorenz Curve, Gini Index, or K-Value, which can provide insights into market distribution and stability. To overcome these limitations, the proposed system analysis historical Bitcoin price data from 2010 to 2021, including the open, high, low, and closing prices. The proposed framework incorporates the Lorenz Curve, Gini Index, and K-Value along with financial data, and a linear regression model is applied for time-series forecasting. The proposed model showed improvements of 1.46%, 6.87%, and 0.07% in RMSE, MAE, and MAPE, respectively, over the baseline. The results indicate that integrating inequality-based features improved prediction reliability and provided a better understanding of market behaviour.

title: AGRICULTURAL CROP-RESIDUE WASTE CONVERTED INTO ELECTRICITY IN INDIA
abstract: The importance of adopting a “waste-to-wealth” approach lies in reusing waste as a valuable resource rather than an economic burden and environmental issue. India’s agricultural residues have the potential to generate over 18,000 MW of power annually. Biogas plants are a progressive step taken by the Government of India to curb crop burning to prevent pollution. In India, as agriculture plays a pivotal role in ensuring food and nutritional security, it also generates significant waste during cultivation, harvesting, and processing. Agricultural waste is generated throughout the journey from farm to food plate. Inadequate management of agricultural waste has become a substantial source of environmental contamination affecting air, soil, and water. Agricultural waste management in India presents both significant challenges and opportunities. Traditional practices, particularly crop residue burning, although ingrained, are often unsustainable and environmentally damaging. Residue burning leads to the depletion of soil nutrients, degradation of soil health, and the emission of greenhouse gases. The implementation of advanced waste valorization methods, like thermochemical and biochemical processes, can transform agricultural waste into valuable products, contributing to the circular economy and sustainable development. Various agricultural wastes are generated in large amounts with…

title: Single-Stock Leveraged ETFs and Underlying-Market Quality: Evidence from Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix
abstract: We study changes in underlying-market quality around Korea's May 2026 introduction of single-stock leveraged ETFs, using Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix as a case study. These were the first eligible underlying stocks. We find little evidence of persistent abnormal returns, but volatility and downside risk are significantly higher for both stocks in the post-listing window. Liquidity improves for SK Hynix but not clearly for Samsung Electronics. Investor-specific net buying changes little, whereas trading participation shifts across groups. Margin balances rise, new margin trading falls, and securities-lending balances decline, indicating changes in conventional leverage activity. Earlier Hong Kong listings provide supplementary evidence that responses vary across firms and venues. Overall, volatility is the most consistent post-listing change across the two stocks. Other dimensions of the trading environment, including liquidity, investor participation, and conventional leverage activity, also change around the listings, although these changes are heterogeneous and need not represent independent ETF-specific channels.

title: PHYSICOCHEMICAL CHARACTERIZATION AND PRELIMINARY ASSESSMENT OF THE COMPOSTING POTENTIAL OF MARKET BIOWASTE IN DIFFA, NIGER
abstract: Urban solid waste management is a major environmental challenge, particularly in markets where commercial activities generate substantial quantities of organic and non-biodegradable waste. This study aimed to characterize market biowaste generated in the urban municipality of Diffa, Niger, and to preliminarily assess its suitability for composting. The study was conducted in the central, vegetable, and fish markets using a stratified sampling approach. Waste generation was monitored through daily weighing, while representative samples of 100 kg from each market were characterized according to waste category, particle-size distribution, apparent bulk density, moisture content, and volatile organic matter. The results showed substantial differences in waste generation among the three markets. The overall mean generation rate was 3.32 ± 2.37 kg/trader/day, with the highest mean rates recorded at the vegetable market (4.32 ± 3.43 kg/trader/day) and fish market (4.07 ± 3.59 kg/trader/day), whereas the central market recorded the lowest rate (1.57 ± 0.09 kg/trader/day). Organic waste was the dominant fraction in the vegetable and central markets, whereas plastic waste predominated in the fish market. title: The Impact of Market Power and Market Concentration in Shaping the Stability of Islamic Banking in Indonesia
abstract: Introduction/Main Objectives: The increasingly concentrated market structure in Indonesia’s Islamic banking industry following the 2021 merger of Bank Syariah Indonesia (BSI) raises critical questions regarding the relationship between market structure and bank financial stability. Novelty: This study examines market concentration, measured by the Herfindahl–Hirschman Index (HHI), and individual bank market power, measured by the Lerner Index, in relation to the stability of Islamic banking in Indonesia over the 2019–2024 period. Research Methods: Using an unbalanced panel dataset of Islamic banking institutions in Indonesia, this study employs panel regression analysis to examine the relationships between HHI, the Lerner Index, and banking stability, measured by the Z-score. The appropriate panel estimation model is determined through model selection tests. Finding/Results: The results show that market concentration has a positive but statistically insignificant relationship with the Z-score, whereas market power has a negative but statistically insignificant relationship with the Z-score. Thus, neither variable provides statistically significant evidence of an association with Islamic banking stability under the estimated model. Conclusion: The findings provide inconclusive evidence regarding the relationship between market structure and Islamic banking stability in Indonesia…

title: Changes in K-Beauty Export Structure and Industry Case Studies, 2021–2025: Focusing on Market Diversification and Directions for Industrial Advancement
abstract: This study examines changes in the K-Beauty export structure from 2021 to 2025 and explores directions for industrial advancement through market diversification and selected industry cases. The study combines a review of previous research, trend and comparative analysis of official export statistics, market-concentration analysis using the Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI), CR3, and CR5, and industry case analysis. The results show that Korean cosmetics exports reached USD 11.42 billion in 2025. China’s share of Korean cosmetics exports declined from 53.2% in 2021 to 17.7% in 2025, while the U.S. share increased from 9.2% to 19.1%. The United States became the largest export market, while Japan maintained a relatively stable share. Over the same period, the HHI declined from 3,058.8 to 892.2, while CR3 and CR5 also decreased, indicating a marked reduction in export-market concentration and a broader distribution of export destinations. Makeup and basic cosmetics remained the dominant export category, although growth was also observed in other product categories. Industry cases showed emerging forms of overseas distribution and brand deployment, as well as business expansion into beauty-tech. A Web-Based Farmer-Buyer Partnership System for Direct Agricultural Market Connectivity
abstract: Agriculture plays a vital role in the Indian economy and provides livelihood opportunities for a large rural population. However, farmers often face difficulties in finding suitable buyers, accessing market information, communicating product availability, and managing agricultural sales. Traditional agricultural marketing systems may involve multiple intermediaries, resulting in limited direct interaction between farmers and buyers. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a Farmer– Buyer Partnership System, a web-based platform that provides a digital connection between farmers and buyers. The proposed system enables farmers to register, create profiles, list agricultural products, specify available quantities and expected prices, and manage buyer requests. Buyers can register, search and view available agricultural products, access relevant farmer and product information, and submit partnership requests. An administrator manages users, products, and partnership activities through a centralized system. The proposed application is developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the frontend, Python Flask for the backend, and MySQL for database management. The system follows a structured approach to improve product visibility, communication, request tracking, and information accessibility. The proposed platform provides a foundation for direct farmer– buyer interaction and…

title: AgriChain: A Farmer-to-Market Intelligence Platform Integrating Satellite Imagery, Deep Learning, and Market Analytics for Precision Agriculture
abstract: Smallholder farmers in developing agricultural economies continue to face significant losses arising from delayed detection of crop stress, undiagnosed plant diseases, and volatile, opaque market pricing. This paper presents AgriChain, an endto-end farmer-to-market intelligence platform that unifies remote-sensing analytics, deep-learning-based disease diagnosis, and data-driven market forecasting within a single accessible interface. The system ingests multispectral Sentinel-2 imagery through the Google Earth Engine API to compute the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) for continuous crop-health monitoring, while a convolutional neural network trained on annotated leaf-image datasets performs on-demand disease classification from farmer-submitted photographs. A Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network forecasts short-term commodity prices from historical mandi (market) records, and a rule-augmented recommendation engine fuses the outputs of these three subsystems to generate actionable, field-specific guidance covering irrigation scheduling, treatment recommendations, and optimal selling windows. The platform is implemented using a React.js frontend, a Node.js/Express backend, and a PostgreSQL/PostGIS spatial database. title: The Role of Banks as Marginal Lenders in the Month-End Repo Market
abstract: This paper investigates banks' liquidity provision and pricing behavior as Repo buyers during month-end squeeze periods in the Korean Repo market. Using transaction-level institutional data from 2018 to June 2025, we estimate panel regressions controlling for transaction volumes, counterparty sectors, month-end indicators, and daily fixed effects. We find that while non-bank financial institutions supply funds at lower spreads than domestic banks during regular periods, their funding capacity contracts sharply at month-ends. Conversely, domestic banks substantially expand Repo purchases, confirming their role as critical marginal lenders during liquidity strains. Crucially, although Repo rates rise at month-ends, domestic banks do not exact a disproportionate pricing premium relative to other participants. Our results indicate that month-end rate spikes stem from supply retrenchment among non-bank sectors rather than banks' exercise of market power. These findings underscore the need to refine regulatory frameworks and haircut systems to preserve banks' stabilizing role as liquidity providers under market stress.

title: EVALUATING THE INFLUENCE OF TECHNICAL INDICATORS AND TEMPORAL FEATURES FOR STOCK MARKET PREDICTION USING MACHINE LEARNING
abstract: Predicting the stock market is an ill-defined and difficult task because of the time dependency, dynamic and non-linear characteristics of financial data. In this paper, the authors explore the impact of more technical indicators and temporal characteristics on the predictive power of machine learning models for stock market prediction. Preprocessing and enrichment of historical stock price data were carried out using technical indicators that are widely used in the finance industry, such as Relative Strength Index (RSI), Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD), Exponential Moving Average (EMA), Simple Moving Average (SMA), Average True Range (ATR), and momentum-based indicators. Further, time-based information like lag values, rolling statistics, trading day, and monthly trends were added to showcase sequential market behaviour. Performance of the various combinations of features was evaluated based on classification and regression performance metrics like accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE). Results from the experiments show that the incorporation of technical indicators with the temporal features can greatly improve prediction performance over the use of raw price data only. title: PERFORMANCE EVALUATION AND OPTIMIZATION OF A MACHINE LEARNING-BASED PREDICTIVE FRAMEWORK FOR STOCK MARKET TREND ANALYSIS USING REAL-WORLD FINANCIAL DATA
abstract: The stock market is a nonlinear, dynamic and unpredictable market, making accurate forecasting a difficult task. In this paper, a machine learning approach for stock market trend prediction is proposed based on real-world financial data and technical indicators. The framework includes a comprehensive data preprocessing pipeline, feature engineering, and hyperparameter optimization, all aimed at enhancing the accuracy of predictions and the robustness of the model. The historical stock market information is loaded, and then converted to useful features such as moving averages, Relative Strength Index (RSI), Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD), Bollinger Bands, trading volume, and daily returns. Various machine learning models, including Logistic Regression (LR), Decision Tree (DT), Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM), XGBoost and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) are tested and compared with classical performance metrics, such as precision, recall, F1-score, cross-validation accuracy and Area under the Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC). The experimental results show that the proposed optimized predictive framework outperforms the conventional machine learning approaches, with an accuracy of 97.13%, an F1-score of 0.970 and an AUC of 0.991. The framework also showed very good performance with 5-fold cross validation, which means good generalizi…

title: Assessment of the accuracy of bank valuations prepared using selected valuation models in stockmarket recommendations on the Polish capital market
abstract:
The aim of the article is to assess the accuracy of bank valuations contained in stock-market recommendations on the Polish capital market and prepared using selected valuation models. The analysis covers 364 recommendations concerning 11 banks issued between 25 October 2005 and 13 August 2021. Valuation accuracy is defined as the percentage deviation of the target price from the closing share price observed on the recommendation’s maturity date, consistent with the investment
horizon specified in the report (3, 6, 9 or 12 months). A three-level classification is applied: 0–5% as accurate, 5–15% as acceptable, and above 15% as unacceptable. A one-sample t-test against the 15% benchmark is used to assess the average level of valuation error. The study identifies four valuation models used in brokerage practice: the ROE–P/BV model, the residual income model (RIM), relative valuation based on multiples, and the dividend discount model (DDM). Relative valuation based on multiples is the most frequently used technique (71.15%), followed by the ROE–P/BV model (61.81%) and RIM (42.31%), whereas DDM appears only marginally (1.37%). The mean valuation errors for the ROE–P/BV model, RIM, and relative valuation are all close to 39–40%, while the highest mean error is recorded for DDM (50.68%). title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Stock Market Trend Prediction and Risk Assessment: A Review
abstract: Machine learning models are now widely used to forecast stock price movements and to measure financial risk, yet most cannot explain their own outputs. In finance that is a serious weakness, because forecasts influence real investment decisions and regulators expect firms to justify the models they use. This review asks how explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) has been applied to stock trend prediction and risk as-sessment, and how far the resulting explanations can be trusted. We first outline the economic theory of predictability and the standard risk measures, then set out the mathematics of the main explanation methods: Shapley-value attribution, LIME, gradient-based attribution, attention, and counterfactuals. We then compare representative studies, summarise regulatory expectations, and propose a five-layer framework for explainable forecasting. Across the literature we find that explanations are most useful as a validation tool, and that they become un-reliable when features are correlated, when markets change regime, or when a model is overfitted. Evidence that expla-nations improve decisions remains thin. We close with open problems, including causal explanation, shared benchmarks, and monitoring of explanations in production.

title: Effect of Advanced High-Strength Steel Microstructure on Hydrogen Embrittlement Behavior of Resistance Spot Welded Joints
abstract: To achieve automotive lightweighting and passenger safety, advanced high-strength steels (AHSS) have been developed with increasing strength levels. However, hydrogen embrittlement (HE) becomes more critical with increasing strength. Despite efforts to improve HE resistance through microstructural control, these steels remain vulnerable after resistance spot welding (RSW), where complex microstructures and defects are introduced. In this study, the effect of initial steel microstructure on HE sensitivity in RSWed steels was investigated using two 1.5 GPa-grade steels with identical compositions but different microstructures: complex-phase (CP) and single-phase (SP) steels. HE resistance of both base metal and welded joints was evaluated using slow strain rate tensile and slow deformation rate tensile-shear tests after electrochemical hydrogen charging. The SP steel, consisting of tempered martensite, exhibited higher HE sensitivity than the CP steel composed of tempered martensite and bainite in both base metal and welded conditions. With increasing hydrogen charging time, the crack propagation path transitioned from the fusion zone (FZ) boundary to the upper-critical heat-affected zone (UCHAZ) interior with intergranular cracking, consistent with the hydrogen-enhanced decohesion (HEDE) mechanism. title: When a Block Trade Becomes a Market Governance Test: The Bayan Resources Share Acquisition, Ownership Concentration, Minority Shareholder Protection, and Indonesia’s Capital Market Credibility
abstract: This article critically examines the October 2026 purchase of approximately 30.25 per cent of PT Bayan Resources Tbk shares by PT Jhonlin Baratama and its potential consequences for corporate control, investor protection, financial interconnectedness and Indonesian capital-market credibility. A qualitative literature review integrates 2020-2026 scholarship on blockholder governance, price formation, share pledging, carbon-related finance and extractive-sector risk with a carefully dated documentary account. The reported purchase of 10,084,088,370 existing shares at IDR 2,588 per share implies consideration of about IDR 26.10 trillion, but the comparison with public quotations does not independently determine fundamental value or illegality. Issuer disclosures reported no change in control, while a subsequent Bank Mandiri explanation characterised its facility to Jhonlin Baratama as business financing secured by a broader asset package. The findings identify conditional channels through which the new shareholding configuration could enhance monitoring and operational efficiency or increase information, governance and collateral risks. MSCI warnings regarding Indonesian market transparency predated the transaction; its October announcement was a consultation, not a final downgrade, and did not attribute causation to BYAN. title: Explainable and Feature-Engineered Machine Learning for Stock Market Forecasting: A Survey of Lexicon-Based, Statistical, and Sentiment-Driven Approaches
abstract: Forecasting the direction and magnitude of stock price movements remains one of the most persistently difficult problems in applied machine learning, owing to the noisy, non-stationary, and weak-form-efficient character of financial time series. This survey examines three recent studies that approach the problem through complementary lenses: an explainable Decision Tree that builds dynamic, industry-specific lexicons from financial news to classify next-day price-change magnitude [1]; a feature-engineering and portfolio-construction pipeline that derives new price-based predictors via Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA), and a proposed Statistical Average Method (SAM) before applying eight regression architectures, including Bi-LSTM [2]; and an LSTM-based trend classifier that fuses FinBERT-scored Twitter sentiment with price data to forecast North American and European bank-stock movements during the macroeconomically turbulent year of 2022 [3]. Beyond summarising each study's objectives, methodology, data, and results, this survey situates the three works within the broader and rapidly evolving literature on deep sequence models (LSTM, Bi-LSTM, GRU, and transformer architectures), sentiment analysis with pretrained financial language models such as FinBERT, and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) in finance. title: MARKET INFORMATION ACCESS AND WOMEN’S PARTICIPATION IN IRISH POTATO MARKETING: A STRUCTURED NARRATIVE REVIEW
abstract: Women contribute substantially to potato production and post-harvest handling, yet they often enter markets with less information, weaker bargaining positions, and fewer productive assets than men. This structured narrative review examines how access to price, demand, buyer, quality, logistics, and risk information shapes women's participation in Irish potato marketing. Literature published between 2000 and 2025 was identified from major academic databases, Google Scholar, and institutional repositories. Potato-specific studies were prioritized, while broader evidence from smallholder agriculture and digital extension was used only to explain mechanisms where direct evidence was limited. The evidence indicates that market information can improve sales timing, market selection, price negotiation, and coordination of storage and transport. However, information availability alone is insufficient. Benefits depend on women's control of communication devices, literacy, mobility, time, working capital, group membership, and the reliability and actionability of the information received. Mobile platforms can widen reach, but radio, extension agents, and farmer organizations remain important for women with limited connectivity. title: Dispersion in Analysts’ Target Prices and Stock Returns in the Korean Stock Market
abstract: This study examines the relationship between the dispersion in analysts' target prices and stock returns for firms listed on the KOSPI and KOSDAQ markets. We find that analyst target price dispersion is positively and significantly associated with next-month stock returns in panel regressions and Fama-MacBeth cross-sectional regressions, and this relation remains robust after controlling for a variety of firm characteristics. To explore the mechanism underlying this association, we divide the sample into subsamples based on firm size, volatility, turnover, and analyst coverage, and conduct the same analyses within each subsample. The results indicate that the positive relation between target price dispersion and returns is stronger for firms that are smaller, have lower volatility or lower turnover, and receive higher analyst coverage. Overall, our findings suggest that dispersion in analysts' target prices reflects uncertainty about firms' future value and contains additional information beyond traditional risk measures in environments with information frictions.

Geometry-Aware Structural-Demand Screening and Vulnerable-Region Identification for a Ship Hull Under Coupled Heave–Pitch Motions
abstract: This paper presents a geometry-aware structural-demand screening framework for a ship hull subjected to coupled heave–pitch motions in head seas. The work addresses the need to move beyond hydrodynamic susceptibility alone toward hull-resolved structural interpretation, particularly for large ships in which wave-induced motions produce concentrated bending, shear, stress and vulnerability patterns. Recent hydroelastic studies on large containerships and segmented-model experiments have shown that vertical-plane response is closely linked to global structural consequences such as vertical bending moment, vertical shear force and local vulnerability concentration, especially in the low-frequency corridor associated with dominant heave–pitch response. Building on this foundation, the present study converts the coupled hydrodynamic-response basis into longitudinal bending-, shear- and stress-demand proxies and maps these quantities onto the ship’s hull geometry. Results indicate that the primary structural-demand corridor is centred in the midship and adjacent central hull span, while shear-sensitive behaviour remains relatively stronger toward the forward and aft ends. The integrated vulnerability field further reveals two mirrored side-surface hotspot bands in the central hull region rather than a single isolated critical point. title: CivicAI - AI-Powered Smart Citizen Analytics & Disaster Response Platform
abstract: CivicAI – AI-Powered Smart Citizen Analytics & Disaster Response Platform is a web-based platform designed to provide a centralized solution for reporting and managing civic issues and emergency situations. Citizens can report problems such as road accidents, potholes, garbage, fire incidents, floods, and other public issues using text, images, and location information. The system uses Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Computer Vision, Natural Language Processing, and Data Analytics to analyze complaints, identify their category, estimate severity, and assign appropriate priority. An interactive dashboard allows authorities to monitor complaints, analyze area-wise trends, identify hotspots, and track response and resolution status. Historical complaint data can also be analyzed to predict future problem areas and support better resource allocation. The proposed system aims to transform traditional complaint management into an intelligent, datadriven civic management and disaster response platform, improving communication between citizens and authorities and supporting faster and more informed decision-making.

title: Effects of a quick response code–based caregiver video education program on peripheral intravenous catheter maintenance–related outcomes in hospitalized children in South Korea: a single-center quasi-experimental study
abstract: Purpose: This study evaluated the effects of quick response (QR) code-based video education on caregivers’ knowledge and attitudes regarding peripheral intravenous catheter (PIVC) maintenance in hospitalized children and on PIVC-related outcomes.Methods: This quasi-experimental study used a nonequivalent control-group design. Participants were 62 caregivers of children aged ≤72 months receiving PIVC therapy in a pediatric ward in Jeonju, South Korea (31 caregivers per group). The groups were recruited sequentially, with a 2-week interval. The control group, recruited from October 17 to 31, 2025, received standard verbal and leaflet-based education. The experimental group, recruited from November 14 to 20, 2025, received the QR code–based video program plus standard education. Knowledge and attitudes were assessed at baseline and 1 and 3 days post-insertion. PIVC dwell time, flushing and dressing-change frequencies, and complications were obtained from observational records. title: Scheduled versus on-demand nonopioid analgesia after cesarean delivery under regional anesthesia: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
abstract: Effective pain relief after cesarean delivery is crucial for maternal comfort, recovery, and breastfeeding. Although scheduled nonopioid analgesics are standard, on-demand regimens have been suggested to reduce drug exposure. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Cochrane CENTRAL were systematically searched from inception to August 20, 2025, for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing scheduled vs. on-demand nonopioid analgesia following cesarean delivery under regional anesthesia. The primary outcomes were postoperative pain intensity and analgesic consumption, and the secondary outcomes were maternal satisfaction, adverse effects, breastfeeding outcomes, and neonatal safety. Three RCTs that included 666 women were identified. At 24 h, scheduled dosing significantly reduced pain scores compared with on-demand regimens (mean difference [MD] 0.98, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.55 to 1.41; P < 0.001, I2 = 78%), but no difference was observed at 48 h (MD 0.76, 95% CI –0.30 to 1.82; P = 0.16, I2 = 96%). Overall analgesic consumption did not differ significantly between groups (standardized MD –0.23, 95% CI –0.62 to 0.16, P = 0.24; I2 = 80%). Maternal adverse effects were rare and similar across groups (risk difference −0.01, 95% CI −0.04 to 0.02; I2 = 0%). title: ADMINISTRATIVE LAW AS A RESPONSE TO CLIMATE CHANGE: REFLECTIONS ON LOCAL EXPERIENCES IN BENIN AND SENEGAL
abstract: The fight against the effects of climate change at the central level does not exclude the need for local authorities to also adapt. The role of municipalities is often overlooked, but remains essential due to their proximity to social realities. While the state is committed to combating climate change at the international level, the effective transfer of some of its powers to sub-state entities would require them to resort to national law. Administrative law, because it aims to serve the public interest, must logically include the fight against climate change through its tools and enforcement powers.

title: Water Demand Prediction and Optimal Redesign of Water Distribution Networks Considering Future Environmental Changes
abstract: Future demographic, industrial, and climate changes increase uncertainty in water distribution network operations. This study analyzes future water demand and hydraulic performance in Paju City from 2021 to 2050 and proposes an optimal network redesign strategy. Changes in unit water demand due to the increasing proportion of one- and two-person households and industrial demand growth were considered together with pipeline aging and extreme climate conditions. Scenario-based hydraulic analysis using EPANET was integrated with genetic algorithm-based optimization. The results show that total water demand will increase despite the eventual population decline, mainly due to increased unit demand. Extreme climate conditions had a greater impact on hydraulic performance than changes in demand or pipeline aging, resulting in 253 pressure-deficient nodes by 2050. Optimization showed that selective expansion of small- and medium-diameter pipes effectively mitigated pressure deficiencies. The proposed framework supports long-term water distribution network operation and redesign under future demographic, industrial, and climate changes.

title: Seismic Performance Evaluation of RC Frames with Post-Tensioned Corner Members Using Response Spectrum Analysis
abstract: Earthquake-resistant design of reinforced concrete (RC) buildings is an important aspect of structural engineering. This study evaluates the seismic performance of a multi-storey RC building by introducing post-tensioned corner members. A G+9 reinforced concrete building located in Seismic Zone V is modeled and analyzed using ETABS software. Two models are considered: a conventional bare RC frame and a post-tensioned corner member frame. Response Spectrum Analysis as per IS 1893:2016 is performed to compare storey displacement, storey drift, base shear, and natural time period. The results indicate that the introduction of post-tensioned corner members improves stiffness and significantly reduces lateral displacement and drift, thereby enhancing seismic performance.

title: INTEGRATED HYDRODYNAMIC-STRUCTURAL PERFORMANCE OF A TENSION-LEG PLATFORM FLOATING WIND TURBINE: A THREE-REGIME RESPONSE MODEL FOR DESIGN ENVELOPE DEFINITION WITH APPLICATION TO THE GULF OF GUINEA
abstract: This study presents an integrated hydrodynamic-structural analysis of a Tension-Leg Platform (TLP) Floating Offshore Wind Turbine (FOWT) using an ANSYS AQWA–Static Structural workflow. The NREL 5-MW turbine was modeled on a four-column TLP with 2.50 MN pretensioned tendons at 170 m water depth. RAOs revealed heave resonance at 0.0376 Hz (3.03 m/m), pitch resonance at 0.081 Hz (3.14°/m), and surge compliance at 0.016 Hz (2.44 m/m). Time-domain simulations across five sea states (Hs = 2.0–10.0 m) demonstrated three response regimes. Under mild conditions (Hs = 2.0 m), surge was ±7.3 m, heave ±1.8 m, and pitch ±9°, with tendon tensions varying ±8%. Under severe conditions (Hs = 5.0 m), responses remained stable. Under extreme conditions (Hs = 10.0 m), catastrophic instability occurred, with surge reaching ±108 m, heave −55 m, and pitch ±25°, with slack-snap events producing 87.57 MN peak tensions. Fatigue life was 165 years for Case 1, while Cases 2–5 resulted in immediate ULS failure. The tower-nacelle interface was critical (von Mises stress = 3.888 MPa). The primary contribution is a validated three-regime model: Regime I (Hs ≤ 3.5 m), Regime II (3.5–6.0 m), and Regime III (>7.5 m). For the Gulf of Guinea (50-year Hs = 5.5 m), the platform operates in Regime II, requiring tendon diameter increase from 0.15 m to ≥0.25 m or synthetic fiber ropes.

title: Analysis of Threshold Differences and Correlations Between Auditory Brainstem Response and Pure Tone Audiometry Across Degrees and Types of Hearing Loss
abstract: Purpose: Pure-tone audiometry (PTA) and auditory brainstem response (ABR) are widely used for hearing assessment. This study investigated PTA-ABR threshold differences, correlations, and agreement according to frequency, hearing loss severity, PTA averaging method, and audiometric configuration in adults with moderate-to-severe hearing loss.Methods: This retrospective study analyzed 1,132 ears from 712 adults who underwent PTA and ABR testing at a tertiary hospital. PTA thresholds (0.125-8 kHz) and five PTA averages (2 frequency average [FA] (L), 2FA(H), 3FA, 4FA, and 6FA) were compared with ABR thresholds.Results: PTA-ABR threshold differences were smallest at 1-2 kHz and generally increased above 3 kHz, particularly in steeply sloping audiograms. Among the PTA averaging methods, 6FA showed the smallest mean absolute threshold difference (3.89 dB), followed by 3FA (4.26 dB) and 4FA (4.75 dB). The 6FA also showed relatively high correlations with ABR (r = 0.890-0.927) and the highest intraclass correlation coefficient (0.904; 95% confidence interval, 0.896-0.911). Bland-Altman analysis revealed the smallest mean bias for 6FA (-1.33 dB), with 95% limits of agreement ranging from -9.62 to 6.97 dB. However, differences between 6FA and 4FA were relatively small, and individual-level variability remained.Conclusion: PTA-ABR threshold relationships varied according to frequenc…

title: Constrictive pericarditis: a structures review of the medical literature Diagnosis, multimodal imaging and contemporary Management
abstract: Constrictive pericarditis (CP) is an uncommon but potentially curable cause of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, in which a fibrotic, inelastic, and often calcified pericardium restricts diastolic filling of the ventricles. The disease remains a diagnostic challenge because its clinical picture overlaps with restrictive cardiomyopathy, severe tricuspid regurgitation, and non-cardiac causes of systemic venous congestion. This review synthesizes the contemporary medical literature on CP, covering its epidemiology and evolving etiologic spectrum, the two cardinal pathophysiologic mechanisms (dissociation of intrathoracic and intracardiac pressures and exaggerated ventricular interdependence), the validated echocardiographic diagnostic criteria, the complementary roles of cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, cardiac computed tomography, and invasive hemodynamics, and current management strategies. Particular emphasis is placed on the identification of transient (inflammatory) constriction, which may resolve with anti-inflammatory therapy, and on the outcomes and risk stratification of radical pericardiectomy, the definitive treatment for chronic disease.

title: An Improved Movie Recommendation System Using Advanced Recommendation Techniques
abstract: We live in a world where people really need something to do. People need entertainment to stay happy and get things done. Watching movies is a way for people to relax and feel good. Movies are a way to unwind and feel better. There are many movies on the internet. It can be really hard to find a people find movies they will really enjoy. The system is for people who watch movies. Movies are what the system is, about. This System is called as Hybrid Recommendation System. It uses two ways of finding movies: one that looks at the movie itself and one that looks at what other people like you have watched. The system puts together what people do when they watch movies and what the movies are about to make suggestions. We also use a tool to make sure the suggestions are accurate. We use another tool to pick the best features of the movies so the system works well.

title: CROSS-CULTURAL PATTERNS OF FEMALE’S SILENCE AND SPEECH: A COMPARATIVE CORPUS-BASED ANALYSIS OF SELECTED AMERICAN AND PAKISTANI NOVELS
abstract: A woman’s silence echoes louder than her words. The patterns of female silence and speech remain a debated issue in literature, whether it is due to oppression, resistance, or any form of trauma. Most previous studies rely on the qualitative interpretation of texts by examining them thoroughly to explore themes related to gender dynamics, male superiority and women's empowerment. However, limited attention is given to data-driven methods that can provide empirical data based on linguistic evidence. This research aims to do a comparative study of selected Pakistani and American novels by using corpus linguistics to explore recurring patterns of female silence and speech. A mixed-method approach has been employed in this research to generate a purposive corpus based on four selected novels. The empirical data has been collected by using AntConc software in the form of frequencies of male and female dialogues, collocations and repeated lexical patterns. This quantitative data has been further analyzed through the lens of Feminist Discourse Analysis to explore the contribution of patriarchal structure, power dynamics, and social and cultural constraints in affecting women’s ability to speak or to remain silent. This research offers that social structure and cultural norms play a crucial role in suppressing or empowering the voice of women.

title: A Field Survey of Fire Protection System Installation in Unattended Retail Stores by Building Size in the Seoul Metropolitan Area
abstract: This study analyzed the installation status of fire protection systems in unattended retail stores according to building size, and examined fire safety improvement measures based on field survey results. As the number of unattended stores increases, the absence of onsite personnel may delay early fire detection and response. Relevant regulations and fire cases were reviewed, and 40 unattended retail stores in the Seoul Metropolitan Area were surveyed. The results showed differences in fire protection system installation according to the building size, with lower installation rates of automatic fire detection and sprinkler systems in small and low-rise buildings. CCTV systems were installed in all the surveyed stores, and remote monitoring functions using mobile applications and communication networks were observed in many stores. Based on these findings, the use of existing CCTV and remote management infrastructure for fire detection and manager notification is proposed, but its performance requires further validation.

title: DESKXI: Design and Development of a Voice-First Desktop AI Mentor for Interactive Learning, Personalized Study Assistance, and Intelligent Task Management
abstract: Students who study alone rarely have a tutor, an interview coach and a study planner within reach, and screen-based assistants pull attention away from the work itself. DESKXI is a voice-first desktop AI mentor that combines these roles in one device: it teaches by conversation, runs mock interviews, sets spoken quizzes, keeps Pomodoro study cycles, delivers reminders and retains durable facts about the learner between sessions, all through a streaming cloud speech-to-speech model. This paper describes how DESKXI divides work between the cloud model, which carries the open-ended conversation, and deterministic local services, which hold exact state such as timers, reminders and quiz keys. It also describes the real-time client runtime that carries these functions: a bounded drop-oldest capture queue, a writer-thread playback path, a microphone mute gate, a threetier recovery design and a SQLite store. We examine selected parts of this runtime by running the unmodified source code on a reference workstation with only the hardware and cloud modules stubbed. The measurements identified four limitations that matter for mentoring: speech that keeps playing for about 1.1 s after the learner interrupts, an unfiltered down-sampler that folds out-of-band energy into the speech band, reminders that fire up to 0.95 s early, and a quiz-answer parser that reached 44.6 % accuracy on our auth…

title: LAPAROSCOPIC MANAGEMENT OF UPPER URINARY TRACT STONES: AN EIGHT-YEAR SINGLE-CENTRE EXPERIENCE: A RETROSPECTIVE CASE SERIES OF 13 PATIENTS (2013-2021)
abstract: Background: Laparoscopic stone surgery now occupies a selective role between endourological treatment and open surgery. This study describes the indications, feasibility, and outcomes of laparoscopic treatment for upper urinary tract stones at a tertiary Moroccan centre. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed 13 consecutive patients who underwent laparoscopic stone extraction in the Department of Urology, Hassan II University Hospital, Fez, from January 2013 to January 2021. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, radiological, operative, and postoperative variables were extracted from the source database. Results: Out of 200 cases of upper urinary tract stones managed over 8 years, 13 patients underwent laparoscopic treatment. The average age of our patients was 56 years, with a sex ratio of 1.16. Thirteen laparoscopic procedures were performed: 11 ureterolithotomies and 2 pyelolithotomies, including one stone extraction in a patient with junctional obstruction. Complete stone-free success was noted in 12 of the 13 patients who underwent laparoscopic stone extraction (92.30%). Only one patient developed a postoperative complication: atrial fibrillation tachycardia. Conclusion: In this small, highly selected series, laparoscopy achieved a high single-session stone-free rate with no conversion. Its contemporary role is best viewed as a rescue or reconstructive option for large impacted…

title: Multi-Modal AI System for Real Time Insider Threat Recognition
abstract: Insider threats pose a major cybersecurity risk as they originate from authorized users who misuse access privileges, causing data breaches and financial losses. Traditional rule-based security systems often fail to detect such threats due to evolving user behaviour patterns. This research proposes a deep learning–based insider threat detection system using Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks and Autoencoders. The LSTM model captures temporal patterns in user activity, while the Autoencoder learns normal behaviour and detects anomalies through reconstruction errors. The hybrid approach improves detection accuracy, reduces false positives, and supports effective monitoring of organizational activities. Although the system shows better performance compared to traditional methods, challenges related to computational complexity and real-time deployment remain areas for future work.

title: AI-Based Crop Monitoring System: Cotton Disease Detection Using CNN
abstract: Agricultural production depends on the diseases that affect plants and pests; early recognition is essential to crop management. Traditional visual analysis is labor-intensive and subjective because it might depend on the expertise of an analyst; this paper presents an AI-driven cotton disease identification system using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). This model is supported by a web dashboard and a mobile app. The model was trained using 9,495 images of cotton leaves from nine categories: Alternaria Leaf Spot, Aphids, Army Worm, Bacterial Blight, Fusarium Wilt, Healthy, Powdery Mildew, Target Spot, and Verticillium Wilt. All images were, in other words, scaled to 224 × 224 pixels and normalized to zero-to-one in the real-life scenario. Augmentation such as rotation, shifting, zooming, horizontal flipping, and shearing is implemented during the training process. What I mean to say is that the dataset was split into 7,594 training images, 947 validation images, and 954 test images. Custom CNN reached the accuracy of 95.18%, with the macro F1-score of 93.49% and the weighted F1-score of 95.15%.Flask-based backend supports the application, while the web dashboard provides the information and the model's analytics. Further evaluation using images collected under the mixed real-field conditions is needed to establish concrete reliability and generalization.

title: Design and Implementation of a Cost-Effective Battery Management System for Electric Vehicles Using Custom-Designed Sensors and Passive Cell Balancing
abstract: As electric vehicles (EVs) become more widely used, the need for battery management systems (BMS) that are safe, reliable, and affordable continues to grow. However, the high cost of commercial BMS solutions remains a major challenge for small-scale applications and markets with limited resources. This paper presents the design and hardware implementation of a low-cost Battery Management System (BMS) for a 5-series, 2-parallel (5S2P) lithium-ion battery pack. The system is intended for small electric vehicles, such as e-bikes and electric scooters, particularly in developing economies. It combines ten custom-designed resistive voltage-divider circuits to measure individual cell voltages while addressing the floating-reference issue in series-connected cells, a current-sensing module using parallel shunt resistors, a thermistor-based temperature sensor using the B-parameter equation, and a programmable TL431-based passive cell-balancing circuit with independent control for each cell. The Arduino Mega 2560 acts as the main controller, estimating the battery state of charge (SOC) from voltage while acknowledging the limitations of this method. It also displays real-time battery readings on a 20×4 LCD. An HC-06 Bluetooth module sends the data to a smartphone app developed using MIT App Inventor. Experimental results show that cell voltage measurements are within 2% of multimeter re…

title: Solar Panel Cleaning Robot Using Embedded System
abstract: Solar photovoltaic (PV) systems are an important source of renewable energy, but dust, dirt and environmental particles accumulate on the panel surface and reduce the useful solar radiation reaching the cells. Regular cleaning is therefore an important maintenance activity. Manual cleaning requires repeated human effort, time and water and can be difficult or unsafe for large or inclined installations. This paper reviews solar-panel cleaning robot technologies and presents the design of a project-scale embedded cleaning robot. Existing approaches including brush-based cleaning, water-assisted cleaning, suction mechanisms, self-propelled robots, Arduino-based systems, ultrasonic sensing and computer vision are reviewed. Based on the reviewed literature and the project hardware configuration, the proposed robot uses Arduino Uno, L298N motor-driver circuitry, 12 V geared DC motors, a 775 DC motor with a nylon brush, a water pump, a lithium-ion battery with 3S,3P BMS, a DC-DC step-down converter and HC-05 Bluetooth communication. The paper covers the problem statement, objectives, literature review, proposed architecture, hardware and software configuration, methodology, implementation, evaluation, limitations and future scope. Numerical performance values are not claimed where experimental measurements are unavailable.

title: QUALITY MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS AND SERVICE DELIVERY: AN EMPIRICAL STUDY OF FOOD AND BEVERAGE COMPANIES IN RIVERS STATE
abstract: This study examined the relationship between Quality Management Systems (QMS) and service delivery in selected Food and Beverage (F&B) companies in Rivers State, focusing on two key dimensions of QMS, Customer Focus, and Continuous Improvement, and two primary measures of service delivery, Service Reliability and Responsiveness. Employing a cross-sectional survey design, data were collected from a sample of 255 respondents using structured Likert-scale questionnaires. Descriptive statistics were used to profile respondents, while multiple regression analysis via SPSS tested the hypothesised relationships between QMS dimensions and service delivery outcomes. The findings reveal that all three QMS dimensions have significant positive effects on both Service Reliability and Responsiveness, with Customer Focus emerging as the strongest predictor. Continuous Improvement was also significant, indicating that organisations that systematically monitor, refine, and structure their operational processes are better able to deliver services accurately, consistently, and adaptively. These results validate the theoretical underpinnings of Total Quality Management theory, demonstrating that customer-oriented strategies, iterative process enhancements, and disciplined operational procedures collectively enhance service delivery in the F&B sector. title: Integrating Explainable Diagnosis, Digital Health, and Life-Stage-Specific Korean Medicine for Obesity Management: A Narrative Synthesis of the Daeat Conference 2026
abstract: Obesity is a heterogeneous chronic disease that requires diagnostic, behavioral, and life-stage-specific approaches beyond body mass index-centered assessment. In this short communication, the 5 invited speakers’ presentations from the Daeat Conference 2026 were reviewed and the content was organized into 4 research domains for Korean medicine (KM) obesity care. These were (1) interpretable diagnosis; (2) digital phenotyping and hybrid care; (3) life-stage-specific management; and (4) response-based personalization. Interpretable diagnosis was framed as a proposed modeling approach which maps multidimensional clinical observations onto inspectable diagnostic structures. Digital phenotyping was considered as a means of extending behavioral measurement beyond clinical consultations while preserving clinician-led care. Life-stage-specific management emphasized sarcopenic obesity and functional outcomes in older adults, while highlighting growth, development, and evidence gaps in children and adolescents. Response-based personalization distinguished nutritional input from interindividual metabolic and behavioral variability. Across these domains, several priorities for future research emerged, including standardized outcomes, longitudinal data, pragmatic multicenter studies, and appropriate data governance. HUMAN ROBOT COLLABORATION AND AI-ENABLED WAREHOUSE SAFETY MANAGEMENT FOR SUSTAINABLE LOGISTICS OPERATIONS IN SAUDI ARABIA
abstract: Robotic warehousing offers opportunities to reduce hazardous manual transport while introducing new risks at shared workstations, aisle intersections and digitally coordinated handovers. This critical integrative review evaluates how human-robot collaboration and artificial intelligence can support safer, more sustainable logistics operations, with Saudi Arabia as the proposed implementation context. Thirty DOI - indexed publications dated 2020 - 2025 were purposively examined across operational research, ergonomics, robotics, occupational safety and logistics management. Evidence was organised around exposure pathways, collaborative task allocation, predictive sensing, safety assurance, workforce acceptance and organisational governance. The synthesis shows that robotics may reduce walking and handling demands, but operational benefits cannot be equated with verified injury reduction. Adaptive speed control, transparent intention signalling, fatigue - aware scheduling and human - centred training appear promising when embedded within independently validated safeguards. Conversely, sensor uncertainty, deadline pressure, opaque algorithmic decisions and fragmented system ownership may transfer rather than remove risk.

title: A COMPARATIVE STUDY OF LANGUAGE ATTITUDE TOWARDS ENGLISH, URDU AND PUNJABI IN GOVERNMENT AND PRIVATE SCHOOLS
abstract: This paper explores the language attitude of students to English, Urdu and Punjabi as an educational language in the Faisalabad city in Pakistan. Using the Language Attitude Theory by Robert Gardner and Wallace Lambert, the study will analyze the integrative and instrumental aspects of motivation, and contrast any of the attitudes between government and private secondary schools. A quantitative survey design was used and 154 students (77 in the government schools and 77 in the private schools) were surveyed using a structured questionnaire, a five point Likert scale. The scores of the composite attitude in each language were created and evaluated with the reliability tests and descriptive statistics, independent samples t-tests, and Pearson correlation. The results indicate that students have an overall positive attitude towards all three languages, but students show the highest level of attitudes and highest levels of proficiency in Urdu, then English, and then Punjabi. School type had a significant impact on English and Punjabi attitude: the students of the private schools expressed more positive attitudes towards English, and the students of the government school expressed more positive attitudes towards Punjabi. There was no significant difference in attitude toward Urdu. The good positive interrelation between integrative and instrumental motivation causes the assumption t…

abstract: This study examines the employment outcomes and workplace competencies of Bachelor of Science in Business Administration (BSBA) graduates majoring in Service Management in Business Process Outsourcing (BPO). Specifically, it determines graduates’ employment status, assesses the relevance of their current employment to their degree, and evaluates their workplace competencies based on employers’ feedback. The study employs a descriptive quantitative research design involving 118 graduates from 2023 to 2025 and 25 employers or immediate supervisors. Data are analyzed using frequency counts, percentages, and weighted means. Based on the supplied figures, 87 of the 118 graduates are employed, representing an overall employment rate of 73.73%. Employment rates are 75.00% for the 2023 graduating batch, 76.92% for 2024, and 65.00% for 2025. Among employed graduates, 27.59% work in positions directly related to Service Management or BPO, 44.83% hold positions related to business or other fields, and 27.59% occupy positions unrelated to their degree. Employers’ competency ratings yield a grand mean of 3.46, interpreted as Highly Competent under the study’s rating scale. Customer service and client relations, together with professionalism and ethical conduct, receive the highest mean ratings of 3.56, whereas technical and computer skills receive the lowest mean of 3.32. abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has rapidly become a part of education, revolutionizing language learning by offering interactive, personalized and instant linguistic help to students. One AI-powered tool that has garnered a lot of attention recently is ChatGPT, which can help with English as a Second Language (ESL) learning, especially in grammar. But, empirical research about its effect on learners' morpho-syntactic awareness is limited particularly in the context of Pakistan. The present study aimed to examine the effects of ChatGPT on the morpho-syntactic awareness of Generation-Z ESL learners in Pakistan employing a quantitative quasi-experimental pre and post-test control group design. The total number of samples were 80 undergraduate students of ESL and consequently 40 students were assigned to experimental group and 40 students were assigned to control group using convenience sampling. The experimental group participated in the grammar learning using ChatGPT for six weeks, while the control group were taught the grammar in a traditional manner. The experimental group was given six weeks of grammar instruction that involved ChatGPT while the control group was given six weeks of traditional grammar instruction. The Influence of Price and Celebrity Endorsement on the Purchase Decision of Hamidah Bergo Hijab Products in the City of Bandung
abstract: The current development of the Muslim fashion business requires companies to use various strategies to attract consumers in order to survive in business competition by improving their marketing mix, one of which is pricing and promotion using celebrity endorsements. In 2024, Hamidah Scarf experienced a decline based on sales data, which means that consumers have a decreased interest in bergo hijab products, thereby impacting purchasing decisions. This study aims to investigate the influence of price and celebrity endorsements on purchasing decisions for Hamidah's hijab bergo products in Bandung City. The study employs a descriptive and confirmatory research design. The sampling technique uses non- probability sampling with a purposive sampling method. Data was collected through a research questionnaire administered to 100 individuals in Bandung City. The analysis techniques used include validity tests, reliability tests, multiple linear regression, correlation coefficient tests, determination coefficient tests, F-tests, and t-tests using SPSS 27. The research results indicate that price and celebrity endorsement have a significant positive partial effect on purchasing decisions and a significant simultaneous effect on purchasing decisions.

title: New evidence on consumer price rigidity in Poland
abstract: Nominal rigidities play a central role in monetary policy transmission, shaping how inflation and real activity respond to various shocks. Using a large longitudinal dataset of granular price data for Poland covering 2000–2024, we contribute to the literature on price stickiness by documenting key features of price-setting behaviour in Poland. First, overall price stickiness in Poland is substantial, with the average (median) implied price duration of four (over six) months. Second, there is considerable heterogeneity and asymmetry present at the sectoral level. Third, the size of price changes is large, underscoring the importance of idiosyncratic shocks in price formation. Fourth, there is little evidence of downward nominal price rigidity outside the services sector, while there is strong evidence that price discounts play a significant role for price-setting. Finally, in recent years the frequency of price changes has increased broadly, indicating strengthened effectiveness of monetary policy in bringing inflation back to target.

title: Subtle Angioid Streaks Point to Underlying Paget’s Disease
abstract: Paget’s disease of the bone (PDB) is a chronic and progressive abnormal remodeling of bones throughout the body and can result in several complications, including deafness and potential paraplegia. Fifty percent of patients with the ocular finding of angioid streaks within the retina are found to have an associated systemic condition, with PDB being one of them.1 This case review highlights the clinical findings of angioid streaks, as well as the necessary laboratory testing, imaging, and referrals required for the detection and management of PDB.

title: The Effect of Employee Service Quality on Customer Satisfaction Mediated by Price At the A2 Aluminum and Glass Shop MSME in Palembang City
abstract: This study examines the effect of employee service quality on customer satisfaction, mediated by price, at UMKM Toko Aluminium dan Kaca A2 in Palembang. As consumer expectations shift toward customization, consultative selling becomes crucial. A quantitative method with a purposive sampling of 100 respondents was employed. Data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling-Partial Least Square (SEM-PLS) via SmartPLS 4.0. The results indicate that service quality significantly affects price perceptions and customer satisfaction. Furthermore, price significantly influences customer satisfaction and partially mediates the relationship between service quality and customer satisfaction. Effectively implementing consultative selling justifies pricing and enhances overall satisfaction.

This study presents a hybrid classical-quantum framework for nonlinear time-series forecasting that integrates causally-filtered Hidden Markov regime detection with multiple VQC architectures. Three nonlinear classical baselines (support-vector regression, gradient boosting, and a multilayer perceptron) are compared alongside a linear autoregressive (AR) baseline, and the Hidden Markov Model (HMM) regime feature is fit only on training data and propagated causally into the test set to remove look-ahead leakage. title: INTEGRATED COST-SCHEDULE AND PROCUREMENT ANALYTICS FOR CONSTRUCTION SUPPLY CHAINS IN SAUDI MEGA-PROJECTS: ENHANCING FORECASTING AND PROJECT DELIVERY UNDER VISION 2030
abstract: Saudi mega-projects operate through dense networks of designers, contractors, manufacturers, logistics providers and specialist suppliers, so cost and schedule performance cannot be governed effectively as separate reporting streams. Procurement commitments shape the timing and price of resources; schedule changes alter purchasing priorities and logistics demand; and commercial variations feed back into forecast completion cost. This review develops an integrated framework for cost-schedule and procurement analytics in construction supply chains, with particular relevance to Saudi Arabias Vision 2030 delivery environment. Thirty peer-reviewed studies published from 2020 to 2025 were synthesised across artificial intelligence in construction management, project cost prediction, schedule forecasting, construction supply-chain modelling, resilience and digital-twin-enabled control. The evidence indicates that predictive value emerges when cost, schedule and procurement records share consistent identifiers, timestamps and decision horizons. Machine-learning and hybrid models can improve forecasting, but isolated accuracy is insufficient unless outputs expose uncertainty, identify drivers and trigger accountable management action.

title: Machine Learning based Stacked Ensemble Model for A Photovoltaic System Power Generation Forecasting: A Case Study of Dammam Saudi Arabia
abstract: As Saudi Arabia makes a significant transition towards renewable energy, solar energy have emerged as a feasible alternative owing to the country's favorable geographical conditions. However, this transition poses critical challenges that necessitate careful consideration. Due to the current energy mix's predominance of oil, the integration and management of solar power plants into the existing grid necessitate accurate forecasting. This, in turn, can help minimize grid instability and enhance the overall sustainability and resilience of the energy infrastructure. The issue is addressed in this work by using machine learning algorithms. For precise solar power prediction, a stacked ensemble model that employes Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) and k-Nearest Neighbours (KNN) as the base models complemented by linear regression as the meta model is proposed in this work. The ensemble model was compared against standalone KNN, ANN, stochastic gradient descent, Adaboost and XGBoost models. The results demonstrate superior performance of the ensemble model compared to the standalone models. The performance of the proposed model is verified using datasets obtained from a 5 MWp solar PV power plant based on real time meteological data from meteonom database situated in Dammam, Saudi Arabia. The proposed stacked ensemble model in this study was compared to existing ensemble models . The…

title: EARNED VALUE MANAGEMENT AND FORECASTING TO IMPROVE COST PREDICTABILITY IN SAUDI INDUSTRIAL PROJECTS
abstract: Cost predictability in industrial projects depends on recognizing the financial consequences of incomplete work before expenditure makes them unavoidable. Earned value management provides a common basis for comparing authorized scope, accomplished work, and incurred cost, but its indicators do not automatically produce a credible estimate at completion. This structured narrative review examines the conditions under which earned value information can support cost forecasting in Saudi industrial delivery.It combines research on earned value systems, statistical forecasting,organizational maturity, and regional construction risks with authoritative estimating guidance. The synthesis develops a proposed forecasting process that separates baseline authorization, performance measurement, remaining-work estimation, uncertainty assessment, and management approval. A worked example shows that identical reporting inputs can generate substantially different completion estimates when assumptions about future efficiency change. The analysis argues for reconciliation between index-based forecasts, bottom-up estimates, and appropriate historical comparisons, with particular attention to procurement, commissioning, scope change, and accounting cut-offs. Forecast quality should be evaluated through preserved historical predictions,consistent scope, and separate measures of error and directional…

title: Real-Time Production Forecasting Using GSS-Optimized Holt DES: An Empirical Comparison with ARIMA
abstract: Kurnia Plastic Factory depended on manual documentation of transactions and production scheduling, leading to postponed reporting, erroneous completion projections, and inadequate decision-making. This research created an online point-of-sale system featuring automated predictions for production duration and assessed its forecasting precision and computational efficacy in comparison to a statistical standard. The system was constructed utilizing the Extreme Programming style, the Laravel framework, PHP, and MySQL. Holt Double Exponential Smoothing technique was refined through the application of the golden section search algorithm. Functional testing verified that all 19 features functioned as intended, whereas user acceptance testing attained a success percentage of 94.74%. The assessment of forecasting efficacy was conducted by rolling one-step-ahead projections utilizing 255 observations of production duration documented from 2023 to 2025. The autoregressive integrated moving average model with parameters of one, one, and one surpassed the optimum smoothing technique in all accuracy measures, recording a mean squared error of 1.69, a mean absolute error of 1.05, and a mean absolute percentage error of 34.99%. The refined smoothing technique necessitated an average processing duration of 2.36 milliseconds, in contrast to 35.77 milliseconds for the fixed-order statistical mode…

title: Time Series Driven E-commerce Sales Forecasting and Intelligent Recommendation System
abstract: The rapid growth of e-commerce has increased the importance of accurate sales forecasting and personalized product recommendations in data-driven business applications. This paper presents Time Series Based E-commerce Sales Forecasting and Intelligent Recommendation System, a web-based application that integrates machine learning-based sales forecasting with intelligent product recommendation techniques. The forecasting component uses the XGBoost Regressor to predict future daily sales based on historical sales data and engineered temporal features, including lag values, rolling statistics, and calendar-based attributes. The recommendation component implements three independent approaches: K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN)-based collaborative filtering for frequently bought products, content-based filtering using TF-IDF and cosine similarity for identifying similar products, and popularity-based ranking for recommending top-selling products within a selected department. The application is developed using React.js for the frontend and FastAPI for the backend, providing an interactive interface for accessing forecasts and generating product recommendations. MongoDB Atlas is used exclusively for user authentication data, while forecasting and recommendation datasets and model artifacts are maintained separately. The system combines predictive analytics and recommendation techniques within…

title: Development of a SWMM-RAS Mutual Feedback-Based Technique for Inland-River Flooding Prediction Using Forecast Rainfall
abstract: Recent increases in localized heavy rainfall have intensified compound flooding in urban river basins. However, previous studies have mainly relied on one-way boundary conditions from rivers to urban areas, and therefore, their ability to account for interactions between urban drainage discharge and river water levels is limited. This study developed a 10-minute mutual feedback framework linking EPA-SWMM and HEC-RAS for the Oncheoncheon watershed in Busan, Korea (NSE = 0.97), using 60 minutes of observed rainfall and 30 minutes of forecast rainfall for real-time flood prediction. The framework enabled prediction of pluvial flooding and river water levels over the following 30 minutes and identification of increasing fluvial flood risk. A depth-weighted flood index was also applied to assess pluvial flood risk. Under an extreme rainfall event, water levels exceeded the design flood level in some downstream sections, demonstrating that the coupled framework can capture the interaction among urban drainage discharge, river water levels, and pluvial flooding. Expanded application of flood-mitigation facilities reduced pluvial flooding but increased river water levels under certain conditions, highlighting the need for integrated flood prediction and facility operation considering both pluvial and fluvial flood risks.

title: COMPARATIVE EVALUATION OF CREDIT RISK AND LOAN DEFAULT PREDICTION MODELS BY MACHINE LEARNING.
abstract: Identifying borrower default is a critical challenge in credit risk management, as inaccurate prediction can lead to financial losses and inefficient lending decisions. This study presents a comparative machine learning approach for loan default prediction using the Home Credit Default Risk dataset, which contains financial, demographic, employment, and credit-related information of loan applicants. Four classification algorithms, namely Logistic Regression, Gradient Boosting, XG Boost and SVM, are evaluated for their ability to classify applicants according to default risk. The proposed methodology involves feature selection, data preprocessing, median imputation for missing numerical values, categorical data handling, stratified data splitting, model training, and performance evaluation. Fourteen predictive variables related to income, credit amount, annuity, employment, demographic characteristics, vehicle ownership, and external credit scores are considered. The study also addresses class imbalance, as the underrepresentation of default cases may make accuracy alone insufficient for evaluating classification performance. Therefore, accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, confusion matrix, and ROC-AUC are considered for comprehensive model evaluation. The comparative framework analyzes the performance of the selected classification techniques using consistent preprocessing an…

title: Big Five Personality Prediction from Essays through Vocabulary Graphs and Contextual Transformer Representations
abstract: This study develops an approach to predict personality traits based on the Big Five model through essay text by combining global and contextual information using a Vocabulary Graph Convolutional Network (VGCN) and Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT). VGCN is used to capture global relationships between words through a vocabulary graph representation built based on NPMI weights, while BERT plays a role in producing richer and more contextual text representations. Experimental results show that the integration of structural and contextual features can provide good performance in multi-label classification tasks. Based on the grid search process and 5-fold cross-validation, the best model configuration obtained a macro F1 score of 0.6827 and a weighted F1 score of 0.6829 in out-of-fold prediction. The evaluation results for each feature show that the recall value is close to 1.0, while the precision value ranges from 0.50 to 0.56. This condition indicates a tendency for the model to produce more positive predictions. Furthermore, the results of the study highlight the importance of optimizing the prediction threshold value to obtain a more optimal compromise between precision and recall. Overall, the integration of graph-based semantic information with contextual representations from BERT shows that the VGCN-BERT approach has good potential for applicati…

title: BRIDGING PROTEOMIC DISCOVERY AND CLINICAL PREDICTION: A REVIEW OF TRANSLATIONAL PATHWAYS FROM CANCER BIOMARKER RESEARCH TO PREDICTIVE SURVIVAL MODELS IN THE UNITED STATES
abstract: Cancer proteomics has generated numerous candidate biomarkers and molecular signatures, but the translation of these discoveries into validated predictive survival models remains incomplete. This systematized review examined the translational pathway from cancer proteomic discovery to predictive survival modeling and clinical implementation in the U.S. oncology context. A structured evidence synthesis of 22 studies was conducted, focusing on biomarker discovery and signature development, survival prediction, analytical and clinical validation, multi-omics and artificial-intelligence-enabled modeling, and clinical translation. The reviewed evidence shows substantial progression from biomarker discovery toward proteomic signatures associated with survival and treatment response and increasingly integrated predictive models. However, the evidence remains uneven across the translational pathway. External validation, analytical reproducibility, integration of molecular and clinical variables, population representation, and prospective evaluation are limited, while direct evidence of clinical utility remains insufficient. The findings indicate that associations between proteomic signatures and survival should not be interpreted as evidence of clinically ready predictive models. Progress toward routine implementation will require rigorous analytical and clinical validation, external e…
