Based on 'The Unity of Heaven and Man': Association Analysis between Air Pollution and Human Health in Beijing and Risk Prediction Using Automated Machine Learning
abstract: To investigate the correlations between air pollutants and hematological parameters, and to develop a risk prediction model for understanding the health impacts of air pollution, grounded in the traditional Chinese concept of “the unity of heaven and man.”Data collected from 2019 to 2021 in the peripheral areas of Beijing were used. Six air pollutants (PM2.5, PM10, CO, SO2, NO2, O3) and 13 hematological parameters (LYP, MONO, MONP, MP, EOSA, EOSP, BASO, BASOP, MCH, MCHC, SD, PDW, PCT) were analyzed. Analytical methods included Pearson correlation, two-tailed tests, three-dimensional clustering, nonmetric multidimensional scaling, variance partition analysis, redundancy analysis, and multi-group and two-group difference analysis. Automated machine learning (AutoML) was used to predict the trends of air pollutant impacts on health indicators. Long-term exposure to air pollutants was positively correlated with MP, BASO, LYP, and EOSP, and negatively correlated with MCH and PCT. Age emerged as a significant factor influencing health, whereas sex did not modify the effect of air pollution on health indicators. This study provides new evidence on air pollution induced health damage and offers novel insights into the underlying mechanisms of how air pollutants affect human health.

Collaborative Prediction Algorithm for Investment and Financing Network System Based on Improved Hypergraph Convolution and Ant Colony Algorithm
abstract: After more than 20 years of rapid development, the Chinese financial market is experiencing a decrease in user traffic dividends. The overall industry growth rate is slowing down, yet the market’s potential demand remains substantial. The industry is transitioning from a phase focused on incremental growth to one that equally emphasizes incremental and existing stock growth, accelerating the exploration of new development models. This paper proposes the CPA-FHA, a collaborative prediction algorithm for investment and financing networks based on improved hypergraph convolution and ant colony algorithms, by integrating TransD embedding method, hypergraph convolution, spatial feature extraction, and ant colony algorithms. The proposed method is compared and analyzed using real-world investment and financing network datasets from Chinese listed companies, Chinese financial institutions, and American listed companies. It is found that, compared to classical algorithms, the Collaborative Prediction Algorithm for Financing and Investment Network System - Forecast and Hazard Analysis (CPA-FHA) has higher accuracy and efficiency in predicting investment and financing network systems.

title: SUSTAINING EMPLOYEE JOB SATISFACTION THROUGH STRATEGIC INTERNAL CRISIS COMMUNICATION IN MALAYSIA’S SERVICE SECTOR
abstract: This qualitative study examines the role of strategic communication management in sustaining employee job satisfaction during internal organizational crises within Malaysia’s service sector. Using in-depth, semi-structured interviews with eight customer service officers, the study explores how internal communication practices influence employees’ emotional well-being and job satisfaction during periods of organizational uncertainty. The interview data were analyzed using thematic analysis with ATLAS.ti, generating four core themes: clarity and transparency, leadership communication, two-way communication and feedback, and employee emotional well-being and job contentment. Findings indicate that timely, transparent, and consistent communication, supportive leadership messaging, and effective bidirectional feedback mechanisms reduce employee stress, anxiety, confusion, and dissatisfaction while strengthening morale and workplace stability. The study proposes a Communication Management Strategies Model that emphasizes employee-centric crisis communication as a strategic mechanism for protecting employee well-being, sustaining job satisfaction, strengthening organizational resilience, and supporting service excellence during internal organizational crises, particularly among frontline service employees.

title: Edukasi Fermentasi Limbah Daun Gugur Menjadi Pupuk Organik Cair di SMA Negeri 1 Kota Serang
abstract: Lingkungan sekolah menghasilkan limbah organik berupa daun gugur yang belum dimanfaatkan secara optimal. Kondisi ini menjadi peluang untuk mengenalkan pengelolaan limbah organik yang bermanfaat melalui kegiatan pengabdian kepada masyarakat. Kegiatan ini bertujuan meningkatkan pengetahuan dan keterampilan siswa dalam mengolah limbah daun gugur menjadi pupuk organik cair (POC) melalui fermentasi. Kegiatan dilaksanakan di SMA Negeri 1 Kota Serang dengan melibatkan 35 siswa dan 1 guru. Metode pelaksanaan menggunakan pendekatan edukatif-partisipatif melalui sosialisasi, demonstrasi, diskusi, dan praktik pembuatan POC menggunakan daun gugur kering, gula, bioaktivator EM4, dan air. Hasil pengamatan selama kegiatan menunjukkan adanya perubahan respons siswa dalam menjawab pertanyaan. Sebelum sosialisasi, hanya sedikit siswa yang mampu menjawab pertanyaan secara langsung, sedangkan setelah sosialisasi dan praktik, lebih dari separuh siswa dapat menjawab pertanyaan dengan cepat. Kegiatan ini juga memberikan pengalaman langsung kepada siswa dalam memanfaatkan limbah daun gugur menjadi produk yang berpotensi digunakan sebagai sumber unsur hara bagi tanaman. Dengan demikian, kegiatan ini diharapkan dapat mendorong pemanfaatan limbah organik dan menumbuhkan kepedulian lingkungan di sekolah.

ECONOMIC ANALYSIS OF THE SERVICE SECTOR IN INDIA AND CHINA (1990-2025): STRUCTURAL TRANSFORMATION, FACTOR PRODUCTIVITY, AND SUB-SECTORAL PERFORMANCE GAPS
abstract: This study provides comparative analysis of the economic performance, structural transformation, and factor productivity of the service sectors in India and China from 1990 to 2025. In 1990, both nations possessed tertiary sectors of virtually identical output scale: India generated $132.80 Billion in service Gross Value Added (GVA) (41.5% of GDP), while China generated $114.50 Billion (31.8% of GDP). By 2025-26, services expanded over 54% of aggregate GDP in both economies. However, Chinas total tertiary output surged to S10.65 Trillion compared to Indias S2.17 Trillion, generating an immense $8.48 Trillion scale gap. Utilizing Solow-Jorgenson Translog KLEMS growth accounting framework and Cobb-Douglas production functions across 11 disaggregated service sub-sectors, this paper investigates the drivers behind this structural divergence.

title: Determinants of Scalp Care Behavior among Beauty Service Users: Customer Experience and Consumption Value
abstract: This study empirically examined the effects of customer experience and consumption value on head spa and scalp care behavior among 261 adult consumers who had used head spa or professional scalp care services. Customer experience was operationalized into two dimensions, management expertise and service environment, while head spa and scalp care behavior was divided into professional care behavior and home care behavior. Data collected from a structured questionnaire were analyzed using SPSS WIN 21.0 through frequency analysis, factor analysis, reliability analysis, descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, multiple regression analysis, and simple regression analysis. The results showed that customer experience and consumption value were significantly and positively correlated with head spa and scalp care behavior. Regarding the regression results, among the sub-factors of customer experience, only management expertise had a significant positive effect on head spa and scalp care behavior as well as on professional care and home care behavior, whereas service environment did not show a significant effect. Consumption value had a significant positive effect on head spa and scalp care behavior overall, and its explanatory power was higher for professional care behavior than for home care behavior. These findings suggest that strengthening scalp care practitioners' perceived exp…

title: Advanced at the Front, Fragile at the Back: SPBE’s Service–Management Gap in Indonesian Agencies
abstract: Indonesia’s Electronic-Based Government System (SPBE) has expanded online services faster than the internal management on which they depend. This study measures the gap between the services domain (front office) and the management domain (back office) in the 2024 evaluation results of 615 central and local agencies and national domain scores for 2021–2024, applying Wilcoxon signed-rank and Kruskal–Wallis tests and a configuration typology. Services outscored management in 99.7% of agencies, with a mean gap of 1.96 points, and the national gap widened from 1.58 to 1.92. The gap was largest among cities and regencies, and 181 agencies, 139 of them regencies, combined very good services with poor management. Strengthening data, asset, and ICT human resource management should precede further service expansion.

title: Internationalizing Marketing Management Education through Academic Exchange, Industry Engagement, and Community Empowerment: An International Community Service Program in Malaysia and Singapore
abstract: International community service can connect marketing education with professional practice and cooperation. This program comprised an interinstitutional assignment to Malaysia and Singapore and academic–industry engagement at Karangkraf Malaysia. Implementation involved preparation, knowledge exchange, an industrial visit, reflective evaluation, and follow-up planning. Academics discussed digital marketing, while practitioners shared publishing management and business experience. Participants encountered editorial, design, printing, and distribution processes. Immediate outputs included industry insights, initial institutional communication, publication materials, and curriculum recommendations. Community empowerment took the form of reciprocal professional knowledge sharing. The program linked international engagement with industry-informed education.

title: The Influence of TikTok Social media marketing and Service Quality on Purchase Decisions at De.u Coffee Dago
abstract: The growth of coffee shop businesses in Indonesia shows a significant trend in line with the lifestyle changes of urban communities, where coffee shops have increasingly become places for socializing, working, or simply relaxing. One widely used strategy is social media marketing, particularly through TikTok, which is currently popular across various demographics. This study aims to examine the influence of TikTok social media marketing and service quality on consumer purchase decisions at De.u Coffee Dago. The research method employed is quantitative, with data collected through questionnaires distributed to 100 respondents. Data analysis was conducted using multiple linear regression tests. The results indicate that TikTok social media marketing has a significant effect on purchase decisions with a significance value of 0.000 (<0.05). Similarly, service quality also has a significant effect on purchase decisions with a significance value of 0.000 (<0.05). Simultaneously, both independent variables contribute 63.9% to purchase decisions, while the remaining 36.1% is influenced by other factors outside this study. These findings highlight the importance of digital marketing strategies through TikTok and the implementation of optimal service quality in enhancing consumer purchase interest. The benefits of this research not only provide academic insights into consumer behavior bu…

title: The Effect of Human Resource Competence and Internal Service Quality on Turnover Intention Among Generation Z Employees Through Job Satisfaction at Pt Permodalan Nasional Madani, Jakarta Branch
abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of human resource competence and internal service quality on the turnover intention of Generation Z employees through job satisfaction at PT Permodalan Nasional Madani Jakarta Branch. This research is driven by a critical phenomenon regarding the imbalance of human resource distribution, specifically the shortage of field Account Officers (AO), which triggers extreme workload spikes and high turnover intention risks among the young employee cohort. Furthermore, this study addresses inconsistencies in previous empirical findings (research gaps) regarding the relationships between these variables. The theoretical framework integrates Social Exchange Theory and Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) Theory. The research method applied is a quantitative approach using explanatory research. Primary data were gathered by distributing structured questionnaires to 200 Generation Z employees holding the position of Account Officer (AO) with a minimum tenure of one year. The sampling technique utilized is purposive sampling. The data analysis technique is performed through Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) based on Partial Least Squares (PLS) assisted by SmartPLS 4 software

title: Effective behavioural regulation strategies as support for children with autism spectrum disorder within a mainstream context
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is one of the most common disabilities in South African schools. However, there is still limited information about children with ASD and their schooling needs in South Africa. Teachers may find it particularly taxing to address behavioral challenges while simultaneously seeking to provide fair and accessible learning opportunities for all learners. This study identifies effective behavioural strategies to help manage the challenging behaviour of learners with ASD. The study conducted observations and semi-structured interviews as part of a qualitative multiple-case study design. The data were analysed inductively, and the results revealed that teachers relied largely on their own informal strategies. These included attempts to meet the child's individual needs, providing positive reinforcement to improve behavioural regulation, practicing positive communication, and using structured routines and regulation breaks. The implementation of these strategies was carried out without formal training or systematic guidance. Learner facilitators also provided valuable support to learners with ASD. These approaches address the inclusion of learners with unique learning capabilities in mainstream learning environments through teacher initiative. This was done to address behavioural challenges in populations with limited systemic support. Given the exploratory…

title: HYDRODYNAMIC COEFFICIENTS AND NUMERICAL VERIFICATION OF A RECTANGULAR BARGE: A FREQUENCY-DOMAIN PANEL-METHOD STUDY
abstract: Rectangular barges are widely used for their high payload capacity and stability, but their bluff geometry creates complex hydrodynamic responses requiring accurate analysis for safe operation. In this study, Hydrodynamic Coefficients and Numerical Verification of a Rectangular Barge: A Frequency-Domain Panel-Method Study was carried out to determine the hydrodynamic behaviour of a 70.0 m × 30.0 m × 7.0 m rectangular barge with 5.0 m draft and 10,762.5 t displacement. The problem addressed is the reliability of panel-method predictions of added mass, radiation damping, wave-excitation forces, and motion responses for a barge. A 3D ANSYS AQWA panel model was used over 0.2–2.0 rad/s for heave, roll, and pitch. Unlike studies reporting hydrodynamic coefficients or motion responses, this work combines coefficient evaluation with mesh convergence, symmetry verification, published comparison, natural-period consistency, and GZ assessment. Results showed heave added mass of 1.54×107 kg at 0.1 rad/s, reducing to 6.33×106 kg at 3.0 rad/s, while roll and pitch added masses decreased from 5.77×10^8 to 2.92×108kg·m² and 2.19×109 to 1.19×109kg·m². Radiation damping reached 5.50×106 N·s/m in heave, 7.00×107N·m·s in roll, and 1.50×109 N·m·s in pitch. Natural periods were 6.22 s, 7.28 s, and 4.84 s, compared with RAO peaks of 6.68 s, 7.35 s, and 5.01 s. Mesh refinement from 3000 to 6000 panels…

title: FIELD-BASED HYDRAULIC PERFORMANCE AUDIT OF A CENTRIFUGAL PUMP IN A FUEL DISTRIBUTION TERMINAL: CAVITATION ASSESSMENT, CAPACITY EVALUATION, AND VARIABLE SPEED DRIVE OPTIMIZATION
abstract: Centrifugal pumps are the operational backbone of fuel distribution terminals, where unplanned downtime or hydraulic failure can cascade into critical supply chain disruptions affecting national energy logistics. Despite their strategic importance, site-specific hydraulic performance evaluations of fuel terminal pumping systems remain underrepresented in the literature, leaving operators reliant on design-stage assumptions rather than field-verified evidence for maintenance decisions and efficiency improvements. This study addresses that gap by conducting a comprehensive hydraulic performance audit of the MCPK 125-100-400 CC centrifugal pump operating within the fuel distribution system at PT Pertamina Patra Niaga Fuel Terminal Tegal, Indonesia. Field observations and operational data collection were performed to evaluate critical hydraulic parameters, including flow velocity, actual and design flow rates, Reynolds number, head loss distribution, Net Positive Suction Head Available (NPSHa), Net Positive Suction Head Required (NPSHr), and Bernoulli equation compliance across the suction and discharge lines. Results confirm that the pump delivers a capacity of 165 m³/h, exceeding the actual operational demand of 1,600 L/min and establishing an adequate reserve for uninterrupted truck loading operations. A calculated NPSHa of 5.23 m exceeds NPSHr of 2.64 m, demonstrating a positiv…

title: ENHANCING MEMBER CAPACITY TO STRENGTHEN THE FUNCTIONAL ROLE OF THE CONSUMER DISPUTE RESOLUTION BOARD (BPSK)
abstract: The Consumer Dispute Settlement Agency (BPSK) plays a strategic role in protecting consumer rights and resolving disputes between consumers and business actors outside the court system in Indonesia. This study aims to examine the dispute resolution mechanisms employed by BPSK and the relevance of enhancing member capacity to strengthen its functional role. Using a normative legal approach, this study analyzes the legal framework governing consumer protection and the implementation of BPSK’s duties and authorities, particularly under Law Number 8 of 1999 concerning Consumer Protection and Minister of Industry and Trade Decree Number 350/MPP/Kep/12/2001. The discussion identifies three principal dispute resolution mechanisms: conciliation, mediation, and arbitration, each with distinct procedures and levels of involvement by BPSK members. However, differences in members’ professional backgrounds, legal interpretations, and levels of competence may hinder the effective resolution of consumer disputes. Therefore, capacity building through specialized education, training, and inter-member discussions is essential to improve members’ legal knowledge, analytical skills, and dispute resolution competencies. Strengthening these capacities is expected to enhance BPSK’s effectiveness in providing accessible, efficient, and equitable consumer dispute resolution, thereby supporting the real…

title: Subsurface Weakness Amplification and Progressive Capacity Loss in Piled Port Structures under Repeated Operational Loading
abstract: Piled port structures experience repeated operational loading that may degrade soil–pile interaction and reduce foundation capacity over time. This study investigates subsurface weakness amplification and progressive capacity loss using three-dimensional finite element modelling of coastal soil profiles and pile systems under cyclic loading. Parametric analyses evaluated soil stiffness and loading variations to quantify degradation mechanisms. Results showed weak soil conditions caused 27.4% capacity reduction compared with 8.6% in stronger profiles, with strong correlation between soil degradation and capacity loss (R² = 0.87). The proposed Subsurface Weakness Amplification Index indicated a 3.2-fold increase in degradation sensitivity under weak subsurface conditions. This framework contributes to long-term reliability assessment of piled port structures subjected to repeated operational loading.

title: Strengthening capacity in high-burden malaria-endemic countries: a strategic analysis of training gaps and blended learning solutions in national malaria control programs
abstract: Abstract Background Malaria remains a significant public health challenge, with approximately 70% of the disease burden concentrated in 11 High-Burden to High-Impact (HBHI) countries identified by the World Health Organization. Despite substantial investments in interventions including insecticide-treated nets, rapid diagnostic tests, artemisinin-based combination therapy, and vaccines, persistent human resource capacity deficiencies undermine the effectiveness and sustainability of malaria control. Training gaps affect community health workers, district officials, and national program managers across various areas, including diagnostics, case management, surveillance, and data analytics. Methods This mixed-methods analysis integrated peer-reviewed literature, WHO and donor agency reports, and case studies from HBHI countries. Data from national health information systems and malaria program reports were evaluated using an Impact-Feasibility Matrix, with systemic relationships mapped across community, district, and national levels. Recommendations were validated through consultations with technical experts, Malaria Policy Advisory Group members, National Malaria Control Program managers, and partner organizations. Results Significant training and workforce shortages were identified at all health system levels. Community-level deficiencies in health worker training and supervisi…

title: Education toward Golden Indonesia 2045: Reforming Welfare, Remuneration, and Career Governance of Lecturers in Public and Private Universities
abstract: Higher education is a strategic instrument for achieving Golden Indonesia 2045, and its quality cannot be separated from the quality and sustainability of the lecturer profession. This article analyses the welfare, remuneration, career development, and governance of lecturers in public (PTN) and private (PTS) universities. Using a normative juridical method with statutory, conceptual, and public-policy approaches, supplemented by descriptive secondary data on the North Sumatra provincial minimum wage, civil-servant base salaries, a campus-worker wage survey, and United States professor salaries, the study finds that between 2021 and 2025 the North Sumatra minimum wage rose by about 19.7% while the entry base salary of civil servants in grade III/c rose by about 8.0%, narrowing the gap from roughly 12% to roughly 1%; that private-university lecturer pay has no single national standard; and that welfare, performance, career, and digital academic records are still treated separately. The article proposes the Integrated Lecturer Welfare and Academic Career Governance Model (ILWAC-GM) and the Academic Digital Career Passport (ADCP), a verified digital academic record portable across institutions. The model is conceptual and requires empirical testing before it is used as a policy basis.

abstract: The substantial presence of Ukrainian migrants in Poland and their active participation in the labour market create a need for a socio-economic integration mechanism that combines migrants’ individual interests with the efficient use of human capital and regional economic security. The article aims to develop a mechanism for the socio-economic integration of Ukrainian migrants in Poland by combining an assessment of individual prerequisites for economic security with the scale of formal economic participation at the regional level. The information base comprises official data on Polish-language proficiency, employment structure, long-term residence intentions, and Ukrainians’ participation in the social insurance system. The methodological approach includes indicator normalisation, objective weighting using the CRITIC method, construction of an integral assessment of personal integration-security prerequisites, assessment of regional integration gaps, and determination of intervention priorities. The proposed mechanism operates at two interconnected levels. At the individual level, it includes the diagnosis of linguistic and professional prerequisites, qualification matching and short-term reskilling, employment and social-insurance formalisation, stabilisation of living conditions, and subsequent career advancement or entrepreneurial activity. At the regional level, the mechan…

title: A potential HCN channel-sensitive mechanism for verapamil’s action in cluster headache
abstract: Abstract Background Cluster headache, a primary headache disorder characterized by recurrent bouts of severe unilateral head pain and characteristic autonomic features, including lacrimation, is often described as the worst pain imaginable to humankind. Current treatments are nonspecific, and preventive treatments particularly are associated with adverse effects, low and delayed efficacy. The first line preventive treatment verapamil is effective in over 50% of patients, albeit at very high doses and with significant cardiovascular effects that limit its utility. Therefore, we sought to dissect the potential mechanisms of action of verapamil. Methods In this study, we used two related preclinical models of trigeminal autonomic cephalalgias (TACs) and a preclinical model of migraine in rats, combined with pharmacological interventions to determine the potential mechanisms of action of verapamil. Results We demonstrate that verapamil reduces superior salivatory nucleus stimulation-evoked cranial autonomic activation and nociceptive responses. However, verapamil has no effect on durovascular-evoked nociceptive responses, in agreement with verapamil’s clinical effectiveness in cluster headache, a TAC subtype but not migraine. Interestingly, verapamil’s effect was prevented or reversed by blockade of hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated channels (HCN), but not calcium…

Implementation of an Effective Code Vulnerability Detection Model Using Deep Learning and Attention Mechanism
abstract: With increasing computational power, deep learning methods have been widely applied to software vulnerability detection. Compared to traditional machine learning, deep learning offers low computational overhead, high accuracy, and eliminates the need for manual feature engineering. However, many existing approaches lack sufficient utilization of code syntax and semantics, limiting performance. This study proposes VDDA (Vulnerability Detection based on Deep learning and Attention mechanisms), an effective model that combines deep learning with attention mechanisms. VDDA employs a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BLSTM) network to capture code features automatically. Source code is transformed into Code Property Graphs (CPG) using the Joern tool to retain rich syntactic and semantic information. To enhance feature representation, several strategies are applied: depth-first traversal-based CPG optimization, three-directional code slicing, code block-based slice organization, and separation of function and variable names during symbolization. These methods convert source code into vector representations suitable as input to the deep model. An attention mechanism is integrated with BLSTM to emphasize the most relevant parts of the input vectors for improved vulnerability detection. Experiments on two datasets of varying sizes demonstrate that VDDA achieves superior detection pe…

abstract: While existing literature recognises mentorship as an important strategy for leadership development, there is limited empirical understanding of how women experience and negotiate mentorship as they advance into school leadership in the South African context. Despite policy efforts to promote gender equity, women remain underrepresented in school leadership, and the role of mentorship in addressing this disparity remains insufficiently understood. This study explores mentorship as a relational mechanism through which women negotiate access, leadership identity, and social capital in their advancement into school leadership. An interpretive qualitative design, underpinned by a narrative phenomenological approach and informed by Social Capital Theory, was used to explore the experiences of six purposively selected women leaders from township schools in a single district in KwaZulu-Natal. Data were generated through semi-structured interviews and were analysed thematically. Participants reported that supportive mentoring relationships provided them with confidence, professional visibility, networking opportunities, leadership guidance, and encouragement to pursue leadership positions. Participants with limited access to mentorship described feelings of isolation, reduced access to leadership guidance, and fewer opportunities for professional development. They also reported seeking…

title: Slow Initiation Mechanism and Accelerated Kinetic Monte Carlo Simulation for Quantifying Metallocene-Catalyzed Ethylene–Norbornene Copolymerization Reaction Rates and Product Microstructure
abstract: Abstract A reaction kinetic model involving a mechanism controlled by chain initiation and catalyst deactivation as well as an accelerated kinetic Monte Carlo (kMC) method predicting copolymer microblocks were developed for the metallocene-catalyzed ethylene–norbornene copolymerization. The outcomes demonstrated excellent agreement with the published experimental data and revealed that the vast majority of polymer chains are formed by initiated ethylene. By combining code optimization with the Numba module, our kMC simulation calculated the intricate copolymer microstructure without conventional quasi-steady-state assumption while optimizing system size to balance computational efficiency against the smoothness of concentration profiles. Found by a systematic sensitivity analysis for all rate constants, the key reactions and their rate constants were finely tuned using a particle swarm optimization (PSO) framework. The integrated kMC-PSO approach effectively captured macroscopic experimental metrics including norbornene conversion and molecular weights. Furthermore, while the model accurately reflects the overall composition, discrepancies in norbornene-containing triad distributions demonstrate the inherent physical boundaries of classical penultimate models in capturing complex stereochemical sequence effects under high feed ratios, providing critical mechanistic insights for…

Quantifying effects of inattention on serial dependence in numerosity and orientation judgments using a Bayesian integration approach
abstract: Abstract Background Our perceptual judgments are influenced by recent experience. In three experiments, we examined how such serial dependence in numerosity and orientation judgments is influenced by attention. Participants estimated numerosity in dot clouds (Experiment 1) or the orientation of Gabor patches (Experiment 2: high contrast, Experiment 3: low contrast). These tasks were paired with an attention-demanding central task to modulate attention in a dual-task design. Results We found stronger serial dependence under divided attention across all experiments. Furthermore, we employed an ensemble of Bayesian models to disentangle the influence of attention, sensory evidence, and prior responses in numerosity and orientation judgments. Our six models differed in which of the three components of prior experience – average sensory evidence, prior sensory evidence and prior response – were included and how they expressed the influence of history on perceptual judgments. We found that all three factors influence perceptual judgments with attractive effects for prior responses and average sensory evidence, but a repulsive effect for prior sensory evidence. Importantly, the strength of the influence on individual components depended on the nature of the task (numerosity or orientation judgment), the quality of sensory evidence, and availability of attention. Conclusions Our findin…

title: When Is POME a Residue? Definitional Boundaries, Carbon Accounting and Policy Integrity in Sustainable Aviation Fuel
abstract: This qualitative literature review examines the definitional controversy surrounding palm oil mill effluent (POME) and its recovered oil as sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) feedstocks. Drawing on 52 cited peer-reviewed journal articles from 2020–2026 and official ICAO and certification documents, it distinguishes unavoidable wastewater, genuinely recovered residual lipids and deliberately diverted primary palm oil. The review interprets the CORSIA POME-HEFA default core lifecycle value of 18.1 g CO₂e/MJ, derived from two modelling estimates, without conflating its assigned indirect land-use change treatment with measured system-wide climate effects. Five thematic findings concern classification boundaries, model-dependent emissions, wastewater methane interactions, plausible recovered-oil supplies and an auditable chain of custody. An origin-and-function framework is proposed to preserve legitimate feedstock eligibility while preventing inappropriate relabelling, duplicate emissions claims and undocumented changes in oil flows. The discussion differentiates official fuel lifecycle accounting from supplementary assessment of methane management and displaced product markets. It recommends mill-level mass balances, independent verification, measured conversion inputs and an adaptive Indonesian policy roadmap. Definitional precision is necessary for regulatory credibility, but canno…

title: A RARE PATTERN OF BREAST CANCER RECURRENCE ON 18F-FLUORODEOXYGLUCOSE-POSITRON EMISSION TOMOGRAPHY/COMPUTED TOMOGRAPHY: ISOLATED MICRONODULES IN DISTANT ADIPOSE TISSUES
abstract: Recurrence of an initially early breast cancer (EBC) occurring exclusively in subcutaneous adipose tissues without skin or distant organ involvement is uncommon. Such recurrence is challenging to diagnose because of its non-specific clinical presentation and imaging characteristics, yet its identification is essential for optimal patient management. In this context, we report the case of an asymptomatic 41years old patient treated 10 years earlier for early left breast cancer, who presented during follow-up with a slight but continuous increase of CA 15-3 levels. Conventional imaging was negative and initial 18F-FDG PET/CT demonstrated three micronodules in the subcutaneous fat, located at a distance from the mastectomy scare, showing no metabolic activity and considered indeterminate. Four months later, a follow-up FDG PET/CT performed for persistent elevation of the tumor markers, revealed progression of the subcutaneous nodules, with the appearance of a moderate-to-high FDG uptake, without any other pathological foci. These findings were suggestive of isolated metastatic relapse in the adipose tissue, which was confirmed histologically. This case is reported from a pedagogical perspective to illustrate and raise awareness of a rare pattern of breast cancer relapse on FDG PET.

title: Voltage–Current-Emission Framework of Time-Resolved Electroluminescence
abstract: Abstract Time-resolved electroluminescence has been a central methodology for the development of LED devices. However, it still lacks quantitative theoretical descriptions of time-resolved electroluminescence. By combining the equivalent circuit models of semiconductor devices and the carrier dynamics of electroluminescence processes, here we have developed a voltage–current-emission framework to illustrate time-resolved electroluminescence from the pulse voltage as input, to injection current, and finally generate electroluminescence as output. The features of different LED devices can be quantitatively interpreted, confirming their universal applicability across LEDs with different materials and device structures. Importantly, the curves of time-resolved electroluminescence can be simulated to quantitatively describe the dynamics of current and carriers of the LED operation. In all, the voltage–current–emission framework offers theoretical guidance for achieving advanced LED devices for artificial intelligence (AI) technology.

title: Arene-Perfluoroarene-Enabled Electrostatic Modulation in Organic Porous Photocatalysts for Ni/Photoredox C–N Coupling
abstract: Abstract How molecular connectivity can tune photoresponsive local electrostatics in porous organic photocatalysts lacking long-range order remains unclear. Here, we use arene-perfluoroarene (AP)-based constitutional design to examine this relationship in 4CzIPN-derived porous photoredox polymers. Carbazole and perfluorocarbazole units are connected through ortho-, meta-, and para-linked biphenyl bridges. Kelvin probe force microscopy reveals local light-induced contact potential difference (CPD) shifts of 27.1, 18.3, 5.0, and 4.3 mV for o-CBCP, m-CBCP, p-CBCP, and the AP-free control P(4Cz), respectively. o-CBCP also exhibits a stronger surface photovoltage response than P(4Cz) and the lowest fitted intermediate-frequency resistance under 425 nm blue LED illumination. In a catalyst-discriminating Ni/photoredox C–N coupling reaction, product yields follow the same order as the local CPD shifts. With 0.2 mg of photocatalyst on a 0.2 mmol reaction scale, o-CBCP affords the product in good yield, whereas P(4Cz) gives only trace product. These findings identify linkage geometry as a molecular handle for tuning photoresponsive local electrostatics and catalytic behavior in disordered porous polymer photocatalysts.

title: A fractal analytical model for coupled thermo-mechanical permeability of porous rocks incorporating cross-coupling effects
abstract: Permeability evolution in porous rocks under coupled thermo-mechanical conditions is critical for deep underground engineering. Since the existing models treat the thermal and stress effects separately, they failed to capture their competing mechanisms of thermoelastic compaction and thermal cracking. To address this, we propose a novel fractal analytical model that incorporates a cross-coupling term into a fractal-based permeability framework. The model naturally produces a non-monotonic permeability evolution with temperature: initially decreasing due to thermoelastic compression, then rising as thermal cracking dominates and finally declining when stress-induced compaction overcomes thermal expansion. The proposed permeability model is expressed as a function of temperature, stress, and key fractal parameters including fractal dimensions for pore area and tortuosity. The model is validated against experimental data under different temperature-stress paths, demonstrating excellent agreement. Parametric analyses further reveal the roles of the thermo-mechanical loading rate and coupling coefficients in controlling permeability behavior, capturing the transition from thermoelastic reduction to thermal cracking enhancement. The proposed model offers a physically based and computationally efficient tool for evaluating coupled permeability evolution in deep high-temperature rock e…

title: The Global Significance of Renewable Energy: Contributions to Economic Growth and Environmental Sustainability
abstract: Renewable energy has moved from the margins of the global energy system to its leading edge, reshaping how electricity is generated, traded, and valued. This review synthesises recent evidence on the economic and environmental significance of renewable energy at a global scale. On the economic side, it examines investment trends, employment generation, the levelised cost of electricity (LCOE), energy security, and energy access, drawing on the latest data published by the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA), the International Energy Agency (IEA), and the International Labour Organization (ILO). On the environmental side, it reviews the contribution of renewables to greenhouse gas (GHG) mitigation, air quality, and the associated trade-offs in land, water, and material use. The review further discusses the policy architecture supporting the global energy transition, including the Paris Agreement and the COP28 tripling pledge, and identifies the principal barriers that continue to constrain deployment: grid integration and intermittency, storage costs, financing gaps in developing economies, and critical-mineral supply chains. The evidence indicates that renewable energy is no longer solely a climate mitigation tool but has become a central pillar of economic competitiveness, energy security, and industrial policy, while significant regional disparities in investment an…

title: EFFECTIVENESS AND IMPACT OF AI INTEGRATION ON TEACHING EXPERIENCES
abstract: The fast growth of artificial intelligence (AI) has created strong interest in how it can change higher education. AI tools brought new useful ways into undergraduate teaching, with the main goal of understanding how AI is currently being used in educational settings. Based on a review of recent studies and learning theories, this paper examines how tools such as intelligent tutoring systems, generative AI platforms, flexible learning technologies, and AI-supported feedback are changing teaching methods at the undergraduate level. The findings show that AI, when used carefully and fairly, can make learning more personal, increase student interest, and help teachers make better decisions based on student data. However, important challenges remain, such as concerns about fairness, student access to technology, teacher readiness, and the risk that students may stop thinking deeply on their own. The paper ends by suggesting a practical guide for using AI in teaching in a responsible and educationally sound way, and it calls for cooperation among schools, teachers, and government leaders to make the most of AI in undergraduate education.

title: CHARACTERISATION AND ESTIMATION OF THE WIND ENERGY POTENTIAL OF THE TOWN OF MELFI IN CHAD
abstract: This study characterised and estimated the wind energy potential of the town of Melfi in the Guera province of central Chad, situated at 11.06 north latitude and 17.93 east longitude at an altitude of 416 m. The data consisted of an hourly time series of wind speed and direction observed at 10 m above ground level over six years, from August 2020 to August 2026, comprising 52,536 valid data points. Monthly wind roses were produced to characterise the distribution of wind directions and intensities throughout the year. The quadratic mean method was chosen to calculate the average wind speed at the site, as it is more representative of the energy content of the wind than the simple arithmetic mean. Three independent methods were compared to extrapolate wind speed to heights of 50, 100 and 150 m: the variable-exponent power law of Justus and Mikhail, the logarithmic roughness law and the fixed-exponent power law of Hellmann. The annual wind speed was 3.50 m/s at 10 m above ground level and ranged from 4.9 to 7.1 m/s at heights of 100 to 150 m, depending on the method used. Of the three methods, that of Justus and Mikhail overestimated wind speed the most. The wind power density, calculated at 10, 50, 100 and 150 m, placed the site in Class 1 (low) at 10 and 50 m and in Class 2 at 100 and 150 m on an annual basis, with more favourable potential during the dry season.

title: Analysis of the Role of DCIM in Energy Optimization for Data Centers in Indonesia
abstract: The global digital transformation, accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic and the massive adoption of generative artificial intelligence (AI) architectures, has triggered an exponential surge in the construction of hyperscale data center infrastructure, positioning data centers among the most energy-intensive industrial facilities in the world. This research presents a comprehensive analysis of the role of Data Center Infrastructure Management (DCIM) as an instrument to diagnose, orchestrate, and improve energy efficiency, quantified specifically through the reduction of the Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) metric. Using a framework of systematic review and empirical multi-case analysis, this research explores the operational thermodynamic dynamics that cause inefficiencies, such as zombie servers and over- provisioning of HVAC systems. Quantitative analysis demonstrates that DCIM intelligence features can help reduce PUE, with several institutional facilities successfully lowering baseline PUE from 1.83 to 1.51 while cutting cooling loads by up to 48%. In Indonesia, DCIM integration supports the fulfillment of the mandates of SNI 8799:2020 and SPBE guidelines and helps mitigate peak load resilience risks for PT PLN (Persero).

title: A Layered Framework for Energy-Efficient Edge Computing in Sustainable IoT Systems
abstract: The proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) installations has resulted in an increased number of sensing, communication, storage, and computation operations performed by devices with limited resources. A typical cloud-centric approach results in unnecessary communication overhead, latency, and additional energy expenditure to transport large volumes of raw sensor data to remote datacenters. The proposed design uses adaptive sampling, data aggregation, compression, a workload-aware offloading mechanism, dynamic voltage/frequency scaling where available, and container consolidation and renewable-energy awareness, and carbon-aware workload placement, all of which are aligned with the direction of current Multi-access Edge Computing (MEC) standardization, and are now considering energy management, power information, and application-specific energy policies as first-class concerns.

title: Digital Integration of Zakat Management Systems in Islamic Fiscal Policy: An Evidence-Based Conceptual Framework
abstract: Zakat can complement public expenditure in addressing socioeconomic vulnerability, yet the records needed to examine their regional relationship remain dispersed across institutions. This study develops an evidence-based conceptual framework for integrating zakat management information, realized regional government expenditure (APBD), and socioeconomic indicators in Indonesia. Drawing on Design Science Research and qualitative document analysis, the study derives five functional and three non-functional requirements and translates them into a four-layer architecture comprising institutional data sources, integration and standardization, analytical information services, and fiscal monitoring outputs. The architecture proposes authorized data exchange, schema mapping, fund classification, geographic and temporal alignment, and cross-cutting governance controls. Three desk-based scenarios examine regional comparisons, the separation of zakat and APBD accounts, and the handling of inconsistent or restricted records. All eight requirements are mapped to architectural components, with four assessed as supported and four as partially supported at the design level. The framework offers a basis for coordinated fiscal analysis without transferring institutional financial authority, although operational feasibility and policy effects remain unverified.

title: Research on the Problems and Countermeasures of the Integration of Ideological and Political Education and Employment Education in the Training of Accounting Professionals
abstract: In the training of accounting professionals, the integration of ideological and political education and employment education is an important way to implement the fundamental task of moral education and enhance students' professional competence. However, there are still some outstanding problems in the process of integration, such as the separation of objectives, the disconnection of content and the lack of coordination between subjects, which restrict the training effect of the comprehensive quality of accounting talents. From the four dimensions of system design, concept cognition, resource allocation and operation mechanism, the causes of the problems are analyzed. Finally, the countermeasures and suggestions corresponding to each cause are put forward : improving the integration system and evaluation system, reshaping the concept of collaborative education, optimizing the allocation of teachers and platform resources, and improving the normal linkage operation mechanism. The purpose of this study is to provide an operable practical reference for the accounting profession to construct an educational model of deep integration of ideological and political education and employment education.

title: ATOMISTIC MOLECULAR DYNAMICS SIMULATION OF CU THIN-FILM GROWTH UNDER MOLECULAR BEAM EPITAXY CONDITIONS: EFFECTS OF SUBSTRATE TEMPERATURE AND INCIDENT KINETIC ENERGY
abstract: A molecular dynamics framework was developed to examine the combined influence of substrate temperature and incident kinetic energy on Cu-on-Cu(001) thin-film growth under molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) conditions. The simulations solve Newton's equations of motion using the Mishin embedded-atom method (EAM) potential for Cu-Cu interactions, while incident Cu atoms are introduced normal to the surface with kinetic energies of 0.1, 1, and 5 eV. Substrate temperatures of 300, 500, and 700 K generate a 3 x 3 process matrix. The deposited layer is quantified using vertical extent, RMS vertical spread, coordination number, and average atomic potential energy. The results reveal a non-monotonic morphology response: at 500 and 700 K the 1 eV condition gives the smallest RMS vertical spread, whereas 5 eV increases local coordination and produces a more negative deposited-atom potential energy but also a larger vertical dispersion. The study therefore identifies a competition between impact-assisted atomic rearrangement and morphology roughening. Because the atom arrival rate accessible to MD is much higher than experimental MBE fluxes, the model is interpreted in terms of relative atomistic trends rather than direct experimental growth rates.

title: Neighbourhood Built Environment and Sense of Community in Tropical Residential Neighbourhoods: An Observation-Based Comparative Study in Malaysia
abstract: The neighbourhood-built environment plays an important role in shaping social interaction and the development of a sense of community, particularly in rapidly urbanising tropical cities. While previous Malaysian studies have primarily used perception-based surveys, limited empirical attention has been given to the actual observation of physical neighbourhood features and their influence on social interaction and community cohesion. This study uses an observational analysis of two master-planned townships in Shah Alam, Selangor: Setia Alam and Bukit Jelutong, to evaluate the link between neighbourhood-built environment characteristics and a sense of community. A structured observation protocol was employed to assess eleven neighbourhoodbuilt environment attributes, including residential density, green infrastructure, architectural style, and recreational facilities, using a three point assessment scale. The findings indicate that although both neighbourhoods possess physical characteristics that support community development, they achieve these outcomes through different spatial planning approaches. Setia Alam scores in architectural, housing design excellence, and strong urban integration, promoting community identity and social interactions. Bukit Jelutong, on the other hand, benefits from lowered density, greater block sizes, and large green networks, which enhance spatial co…

title: Exploring Space Availability and Constraints for Children’s Leisure Activities in Kampung Gedong Pompa, North Jakarta
abstract: Children are vital to any nation, highlighting the long-term benefits of investing in their growth and well-being. This research addresses the knowledge gap regarding children’s leisure activities in densely populated urban neighborhoods. Specifically, it examines how children in Kampung Gedong Pompa, North Jakarta, navigate and utilize the limited available spaces for leisure within a community shaped by its proximity to the fishing industry infrastructure. The study uses observations, interviews, and photography to explore how children spend their leisure time and the spaces they select for these activities. The findings reveal the resourcefulness of children in Kampung Gedong Pompa in maximizing the limited spaces available for play, shaped significantly by community relationships and local cultural practices. However, the inadequate conditions of these spaces highlight an urgent need for interventions to provide safe, accessible, and enriching recreational areas. To improve children’s, play spaces in densely populated urban areas, the government must collaborate closely with local communities during planning, focusing on developing recreational facilities aligned with children’s preferences. title: BEYOND USABILITY: CRITICALLY EXAMINING USER-CENTERED WARDROBE DESIGN, INCLUSIVE ADAPTATION AND CONTEXTUAL OPTIMIZATION TRADE-OFFS
abstract: This systematic review comprehensively explores the multi-dimensional application mechanism, practical optimization effects and current research status of user-centered design (UCD) in residential wardrobe innovation. Guided by the PRISMA framework, this study adopts a rigorous systematic literature review methodology to ensure the standardization and transparency of the screening and synthesis process. Relevant literature covering wardrobe design, user-centered design, furniture usability and residential user experience was retrieved from the Web of Science and Scopus databases. Following strict screening based on unified inclusion and exclusion criteria, 48 peer-reviewed academic studies were finally selected for thematic coding and systematic synthesis. A standardized coding matrix was developed to extract core variables, including UCD dimensional characteristics, wardrobe functional and experiential performance, user adaptive effects and scenario-based boundary conditions. This review clarifies that UCD improves wardrobe comprehensive performance through three hierarchical pathways: physiological ergonomic adaptation, precise functional demand matching, and multi-scenario experience upgrading. This study is motivated by the phenomenon of increasing revenue and total assets during the 2022–2025 period, which was not followed by an improvement in asset utilization efficiency and company profitability. Revenue increased from IDR 178.765 billion in 2022 to IDR 260.329 billion in 2025, while total assets increased from IDR 57.361 billion to IDR 412.354 billion. During the same period, TATO decreased from 3.12 times to 0.63 times, while ROA decreased from 133% to 29%. This condition indicates a gap between the growth of assets and revenue and the effectiveness of asset utilization and company profitability. This study employs a quantitative approach using causal or explanatory research. The data consist of secondary data obtained from the financial statements of PT PNM Kabanjahe Branch for the period from January 2022 to December 2025. The research sample consists of 48 monthly financial statement observations selected using a saturated sampling technique. title: Regulatory Direction for Physical Protection Systems in the Standard Design Approval Stage of Light-Water Small Modular Reactors
abstract: As the deployment of small modular reactors (SMRs) and advanced reactors expands, physical protection system regulatory frameworks are shifting from prescriptive, compliance-driven approaches to risk-informed and performance-based methodologies. In Korea, the amendment to the Act on Physical Protection and Radiological Emergency, promulgated on March 31, 2026, establishes a legal basis for the institutionalization of Security by Design (SbD) by requiring physical protection regulations to be reviewed from the Standard Design Approval (SDA) stage onward. This study examines the applicable regulatory direction for the SDA stage of Light-Water SMRs based on an analysis of regulatory trends in major countries. It investigates alternative requirements reflecting SMR-specific characteristics and performance-based regulatory approaches and proposes a preliminary regulatory framework incorporating performance assessment feedback into design improvement. The findings serve as a technical foundation for developing review guidance at the SDA stage to advance SbD institutionalization in Korea.

title: Creative Tensions: Leveraging Cultural Diversity through Innovation to Drive Design Entrepreneurship
abstract: In today’s culturally diverse world, design entrepreneurs increasingly engage with people from various backgrounds but often struggle to leverage cultural differences for creative and business growth. While interest in inclusive innovation is rising, the role of cultural diversity in design entrepreneurship success remains unclear. This study explores how cultural diversity influences design entrepreneurship performance, emphasizing the mediating role of cross-cultural innovation. A narrative review of 22 peer-reviewed articles from the Scopus database, spanning entrepreneurship, design thinking, cultural studies, and innovation management was conducted. The findings informed a conceptual framework built on four key ideas: cultural diversity directly impacts both cross-cultural innovation and design entrepreneurship outcomes; cross-cultural innovation enhances entrepreneurial performance; and it also mediates the link between cultural diversity and business success. The analysis reveals that diverse perspectives create creative tension and generate richer, more culturally resonant solutions, particularly when innovation practices are inclusive. The study establishes new theoretical links among cultural intelligence, design thinking, and resource-based views. It also offers practical insights for entrepreneurs and educators on fostering culturally aware and innovative teams. Fur…

title: Design of an Adaptive English Vocabulary Learning System Based on Fuzzy Modeling of Second Language Vocabulary Features
abstract: Second language vocabulary acquisition is dynamic, individualized, and uncertain. Traditional vocabulary learning systems often use static difficulty grading or simple frequency statistics, which are difficult to accurately adapt to learners’ cognitive states and real-time needs. In response to this issue, this article designs and implements an adaptive English vocabulary learning system based on fuzzy modeling of second language vocabulary features, using the cognitive psychology knowledge acquisition theory (three stages of understanding consolidation application) as the teaching framework. The system focuses on personalized vocabulary resource recommendation as its core goal, aiming to improve learning efficiency and stimulate learning interest. The overall architecture includes five functional modules: pre-test diagnosis, vocabulary acquisition, consolidation and application, effectiveness testing, and learning feedback, forming a closed-loop iterative learning path. At the algorithmic level, the system introduces fuzzy logic as the main inference mechanism, breaking through the rigid discrimination of “right or wrong” in classical binary logic, and using multi value membership degrees to describe the continuous spectrum of learners’ abilities. In the fuzzification stage, four behavioral indicators are selected as input variables: daily online learning duration, daily vocab…

title: Hacia un consenso colombiano sobre el trastorno bipolar: protocolo y diseño de un Delphi modificado para la adaptación de la evidencia al contexto nacional
abstract: Introducción: El trastorno bipolar es una condición mental crónica y recurrente asociada con elevada carga de enfermedad, discapacidad funcional, mortalidad prematura y riesgo de suicidio. Aunque existen guías internacionales para su diagnóstico y tratamiento, su aplicabilidad puede verse limitada por diferencias entre sistemas de salud y contextos asistenciales. Objetivo: Describir el desarrollo metodológico del Consenso Colombiano sobre el Trastorno Bipolar, realizado mediante un Delphi modificado para contextualizar la evidencia científica al escenario nacional. Métodos: Se desarrolló un consenso de expertos basado en evidencia mediante un Delphi modificado. El proceso incluyó priorización de preguntas clínicas, estructuración PICO cuando fue aplicable, revisión estructurada y pragmática de la evidencia, formulación de enunciados y dos rondas Delphi virtuales. Los enunciados se valoraron en una escala de nueve puntos. Los criterios de consenso, establecidos a priori, fueron mediana ≥7, rango intercuartílico ≤2 y acuerdo ≥80%, sin objeciones cualitativas sustantivas. Los enunciados susceptibles de modificación fueron reformulados antes de la segunda ronda; aquellos que no alcanzaron los criterios tras esta fueron clasificados como sin consenso. Conclusiones: El proceso proporciona un marco estructurado y transparente para contextualizar la evidencia sobre el trastorno bipolar…

abstract: Security teams must prioritize telemetry collection, but technique-level coverage counts do not show whether the evidence declared by a detection analytic is available in a selected portfolio or how strongly that support depends on individual components. This study formulates identity-telemetry selection as an exact portfolio problem using MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise Detection Strategies, Analytics, and Data Components. A prespecified name rule identified 18 active identity components. A strategy was conditionally supported (identity-side) when at least one associated Analytic had all its identity-component requirements in the portfolio, assuming that all nonidentity requirements are available. Exhaustive enumeration calculated nominal support and support under a single-component omission stress test across ATT&CK releases 18.0–19.2, together with a lower-bound measure that counts only Analytics declaring no nonidentity requirements. Each release contained 150 eligible strategies. In release 19.2, six components supported 129 strategies (86.0%), seven 135 (90.0%), ten 144 (96.0%), and fifteen all 150. Complete collection retained only 111 strategies (74.0%) after omission of the most damaging component; Logon Session Creation, User Account Authentication, and Logon Session Metadata accounted for losses of 39, 30, and 17 strategies. Only 123 of 326 eligible Analytics were identity-o…

title: Digital Technologies and Virtual Environments in Language Learning
abstract: Digital technologies can expand opportunities for language practice, feedback, and access to learning materials, but their educational value depends on how they are integrated into instruction. This conceptual article draws on a selective narrative review to examine automatic speech recognition, conversational agents, machine translation, and virtual environments in language learning. It distinguishes the functions of these technologies from the learning outcomes that teachers must evaluate. The discussion identifies opportunities for pronunciation practice, sustained interaction, reflective revision, and contextualized communication, alongside problems involving unreliable feedback, cognitive demands, unequal access, and personal data. Alpha School is considered briefly as an institutional illustration of adaptive learning and human guidance, rather than as evidence of foreign-language learning effectiveness. Four proposed classroom applications show how teachers can connect digital activity to observable language performance. The article argues that responsible integration requires clear learning objectives, appropriate scaffolding, human review of feedback, and opportunities to demonstrate learning beyond the original tool. Its contribution is a practical framework for evaluating instructional use; the proposed applications require subsequent classroom investigation.

title: Plant Dehydrin-Derived, Lysine-Rich Peptides Show Both Antifungal Activity and Blood–Brain Barrier Penetration
abstract: Abstract The plant-based, dehydrin-derived peptides represent an underexplored source of antifungal agents. In this study, we investigated the antifungal activity, cellular association, and blood–brain barrier (BBB) permeability of a lysine-rich peptide (ERD-A) derived from the Arabidopsis thaliana dehydrin ERD14, as well as its rationally designed sequence variants. The amino acid substitutions were engineered to modulate charge, aromatic residue content, and conformational flexibility. Antifungal activity was assessed against clinically relevant yeasts, including Candida albicans, Candidozyma auris, and Cryptococcus neoformans. The parental ERD-A peptide exhibited moderate activity against C. albicans and C. neoformans, while most variants showed species-dependent changes in potency. Increased cationicity or introduction of tryptophan residues enhanced activity against C. neoformans, with several variants displaying 4-fold lower MIC values than the parental peptide. In contrast, C. auris showed limited susceptibility to all tested variants. Fluorescence microscopy and flow cytometry demonstrated strong, time-dependent cell association of carboxyfluorescein-labeled ERD-A in C. albicans, reaching ∼98 to 99% positive cells after 16 h. BBB permeability was evaluated using an in vitro model of cocultured human brain endothelial cells with pericytes. All ERD-A-derived peptides exhi…

title: Medicinal Plant Used in Management of Mouth Ulcer: A Review
abstract: Mouth ulcer is a common oral condition that may be associated with local trauma, aphthous stomatitis and other factors. Herbal medicines have been traditionally used for the management of oral disorders because many medicinal plants contain bioactive constituents with reported antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, antioxidant and wound-healing properties. This review summarizes medicinal plants reported for the management of mouth ulcer and discusses their traditional or experimental use in herbal formulations. Plants such as Aloe barbadensis, Psidium guajava, Glycyrrhiza glabra ,Curcuma longa, Punica granatum, Piper betle, Cordia dichotoma, Capsicum annuum and Morinda citrifolia have been reported in the literature. Herbal gels and other preparations containing these plants have also been investigated. The available literature provides a basis for further research and formulation development; however,evidence varies among individual plants and many reports are experimental rather than clinical. The two most causes are aphthous stomatitis, alsoknown as canker soreness, and local injury or trauma, such as rubbing agains t a tooth or dental filling's sharp edge. Aphthous stomatitis causes mouth ulcers to occur repeatedly, and its exact cause is often not known.

title: Deep generative virtual staining for breast cancer: from H&E histology to HER2 immunohistochemistry
abstract: Abstract Immunohistochemistry (IHC) remains the clinical gold standard for molecular profiling in breast cancer; however, traditional workflows are hindered by high costs, reagent dependency, and tissue exhaustion. Virtual staining has emerged as a computational alternative; however, prevailing virtual staining models often fail to preserve high-frequency structural details critical for perceptual and histological fidelity. We present a novel chemically-informed, two-stage conditional Generative Adversarial Network (cGAN) framework designed for high-fidelity H&E-to-IHC translation. Our approach uniquely decouples chemical stain extraction from high-resolution textural refinement through a specialized StainMapper (G₁) and a score-conditioned RefineGenerator (G₂). By integrating multi-scale hierarchical score conditioning with a hybrid loss function including adversarial, perceptual, Sobel edge, and stain-consistency terms, the framework enforces both global distributional realism and local morphological precision. Evaluated on the BCI and HER2match benchmarks, our model achieves state-of-the-art performance, reaching a Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) of 59.67 , PSNR of 22.50 dB , SSIM of 0.4773 , LPIPS of 0.5279 and KID of 0.0264 ± 0.0086 on BCI; PSNR of 20.66 dB , LPIPS of 0.4486 , FID of 20.42 , and KID of 0.0124 ± 0.0092 on HER2match, outperforming all baselines on distribut…

abstract: Abstract This paper proposes an innovative method for optimizing power grids with high renewable energy penetration by employing particle swarm optimization (PSO) to strategically allocate static synchronous compensators (STATCOMs). The approach, implemented through DIgSILENT’s programming language (DPL), aims to minimize voltage deviations and power losses while maximizing the reactive power reserve (RPR) from solar power plants to enhance grid stability and efficiency. The effectiveness of the method is tested under various system contingencies, including short-circuit faults and generation loss events. Results demonstrate that optimally placed STATCOMs significantly improve voltage profiles in the neighboring areas during disturbances. The study also evaluates different control modes for photovoltaic (PV) solar systems, with findings highlighting the importance of voltage control mode in preventing system collapse. Additionally, integrating RPR from solar power plants, particularly in combination with STATCOMs, is highly effective in maintaining a healthy voltage profile.

abstract: Abstract The CH₄ content of the LFG declines progressively while CO₂ increases, degrading combustion stability until engines can no longer sustain reliable operation below a CH₄ threshold of approximately 40 volume percent (vol.%). This paper investigates the combustion physics behind this degradation and evaluates hydrogen enrichment as a mitigation strategy that projects to extend plant operational life by more than a decade beyond the conventional shut-off point, under the assumptions and the empirically calibrated stability mapping. A custom numerical solver was developed in MATLAB and was validated against the canonical coflow diffusion flame benchmark experiments. Parametric simulations systematically varied the CO₂ fraction from 0 to 60 vol.% and the hydrogen (H₂) enrichment level from 0 to 40 vol.%, yielding quantitative maps of adiabatic flame temperature, equivalent flame speed, ignition delay, and radical pool concentrations. Increasing CO₂ from 0 to 60 vol.% reduces Da (Damköhler number) by 83%, doubles ignition delay to 3.16 ms, and depresses the OH radical pool by 49%; 30 vol.% H₂ enrichment fully restores stable operation (Da ≥ 5 in the laminar flame model), projecting, under the stated assumptions and pending engine-level validation, a 14-year plant-life extension and doubling CO₂-equivalent avoidance to 60,700 tonnes. title: Effects of DBC Copper Layer Thickness on the Electrical, Thermal, and Thermo-Mechanical Performance of Parallel SiC Chip Power Modules
abstract: Direct Bonded Copper (DBC) substrates simultaneously provide current conduction, heat spreading, and structural support in multi-chip power modules, making Cu thickness a key trade-off variable. This study investigates the effects of DBC Cu thickness on the electrical, thermal, and thermo-mechanical responses of a 300 A parallel SiC chip power module. Thermal-coupling analysis was performed to distinguish the temperature effects of chip spacing from those of top Cu thickness. Electro-thermal simulation showed that conduction loss and maximum chip temperature increased as the top Cu thickness decreased, with a pronounced change between 0.175 and 0.160 mm under the 300 A condition. Thermo-mechanical analysis showed that reducing the symmetric top/bottom Cu thickness from 0.30/0.30 to 0.15/0.15 mm decreases reflow warpage of the baseplate from 183.930 to 30.091 μm. Thermal-cycling analysis showed that the cycle increment in volume-averaged inelastic strain energy density in the evaluated solder region decreased by 17.2%. The results showed distinct thickness-dependent responses: reducing the top Cu thickness increased conduction loss and maximum chip temperature, whereas symmetrically reducing both the top and bottom Cu thicknesses decreased reflow warpage and solder inelastic strain energy density in simulation.

Secure Sharing Governance of User-Generated Content in Blockchain-enabled Virtual Communities
abstract: User Generated Content (UGC) is an important repository of knowledge in virtual communities but there are risks to it being widely available and replica. These risks include loss of privacy, unauthorized reuse, experience of misinformation, the infringements of rights, and maliciously distributed knowledge. Current governance on platforms concentrates on the ability to access the knowledge freely but also on reviewing and removing that data once the user generates it and subsequently posts it. Current governance structures cannot sufficiently balance the goals of knowledge sharing, user autonomy, accountability of the platform for the actions of the user, and the security of the user’s generated content. This paper presents a framework for governing UGC using a decentralized governance approach utilizing a blockchain. The technical approach to governance of blockchain was used in developing programmable trust infrastructure. This includes the use of decentralized identity, traceability of UGC content, a chain of evidence prohibiting modification of evidence, the use of smart contracts for providing consent, the ability to provide privacy for access, and providing both the incentive to share and accountability for why that incentive is used. abstract: High-rise mixed-use towers in tropical climates, including Abuja's tropical savanna environment, face environmental conditions that can increase cooling demand, particularly high solar exposure, substantial diurnal temperature variation and the need for reliable environmental control. This study examines the extent to which sustainable design strategies are incorporated in selected mixed-use and high-rise precedents, with particular relevance to Abuja's Central Business District. A purposive case-study approach was employed to examine five precedents: World Trade Center Abuja, Pixel Building in Melbourne, The Edge in Amsterdam, PARKROYAL on Pickering in Singapore, and Oasia Hotel Downtown in Singapore. The cases were analysed thematically using architectural documentation, published project information, certification records and available performance literature. Recurring strategies included external solar shading, perforated and layered façades, controlled glazing, natural or mixed-mode ventilation, vertical functional zoning, atrium and void spaces, thermal buffering and integrated greenery. The analysis indicates that environmental performance in the selected precedents is generally approached through combinations of complementary architectural and building-system strategies rather than through a single intervention. title: Energy Efficiency and Thermal Performance Analysis of a Centrifugal Pump: Effect of Insulation Retrofit on Heat Loss Reduction
abstract: Centrifugal pumps are widely used in industry, agriculture, and the home. Their energy efficiency is determined by hydraulic losses, friction, and electrical losses in the drive system. This study experimentally examines the effect of external thermal insulation on the case heat transfer and the overall efficiency of a 0.5HP (0.373 kW) centrifugal pump. The suggested approach studies the case of an uninsulated pump at different insulation thicknesses – 5, 10, 15, 20 mm. The electric power, flow rate, head, surrounding temperature, fluid temperature, and case surface temperature are estimated to evaluate the hydraulic and thermal efficiency of the pump. The approximated heat loss from the case is observed to reduce from 31.5 W (uninsulated) to 16.8 W (with 20 mm insulation), suggesting a 46.7% reduction. The wire-to-water efficiency increases slightly from 12.25% to 12.28%. The findings suggest that insulating the external case might be successful in minimizing heat losses from the pump case. However, its effect on the overall efficiency of the pump seems to be small. The findings have to be considered within the framework of the measurement approach, experimental variability, and the necessity to ensure adequate cooling for the motor and other essential components.

title: Promoting Energy-Saving Behaviour in Households: The Integrated Technology Engagement Canvas (iTECH)
abstract: Home technology adoption in Sustainable Smart Cities (SSCs) is essential for reducing carbon emissions, yet household engagement remains limited and existing energy-saving strategies are often weakly grounded in behavioural theory. This study aims to systematically review household energy-saving intervention strategies and to develop a theory-informed framework to address this gap. A systematic review was conducted using Scopus, including peer-reviewed journal articles published from 2012 to 2024 that propose or evaluate household-level strategies for promoting energy-saving behaviour (ESB). Following screening and eligibility assessment, 24 studies were included in the review. The extracted strategies were analysed and synthesised using constructs from cognitive and technology adoption theories to develop the integrated Technology Engagement Canvas for Households (iTECH). The review shows that 38% of studies focus on knowledge enhancement strategies, primarily targeting perceived usefulness and social norms, while strategies addressing beliefs, personal norms, and awareness of consequences are rarely considered. By systematically linking existing intervention strategies with behavioural theory, this study moves beyond prior strategy-based approaches and proposes iTECH as a holistic, theory informed framework for evaluating and strengthening household energy-saving intervention…
