title: Predicting 30-Day Hospital Readmission in Diabetic Patients Using Machine Learning
abstract: Hospital readmissions are a significant problem in healthcare, particularly in diabetic patients. The research question guiding this study was: Can 30-day hospital readmission for diabetic patients be predicted using common machine learning models applied to hospital record data? This study aims to predict this using three machine learning models: Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and XGBoost. The analysis was conducted on the Diabetes 130-US Hospitals dataset from the UCI Machine Learning Repository, which contains over 100,000 patient records. After data cleaning, 98,053 complete records with 20 features were used for model training and evaluation. Random Forest achieved the highest accuracy at 88.73%, Logistic Regression at 88.67%, and XGBoost at 88.59%. Moreover, the XGBoost model’s Area Under the Curve (AUC) was only 0.653, indicating performance slightly better than random guessing. The number of lab procedures were found to be the strongest predictor of readmission, followed by different diagnoses and number of medications. The models struggled to identify readmitted patients due to dataset imbalance, with only 11.3% of patients readmitted. These findings suggest that while machine learning can predict readmission status with reasonable overall accuracy, current models are not reliable enough for clinical use without additional features and improved data quality.

title: An Analysis of Dimensions of English Learning Motivation among Female Secondary School Students in Quetta, Balochistan
abstract: Motivation significantly influences second and foreign language learning by impacting learners' behaviors, including their involvement, effort, persistence, and participation in related activities. This study aimed to examine the aspects of English learning motivation of female secondary school students in government schools in Quetta, Pakistan. A quantitative descriptive survey design was utilized, focusing on female students in Grades 9 and 10 from government girls' secondary schools in Quetta, with a sample of 364 students chosen through simple random sampling. The data were obtained by using a structured questionnaire to measure four dimensions of English learning motivation which are namely engagement, interest, persistence, and intrinsic/extrinsic motivation. Descriptive statistics such as frequency, percentage, and mean and standard deviation were used to analyze the data. The findings showed that the students' overall level of English learning motivation was high, the mean score of which was 3.55 and the standard deviation was 0.70. The mean scores for the four dimensions were: intrinsic/extrinsic motivation (M = 3.79), interest (M = 3.68), engagement (M = 3.50), and persistence (M = 3.29). The study revealed that students exhibited a good level of motivation for learning English, although their persistence remained moderate. While overall attitudes toward learning Engl…

title: Exploring Outcomes of a Learning Theory–Driven Pilot Medical Pathway Program: A Preliminary Evaluation
abstract: Background/Introduction Premedical pathway programs serve as vehicles to advance equity and access for students who have experienced systemic barriers to education, yet few explicitly address the academic skill development necessary for success in rigorous science courses. Undergraduate premedical students face significant cognitive load, and success requires not only content knowledge but also the metacognitive learning strategies (MLS) needed to process, integrate, and retrieve information. Methods This pilot study examined whether a learning-theory-driven summer intensive delivered by a trained learning specialist was associated with statistically significant gains on the Learning and Study Strategies Inventory (LASSI) scales based on the foci of the curriculum. A pre-post design was employed with 16 students in the Program. All ten LASSI scales were administered at program entry and exit. Six scales targeted by the curriculum were designated primary outcomes, and the remaining four were reported as secondary outcomes. Open ended survey responses were analyzed using deductive thematic coding. Results/Findings Paired samples t-tests revealed significant gains on all six targeted scales, each of which remained significant after Holm correction: Information Processing (p = .011), Selecting Main Ideas (p = .012), Test Strategies (p = .003), Self-Testing (p = .003), Time Manageme…

title: Effect of Team Assisted Individualization on Fabric Embellishment Practical Learning Outcomes
abstract: Students in vocational practical courses start with uneven skills, so an instructional model has to cope with that gap without losing sight of individual accountability. This quasi-experimental pretest–posttest study compared Team Assisted Individualization (TAI) with conventional instruction in a Fabric Embellishment Techniques course of a Diploma III Fashion Design program. Two intact parallel classes of 13 students each (N = 26) took part in the second semester of academic year 2024–2025, and a lottery decided which class received TAI. Practical performance was scored on a 0–100 scale before and after instruction. The TAI class rose from 72.38 to 88.85 and the conventional class from 70.77 to 81.31, mean gains of 16.46 and 10.54 points. The classes did not differ significantly at pretest (p = .231), although the TAI class started 1.62 points higher. At posttest the difference was 7.54 points, t(24) = 4.42, p < .001, and the difference in gains was 5.92 points, t(24) = 6.48, p < .001. Because each condition was delivered to a single intact class, these student-level tests cannot separate the teaching model from class-specific influences, and the results are best treated as preliminary evidence.

abstract: Aims: This study aims to identify the need for Islamic financial technology (Islamic fintech) as an alternative to support Islamic financial literacy and inclusion in Indonesia. It also describes the factors that hinder the conversion of Islamic financial knowledge into the actual use of formal financial services and summarizes governance pillars, drawn from the literature and oriented toward Maqashid al-Shariah, to promote equitable and sustainable financial inclusion. Method: This study employs a library research method with a qualitative-descriptive approach. Data were collected through a review of scientific literature, regulations, and official reports relevant to Islamic financial literacy, financial inclusion, and the development of Islamic fintech in Indonesia. The literature was identified, selected, classified into five dimensions (Table 1), and synthesized descriptively to describe the literacy-inclusion gap, its contributing factors, and the opportunities and challenges of Islamic financial digitalization. The study does not apply thematic coding, empirical testing, or the development of a formal framework. Results: The findings reveal a substantial gap between Islamic financial literacy and Islamic financial inclusion in Indonesia, as reported in national survey data. This gap indicates that public knowledge has not been fully translated into the utilization of Isl…

abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengkaji pengaruh penerapan model pembelajaran Project Based Learning (PjBL) yang didukung oleh media pembelajaran tiga dimensi terhadap peningkatan hasil belajar kognitif siswa pada materi sistem ekskresi manusia. Data dikumpulkan melalui tes pilihan ganda yang telah melalui uji validitas, reliabilitas, tingkat kesukaran, dan daya pembeda. Analisis data dilakukan dengan menghitung nilai N-Gain, melakukan uji normalitas, serta uji hipotesis menggunakan One Sample T-Test melalui aplikasi SPSS. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa nilai rata-rata N-Gain sebesar 0,72, yang termasuk dalam kategori tinggi. Uji T menghasilkan nilai signifikansi 0,001 yang lebih kecil dari 0,05, sehingga H₀ ditolak dan H₁ diterima, menandakan adanya pengaruh signifikan dari penerapan model PjBL terhadap hasil belajar kognitif siswa. title: From competency to enterprise impact: a decision architecture for talent development in AI-enabled work
abstract: Purpose Competency evidence alone can be insufficient for forward-looking talent decisions when AI materially redesigns work. This article introduces STEP-I (Systemic Talent Evolution and Performance Impact), a decision architecture for roles in transition. Design/methodology/approach A practice-informed synthesis based on the author’s capability-acceleration work in delivery centers and financial services, now applied at an organizational evaluation site. Findings Competency frameworks remain necessary for current-role readiness. During bounded AI-enabled redesign, decisions should also consider separate evidence of developmental capacity, enabling conditions and prospective contribution. Research limitations/implications STEP-I has not been validated. A longitudinal evaluation is planned and will be reported separately, testing whether the pillars yield distinguishable evidence, whether assessors judge consistently, whether development produces contribution, and under which conditions it is useful. Practical implications Leaders can use STEP-I alongside essential role criteria to differentiate development and reassess evidence, never as a single score or an override of lawful requirements. title: Emerging sociotechnical imaginaries of Edtech and AI in education policy discourse in Nigeria
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the dominant actor imaginaries of Edtech and Artificial Intelligence in education (AIED) embedded in Nigerian policy discourse under the Tinubu administration, and the argumentation strategies used to legitimise them. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on the Discourse-Historical Approach (DHA), this study combines a socio-historical analysis with an analysis of a corpus of public texts emerging from the most salient events related to this policy discourse in Nigeria since 2023. Findings Education policy discourse in Nigeria is increasingly driven by a sociotechnical imaginary that positions Edtech and AI as a solution to the persistent problem of education access and equality, and as a catalyst for economic growth. This discourse frames local actors as lacking capacity, and collaboration with transnational corporate and philanthropic actors as necessary to provide the technical, financial, and institutional capacity. It also rests on a demographic argument that constructs the country’s large youth population as a demographic risk/opportunity, whose value lies in its capacity to be mobilised as a workforce for the emerging global technologies market. Strategic Formulation of Digital Literacy Learning in Indonesian Elementary Education: A SWOT-AHP Approach
abstract: The implementation of digital literacy in Indonesian elementary schools is essential for 21st-century education, yet it faces persistent challenges in teacher competence, infrastructure availability, and curriculum integration. This study aims to develop prioritized digital literacy strategies for elementary schools in Indonesia based on a comprehensive analysis of internal and external factors. A sequential mixed methods approach was used. The qualitative phase involved focus group discussions and interviews with 71 educators and experts, selected through purposive sampling, to identify Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, and Threats (SWOT). The quantitative phase applied the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) with eight key experts to weigh the SWOT factors and the resulting alternative strategies. The SWOT analysis identified high student motivation and potential for developing 21st-century skills as key strengths; limited teacher pedagogical and technological competence and limited access to infrastructure as major weaknesses; government support and digital learning resources as main opportunities; and cybersecurity and disinformation as serious threats. The AHP results showed that Opportunities had the highest priority (weight 0.385), followed by Weaknesses (0.310). title: Artificial Intelligence for MPLS and Segment Routing Traffic Engineering: A Systematic Review of Machine Learning, Reinforcement Learning, and Deep Reinforcement Learning
abstract: The growing complexity and variability of network traffic have increased the demand for adaptive traffic engineering in Multiprotocol Label Switching (MPLS) and Segment Routing networks. Conventional approaches, including constraint-based routing, mathematical programming, and heuristic optimization, provide established mechanisms for path selection and resource allocation but may encounter computational and operational limitations under dynamic network conditions. Artificial Intelligence (AI), particularly Machine Learning (ML), Reinforcement Learning (RL), and Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL), offers alternative approaches to traffic prediction, adaptive routing, congestion management, and policy optimization. This paper presents a systematic literature review framework for AI-assisted traffic engineering in MPLS and Segment Routing networks, guided by PRISMA(Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses.) 2020. The review aims to classify intelligent optimization techniques, examine their integration with forwarding and control architectures, and critically evaluate their effectiveness against conventional routing approaches. Key evaluation dimensions include link utilization, throughput, latency, packet loss, computational overhead, routing stability, generalization, and constraint satisfaction. Particular emphasis is placed on experimental methodologi…

title: The Effect of Implementing Slow Deep Breathing Therapy and Warm Foot Soaks on Blood Pressure in Elderly Hypertension Patients in The Inpatient Areas at Grandmed Hospital, Lubuk Pakam
abstract: Hypertension is a chronic disease often experienced by the elderly and is a major risk factor for cardiovascular disease. Blood pressure control in the elderly can be done through pharmacological and non-pharmacological therapy. Non-pharmacological therapy that is easy, safe, and can be done independently is Slow Deep Breathing Therapy and soaking feet in warm water. The combination of these two therapies can provide a relaxing effect, reduce the activity of the sympathetic nervous system, and increase peripheral vasodilation. This study aims to determine the effect of the application of Slow Deep Breathing Therapy and soaking feet in warm water on blood pressure in elderly people with hypertension in the inpatient ward of Grandmed Hospital Lubuk Pakam in 2025. Method: This study used a quantitative design with a pre-experimental method through a one group pretest-posttest approach. The study sample consisted of 20 elderly people with hypertension who were selected using a purposive sampling technique. Blood pressure measurements were taken before and after the intervention. Data analysis was carried out using the Shapiro-Wilk normality test and the Wilcoxon Signed Rank Test with a significance level of 0.05. title: Dimension-independent approximation of smooth functions on Riemannian manifolds using deep ReLU neural networks
abstract: Deep neural architectures owe much of their remarkable success to their capacity to approximate high-dimensional data while seemingly bypassing the curse of dimensionality — a phenomenon often linked to the capability to uncover intrinsic lower-dimensional structures within the data. To provide a theoretical foundation for this phenomenon, we investigate the problem of approximating functions defined on a [Formula: see text]-dimensional manifold embedded within a space of potentially much higher ambient dimension [Formula: see text]. We prove that [Formula: see text]-deep ReLU neural networks with fixed width that scales polynomially with [Formula: see text] can approximate [Formula: see text]-times continuously differentiable functions with an error of order [Formula: see text]. The innovation of this result lies in the total removal of the ambient dimension [Formula: see text] from the approximation constant. By ensuring that the constant [Formula: see text] is independent of [Formula: see text], we offer a significant improvement over prior work and provide a definitive theoretical explanation for the network’s resilience to high-dimensional environments.

title: Coupled carbonate-shale thallium isotopes reveal the evolution of deep-marine anoxia during the end-Permian mass extinction
abstract: Ocean anoxia played a key role in the end-Permian mass extinction, the most severe biotic crisis in Earth’s history, yet reconstructions of oxygenation through this event have lacked a focus on deep-water oxygen loss. Thallium isotopes, which track deep-ocean oxygenation via manganese oxide burial, offer a potential solution but have only been applied to siliciclastic sections, limiting spatial and temporal coverage. Here, we present a combined carbonate-shale Tl isotope record, spanning four geographically distant regions and providing a near-continuous record of global-scale redox change during the extinction interval. Both lithologies record deep-marine anoxia beginning 1 million years before the extinction, demonstrating that carbonate- and shale-hosted Tl isotopes preserve consistent redox signals. Late Permian oxygen depletion likely remained largely constrained to the deep ocean and was distinct from the shelf- and slope-depth euxinia of the Early Triassic that was coupled with climate warming and central to the loss of animal diversity.

Isothermal annealing optimization for enhanced mechanical performance of FFF-printed PEKK gyroid structures
abstract: Purpose This study aims to establish a systematic isothermal annealing post-treatment to mitigate residual stress and poor interlayer adhesion inherent in fused filament fabrication (FFF) of polyetherketoneketone (PEKK), thereby enhancing the mechanical performance of printed components. The optimized protocol is further extended to gyroid triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) structures to evaluate its broader applicability. Design/methodology/approach Thermal transitions and stability were characterized via differential scanning calorimetry and thermogravimetric analysis, revealing a glass transition temperature of ∼218 °C and stability up to 542 °C. X-ray diffraction and molecular dynamics simulations confirmed predominantly amorphous behavior. Annealing was conducted at 180, 200, 220, 240 and 260 °C for 6 h under constrained conditions followed by furnace cooling, with flexural testing used for the optimization. Failure mechanisms were examined via digital microscopy and scanning electron microscopy. The optimized protocol was validated on cylindrical gyroid structures under compression. Findings Annealing at 240°C increased flexural modulus and strength by 58.7 % and 72.7 %, respectively, shifting failure from delamination to bulk fracture. title: Spatial optimization of rainwater harvesting infrastructure using comparative GIS-MCDM approaches in a semi-arid basin
abstract: Abstract Water scarcity in semi-arid regions is intensifying under climate variability and growing pressure on water resources, necessitating the development of efficient and spatially optimized Rainwater Harvesting (RWH) systems. This study presents a GIS-based decision-support framework to optimize RWH infrastructure siting in the Dinarta basin, by integrating hydrological analysis with Multi-Criteria Decision Making. Five methods, Weighted Overlay, SAW, TOPSIS, ELECTRE, and VIKOR, were applied to spatial criteria derived from remote sensing and terrain analysis. Model performance was evaluated through statistical and hydrological validation. ROC analysis against existing RWH infrastructure locations showed that VIKOR achieved the highest spatial discrimination capacity (AUC = 0.822), followed by Weighted Overlay (AUC = 0.816). Independent hydrological validation against SCS-CN-derived runoff using the Quality Sum framework further confirmed the physical consistency of the predicted priority zones. The final VIKOR map indicates that about 10.5% (42.7 Km 2 ) of the basin falls within high to very high suitability classes, concentrated in southern and central lowlands where specific conditions enhance storage feasibility and recharge potential. title: Formulation Optimization and Evaluation of Metronidazole Emulgel for Localized Management of Periodontal Infections
abstract: Background: Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory condition associated with periodontal pathogens, and conventional systemic antimicrobial therapy may be associated with systemic adverse effects and antimicrobial resistance. Localized delivery of antimicrobial agents directly into periodontal pockets may improve drug retention at the site of infection while reducing unnecessary systemic exposure. Metronidazole is particularly useful against anaerobic microorganisms associated with periodontal infections. The present study aimed to develop and evaluate a metronidazole-loaded mucoadhesive emulgel for localized periodontal drug delivery. Methods: Metronidazole emulgels were prepared using Carbopol 940 and Carbopol 934 as gelling agents. The formulation consisted of an oil-in-water emulsion incorporated into a gel base containing liquid paraffin, Span 20, Tween 20, propylene glycol, hydroxypropyl methylcellulose, and other suitable excipients. The prepared formulations were evaluated for physical appearance, homogeneity, pH, viscosity, spreadability, extrudability, drug content, and grittiness. Acute medicine at the hospital front door: A Singapore health system priority
abstract: Hospital crowding in Singapore is often experienced at the emergency department front door, but for many older and medically complex adults, it may signal vulnerabilities across the early acute care pathway. Delayed senior decision-making, fragmented handover between emergency and inpatient teams, limited alternatives to admission, and weak transitions back to community care create risks to safety, patient experience, and bed capacity. Acute medicine offers a practical way to redesign this interval by concentrating diagnostic breadth, senior review, rapid diagnostics, multidisciplinary assessment, and disposition planning during the first 48–72 hours of undifferentiated acute medical illness. This commentary argues that the policy value of acute medicine in Singapore lies not in replicating a UK specialty model but in defining how its core functions can complement existing medical and emergency care pathways. It examines progress in Singapore, distinguishes acute medicine from adjacent models of care, and identifies the workforce, governance, and measurement requirements for further development.

abstract: Transformer models have demonstrated strong performance across a variety of reasoning tasks. However, understanding how these models perform arithmetic reasoning remains an open challenge. This study focuses on investigating the factors that influence arithmetic performance and the interpretability of character-level transformer models. These models were trained on increasingly complex tasks including one-digit arithmetic, two-digit arithmetic, and natural language prompts containing arithmetic expressions embedded within them. Model performance was evaluated by examining the effects of altering training iterations, dataset size, and model configurations. In order to account for training variability, representative two-digit configurations were trained using five independent random seeds and evaluated using a standardized prompt-level procedure. In order to perform the interpretability analysis, Integrated Gradients was utilized to calculate token-level attribution for each input token across zero embedding and mean embedding baselines. title: Case Report: Subdural evacuating port system for the management of acute on-chronic subdural hemorrhage
abstract: Background: Traumatic subdural hematomas (SDHs) carry high morbidity and mortality without timely decompression, posing major challenges in settings lacking immediate neurosurgical support. Case Description: A 75-year-old man with hypertension and hyperlipidemia on aspirin fell from a 3-foot ladder sustaining brief loss of consciousness. He presented with amnesia, headache, and nausea with Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) 15. Computed tomography of the head (CTH) showed subarachnoid hemorrhage and bilateral SDH with acute and chronic components (left: 9 mm, right: 7 mm). Four hours later, GCS declined to 10 (E2V3M5) with the motor examination notable for localization to pain on the right and absent response on the left. Anisocoria also developed, with a fixed, non-reactive right pupil (4.6 mm, NPi 0) and a reactive left pupil (3.2 mm, NPi 2.9). Repeat CTH demonstrated SDH expansion (left: 17mm, right: 11mm). The patient was intubated and underwent right-sided subdural evacuating port system (SEPS) drainage (674 cc cumulative output over 2 days). Follow-up CTH showed reduction of the right SDH to 5 mm and left to 14 mm. His examination improved to GCS 11T; he was extubated the next day. He subsequently underwent middle meningeal artery embolization 4 weeks later. CTH 7 months post-injury demonstrated near-complete resolution of bilateral SDHs. Conclusion: SEPS is well established for th…

title: The Cuntz–Pimsner algebra of the simplest Motzkin subproduct system is 2-subhomogeneous
abstract: The Motzkin subproduct system (SPS) is constructed from the Jones–Wenzl idempotents of the Motzkin algebras, which generalizes the Temperley–Lieb SPS. The simplest Motzkin SPS, which is not a Temperley–Lieb SPS, is constructed from a three-dimensional Hilbert space. We explicitly describe the spectrum of the corresponding Cuntz–Pimsner algebra, which remarkably admits only irreducible representations of dimensions [Formula: see text] and [Formula: see text], and can thus be viewed as a mildly quantum space. Moreover, we analyze representations of the Richard Thompson groups and of the Cuntz algebra that are associated to this spectrum.

abstract: The increasing dependence on synthetic pesticides in agriculture, public facilities, residential areas, and commercial environments has raised significant concerns regarding food safety, environmental sustainability, and human health. Although chemical pesticides have contributed substantially to agricultural productivity, their long-term impacts include pesticide residues in food, contamination of water resources, biodiversity loss, and adverse health outcomes. Organic Pest Management (OPM) has emerged as a sustainable alternative that minimizes reliance on hazardous chemicals while maintaining effective pest control. However, implementation across the United States remains fragmented due to inconsistent policies, varying institutional capacities, and limited coordination among sectors. This study explores the development of a nationally integrated Organic Pest Management System designed to improve food safety and public health outcomes across agricultural, educational, healthcare, residential, and commercial environments. Using a qualitative review of existing literature, policy frameworks, and sustainable pest management practices, the research evaluates the potential benefits, challenges, and implementation strategies associated with nationwide OPM adoption. abstract: Kegiatan pengabdian kepada masyarakat ini bertujuan memperkuat kolaborasi multipihak dalam penyediaan dan pengelolaan air bersih berkelanjutan melalui kerja sama antara PDAM Kota Jayapura, dosen UNIYAP Jayapura, masyarakat, dan pemerintah daerah di Sentani, Kabupaten Jayapura. Metode yang digunakan adalah pendekatan partisipatif yang meliputi identifikasi masalah, sosialisasi, edukasi pengelolaan serta konservasi air, diskusi bersama masyarakat, dan penguatan koordinasi antara penyedia layanan dengan pengguna. Permasalahan utama yang ditemukan mencakup keterbatasan akses air bersih, ketidakstabilan kontinuitas layanan, pemeliharaan fasilitas yang belum optimal, serta rendahnya partisipasi masyarakat dalam mendukung keberlanjutan layanan. Kondisi tersebut menunjukkan bahwa pengelolaan air bersih tidak cukup berfokus pada pembangunan infrastruktur, tetapi juga memerlukan penguatan komunikasi, koordinasi, dan sinergi antarpemangku kepentingan. Hasil kegiatan menegaskan pentingnya kolaborasi berkelanjutan antara UNIYAP, PDAM Kota Jayapura, pemerintah daerah, dan masyarakat guna menjaga sumber daya air serta meningkatkan kualitas layanan. Pendekatan ini diharapkan menjadi model pengelolaan air bersih yang adaptif, inklusif, partisipatif, dan berkelanjutan bagi Jayapura.

title: What Matters for Lightweight Multi-Label Chest X-Ray Classification? A Controlled Multi-Seed Study of Attention, Loss, Width and Resolution
abstract: Attention modules and imbalance-aware losses are often credited with gains in multi-label chest X-ray classification, but their effects are seldom separated from training length, model width, input resolution and seed-to-seed variation. We integrate three existing components, squeeze-and-excitation (SE) channel attention, the class-specific residual attention (CSRA) classifier and the asymmetric loss (ASL), into a lightweight residual network (SECA-Net) and evaluate them on the 14-label ChestMNIST benchmark in 87 training runs. A 2×2×2 factorial ablation with five seeds, a loss study, a width study, three lightweight reference models and a 64- and 128-pixel resolution study were all trained to convergence under one protocol. None of the three components changed macro-AUROC significantly (seed-blocked three-way ANOVA: SE p = 0.84, CSRA p = 0.29, ASL p = 0.86), and their combination did not significantly beat the baseline at width 64 (+0.0018, p = 0.085) or at 64 and 128 pixels. In contrast, input resolution raised macro-AUROC from 0.789 at 28 pixels to 0.815 at 128 pixels with the same 0.70 M-parameter network, training to convergence instead of eight epochs added 0.014, and widening the network from 16 to 64 base channels added 0.007. title: DESIGN THINKING AS A TOOL FOR DEVELOPING STUDENTS’ THINKING SKILLS
abstract: The article examines design thinking as a pedagogical tool for developing students’ thinking and problem-solving skills. The aim of the paper is to analyze the educational potential of the stages of design thinking—empathy, problem definition, idea generation, prototyping, and testing. Based on examples from different subject areas, particularly in the contexts of teaching mathematics, history, and natural sciences, it is demonstrated that this approach helps students understand problems, generate alternative solutions, put their own ideas into practice, and evaluate and improve the results obtained. The paper demonstrates that design thinking contributes to the development of students’ critical, creative, analytical, and problem-solving skills.

title: Utilizing silica-enriched filter cake as a cement replacement and rheology modifier in 3D-printable mortar containing coffee husk and palm leaf ashes
abstract: Abstract This study evaluates a novel combination of coffee husk ash (CHA), palm leaf ash (PLA), and silica-enriched filter cake (SEFC) for extrusion-based 3D concrete printing (3DCP), where CHA and PLA serve as waste-derived supplementary cementitious materials (SCMs) and SEFC functions both SCM and as a rheology-modifying additive to enhance fresh and hardened performance. Physicochemical characterization revealed high silica contents in SEFC (80.6%), CHA (39.3%), and PLA (42.4%), with elevated specific surface areas compared to ordinary Portland cement (OPC), indicating potential pozzolanic characteristics. X-ray diffraction analysis confirmed the presence of amorphous phases favorable for hydration reactions. SEFC significantly improved rheological behavior, enhancing extrudability, shape retention, and buildability, enabling stable layer-by-layer printing. Fresh-state results indicated controlled workability loss and suitable setting behavior for layer-by-layer deposition. In the hardened state, SEFC-modified mortar (optimized mix) exhibited compressive strength improvements of 19.3% and 12.8% at 7 and 28 days, respectively, compared to the CHA–PLA reference mixture (M11). Microstructural analysis showed a denser matrix with reduced porosity and increased calcium silicate hydrate formation, explaining the improved mechanical performance. title: Charity Property Assets in Australia: A Case for Reform?
abstract: Drawing on a corporate real estate management (CREM) perspective, this paper examines the property holdings of two long-established Australian charities to explore how real estate assets are governed, managed, and reported. The study investigates how charities account for property wealth, address associated risks and liabilities, and disclose information relevant to organisational accountability. Findings indicate that current reporting frameworks and the limited application of CREM principles obscure the scale, value, and performance of charitable property portfolios. Consequently, stakeholders may be unable to fully assess organisational financial health or long-term sustainability. The paper argues for stronger asset management practices, asset registers, and enhanced reporting frameworks that provide a more complete understanding of charities’ financial position and property-related risks.

title: Multiamino Polydiacetylene-Mediated Interfacial Engineering of Boron Nitride Nanosheet/Polyimide Composites for Low-Dielectric Thermal Management
abstract: Abstract The rapid advancement of high-frequency and highly integrated semiconductor devices urgently calls for dielectric materials that combine high thermal conductivity, low dielectric constant, and excellent thermal stability. Herein, multiamino polydiacetylene-functionalized boron nitride nanosheets (BNNS@MAPDA) have been incorporated into a MAPDA-containing polyimide matrix to improve filler–matrix interfacial coupling. The functionalized nanosheets exhibit high aspect ratios, few lattice defects, high yields, and excellent dispersion in the PI-MAPDA matrix. At a filler loading of only 7.5 wt %, the PI‑MAPDA/BNNS@MAPDA‑7.5 composite film achieves an in‑plane thermal conductivity of 1.67 W m–1 K–1, representing a 422% enhancement over pristine PI‑MAPDA. Benefiting from the ultralow polarizability of fluorinated groups and the strengthened interfacial coupling, the nanocomposite simultaneously maintains a low dielectric constant of 2.20 and a low dielectric loss tangent (tanδ) of 0.0066 at 1 MHz, alongside a volume resistivity of 9.7 × 1011 Ω cm. The density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that MAPDA functionalization enhances interfacial affinity and energy transfer, while molecular dynamics (MD) simulations elucidate its influence on thermal conductivity and dielectric properties. Inter-Provincial Disparities in Students’ ICT Use in Indonesia: Insights for Digital Education Management
abstract: Digital transformation in education requires equitable student access to information and communication technology (ICT), yet conditions differ between regions. This study analysed inter-provincial disparity in ICT use among students in Indonesia and discussed its potential implications for digital education management. It was a descriptive analysis of secondary, aggregate provincial statistics from the 2025 Education Statistics, based on the March 2025 National Socio-Economic Survey (Susenas). Three indicators for students aged 5–23 years were examined: use of mobile phones, computers or laptops, and the internet. Descriptive statistics comprised the mean across provinces, standard deviation, minimum, maximum, and range. Disparity was largest for internet use (range 84.18 percentage points; standard deviation 16.32), followed by mobile phone use (76.48; 14.76) and computer or laptop use (35.51; 6.98). Mobile phone and internet data covered 38 provinces, whereas computer or laptop data covered 37 because no value was available for Papua Pegunungan. DI Yogyakarta ranked highest on all three indicators, and the lowest values were concentrated in the Papua region, suggesting that disparities cluster in specific regions. Computer or laptop use was low in nearly every province and showed the greatest relative dispersion. Interpreted through the UNESCO Six Pillars for the Digital Tran…

title: Digital Technology Adoption and Accounting Literacy in Financial Recording Practices: A Qualitative Case Study of a Rural Food Micro Small Medium Enterprise (MSME) in Negeri Sembilan, Malaysia
abstract: Financial recording is essential for improving the sustainability and financial management of micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs). Previous studies have mainly focused on MSMEs that either lack financial records or adopt digital bookkeeping through formal training, while limited attention has been given to businesses that independently adopt digital recording technologies despite having limited accounting literacy. This study addresses this gap by examining the financial recording practices of 48 Salai Smoke House, a rural smoked-food MSME in Kampung Terachi, Kuala Pilah, Negeri Sembilan, Malaysia. Using a descriptive qualitative case study, data were collected through semi-structured interviews with the business owner and analysed thematically. The findings show that the enterprise uses a Point-of-Sale (POS) system as its primary recording tool, supported by manual verification of cash, QR (MAE/DuitNow), and bank transfer transactions, while maintaining a separate business bank account. Despite this level of digital technology adoption, financial records are not prepared within a structured accounting framework, and the owner has not received formal accounting or financial management training. These findings reveal a critical implementation gap between technology adoption and accounting literacy, indicating that digital tools alone are insufficient to strengthen finan…

title: Global Mental Wealth: A Multidimensional Analysis of Social, Financial, and Emotional Well-Being in 92 Countries
abstract: Abstract Governments and organizations increasingly endorse the importance of mental health in all forms of policy, though emphasis in measurement still remains on indicators such as GDP, depression, and other common disorders. In this study of 92 countries ( n = 53,799), we assess the mental health of individuals around the world alongside measures of financial and social well-being. Findings include a trend of languishing mental health across many groups, particularly among younger adults and within higher-income countries. While positive trends are observed for education and income, a number of concerning trends also emerge, particularly the poor results for young adults and generally moderate results for employed individuals. In sum, we find an alarming but perhaps unsurprisingly low level of positive mental health in a substantial number of countries, but also identify specific economic, social, and other indicators that policymakers could target in improving the well-being of the populations they serve.

title: Efficacy of permethrin/imidacloprid (Advantix®) in preventing Leishmania infantum transmission in naturally exposed dogs in Greece
abstract: Abstract Background Canine leishmaniosis (CanL) by Leishmania infantum is a potentially fatal sand fly-borne zoonosis. Transmission can be reduced by regular use of repellent insecticides. This 12-month study, conducted in a highly endemic CanL area, assessed the efficacy of a repeated spot-on application of imidacloprid 10%/permethrin 50% (Advantix ® , Elanco) to prevent L. infantum transmission in dogs naturally challenged by sand flies versus a negative control. Methods Forty purpose-bred Beagle dogs were allocated to two groups. Group 1 was treated four-weekly with Advantix ® , while group 2 was left untreated. This study was performed in an open-air kennel, consisting of two phases: Phase 1 (Day 0–224; April–November [sand fly season]) allowed natural Leishmania transmission; Phase 2 (Day 225–341; November–March [post sand fly season with insect-proof environment and licensed preventative treatment]) enabled time for seroconversion and disease development. Clinical examinations plus scoring, SNAP serology, and PCR (conjunctival swabs) were performed four-weekly. IFAT, haematology, blood biochemistry, and urinalysis were performed at study start and end. Bone marrow PCR was performed at study end. Sand fly activity was recorded every four weeks by trapping. title: “I don’t have the right to decide by myself, as it is his child too.” Exploring the process of abortion decision-making among women in Nepal
abstract: Abstract Background In Nepal, the legalization and expansion of safe abortion services have significantly reduced severe abortion-related complications. However, despite the availability of safe abortion care, many individuals face challenges in accessing these services. This study aims to explore the complexities of abortion decision-making among women seeking abortion care in Nepal, focusing on the socio-cultural, economic, and interpersonal dynamics that influence their decisions. Methods As part of a longitudinal cohort study, we conducted 43 in-depth interviews with women accessing abortion services in 2022. Among these women, 19 received abortion services, while 24 were denied abortions and continued their pregnancies. Using the socio-ecological model (SEM) as the analytical framework, we employed thematic analysis to examine how individual characteristics, interpersonal relationship, community norms and health system factors influenced abortion decision-making. Results Our findings reveal a complex interplay of factors, including individual health concerns, financial limitations, partner influence, family dynamics, and societal norms, such as gender preference for sons that influence abortion decision-making. Among these, societal norms and partner influence had the most significant impact while making decisions. Conclusion This study underscores the urgent need for targ…

abstract: شهد القطاع المالي السعودي تحولًا رقميًا متسارعًا مدفوعًا بمستهدفات رؤية السعودية 2030، مما أسهم في إعادة تشكيل نماذج تقديم الخدمات المالية وتطوير مبيعاتها من خلال توظيف تقنيات التحول الرقمي، والتقنية المالية (FinTech)، والذكاء الاصطناعي. تهدف هذه الدراسة إلى تقديم مراجعة نظرية تحليلية للأدبيات المنشورة خلال الفترة (2020–2026) حول تطوير مبيعات الخدمات المالية في ظل التحول الرقمي، مع التركيز على دور الشفافية في بناء ثقة العملاء في القطاع المالي السعودي، والكشف عن أبرز العوامل المؤثرة في هذه العلاقة والفجوات المعرفية التي ما تزال قائمة في الأدبيات. وتعتمد الدراسة المنهج النظري التحليلي القائم على مراجعة نقدية للأدبيات العلمية والدراسات المحكمة والوثائق والتقارير الرسمية ذات الصلة، التي جرى اختيارها من قواعد البيانات الأكاديمية والمصادر المؤسسية الموثوقة وفق معايير محددة تشمل الصلة بموضوع الدراسة، وحداثة النشر، والجودة المنهجية، بما يضمن التمييز بين الأدلة العلمية والوثائق التنظيمية عند تفسير النتائج واستخلاص الاستنتاجات. وشملت المراجعة النهائية (17) دراسة ومصدرًا علميًا وتنظيميًا ذا صلة، من بينها (8) دراسة تناولت السياق السعودي بصورة مباشرة. وأظهر التحليل أن عددًا محدودًا من الدراسات تناول بصورة تكاملية العلاقة بين التحول الرقمي والشفافية وثقة العملاء وتطوير مبيعات الخدمات المالية. وتشير نتائج التحليل إلى أن التحول الرقمي يسهم في تطوير مبيعات الخدمات المالية من خلال تحسين سهولة الوصول إلى الخدمات، ورفع كفاءة العمليات، وتطوير تجربة العميل، وإتاحة قنوات جديدة للتواصل وتقديم المنتجات…

ZOONOTIC DISEASE TRANSMISSION BETWEEN BABOONS AND HUMANS IN AL-BAHA: A CAPUTO–FABRIZIO FRACTAL–FRACTIONAL ORDER MODELING STUDY
abstract: Baboons in Saudi Arabia’s Al-Baha province frequently interact with people, creating cross-species transmission settings that classical, integer-order epidemic models cannot reproduce. By utilizing the Caputo–Fabrizio fractional operator, we are able to encode history effects via a nonsingular kernel over two hosts with nonlocal memory. Memory strength determines outbreak magnitude, decay rates, and oscillatory patterns across a range of fractional indices. It can precipitate a variety of complex and chaotic transients absent from the integer-order limit. Mathematically, we establish Hyers–Ulam stability for the proposed dynamics, ensuring solution robustness under small perturbations and modeling noise. The resulting methodology offers a principled tool for designing public-health actions and wildlife management policies in regions with sustained human–wildlife interfaces.

title: Foreign direct investment, trade openness, and financial development as drivers of economic growth: evidence from Sri Lanka
abstract: Purpose This study examines the short- and long-run relationships between foreign direct investment (FDI), trade openness, financial development, and economic growth (GDP) in Sri Lanka. It aims to clarify how these variables interact to inform sustainable growth policies. Design/methodology/approach The study employs annual time series data for Sri Lanka spanning 1970–2024. The variables include GDP (annual growth rate of real GDP), FDI (net inflows in current US$ million), Trade Openness (total trade as a percentage of GDP), and Financial Development (domestic credit to the private sector as a percentage of GDP). The study applies the Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) bounds testing approach and Error Correction Model (ECM) to analyze both short-run dynamics and long-run equilibrium relationships. The optimal model, selected by the Akaike Information Criterion, is ARDL (1, 4, 0, 0). Findings Results confirm a long-run cointegrating relationship among the variables. In the long run, FDI, trade openness, and financial development are statistically insignificant, while in the short run, FDI has a strong positive effect on GDP. Practical implications FDI stimulates short-term growth, but long-run development requires structural reforms, institutional strengthening, and improved financial market efficiency. title: Modeling corporate financial distress using explainable machine learning: evidence from macro-financial panel data
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine whether firm-level market indicators and lagged macroeconomic information can be integrated within an explainable predictive framework for corporate financial distress, with particular attention to temporal dynamics, model performance and interpretability. Design/methodology/approach This study uses an unbalanced panel of 15,664 firm-month observations from 99 large-cap US listed equity series covering July 2012–September 2025. Regularized logistic regression, Random Forest, HistGradientBoosting and XGBoost are evaluated using chronological training, validation and held-out testing. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) provide model interpretability, while alternative macroeconomic lag structures, calibration diagnostics and robustness checks assess the stability of the predictive evidence. Findings Regularized logistic regression records the strongest full-test point estimates (AUC = 0.7886; average precision = 0.3085), while XGBoost is the strongest nonlinear benchmark (AUC = 0.7314; average precision = 0.2049). However, model rankings vary across evaluation periods. The combined one-, three- and six-month lag specification performs best, indicating that predictive macroeconomic information is distributed across multiple horizons. title: Davlat moliyaviy nazorati jarayonlarini sun'iy intellekt yordamida riskka yo'naltirilgan raqamli nazorat modeli asosida takomillashtirish
abstract: В статье исследованы теоретико-методологические и институциональные аспекты трансформации государственного финансового контроля и внутреннего аудита на основе искусственного интеллекта. Задачи цифровизации внутреннего аудита, определенные в Узбекистане в 2026 году, сопоставлены с материалами OECD, IMF, Всемирного банка, IIA и современными научными исследованиями. Показано, что наряду с техническими возможностями ключевое значение имеют качество данных, объяснимость, человеческий контроль, алгоритмическая предвзятость, конфиденциальность и компетенции аудиторов. Предложена модель «AI-Risk Control», объединяющая интеграцию данных, выявление аномалий, многокритериальный риск-скоринг, приоритизацию объектов контроля и верификацию аудитором. title: The impact of artificial intelligence and data science on construction and architectural management systems: the mediating role of the technological environment
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) and data science (DS) capabilities on the performance of construction and architectural management systems (CAMS), with technological environment (TE) operating as a mediating variable. Design/methodology/approach A structured questionnaire survey was administered to professionals engaged in construction-related intelligent systems and software development activities in China. A total of 285 usable responses were retained for analysis. The data were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) to test the hypothesised relationships among AI, DS, TE and CAMS performance. Findings The empirical results indicate that both AI and DS capabilities have positive and statistically significant effects on CAMS performance. The TE partially mediated these relationships, indicating that well-developed digital infrastructure, interoperability and data governance mechanisms significantly enhance the performance outcomes of AI- and DS-enabled CAMS. Practical implications The findings highlight the importance of strengthening technological readiness within construction and architectural management organisations. Firms should prioritise investments in interoperable TE infrastructure, integrated DS platforms and workforce capability development to fully realise the operational efficiency…

title: Impact of Digital Payments on the Financial Performance of Commercial Banks in Pakistan: An Empirical Investigation
abstract: This study explores the effect of the adoption of electronic payment on the financial performance of top 10 commercial banks during 2014–2024 in Pakistan. The analysis is performed using a quantitative research approach and the panel data econometric techniques are used to compare three digital banking indicators (mobile banking registered users, internet banking registered users and Point-of-Sale (POS) terminals with two profitability measures Return on Assets (ROA) and Return on Equity (ROE). Fixed Effects (FE) and Random Effects (RE) are used to estimate contemporaneous and 1-year lagged models. The estimates made at the time suggest digital payments have no immediate statistically significant impact on bank profitability, as the initial costs of technology investment, regulatory compliance and customer uptake have yet to be factored in. The lagged models show a very strong positive relationship (p<0.01), which implies that the financial returns from the digitalization show up after the implementation time. The lagged FE model accounts for 11.38% of ROA variation and 12.87% of ROE variation with the most influential positive effect of POS terminal expansion. These results prove that long-term investments in digital payment systems are beneficial to the banks' performance and emphasize the need for long-term strategic planning and enabling regulatory frameworks.

abstract: This article presents an analysis of the current state of financial stability indicators of commercial banks in the Republic of Uzbekistan. It examines the CAMELS rating system used in international banking practice and analyzes the key performance indicators of banks with and without state participation, including the dynamics of their assets, loans, deposits, and capital. In addition, the article analyzes the dynamics of the main financial stability indicators of the banking system in 2024, including capital adequacy, asset quality, return on assets and capital, liquidity, and a number of other indicators. The article also provides conclusions and proposals aimed at ensuring the financial stability of commercial banks by optimizing their interaction in the financial sector and improving the formation of decentralized financial resources

title: Long-term electricity load forecasting model based on multi-period and multi-scale analysis
abstract: Existing long-term power load forecasting models face significant challenges due to the complexity of non-stationary electricity data, inadequate information representation, and suboptimal prediction accuracy. To address these issues, this study introduces PowerNet, a novel forecasting framework based on a multi-period and multi-scale approach. PowerNet first employs Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) to perform multi-period analysis, transforming one-dimensional time series data into two-dimensional (2D) tensors to capture latent periodic patterns. A multi-scale information representation module is then implemented using computer vision-inspired techniques, including Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Gated Recurrent Units (GRU), and non-local attention mechanisms to extract robust features from these tensors. Finally, a fully connected layer performs feature reconstruction, while residual connections facilitate multi-step load forecasting. PowerNet was evaluated against state-of-the-art models such as Informer, LogTrans, and ETSformer across two public electricity datasets and one weather dataset. At prediction horizons of 96, 192, 336, and 720 time steps, experimental results demonstrate that PowerNet achieves competitive or superior accuracy on the evaluated datasets. Notably, compared with Autoformer, PowerNet reduces the Mean Absolute Error (MAE) by 18.77% to 37.41% and the M…

title: EARLY WARNING SYSTEMS FOR FORECASTING ECONOMIC CRISES: AN APPLICATION TO THE TURKISH ECONOMY
abstract: The history of the global economy has witnessed numerous structural and cyclical crises up to the present day. In particular, the frequency of financial turmoil since the 1990s has intensified debates regarding the predictability of these phenomena and the theoretical models used to explain them. While early studies focused on critical threshold values to determine the limits of financial fragility, current literature has turned to advanced econometric analysis methods aimed at identifying leading indicators. In this context, empirical models known as “early warning systems” have been designed to detect potential shocks in advance. Although making predictions about the future is extremely difficult when considering past crisis dynamics and macroeconomic variables, it is still possible. As important forecasting tools, these systems lay the groundwork for preventing major economic disruptions and enabling policymakers to make proactive decisions. This study focuses on early signal mechanisms by identifying leading indicators related to past and potential future crisis waves in the Turkish economy. In this context, crisis probabilities were analyzed using a Probit model based on monthly data from January 2006 to May 2022. The financial stress index, constructed to identify crisis periods, was included in the model as the dependent variable. The findings indicate that the CPI-based…

title: Food Security at What Cost? An Economic and Fiscal Analysis of the Php 20 Rice Price Policy in the Philippines
abstract: The evaluation assesses the economic sustainability, social implications, and fiscal impact of the Philippine government's goal to establish a universal retail price of Php 20 per kilogram for rice, which serves as a vital food security measure and a powerful political icon. The research evaluates this extensive policy through analyses of official statistics, academic studies, and industry reports. The research data shows that the Php 20/kg target price remains far from the actual market prices, which reached more than Php 40/kg during the first months of 2025. The analysis shows that the raw material cost of palay (unmilled rice) at the farmgate already reaches or exceeds the Php 20 target when converted to its milled rice equivalent before adding milling and logistics expenses and retail margins. The government would need to provide annual subsidies of between Php 178 billion and Php 329 billion to implement a universal price ceiling, which would exceed the Department of Agriculture's total budget. The research shows that farmer profitability and livelihood sustainability are under severe threat, which could lead to decreased production and increased import dependence. The policy would provide immediate benefits to consumers, yet it would generate substantial market disruptions, leading to stockpiling, decreased private-sector investment, and permanent harm to agricultural va…

title: Application of tree-based machine learning models for winter-spring visibility forecasting at Noi Bai International Airport: A combined regression and classification approach
abstract: This study aims to develop and evaluate a machine learning (ML)-based visibility forecasting method for the winter-spring months (January, February, and March) at Noi Bai International Airport, Vietnam. We developed tree-based machine learning models, including Decision Tree (DT), Random Forest (RF), and XGBoost (XGB), using surface meteorological variables and Global Forecast System (GFS) data to forecast visibility at 1-, 2-, and 3-hour lead times. The results indicate that many predictors did not improve forecasting performance. In contrast, DT models with just 3–5 key predictors (selected via RFECV and SHAP) achieved optimal results, particularly in detecting low- and rare-visibility events. The most influential predictors included lagged visibility, time of day, and the vertical gradient of relative humidity within the near-surface and atmospheric boundary layers. The optimal DT models consistently achieved skill scores for the Probability of Detection (POD) of low- and rare-visibility classes ranging from +10% to +35% compared to the persistence forecast, while operating stably without evidence of overfitting.

title: Optimal Scheduling Strategy for Port Virtual Power Plant Based on DQN Algorithm: Considering the Dual Impact of Electricity–Carbon Trading
abstract: In order to address the challenge of cooperative optimization of port virtual power plants (VPPs) participating in both electricity and carbon trading markets, this paper proposes a two-stage day-ahead–intraday optimal scheduling strategy using the deep Q -network (DQN) algorithm strategy, which can achieve both economic and environmental benefits for the port. First, a physical model of a port VPP was constructed in which the wind and photovoltaic (PV) power, energy storage systems (ESS), and multiple types of loads are integrated. Second, a detailed carbon accounting model was developed to refine current carbon accounting methods and quantify in detail the carbon emissions from the port’s energy system, i.e., gas-fired power generation, grid electricity purchases, and other sources. Based on this, a two-stage scheduling framework is proposed. During the day-ahead stage, the DQN algorithm is employed to derive the optimal day-ahead electricity sales declaration curve. In the intraday stage, according to real-time deviations, the DQN algorithm is reapplied to dynamically adjust the charging and discharging power of energy storage and the output of gas-fired units, while incorporating an ε -greedy strategy to address uncertainties. Finally, the effectiveness of the developed method was verified with a comprehensive set of case studies. Experimental results show that the develope…

title: Optical soliton perturbation, phase portrait and sensitivity analysis in birefringent fibers with the stochastic complex Ginzburg–Landau equation having cubic–quintic–septic–nonic nonlinearities
abstract: Optical soliton solutions, chaotic behaviors and bifurcation analysis of the perturbed complex Ginzburg–Landau equation having non-Kerr law media with the effect of multiplicative white noise in birefringent fibers are researched, for the first time, in this study. Perturbation terms of the Hamiltonian type and cubic–quintic–septic–nonic form of self-phase modulation are taken into consideration. Two integration schemes, namely the extended trial function algorithm and the extended [Formula: see text]-expansion technique are applied to reveal a variety of wave profiles such as bright, dark and singular soliton solutions, rational waves and periodic solutions to the governing equation. Existence criteria of the soliton solutions are also provided. In addition 2D, 3D and contour figures are presented to illustrate dynamic behavior of the solutions. Moreover, by virtue of the traveling wave hypothesis, the model is turned into a two-dimensional dynamical system. Then, the behaviors of this system and its periodic disturbance system are analyzed in detail utilizing methods such as equilibrium point analysis, time series, phase portraits, Poincaré sections and sensitivity to initial conditions to verify the presence of deterministic chaotic behavior. Additionally, chaotic and quasi-periodic behaviors are exhibited for a range of parameter values after adding a perturbation term. The…

title: Does market participation impact profitability and per capita consumption? Evidence from lowland rice farmers in southern Ghana
abstract: Purpose This paper examines the impact of market choice(s) on profitability and per capita consumption among lowland rice farmers in southern Ghana. Design/methodology/approach Using a sample of 967 farmers, we employ the Multinomial Endogenous Switching Regression (MESR) to address self-selection and endogeneity biases, with a robustness check using the three-stage multivalued inverse probability weighted regression adjustment (3S-IPWRA). Findings The results reveal that market choice is significantly influenced by household, farm and institutional factors, including age, gender, access to agricultural extension and proximity to markets. Our results indicate that farmers who sell in both community and regional markets achieve the highest profitability (ATT = USD 362.1 per acre), followed by those selling only in district markets (USD 47.56 per acre over community markets). Additionally, the market choice with the highest profitability also exhibits the highest per capita consumption. Research limitations/implications The paper focused on lowland rice farmers which may limit the generalizability of findings to other crops. Future studies should therefore analyse the impact of market choice(s) on profitability and per capita consumption among other crop farmers. Originality/value Most of the related literature fails to examine the possible nexus between market choice, profitabil…

title: AI-Based Decision Support for Asset Allocation Management as a Component of Business Models under Market Uncertainty
abstract: Objectives The aim of the study was to identify and evaluate the possibilities of using artificial intelligence assistants to support decision-making processes related to asset allocation, treated as an important component of the business model of an enterprise operating under conditions of market uncertainty. Material and methods The study was conducted on the example of three companies from the construction sector listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange: Budimex S.A., Polimex Mostostal S.A., and Mirbud S.A. The analysis covered the years 2020–2024 and was based on two groups of data: annual fundamental indicators and daily closing stock prices. In the fundamental part, return on equity, debt ratio, asset utilization ratio, and the Altman discriminant model were used to construct a synthetic fundamental index. In the market part, daily logarithmic rates of return and the Sharpe ratio were calculated. Results The results indicate that AI assistants can effectively support the analytical process by accelerating calculations and increasing the repeatability of the procedure. At the same time, differences in model performance were observed, indicating the risk of errors in data interpretation. Conclusions The study demonstrates that AI can be a useful tool supporting asset allocation management; however, its effectiveness depends on data quality, the precision of the analytical proced…

title: Factors influencing the development of information modeling technology market in urban planning: Expert-analytical assessment of the limits of the Laissez-Faire model
abstract: Subject. Organizational, economic, and institutional factors in the development of the market for information modelling technologies (IMT) in urban development activities. Objectives. To carry out an expert‑analytical assessment of the factors driving the IMT market development and to define the applicability limits of the laissez‑faire model. Methods. The analysis involved regulatory documents of the Russian Federation, official materials from DOM.RF, the Ministry of Construction of Russia, the European Commission / EU BIM Task Group, and buildingSMART International. A scoring matrix for factor validation was applied. The evaluation criteria are explicitly defined: the scores reflect the type and number of supporting sources rather than the magnitude of the economic effect. The reproducibility of the procedure is ensured by a fixed scale and the principle of triangulation. Results. It has been established that the spread of IMT is not determined solely by market demand for software products. The factors most robustly confirmed are regulatory obligation, data standardization, staffing availability, implementation cost, the competencies of clients and developers, and the readiness of organizations to restructure their processes. International BIM mandates and Russia’s transition to mandatory use of IMT confirm the institutional nature of the market. Conclusions and Relevance. Th…

title: Knowing the law, trusting the state: legal literacy and investor confidence in Vietnam’s digital asset market
abstract: Purpose Despite the rapid expansion of cryptocurrencies and other digital assets, Vietnam’s young digital asset market has witnessed a lack of robust regulatory frameworks. This study examines how legal knowledge, trading behavior and prior risk experience shape legal risk exposure and trust in government oversight. Design/methodology/approach Structural equation modeling was carried out on a sample of 224 investors to analyze the relationships between legal knowledge, trading frequency, prior risk experience, legal risk exposure, perceived legal risk and trust in government regulation. Findings Greater legal knowledge dampens exposure to legal risks while strongly strengthening perceived legal risks. Trust in government regulation is significantly enhanced by both perceived and actual legal risks. High trading frequency increases exposure to legal risk, while prior negative experiences weaken the relationship between risk exposure and trust in government oversight. Practical implications The paper provides practical insights for lawmakers when building Vietnam’s new digital asset regulatory frameworks, emphasizing the need for holistic investor education, transparent regulations and robust consumer protection mechanisms. Originality/value The study offers empirical evidence from an emerging digital asset market, highlighting how legal knowledge and risk experiences jointly sha…
venue: Asian Journal of Economics and Banking

title: Tariff regulation in the industrial railway services market: Experience of Russian regions
abstract: Subject. Ensuring cargo transportation, the role of Russian regions in developing the tariff regulation system in the industrial railway transport market. Objectives. Identification, systematization, and analysis of tariff regulation models used in the industrial railway transport services market. Methods. Typologization, content analysis. Results. Four models of tariff regulation used in the industrial railway transport market have been identified. The declarative model, implemented in the Perm region, helps reduce the administrative burden on market participants while maintaining a mechanism to prevent abuse. Conclusions. The lack of unified approaches to defining the scope of services and choosing units of measurement leads to significant price differences and conceptual confusion. It's necessary to develop federal methodological guidelines to harmonize the terminology and approaches to pricing, while still allowing regions to keep their independence in choosing models for regulating the industrial railway transport service market.

title: Sanitizing the stain: a critical integrative review of sportswashing discourse
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to develop a marketing-oriented understanding of sportswashing by synthesizing its burgeoning, fragmented and cross-disciplinary scholarship through Mary Douglas’s anthropology of purity and pollution, explaining how sportswashing operates as a symbolic purification process. Design/methodology/approach This research uses a critical integrative review of 45 peer-reviewed articles, identified through systematic searches of major academic databases. After two-stage screening, the corpus was analyzed qualitatively from an interpretive stance, using thematic synthesis followed by abductive theorization. Findings This study first maps the sportswashing ecosystem − stains, actors, motivations, mechanisms, phases and outcomes − revealing complexity and tensions pervading the literature. Building on this synthesis, it identifies five cleansing logics through which sportswashing operates as a symbolic purification process: separation, dilution, displacement, containment and sanctification. Each logic illuminates how sportswashing operates as a contest over cultural classification through association without explicit claims. Research limitations/implications This synthesis advances a research agenda for interpretive marketing and consumer research, highlighting what qualitative inquiry could reveal about sportswashing across consumer resistance, platformization of …
