title: Transformation of exchange rate formation mechanisms and the infrastructure of the Russian currency market under the influence of external restrictions (2022–2025)
abstract: Subject. The foreign exchange market under external restrictions in 2022–2025. Objectives. To quantitatively assess the scale of price anomalies manifested in heightened volatility, discrepancies between various exchange rate indicators, and changes in the cost of foreign exchange funding, as well as to identify the consequences of sanctions pressure for foreign exchange risk management practices. Methods. Statistical time‑series analysis methods were applied: calculation of standard deviation, spreads between various exchange rate indicators (the USD/RUB cross‑rate via CNY/RUB and USD/CNY, the OTC market indicator NTPro, the “perpetual” futures contract USDRUBF, and the official exchange rate of the Bank of Russia), and comparative analysis of the cost of CNY funding against the benchmark lending rate of the People’s Bank of China. Data sources included information from the Bank of Russia, the Moscow Exchange, NTPro, and others. Results. Several stages of market transformation were identified. It was shown that after the suspension of exchange trading in USD and EUR, spreads between alternative indicators reached a peak of 10% and subsequently acquired a systemic character. Periods of backwardation in currency futures on the derivatives market were recorded, indicating local liquidity shortages. Additionally, periods of sustained deviation of RUSFARCNY from the global benchmar…

title: A graph-augmented dual-task forecasting framework using GAT-XGBoost for global ICT goods trade and export market opportunity identification
abstract: Introduction Identifying promising export destinations requires considering both the likelihood of establishing a bilateral trade relationship and the potential trade scale once that relationship is established. Methods This study develops a graph-augmented dual-task forecasting framework for global information and communication technology (ICT) goods trade using GAT-XGBoost. The framework integrates BACI bilateral ICT goods trade data under the HS 2012 classification for 2012–2024 with country characteristics, gravity variables, historical trade information, and network features. A strict chronological design uses 2014–2021 for training, 2022 for validation, and 2023–2024 for out-of-period testing. Results On the 2024 test set, the framework achieves an AUC of 0.9631 and an Average Precision of 0.9394 for trade-link prediction, while conditional log-flow prediction achieves an RMSE of 1.7711 and an R 2 of 0.8344. Ablation results indicate that historical bilateral trade provides the dominant predictive signal, while observed network measures and graph-derived representations contribute complementary information. Discussion By combining predicted trade-link probabilities with conditional trade magnitudes, the framework produces exporter-specific destination rankings and opportunity classifications. The resulting measures support systematic screening of potential ICT export mark…

title: Advancing value creation in B2B market research – a human–AI collaboration framework for large language model
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how prompt design influences the quality of large language model (LLM)-generated business-to-business (B2B) market research outputs. It also proposes a switch-point governance mechanism for converting LLM-generated drafts into decision-ready market intelligence artefacts. Design/methodology/approach The study uses an exploratory pilot evaluation of three market-facing LLM-based tools: ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity AI. The tools are compared across three benchmark B2B market research tasks and three prompt types: basic, context-augmented and role-specific. In total, 81 outputs were generated. A role-specific benchmark subset of 27 outputs was then assessed using automated metrics and blinded human ratings. The automated metrics included relevance through cosine similarity, reference overlap through ROUGE-F1, cross-run semantic stability, latency, token length and readability through Flesch Reading Ease. Human evaluators rated the outputs on relevance, completeness, factuality, instruction-following and insightfulness. One-way ANOVA and non-parametric checks are reported as exploratory task-level tests, not as confirmatory evidence of model superiority. Findings Role-specific prompts produced the strongest descriptive scores in this pilot setting. Within the benchmark subset, Gemini showed the strongest observed profile, with higher average rel…

title: Market Opportunity and Strategic Development of Early Childhood Education Institutions: A Literature Review
abstract: Tinjauan literatur sistematis ini mensintesis dinamika peluang pasar dan strategi pengembangan institusi Pendidikan Anak Usia Dini (PAUD) di Indonesia, mengonfirmasi peran fundamental PAUD sebagai agen transformasi holistik yang mengoptimalkan triad kompetensi kognitif, afektif, dan sosial-emosional anak selama periode golden age (0-6 tahun), dengan efek jangka panjang terukur melalui Heckman Equation (ROI 7-13% tahunan) terhadap prestasi akademik, school readiness, dan adaptabilitas Society 5.0. Prospek sektoral yang ekspansif didorong kenaikan Angka Partisipasi Kasar (APK) 36,19% pada 2025, kebijakan PAUD Holistik-Integratif (Perpres 60/2013), serta kesadaran parental dual-earner household menciptakan market opportunity untuk inovasi layanan seperti forest school, bilingual immersion, dan edtech gamification, menghasilkan efek ekonomi multiplier melalui penciptaan lapangan kerja lokal dan penguatan social capital komunitas (parental involvement index >60%). Studi empiris terkini (Firman & Ali, 2023; Mardiyah et al., 2026) menegaskan strategi sukses berbasis glokalisasi kurikulum (narasi lokal Jawa/Papua), digital storytelling marketing (Instagram Reels CTR 4,2%), faculty upskilling (CPD 40 jam/tahun, r=0,72 dengan developmental outcomes), dan infrastruktur child-centered yang meningkatkan competitive moat di pasar hiperkompetitif (churn rate 23%). Namun, hambatan struktural s…

title: Sustainability reporting readability, stock liquidity and the role of corporate governance: evidence from an emerging market
abstract: Purpose This study investigates whether the readability of sustainability reports affects stock liquidity and how corporate governance mechanisms shape this relationship. Drawing on agency theory, we ask whether investors reward clear non-financial disclosure. By answering this in Iran – a sanctioned emerging market with concentrated ownership – we test the boundaries of Western-developed theories and offer novel evidence from an institutionally distinct context. Design/methodology/approach Our sample comprises 612 firm-year observations from the Tehran Stock Exchange over 2016–2024. We measure sustainability report readability using the Gunning Fog Index and capture stock liquidity using three proxies: the bid-ask spread, Amihud’s illiquidity ratio and the average daily transactions. We examine four governance moderators: blockholder ownership, institutional ownership, board independence and audit firm type. The analysis employs panel data models with fixed effects and Newey–West adjustments. Findings More readable sustainability reports are associated with higher stock liquidity. However, this relationship depends on governance structures. Blockholder ownership and board independence significantly amplify the positive effect of readability on liquidity. Institutional ownership does not emerge as a significant moderator, and audit firm type matters only for specific liquidity …

title: Observed Service Utilization Differences and Audiometric Profiles Among Adults With Hearing Loss in Eastern Coastal Provinces in China
The future workplace: developing the human-machine symbioscape
abstract: Purpose This paper develops the concept of the human-machine symbioscape to explain how work environments shape collaboration between humans and AI-enabled machines. Extending servicescape thinking from customer-employee encounters to hybrid human-machine work systems, the paper positions environmental design as a core antecedent of human–machine adaptive collaboration, with particular relevance for service and frontline settings where visibility, coordination, and role clarity are critical. Design/methodology/approach The paper is conceptual and theory building in nature. It synthesises insights from biological symbiosis, servicescape research, sociotechnical and sociomaterial theory, organisational sensemaking and team adaptation research to develop a deductive typology of the human-machine symbioscape as a three-tiered environmental construct, its cue categories, and its design-critical properties. The framework is further illustrated through a structured coding of relevant human-machine collaboration studies. Findings The paper conceptualises the symbioscape as a three-tier environmental architecture comprising physical–digital, socio-relational, and institutional–ecosystem conditions. Across these tiers, six cue categories shape what human and AI-enabled actors can notice, how they coordinate work, and how collaborative routines are reinforced over time. Drawing on Weick's…

title: From responsibility to reputation: how perceived corporate social responsibility shapes corporate brand image
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how perceived corporate social responsibility (PCSR) shapes corporate brand image by unpacking the psychological mechanisms and boundary conditions underlying this relationship in the telecommunications service sector. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on the Stimulus–Organism–Response framework, this study develops an integrated moderated–mediation model in which brand familiarity and brand equity function as cognitive and affective mediators respectively, and customer trust operates as a key boundary condition. Survey data from 350 customers of leading telecommunications providers in India were analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling. Findings The results show that PCSR has a non-significant direct effect on corporate brand image and indirect effects through both brand familiarity and brand equity, indicating complementary full mediation. PCSR strengthens brand familiarity by enhancing cognitive accessibility and recognition, while simultaneously increasing brand equity through value based and emotional evaluations. Customer trust significantly moderates these relationships, amplifying the branding effects of perceived CSR under high trust and weakening them when trust is low. Practical implications The findings highlight the importance of treating PCSR as a strategic, trust anchored branding capability rather th…
venue: International Journal of Quality and Service Sciences

title: Forwarding Order Management in Logistics Service Providers: The Forwarding Order as the Profit-Bearing Object in Enterprise Transportation Management
abstract: Purpose: This paper examines forwarding order management in SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) as configured for logistics service providers and tests one organizing idea: the forwarding order is the profit-bearing object of the business, meaning the document on which sell-side revenue and buy-side cost can be read together. Methodology: The study is a descriptive, design-level analysis supported by one documented deployment. It analyzed the forwarding order in SAP TM using the vendor’s application documentation, a reference text on the system, and the configuration and project records of the deployment. A feature was included if it changes what the provider charges, what the provider is charged, or when either figure becomes known. The deployment is a single case at the North America operations of a large global transportation company. Its data are two counts: new settlement disputes per week and the size of the dispute backlog. The study has no survey, sample, or human subjects. Findings: Three results emerged. First, three design elements carry margin directly: the item hierarchy, which sets chargeable weight on both sides; the stage model, which fixes when cost is recognized; and the cost pull, which sets the boundary between customer revenue and provider cost. Second, buy-side cost reaches the forwarding order by distribution from execution documents, so margin per ord…

title: Establishment and Early Service Development of an Academic Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery Unit : A Retrospective Service Report
abstract: Objectives: To describe the establishment, early service development, and procedural activity of the Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery Unit at Sultan Qaboos University Hospital (SQUH) from July 2023 to December 2025 and to summarize its initial training and regional collaborative activities. Material and Methods: We retrospectively evaluated operative records from August 2023 to December 2025; 2023 represented a partial five-month period. Counts represented documented procedures rather than unique patients or operative encounters, and separately coded procedures within one encounter were counted individually. Procedures were assigned to ten mutually exclusive categories by principal operative purpose and summarized descriptively; clinical outcomes were not assessed. Results: A total of 461 procedures across 104 distinct recorded procedure types were documented. Activity increased from 30 procedures during August–December 2023 (6.0/month) to 163 in 2024 (13.6/month) and 268 in 2025 (22.3/month). The leading categories were skin and soft tissue tumor surgery ( n = 148, 32.1%), hand and peripheral nerve surgery ( n = 97, 21.0%), and wound management ( n = 95, 20.6%). Training and collaborative activities included a facial anatomy course and participation in a free-flap procedure at another Muscat institution. Conclusion: Increasing procedural volume suggests growing demand for sp…

title: Anthropomorphism in service robots and consumer acceptance: investigating the relationship via a systematic literature review
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to investigate the effect of social robots anthropomorphism on consumers’ attitudes, acceptance and intention to use social robots. Design/methodology/approach A systematic literature review was conducted to a total of 96 articles that were selected from reputable scientific journals according to the Chartered Association of Business Schools (CABS) Journal Guide, published between 2015 and 2025. The TCCM (Theory-Content-Characteristic-Methodology) framework was used for data analysis, while a systematic content analysis was also performed. Findings The findings of the application of the TCCM framework highlight the most frequently used theories, research development frameworks, methodologies followed and research outcomes. In addition, it draws attention to the factors that act as moderators and mediators in the relationship between the anthropomorphism of social robots and the attitude, acceptance and intention to use them. Finally, the study concludes with recommendations for further research. Originality/value No literature review has examined all related literature on anthropomorphism attitude, acceptance and intention to use social robots.

title: Adoption of mobile money service: a customer experience perspective
abstract: Purpose This study aims to understand the impact of customers’ experience with mobile money services (MMS) on users’ adoption behavior by proposing an integration of the extended Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT2) and the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB). Design/methodology/approach We collected data from 316 MMS users through a questionnaire survey. The partial least squares-structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) technique was employed to test the structural model. Findings The results provide empirical support for the existence of users’ multi-dimensional (i.e. seven) MMS experience comprising performance expectancy, effort expectancy, social influence, facilitating conditions, hedonic motivation, price value, and habit. We also find that users’ performance expectancy, effort expectancy, social influence, facilitating conditions, and habit drive their attitude formation toward a mobile money service, in turn impacting users’ adoption behavior. Originality/value This study advances the literature by providing a comprehensive and systematic exploration of the multi-dimensional (vs. uni-dimensional) view of customer usage experience in MMS through an integrated model of UTAUT2 and TPB. Unlike previous studies that often focus on isolated aspects, this study integrates complementary theoretical perspectives to offer a holistic understanding of customer e…

title: Thresholds and spatial effects of urbanization on ecosystem service supply-demand relationships: a multiscale study of the Wuhan Metropolitan Area
abstract: Rapid urbanization continues to reshape the supply–demand relationships of ecosystem services (ESs), posing increasing risks to regional sustainable development. Previous work has looked at the scale dependence and spatial heterogeneity of urbanization and how they independently impact supply–demand relationships of ESs but they have not been considered jointly. This study investigated the nonlinear effects of urbanization drivers on ES supply–demand relationships in the Wuhan Metropolitan Area (WMA). The supply–demand relationships of grain production (GP), carbon sequestration (CS), and water yield (WY) were analyzed from 2000 to 2020 at 3 km grid, 5 km grid, and town scales using random forest (RF), SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and multiscale geographically weighted regression (MGWR). The results showed that (1) GP and WY exhibited slight deficits with increasing supply–demand imbalances, whereas CS remained in surplus but with a continuous decline. (2)RF and SHAP showed significant nonlinear responses to built-up land proportion (BUILT), population density (POP), and GDP density (GDP). The importance and response patterns of drivers also exhibited scale dependence. (3) The MGWR indicated that urbanization drivers generally exerted negative effects on the ecosystem service supply–demand ratio (ESDR), while their direction and magnitude exhibited pronounced spatial h…

title: Service Delivery of Coordinated Specialty Care Programs Participating in the Early Psychosis Intervention Network
Understanding the Influence of Hotel Staff’s Service Quality on Guest Loyalty: A Qualitative Study
abstract: This qualitative study aimed to determine what affects guest loyalty when guests receive service from hotel employees. This included how guests feel about their experience at the hotel and if they will come back or refer others. We wanted to understand guests' perceptions of the quality of service provided by hotel employees. We also examined how employees' service affected guests' loyalty and behavioral intention. We chose a qualitative study to better understand participants' experiences and perceptions. We used purposive sampling because participants met our criteria as hotel guests. We gathered information by interviewing participants about their experiences with hotel employees, their perceptions of the service they received, what made a good service experience, and why they would return to a hotel or refer someone to it. The collected information was coded and analyzed using thematic analysis to identify common trends and themes. The participants felt that quality of service was achieved when the employee gave the guest a positive interaction. Service was given in a timely manner. Service that they could trust and was professional. Guests felt cared for by the employee and had their problems resolved. Communication was of quality, and service was provided in a pleasant environment. Guests also liked it when employees went above and beyond by offering extra services or ges…
venue: International Journal of Innovative and Multidisciplinary Research

title: Longitudinal changes in crisis and broader mental health service use following access to the Brain in Hand digital support service
abstract: Purpose Demand for mental health services in the UK has increased, including crisis care. Digital support tools are positioned as adjuncts to existing services, but there is limited real-world longitudinal evidence on how they relate to service use. This study aims to examine changes in crisis and broader mental health service use following access to the Brain in Hand (BiH) digital support service. Design/methodology/approach In this observational cohort study, adults accessing BiH (N = 149 at baseline) self-reported their use of mental health services at baseline, three months and six months. Most participants were autistic, had ADHD, or were students. Crisis and expanded mental health service use were modelled using two-part (hurdle) models to estimate changes in the likelihood and frequency of service contact between baseline and follow-up, with inverse probability weighting to adjust for differential attrition. Findings Reductions in both the probability of accessing services and the frequency of contacts were observed at three and six months. Reductions were concentrated among participants with higher baseline service use. Estimates were imprecise, reflecting modest sample size and variability. As an observational study without a comparator group, these findings describe how service use changed over the period rather than establishing that BiH caused the change. Practical …

title: Between Vocation and Pragmatism: Motivations, Expectations, and Concerns of Officers and Candidates for the Prison Service
abstract: Cel pracy Celem artykułu jest analiza motywacji, oczekiwań i obaw funkcjonariuszy oraz kandydatów do służby, ze szczególnym uwzględnieniem zgodności między oficjalnym systemem motywacyjnym a rzeczywistymi doświadczeniami pracowników. Materiał i metody Źródłem wiedzy na temat motywacji pracowników są wyniki badań empirycznych przeprowadzonych z wykorzystaniem metody sondażu diagnostycznego. Jako technikę badawczą zastosowano anonimową ankietę kwestionariuszową skierowaną do funkcjonariuszy oraz kandydatów do służby. Wyniki Stopień dopasowania systemu motywacyjnego SW do potrzeb pracowników i kandydatów jest częściowy. Dobrze adresowane są kwestie stabilności finansowej i formalnej ścieżki kariery. Niedostatecznie ujęto wartości związane z rozwojem osobistym, misją społeczną i równowagą życiową – szczególnie istotne dla młodszych kandydatów. Funkcjonariusze wskazują na realne problemy organizacyjne, które obniżają skuteczność systemu motywacyjnego (brak uznania, nadmierna dyscyplina, biurokracja). Natomiast znacznie większe rozbieżności można zauważyć w przypadku analizy obaw i zagrożeń, związanych z pełnieniem służby. Technological Sovereignty of Russia: Legal Collisions and Reserves for Improving Regulation
abstract: The article proposes a position that reveals the possibilities of implementing technological sovereignty in Russia at the present stage. By means of the developed author's criteria, the analysis of legal regulations, technological processes, financial capabilities, intellectual and personnel needs for the implementation and improvement of the regulation of the economy of the Russian state and its technological sovereignization is carried out.

title: Heterogeneity in organizational responses to legally mandated hybrid practices: the example of the EU Taxonomy Regulation
abstract: Purpose Using the EU Taxonomy Regulation as an example, this paper aims to explore how companies respond to regulations that mandate novel hybrid practices, which combine elements of multiple institutional logics, such as environmental and financial. Design/methodology/approach Combining the institutional logics perspective and the attention-based view, the authors analyze how companies process regulatory pressures based on their internal structures and practices. This study draws on 22 semi-structured interviews across seven countries, supported by document analysis of nonfinancial reports and practitioner literature. Findings The authors find that companies allocate attention differently based on the degree of integration between environmental and financial logics in their structures. The perceived compatibility of mandated practices with existing internal structures and practices significantly influences the strategic responses adopted. Practical implications This study emphasizes that early preparedness and the internal integration of sustainability and financial practices facilitate regulatory compliance and enhance competitive positioning. Policymakers should support this through capacity-building measures to promote effective regulation adoption. Social implications The results indicate that the increase in corporate sustainability–related activities depends on the strat…

title: Multi-omics identifies PCK1-associated immunometabolic regulation underlying the protective effects of sinomenine in vascular dementia
abstract: Background Vascular dementia (VaD) is one of the major causes of cognitive impairment among older adults. However, effective treatments that can modify the progression of the disease are still lacking. Emerging evidence indicates that metabolic remodeling in microglia influences inflammatory responses during vascular brain injury. Microglial immunometabolic regulation has therefore been proposed as an important contributor to the pathogenesis of vascular dementia (VaD). Methods Transcriptomic integration, WGCNA, network pharmacology, and single-nucleus RNA sequencing were combined to identify disease-associated microglial alterations and potential targets involved in sinomenine (SIN)-mediated regulation. The interaction between SIN and phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase 1 (PCK1) was investigated using molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations. The biological effects of SIN were then validated in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated BV2 microglia. Results Integrated analyses highlighted PCK1 as a potential mediator associated with SIN-induced metabolic regulation in VaD. snRNA-seq demonstrated expansion of metabolically stressed microglial states accompanied by PCK1-related metabolic alterations. Stable binding between SIN and PCK1 was supported by molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations. In LPS-stimulated BV2 microglia, SIN suppressed inflammatory activati…

title: Regulation of Amplified Spontaneous Emission Dynamics in Quasi-Two-Dimensional Perovskites via the Energy-Funneling Effect
abstract: Abstract Quasi-two-dimensional perovskites with mixed-phase multiple-quantum-well distributions are promising gain media for amplified spontaneous emission (ASE), but the regulatory role of phase distribution in ASE behavior remains unclear. Here, quasi-two-dimensional (BA)2(MA)n−1PbnBr3n+1 films with different phase distributions were investigated using steady-state optical spectroscopy, femtosecond Kerr-gated time-resolved ASE measurements, and transient absorption spectroscopy. Compared with large-n-dominated films, those with a more balanced phase distribution exhibit a lower ASE threshold, smaller emission-peak shift, and weaker line width broadening. Time-resolved ASE and transient absorption analyses further indicate that small-n phases buffer photoexcited carriers and delay their transfer into large-n emissive phases, thereby moderating carrier accumulation in the emissive phase and yielding a more stable emission wavelength and narrower line width. These findings clarify how phase distribution regulates ASE through carrier buffering and redistribution, demonstrating phase engineering as an effective strategy for stable perovskite gain media.

title: Public Debt Digital Financial Assets as an Object of Financial-Legal Regulation
abstract: In the current economic climate, the scholarly analysis of the legal regulation of public debt digital financial assets-viewed as objects of financial-legal regulation — has become particularly relevant. This importance stems from the need to mobilize additional funds for the state’s budgetary system and the ongoing development of digital financial technologies. The study employed both general scientific and specialized research methods: dialectical, systems, logical, and synthesis-based approaches, as well as formal-legal and comparative-legal analysis. The study concludes that: 1) national legislation concerning digital financial assets and their various types — including debt-based digital financial assets — is currently emerging and evolving; 2) corporate debt-based digital financial assets are the primary type currently developed and regulated; 3) in recent years, as part of an experiment in two constituent entities of the Russian Federation (the Chuvash Republic and the Republic of Crimea), provision has been made for the issuance of debt-based digital financial assets; 4) in recent years, a number of countries (Slovenia, Thailand, the UK) have attempted to issue public debt-based digital financial assets, primarily to test digital financial technologies. The scientific and practical relevance of the study lies in its enabling a critical re-examination of existing theoret…

title: MASLD Liver Transplant: Evolution of Frequency, Age Trends, and Factors Associated With Outcomes
abstract: Background. Metabolic dysfunction–associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has rapidly emerged as a leading indication for liver transplantation (LT) in the United States. There remains a need to understand the evolution of transplant volumes and recipient profiles and outcomes. In this study, we aim to analyze current MASLD LT trends to aid in identifying opportunities for this patient population. Methods. We analyzed UNOS data for primary liver transplants (2010–2024), identifying MASLD by diagnosis codes and stratifying transplants into three eras (2010–2014, 2015–2019, and 2020–2024). Analyses included annual MASLD transplant counts and proportions, era-specific annual percent change, comparisons of donor, operative, and recipient characteristics, Kaplan–Meier curves, multivariable Cox regression for overall post-LT mortality, and competing-risk regression for waitlist outcomes. Results. In total, 18 153 MASLD LT recipients were included (Era 1: 2734; Era 2: 6127; Era 3: 9292). Annual MASLD LT volume increased from 461 in 2010 to 2090 in 2024. Annual percent change was +10.6% (Era 1), +20.1% (Era 2), and +5.9% (Era 3). In Era 3, recipients were as young as 8 y. Era 3 waitlist candidates had significantly higher likelihood of transplant (sHR 1.52; 95% CI, 1.46–1.58) and lower risk of waitlist mortality (sHR 0.44; 95% CI, 0.40–0.48). Recipient survival increased from 97.0% …

title: Organ-Specific Regulation of Folic Acid Bioavailability by Bioactive Small Molecules from Whole Wheat Steamed Buns
abstract: Abstract The in vivo conversion of folic acid (FA) to its bioactive form is inefficient, and unmetabolized FA poses health concerns. This study investigates the regulatory mechanisms of active small molecules derived from whole wheat on FA intestinal absorption, liver metabolism, and brain accumulation. UPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS was used to identify active constituents, combined with network pharmacology and molecular docking for target prediction, and a 48 day mouse study with multitissue quantification of FA and 5-methyltetrahydrofolate (5-MTHF). Network pharmacology revealed enrichment in endocytosis, organic acid transport, and blood–brain barrier pathways; molecular docking showed differential affinities for proton-coupled folic acid transporter, reduced folic acid carrier, folic acid receptor alpha, DHFR, and MTHFR. Animal studies confirmed that quercetin promoted intestinal absorption; D-calcium pantothenate enhanced liver 5-MTHF conversion; ferulic acid elevated circulating FA; and δ-tocopherol mediated brain-targeted accumulation of total folate (predominantly FA). These findings demonstrate that whole wheat-derived small molecules exert node-specific regulatory effects on folate metabolism, offering insights for developing FA-fortified foods.
venue: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry

title: Bilateral cerebellar high-frequency rTMS for refractory epilepsy: a randomized, single-blind, sham-controlled study
abstract: Background For patients with drug-resistant epilepsy who are not suitable for surgery, transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) is an important non-invasive neuromodulation therapy. The cerebellar cortex can inhibit cortical excitability via the cerebello-thalamo-cortical pathway. Here, we explore whether high-frequency (20 Hz) cerebellar repetitive TMS (rTMS) reduces seizure frequency and interictal epileptiform discharges (IEDs) in refractory epilepsy. Methods Eighty-seven patients with refractory epilepsy were included in the intention-to-treat (ITT) population ( n = 87) and then randomized to active rTMS ( n = 44) or sham stimulation ( n = 43). One patient in treatment group had no post-baseline efficacy data; efficacy analyses were therefore performed in the modified intention-to-treat (mITT) population ( n = 86). The active group received two cycles of 20 Hz rTMS targeting the cerebellum. Seizure frequency and IEDs were assessed before and after treatment. Results Poisson generalized linear mixed models revealed a significant group×time interaction for seizure frequency [ F (2,236) = 162.65, p < 0.001]. The active group had significantly lower seizure frequencies at months 1, 2, and 3 (all p < 0.001), with the largest difference at month 2. Percentage reductions of seizure frequency in the active group were 64.6%, 73.2%, and 13.3%, respectively, compared with 3.9%, 0…

title: Revealing the restrictiveness-fairness paradox in general data protection regulation consent practices: evidence from a mixed-methods study
abstract: Purpose Restrictive cookie consent may satisfy regulatory requirements while limiting meaningful privacy choice. Existing privacy research explains why users disclose information despite privacy concerns, but less is known about why they continue using digital services after judging consent procedures as unfair. This study examines how users interpret restrictive consent, how regulatory contexts shape evaluations and why unfairness coexists with continued engagement. Design/methodology/approach An exploratory sequential mixed-methods design was used. Study 1 analyzed qualitative responses from users in General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and non-GDPR contexts to develop a Communication Privacy Management (CPM)-based model. Study 2 tested the model through two experiments and a pooled post hoc analysis examining how restrictiveness and institutional privacy boundaries shape privacy risk-control assessments, fairness and intention to use online flight-booking websites. Findings Restrictive consent consistently reduced perceived fairness without reliably reducing intention to use website services, revealing a Restrictiveness-Fairness Paradox: users continue engaging despite judging consent procedures as unfair. GDPR also functions as an institutional privacy boundary that changes the fairness cues users rely on. Research limitations/implications The study identifies procedur…

title: Beyond social skills: emotion regulation as a potential mechanism linking physical exercise to social anxiety in left-behind adolescents
abstract: Introduction This cross-sectional, exploratory study investigated the association between physical exercise (PE) and social anxiety (SA) among 862 left-behind adolescents in China. It examined emotion regulation abilities (ERA) and peer relationships (PR) as potential mediators and gender as a moderator in this association. Methods A cross-sectional exploratory design was adopted. Participants were 862 Chinese left-behind adolescents. Path analysis was used to test the hypothesized sequential mediation model and gender moderation effect. Results Path analysis revealed that PE was negatively associated with SA. Each separate path of the hypothesized sequential chain (PE → ERA, ERA → PR, PR → SA) was statistically significant, while the overall sequential mediation effect (PE → ERA → PR → SA) was non-significant (95% CI included zero). This indicated that the significant PE–ERA association had a small effect size and could not propagate fully through the chain to SA. The direct path from PE to PR was also non-significant. The data favoured independent mediation pathways rather than a sequential mediation process. Gender moderated the pathway: the positive PE–ERA association was significant for females but non-significant for males. Discussion The findings are hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory and require replication via longitudinal research. For vulnerable adolescen…

title: Development Lease: Improving Legal Regulation in the Existing System of Property Rights
abstract: The right of development lease, which is currently the primary legal mechanism facilitating the development of publicly owned land, exhibits a number of drawbacks that compromise the stability of legal relations when the designated use of the land is altered; these issues require a legislative solution. The authors identify the potential of the rental form of land use to ensure the strength of the lease-mediated development right in the context of the suspension of the reform of property rights. A legal mechanism is proposed to strengthen the right of development lease of a land plot when the designated use of the latter changes, which, being based on a balance of private and public interests, is focused on the creation of capital construction projects.

title: Regulation of prices for food and non-food products: Impact on economic results of producers
abstract: Subject. State regulation of producer prices of food and non-food industrial products in the Russian Federation. Objectives. The study of the impact of state price regulation in the Russian Federation on the performance of manufacturing enterprises and the assessment of the possibility of forecasting profits and profitability of industrial enterprises, taking into account the price indices for their products. Methods. The methods of screening abstract databases and citation systems, regulatory documents of the Russian Federation, methods of correlation and regression analysis and forecasting are used. Results. The key trends in the indicators have been identified. The impact of government intervention in price formation policy on the performance indicators of food and non-food producers in the Russian Federation is assessed. A methodological approach to forecasting the profits and profitability of industrial enterprises has been developed, taking into account the price indices for their products. Conclusions. The research hypothesis has been confirmed about the existence of a correlation between the producer price index of industrial products and the growth rate of profit from sales and profitability of sales, about the impact of regulatory measures taken by the state on this dependence, about the possibility of forecasting the listed performance indicators for industrial enter…

title: Synergistic regulation of electron and phonon transport in SrTiO 3 -based thermoelectric perovskites via entropy engineering of A-site cations
abstract: Abstract SrTiO3-based thermoelectric oxides are promising candidates for high-temperature energy conversion because of their low cost, environmental compatibility, and excellent thermal stability. However, their relatively low thermoelectric performance remains a key limitation to practical applications. In this work, a series of multicomponent A-site medium- and high-entropy perovskite oxides, (Sr1/2Ba1/4Ca1/4)1-x(La1/3Nd1/3Sm1/3)xTiO3 (SBC-REx; x = 0.08–0.18), were developed to simultaneously regulate electron and phonon transport. All samples maintain a cubic SrTiO3 perovskite phase with Pm–3m symmetry and homogeneous elemental distribution. The doping of La3+, Nd3+ and Sm3+ electron donors modulates the electron carrier concentration, thereby increasing electrical conductivity while preserving moderate carrier mobility and effective mass, leading to enhanced power factor at x = 0.14. Meanwhile, entropy engineering via co-incorporation of multielement rare earth cations in the A-site induces chemical disorder, local lattice distortion and strain fields, which suppress grain growth and intensify phonon scattering, leading to reduced lattice thermal conductivity. Consequently, the optimized SBC-RE0.14 sample achieves a power factor of 1.24 mW m−1 K−2 and thermal conductivity of 3.08 W m−1 K−1, reaching a maximum ZT of 0.31 at 773 K. This work demonstrates that A-site entropy e…

title: Admission systemic inflammation response index is associated with 14-day adverse clinical outcomes in patients with pyogenic liver abscess: a single-center retrospective cohort study
abstract: Objective To assess the association between the systemic inflammation response index (SIRI) at admission and 14-day adverse clinical outcomes in patients with pyogenic liver abscess (PLA), and to evaluate its discriminatory performance. Methods This single-center retrospective cohort study included 670 adults with PLA admitted to Linyi People’s Hospital between January 2021 and December 2024. SIRI was calculated from the first complete blood count obtained within 24 hours after admission according to the study data-collection criteria. The primary outcome was a composite of adverse clinical events within 14 days. A base logistic regression model and a model additionally including SIRI were fitted in 30 multiply imputed datasets, with complete-case and death-exclusion sensitivity analyses. Restricted cubic splines, receiver operating characteristic curves, and exploratory measures of incremental performance were evaluated. Results Of the 670 patients, 100 (14.9%) experienced an adverse clinical outcome, including four deaths. Median SIRI was higher in patients with adverse outcomes [8.95 (4.14-15.64) vs. 5.80 (2.93-11.64); P< 0.001]. In the multiply imputed linear model, the adjusted OR for SIRI was 1.0187 (95% CI, 1.0022-1.0354; P = 0.0262); the complete-case estimate was 1.0163 (95% CI, 0.9994-1.0334; P = 0.0588). After exclusion of four deaths, the adjusted OR was 1.0191 (…

title: Unmet demand for flexibility: remote work preferences of office workers in Poland
abstract: Purpose Remote-work preferences are usually explained either by what jobs technically permit or by workers' household circumstances. This study proposes a third reading, in which preferences reflect a worker's position in an ongoing negotiation over flexibility, and tests it against a needs account using original survey data on office workers in Poland. Design/methodology/approach An original survey of 639 office workers in Polish cities of over 100,000 inhabitants, fielded in June 2024 once post-pandemic attitudes had stabilized. Ordinal logistic regression relates stated preferences to socio-demographic, employment-related, and experiential factors, entered jointly, allowing their relative weights to be compared directly; a partial proportional odds model then tests whether the same factors govern the move from office-based to hybrid work and from hybrid to fully remote work. Findings Preferences align with position within the employment relationship rather than household need: ownership and tenure predict strongly, while gender, education, and children do not; age is the sole demographic exception. Lived experience, especially perceived gains in non-work-life quality, is the strongest predictor, but its effect is asymmetric. It determines whether workers want any remote work far more than whether they want all of it, which makes hybrid work a distinct settlement rather than …

title: Determinants of response to a nutritional intervention in depression: sociodemographic factors and lifestyle changes
abstract: Purpose Dietary interventions are needed alongside the treatment of depression, with a focus on factors contributing to their effectiveness. This study aims to assess the influence of sociodemographic factors, intervention adherence and lifestyle changes on response to a nutrition intervention and a social support group intervention for depressive disorder. Design/methodology/approach The authors examined the impact of sociodemographic and lifestyle factors as well as adherence on response to an 8-week controlled trial with two arms (a nutrition intervention group, a social support group) to which 93 patients with moderate to severe depressive disorder were randomized. Analyses were taken at baseline, eight weeks, six months and 12 months. We performed chi-square tests, independent-samples t-tests and Mann–Whitney U tests to analyze the differences between responders (i.e. = reduction of at least one 1 point decrease in the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale, CES-D) and non-responders (i.e. = no change or an increase of at least 1 point in CES-D), separately for each group. Findings At 8 weeks and 6 months, non-responders consistently differed from responders in two ways: lower baseline depressive symptoms (p = 0.002, p = 0.02) in the social support group, and increased fast-food intake (p = 0.025, p = 0.025) in the nutrition group. Neither sociodemographic facto…

Microscopic observation of magnetization response shaped by magnetic anisotropy in a single magnetic nanoparticle
abstract: Abstract Magnetization response under a magnetic field with thermal fluctuations is important for designing magnetic nanoparticles, which are extensively studied for biomedical applications. The magnetic properties of magnetic nanoparticles have conventionally been measured as net magnetization. In this study, the magnetization distribution in a single magnetic nanoparticle under a static magnetic field was observed using magnetic force microscopy. After the easy axis of the particle associated with magnetic anisotropy was aligned, the effects of magnetic anisotropy, the applied magnetic field, and thermal fluctuations on the magnetization orientation were analyzed. The single-particle magnetization response was then compared with the net magnetization response obtained from the static measurement and numerical simulations. The effects of magnetic moment and anisotropy energy on the magnetization distribution were evaluated by measuring single-core magnetic nanoparticles with different core diameters. Our measurement approach for magnetization response in a single magnetic nanoparticle also contributes to the analysis of the dipolar field affecting surrounding particles.

title: Immunohistochemical Subtype Conversion and Pathological Response After Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy in Luminal B HER2-Negative Locally Advanced Breast Cancer: A Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Background: Luminal B HER2-negative breast cancer responds only modestly to neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC), and the receptor profile of its residual tumor may differ from that of the original biopsy. Objective: To test whether subtype conversion after NAC is associated with pathological response. Methods: This retrospective cross-sectional study included 49 consecutive women with stage IIIA–IIIB Luminal B HER2-negative cancer who received doxorubicin–cyclophosphamide or docetaxel–cyclophosphamide before mastectomy at Dr. Hasan Sadikin General Hospital, Bandung, Indonesia (2024–2025). Conversion meant any change in immunohistochemical surrogate subtype between core biopsy and mastectomy. The outcomes were the Miller–Payne grade (primary) and the Residual Cancer Burden (RCB) class. Exact tests, proportional-odds and Firth logistic regression, and Holm correction were applied. Results: Conversion occurred in 14 patients (28.6%; 95% CI 17.8–42.4), most often to Luminal B HER2-positive. Converted tumors had lower Miller–Payne grades (exact p = 0.027). None reached grade 4–5 (0/14 vs 9/35; p = 0.045). The adjusted cumulative odds ratio was 0.27 (95% CI 0.08–0.91). RCB-III was more frequent after conversion (78.6% vs 31.4%; adjusted OR 6.54, 95% CI 1.69–31.63). The association between conversion and the RCB class was the only one surviving Holm correction (p = 0.019), and the RCB-III …

title: Decision support framework for designing out waste implementation in the wall system of residential projects: a New Zealand case study
abstract: Purpose Designing out waste (DoW) is recognised as an effective strategy for minimising construction and demolition waste (CDW) at the design stage. However, existing DoW guidance remains largely generic and provides limited support for identifying, evaluating, and selecting suitable DoW alternatives in practice. As wall elements are a major source of waste in residential construction, this study develops a decision support framework for implementing DoW in the wall system of residential projects in New Zealand. Design/methodology/approach A mixed-methods research design was adopted, comprising three phases: conceptual framework development, framework development, and framework evaluation. Exploratory studies and a systematic literature review informed the conceptual framework. Desktop analysis and expert interviews were then undertaken to develop the framework. A hybrid fuzzy analytic hierarchy process (FAHP) and fuzzy technique for order preference by similarity to ideal solution (fuzzy-TOPSIS) was applied to evaluate and rank DoW alternatives against multiple sustainability criteria. The framework was subsequently evaluated and refined through a focus group with industry experts. Findings The framework provides a structured process for supporting DoW implementation from the design stage by identifying applicable DoW alternatives, integrating project-specific implementation f…

title: Merchandise and retail behaviour at music concerts in sports stadiums
abstract: Purpose Live music concerts in sports stadiums have evolved into high-intensity experiential retail environments characterised by constrained infrastructure, high customer throughput and concentrated temporal demand, in which merchandise, food and beverage sales represent key revenue streams. However, limited research examines how emotional, social and digital influences interact with these operational conditions to shape retail decision making. This article investigates how concertgoers evaluate and prioritise on-site retail categories during stadium events. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative research design combined participant observation at nineteen concerts across ten UK sports stadiums with informal conversations involving 375 attendees. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis to identify patterns in retail decision making, identity expression, digital engagement and price negotiation. Findings Findings reveal a strong pattern in which merchandise is prioritised relative to food and beverages. This prioritisation emerges from the interaction between symbolic value and spatial compatibility: merchandise is valued for its role in identity signalling and smartphone-mediated visibility, while also remaining compatible with the embodied and temporal demands of participation. In contrast, food and beverages are perceived as short-lived, more price sensitive …

title: Needs assessment for a laboratory information system at Diagnopath Medical Laboratories in Zimbabwe
abstract: Background: Laboratory information systems (LIS) are increasingly recognised as essential for improving efficiency, accuracy and data management in medical laboratories. While public sector LIS implementations have been documented in Zimbabwe, little information is publicly available about needs assessments in the private sector. Aim: To identify user requirements for an LIS at Diagnopath Medical Laboratories (DML) to inform future implementation. Setting: The study was conducted in a multidiscipline private medical laboratory setting. Methods: A two-round Delphi study involved 14 experts (Round 1) and 30 experts (Round 2). Round 1 used interviews and observations; Round 2 employed questionnaires. Statistical analyses included independent t-tests and Pearson correlation. User stories were converted to requirements using Agile methodologies. Results: Experts aged 22–52 years participated. Experts anticipated that an LIS would reduce task completion times by an average of 70%. Significant differences existed between current and expected task times (t[50] = 3.611, p < 0.001, Cohen’s d = 1.001), indicating a large and practically meaningful effect. No significant relationship was found between task frequency and time reduction (r = –0.306, p = 0.121). Forty user stories yielded 153 requirements, showing strong correlation (r = 0.70, p < 0.001). Conclusion: This study demonstrates a…

title: Preoperative Keratometric Power as the Primary Biometric Determinant of Thirty-Day Visual Rehabilitation Following Phacoemulsification: A Retrospective Cohort Study in West Sumatra, Indonesia
abstract: Background: Visual recovery after phacoemulsification depends on accurate preoperative biometry. The influence of corneal curvature in eyes with normal axial dimensions remains uncertain. Objective: To assess associations between axial length (AL), anterior chamber depth (ACD), keratometry (K), and 30-day postoperative visual outcomes in West Sumatra, Indonesia. Methods: This retrospective cohort included 51 consecutive patients (51 eyes) undergoing uncomplicated phacoemulsification with posterior chamber intraocular lens implantation during May–July 2025. Preoperative immersion A-scan biometry and automated keratometry were recorded. Best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) at 30 days was categorized using WHO criteria. Spearman correlation and multivariable logistic regression were performed. Result: Mean age was 65.55 ± 8.12 years; 52.94% were female. Mean AL, ACD, and K were 23.57 ± 1.19 mm, 2.92 ± 0.34 mm, and 43.62 ± 1.46 D. At 30 days, 15.69% achieved emmetropia, 76.47% had mild impairment, and 7.84% had moderate impairment. Keratometry correlated with BCVA (r = −0.280, p = 0.046); AL (p = 0.249) and ACD (p = 0.592) did not. Physiological keratometry (43.00–44.50 D) independently predicted favorable rehabilitation (adjusted OR 3.84, 95% CI 1.18–12.50; p = 0.026). Conclusion: Preoperative keratometry was the principal biometric predictor of 30-day visual recovery in this cohor…

title: Built to leave: how human resource management gaps shape early-career turnover intentions in college athletics
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to critically examine the hiring and work practices of early-career athletic employees through a human resource management perspective. Design/methodology/approach We used a critical phenomenological approach to conduct semi-structured qualitative interviews with fourteen early-career college athletic employees. Findings Our findings suggest that early-career athletic employees experience limited organizational socialization practices. Our participants discussed dysfunctional hiring practices, insufficient onboarding, inadequate development and leadership and a culture of replaceability in their roles, which could be an explanation why for every participant discussed their turnover intentions. Originality/value Early-career athletic employees represent a significant portion of the sport industry workforce. Our findings offer insights into how early-career employees navigate and experience their first full-time roles in sport. Understanding their experiences is critical for developing sustainable HRM practices that retain talent and strengthen the long-term health of sport organizations.

title: The European Union’s Hard Power in the International Arena: The Case of Migration Policy
abstract: Objectives The aim of this article is to demonstrate the European Union’s hard power in its response to international migration. To illustrate the importance of hard power in EU migration policy, an analysis of the set of tools and mechanisms through which the European Union and its member states project their power and exert pressure on other actors in international relations is conducted. Material and methods The research process utilises a case study that examines the military operation EUNAVFOR MED Sophia/Irini, the issue of instrumentalisation of migration in the context of the border crisis between EU Member States and Belarus, and partnerships with third countries, illustrated by the example of the EU’s relations with Tunisia. Results The research hypothesis assumes that while the European Union continues to base its actions on soft and normative instruments, it is increasingly using hard power in its migration policy. Key factors driving the EU to use hard power in migration policy and border protection are the shifting balance of international power and the growing challenges associated with managing migration flows. Conclusions Today, hard power serves not only a deterrent function, related to border control and the use of coercive measures, but is increasingly becoming a tool for legitimizing EU' actions in the international environment. It is therefore an increasing…
