title: Dynamics of energy expenditure in severe traumatic brain injury during intensive care: the influence of infection and sedation
abstract: Aim : To investigate the dynamics of energy expenditure in patients with severe traumatic brain injury (TBI) during an intensive care unit (ICU) stay and to assess the effects of infection, sedation, sedation depth, and neurological status. Materials and methods : This prospective observational study was conducted in the ICU of St. George University Hospital in Plovdiv over 18 months. Thirty patients with severe TBI were included. Measured resting energy expenditure (mREE) was assessed using indirect calorimetry (Q-NRG+, Cosmed). Metabolic status was defined using the energy metabolic index, expressed as a percentage of Harris–Benedict predicted energy expenditure. Results : The measured REE increased progressively during ICU stay, reaching peak values between days 11 and 20 (31.08±4.61 kcal/kg/day; 115±15%), followed by a moderate decline while remaining above predicted levels. Marked interindividual variability was observed, with hypo-, normo-, and hypermetabolic states throughout all periods. Energy expenditure was significantly higher during infection compared to non-infectious periods (111±23% vs. 103±21%, p =0.037). Sedation was associated with lower energy expenditure (103±20% vs. 111±25%, p =0.041), with a significant inverse relationship between sedation depth and metabolic rate ( p <0.001). Neurological status and inflammatory markers showed no significant associat…

title: Heterogeneous Effects of Determinants of Energy Consumption in Developed and Developing Countries: Evidence from Quantile Regression
abstract: This study examines the determinants of energy consumption in developed and developing countries using 2024 data and applying the quantile regression method. In this context, the study contributes to the literature by presenting up-to-date cross-country evidence and highlighting the heterogeneous effects of energy consumption determinants at different consumption levels. Unlike OLS method, which estimates only the conditional mean, quantile regression estimates these effects at different points in the conditional distribution of energy consumption. Building on previous studies, the analysis initially included GDP, population, urbanization, HDI, industrialization, FDI, and CO₂ emissions; however, GDP, HDI, and CO₂ were excluded because they were found to be insignificant. The results reveal statistically significant differences between quantiles for industrialization and for population the strongest variation was observed in industrialization. The findings indicate that the determinants of energy consumption are not homogeneous and vary across different consumption groups.

title: Geoclimatic changes, industry structure and external energy dependence as factors of economic dynamics
abstract: Subject. The impact of geoclimatic shifts – temperature anomalies and extreme hydrometeorological events – on the economic development of national economies. Objectives. Construction and econometric verification of a panel model that makes it possible to assess the direction and impact of geoclimatic factors on the logarithm of per capita GDP for a sample of 54 countries for 2000–2024. Methods. The study is based on a synthesis of theoretical analysis of the climate-economic literature and an empirical assessment using panel data. Results. An increase in the average annual temperature by 1°C relative to the climatic norm of 1961–1990 reduces per capita GDP by an average of 1.8%, and each additional extreme event (drought, flood, storm) – by 2.6%. The share of agriculture in GDP and energy dependence significantly increase climate vulnerability, while increased grain yields and trade openness act as compensating mechanisms. The model explains 80.7% of the intra-country variation in per capita GDP. Conclusions. Taking into account the combined effects of temperature anomalies, extreme events, and structural characteristics of the economy allows for more accurate estimates of climate damage compared to traditional approaches that consider these factors in isolation. The high share of agriculture and energy dependence create a "structural trap" that increases vulnerability, while t…

title: Colonial mediations and sovereign possibilities: a synthesis-derived decolonial heuristic layered equity framework for equitable generative AI integration in K-12 and higher education
abstract: Purpose This critical integrative synthesis examines generative AI integration in K-12 and higher education through an explicit decolonial lens. It focuses on how colonial mediations shape opportunities, challenges and strategies for equitable access and outcomes aligned with UN SDG 10. Design/methodology/approach Following a critical integrative review paradigm that fuses the integrative logic of Whittemore and Knafl (2005) with reflexive thematic analysis (Braun and Clarke, 2006) and decolonial theory, 58 sources (2020–2026) were identified through systematic search and purposive theoretical sampling. Sources prioritizing structural critique, Global South perspectives, K-12 evidence gaps, output-level neocolonial patterns and contextual agency were retained. Sources were appraised with the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool and analyzed through a seven-phase relational mapping protocol that translated thematic codes into the layered architecture of the Decolonial Heuristic Layered Equity Framework (DHLEF). Robustness of core pathways was confirmed through sensitivity analyses. Findings Three interdependent themes – transformative opportunities, interlinked challenges and enabling strategies – emerge when read through decolonial theory. Opportunities appear as outer potential outcomes mediated by challenges whose effects are conditioned by data colonialism, epistemic colonialism, in…

title: Gestión energética y economía circular en las pequeñas y medianas empresas de Jalisco, México: análisis cuantitativo hacia una transición energética empresarial
abstract: En el marco de los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible (ODS) 7 y 12, este estudio analiza la influencia del conocimiento en gestión energética sobre la economía circular y la madurez energética, así como el papel mediador de esta última, en pequeñas y medianas empresas (pymes) de Jalisco, México. Mediante un diseño cuantitativo y transversal, se aplicó un cuestionario a 205 personas empresarias de pymes de la Zona Metropolitana de Guadalajara y se contrastaron cuatro hipótesis mediante mínimos cuadrados parciales. Los resultados muestran una baja sistematización de las prácticas sostenibles, motivadas principalmente por criterios de productividad y beneficios empresariales. El conocimiento en gestión energética influye positivamente en la economía circular (β = 0,275; p = 0,002) y en la madurez energética (β = 0,824; p < 0,001); a su vez, la madurez energética influye en la economía circular (β = 0,553; p < 0,001) y media significativamente la relación entre conocimiento energético y economía circular (β = 0,455; p < 0,001). Se concluye que fortalecer el conocimiento y la madurez en gestión energética puede favorecer la incorporación sistemática de prácticas de economía circular y contribuir al avance de las pymes hacia los ODS 7 y 12. title: From numbers to narratives: perceived SDG integration and reported professional and ethical behaviour in accounting and marketing education
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine whether perceived SDG integration within accounting and marketing education is associated with reported professional and ethical behaviour among business students and graduates. It also evaluates the indirect association through cognitive and value transformation. Design/methodology/approach The study uses a cross-sectional survey of 400 students and graduates from business schools in 52 Arab universities across eight countries. Multi-item scales measured perceived SDG integration, cognitive and value transformation and reported professional and ethical behaviour. The hypothesised direct and indirect associations were analysed using PLS-SEM in SmartPLS 4 with 5,000 bootstrap resamples. Findings Perceived SDG integration was positively associated with reported professional and ethical behaviour. The indirect association through cognitive and value transformation was also significant, but the direct association remained significant after the mediator was included in the model. Cognitive and value transformation therefore accounts for part of the estimated association, not all of it. Originality/value The paper examines accounting and marketing education within the same analytical model but treats them as distinct disciplinary settings. Its contribution lies in a conceptual framing of the relationship between sustainability evidence and the claim…

title: Neuroepithelial Tumor with AAV Integration
The computational and neural network analysis of the Williamson hybrid nanofluid for solar energy applications
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to explore the efficiency in the solar energy system using the TiO2 and Ag hybrid nanofluid. In this work, the focus has been on solar energy efficiency. The theoretical, computational and artificial neural network (ANN) combination has been used to determine the heat transfer efficiency in terms of solar radiation and its utilization in the solar system. Design/methodology/approach The thin layer of the TiO2–Ag hybrid nanofluid has been used to consider the 3D formation of the sheet. The finite element method (FEM) is used to solve the transformed nonlinear governing equations numerically. ANN and Levenberg–Marquardt neural network models are used to verify the numerical results further. Findings Solar radiation increases the thermal energy of the fluid, leading to higher temperature profiles and improving energy efficiency. It has been found that the higher the nanoparticle volume fraction, up to 5%, the higher the heat transfer rate and the hybrid nanofluid has superior performance over other fluids. The statistical comparisons demonstrate that the proposed solution methodology for complex radiative non-Newtonian hybrid nanofluid flows is reliable due to an excellent match between numerical and intelligent predictions. Originality/value To the best of the authors’ knowledge, a first analysis of fluid flow over a 3D sheet under Williamson …

title: Storytelling as a preventive public health tool: the batyr model and its implications for youth mental and physical health integration
abstract: Purpose Youth mental ill-health is a pressing global challenge that frequently predicts downstream physical comorbidities. Despite increased clinical provision, a significant public health implementation gap remains, driven by stigma and low mental health literacy. This case study aims to explore peer-to-peer storytelling as a scalable, preventive intervention to bridge this gap and promote holistic wellbeing among young people. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on a comprehensive 10-year evidence base (2016–2026), including four mixed-methods program evaluations, a cluster randomised controlled trial and published qualitative research, this paper synthesises the systemic impact of the Australian batyr model across secondary and tertiary education settings. Findings Safeguarded, lived-experience storytelling significantly improves youth mental health literacy and help-seeking intentions while reducing isolation and stigma. The model is mutually beneficial, fostering self-acceptance among storytellers and creating enabling conditions for holistic self-care, which acts as a critical protective factor against risky physical health behaviours. However, to ensure sustainability, universal programs should be complemented by whole-of-setting approaches, such as embedded curriculum initiatives, to scaffold educator capacity. Practical implications The batyr model provides a proven, c…

title: Analysing the Dynamic Relationship between Foreign Direct Investment, Trade Openness, and Economic Growth: Evidence from a Global Panel with Income-Group Heterogeneity
Optimized dual-energy CT protocol for inferior vena cava CT angiography using 60 keV virtual monoenergetic imaging and 60% ASIR-V
abstract: Objective To investigate the effects of a dual-energy CT (DECT) protocol combining virtual monoenergetic imaging (VMI) with adaptive statistical iterative reconstruction-V (ASIR-V) on image quality and radiation dose for inferior vena cava (IVC) CT angiography (CTA), and to compare the optimized protocol with a conventional 120 kVp protocol. Methods 120 consecutive patients undergoing IVC-CTA were enrolled and allocated sequentially to two groups ( n = 60 each). Group A underwent conventional 120 kVp scanning with 400 mgI/mL contrast medium at 1.5 mL/kg and 50% ASIR-V reconstruction. Group B underwent DECT (rapid 80/140 kVp switching) with 320 mgI/mL contrast medium at 1.2 mL/kg. In Group B, seven VMI datasets from 40 to 70 keV in 5 keV increments were first reconstructed with 50% ASIR-V. At 60 keV, images were reconstructed with filtered back projection (FBP; 0% ASIR-V) and ASIR-V levels from 20% to 100% in 20% increments. Objective image quality was assessed using CT attenuation, standard deviation (SD), background noise, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) at five venous levels. Two radiologists independently rated subjective image quality and diagnostic confidence on 5-point Likert scales. Dose-length product (DLP), effective dose (ED), contrast medium volume, and iodine intake were also recorded and compared between protocols. Results In Group B,…

title: Design of a High-Speed Bit-length-Independent FinFET-based Hybrid Carry Look Ahead-Carry Skip Adder for Future Signal Processing Systems
abstract: In this work, an energy-efficient, high-speed 16-nm FinFET-based hybrid wide-bit-length CLA-CS adder is implemented over a wide range of [Formula: see text]-levels. The proposed architecture combines an 8-bit CMOS domino-structure-based MCC adder module with a carry-skip module employing concatenation and incrementation techniques. The carry outputs of the proposed hybrid adder are obtained in parallel by adopting two separate FinFET-based 4-bit even and odd MCC chains. Concatenation and incrementation blocks are additionally used to boost the speed of the innovative wide bit-length hybrid CLA-CS adder. Finally, the new hybrid CLA-CS wide bit-length adder uses AOI (AND-OR-Invert) and OAI (OR-AND-Invert) logic gates for the carry-skip logic circuit instead of multiplexer logic. The 16[Formula: see text]nm FinFET-based adder with 8-, 16-, 32-and 64-bit sizes implemented with [Formula: see text][Formula: see text]V offered a [Formula: see text] of 60.39/79.87, 98.7/123.5, 101.1/124.1 and 103.8/124.1[Formula: see text]pS, respectively, and these hybrid CLA-CS wider bit-size adders showcased a [Formula: see text] of 188.1/148.5, 418.6/333.5, 850.4/674, and 1680/1350[Formula: see text][Formula: see text]W, respectively, at [Formula: see text]C/[Formula: see text]C. When the bit length is 16 or more, the proposed adder shows approximately similar delays, which indicate the size-indepe…

title: Exploring the relationship between cultural landscapes and psychological well-being through indigenous environmental design in rural China
abstract: Introduction Indigenous environmental design in rural China is increasingly affected by modernization, tourism development, and ecological change. However, empirical evidence concerning the relationship between cultural landscape fidelity and residents’ psychological well-being remains limited. This study developed the Cultural Landscape–Psychological Well-being (CL-PWB) Nexus Model to examine the association between Indigenous Environmental Design Fidelity (IEDF) and psychological well-being, considering place attachment, perceived restorativeness, and cultural identity continuity as mediators, and ritual-spatial synchrony (RSS) and social cohesion (SC) as potential moderators. Methods A sequential explanatory mixed-methods design was employed. The quantitative phase involved a cross-sectional survey of 420 residents from four ethnic minority villages in rural China. Confirmatory factor analysis and regression-based moderated mediation analysis with bootstrapped confidence intervals were used to examine the proposed relationships. The qualitative phase comprised thematic analysis of 40 in-depth and key-informant interviews to contextualise and complement the quantitative findings. Results IEDF was positively associated with psychological well-being. This association was statistically accounted for by place attachment, perceived restorativeness, and cultural identity continuity…

title: Human-induced vibrations in light-gauge steel floors: tests, finite-element analysis and design guides
abstract: This study examines the dynamic response of light-gauge steel (LGS) floor systems subjected to human-induced vibrations, with emphasis on occupant comfort and serviceability. A full-scale LGS floor was experimentally tested using heel-drop and fast-walking excitations to identify its fundamental frequency and acceleration response. The heel-drop test provided natural frequency and damping characteristics, while fast-walking tests represented realistic occupant activity. A detailed finite-element model was developed to perform modal and time-history analyses, and numerical results were compared with predictions from the American Institute of Steel Construction design guide 11 (DG11). Experimental measurements indicated a fundamental frequency of 6.25 Hz and root mean square (RMS) acceleration responses between 5.47%g and 5.58%g. Numerical simulations showed that assuming a 20% live load contribution yielded a fundamental frequency of 6.23 Hz, which closely matched the experimental results. Time-history analyses predicted RMS accelerations ranging from 5.18%g to 7.10%g, with damping ratios of 3–4% providing the best agreement with measured data. In contrast, DG11 significantly underestimated vibration response, predicting only 1.1%g. The findings demonstrate the limitations of current guideline-based approaches and support the adoption of distributed walking load models, RMS-base…

title: DESIGN AND ANALYSIS OF MICROWAVE PRESSURE SENSOR USING METAMATERIAL ABSORBER
abstract: This paper presents the design, analysis, fabrication and testing of an ultra-thin narrow-band metamaterial (MM) absorber tailored for improving the sensitivity of pressure sensors. The proposed resonator achieves an impressive absorption characteristic of 99.85% at 5.355[Formula: see text]GHz. A prototype is fabricated using standard PCB technology and experimental validation is conducted in an anechoic chamber to verify the simulated results. The sensor design incorporates an analytical diaphragm layer between two substrates, demonstrating the ability to detect minor shifts in pressure with an average sensitivity of 2080[Formula: see text]MHz/mm. Key sensor characteristics include a high quality factor of 49.28 and a substantial Figure of Merit of 43.45. The linear behavior of the sensor is quantified through curve fitting, showing good agreement with the simulated sensitivity. The designed MM absorber exhibits merit such as perfect absorptivity, linear sensitivity, narrow bandwidth, high Q-factor, and a substantial Figure of Merit, making it a strong contender for pressure sensing applications.

title: Infection-osteogenesis crosstalk on TiO2 nanotube surfaces: mechanisms and synergistic design strategies
abstract: Titanium dioxide nanotubes (TNTs) fabricated via anodization have emerged as a versatile platform for surface modification of orthopedic and dental implants, owing to their tunable nanotopography and excellent potential for multifunctional biofunctionalization. However, the concurrent challenges of implant-associated bacterial infection and insufficient osseointegration remain formidable obstacles in clinical practice. Rather than being independent processes, bacterial infection and bone regeneration are intimately coupled through a complex signaling network—a concept increasingly recognized as the “infection-osteogenesis crosstalk.” We begin with how TNT morphology—nanotube diameter above all—differentially steers osteoblast behavior and bacterial adhesion, and how the initial protein corona and immune microenvironment set the infection-to-bone-healing trajectory. From signaling, we move to the pathways behind infection-driven osteogenic suppression: the core signaling pathways through which bacterial virulence factors suppress osteogenesis, including TLR-mediated NF-κB activation, RANKL/OPG imbalance-driven osteoclastogenesis, and biofilm hypoxia-induced metabolic reprogramming. We then look at how macrophages (M1/M2 polarization, NLRP3 inflammasome), neutrophils (NETosis), and T cells shape the host response to infection and bone repair. We close with current synergistic des…

title: Communicating the business of architecture: how a global architecture firm mediates design and business through social media
abstract: Purpose The article examines how a globally recognised architecture firm uses social media to mediate between design considerations and the commercial, institutional and professional constraints of practice. Design/methodology/approach The study involved qualitative content analysis and multimodal analysis of firm-authored posts by Snøhetta on Instagram, LinkedIn and Facebook. The dataset covers September 2023 to October 2024 and comprises 345 leading images with their captions and a gallery subset of 75 posts. We use inductive coding and multimodal analysis to understand how these posts demonstrate symbolic capital. Findings Images posted by Snøhetta are predominantly used to communicate design ideas; written captions are used to integrate business themes. Recurring alignments between image and caption suggest a consistent division of labour between the two modes wherein design is carried visually, business is carried textually. We describe this as a multimodal compartmentalisation of design and business. Originality/value The article brings a multimodal lens to understanding symbolic capital in architectural practice, showing that the separation of design and business ideas across image and caption supports a firm's aesthetic authority while simultaneously conducting commercial communication. It contributes the concept of multimodal compartmentalisation and an analytical appr…

title: Pengembangan Landing Page Carenesia: Implementasi UI/UX Design dalam Program Magang MSIB VINIX7 Batch 3
abstract: Proyek magang ini berfokus pada pengembangan landing page Carenesia sebagai keluaran akhir dari peran Junior Web UI/UX Designer dalam Program MSIB VINIX7 Batch 3. Seluruh kegiatan magang dilakukan secara daring melalui sesi briefing mingguan, modul studi independen, dan diskusi kelompok. Tujuan proyek ini adalah menerapkan prinsip UI/UX dalam pembuatan landing page modern, fungsional, dan berpusat pada pengguna untuk platform layanan kesehatan digital yang memiliki konsep serupa Halodoc. Desain akhir menonjolkan kejelasan informasi, kemudahan penggunaan, dan konsistensi visual, serta mengikuti alur kerja profesional seperti riset, wireframing, pembuatan prototipe, dan iterasi berdasarkan umpan balik. Hasilnya menunjukkan keberhasilan integrasi teori UI/UX dari kampus dengan praktik desain industri

title: Green synthesized plant mediated zinc oxide nanoparticles as potential nano phytotherapeutic agents for reactive oxygen species driven anticancer activity in HepG2 liver cancer cells
abstract: Green nanotechnology has emerged as a promising approach for the sustainable synthesis of metal oxide nanoparticles with potential applications in cancer therapy. In this study, aqueous extracts of Galinsoga parviflora (GP), Ageratum conyzoides (AC), and Argemone mexicana (AM) were employed as green agents for the biosynthesis of zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO-NPs). Characterization confirmed the formation of phase-pure, crystalline ZnO-NPs with a hexagonal wurtzite structure and predominantly spherical morphology. The mean particle sizes were 12.33 ± 5.58 nm (GP-ZnO), 12.05 ± 4.51 nm (AM-ZnO), and 10.32 ± 1.98 nm (AC-ZnO), with the overall observed size range of 5–36 nm. Zeta potentials ranging from −8.2 to −8.6 mV indicated weak electrostatic stabilization and a tendency for some aggregation, as observed in FE-SEM images. FT-IR confirmed ZnO formation with residual surface-associated plant-derived constituents, while XRD exhibited characteristic reflections corresponding to the (100), (002), (101), (102), (103), (110), and (112) crystal planes of wurtzite ZnO. The biosynthesized ZnO-NPs demonstrated favorable biocompatibility, exhibiting minimal haemolysis and negligible cytotoxicity against normal THLE-2 liver cells. GP-ZnO, AM-ZnO, and AC-ZnO-NPs exhibited concentration-dependent cytotoxicity against HepG2 carcinoma cells, with IC 50 values of 60.25 ± 3.2, 68.35 ± 3.4, and 7…

title: The effects of long-term residues of poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) mulch film on soil microbial communities and tobacco growth
Tipología de ingenios azucareros por eficiencia en planta basada en pérdidas de sacarosa
abstract: The sugar agribusiness requires tools that enable comparison of mill performance and focus actions to reduce in-plant sucrose losses. This study aimed to construct a typology of Mexican sugar mills based on indicators of sucrose losses and factory performance. The research was conducted in Mexico by analyzing secondary information from 46 mills observed in 10 harvests (2012/13-2021 and 2022), which was processed and synthesized in 2025. The base was collapsed at the mill level using the median by variable and standardized with Z-scores. Principal component analysis was applied to integrate four dimensions: sucrose losses, quality and technological potential of cane and juice, sucrose extraction from juice and industrial yield, and operational-energy intensity in the plant. The dimensional scores were used to perform hierarchical clustering (Ward’s method and Euclidean distance), which allowed the identification of six types of mills. Types IV and V concentrated the best overall performance by combining high quality/potential and higher extraction-yield with lower operational-energy intensity; Bellavista and Atencingo stand out. Types I and II showed lags associated with low quality/potential and lower extraction-yield; type VI presented high losses and operational-energy intensity despite relatively high potential, and type III corresponded to the El Carmen mill as an atypical …

title: Genome-wide characterization of the RCI2 gene family reveals conserved protein features and divergent responses to salt and osmotic stress in pea
abstract: Introduction Salinity and drought are major abiotic stresses limiting pea ( Pisum sativum L. ) growth and productivity. The RCI2 family has been implicated in plant responses to environmental stress, but its characteristics and potential roles in pea remain insufficiently understood. Methods Six PsRCI2 genes were identified and characterized using phylogenetic, gene structure, promoter, transcriptomic, quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR), and subcellular localization analyses. Results PsRCI2-2 to PsRCI2-5 formed a gene cluster on chromosome 3, whereas no clear intragenomic collinear pairs were detected. Most PsRCI2 proteins showed conserved sequence and transmembrane features, whereas PsRCI2-6 exhibited distinct structural characteristics. Promoter analysis revealed diverse stress- and hormone-responsive cis-acting elements among family members. Transcriptome analysis revealed differential transcriptional responses to salt and PEG-induced osmotic stress. Notably, PsRCI2-2 , PsRCI2-3 , and PsRCI2-5 were induced by both treatments, and their expression patterns were validated by qRT-PCR. These three proteins also exhibited fluorescence patterns largely overlapping with the ER marker in Nicotiana benthamiana . Discussion The pea RCI2 family displays conserved structural features but divergent transcriptional responses. PsRCI2-2 , PsRCI2-3 , and PsRCI2-5 are promising candidates f…

title: Intersectional masculinism: how patriarchal power adapts across regime changes in Indonesia
abstract: Globally, women’s political empowerment remains a resistant frontier of gender equality, particularly in sub-national executive positions. This study introduces intersectional masculinism as a theoretical framework to explain the durability of women’s political exclusion in executive positions, moving beyond static patriarchy accounts. Drawing on 6-month ethnographic fieldwork in Bone Regency, Indonesia, a site maintaining an absolute male executive monopoly for seven decades despite meeting legislative quotas, we identify three adaptive configurations of masculine dominance: feudal-aristocratic (kingdom era), military-bureaucratic (New Order), and capitalist-electoral (Reform era). Synthesizing Foucault’s analytics of discontinuity and technologies of the self with Crenshaw’s intersectionality, we demonstrate that Bugis siri’ (honor/shame) operates as an intersectional technology of the self that disciplines women’s political subjectivity through spatial confinement, internalized self-regulation, and differential operation across class and lineage. Our findings reveal a pattern of “discontinuity without transformation”: while political regimes shift radically from kingdom to republic, from authoritarianism to democracy, male executive monopoly persists through reconfiguration of privilege-conferring intersections (lineage, military affiliation, economic capital). This study co…

title: Effect of Bentonite amendment on Lead and Cadmium accumulation and plant 2 growth indicators
abstract: The objective of this study was to determine the effect of bentonite on lead (Pb) and cadmium (Cd) accumulation in Indian mustard (Brassica juncea), as well as to evaluate the growth parameters of plants grown in soil contaminated with different levels of Pb and Cd. In this study, a pot experiment was conducted using a (3 × 3) factorial arrangement consisting of three levels of lead (10, 100, and 200 mg kg⁻¹), three levels of cadmium (5, 15, and 25 mg kg⁻¹), two bentonite application rates (25% and 50%), and an untreated control. The results showed significant differences (P ≤ 0.05) in metal concentrations in roots and leaves, as well as in growth parameters such as fresh weight and plant height. A progressive increase in Pb and Cd concentrations was observed in both roots and leaves with increasing contamination levels. In contrast, the application of bentonite at 50% significantly decreased metal concentrations; Pb concentration in roots decreased from 75.03 to 41.20 mg kg⁻¹, while Cd concentration at the highest contamination level decreased from 0.29 to 0.19 mg kg⁻¹, respectively. The results also indicated significant reductions in shoot and root biomass under high Pb and Cd concentrations. In the control treatment, fresh shoot weight was 204.67 g, which decreased by 62.53% under 200 mg Pb kg⁻¹ + 25% bentonite and by 61.56% under 25 mg Cd kg⁻¹ + 25% bentonite. Fresh root w…

title: Strategic leadership at the limits of care: a discursive sensemaking perspective on virtual presenteeism in remote work
abstract: Purpose This study examines how managers construct and communicate understandings of illness, availability, responsibility and recovery. Drawing on discursive leadership and organizational sensemaking, it conceptualizes leadership as a process of meaning construction and explores how this process shapes the emergence of virtual presenteeism as a workplace norm. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts a qualitative, discourse-informed interpretive design. Open-ended survey data were collected from 88 managers in the Turkish private sector. The analysis combines reflexive thematic analysis with interpretive discourse analysis, focusing on both linguistic patterns and the broader discourses of professionalism and remote work. The analysis examines how managers use language to frame care, performance, responsibility, and recovery, and how these framings shape expectations regarding employee availability. Findings Three leadership vocabularies are identified: Continuity and Reliability, Individual Judgment and Self-Responsibility, and Care and Legitimated Withdrawal. These vocabularies show how managers interpret digital cues, construct narratives of availability, and normalize virtual presenteeism through framing, normalization, and identity regulation. Across these vocabularies, managers establish different expectations regarding availability, responsibility, and recovery, sh…

title: EFEKTIVITAS LABORATORIUM VIRTUAL PHET TERHADAP PEMAHAMAN KONSEP LISTRIK DINAMIS PESERTA DIDIK MTS ALKHAIRAAT BIROMARU
abstract: Understanding dynamic electricity is important because students often experience difficulties in understanding the relationships among electric current, voltage, and resistance in series and parallel circuits. This study aimed to analyze changes in students’ conceptual understanding before and after learning with the Physics Education Technology (PhET) virtual laboratory supported by student worksheets (LKPD), test the statistical significance of these changes, and determine the magnitude of improvement. The study employed a quantitative approach using a one-group pretest-posttest design without a comparison group. The participants were 20 eighth-grade students at MTs Alkhairaat Biromaru. Data were collected through conceptual understanding tests administered before and after instruction and an observation checklist assessing implementation. The data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, a paired-samples t-test, and N-Gain. The results showed that the mean score increased from 43.75 to 53.75, with a statistically significant difference (t(19) = −5.210; p < 0.001). Cohen’s dz was 1.17, indicating a large effect size, whereas the N-Gain of 0.18 was categorized as low. All instructional stages were implemented as planned. Thus, students’ scores increased following the intervention; however, the effectiveness of PhET supported by LKPD cannot be conclusively established withou…

title: Iran’s Proxy Networks as Instruments of Regional Power: Ideology, Strategy, and Consequences in the Middle East
abstract: Since the 1979 Islamic Revolution, Iran has strategically co-opted a network of non-state armed actors across the Middle East. While existing scholarship itemizes these linkages, multifariously termed “proxy forces” or “the axis of resistance”, the constitutive logic underlying such alliances is undertheorized. This article maintains that Iran’s proxy networks are not opportunistic but establish a comprehensible grand strategy constituted by ideological affinity, emphasized threat perception, and asymmetric deterrence calculus. Based on multi-case study methodology including Lebanon, Iraq, Syria, and Yemen, and proceeding from foreign policy analysis and proxy warfare theory, the study scrutinizes the political, ideological, and financial mechanisms reinforcing these ties within Iran’s post-revolutionary security doctrine and its rivalry with the United States and Israel. The findings reveal that proxy deployment represents an asymmetric advantage authorizing power projection while diminishing direct military contact.
venue: International Journal of Politics and Security

title: Impact of higher-order interactions on dynamics of plant-pollinator-herbivore systems
abstract: Complex interactions exist among plants, pollinators, and herbivores, involving not only predation and mutualism but also higher-order interactions. This study devotes to exploring how higher-order interactions between pollinators and herbivores affect the dynamics of such systems. An interference parameter is introduced to characterize the interaction. Qualitative analysis is conducted to investigate the existence and stability of various ecological equilibria, and to reveal bifurcation phenomena such as transcritical and hopf bifurcations. Sensitivity analysis confirms the significant effect of the interference parameter. Theoretical analyses and numerical simulations reveal the following facts: (1) herbivore interference increases the extinction risk of pollinators while exerting limited impact on the plant population; (2) interference can induce transitions between oscillatory and stable coexistence states; (3) strong mutualistic interactions promote pollinator persistence yet can destabilize the coexistence equilibrium, and in contrast, a low intrinsic growth rate of plants facilitates three-species coexistence, though it does not enhance equilibrium stability; (4) higher-order interactions affect the stability of the system and cause complex dynamical behaviors.

title: LoGA: Loop-Carried Graph Attention Based Looped Vision Transformers for Fine-Grained Plant Disease Classification
abstract: Fine-grained plant disease classification requires separating classes of the same crop that often differ only in small, sparse lesion patterns. Looped Vision Transformers (LoopViTs) obtain depth by applying a small stack of weight-tied blocks repeatedly, yet each block rebuilds its attention graph from scratch at every iteration, although the same block has just computed a graph over the same tokens. We propose LoGA, a looped vision transformer with Loop-Carried Graph Attention, in which the attention graph of each block at iteration $t$ is biased by the graph the same block produced at iteration $t-1$, used as a tempered prior. In its log-prob form the update $A_t \propto \exp(QK^\top/\sqrt{d})\odot A_{t-1}^{\gamma}$ is, when the floor is inactive, equivalent to attending with a geometrically discounted sum of past query-key logits; a flash-compatible qk variant carries one step of raw logits. LoGA adds 24 scalars to a 9.91\,M-parameter model and reduces exactly to vanilla LoopViT at initialisation. We also study a parameter-free graph-stability signal $\Delta_t$ and show that, under label smoothing, predictive entropy stays near 0.671 nats, so a common entropy-exit threshold is never reached. Trained from scratch, LoGA-logprob reaches 99.78%, 94.2%, 98.6% and 99.53% top-1 accuracy on the held-out splits of PlantVillage, PlantDoc, Cassava and Plant Pathology 2020, versus 98.11…

title: Seed-dressing treatments improve wheat germination and seedling growth under contrasting sowing conditions in a rice–wheat rotation system
abstract: Introduction Delayed sowing after rice harvest increasingly compromises wheat establishment and yield formation across rice–wheat rotation regions. Seed dressing may alleviate these constraints, but its effectiveness under humid, late-sown conditions and contrasting soil-cover practices remains insufficiently understood. Methods A two-year, two-factor split-plot field experiment was conducted in Sichuan Province, China. Soil-covered and uncovered surface sowing were assigned to the main plots, and eight seed-dressing regimes were assigned to the subplots. Treatments included Coolas, brassinolide, and Ju Chuan, applied individually or in combination. Germination traits, field emergence, seedling morphology, root architecture, population growth, yield components, and grain yield were evaluated. Results Seed-Dressing Treatments significantly improved seed germination and early stand establishment. Compared with the untreated control (CK), Ju Chuan combined with brassinolide and half-rate Coolas (T J+B+50%C ) increased germination percentage, germination index, and vigor index by 12.89%, 96.12%, and 22.88%, respectively. Coolas alone (T C ) produced the greatest improvement in seedling vigor index, which was 97.69% higher than that of CK. T C also promoted root system development, crop growth rate, and dry matter accumulation. Soil cover shortened field emergence time and increased…

title: Evaluation of the Anti-Inflammatory, Antidepressant and Antioxidant Activity of Schweinf. ex Hiern Fadogia ancylantha Plant Leaf Extracts
abstract: Fadogia ancylantha is an indigenous African medicinal plant widely used in traditional medicine for immune boosting and the treatment of infections and inflammation. This study investigated the phytochemical composition, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antidepressant activities of ethanol and methanol leaf extracts of F. ancylantha. Phytochemical analyses were conducted using standard chemical screening and spectrophotometric methods. Antioxidant activity was evaluated using the DPPH assay whilst anti-inflammatory activity was done using the carrageenan-induced paw oedema model in rats and the cyclooxygenase assay. Antidepressant activity was assessed using the tail suspension, forced swim, and sucrose preference tests. Both ethanol and methanol extracts contained saponins, tannins, flavonoids, and phenolic compounds. The ethanol extract exhibited higher TPC (0.3914 ± 1.8 mg GAE/g) than the methanol extract (0.2183 ± 1.4 mg GAE/g). Similarly, the ethanol extract showed a higher TFC (0.27373 ± 1.31 mg QE/g) than the methanol extract (0.26587 ± 1.31 mg QE/g). The ethanol extract demonstrated concentration-dependent DPPH radical scavenging activity comparable to ascorbic acid. The extract produced dose-dependent anti-inflammatory effects, with higher doses exhibiting greater activity than lower doses. The extract also reduced COX-1 activity in a concentration-dependent manner,…

title: Making Peer Review More Sustainable: Let Technology Do The Heavy Lifting
Medicaid Work Requirements and Behavioral Health: Risks and Opportunities for Peer Support
The Inequality-Energy Nexus: The Distribution of Energy Poverty and Renewable Transitions
abstract: This study looks at energy poverty from social, economic, environmental and infrastructure perspectives. Energy poverty is shown to stem from economic inequality due to income differences affecting the availability, affordability and reliability of energy sources in developing countries. In addition, this has led to negative impacts on the environment and human health. This study uses regression analysis to understand energy poverty and income inequality. The regression is done using the Panel-Corrected Standard Errors (PCSE) and Feasible Generalised Least Squares (FGLS) techniques. The results show that increasing public investment and renewable energy consumption will reduce energy poverty. However, urbanisation and income inequality will increase energy poverty. Innovative and inclusive approaches are recommended to ensure that sustainable energy is available for all to boost long-term socio-economic growth globally.

title: О приведении энергии деформации гемитропных тел к каноническому виду методом Якоби
abstract: Гемитропные тела представляют собой класс микрополярных сред, характеризующийся инвариантностью определяющих тензоров относительно произвольных поворотов и изменением при зеркальных отражениях пространства. Приведение квадратичной формы энергии деформации таких материалов к каноническому виду является необходимой задачей для анализа устойчивости, идентификации материальных параметров и построения эффективных вычислительных моделей в механике деформируемого твердого тела. Исследование выполнено в рамках линейной теории микрополярной упругости. Используется аппарат линейной алгебры и теории квадратичных форм. Приведение квадратичной формы энергии деформации к каноническому виду осуществляется методом Якоби, основанным на вычислении угловых миноров матрицы квадратичной формы. Положительная определенность энергии деформации проверяется посредством критерия Сильвестра. Сформулирована система определяющих неравенств для девяти материальных констант, обеспечивающих положительную определенность энергии деформации. Показано, что метод Якоби позволяет объединить процедуру приведения квадратичной формы с проверкой физической корректности материала по критерию Сильвестра. Hemitropic solids are a class of micropolar media whose constitutive tensors are invariant under arbitrary rotations but vary under spatial mirror reflections. Reducing the strain energy quadratic form of such materials t…

title: Study on fractal characteristics of fragmentation and energy dissipation of fissured sandstone under impact loading
MOEDO-Based Multi-Objective Optimization of Laser Remelting for Surface Roughness, Microhardness, and Energy Consumption
abstract: In the context of low-carbon and energy-efficient manufacturing, this study investigated laser remelting of 35CrMo/Fe45 cladding layers to improve surface quality and microhardness while reducing energy consumption. Laser power, scanning speed, and overlap ratio were selected as the main process parameters, while surface roughness, microhardness, and electrical energy consumption during laser-on processing were taken as the optimization objectives. Based on the experimental data obtained using an enhanced Latin hypercube sampling design, a surrogate model was constructed. The multi-objective exponential distribution optimizer (MOEDO) was then used to generate a Pareto-optimal solution set, from which CRITIC-TOPSIS selected the optimal process parameters. Relative to the as-clad condition, the surface roughness of the cladding layer decreased from 8.56 μm to 0.789 μm, while the microhardness increased from 536 HV0.5 to 625.3 HV0.5. Compared with the reference condition, the optimized process reduced surface roughness by 39.6%, increased microhardness by 31.5%, and reduced electrical energy consumption during laser-on processing by 55.7%. The proposed approach provides a practical basis for balancing surface-quality improvement, hardness enhancement, and energy saving in energy-efficient laser remelting of cladding layers.

title: Natural resource intensity and financial distress dynamics: an empirical investigation across South Asian energy firms
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the relationship between natural resource inefficiency, measured by the Natural Resource Intensity Ratio (NRIR), and financial distress among energy firms in South Asia. This study further examines the moderating role of firm size and the country-specific effects of NRIR in Bangladesh, India and Pakistan. Design/methodology/approach This study uses 300 firm-year observations (2015–2024) covering all 30 listed energy firms in the three markets that satisfy the continuous-listing and resource-cost disclosure criteria. Financial distress is measured through Altman’s Z-score and Ohlson’s O-score. Estimation uses fixed effects, cluster-robust variance estimation, PCSE, Driscoll–Kraay standard errors, the system generalised method of moments and further robustness checks. Findings Higher NRIR is associated with lower Z-scores and higher O-scores, indicating increased financial distress. Firm size moderates this relationship, and the NRIR–distress slope varies across markets: the total marginal effect is steepest in Pakistan (−21.44), followed by India (−13.59) and Bangladesh (−9.79). Research limitations/implications This study covers listed fuel and power sector companies in three South Asian countries, so caution is required in generalising the results to other sectors or economies. Practical implications The results of this study indicate that im…
venue: International Journal of Energy Sector Management

title: Hybrid hydroinformatic assessment of groundwater-storage depletion in Saudi Arabia (2002–2024): integrating GRACE/GRACE-FO gravimetry, land-surface modeling, and dependence-aware machine learning
abstract: Introduction Saudi Arabia meets most of its water demand from largely non-renewable aquifers, yet the magnitude and spatial organization of storage depletion and the expression of interannual hydroclimate in the storage record have rarely been examined within one baseline-benchmarked framework. Methods We integrate 22 valid years (2002–2024) of GRACE/GRACE-FO mascon gravimetry with GLDAS-2.1 surface storage; CHIRPS precipitation; and MODIS vegetation, temperature, evapotranspiration, and land-cover observations on a 0.5° grid and decompose each cell’s groundwater-storage (GWS) anomaly into a Theil–Sen trend and a detrended residual. Results Kingdom-mean GWS declined at –0.91 cm yr -1 (95% CI –0.93 to –0.88; –19.8 cm in total, ≈4.3 × 10 2 km 3 , range 2.5−4.3 × 10 2 km 3 across surface-storage treatments), with a median detrended residual variance fraction of 4.3%. Under leave-one-year-out validation, five machine-learning models do not exceed a climatological baseline for the residual (best R 2 = –0.02; 0.05 with fold-wise detrending), whose magnitude (≈1.5 cm RMSE) is comparable to GRACE annual-mean uncertainty. A rate-based Pettitt test detects no Kingdom-wide change point in the depletion rate (p = 0.96). Regional interrupted-time-series and difference-in-differences tests regarding the 2016–2018 agricultural reforms show a post-2018 deceleration over the north-western wheat…

title: A matrix approach to revenue disclosure as a tool to increase the investment attractiveness of fast-growing companies
abstract: Subject. Increasing the investment attractiveness of fast-growing companies. Objectives. Development of a scientifically based approach to improving accounting support for assessing the investment attractiveness of fast-growing companies through additional revenue disclosures in financial statements. Methods. The methodological basis of the research is based on the integrated application of a systematic approach, accounting methods, as well as deductive and inductive methods used to develop a uniform matrix structure for revenue disclosure. Results. A matrix for revenue disclosure by business segment of a fast-growing company has been developed and applied as part of a practical case using the example of the Yandex ICPAO. The proposed matrix has advantages both for the company integrating it into its activities and for potential investors. Conclusions. In the context of fast-growing companies, the matrix will increase information transparency, which will eventually lead to an increase in investment attractiveness. The matrix will allow investors to make more accurate forecasts about the future development of the company and make more informed investment decisions.

title: Financial accountability and revenue paying behavior of citizens in local governments in Ghana: the role of trust and information technology
abstract: Purpose This study examines the direct effect of financial accountability on citizens' revenue-paying behavior in local governments in Ghana, as well as the mediating role of trust and the moderating role of information technology in this relationship. Design/methodology/approach Grounded in stewardship theory and the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT), the study employs a quantitative survey research design and uses Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to analyze data collected from 472 citizens across four local governments in Ghana. Findings The results show that financial accountability positively influence citizens' paying behavior of taxes and levies. Also, while information technology significantly enhances and moderate the link between financial accountability and citizen revenue paying behavior, trust is found to partially mediate this relationship. Research limitations/implications This scope of the study is limited by its reliance on self-reported data, which may result in response bias and social desirability effects. The representativeness of the sample may have been compromised as a result of the electronic survey's exclusion of individuals who did not have access to electronic media or internet. The generalisability of the study is limited by its focus on only four of the twenty-nine local governments within the res…

title: Developing an Oscillatory Flow Packed Column for Intensified Sequential Metal Extraction from Spent Lithium-Ion Battery Leachate: Process Optimization and Environmental Assessment
abstract: Abstract An intensified solvent extraction process using an oscillatory flow packed column (OFPC) was developed for sequential recovery of Mn, Co, and Ni from lithium-ion battery (LIB) leachate streams. Hydrodynamic feasibility was first evaluated to establish the operating window of the OFPC, followed by single-factor experiments and response surface methodology (RSM) to systematically investigate the effects of pH, phase ratio, and residence time on extraction performance. Under optimal conditions, extraction efficiencies exceeding 99% were achieved for Mn, Co, and Ni with high separation factors, confirming efficient sequential metal partitioning in a continuous intensified system. Experimental results showed good agreement with model predictions, validating the robustness of the RSM-based optimization strategy. A Waste Reduction Algorithm-based environmental assessment was further conducted to benchmark the OFPC process against a conventional mixer–settler configuration. Owing to enhanced mass-transfer efficiency and reduced energy demand, the OFPC process achieved a 37.6% reduction in total potential environmental impact (PEI) output rate and a 50.8% decrease in PEI generation rate. Overall, the coupling of oscillatory hydrodynamics with packed column intensification enables high-efficiency sequential recovery of critical metals while significantly reducing environmental b…

title: Wound-Relevant Electric Fields and Directional Keratinocyte Migration in Skin Repair: A Preclinical Systematic Review
abstract: Skin wounds generate small natural electric fields. Researchers have long proposed that these fields help guide repair of the epidermis. Cell movement guided by an electric field is called electrotaxis, also known as galvanotaxis. This review asked whether wound-relevant electric fields direct epithelial or keratinocyte migration in preclinical models. We searched the PubMed biomedical literature database and Web of Science using broad terms related to wound bioelectricity. A second search added electrotaxis and galvanotaxis. We also checked Google Scholar, records indexed in MEDLINE (Medical Literature Analysis and Retrieval System Online), and papers suggested by colleagues. Eligible studies measured migration direction in keratinocyte, epidermal, or skin-wound models. Two reviewers assessed risk of bias using a tailored Office of Health Assessment and Translation approach. One author screened titles and abstracts. A second author assessed full texts. Two authors divided the extraction work. Each study was extracted once by one author. Screening and extraction were not performed in duplicate. Thirty-one studies were included. At the study level, 20 were classified as cathodal. Five were anodal. Three were classified as toward the wound center. Three were not polarity-specific. Most numerical field strengths were between 10 and 400 mV/mm. Risk of bias was rated as some concern…

title: Cognitive changes following rTMS, tACS, and their combination in bipolar II disorder: an exploratory study integrating degree centrality and individualized electric field modeling
Coping with tropical cyclone Fani’s impact on housing: roof repair as a strategy
abstract: Purpose A tropical cyclone produces high wind speeds, impacting houses, particularly the semi-engineered and non-engineered types. This paper aims to understand how people in Puri district of Odisha, India, where approximately 278,000 houses were affected by tropical cyclone Fani in 2019, coped with its impact in the immediate context and over a period of time. It explores the government strategy of distributing polythene sheets for damaged house’s roof, those households’ experiences with such an arrangement, and in ways the house damage assessment is interlinked with “repair” as a strategy. Design/methodology/approach This is a qualitative study that follows a case study method. It uses data collected from the field with secondary-sourced data such as reports and documents. Fieldwork was conducted in four coastal blocks of the most affected Puri district. In total, 14 focused group discussions (FGDs) were conducted in 10 villages and 5 personal interviews with key informants to triangulate findings derived from the FGDs. Findings The study finds that although, in the immediate context, the polythene sheets were helpful for cyclone-affected families to return to their own houses, they lasted much longer than expected and, in some cases, turned out to be permanent ones. Further, in the absence of clear guidelines on criteria for conducting damage assessment, the process was repe…

title: PENERAPAN MODEL PEMBELAJARAN PROBLEM BASED LEARNING UNTUK MENINGKATKAN HASIL BELAJAR PENDIDIKAN PANCASILA SISWA KELAS IV UPTD SD NEGERI 075062 DOLI-DOLI
abstract: This study was motivated by the low learning outcomes of fourth-grade students in Pancasila Education at UPTD SD Negeri 075062 Doli-Doli. In the pre-cycle assessment, only 4 of 19 students (21.05%) met the Learning Objective Achievement Criteria (KKTP). This study aimed to describe the implementation of the Problem-Based Learning (PBL) model and improve students’ learning outcomes through its application. The study employed classroom action research based on the Kemmis and McTaggart model and was conducted in two cycles. Each cycle consisted of planning, action, observation, and reflection. The participants were 19 fourth-grade students. Data were collected through observation, learning outcome tests, and documentation, then analyzed descriptively. The results showed that the average teacher activity score increased from 56.73% in Cycle I to 79.81% in Cycle II, while student activity increased from 59.71% to 80.59%. The average learning outcome score rose from 48.16 in the pre-cycle to 65.26 in Cycle I and 87.37 in Cycle II. Classical learning mastery also increased from 21.05% to 52.63% and 89.47%, respectively. Therefore, implementing PBL can improve the learning process and learning outcomes in Pancasila Education among fourth-grade students. title: PENGEMBANGAN BUKU CERITA ANAK BERBASIS KEARIFAN LOKAL PADA MATA PELAJARAN BAHASA INDONESIA KELAS V UPTD SD NEGERI 074044 DAHANA BAWODESOLO
abstract: The availability of contextual learning materials grounded in local wisdom is essential for supporting literacy and introducing cultural identity to elementary school students. This study aimed to develop a local wisdom-based children's storybook for Grade V Indonesian language learning at UPTD SD Negeri 074044 Dahana Bawodesolo and to evaluate its validity, practicality, and students' learning outcomes after using the product. This study employed a Research and Development (R&D) approach using the 4D model (Define, Design, Develop, and Disseminate). The participants were 20 fifth-grade students, comprising six students in a small-group trial and 14 students in a field trial. Data were collected through observations, interviews, expert validation questionnaires, student response questionnaires, and learning outcome tests. The data were analyzed using descriptive quantitative techniques. Following revision, the book received validation scores of 100% for content, language, and design/media, all categorized as highly valid. Student responses reached 81% in the small-group trial and 97% in the field trial, indicating practical and highly practical levels, respectively. The average learning outcome scores were 79 in the small-group trial and 87 in the field trial, with 100% of students in both groups meeting the Minimum Competency Criterion (KKM) of 75. In conclusion, the developed…

title: Highly Emissive NIR-II Unimolecular Micelles via a Core–Cap Synthetic Strategy for Deep-Tissue Imaging and Image-Guided Surgery
abstract: Abstract High-performance fluorescence imaging in the second near-infrared (NIR-II, 1000–1700 nm) window holds promise for deep-tissue optical diagnostics. However, simultaneously achieving high fluorescence quantum yields (QYs) and ultrasmall dimensions in physiological aqueous environments remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we report a de novo core–cap synthetic strategy to construct highly emissive, renal-clearable NIR-II fluorophores based on a unimolecular micelle architecture. By integrating a rigid, donor–acceptor–donor (D–A–D) hydrophobic core containing orthogonal axial and lateral steric shielding networks with a hydrophilic polyethylene glycol (PEG) outer cap, we successfully suppress water-induced nonradiative decay and intermolecular aggregation-induced quenching without compromising lateral conjugation. Molecular dynamics simulations and experimental characterizations reveal that these amphiphilic structures self-assemble into highly monodisperse unimolecular micelles featuring an ultrasmall hydrodynamic diameter of ∼5 nm. The optimized fluorophore exhibits a peak NIR-II emission centered at 1034 nm with a high aqueous QY of 4.6%. Owing to their sub-5 nm dimensions, unimolecular micelles undergo dual renal and hepatic clearance pathways, circumventing the biosafety concerns of prolonged tissue retention typical of conventional nanoparticles. Capitalizing on th…

title: Sustainable desulfurization through coupled extraction-catalytic oxidation strategy: Mechanisms, materials, and process intensification
abstract: In response to the imperative for sustainable energy and environmental protection, ultra-deep desulfurization of fuels poses a critical challenge. Conventional hydrodesulfurization and emerging non-hydrogenation techniques face limitations in efficiency, economic viability, and ecological sustainability, particularly for refractory sulfur species. Among alternatives, extractive catalytic oxidative desulfurization (ECODS) has emerged as a prominent approach by integrating catalytic oxidation and liquid-phase extraction under mild conditions. It employs green solvents such as ionic liquids and deep eutectic solvents, along with recyclable heterogeneous catalysts (e.g., polyoxometalates and metal-organic frameworks). This review examines the reaction mechanisms-both radical and non-radical pathways-underpinning ECODS, alongside material design strategies for catalysts and sustainable solvents. We further evaluate process parameters and techno-economic factors critical for scalability. ECODS demonstrates high efficiency (typically >97% sulfur removal) and robust reusability, in alignment with green chemistry principles through minimized energy input, avoidance of hazardous reagents, and emphasis on atom economy and recyclability. This work underscores the potential of ECODS as a sustainable pathway toward ultra-clean fuels (sulfur content < 10 ppm) and outlines future directions fo…

title: Enacting strategy without authority: a conceptual model of strategy translation by middle academic leaders
abstract: Purpose The existing literature does not clearly specify how institutional strategy signals affect the local practices of middle academic leaders, particularly when they operate under conditions of professional autonomy and institutional constraint. This study provides a process-based model explaining how institutional strategy signals are translated into localized middle-management practices under conditions of professional autonomy and structural constraints. Design/methodology/approach This study employs an integrative theoretical approach drawing on strategy-as-practice, institutional complexity and middle-management perspectives to develop a recursive framework for strategy translation under institutional constraint and a set of propositions describing the relationships among signal multiplicity, interpretive ambiguity, dual positioning, institutional constraints and localized variation. Findings Middle academic leaders are positioned as actors who interpret, negotiate and enact institutional strategy signals through bounded, iterative translation processes shaped by dual accountability and structural constraint. The model demonstrates that institutional coherence can coexist with variation in local enactment and positions the ambiguity associated with policy implementation as a function of structure (i.e. the system) rather than communication (i.e. a lack of information o…

title: The relationship of autonomy with hybrid worker well-being and productivity - the mediating role of managerial culture
abstract: Purpose Knowledge work is extensively location-independent, making flexible work designs more common. However, organizations foster various practices regarding the level of autonomy and control, affecting employee well-being and productivity. To support strategic and operative work design, this paper aims to explain the relationship of autonomy with hybrid worker well-being and productivity, considering the mediating role of managerial culture. Design/methodology/approach This paper describes a quantitative survey featuring 1,057 respondents. It tests with a regression analysis a hypothesized model, in which the level of individual work autonomy, mediated by managerial culture, predicts well-being and productivity. Findings The analysis indicated that decision-making autonomy has a direct positive relationship with productivity. Furthermore, autonomy in working practices has a direct positive relationship with both well-being and productivity. Managerial culture mediates the relationship between decision-making autonomy and both outcome variables. Originality/value This paper provides empirical evidence of the relationship of autonomy with hybrid worker well-being and productivity. The academic value of this paper lies in the multiple dimensions of autonomy it addresses, yielding novel data on the outcomes in a comparative manner. As a pragmatic contribution, it provides input …

title: ANALISIS PERSEPSI GURU TERHADAP EFEKTIVITAS INSTRUMEN PENILAIAN FORMATIF DALAM PEMBELAJARAN PENDIDIKAN PANCASILA KELAS V SD NEGERI 071202 HELEZALULU
abstract: The urgency of this research lies in the importance of formative assessment for monitoring students’ learning progress and improving Pancasila Education in elementary schools. However, its implementation still faces challenges, including limited time, administrative workload, insufficient instrument variety, and suboptimal use of feedback. This study aims to analyze teachers’ perceptions of the effectiveness of formative assessment instruments, identify implementation barriers, and describe teachers’ efforts to overcome these challenges in Grade V at SD Negeri 071202 Helezalulu. This research employed a descriptive qualitative approach involving two Grade V teachers, one school principal, and four students as informants. Data were collected through observation, semi-structured interviews, and documentation, then analyzed using open coding, axial coding, and selective coding. Data trustworthiness was examined through source and technique triangulation. The findings indicate that teachers perceived formative assessment instruments positively because they helped monitor students’ understanding, identify learning difficulties, provide feedback, and determine instructional follow-up. The identified barriers were addressed through instrument simplification, careful planning, staged assessment, reflection, and teacher collaboration. The study concludes that formative assessment effect…

title: Effectiveness of Using the Six-Dimensional Strategy on Skill Performance of Selected Handball Skills and Development of Decision-Making Among Students
abstract: The purposes of this study are to examine the difference between pre-test and post-test results of students' skill performance in the selected handball skills after applying the 6 dimensional strategy, and to examine the contribution of the 6 dimensional strategy to improve the decision making skill of students. In addition, the study aims to find out whether there are differences between the six-dimensional strategy and the traditional teaching method in the development of the performance of the handball skills in the post-test. It also compares the results of these two methods of teaching on enhancing students decision making after the educational program. The researcher used the experimental method because of its appropriateness that has been considered in light of the nature and objective of the study. The research sample consisted of two physical education second year student sections at the College of Physical Education and Sports Sciences, University of Mosul and selected randomly. The experimental group was Section (C) and Control group was Section (Y). Prior to education program implementation, homogeneity and equivalence of the two groups was achieved. The researcher examined the approved handball curriculum of the second-year students in the first semester of the academic year and then developed an educational program based on the strategy of six dimensions. The prog…

title: Strategic digital transformation from digital value creation to business sustainability in SMEs
abstract: Purpose Digital transformation presents substantial opportunities for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) but also necessitates strategic changes. Motivated by value creation, it involves delivering digital offerings through innovative business models. From a resource-based view (RBV), digital transformation creates competitive advantage. However, realizing this potential requires strategies that combine digital technologies with business objectives. Design/methodology/approach This empirical analysis is based on data from 203 Finnish SMEs. The study examines the connection between digital value creation, via digital collaboration and digital channels, and business sustainability, positing that relationships can be mediated through digital strategy measurements. Findings Digital value creation alone does not necessarily lead to positive sustainability outcomes for SMEs. Creating value in digital settings is more complex; however, when combined with digital strategy measurements, its positive effects on the social, environmental, and economic dimensions of sustainability are conveyed. Research limitations/implications The results identify digital strategy measurement as a key capability mediating digital value creation and business sustainability in SMEs. By adopting a RBV lens, this study advances the understanding of the digital transformation–sustainability nexus. Pract…

title: ANALISIS IMPLEMENTASI INSTRUMEN PENILAIAN UNTUK MENGUKUR SIKAP KEDISIPLINAN PESERTA DIDIK DI SEKOLAH DASAR NEGERI 071206 TALUZUSUA
abstract: Discipline assessment in elementary schools is essential for systematically monitoring students’ character development and providing a basis for continuous guidance. However, effective assessment depends not only on the availability of instruments but also on consistent implementation and the appropriate use of assessment results. This study aimed to describe the implementation of discipline attitude assessment instruments and the disciplinary behavior of students at SD Negeri 071206 Taluzusua. The study employed a qualitative approach with a descriptive method. The informants consisted of two homeroom teachers and one subject teacher selected purposively based on their direct involvement in teaching and attitude assessment. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, observations, and documentation, then analyzed through data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing. Data credibility was strengthened through source, technique, and time triangulation. The findings indicated that instrument implementation involved three stages: planning, assessment, and utilization of results. Teachers used observation sheets and attitude assessment journals to assess punctuality, compliance with rules, and responsibility for completing assignments. Students generally demonstrated fairly good discipline, although their behavior was not yet consistent across all indicators. Assessment…
