title: A Two-Stage Distributionally Robust Restoration Strategy for Typhoon-Affected Distribution Networks Using a Fuzzy Bayesian Network
abstract: Extreme typhoons cause correlated distribution-line outages and disrupt access for restoration resources. This paper formulates a two-stage framework linking state-conditioned fragility, fuzzy Bayesian evidence updating, tail-aware scenario reduction, distributionally robust planning, and coordinated restoration. A reproducible physics-informed Monte Carlo experiment evaluates source-to-bus connectivity and heuristic crew staging over 2,000 paired events generated from a common state-conditioned hazard model. Prior- and posterior-informed staging select the same crew bases, and both yield a mean unserved energy of 29.612 MWh. Energy-limited local mobile storage reduces the mean to 28.173 MWh, a reduction of 4.86%. Bayesian updating changes the conditional source-disconnection risks of Buses 17 and 30 from 0.665 to 0.974 and from 0.590 to 0.945, respectively. The paired design holds fault, repair, access, and load realizations identical across policies, thereby isolating the effect of risk updating on deployment decisions. The results demonstrate stable staging under the updated risk distribution and quantify the energy contribution of local mobile storage. Together, the formulation and reproducible mechanism experiment establish a traceable numerical basis for studying the interaction between risk information, resource access, and energy availability in typhoon restoration.
venue: International Journal of Modeling, Simulation, and Scientific Computing

title: Assessing the robustness of machine learning-based automated valuation models across heterogeneous residential markets in Malaysia
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the comparative robustness of machine-learning-based automated valuation models (AVMs) for residential property valuation across different Malaysian market settings. It evaluates random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) and artificial neural network (ANN) models by considering predictive accuracy, temporal consistency and computational feasibility, while distinguishing comparative performance across independently modelled data sets from genuine cross-market transferability. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative comparative approach is applied using an empirical residential property data set from Johor Bahru and simulated scenarios representing Kuala Lumpur and Penang in Malaysia. RF, XGBoost and ANN models are independently developed and evaluated within each case using prediction-error measures and reported temporal performance. Computational execution is assessed separately as an indicator of technical feasibility. The analytical framework interprets model performance as conditional on the interaction between algorithm characteristics, data set structure, preprocessing and validation design rather than as an inherent property of a particular modelling technique. Findings The findings show that relative model performance varies across the evaluated data sets, with different machine-learning approaches demonstrating stronge…
venue: International Journal of Housing Markets and Analysis

title: Shifting from Pseudo-Compliance to Ecological Citizenship: Transformative Learning through the Waste Alms Program
abstract: The plastic waste crisis in Adiwiyata Mandiri-predicated schools often stems from the limitations of instructive-regulatory approaches (top-down compliance) that only trigger pseudocompliance. This study aims to analyze the implementation process of the Project Citizen learning model based on Experiential-Transformative Learning specifically in the syntax of alternative policy formulation through the "Waste Charity" (Sedekah Sampah) initiative in transforming normative awareness into authentic ecological citizenship at SMP Negeri 2 Balen, Bojonegoro Regency. This qualitative case study involved Civics teachers, Class 9C students, the Adiwiyata Team, canteen vendors, and local waste collectors. Data were gathered through passive participant observation, in-depth interviews, and document analysis, and analyzed using the interactive model of Miles, Huberman, and Saldana. The findings indicate that the disorienting dilemma of canteen plastic waste leakage was successfully transformed into bottom-up civic action. Through the "Waste Charity" program, students independently collected, sorted, and converted inorganic waste into a funding source for the school's Adiwiyata ecosystem (maintaining fish ponds and classroom gardens). This integration of spiritual values, circular economy, and community partnerships proved effective in shifting student disposition from passive sanction-based …
venue: International Journal of Educational Research & Social Sciences

title: Machine Learning Predictions of Experimental Mössbauer Properties of Fe-Containing Molecular Complexes and Protein Models
abstract: Abstract Mössbauer spectroscopy is among the best techniques for probing molecular structures of iron complexes and proteins. Extracting structural insights from experimental spectra often necessitates accurate DFT predictions of isomer shift (IS) and quadrupole splitting (QS) parameters. However, substantial computational cost and sensitivity to the choice of functional and basis set limit their utility for high-throughput structural screening. To address this gap, various traditional machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) models were investigated, using a curated experimental data set of 522 diverse compounds. After engineering models and descriptors, the DL model Chemprop has the highest coefficient of determination (R2) for the test data set (0.92 for IS; 0.73 for QS), with R2 = 0.98/0.91 for IS/QS in the overall data set. Validation of this model corroborates its high, close-to-DFT accuracy for IS predictions, and also shows a significant improvement room for QS predictions. Its predictions of several iron sites in both heme and nonheme proteins and both first- and second-coordination sphere models with challenging and/or unique novel structural features replicated previous DFT structural predictions that are in excellent agreement with experiment, which is a significant application given that no protein data was used to train the ML model. This approach achieved a …
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Do I see myself as a digital entrepreneur? How entrepreneurial mindset and mentoring shape the digital education–venture intention pathway
abstract: Purpose This study examines how digital entrepreneurship education (DEE) relates to students' digital venture intention (DVI) in an emerging-economy higher education context. Drawing on experiential learning theory as a process lens, the study investigates Entrepreneurial Mindset (EM) as a cognitive explanatory mechanism and mentoring support (MS) as a boundary condition of the DEE–EM relationship. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 418 university students in Punjab, Pakistan, using a three-wave time-lagged survey design. Digital entrepreneurship education and mentoring support were measured at Time 1, entrepreneurial mindset at Time 2, and digital venture intention at Time 3. The measurement model was assessed through CFA, while the hypotheses were tested using PROCESS Models 4 and 7 with 5,000 bootstrap resamples. Findings DEE was positively associated with DVI and with EM, while EM was positively associated with DVI. The indirect relationship between DEE and DVI through EM was significant, supporting EM as an explanatory mechanism. MS significantly conditioned the DEE–EM relationship, such that this association, and the corresponding indirect relationship between DEE and DVI through EM, were stronger at higher levels of MS. Originality/value The study advances digital entrepreneurship education research by explaining not only whether DEE is associated with …
venue: Higher Education, Skills and Work-Based Learning

title: Training and salesperson performance in an emerging economy: a moderated mediation perspective
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to investigate the underlying psychological mechanisms and boundary conditions of the relationship between training and performance, in light of inconsistent empirical evidence. Design/methodology/approach This study employed a face-to-face survey involving 163 salespersons in Cirebon, Indonesia. Data were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling with SmartPLS 4. Findings The results show that all hypotheses were supported. Training has a positive and significant relationship with salesperson performance, and self-efficacy partially mediates this relationship. In addition, person–job fit (P–J fit) moderates the relationship between training and self-efficacy. Originality/value Using the perspectives of job demands–resources theory, self-efficacy theory and person–environment fit theory, this study is one of the first to examine a moderated mediation model between training and salesperson performance in the context of a developing country, with self-efficacy as a mediator and P–J fit as a moderator of this relationship.

title: Machine learning for biomarker-driven thalassemia diagnosis: a framework for causal effect estimation
abstract: Thalassemia is one of the most heterogeneous diseases, with more than a thousand mutation types recorded worldwide. Molecular diagnosis of thalassemia by conventional PCR-based DNA analysis is time- and resource-consuming owing to the phenotype variability, disease complexity, and molecular diagnostic test limitations. Thalassemia diagnosis relies heavily on complex interactions among hematological biomarkers, making it challenging to distinguish causal relationships from mere statistical correlations. To address this limitation, this study proposes a causal machine learning framework that integrates causal discovery and counterfactual inference to identify biomarker-driven treatment effects for thalassemia diagnosis. The proposed approach models clinical variables using a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) to capture underlying causal dependencies and enables robust estimation of treatment effects while accounting for confounding factors. To address the primary objective from complementary causal perspectives, the framework combines adjusted regression for confounding control, inverse probability weighting for propensity-based estimation, Random Forest-based analysis for nonlinear feature importance and heterogeneous treatment effects, and bootstrap resampling for uncertainty quantification. The adjusted linear regression model yielded a conservative causal effect estimate of 0.3008…

title: The evolution of entrepreneurship education in the digital era: a bibliometric roadmap of AI-driven experiential learning (2016–2026)
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this paper is to examine the evolution of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven experiential learning in entrepreneurship education in the digital era and to identify the main research trends, intellectual foundations and future directions shaping the field. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts a bibliometric approach using 204 Web of Science-indexed articles and reviews published between 2016 and June 2026. Performance analysis and science mapping were conducted using VOSviewer 1.6.20, including publication trajectory, source performance, co-citation, document citation, author productivity, keyword co-occurrence and overlay analyses. Findings The findings show that the field has shifted from limited early activity to rapid expansion during 2024–2026, driven by growing attention to generative AI, AI literacy and educational technology. Three knowledge bases are identified: educational technology and digital pedagogy; entrepreneurship, business and management education; and sustainability-oriented transformation. Five thematic clusters further highlight behavioural competency, AI integration in higher education, socio-technical adaptation, crisis-driven experiential learning and student-centred instructional design. Originality/value The paper contributes a bibliometric research roadmap for AI-driven experiential entrepreneurship education by identif…

title: Adaptive critic learning control for wastewater treatment plants
Interpretable and backpropagation-free Green Learning for efficient multi-task echocardiographic segmentation and classification
abstract: Purpose This study develops an interpretable, backpropagation-free multi-task Green Learning (MTGL) framework for automated echocardiographic analysis. It addresses the need for reliable left ventricular (LV) segmentation and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) classification while reducing the parameter burden, energy demand and opacity associated with conventional deep learning (DL) models. The objective is to determine whether a unified feed-forward framework can deliver clinically relevant accuracy, computational efficiency and interpretable feature representations. Design/methodology/approach The framework uses a four-hop, PCA/Saab-based unsupervised VoxelHop encoder followed by a coarse-to-fine XGBoost residual-regression decoder for LV segmentation and a pooled multi-scale XGBoost classifier for three-class LVEF classification. Experiments used the predefined EchoNet-Dynamic training, validation and test partitions. MTGL was evaluated against matched 3D V-Net, 3D U-Net, 3D UNETR and 3D nnU-Net baselines using classification accuracy and balanced accuracy, and Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) and intersection over union (IoU). Findings On the EchoNet-Dynamic test set, MTGL achieved 94.3% accuracy for three-class LVEF classification, and 0.912 DSC for LV segmentation, outperforming all compared baselines. It used 1.13 million parameters, versus 10.47–49.08 million f…

title: Routine CBC–based machine learning for individualized correction of lipemia-induced hemoglobin bias
abstract: Background Lipemia can interfere with photometric hemoglobin (HGB) measurement, causing spurious elevation and distortion of HGB-derived erythrocyte indices. We investigated whether routine complete blood count (CBC) parameters could continuously quantify lipemia-induced HGB bias and support individualized correction. Methods We screened 310 clinical lipemic specimens from 310 unique patients measured on a Sysmex XN-9000. Twenty-seven specimens with a pre- versus post-plasma-replacement red blood cell (RBC) difference of ≥3% failed the prespecified procedural quality-control criterion and were excluded, leaving 283 specimens from 283 patients for analysis. Plasma-replacement HGB (HGB-PR) was used as the practical reference comparator. Relative bias was defined as Bias_PR = (HGB-I−HGB-PR)/HGB-PR × 100%. A random forest model used routine RBC count (RBC-I), routine photometric HGB (HGB-I), hematocrit (HCT-I), mean corpuscular hemoglobin (MCH-I), and mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration (MCHC-I), with nested cross-validation (5 outer and 3 inner folds). Hyperparameters minimized the mean absolute error (MAE) of machine-learning-corrected HGB (HGB_ML) versus HGB-PR. All primary estimates used out-of-fold (OOF) predictions. Benchmarking, OOF SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), lipid augmentation, and coupling sensitivity analyses were performed. Results In the 283-specimen an…

title: Integrated first-principles calculation and machine learning-assisted optimization of high-efficiency lead-free Sb 2 Se 3 /Cs 2 TiI 6 double-absorber solar cells
abstract: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) are widely investigated due to their low fabrication cost, compatibility with lowtemperature solution processing and the continual improvement in power conversion efficiency (PCE). The efficiency of singlejunction architectures is restricted by the Shockley–Queisser limit, which constrains further advances. This study develops a high-performance, lead-free PSC architecture utilizing Sb 2 Se 3 and Cs 2 TiI 6 as complementary absorbers. First-principles calculations were performed to evaluate the intrinsic structural, electronic and optical properties of bulk Sb 2 Se 3 and Cs 2 TiI 6 . The interfacial energy alignment and charge transport in the double-absorber device were subsequently evaluated using SCAPS-1D, through which the device parameters were systematically optimized and the PCE increased from 15.73% to 29.57%. By incorporating realistic losses, including series and shunt resistances, temperature, illumination effects and radiative recombination, a corrected efficiency of 25.79% was achieved. To predict photovoltaic parameters and identify the governing performance factors, five machine-learning models were trained on 1500 simulated datasets, with the light gradient boosting machine (LGBM) exhibiting the highest predictive accuracy. SHapley Additive exPlanation (SHAP) analysis identified the bulk defect density of Sb 2 Se 3 as the dominant f…

title: Targeted cystatin C testing for large negative eGFR discordance in adults with diabetes: development and external validation of a machine-learning model
abstract: Background Large negative discordance between cystatin C- and creatinine-based estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) may reveal clinically relevant renal-function differences that are not apparent from creatinine alone. When universal cystatin C testing is impractical, a method to prioritize patients for additional testing may improve testing efficiency. Methods We conducted a retrospective two-center study of adults with diabetes. Large negative eGFR discordance (D2) was defined as eGFRcys/eGFRcr <0.70. Seven machine-learning algorithms were evaluated in a development cohort of 1,170 participants (214 D2-positive), followed by SHAP-guided feature reduction. The final model was applied unchanged to an independent external validation cohort of 1,619 participants (112 D2-positive). Performance was compared with a prespecified clinical core (age, sex, and eGFRcr); additional analyses evaluated logistic regression using eGFRcr alone or with blood urea nitrogen and albumin. Prespecified cystatin C testing allocations of 10%-50% were evaluated using model-based risk ranking. Results The final nine-predictor XGBoost model achieved an AUROC of 0.863 (95% CI, 0.833-0.889) and an AUPRC of 0.600 (95% CI, 0.532-0.668) in development. In independent external validation, AUROC was 0.806 (95% CI, 0.769-0.840) and AUPRC was 0.258 (95% CI, 0.193-0.337), compared with 0.661 and 0.126, r…

title: Nonlinear Membrane-System-Based Multiscale Feature Purification Learning Framework
abstract: Deep neural networks have achieved remarkable performance in visual representation learning, but their hierarchical feature aggregation often introduces redundant and task-irrelevant responses, limiting representation quality in fine-grained visual analysis tasks. To address this issue, this paper proposes FPNet-NSNP, an NSNP-inspired multiscale feature purification framework for image forgery localization. The proposed framework integrates three complementary components: a Cross-layer Feature Fusion (CFF) module for hierarchical feature interaction, a Visual Perception (VP) module for multiscale contextual representation, and a Feature Purification (FP) module for adaptive feature refinement. In particular, the proposed ConvSNP unit incorporates nonlinear response regulation inspired by Nonlinear Spiking Neural P Systems (NSNP), enabling more effective feature transformation and redundancy reduction during propagation. Extensive experiments on benchmark image forgery localization datasets demonstrate that FPNet-NSNP achieves competitive performance compared with existing methods. Moreover, robustness evaluations under noise perturbation and JPEG compression, together with cross-domain experiments on medical image manipulation data, further verify the stability and generalization capability of the proposed framework. The results indicate that NSNP-inspired nonlinear regulation …

title: Análise de Padrões em Casos Jurídicos com Mineração de Processos e Machine Learning
abstract: A morosidade na tramitação de processos judiciais representa um desafio crítico para a eficiência do sistema de justiça. Este artigo apresenta uma metodologia que integra Mineração de Processos e Machine Learning para analisar o tempo de processamento de casos na Justiça Comum brasileira. A abordagem inicia com a aplicação do algoritmo K-means, utilizando a representação bag of activities, para agrupar processos com fluxos de trabalho similares. Posteriormente, esses aglomerados são subdivididos com base na duração dos traços, classificando-os em categorias de execução rápida, média e lenta. A etapa final emprega o algoritmo PrefixSpan para identificar padrões sequenciais de atividades recorrentes dentro de cada perfil temporal. Os resultados demonstram comportamentos processuais característicos e sequências de atividades predominantes para cada faixa de duração, fornecendo subsídios essenciais para a otimização da gestão judiciária e o aprimoramento dos fluxos de trabalho nos tribunais.
venue: Revista de Engenharia e Pesquisa Aplicada

title: Identifying critical aspects of a complex object of learning in history – the value of treating critical aspects as interrelated
abstract: Purpose This study explores how Learning Study grounded in variation theory can be used to identify and inform the teaching of critical aspects in relation to a complex object of learning within the subject of history: students’ ability to provide a reasoned argument explaining why two plausible historical accounts addressing the same phenomenon differ. Design/methodology/approach This study reports on an upper secondary history Learning Study in which students’ written responses were subjected to a systematic two-stage analysis informed by variation theory and grounded in contemporary research within the field of history education. Findings The findings suggest that the critical aspects of a complex object of learning may be understood as relational and interdependent rather than as discrete components. This implies that teaching needs to open variation both in individual aspects and in their relationships, and that learning can be conceptualised as a shift from discerning isolated elements to experiencing a coherent whole. Research limitations/implications The findings can provide methodological insights into the process of how to identify critical aspects of a complex object of learning in Learning Studies. Originality/value The results reconceptualise critical aspects in Learning Study as relational and interdependent rather than discrete and suggest that, for complex objec…

title: 28% to 18%: Scholarly Publishing’s First Real AI Governance Deep-Dive
Between curiosity and uncertainty: artificial intelligence in the social perception of seniors. A qualitative analysis
abstract: Cel pracy Celem artykułu jest analiza społecznej percepcji AI wśród osób 60+ oraz identyfikacja czynników edukacyjnych i społecznych kształtujących poziom ich wiedzy i postawy wobec tej technologii. Materiał i metody W badania zastosowano jakościową strategię badawczą. Materiał empiryczny pozyskano w toku indywidualnych wywiadów z osobami w wieku 60+. Próba badawcza liczyła 10 osób, w tym 5 kobiet w wieku 60–68 lat oraz 5 mężczyzn w wieku 62–70 lat, różniących się poziomem wykształcenia i doświadczeniem w korzystaniu z narzędzi AI. Zgromadzone dane poddano indukcji analitycznej, co umożliwiło wyodrębnienie dominujących sposobów definiowania AI, źródeł wiedzy o niej, doświadczeń związanych z technologiami cyfrowymi oraz ocen dotyczących jej społecznych konsekwencji. Wyniki Z przeprowadzonych badań wynikają wnioski nie tylko o charakterze poznawczym, ale również praktyczno-kierunkowym Analizy jakościowe wskazują na to, że wiedza badanych seniorów na temat AI jest oparta przede wszystkim na przekazach medialnych i doświadczeniach pośrednich. Wnioski Stąd też istotne jest podejmowanie działań systemowych w zakresie informacyjno-edukacyjnym ukierunkowanych na rozwój kompetencji cyfrowych seniorów wzmacniających ich uczestnictwa w procesach transformacji technologicznej.

title: Immediate changes in self-reported apprehension and uncertainty across 41 emergency scenarios following a structured emergency medicine course
abstract: Background Emergency physicians face high cognitive and emotional stress in acute care, especially in prehospital settings. Structured training is an essential component of emergency medicine education and may increase familiarity with high-pressure clinical situations. In Germany, an 80-hour standardized emergency physician course is mandatory for certification. Objective/design This study evaluated the impact of this course on physicians’ self-perceived apprehension and uncertainty in acute emergency scenarios using a prospective pre–post design. Settings and participants The study was conducted in five consecutive emergency courses. 162 physicians from different specializations and departments throughout Germany completed pre- and post-course questionnaires. Intervention Participants completed the standardized 80 h course, which combines theoretical instruction, structured decision-making, team communication, and high-fidelity simulation. Analysis The primary endpoint was the change in a single combined self-reported rating of apprehension and uncertainty, assessed using a 5-point Likert scale across 41 questionnaire items. Analyses of the predefined categories constituted secondary analyses, while analyses of the 41 individual items and subgroup analyses were exploratory. Results A significant overall reduction in combined self-reported apprehension and uncertainty was obse…

title: High-accuracy solution of PDEs by iterative refinement of global stochastic solvers with applications to interior and exterior Dirichlet problems
abstract: Abstract The statistical convergence barrier of Monte Carlo methods has long been regarded as the principal obstacle to high-accuracy stochastic solution of elliptic boundary value problems. In this paper, we show that this barrier can be overcome by a general residual-based iterative refinement framework applicable to stochastic solvers that permit evaluation of the residual. As a representative example, we develop the theory for the Global Random Walk on Spheres (RWS) method. Our main theoretical result is a proof of exponential convergence of the complete iterative algorithm, together with explicit error estimates and computational complexity bounds. The analysis shows that each additional order-of-magnitude reduction in the error requires only about a twofold increase in computational effort, whereas conventional Monte Carlo methods require approximately a hundredfold increase. Thus, the statistical convergence barrier of Monte Carlo no longer determines the computational complexity of high-accuracy stochastic computation. Numerical experiments for both interior and exterior Dirichlet problems confirm the theoretical predictions. Using global RWS as the underlying stochastic solver, the proposed framework achieves several orders of magnitude higher accuracy while substantially reducing the computational time compared with the standard RWS algorithm, making it particularly a…

title: A Framework for Time-Explicit Life Cycle Optimization
abstract: Abstract Life cycle optimization (LCO) selects optimal processes and supply chains from a set of alternatives given environmental constraints and objectives, supporting the design of sustainable systems and their transitions. However, current approaches rely on static assumptions, overlooking two interacting temporal dimensions: temporal distribution (flows are spread over time) and temporal evolution (processes and supply chains change over time). Because distribution and evolution jointly dictate the magnitude of a flow at a given time, both must be considered simultaneously to accurately optimize against cumulative environmental impacts and time-specific environmental constraints. We present a framework for time-explicit LCO that captures these interdependencies to determine optimal transition pathways. The framework tracks flow timing relative to process installation and dynamically determines flow magnitudes from time-specific process parameters and background supply chains. A case study on integrated methanol and pig iron production demonstrates how time-explicit LCO enables optimization against time-resolved environmental impacts and constraints, revealing mitigation strategies inaccessible to static approaches: prioritizing early high-efficiency technology installation to idle older processes as operational savings outweigh embodied impacts of stranded assets, and avoid…

title: DRL-Based Adaptive Planner Switching for Mobile Robots: CPN Modeling, Verification and Optimization
abstract: Mobile robots operating in complex environments must switch planners as road conditions change, yet concurrent triggers make the switching logic difficult to validate through code inspection and empirical tuning alone. We use Coloured Petri Nets (CPN) to analyze a four-mode scheme, expose unbounded transition-buffer accumulation and rollback oscillation, and derive a Guide–Safe–Emergency architecture with explicit responsibilities, unified arbitration, and single-channel execution. Exhaustive exploration of its finite interface instance covers 3,486 reachable markings and 13,097 arcs; all five specified correctness properties are satisfied. Within this architecture, we adopt a safety-constrained reinforcement learning approach: the DQN is authorized only to optimize Guide–Safe switching based on recent environmental complexity and switching history, whereas a non-learning Supervisor and an independent Safety Guard enforce mode mutual exclusion, priority arbitration, Emergency intervention, and conservative recovery. The DQN cannot alter or bypass these constraints. In simulation, the constrained policy improves average cumulative reward by 10.1% over a fixed-threshold baseline. Deployment on an Ackermann-steering robot demonstrates multi-goal planner switching and two closed-loop Emergency stop–recovery cycles, confirming hardware executability of the CPN-derived constrained-AI…

title: BIPV for Heritage Buildings and Historic Context: An Integrated and Comprehensive Framework for Nizwa Fort, Oman
abstract: Building-integrated photovoltaic (BIPV) systems in culturally significant buildings represent one of the key challenges in the transition to renewable energy, as highlighted in Oman Vision 2040. As the world moves towards decarbonization, the use of photovoltaic technologies in protected heritage sites must be approached with utmost care and respect to conservation principles, as stated in the Venice Charter (1964) and other ICOMOS guidelines, such as the criteria of authenticity and reversibility. This study aims to fill a gap and propose a multi-criteria assessment framework for BIPV integration in the culturally significant buildings. Taking the case study of Nizwa Fort in Oman, a sequential mixed-methods approach is used, including: (i) benchmarked energy demand estimation (200–300 kWh/day) with solar irradiance analysis (5.5–6.5 kWh/m²/day) and PV system sizing (50 kWp); (ii) a structured stakeholder survey (n = 42) across general public, architectural conservation specialists, and PV technology experts, with responses analyzed through weighted scoring (0.45/0.35/0.20) and Spearman rank correlation; (iii) scenario-based visual impact assessment of 40 BIPV configurations, derived from four PV technologies (monocrystalline, polycrystalline, PERC, thin-film) applied to ten spatial positions on primary and secondary building elements; and (iv) techno-economic analysis incorpor…

title: Human-centered economy: Conceptual features of developing a system for training and promoting management personnel – Considering hotel business as a case study
abstract: Subject. Problems of managing human resources in economic entities. Objectives. Development of a conceptual model for the training system of managerial staff for hotel businesses, reflecting the characteristics of modern business conditions. Methods. Content analysis, comparative analysis. Results. A model has been developed that takes into account the specifics of the hotel business and focuses on the partnership between the manager and the business owner. Conclusions. The research results can be taken into account when developing programs for the overall tourism industry and, in particular, the hospitality sector.

title: Multi-omics analysis revealed that Jingfang Mixture alleviates inflammation in an OVA/Al(OH)3-induced urticaria-like rat model by regulating the AMPK/p38 MAPK/PI3K-Akt pathway associated with the gut-skin axis
abstract: Background The systemic and relapsing nature of urticaria cannot be fully explained by cutaneous mast-cell activation alone. Whether the gut contributes, and whether a multi-component formula such as Jingfang Mixture (JF) acts through a gut-skin route, have not been tested together at the level of microbiota, metabolites, and skin signaling together. Methods Using an OVA (ovalbumin)/Al(OH) 3 -induced urticaria-like allergic inflammation rat model, we integrated 16S rRNA gene sequencing, fecal untargeted metabolomics, and skin DIA (data-independent acquisition)-based quantitative proteomics to investigate the therapeutic mechanisms of JF. Results JF suppressed both Th2 (IgE (immunoglobulin E), IL-4 (interleukin-4)) and Th17/pro-inflammatory (IL-6 (interleukin-6), TNF-α (tumor necrosis factor-α), IL-17 (interleukin-17)) responses, improved intestinal barrier-associated abnormalities, and partially reversed gut dysbiosis by restoring SCFA-producing bacteria ( Bacteroidia, Clostridia, Lachnospirales, Oscillospirales ) while reducing Proteobacteria and Enterobacterales . JF normalized the fecal metabolome, elevating anti-inflammatory metabolites including butyrate, indole, indole-3-acetic acid, docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) and reducing pro-inflammatory mediators such as arachidonic acid, leukotriene B4, secondary bile acids. At the skin level, JF activated AMPK (AMP-activated protein …

title: Global logistics priorities before and after COVID-19: A multi-criteria assessment of logistics performance index dimensions across income groups
abstract: This study examines changes in global logistics priorities by comparing the relative importance of the six Logistics Performance Index (LPI) dimensions across income groups in the 2018 and 2023 evaluation periods. A fixed common panel of 134 countries is classified into high-, upper-middle-, lower-middle-, and low-income groups to ensure comparability between the two periods. Criterion weights are determined using three objective weighting methods, LODECI, LOPCOW, and SITDE, and integrated through arithmetic averaging. Countries are then ranked using the ALPAS method. The findings reveal different weighting patterns across income groups and periods. International shipments remain the highest-weighted dimension in the high-income group, while customs retain the highest weight in the lower-middle-income group. In the upper-middle-income group, tracking and tracing remains the highest-weighted dimension in both 2018 and 2023, although its weight decreases from 0.201 to 0.184. The most notable change is observed in the low-income group, where the weight of timeliness decreases from 0.160 to 0.112, while international shipments gain relative importance and tracking and tracing retains the highest weight despite declining from 0.213 to 0.191. Country rankings also show both stability and substantial movements within each income group. Comparisons with AROMAN, CRADIS, MABAC, and MAIRC…
venue: International Journal of Business and Economic Studies

title: Walkability and Mobility in the Historic District of Nizwa, Oman: A Space Syntax and Multi-Indicator Assessment for Heritage-Led Urban Regeneration
abstract: The issue of walkability in hot, arid heritage cities is still very much under-theorized, as the traditional configurational frameworks have been developed in temperate environments where the thermal barrier and vehicular encroachment do not dominate spatial network logic. This study aims at filling this gap by performing the first quantitative configuration experience coupling test for an Omani historic city, Nizwa. We combine DepthmapX v0.8 Space Syntax analysis of an axial map (428 lines, 612 nodes; eight configurational indicators) of a 1.32 km² area with a validated MAPS-Global/Gehl perceptual audit of 11 purposively sampled streets in four functional zones and 42 semi-structured stakeholder interviews using a sequential explanatory mixed-methods design. The statistical coupling uses Pearson correlation and OLS regression (Bonferroni corrected α = 0.0009) and a weighted Composite Walkability Index (CWI, max 50). The organic historic fabric shows good syntactic coherence (Connectivity–Integration r = 0.91, p < 0.001; configurational family r = 0.80–0.91), which indicates a well-developed pedestrian network. However, only 19% of the variance in Safety can be accounted for by Global Integration, and 2% of the variance in Accessibility (R² = 0.19 and 0.02 respectively); given the small street sample (n = 11), these associations are exploratory and hypothesis-generating rather …

title: Hierarchical modeling of retailers' issues for lean dairy supply chain: a data-driven decision-making approach
abstract: Purpose This research identifies key retailer-related issues causing inefficiencies in the Indian Dairy Supply Chain (DSC) and develops a hierarchical model aimed at guiding decision-makers towards a leaner and more productive DSC. The study addresses a significant gap in the lean DSC literature, focusing on the challenges retailers face in emerging markets such as India. Design/methodology/approach The study employs a mixed-method approach, beginning with a comprehensive literature review and expert consultations to identify 15 critical retailer issues. A structured questionnaire was administered to industry professionals and academics, resulting in 290 valid responses. Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) was applied to uncover underlying constructs, followed by Total Interpretive Structural Modeling (TISM) to map relationships among these issues. The model was statistically validated using a one-sample t-test, and MICMAC analysis classified issues by their driving power and dependence. Findings The study categorizes the identified retailer issues into four constructs: strategic, tactical, operational, and performance. Strategic issues (lack of top management commitment, insufficient financial support, and lack of assured long-term contracts) emerged as the most powerful drivers, underscoring their fundamental role in addressing other retailers' concerns. Tactical issues, includ…
venue: International Journal of Productivity and Performance Management

title: From safety data to safer practice
Consumer responses to conflicting brand news in digital feeds
abstract: Purpose This study aims to explain how negative brand information gains influence when presented alongside positive information in digital feeds. This study addresses a gap in brand-crisis research, which has not traced how competing cues capture attention, activate violation-specific emotions, alter corresponding legitimacy beliefs and persist over time. Design/methodology/approach Three studies test a process model grounded in negativity bias and cognitive appraisal theory. Study 1 uses within-participant eye tracking (n = 117). Study 2 combines eye tracking and survey measures in a randomised experiment (n = 285). Study 3 uses a three-wave longitudinal experiment (n = 279 at T3). Findings Negative information attracted more visual attention than concurrent positive information. Greater negative attention share (NAS) intensified contempt towards worker-treatment violations and disgust towards integrity violations, which, respectively, reduced perceived employee care and ethical integrity. Anger and sadness did not mediate these relationships, while social identification strengthened both pathways. Legitimacy threats also produced larger, more persistent changes in the affected legitimacy belief than in overall brand evaluation. Research limitations/implications Brand-crisis research should treat attention as an early selection mechanism and distinguish discrete moral emotions…

title: The synergy between leadership and Green AI capability in environmental management systems toward social value
abstract: Purpose Although the role of green artificial intelligence (Green AI) in firm innovation has been widely examined, its influence on social value remains insufficiently understood. Moreover, empirical evidence on how digital leadership facilitates the effective integration of Green AI into environmental management systems is limited. This study aims to (1) examine the impact of Green AI capability on social performance through internal environmental management systems, particularly environmental management accounting (EMA) and (2) investigate whether the synergy between digital leadership and Green AI capability enhances the effectiveness of EMA in a sustainable management context. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research design was employed using survey data collected from 235 chief executive officers and chief financial officers of Vietnamese manufacturing firms. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling was conducted using SmartPLS version 4.1.1.2. Findings The results indicate that Green AI capability significantly enhances the effectiveness of EMA systems. Furthermore, EMA extends beyond traditional financial and environmental boundaries to positively influence firms’ social performance. The findings also demonstrate that digital leadership strengthens the relationship between Green AI capability and EMA effectiveness, creating a synergistic effect that …

title: Knowledge flows and knowledge management in a public research center: an empirical study
abstract: Purpose This research aims to examine how knowledge flows circulate within a public innovation unit, how multidisciplinary teams interact and what these dynamics reveal about knowledge management (KM) maturity. Design/methodology/approach A survey-based case study with embedded qualitative responses was conducted at CeMEPI-PGE. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire administered to researchers from different teams. Closed-ended responses were analyzed using descriptive statistics, while open-ended responses were examined through thematic content analysis. Findings Semantic knowledge boundaries emerged as the most salient perceived integration barrier among the dimensions assessed, although collaborative potential remained high. Research limitations/implications The study is limited to a single case and relies primarily on questionnaire data, which restricts statistical generalization. Future research could adopt longitudinal and comparative designs to examine the evolution of KM maturity in emerging public innovation units. Practical implications The findings highlight the importance of strengthening knowledge governance through structured repositories, standardized documentation practices and institutionalized knowledge-sharing routines. Social implications Strengthening KM in public organizations contributes to improving the quality of public decision-making a…
venue: VINE Journal of Information and Knowledge Management Systems

title: Hospital violence
abstract: ABSTRACT Workplace violence remains a significant threat to health care personnel, contributing to staff injury, burnout, turnover, and reduced quality of care. Nurse managers play a critical role in addressing this challenge through the implementation of effective de-escalation programs. This article reviews the prevalence and impact of workplace violence, outlines evidence-based de-escalation models and strategies, and discusses methods for recognizing and responding to escalating behavior. The role of technologies, such as staff duress systems, in supporting rapid response and enhancing safety is also examined. Comprehensive approaches that combine training, protocols, technology, and postincident support can help create safer care environments.

title: Pathway to Excellence®: A strategic framework for sustaining workforce engagement and organizational performance: Erratum.
The psychology of deception: exploring behavioral drivers of Ponzi investments
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the impact of social networks, greed and financial literacy on individuals’ decisions to invest in Ponzi schemes in Indonesia. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative analysis was used, based on an online survey completed by 385 individuals who had potentially invested in Ponzi schemes. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares–Structural Equation Modeling to test the proposed relationships between the variables. Findings The analysis revealed that all three variables: social networks, greed and financial literacy significantly influence Ponzi investment decisions. Social networks play the most prominent role by facilitating information spread through direct or indirect interpersonal connections. Greed motivates individuals to pursue high-return schemes despite known risks. Unexpectedly, higher financial literacy is positively associated with Ponzi investment participation, suggesting that financially literate individuals may be overconfident in their ability to manage risk. Practical implications These findings suggest the urgent need for targeted public education and awareness campaigns. Policymakers should consider generational approaches to financial literacy that address both knowledge and behavioral biases. Preventive measures should focus not only on increasing financial knowledge but also on addressing emotional motivations…

title: Staple-line disruption of a short left–middle hepatic venous common trunk causing right atrial injury during extended left hepatectomy: A case report
Financial Feasibility of Investment in the Development of Kubu Alvian Guest House
abstract: This study reassesses the financial feasibility of investing in the development of Kubu Alvian Guest House in Denpasar by reanalyzing historical data and examining sensitivity in present-value terms. The descriptive quantitative case study draws on documented occupancy and room-rate data for 2011 2017, an initial investment of IDR 4,135,040,000, a 20-year analysis horizon, and a discount rate of 12%. Recent literature and Bali tourism statistics for 2026 inform the discussion. The analysis comprises trend re-estimation, capacity checks, cost reconciliation, net present value (NPV), benefit cost ratio (BCR), and sensitivity tests involving one or two variables. The linear model indicates an annual occupancy increase of 1.6675 percentage points, yet its extrapolated values exceed 100% from 2035 onward. The reported NPV of IDR 701,159,080 and BCR of 1.084 are arithmetically reproducible if total discounted costs include the initial investment. Under this interpretation, the investment reaches break-even when the present value of benefits falls by 7.74% or subsequent costs rise by 16.61%, with all other variables held constant. If the reported costs exclude the initial investment, NPV falls to −IDR 3,433,880,920. The documented internal rate of return of 13.56% and payback period of three years and three months cannot be verified without annual cash-flow data. Financial feasibility…

title: Al-Dakhīl by Transmission in Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī's Interpretation of Sūrat al-Baqarah: An Analytical and Critical Study
Strategic shield or financial fad? Investigating derivative use by Indian firms
abstract: Purpose This study aims to explore the determinants of derivatives usage for nonfinancial firms in India. A fast growing developing emerging economy that is characterized by its own distinctive institutional and regulatory environment. Beyond identifying firm-level drivers, this paper contributes to the literature by simultaneously examining the association between derivative use and firm performance (Return on Assets [ROA]) and firm value (Tobin’s Q), an aspect underexplored in the Indian context. The study further documents the role of institutional ownership and governance structures in derivative adoption decisions during the post-liberalization period 2015–2022, and grounds its hypotheses explicitly in hedging (risk-management) theory and agency theory. Design/methodology/approach The analysis is based on a sample of 184 nonfinancial companies listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) between 2015 and 2022 (1,472 firm-year observations). The study employs logit regression on pooled cross-sectional data, complemented by univariate tests, and descriptive statistics to examine the relationship between firm characteristics and the use of derivatives. Robustness checks include a random-effects panel logit model that exploits the full panel structure of the data, industry fixed-effects specifications, and an alternative keyword-coding protocol for the dependent variable. Finding…

title: The Effect of Audit Committee Size, Capital Structure, and Company Size on Financial Distress
abstract: Financial distress is a condition of financial decline that can threaten the sustainability of a company and needs to be identified through various internal company factors. This study aims to analyze the effect of audit committee size, capital structure, and company size on financial distress in infrastructure sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange for the 2020–2024 period. The study used a quantitative approach with a purposive sampling method and secondary data in the form of financial reports and company annual reports. The study population consisted of infrastructure sector companies listed on the IDX, with 44 companies selected as samples and 220 observations over five years. Financial distress was measured using the Zmijewski X-Score, audit committee size based on the number of members, capital structure using the Debt to Equity Ratio, and company size based on the company size indicator used in the study. Data analysis was performed using descriptive statistics and panel data regression with EViews 12. The results showed that audit committee size and capital structure had no significant effect on financial distress, while company size had a negative and significant effect. Simultaneously, all three variables had a significant effect on financial distress. In conclusion, company size is a factor that has a significant influence on the financial distress …

title: The use of project analysis in assessing the financial effectiveness of an investment project
abstract: Subject. Assessment of the financial efficiency of an investment project. Objectives. Analysis and systematization of existing approaches to assessing the financial effectiveness of investment projects and their use in calculating the effectiveness of a specific investment project. Methods. The research methodology is based on the method of theoretical analysis and systematization of project approach methods and their use in practical calculations of financial assessment of the effectiveness of an investment project. Results. The existing methods of project analysis are ordered, systematized and analyzed, their comparative characteristics are proposed and the calculation of the indicators necessary for their practical use is given. The necessity of using an integrated approach in the selection of indicators for assessing the financial effectiveness of investment projects is substantiated. Based on the methods and indicators considered, an assessment of the financial efficiency and expediency of a specific investment project was carried out. Conclusions. For a comprehensive review of the financial effectiveness of the project, several assessment methods must be applied. Conclusions are based on a comparison of the results obtained with the estimates of other similar projects, if any. If there are none, then the choice of an effective project should be chosen based on the importa…

title: Probing spin order via magnon transmission across quantum Hall ferromagnet heterojunctions
Climate justice: Is there an individual right of citizen to climate neutrality?
abstract: This paper analyzes citizens' access to climate justice under European and Spanish law. Despite ambitious legislation rendering climate neutrality targets binding and imposing corporate sustainability due diligence (CSDDD), procedural standing (legitimación activa) remains strictly constrained. Both CJEU and Spanish jurisprudence require proof of direct, individualized harm, preventing citizens from challenging public or corporate inaction on an individual basis. Currently, regulatory mechanisms reduce citizens to submitting administrative complaints or claiming post-damage civil compensation. De lege ferenda, achieving effective climate justice requires recognizing an autonomous, enforceable individual right to climate neutrality, transforming citizens into active guarantors of mandatory sustainability standards.

title: Synaptic transmission and plasticity: molecular mechanisms, biological functions and therapeutic opportunities in neurodegenerative diseases
Multifactor analysis of financial flows in the tourism industry
abstract: Subject. Financial flows in the tourism industry of the Russian Federation. Objectives. To conduct a comprehensive multifactor analysis of financial flows in tourism and to develop recommendations for improving financial planning to support managerial decision‑making. Methods. Data from the Federal State Statistics Service for 2014–2024 were used. Methods of descriptive statistics, correlation and regression analysis, and statistical hypothesis testing were applied. The normality of the distribution of quantitative indicators was assessed using the Shapiro–Wilk test; if deviations from normality were detected, nonparametric methods (median, quartiles) were employed. Calculations were performed in the StatTech software environment, v. 4.9.5 (RRID: SCR_023071). Results. It was found that over the period 2014–2024, the average volume of funds received from the sale of tourism products amounted to 298.17 billion rubles. At the same time, payments to non‑residents exceeded payments to residents by a factor of 2.8, indicating a persistent dependence on outbound tourism. A statistically significant high correlation between payments to residents and the number of tour operators was also identified, pointing to growing domestic tourism demand. Linear regression models were constructed, demonstrating a direct impact of tourism product sales volumes on the number of market participants. C…

title: Digital payments in Morocco and cash persistence: prioritizing barriers and enablers through a Delphi study
abstract: Purpose Cash remains the dominant payment instrument in Morocco despite continued infrastructure upgrades and a more active FinTech ecosystem. Prior research identifies many determinants of digital payment adoption, but rarely clarifies their relative importance from the perspective of ecosystem actors. This study aims to identify and prioritize the barriers sustaining cash use and the enablers most likely to expand digital payment adoption in Morocco. Design/methodology/approach A three-round Delphi study was conducted with 29 payment-ecosystem experts. Round 1 used open-ended questions. Round 2 retained eight barriers and eight enablers based on a majority rule. Round 3 asked experts to rank the retained items; ranks were aggregated to obtain collective priorities and Kendall’s W measured consensus. Findings Cultural attachment to cash and behavioral inertia are ranked as the most influential barriers, followed by merchant-side economic constraints and transaction costs. These barriers matter because they shape the effective cost-benefit calculus of payment choice and slow the conversion of formal access to digital tools into routine use. Interoperability and digital skills receive lower priority. On the enabling side, targeted fee reductions for low-value transactions, lower merchant acceptance costs and the digitization of recurring payments emerge as the top priorities. Co…

title: Financial innovations in the context of spatial economics: The inflation aspect
abstract: Subject. Implementation of financial innovations in the context of the uneven economic landscape of Russia. Objectives. Identifying the conditions under which financial innovations help reduce spatial costs, smooth out interregional price differences, and increase the resilience of territorial development, as well as determining the factors under which they strengthen local inflationary pressure. Methods. Comparative, structural-logical, and typological analysis. Results. The impact of financial innovations is uneven and depends on the type of region, characteristics of local supply, and specifics of economic connections. In northern, remote, agricultural regions, as well as in areas with underdeveloped infrastructure, financial innovations can reduce logistics, coordination, and transaction costs, support supply, and ease price imbalances. In agglomeration, tourist, subsidized, and rent-oriented regions, where supply is inelastic, financial innovations can mainly boost demand and amplify inflationary effects. Conclusions. The policy of introducing financial innovations should primarily focus on reducing the 'cost of space,' developing infrastructure, strengthening logistics, and expanding regional offerings.

title: The dark side of impact fintech ecosystems: unstraining the “tug of war” among stakeholders
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the underlying tensions that constrain the potential of fintechs to address inequality and drive sustainable change in impact ecosystems. It focuses on how tension among key stakeholders create an invisible “tug of war” that undermines socio-environmental value creation and dissemination. Design/methodology/approach This research adopts a qualitative approach based on semi-structured interviews with 12 founders and co-founders from ten Brazilian impact fintechs. The authors analysed tensions between fintechs and six main stakeholders within the ecosystem: investors, customers, traditional financial institutions, regulators, supporting organizations and technology providers. Findings This study reveals that misalignments in interests, values and priorities across ecosystem stakeholders hinder innovation and limit effective value co-creation. These tensions manifest in various forms, contributing to persistent friction and reducing the overall impact potential of fintech initiatives. The findings also highlight the need for mechanisms to attenuate these tensions, such as trust-building, regulatory simplification and enhanced collaboration among stakeholders. Originality/value Drawing on stakeholder theory and paradox theory, this study contributes to the literature by advancing a “tug-of-war” perspective for understanding stakeholder tension…

title: Consequences of eating disorders in children: Pedagogical observations in the context of the right to healthy and safe food
abstract: Cel pracy Negatywne skutki zaburzeń odżywiania u dzieci są szczególnie przykre i niebezpieczne. Celem artykułu jest zatem zasygnalizowanie problemu poprzez przybliżenie (w oparciu o dostępną literaturę), zwłaszcza rodzicom, opiekunom i nauczycielom, symptomów zaburzeń, które manifestują się na różne sposoby przykrymi dolegliwościami – psychicznymi i somatycznymi łącznie oraz zachęcenie do podejmowania działań zapobiegawczych bądź ratujących. Materiał i metody Na potrzeby badania posłużono się materiałami z zakresu psychologii dziecięcej, pediatrii, patopsychologii dziecięcej, dietetyki, międzynarodowego prawa praw człowieka, praw dziecka. Wyniki Cierpiące na zaburzenia odżywiania dzieci zwykle doświadczają najróżniejszych problemów psychicznych wynikających z trudności nawiązania poprawnych relacji interpersonalnych. Z tego powodu często odczuwają silną presję, potrzebę spełniania oczekiwań, realizacji stawianych sobie/im celów. Chętnie używają jedzenia jako regulatora emocji. Jednak zaburzenia tego rodzaju, nieleczone, mogą powodować problemy ze zdrowiem. Problem zatem wymaga stałej czujności i dostarczania aktualnej wiedzy rodzicom i edukatorom. Wnioski Sama diagnoza wystąpienia zaburzeń odżywiania nie zawsze jest łatwa do postawienia, a późniejsza terapia to zwykle proces długotrwały i złożony, gdyż objawy z tym związane wykazują zarówno charakter psychiczny, jak i somatyczn…

title: The Number of Minor Children and Household Allocation to Risky Financial Assets: Evidence from the 2021 China Household Finance Survey
abstract: Using microdata on 17,744 households from the 2021 China Household Finance Survey (CHFS), this study employs Probit and Tobit models to examine the association between the number of minor children and household participation in risky financial markets, as well as the share of financial assets allocated to risky assets. After controlling for homeownership, marital status, and household economic characteristics, each additional minor child is associated with an average decrease of 0.54 percentage points in the probability of market participation and 3.32 percentage points in the risky asset share. Both baseline estimates are statistically significant at the 10% level. These findings are consistent with liquidity constraints and precautionary saving. Estimates by number of children suggest a nonlinear pattern: the coefficients for households with two or more minor children are negative and statistically significant, whereas those for households with one minor child are not statistically significant. The negative association is more pronounced in the rural sample; the corresponding coefficients in the urban sample are not statistically significant. By jointly examining market participation, portfolio allocation, nonlinear patterns, and urban–rural differences, this study adds microeconomic evidence on the relationship between household demographic structure and financial asset allo…

title: ESG Disclosure, Political Connections, and Financial Risk: The Moderating Role of Accounting Information Systems in Indonesian SOEs
abstract: Background: Financial risk remains a critical governance concern for Indonesian state-owned enterprises (SOEs), particularly regarding sustainability disclosure, political connections, and accounting information systems (AIS). Objective: This study examines the effects of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) disclosure and political connections on financial risk and evaluates the moderating role of AIS. Methods: A quantitative explanatory approach was applied to 34 SOEs listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2020–2024, comprising 170 firm-year observations. Secondary data were obtained from annual reports, sustainability reports, and financial statements. Financial risk was assessed using the Altman Z-score proxy, ESG disclosure through GRI indicators, political connections through board affiliation proportions, and AIS through ERP implementation. Data were analyzed using PLS-SEM with SmartPLS. Results: ESG disclosure had no significant effect on financial risk (β = 0.099; p = 0.234), whereas political connections showed a positive and significant association (β = 0.521; p < 0.001). AIS did not significantly moderate the ESG disclosure–financial risk relationship (β = 0.071; p = 0.280) or the political connections–financial risk relationship (β = −0.097; p = 0.296). Including moderation terms increased R² marginally from 0.260 to 0.275. Conclusion: Political conne…

title: The Correlation of Public and Private Principles in Financial Law and Their Impact on Human Well-Being
abstract: The article examines the question of the correlation between public and private principles in Russian financial law. The thesis is substantiated that although financial law is a public branch of law, it must be aimed at ensuring both public and private interests, which are in many respects interrelated and inseparable. It is noted that without maintaining a balance of public and private interests, it is impossible to ensure the socio-economic development of the state, as well as human well-being.

title: Associations between Right-wing Authoritarianism and Attitudes toward Criminal Justice
A Meshfree RBF Partition-of-Unity Collocation Method for Structural Yield Design
abstract: This paper presents a radial basis function partition-of-unity method (RBF–PUM) nodal collocation framework for structural yield design based on kinematic limit analysis under monotonic proportional loading. Localised meshfree approximations are combined with nodal evaluation of the kinematic relations and a nodal area approximation of the dissipation and external-work functionals. The resulting norm-constrained optimisation problem is recast as a second-order cone programming (SOCP) problem without conventional element-wise Gauss quadrature. The numerical results show favourable resistance to volumetric locking under the investigated plane strain conditions while retaining the geometric flexibility of meshfree discretisations for complex geometries and localised collapse phenomena. Benchmark examples demonstrate stable numerical convergence, close agreement with analytical and published reference solutions, and consistent representation of localised plastic collapse mechanisms. A parametric investigation further clarifies the influence of the RBF shape parameter and support domain size on solution accuracy, dissipation-field localisation, numerical stability, and computational cost. Because the continuous functionals and incompressibility condition are enforced through discrete nodal approximations, the computed values are interpreted as kinematic collocation estimates rather …

title: Biomimetic functional materials, devices, and systems: integrating nature-inspired design across flexible electronic scales
Agentic, Autonomous Design Evolution of Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials
abstract: Abstract Recent AI systems can autonomously execute scientific workflows and empirical software tasks. We investigate whether an autonomous agent can use evaluation feedback to iteratively develop a scientific model. To address this question, we developed AutoResearch-MLIP, a research protocol in which the agent follows predefined instructions to propose, implement, and evaluate MLIP designs, with outcomes carried forward to guide subsequent iterations. Starting from a simple pair-distance MLIP, each generation selects a parent model by balancing exploration and exploitation, while structured design records guide subsequent proposals. Across 40 generations, the agent explores MLIP designs spanning local message passing, radial representations, scalar-vector states, body-order terms, residual readouts, long-range-inspired terms, and periodic image-offset graph construction. The final G40 model is competitive with established MLIP baselines in post hoc benchmarks. These results show that, within predefined rules, an autonomous agent can use evaluation feedback to iteratively improve MLIP implementations.

title: The Effect of the Future Design Psychoeducation Program Applied to Parents of Gifted Children on Career-Related Parental Behaviors
abstract: The aim of this study is to examine the effect of the “Future Design Family Education Program,” developed by the Ministry of National Education, on the career-related behaviors of parents of gifted students. The study was conducted with 24 parents of gifted children at a Science and Art Centre in Istanbul, Türkiye. A 2×2 factorial quasi-experimental design with experimental and control groups based on pre-test and post-test measurements was used in the study. Within the scope of the study, the psychoeducation program, consisting of eight 40-minute sessions, was delivered to the experimental group by the researcher, whereas no intervention was applied to the control group. To evaluate the effectiveness of the program, the Career-Related Parental Behaviors Scale–Parent Form and a personal information form were used as data collection instruments. The data were analysed using paired-samples t-test and independent-samples t-test through SPSS 25. The findings indicated that the career-related parental behaviors of the parents in the experimental group significantly increased in the post-test compared with their pre-test scores. The results show that the psychoeducation program was effective in improving career-related parental behaviors among parents of gifted children.

title: On the Welfare Effects of Compatibility with Hotelling Competition: The Role of Market Coverage
How markets forecast and "front run" information: Bayesian market efficiency
abstract: Abstract Bayesian investors, rather than waiting, infer a probability distribution over what will be in the company’s report and re-price the stock based on that probability distribution. To allow for their uncertainty about the report’s content and the resulting stock price, the asset pricing formula includes a risk premium related to the precision or quality of the firm’s future financial reporting. The premium can be positive or negative, meaning that the firm affects its cost of capital up or down by its choice of information system or reporting quality. Conservative accounting or any source of anticipated future information that is predisposed to reveal unfavorable news more efficiently than favorable news adds to the firm’s current cost of capital.

title: Hot spot suppression in cell-level TCT-interconnected modules and verification by circuit simulation
abstract: Abstract The output performance of photovoltaic modules with cell-level Total Cross-Tied (TCT) interconnection was compared with that of conventional Series-Parallel (SP) modules under partial shading conditions. In the SP module, partial shading reduced the short-circuit current, resulting in a significant decrease in output power. In addition, hot spots were observed in several cells. Although the TCT module exhibited a similar reduction in short-circuit current, the output power loss was smaller because of an improved fill factor (FF). The experimental results demonstrate that TCT cell interconnection effectively suppresses hot-spot formation under partial shading conditions. Circuit simulations reproduced the experimental results and enabled prediction of cell temperature rise under partial shading conditions.

title: Data-Driven Option Pricing: Neural Network Learning of the Time-Fractional Black–Scholes Model with Market Validation
Fitting structural models to electricity prices
Youth in the Labor Market: Forms of Support and Behavioral Strategies in an International Perspective
abstract: The article examines forms of support for youth in the labor market. Based on an analysis of the results of the second wave of an international sociological study conducted by a group of sociologists at Kazan (Volga Region) Federal University in June–July 2026, the study aims to identify key international trends in the professional and career trajectories of young people in different countries; it assesses young people’s awareness of existing state and public support measures for employment, determines the effectiveness and efficiency of existing mechanisms and forms of promoting youth employment, and examines the degree of influence of various factors on young people’s entry into the labor market. The authors note that in current conditions, investments in youth in the form of support and guidance throughout their professional and career development can create a synergistic effect for successfully providing personnel for economic sectors in different countries. The value and novelty of the study lie in the fact that the authors provide a detailed interpretation of the results of the second wave of an international sociological study, within which, on new empirical material, international trends are identified and systematized in young people’s assessments of the labor market, their awareness of state and public support measures, and their preferences regarding forms of employm…
