title: Papering over the cracks: How residents and professionals experience market-led regeneration in four English coastal towns
abstract: English coastal towns were once celebrated for their salutogenic qualities; today, however, many experience persistent deprivation and poor health. Successive governments have responded with market-led regeneration programmes focused on physical infrastructure, yet health inequalities remain entrenched. This paper draws on interviews and focus groups with 140 residents and local professionals in Hartlepool, Blackpool, Hastings, and Torbay, conducted in 2023 as part of a wider study of the north-south health divide. Across all four towns participants experienced market-led regeneration as highly visible but superficial, producing short-lived improvements to the built environment while leaving the structural drivers of poor health untouched. Residents described schemes designed for tourists and wealthier incomers, reshaping their towns around middle-class tastes while obscuring poverty. Professionals recognised these limits but felt compelled to compete for whatever funding was available. I interpret these narratives through three concepts. Slow violence captures how harm accumulates across decades of cosmetic investment, symbolic violence highlights the devaluing of local culture and residents’ needs, and cruel optimism helps explain why people stay attached to the promise of revitalisation despite this approach consistently failing to deliver. I argue that market-led regenerati…

title: Effect of Strategic Management Practices on Market Performance of Clothing SMEs in Nakuru Central Business District, Kenya
abstract: Clothing SMEs in Nakuru CBD contribute to employment and local economic growth, yet they continue to experience fluctuating sales, intense competition from boutiques, second-hand clothing traders, chain stores and online sellers, and pressure on profitability. Limited sector-specific evidence exists on whether structured strategic management practices improve their market outcomes. Consequently, the study examined the effect of strategic management practices on the market performance of clothing small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in Nakuru Central Business District (CBD), Kenya. Specifically, the study assessed the effects of strategic planning, goal setting, resource allocation and environmental scanning practices on market performance. The study was anchored on the Resource-Based View, Goal-Setting Theory and Dynamic Capabilities Theory and adopted a descriptive correlational research design. The target population was 132 owners, supervisors and sales staff drawn from 16 licensed clothing SMEs. A sample of 112 respondents was selected through census and stratified random sampling. Primary data was collected using a structured questionnaire, and 94 usable questionnaires were returned (83.9% response rate). Data was analysed in SPSS Version 29 using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation and multiple regression analysis. Findings revealed that all four practices had posit…

title: Development and Preliminary Verification of Specific KASP Markers for Mango Resistance to Bacterial Angular Leaf Spot
abstract: Bacterial angular leaf spot, caused by Xanthomonas citri pv. mangiferaeindicae (Xcm), is an important disease that constrains mango production. Resistance-associated molecular markers can improve the efficiency of resistant germplasm screening and accelerate mango breeding; however, such markers remain limited for bacterial angular leaf spot. In this study, transcriptome and whole-genome resequencing data from the highly resistant cultivar ‘Renong No. 1’ and the highly susceptible cultivar ‘Keitt’ were reanalyzed to identify nonsynonymous single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in candidate resistance-related genes. Among 86 candidate SNPs converted into Kompetitive Allele-Specific PCR (KASP) assays, 37 generated clear and stable genotype clusters in 25 mango accessions with known resistance phenotypes. SNP26 showed high consistency with the resistance phenotypes of these accessions and was subsequently used to genotype 322 mango germplasm accessions, which were separated into two genotype groups containing 34 and 288 accessions, respectively. Based on the SNP26 genotyping results, 72 accessions were selected for indoor fruit-puncture inoculation and classified into five resistance levels according to lesion development. SNP26 was located at position 1,299,510 on chromosome 15 within the coding region of HSP83A. The alleles were G in ‘Keitt’ and A in ‘Renong No. 1’, resulting in…

title: Interaction of electricity futures prices with economic and financial indicators: A case study of Türkiye
abstract: Purpose — This study examines the relationship between macroeconomic variables and monthly base-load electricity futures prices. In particular, it investigates how exchange rates, electricity consumption, inflation, Brent oil prices, and interest rates influence electricity futures contracts in financial markets.Methods — Using monthly data from January 2016 to July 2025, the study applies the Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) bounds testing approach to analyze short-run and long-run dynamics. This method is well suited to examining relationships among variables with different integration orders and allows simultaneous estimation of equilibrium and adjustment processes.Findings — The empirical results show that Brent oil prices, electricity consumption, and exchange rates positively affect electricity futures prices in the long run, whereas interest rates have a negative effect. Short-run estimates largely confirm these long-run relationships, indicating consistency across time horizons.Implication — These findings have implications for investors, energy market participants, and policymakers by highlighting the sensitivity of electricity futures prices to key macroeconomic indicators, thereby informing pricing, hedging, and energy policy decisions.Originality — This study contributes to the literature by providing comprehensive empirical evidence on the dynamic interactions…

title: Herding Effect in Public Mutual Funds under Extreme Market Conditions: A Literature Review
abstract: The concentrated trading of public mutual funds may affect stock prices, liquidity and market stability. Identifying changes in herding behavior in extreme markets and their asymmetry helps to explain the relationship between institutional transactions and market volatility. The existing conclusions are influenced by the definition of behavior, measurement methods and market-state classification, which motivates this analytical literature review. This study compares what the LSV, Wermers and Sias methods identify and what data they require, examines formation mechanisms in relation to information learning, career concerns, relative performance and fund flows, and compares international evidence and research on Chinese public mutual funds along three dimensions: market conditions, trading direction and market pressure. The analysis shows that contemporaneous concentration, directional differences and intertemporal following belong to different measurement dimensions, and the results cannot be directly compared. Changes in herding behavior under extreme market conditions depend on the information environment, transaction constraints and fund characteristics, and common transactions cannot directly prove intentional imitation. Future research should match the market conditions and data frequency, compare different indicators under a unified sample, and identify the source of behav…

title: Coupling and Coordinated Development of the Digital Economy and Economic Resilience in the Pearl River Delta under the Background of a Unified National Market
abstract: Against the backdrop of China’s ongoing efforts to build a unified national market, the coordinated evolution of the digital economy and economic resilience has become central to regional high-quality development. Using panel data for nine cities in the Pearl River Delta from 2012 to 2022, this study constructs evaluation indicator systems for the digital economy and economic resilience, and applies the entropy weight method, coupling coordination model, obstacle degree model, and spatial visualization to examine their development levels, coordination dynamics, spatiotemporal patterns, and key constraints. The results show that both systems improved over the study period, with faster and more volatile growth in the digital economy and steadier gains in economic resilience. Spatially, both systems show a core–periphery pattern, with the three subregions of Shenzhen–Dongguan–Huizhou, Guangzhou–Foshan–Zhaoqing, and Zhuhai–Zhongshan–Jiangmen forming an increasingly distinct spatial gradient in the later years. High-value digital economy areas are concentrated in Guangzhou, Shenzhen, and nearby cities, while economic resilience shows a more stable hierarchy, with manufacturing-based cities such as Foshan and Dongguan gradually catching up and peripheral cities improving more slowly. Coupling coordination also improved overall, though with periodic fluctuations, and the improvement i…

STG-Mixer: A Multi-Region, Multi-Step Forecasting Network for Hand, Foot, and Mouth Disease with Multi-Timescale Feature Extraction and Spatial Association Learning
abstract: Accurate forecasting of hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) incidence is crucial for effective prevention and control. However, existing multi-region HFMD forecasting models remain limited in jointly capturing multi-timescale temporal patterns and interregional spatial associations, which affects multi-step forecasting performance. In this study, we propose Spatiotemporal Graph Mixer (STG-Mixer), a multi-region, multi-step forecasting network for HFMD based on multi-timescale feature extraction and spatial association learning. STG-Mixer constructs a graph structure based on interregional adjacency relationships and adopts a dual-branch spatiotemporal encoder consisting of an Adaptive Fusion Spatial Branch (AF-SB) and a Multi-Scale Energy-Gated Temporal Branch (MEG-TB). Specifically, AF-SB employs a dual-layer Temporal Graph Convolutional Network (T-GCN), TimeKAN block, and Orthogonal Residual Gated Fusion mechanism to learn spatial representations, while MEG-TB extracts and adaptively weights temporal features across multiple scales using dilated temporal convolutions and an energy-gated mechanism. The learned spatial and temporal representations are fused and fed into an autoregressive decoder for multi-step forecasting. Experiments on HFMD surveillance and meteorological data from 47 prefectures in Japan demonstrate that STG-Mixer outperforms baseline models in one- to four…

title: Preoperative coronal tibiofemoral subluxation does not affect 2-year outcomes after mobile-bearing medial unicompartmental knee arthroplasty for anteromedial osteoarthritis
abstract: Abstract Introduction Coronal tibiofemoral subluxation (CTFS) is frequently observed in patients with medial knee osteoarthritis; however, its clinical relevance and the acceptable degree of CTFS when considering unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA) remain unclear. This study aimed to determine whether preoperative CTFS influences short-term postoperative clinical outcomes in patients with anteromedial osteoarthritis (AMOA) undergoing medial UKA. Methods In this retrospective cohort study, 457 consecutive knees with AMOA who underwent mobile-bearing UKA performed at a single center between August 2016 and May 2023 were analyzed. CTFS, defined as medial translation of the femur relative to the tibia, was measured on preoperative weight-bearing anteroposterior radiographs and expressed as the percentage of tibial plateau width. Patients were categorized into mild (0–5%), moderate (≥ 5% to < 10%), and severe (≥ 10%) CTFS groups. Clinical outcomes were evaluated using the Oxford Knee Score (OKS) preoperatively and at 3 months, 1 and 2 years postoperatively. Pairwise comparisons of changes in OKS were performed using a general linear model with Bonferroni-adjusted post hoc tests, and adjusted mean differences were calculated controlling for age, sex, body mass index, and preoperative OKS. Results At 2 years, mean OKS improvements were 16.6 ± 8.9, 14.8 ± 8.3, and 16.0 ± 9.3 in th…

title: Climate Variability, Crop Yields, and Staple-Food Price Volatility in Pakistan: Provincial Panel Evidence
abstract: Climate variability influences agricultural productivity and staple-food markets; however, comparable provincial evidence from Pakistan is limited. This retrospective ecological panel analysis included Punjab, Sindh, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and Balochistan. ERA5-Land-based annual temperature and precipitation data spanned 2019 to 2024. Official provincial wheat yields were available for harvest years 2019 to 2024 (24 province-year observations), and rice yields for 2019 to 2023 (20 observations). January retail prices of wheat flour and broken basmati rice were collected for 2021 to 2025 from Lahore, Karachi, Peshawar, and Quetta, serving as urban market proxies for the provinces. Yield–price panels comprised 16 wheat observations (2021 to 2024) and 12 rice observations (2021 to 2023). Two-way fixed-effects models with HC3 robust standard errors assessed climate–yield and yield–price associations. Price fluctuations were defined as absolute January-to-January logarithmic changes, rather than within-year volatility or province-wide average prices. Wheat yields increased by 26.4% in Balochistan, 21.4% in Punjab, and 5.7% in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, but declined by 7.3% in Sindh. Balochistan’s rice yield decreased sharply in 2022 before recovering. Annual food-price movements varied by city and commodity. Neither climate–yield nor yield–price coefficients reached statistical significance; …

title: Comparative evaluation of ARIMA and ETS models for short-term wind speed forecasting across twelve meteorological stations in Pakistan using the expanding-window method
abstract: This article presents a statistical forecasting framework for wind speed using two well-known classical forecasting models, the autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) and the exponential smoothing state space (ETS) models with the naïve model as a benchmark for comparison. Twelve meteorological stations across Pakistan were selected based on data availability and analyzed using a comprehensive and rigorous expanding-window data-splitting method. The expanding window method iteratively extends the training data over ten successive splits, with each split used to generate seven-day-ahead wind speed predictions. This approach allows the forecasting performance of the models to be evaluated over multiple forecast origins while progressively incorporating newly available observations into the training data. Root mean square error (RMSE) and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) were used to examine the predictive behavior of all models and to evaluate their consistency and responsiveness over time. Model comparisons were further assessed by the Diebold-Mariano (DM) test on forecast errors for each model. The ARIMA model performed better (based on RMSE) for short-term wind speed forecasting at seven stations in Pakistan while the ETS model performed better at two stations and performed equally at three stations covered by this study. The DM test also supports the RMSE- and …

title: Exchange rate pass-through effects on consumer price inflation and macroeconomic shocks in Nigeria
abstract: Purpose — The objective of this research is to reassess the elasticity of exchange rate pass-through, recompute the exchange-rate pass-through elasticity, and examine inflation dynamics in the Nigerian economy.Methods — The paper uses a structural vector autoregression (SVAR) model to examine the effect of macroeconomic shocks on exchange-rate pass-through to domestic consumer price inflation, using data from 1986 to 2021. Findings — The results show that exchange-rate pass-through to consumer price inflation in Nigeria is low and incomplete. Moreover, the speed of adjustment to structural shocks, such as exchange rate, output, monetary policy rate, and the money supply, is fast. The effects of such shocks are highly volatile and therefore can potentially distort the status quo. Implication — The forecast variance decomposition results show that consumer price inflation own shocks, positive money supply shocks, and output shocks dominate other factors in explaining consumer price inflation in the Nigerian economy. Therefore, Nigeria should pursue more effective monetary policy through deliberate action by the monetary authority. The authorities should adopt a fully-fledged inflation-targeting framework. Originality — In this study, we use SVAR to identify the structural exchange rate shock and the monetary policy transmission channel, guided by ex-ante, theory-justified restric…

title: Compute-Constrained Adaptive Electricity Load Forecasting via Offline Policy Learning
abstract: Background: Electricity load forecasting services must allocate inference across models with different accuracy and compute costs under a shared daily budget. Methods: We evaluate offline policies using only pre-call information, complete-day rolling folds, outcome-time embargoes, and a reservation rule that preserves minimum service for later origins. Four public datasets are tested at four horizons and three budgets, comparing contextual allocation with fitted Q iteration (FQI), double FQI, and neural FQI against a feasible static forecaster. Results: All 960 formal policy evaluations satisfy the budget. The mean gains in mean absolute error (MAE) are 9.22%, 7.37%, 7.77%, and 3.83% for the four methods, respectively. The contextual gains are positive on Steel, Tetouan, and Open Power System Data (OPSD) but negative on UCI ElectricityLoadDiagrams (UCI–ECL). A disjoint deployment gate yields a 10.63% aggregate gain at 51.7% coverage with six harmful activations and 61 missed beneficial cases; this empirical risk-control filter is not a safety guarantee. The lightweight multilayer perceptron (MLP) extension and sequential audits find no uniform benefit from a larger action pool or deeper Bellman backups; FQI improves over contextual allocation only at the smallest tested switching penalty in the cache-state experiment. Conclusions: Offline policy learning can support budget-feas…

Uncertainty, Volatility, and Renewable Energy Stock Returns: Evidence From Regime‐Dependent and Machine‐Learning Forecasting Models
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines the predictability of renewable energy stock returns under economic, financial, and policy uncertainty within a real‐time forecasting framework. Using monthly data from May 2007 to May 2025, we compare conventional econometric models, shrinkage estimators, machine‐learning algorithms, and regime‐dependent forecasting models using a recursive expanding‐window design. Forecast performance is evaluated using statistical accuracy measures, robustness analyses, and an economic portfolio evaluation. The results show that nonlinear forecasting methods consistently outperform conventional linear benchmarks. Gradient boosting achieves the lowest forecast errors, while principal component regression provides stable performance across alternative evaluation designs. Regime‐dependent forecasting models improve directional prediction during periods of heightened financial uncertainty but generate more modest gains in forecast accuracy. Predictor‐importance analysis identifies financial‐market volatility as the dominant source of forecasting information, followed by oil‐market volatility and broader policy uncertainty. Overall, the findings demonstrate that combining multiple sources of uncertainty with flexible forecasting methods improves both statistical forecasting performance and the economic value of investment decisions. Strengthening Financial Management Capacity to Support Community Income and Sustainable Ecotourism Development in Kairatu, West Seram Regency, Maluku
abstract: Community-based ecotourism offers meaningful opportunities for local communities to strengthen their livelihoods while preserving the natural and cultural resources of their region. In Kairatu, West Seram Regency, the development of tourism-related microenterprises presents promising economic opportunities. However, limited financial management skills remain a challenge for small business owners in managing income, monitoring expenses, and planning for business sustainability. This community service initiative focuses on strengthening the financial management capacity of microentrepreneurs supporting ecotourism through participatory training and mentoring. The activities cover basic financial recordkeeping, separation of personal and business finances, cash flow management, cost calculation, and profit evaluation. Field documentation also highlights the coastal environment, recreational facilities, and tourism-supporting services that contribute to Kairatu’s local economic potential. The initiative emphasizes the importance of accessible and practical financial knowledge in helping community members make informed business decisions. Strengthening these skills is expected to support more sustainable microenterprises and encourage greater local participation in ecotourism development. Molecular Dynamics Simulations of Pseudomonas aeruginosa Membranes Aid in Understanding Resistance Mechanism to Polymyxin B1
abstract: One of the major causes for hospital acquired infections is multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa strains. Polymyxins are a group of lipopeptide antibiotics used as a last-line resort for treatment of Gram-negative infections. Polymyxins initially target Lipid A’s of lipopolysaccharides in the bacterial outer membrane via both electrostatic and hydrophobic interactions. Resistance to polymyxins in P. aeruginosa includes modification of Lipid A’s to attenuate the interactions with polymyxins but to date our understanding of underlying mechanisms is still limited. This study was conducted to investigate the molecular mechanisms of Polymyxin B1 interacting with outer membranes of P. aeruginosa strains including wild-type strain PAK (Polymyxin B1 MIC = 1 mg/L) control and treated and PAKpmrB6 strain (MIC = 8 mg/L) control and treated. Molecular models of PAK as well as PAKpmrB6 membranes were established, and each of those four membrane compositions were simulated as eight independent simulation systems, excluding and including six Polymyxin B1 molecules. The created membrane systems were evaluated running Molecular Dynamic (MD) Simulations for up to 1150 ns each. MD simulations showed that different membrane compositions and Polymyxin B1 interaction affect the general membrane behaviour. In addition, Polymyxin B1 interacts with mutant PAKpmrB6 membranes more slowly and penetr…

title: Mechanism‐Driven Purification of High‐Purity Quartz: Impurity Speciation, Surface Chemistry, and Advanced Beneficiation Technologies
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐purity quartz (HPQ) is essential for semiconductor manufacturing, photovoltaics, optical systems, and other advanced technologies, where even trace impurities can compromise material performance. Despite extensive research on quartz beneficiation, the mechanisms governing impurity removal, interfacial reactions, and purification efficiency remain poorly understood. This review establishes a mechanism‐driven framework linking geological provenance, impurity speciation, surface chemistry, and purification performance. Impurities are classified as surface‐bound species, mineral inclusions, and lattice‐substituted elements, each posing distinct removal challenges, affecting optical transparency, electronic defects, and thermal stability. Emphasizes silanol groups, surface charge, adsorption, and interfacial reactions that govern flotation selectivity and leaching kinetics. Conventional beneficiation and advanced pretreatments, including ultrasonic activation, thermal roasting, and microwave‐assisted processing, are critically evaluated for their roles in liberating impurities, modifying defects, and enhancing reactivity. Emerging strategies, particularly chlorination roasting and hybrid acid‐thermal treatments, are assessed for removing refractory impurities, along with their environmental impacts and industrial scalability. Key research gaps include limited atomistic…

abstract: The article investigates the methodological foundations for the formation of the economic mechanism of sustainable enterprise development under conditions of increasing economic, social, environmental, institutional, and technological challenges. It is substantiated that ensuring sustainable development requires the transition from the fragmented application of individual management tools to the creation of an integrated economic mechanism capable of coordinating strategic objectives, management functions, resource provision, and expected development outcomes. The purpose of the study is to substantiate the methodological foundations for forming the economic mechanism of sustainable enterprise development and to develop its conceptual model. The research is based on the application of the systems, process, integrated, adaptive, and stakeholder approaches, as well as methods of scientific abstraction, analysis, synthesis, comparison, systematization, and conceptual modelling. The study clarifies the essence of the concept of the economic mechanism of sustainable enterprise development, which is interpreted as an adaptive system of interconnected principles, functions, methods, instruments, management levers, and resources aimed at ensuring balanced economic, social, environmental, innovative, and institutional development of an enterprise. Intelligent energy management of a novel non-isolated bidirectional dual-input single-output converter for electric vehicle applications
abstract: For use in electric vehicle (EV) applications, this paper suggests a non-isolated bidirectional Dual-Input Single-Output (DISO) DC–DC converter with an intelligent energy management method. The proposed converter integrates photovoltaic (PV) and battery energy sources in a single power conversion structure, which results in fewer components, higher efficiency and bidirectional power flow capability. The converter is designed based on a two-phase interleaved boost topology with a relay-assisted reconfiguration stage that facilitates flexible source selection, battery charging/discharging and regenerative braking operation. A Modified Deep Neural Network (MODNN) based intelligent energy management strategy is proposed to enhance energy utilization and adaptive power sharing. The proposed MODNN modifies a conventional single-task feedforward DNN by introducing a shared-trunk, multi-head architecture that jointly predicts the discrete operating mode and the continuous converter duty ratios through a composite classification-regression loss function, benchmarked against recent machine-learning baselines (k-NN, a bagged neural-network ensemble, and LSTM) under identical training/test conditions. In the proposed MODNN framework, the PV voltage, PV current, battery state-of-charge, battery voltage, and load demand information are used to decide the optimal operating mode and power flow…

title: A Data-Driven Multi-Objective Optimization Approach for Improving Energy and Comfort Performance in Residential Buildings
abstract: Examining energy-related issues and comfort conditions in residential buildings is essential for achieving sustainable development. Accordingly, this study aims to optimize building envelope design parameters—including air-tightness values derived from empirical measurements—to strike a balance between energy consumption, thermal comfort, and visual comfort. A multi-stage, systematic methodology is proposed, featuring a hybrid artificial intelligence-based framework for prediction and optimization, grounded in building performance simulations. A BlowerDoor test was conducted on the residential building under study, and the results were integrated into a building performance model. Data generated through these simulations were used to compare the performance of various machine learning meta-models, including Artificial Neural Networks, Support Vector Regression (SVR), and XGBoost. The SVR model, which demonstrated the lowest error rate and highest reliability across most objectives, was selected as the meta-model for the optimization phase. This model served as the objective function for a multi-objective optimization process carried out using the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II). The results of this surrogate-model-based optimization indicate a 21.69% reduction in energy consumption, alongside improvements of 17.2% in visual comfort and 20% in thermal comfor…

title: Comparative Evaluation of Cold Plasma‐Assisted Infrared and Hot Air Drying of Yam: Drying Kinetics, Energy Consumption, and Quality Attributes
abstract: ABSTRACT Conventional hot air drying (HAD) of yam is associated with prolonged processing time, high energy consumption, and quality deterioration caused by extended thermal exposure and nonuniform moisture removal. Infrared drying (IRD) can accelerate energy transfer, but rapid energy input does not necessarily eliminate limitations associated with internal moisture migration in high‐moisture plant tissues. In this study, cold plasma (CP) pretreatment was combined with IRD to improve the drying performance of yam, and its effects were systematically compared with HAD, IRD, and CP‐assisted HAD (HAD + CP). Drying temperature evolution, drying kinetics, energy consumption, drying uniformity, structural and microstructural characteristics, and selected quality attributes were evaluated. Compared with HAD, IRD increased the drying rate by 37.5% and reduced energy consumption from 8847.23 to 6524.625 kJ/mol. CP pretreatment further accelerated moisture removal and improved drying uniformity, with the final moisture‐content relative standard deviation decreasing from 25.23% for HAD to 13.10% for IRD + CP. Microstructural observations indicated that CP‐assisted drying reduced excessive tissue collapse and maintained a relatively more intact cellular morphology. Consequently, IRD + CP achieved the highest rehydration ratio of 2.76, and improved retention of total flavonoids compared wi…

title: Investigation on the Anti-Freezing and the Heat Preservation Characteristics for a Semi-Underground Water Storage Tank
abstract: In cold regions, semi-underground water storage tanks (WSTs) have problems such as low water temperatures and local freezing during winter operation. For its anti-freezing and heat preservation, relevant theoretical analysis and technical exploration are urgently needed. The study employs numerical simulation to investigate the effects of different thermal insulation measures on the anti-freezing performance of WSTs. Firstly, the numerical models were established to analyze the temperature distribution characteristics of the water body under low-temperature ambient conditions. Secondly, an experimental platform was also constructed, and the numerical models were validated through experimental measurements. On this basis, a 1200 h transient numerical simulation was conducted for a large-scale semi-underground WST. Finally, comparative analyses were performed on temperature variations between the uninsulated and variably insulated cases, and insulation layers of varying thicknesses and materials. The results indicate that significant heat dissipation occurs through the top and sidewalls of the tank if there is no insulation, leading to a continuous decline in water temperature and a risk of localized freezing. As the insulation thickness increases, the internal temperature of the tank gradually rises. However, when the thickness reaches 150 mm, further increases yield only margin…

title: Evaluation of the Postharvest Storage Performance of Six Onion (Allium cepa L.) Varieties under Ambient Storage Conditions in Bambey, Senegal
abstract: Onion (Allium cepa L.) storability is important for reducing postharvest losses and maintaining market availability in Senegal. This study evaluated the postharvest performance of six onion varieties under ambient storage conditions in Bambey. The varieties were Violet de Galmi, Gandiol+, Safari, Texas Early Grano, Red Bombay and VDG American. Field production was undertaken during the 2021–2022 cool off-season using a randomised complete block design with three replicates. After harvest, bulb dry matter content was determined, and weight loss, sprouting and rot were assessed during storage. Dry matter content did not differ significantly among varieties (p = 0.069), although VDG American recorded the highest numerical value (13.24%) and Texas Early Grano the lowest (8.69%). In the storage analysis, VDG American exhibited the lowest numerical weight loss (10.91%), with no recorded sprouting or rot. Safari also had relatively low weight loss (11.61%), no sprouting and a rot rate of 2.22%. Red Bombay showed the highest sprouting (24.33%) and rot (31.11%), while Texas Early Grano had the highest numerical weight loss (32.49%). Varietal differences in sprouting were significant (p < 0.001), whereas those in weight loss and rot were not significant at the 5% level. Under the conditions assessed, VDG American and Safari showed favourable storage performance, although further evaluati…

title: Financial Fitness for Small Businesses in Bayelsa State: Role of Cost Management Strategies in Driving Revenue Growth
abstract: This study examines the relationship between cost management strategies and revenue growth of small businesses in Bayelsa State. Specifically, it investigates the impact of Activity-Based Costing (ABC), Cost Reduction Strategies, and Pricing Decisions on revenue growth. A quantitative research design was adopted, and data were collected from 228 small business owners using structured questionnaires. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation analysis, and hypothesis testing were employed to analyze the data. The correlation results showed a significant positive relationship between Activity-Based Costing and revenue growth (r = 0.643, p = 0.000), Cost Reduction Strategies and revenue growth (r = 0.839, p = 0.000), and Pricing Decisions and revenue growth (r = 0.641, p = 0.000). These findings suggest that cost management strategies play a crucial role in driving business performance. Based on these results, the study recommends that small businesses adopt structured cost management practices, such as ABC and expense tracking, to enhance operational efficiency. Additionally, businesses should implement datadriven pricing models and regularly review their pricing strategies to remain competitive. The study also highlights the need for government and financial institutions to provide financial support and capacity-building programs to help small businesses implement effective cos…

Two-Step Crystallization Process Strategy for Cannabidiol Isolation at Higher Yields
abstract: Abstract We describe a Two-step DMA-MediAted Crystallization method (2DMAC-method) for the first time. This two-step strategy for the purification of cannabidiol (CBD) utilizes N,N-dimethylacetamide (DMA) to form an isolable CBD·2DMA solid solvate, which precipitates from cooled heptane. The 2DMAC-method is selective for CBD, as the solvate is free of tetrahydrocannabinol (THC). DMA can subsequently be removed via aqueous washing, and the free CBD is crystallized from heptane. Overall, the 2DMAC-method delivers higher recovery and tighter impurity control compared to a standard industry method. Across three samples, final CBD recoveries averaged 61% with the 2DMAC-method, versus 48% for a standard heptane crystallization. All CBD isolates obtained via the solvate reached ≥97.5% CBD, with nondetectable THC by HPLC, LC-MS, and NMR, in line with common method purities. Additionally, the 2DMAC-method was more effective in removing cannabidivarin (CBDV) and the toxic, oxidative impurity HU-331 (CBD hydroxyquinone).

title: Tail Risk and Earnings Management: The Role of Gender Diversity and Environmental–Social Reporting in International Banking
abstract: ABSTRACT We examine the impacts of earnings management on the tail risks of banks using a dataset of 3297 bank‐year observations across 157 publicly traded commercial banks from 12 countries, covering 2002–2022. Our findings suggest that banks engaging in earnings management activities exhibit higher tail risks. However, this relationship is moderated by two critical factors: board gender diversity and environmental–social (ES) reporting. Specifically, our analysis indicates that the elevated tail risks associated with higher levels of earnings management can be mitigated by stronger female representation on boards or through higher ES ratings. These insights provide important financial implications and policy guidelines for multiple stakeholders engaging with the international banking sector and ES seeking to strengthen governance framework structures while mitigating risk‐taking.

title: Ultra-broadband integrated asymmetric power splitters for the mid-infrared based on refractive-index-engineered femtosecond laser written Y-junction
abstract: Abstract As the mid-infrared range finds increasing interest in numerous applications, the demand for integrated optical components operating at these wavelengths is becoming ever more critical. In this work, we present a novel method for fabricating 1×2 beam splitters with precisely controlled power distribution among the two output arms. The devices are realized using femtosecond laser writing in chalcogenide glass and the output power balance is tuned by inducing refractive index variations (∆n) of different magnitudes in the splitting region of each arm. The power ratio between the two outputs can be continuously adjusted from 50:50 to 95:5 without introducing additional losses. The components are evaluated at a wavelength of 4.5 µm, but measurements using a supercontinuum source show that the coupling ratio remains constant over an unprecedented spectral range exceeding 1 µm. Finally, these results are extended to three-dimensional components with the fabrication of a 1×6 splitter featuring controlled power distribution across the output arms.

title: The power of visual perspective and language arousal: Tailoring short videos for tourism activities
abstract: Tourism short videos have become a crucial tool for sparking travel inspiration. However, how to integrate different short-video elements to enhance marketing effectiveness remains underexplored. Grounded in the elaboration likelihood model, this study investigates the matching effects and underlying mechanisms between visual perspective (first-person vs. third-person) and tourism activity type (challenging vs. relaxing). The research approach contains one secondary data analysis and three scenario-based experiments. Our findings indicate that in tourism short videos, relaxing activities combined with a third-person perspective evoke aesthetic pleasure, whereas challenging activities paired with a first-person perspective elicit awe, both of which enhance travel inspiration. Additionally, language arousal moderates the aforementioned matching effect and its indirect effect on travel inspiration through awe. This article enriches theoretical research on tourism short video marketing by confirming the integration framework of visual and language elements, and offers practical insights for different tourism activity marketing.

title: Robust Sliding-Mode Control of High-Power DC Motors Under Internal Parameter Disturbances
abstract: This paper proposes a sliding-mode control (SMC) strategy to enhance the dynamic performance and disturbance rejection of high-power DC motors subjected to internal parameter variations, such as armature resistance changes due to temperature rise and inductance fluctuations from magnetic saturation. Conventional PID controllers exhibit limited effectiveness under such conditions, leading to compromised stability and increased steady-state error. A mathematical model of the motor is derived, and a sliding-mode controller is designed to ensure rapid convergence to a desired sliding surface, guaranteeing robust stability. The system is implemented and tested in Matlab/Simulink. Simulation results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed SMC over a traditional PID controller. The SMC effectively eliminates overshoot, achieves settling time 0.01 seconds following a disturbance, and reduces steady-state error by 0.3%. The controller shows significant robustness against internal parameter disturbances, making it a suitable candidate for high-performance industrial DC drive applications.

title: A weather integrated neural symbolic dispatch framework for power system operational security
abstract: Abstract Modern power systems face unprecedented challenges from rapid digitalization, electrification of new sectors, and increasing renewable integration. These changes demand real-time operational decisions based on accurate weather forecasting, as traditional dispatch methods cannot handle the speed and complexity of weather-driven variability in renewable generation. This paper thus proposes the Weather-Integrated Neural-Symbolic Dispatch System (WINDS), a novel methodological framework designed to incorporate weather-driven uncertainties into power system dispatch decisions. The WINDS framework combines weather forecasting and neuro-symbolic reasoning, where neural learning methods address weather-related uncertainties and symbolic methods enforce system security constraints, to provide operators with actionable dispatch strategies. Through a detailed set of study cases comprising normal operations, extreme weather events, missing data conditions, and multi-scenario risk analysis, evaluated on both a controlled experiment and measured wind and load data from the Danish DK1 bidding zone, WINDS reduces operational cost by 11.4% to 26.7% compared to static climatology-based dispatch depending on weather volatility, while reducing constraint-violation volume by more than 80% relative to forecast-only dispatch and substantially limiting violations during a measured extreme ram…

title: Digital retail management
Plot morphology and retail patterns: a morphological assessment of peripheral retail clusters
abstract: Retail clusters represent an important spatial expression of urban vitality, yet how urban form relates to retail patterns remains underexplored, particularly at the plot scale where compositional and configurational attributes intersect. This research examines how plot-level structural and network-based contextual attributes are associated with retail density, agglomeration, and diversity in peripheral areas, and whether they correspond with retail cluster form. The Morphological Assessment Framework (MAF) weights plot at- tributes by their spatially varying associations with each retail metric, estimated through multiscale geographically weighted regression. Using municipal plot data and retail point-of-interest data, 19 peripheral clusters (5064 plots) were selected from DBSCAN-identified clusters (120, 200, and 216 m) in Ankara, Helsinki, and Vilnius. Retail diversity is positively associated with the configurational character of plots in all cities (0.13–0.60), and retail density with their compositional character, most strongly in Helsinki (0.46). The MAF indicates that these associations are configuration-led in Ankara, composition-led in Helsinki, and intermediate in Vilnius, while cluster form varies between cities rather than with plot morphology. As an analytical framework, the MAF identifies which morphological dimension is most closely associated with retail vitali…

title: Optimized, sustainable and scalable strategy for producing disodium crocetinate from Crocus sativus L. stigmas
abstract: Introduction Saffron ( Crocus sativus L.), one of the world’s most valuable spices, has significant potential as a source of bioactive compounds for food, pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, and cosmetic applications. Among its constituents, crocetin has attracted increasing attention because its sodium salt, disodium crocetinate, exhibits much higher water solubility and is of interest in pharmaceutical sciences. This study aimed to develop and optimize a potentially scalable, non-chromatographic approach for the high-purity production of crocetin and its water-soluble disodium salt from saffron crocins, while simultaneously recovering safranal as a valuable co-product. Methods An integrated and sustainable process was developed for the production of disodium crocetinate through sequential conversion of saffron crocins by hydrolysis, purification, and crystallization. Hydrolysis of total crocin extracted from saffron stigmas was optimized using response surface methodology (RSM). In parallel, safranal was concentrated and isolated by liquid–liquid extraction. The crocetin produced after hydrolysis was purified using a non-chromatographic procedure consisting of aqueous extraction for carbohydrate removal, methanolic extraction of polyphenolic impurities, and recrystallization in dimethylformamide. In addition, the greenness parameters were calculated for the process of purification…

title: METHODOLOGICAL APPROACH TO FORMING A SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT STRATEGY FOR INDUSTRIAL SMES BASED ON A MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
abstract: Industrial SMEs link sustainable development with digital transformation, but often build their strategy by a universal scheme, the same for all dimensions, and a limited budget is often spent where the lag is not the greatest. The aim of the article is to develop a methodological approach to forming a sustainable development strategy for industrial SMEs based on a management system linking sustainability indicators with digital maturity. The study uses the systems and scenario approaches, a scenario matrix built on the level of sustainable development and the level of digital support, a coupling matrix of sustainability dimensions and digital maturity components, and selection of digital initiatives by their contribution under a budget constraint. A six-stage algorithm is proposed. The management scenario is determined twice, for the enterprise as a whole and for each of seven dimensions, which gives a scenario profile. Each dimension receives a target at the boundary of the next level and a deadline depending on its digital support. Dimensions in the stabilization scenario receive basic non-digital measures and are excluded from the priority calculation for digital initiatives. The portfolio is formed by the specific contribution of initiatives to reducing the lag, considering the maturity already achieved by components. In an with a budget of 8 million rubles, three of five …

title: Correction: Optimal adjuvant strategy in intermediate-risk cervical cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis
@veedfox Instagram Account’s Digital Communication Strategy for Building Brand Awareness
abstract: The rapid development of digital technology has transformed the way organizations communicate with their audiences. Social media, plays a vital role in building relationships, and strengthening brand awareness. @veedfox, an independent digital media platform, uses Instagram to share news and educational content aimed at a young audience. This study examines the digital communication strategy of the @veedfox Instagram account in relation to brand awareness. It employs a descriptive qualitative approach, drawing on Middleton’s communication strategy framework—communicator, message, medium, audience, and effect—and David Aaker’s Brand Awareness Pyramid. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, observation, and documentation. The findings indicate that @veedfox uses a structured communication strategy characterized by role division, audience-oriented messages, consistent visual presentation, and the use of Instagram features, particularly Feed and Reels. The findings suggest that the account has established Brand Recognition and Brand Recall among the interviewed audience, while Top of Mind has not been consistently achieved. The study highlights the importance of connecting communication processes with audience-based evidence of brand awareness.

title: Research on Basketball Defensive Strategy Modeling Based on Movement Trajectory Data
abstract: In the process of half-court defense, the defending team often has a weak link in the defense due to the slow rotation speed, resulting in a certain gap. In order to formulate a reasonable defense plan, this paper uses the NBA tracking data and builds a defense scheduling model based on MIP. In the study, the planar coordinates of the players are extracted, and the movement speed is analyzed. Voronoi diagram is used to calculate the open space of the offensive players, and the risk of defensive breakdown is calculated. In order to achieve the goal of minimizing the total rotation time of the whole team, Python is used to calculate and solve the problem. The results show that the defense plan formulated by the model can make up for the shortcomings of the traditional man-to-man defense. When facing a ball handler with a higher threat, the system can automatically generate a double team strategy, and the offensive players in the low-efficiency scoring area can be left open. By introducing physical coordinates and spatial geometric data, this paper can provide reference for the formulation of defense plan.
venue: Journal of Education, Behavior and Humanities

title: Merging Reaction to Cognition: A Hybrid Cognitive Strategy for Odor Source Localization in Natural Environments
abstract: ABSTRACT Chemical pollutants released into the environment are transported by turbulent flows, generating complex and intermittent plume structures that threaten ecosystems and human health. Rapid localization of emission sources is critical, and field robots equipped with chemical sensors provide a viable means to perform this task. Nevertheless, inferring source location from sensor readings remains difficult due to sparse detections and the absence of reliable concentration gradients. Existing approaches broadly fall into two paradigms. Bioinspired strategies rely on reactive behaviors triggered by chemical detections, such as surge‐casting, offering efficiency but requiring scenario‐specific tuning. Cognitive strategies integrate observations into a probabilistic belief over source location to guide exploration. While more robust, these methods suffer from excessive exploration and strong dependence on belief accuracy. The Fast‐Cognitive algorithm alleviated the computational burden of cognitive approaches but preserved their fundamental limitations. Previous Markov chain analysis revealed that source‐directed motions occur approximately twice as often following odor detections, indicating that reactive behaviors naturally emerge within cognitive frameworks. This work proposes a targeted extension of Fast‐Cognitive in which the continuous uncertainty‐based mixing of explora…

title: Critical Success Factors for Sustainable Logistics MNE Strategy in China
abstract: Background: This study examines how logistics multinational enterprises (MNEs) operating in China shape and adapt their strategies under complex institutional and competitive conditions. Existing research provides limited insight into how foreign logistics MNEs adjust strategy after market entry and sustain competitive performance over time. Methods: A qualitative longitudinal case-study design was employed using 217 sources collected over nine years, including expert interviews, televised professional interviews, media reports, and company publications. The study develops the Tent Pole Strategy Framework by integrating ownership, location, and internalisation considerations with firm resources, industry competition, and institutional conditions. Results: The findings identify five strategic capabilities that emerge as critical success factors: strategic service portfolio adaptation, technology-enabled customer integration, organisational capability and talent development, institutional embeddedness and local footprint, and strategic governance and market penetration. Conclusions: The study contributes to logistics and international business research by explaining post-entry adaptation and sustained competitive performance among logistics MNEs operating in China. It extends understanding of how strategic capabilities support long-term strategic viability in a complex institutio…

title: Left atrial appendage closure after anticoagulation failure: a promising hybrid strategy, but for whom?
Is parents’ employment uncertainty linked to children's development? Analysing patterns and mechanisms in France
abstract: Abstract Early childhood is a critical period for the reproduction of social inequality. While extant literature focuses on socio-economic background, less is known about the role of parents’ employment uncertainty, notwithstanding its significant presence in post-Fordist societies. We investigate the relationship between household employment uncertainty (HEU)—including temporary work and unemployment—and children's cognitive and socio-emotional development, as well as their physical health. We leverage four waves of the nationally representative French Longitudinal Study of Children (ELFE). First, using ordinary least squares and linear probability models, we find that the accumulation within the household and the persistence of HEU over time are both associated with lower cognitive development (up to −0.2 SD) at ages 2 and 3.5. Results for socio-emotional development are less robust, and physical health appears not to be correlated with HEU, possibly due to comprehensive healthcare. Second, we examine potential mechanisms using counterfactual mediation analysis. In line with the family investment and the family stress models, income and parental investment in cognitively-enhancing activities mediate the link with cognitive development, whereas parental stress mediates the association with socio-emotional development. Robustness tests include regression-with-residuals to accou…

title: The Privacy Challenge in Distributed Energy Resource Aggregation: Privacy-Aware Aggregation of Distributed Energy Resources for Sustainable Power Systems: Risks, Methods, and Challenges
Teaching energy geographies in transition: evolving content and pedagogical shifts
abstract: In the decade since the 2016 special issue on teaching energy geographies in the Journal of Geography in Higher Education, much has changed in both energy geographies research and how it is taught. Research has proliferated, moving into a variety of new topical areas and incorporating a wide variety of methodological approaches. At the same time, higher education teaching has been upended, with the COVID-19 pandemic and calls for greater efforts around diversity, equity, and inclusion changing students and their expectations. These have led to a rethinking of teaching modalities and pedagogies. In this article I reflect on a decade of teaching energy-related courses, first charting a topical evolution that includes the rise of renewable energy, the evolving geographical political economy of fossil fuels, and challenges related to electricity market design and its effects on the energy transition. The article then addresses evolutions in pedagogical approach, describing assignments that illustrate my shift from problem-based to challenge-based learning which, I argue, helps move knowledge creation out of the classroom and into the local community. In the conclusion I direct energy geographers towards four topics and challenges I believe will be important for energy scholar-teachers to contend with in the coming years.
venue: Journal of Geography in Higher Education

title: Governing the Unmeasured Load: Hyperscale Data Centres, Systemic Risk and the Assessment–Management Gap in EU Law
abstract: European Union law regulates hyperscale data centres through four distinct risk frameworks: energy efficiency, electricity market design, critical-infrastructure resilience and artificial-intelligence safety. None was designed for very large, rapidly fluctuating, geographically concentrated electrical loads. This article argues that the resulting regime is not incoherent, but arrested at the assessment stage of the risk-regulation cycle. The Union has created mechanisms for collecting information about data centres while withholding Union-level instruments capable of converting that knowledge into risk management. The Commission’s first assessment under Article 12 of the recast Energy Efficiency Directive, published in July 2025, illustrates this gap: it captured some 770 reporting facilities, by the Commission’s own estimate only about one third of those obliged to report. Subsequent developments – the final ENTSO-E report on the Iberian blackout of April 2025, the Commission’s June 2026 Cloud and AI Development Act proposal, and Ireland’s December 2025 connection decision – show the consequences. Member States and regulators are improvising uncoordinated management tools across the Union. Drawing on the engineering and energy-systems literature as well as on legal scholarship, the article characterises the hazard posed by hyperscale artificial-intelligence loads and proposes …

title: Impact of prolonged elevated heart rate on sepsis-associated acute kidney injury patients: a causal inference and prediction study
abstract: Background: This study investigates the relationship between prolonged elevated heart rate (pe-HR) and mortality among patients with sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (S-AKI) using causal inference and machine learning.Method: Pe-HR was defined as a heart rate exceeding 100 beats/min for 11 hours within a 12-hour interval. The average treatment effect (ATE) was a measure of the therapeutic effect of β-blockers. The primary outcome measure of the study was the 90-day survival and hospitalization survival as the secondary endpoint. Four machine learning algorithms were employed to assess whether an increase in pe-HR enhanced the performance of predictions.Results: The study included a total of 14,388 patients with S-AKI from MIMIC (Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care)-IV. The results revealed that both 90-day and in-hospital survival were lower in patients with pe-HR than in those without (hazard ratio: 1.62 for 90-day survival and 1.22 for in-hospital survival). The ATE of development pe-HR was 56.3 days survival higher than without pe-HR. The ATE of β-blocker use was 40.2 days survival higher than no use. Four machine learning algorithms showed that the inclusion of pe-HR improved the accuracy of 90-day survival predictions (p < 0.05), with the best area under the receiver operating characteristic curve reaching 0.76.Conclusion: In S-AKI patients, pe-HR was signific…

title: Emergency department visits for patients with end-stage kidney disease in Korea: registry data from the National Emergency Department Information System 2019–2021
abstract: Background: Patients with end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) frequently visit the emergency department (ED) due to complications from comorbidities and dialysis. This study aimed to investigate the clinical outcomes and patterns of ED visits, hospitalizations, and in-hospital mortality among ED visits by ESKD patients in South Korea. Methods: This study utilized data from the National Emergency Department Information System from 2019 to 2021. ED visits were analyzed for ESKD patients and compared with non-chronic kidney disease (non-CKD) patients. Logistic regression analyses were conducted to assess factors associated with hospitalization and mortality, adjusting for demographics, insurance, and clinical characteristics, including the Korean Triage and Acuity Scale (KTAS). Results: The study included 125,392 ED visits from ESKD patients and 19,287,972 from non-CKD patients. ED visits by ESKD patients had significantly higher hospitalization (66.7%) and in-hospital mortality (9.4%) rates compared to those by non-CKD patients (21.0% and 5.1%, respectively). ESKD patients were older, more frequently female, and more likely to receive medical aid. Factors strongly associated with higher hospitalization and mortality rates included advanced age, male sex, transfer from another facility, higher KTAS scores, and prolonged ED stays. Common causes of ED visits in ESKD patients included va…

title: Genetic variants shape single-cell chromatin accessibility and disease risk
Co-design in real-world laboratories: Fostering transformative capacity for sustainable mobility
abstract: How can co-design processes in transdisciplinary real-world laboratories support social-ecological transformations? Drawing on three mobility-related projects, this article highlights how co-design helps manage complexity, align visions, and foster agency for change.Transdisciplinary research addresses complex sustainability challenges by integrating scientific and practical knowledge through collaborative approaches such as co-design. This article explores how co-design processes within three real-world laboratory (RwL) projects ‐ WohnMobil , PendelLabor , and transform-R ‐ support social-ecological transformations, particularly in the context of sustainable mobility. We offer coordinates and guidance for the set-up, design and organization of co-design processes in mobility research, pointing out learnings, areas of flexibility and adaptations from the ideal type. Using document analysis and reflective workshops, we examine how co-design contributes to handling complexity and uncertainty, to mediating differing visions of the future, and to fostering agency for change. The results show that co-design enables shared problem framing, joint experimentation, and stakeholder engagement across governance levels. However, the success of co-design depends on strategic actor selection, facilitation, and the alignment of research and practice goals. We conclude that flexible, well-faci…
venue: GAIA - Ecological Perspectives for Science and Society

title: Nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist in diabetic kidney disease: mechanistic insights and clinical integration
abstract: Nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (ns-MRA) have emerged as a key therapeutic option for patients with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease, addressing the unmet cardiorenal risk that persists under standard renin-angiotensin system therapy. Finerenone, the most extensively studied ns-MRA, has demonstrated significant reductions in kidney and cardiovascular outcomes across a broad spectrum of CKD severity, with a favorable safety profile. Recent guideline recommendations endorse ns-MRAs in patients with persistent albuminuria despite optimized standard therapy. Moreover, combination strategies with sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors show additive benefits, supporting a multi-targeted treatment approach. This review summarizes the pathophysiological rationale, clinical evidence, safety considerations, and combination strategies involving ns-MRAs in contemporary diabetic kidney disease management.

title: Interweaving participation formats to strengthen representation and deliberation in urban mobility transformations. Lessons from designing Kiezblocks in Berlin
abstract: How can cities engage diverse residents in urban mobility transformations? Drawing on a multi-format participation process for two Berlin Kiezblocks, this paper shows that combining participation formats with different recruitment methods, interaction types, and levels of public influence on planning decisions can strengthen representation and constructive deliberation.Engaging residents in urban mobility transformations can support implementation by mitigating polarization and strengthening governance, yet designing inclusive participation processes remains challenging. We present a multi-format participation process for two Kiezblocks in Berlin-Mitte, developed with municipal planners, to engage diverse residents in constructive deliberation (external inclusion), make their perspectives heard (internal inclusion), and enable different levels of public influence on planning decisions. Drawing on field notes and structured reflections within the transdisciplinary consortium, we describe the participation formats including their recruitment methods, interaction types, and main strengths and weaknesses. Although suitable format combinations depend on goals, target groups, and local contexts, experiences suggest that interweaving stakeholder meetings, targeted outreach formats, and formats based on random selection can strengthen inclusion while providing different levels of publi…
