title: Incretin-based therapies in diabetic kidney disease: toward integrated cardio-kidney-metabolic disease modification
abstract: Obesity and type 2 diabetes (T2D) are dominant drivers of chronic kidney disease (CKD) within the cardio-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome. Despite advances with renin-angiotensin system inhibitors and sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors, substantial residual cardiovascular and renal risk persists, highlighting the need for therapies targeting upstream metabolic dysfunction. Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists (RAs) have emerged as key modulators of CKM disease through integrated metabolic, vascular, and anti-inflammatory mechanisms. Cardiovascular outcome trials first established their cardioprotective effects, while the FLOW trial definitively demonstrated kidney protection, showing a 24% reduction in major kidney outcomes in patients with T2D and CKD. Mechanistic insights from translational studies further suggest that GLP-1 receptor activation promotes metabolic decongestion, improves intrarenal hemodynamics, and attenuates inflammatory and fibrotic pathways. Beyond selective GLP-1 receptor agonism, dual (glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide [GIP]/GLP-1) and triple (GIP/GLP-1/glucagon) incretin agonists, including tirzepatide and retatrutide, extend this paradigm by delivering greater weight reduction and systemic metabolic reprogramming, with emerging signals for cardiovascular and renal benefit. Contemporary CKD management is shifting tow…

title: Renin-angiotensin system blockade in diabetic kidney disease: an old pillar that still stands at the core of therapy
abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is the leading cause of chronic kidney disease and end-stage kidney disease worldwide. Activation of the renin-angiotensin system (RAS) plays a central role in the pathogenesis of DKD by promoting intraglomerular hypertension, albuminuria, inflammation, oxidative stress, and progressive fibrosis. Angiotensin II-mediated efferent arteriolar constriction increases glomerular capillary pressure, while non-hemodynamic effects, including upregulation of transforming growth factor-β, NADPH oxidase-dependent reactive oxygen species generation, and podocyte apoptosis, contribute to structural kidney injury. Large, randomized trials have consistently demonstrated that angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors and angiotensin receptor blockers reduce albuminuria, slow the glomerular filtration rate decline, and delay kidney failure across different stages of DKD. Evidence also supports cardiovascular benefits, including reduced heart failure events, in patients with DKD. A reduction in albuminuria is closely correlated with long-term kidney outcomes, underscoring its role as a mechanistic and therapeutic marker. Concerns regarding safety in advanced chronic kidney disease have been addressed by recent evidence indicating that routine discontinuation of RAS blockade does not improve kidney function and may increase cardiorenal risk. Although newer agents have …

title: A novel approach to the relation of multi-pollutant effect and kidney dysfunction: data analysis from the Korean National Environmental Health Survey Cycle 3 (2015–2017)
abstract: Background: Traditional statistical models for estimating the impact of multiple environmental chemicals on kidney outcomes have limitations. This study aimed to evaluate the risk prediction of kidney disease in the general population using innovative methodologies.Methods: Serum persistent organic pollutant (POP), urinary chemical, serum creatinine, and urinary albumin levels were measured in a subpopulation of adults (n = 1,266) drawn from the Korean National Environmental Health Survey Cycle 3 (n = 3,787). Various machine learning (ML) models, including bagging, ridge, lasso, and random forest, were used to predict chronic kidney disease (CKD) risk, and their results were compared with those of conventional logistic regression methods. Furthermore, the weighted quantile sum (WQS) approach, which assigns weights to mixture components, was employed to evaluate multi-pollutant effects. Presplit was attempted to incorporate existing domain knowledge.Results: A total of 42 variables, including baseline characteristics and laboratory findings, were analyzed during the ML modeling process. The decision tree algorithm generally outperformed logistic regression in risk prediction. Based on the decision tree models, lipid-corrected polychlorinated biphenyl 153 (PCB153) emerged as the strongest predictor of CKD. PCB153 remained a significant predictor of CKD in middle-aged adults (<50 …

title: Ergonomic interventions for treating work-related complaints of the arm, neck or shoulder in adults
Bayesian neural networks for geothermal resource assessment: Prediction with uncertainty
abstract: Abstract In this work, the application of machine learning to the evaluation of geothermal resource potential is considered. A supervised learning problem is defined where maps of ten geological and geophysical features within the state of Nevada, USA, are used to define geothermal potential across a broad region. With the availability of a relatively small set of positive training sites (known resources or active power plants) and negative training sites (known drill sites with unsuitable geothermal conditions) two classes of artificial neural networks, for this classification task, are constrained and optimised. The main objective is to predict the geothermal resource potential at unknown sites within a large geographic area where the defining features are known. These predictions could be used to target promising areas for further detailed investigations. The work evolves from defining a specific neural network architecture to training and optimisation trials. The inevitable problems of model variability and resulting prediction uncertainty are exposed. Finally, to address these problems, the concept of Bayesian neural networks, a heuristic approach to regularisation in network training, is exploited, together with the practical interpretation of the formal uncertainty measures they provide.

title: R Tech Engineering: from nurturing the grassroots to scaling the market tree
abstract: Learning outcomes After completion of the case study, the students will be able: To analyse the process of development, adoption and scaling of grassroots innovations using entrepreneurship, innovation and strategic management frameworks (e.g. resource-based view, diffusion of innovation, etc.).To assess the relevance of intellectual property protection, standardisation and certification in scaling grassroots innovation.To identify and assess the role of individual behaviours that shape the innovation and entrepreneurial journey.To assess the role of institutional factors in supporting and sustaining the grassroots innovation ecosystem.To analyse the challenges faced by a grassroots innovator-entrepreneur in achieving business growth and sustainability under resource constraints.To apply customer engagement frameworks to develop strategies for value creation and market expansion of grassroots innovations. Case overview/synopsis Sree Vardhan, the chief executive officer of R Tech Engineering (Coimbatore, India), joined his father’s business in 2015, that manufactured and sold an innovative product, a tree climbing implement called Multi-Tree Climber. The innovator of this device was D.N. Venkat, his father, who had been recognised with numerous awards for its utility and safety features, in the grassroots agricultural sector. The growth of R Tech Engineering was no mean achievem…

title: Empowering youth – strengthening educational and labor market pathways through strategic partnerships and entrepreneurial education
abstract: Purpose This study examines the role of strategic partnerships between education providers, the labor market and policymakers in fostering youth educational engagement and work readiness in the rural, regional area of Mellersta Norrland, Sweden. Design/methodology/approach Grounded in educational ecosystem theory (Hargreaves, 2014), professional capital (Hargreaves and Fullan, 2012), and entrepreneurial education frameworks (Fayolle and Gailly, 2015; Seikkula-Leino et al., 2010, 2021), the study explores how collaboration can address youth unemployment and skill mismatches. A qualitative focus group interview with key stakeholders was employed. Findings We identify four critical challenges: (1) limited integration between education and work, (2) barriers to labor market entry, (3) the need for strengthened partnerships and (4) the need to create better opportunities for innovative solutions. The findings underscore the importance of digitalization, structured mentorship programs and entrepreneurship education in enhancing youth employability, specifically in rural contexts. Originality/value This study contributes unique findings to international discussions on entrepreneurial ecosystems and labor market alignment by exploring scalable, policy-relevant recommendations that bridge the gap between education and employment for supporting student pathways in a rural context. Althou…

title: On the optimal public debt thresholds for electricity infrastructure and clean energy investment in sub-Saharan Africa
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine whether public debt has a nonlinear effect on electricity infrastructure and clean energy investment in 28 sub-Saharan African countries. It identifies the debt levels beyond which public borrowing ceases to support energy-sector development and becomes a fiscal constraint. The analysis also distinguishes between total public debt and external public debt to assess whether debt composition influences the emergence of adverse effects. Design/methodology/approach This study uses panel data covering 28 sub-Saharan African countries from 2010 to 2021. Linear and quadratic dynamic panel models are estimated using system generalized method of moments. The Lind–Mehlum test is applied to validate the inverted U-shaped relationships and calculate the turning points. Robustness is assessed using the Seo–Shin dynamic panel threshold model, which accounts for endogeneity and identifies regime changes associated with total and external public debt. Findings Public debt initially supports energy development but becomes detrimental beyond critical levels. The quadratic estimates identify total public debt thresholds of 82.3% of gross domestic product for electricity infrastructure and 47.5% for public investment in renewable energy. The corresponding external debt thresholds are lower, at 59.9% and 38.5%, respectively. The Seo–Shin estimates confirm the same…
venue: International Journal of Energy Sector Management

title: Termination Rate Regulation and Retail Outcomes: Pass-Through and Competition in Botswana’s Mobile Market
abstract: Abstract This study examines the effects of termination rate regulation on retail outcomes and competition in Botswana’s mobile market. Using quarterly operator level data for 2006Q1–2016Q2, estimates from panel instrumental variable approach show that a 10% reduction in M2M termination rates lowers average subscriber expenditure by approximately 2.7%, indicating partial pass through and little evidence of a strong M2M waterbed effect. In contrast, lower F2M rates are associated with higher ARPU, suggesting a waterbed response. The contrasting effects support the diminishing waterbed hypothesis as mobile traffic becomes increasingly dominant. Results from the demand estimation indicate that estimated demand is elastic with respect to average subscriber expenditure. The average own-demand elasticity in relation to subscriber expenditure for the dominant operator is -1.57, smaller in magnitude as compared to -2.22 for Orange Botswana and -1.92 for beMobile. Lastly, the study finds that the policy to reduce termination rates had an increasing effect on competition in the mobile telephony market. The estimates indicate that the regulatory intervention was associated with a 13.9% reduction in market concentration, as measured by the HHI. The findings suggest that termination rate regulation can improve consumer welfare and market competitiveness without generating substantial advers…
venue: Journal of Industry, Competition and Trade

title: When quality does not pay: trader market power, pricing outcomes and smallholder profitability in the Lao mountain goat chain
abstract: Purpose This study investigates how trader market power can contribute to buyer-induced price discrimination and potentially affect smallholder profitability in the mountain goat value chain of Laos and Vietnam. Design/methodology/approach Cross-sectional survey data were analysed from 152 smallholder farmers in Laos and traders, abattoirs, restaurant owners and consumers in Laos and Vietnam. Econometric models were applied to examine how smallholder characteristics, farm characteristics and market orientation influence farmgate prices and profits under informal selling arrangements. Findings Education, proximity to markets and herd size significantly increase farmgate prices and profits. However, smallholders oriented toward producing higher-quality, mature goats, tend to earn lower profits, revealing the fact that price premiums fail to cover additional costs of quality-focused production. The findings provide evidence of systematic pricing differentials consistent with buyer-induced price discrimination under trader market power that might undermine incentives and restrict income growth. Research limitations/implications This analysis is based on cross-sectional survey data from two countries. Future work could extend this analysis using more variables and assess other chains. Originality/value To our knowledge, this is one of the first studies to examine systematic pricing …
venue: Journal of Agribusiness in Developing and Emerging Economies

title: Unknown Primary Undifferentiated Carcinoma with Good Response to Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Cancer of unknown primary (CUP) is a metastatic malignancy with an unidentified origin and poor prognosis. We report a 60-year-old male with extensive supraclavicular and para-aortic lymphadenopathy who progressed on multiple lines of empiric chemotherapy. Biomarker re-evaluation revealed high programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression, prompting treatment with the PD-1 inhibitor pembrolizumab. The patient achieved a near-complete radiographic response after four cycles of pembrolizumab, accompanied by the development of vitiligo – a recognized immune-related adverse event. He maintained a durable response 1 year after discontinuing immunotherapy. This case underscores the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors in CUP with a high expression of PD-L1 involving only the lymph nodes and the clinical importance of biomarker profiling.
venue: Journal of Cancer Research and Practice

title: Asymmetric In-Plane Dielectric Response of Interfacial Water to Biaxial Strain: Decoupling Orientational and Positional Order
abstract: Abstract Antiferroelectric (AFE) ordering in interfacial water strongly suppresses its in-plane dielectric constant, yet how to actively tune the dielectric response of AFE ordered water remains largely unexplored. Here, using molecular dynamics (MD) simulations on a model platinum surface, we investigate the influence of mechanical strain on the dielectric behavior of ordered interfacial water. The in-plane dielectric constant ε∥ exhibits an asymmetric V-shaped response to biaxial strain, where compression drives a sharp increase in ε∥ (∼2.52-fold), while tension induces a modest rise (∼1.62-fold). This asymmetry originates from the fact that the regular oxygen sublattice is preserved under tension, which continues to constrain dipole orientations. As a result, the AFE order parameter η decreases by only ∼11%. By contrast, the ordered structure is severely disrupted under compression, with η dropping by ∼49%. Tension thus selectively decouples orientational order from positional order in AFE interfacial water, which limits the release of dipolar fluctuations, leading to a moderate rise in the Kirkwood correlation factor GK and, consequently, a gentle enhancement of ε∥. Our findings identify mechanical strain as an effective physical tool for selectively decoupling orientational and positional order at interface.

title: Bibliometric analysis of aviation unsafe event research: from reactive response to intelligent prediction
abstract: Purpose The post-pandemic recovery of global air transport and rapid developments in artificial intelligence are shifting aviation safety management from reactive accident investigation to proactive risk prediction. To examine how this trend is reflected in recent literature, this study aims to conduct a bibliometric analysis of aviation unsafe event research published between 2020 and 2025. Design/methodology/approach Based on 512 publications retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection, the authors use Bibliometrix and VOSviewer to construct keyword co-occurrence and co-citation networks. Findings The results show a rapid increase in research output following a temporary decline in 2022, reflecting the field’s resilience and growing attention to post-pandemic safety challenges. Thematic evolution analysis identifies a clear departure from traditional system-level investigations. This field increasingly prioritizes mining valuable information from flight data and unstructured safety reports using machine learning, deep learning and natural language processing. Current studies largely revolve around anomaly detection under complex meteorological conditions, causal inference using Bayesian networks and the application of large language models for safety text analysis. Originality/value These findings suggest that data-driven approaches have established themselves in aviati…

title: Fatigue response of pre-corroded chromic-acid-anodized AA7050-T7451 and phase-field analysis of stress-dependent localized dissolution
abstract: Abstract Understanding the effects of environmental exposure and cyclic loading on localized damage is important for assessing the fatigue performance of anodized aluminium. This study investigates the fatigue response of chromic-acid-anodized AA7050-T7451 and the stress-dependent evolution of localized corrosion. Cyclic-immersion and intermittent-salt-fog exposures were followed by mass-loss measurements, microscopic observations and axial fatigue testing in laboratory air at R = 0.06. Small average mass losses coexisted with localized surface changes and appreciable fatigue-life scatter. At 180 MPa, the cyclic-immersion groups exhibited sample mean fatigue lives 57.1–73.6% below the uncorroded reference, with a non-monotonic dependence on exposure duration. Increasing the maximum nominal stress from 180 to 200 MPa reduced the mean fatigue life by 22.0–45.9% at the same cyclic-immersion durations. A two-dimensional displacement–phase-field–concentration model examined localized dissolution under cyclic loading for initial cavity depths of 0.01 and 0.02 mm. Higher cyclic stress promoted local plastic deformation and increased interface mobility, accelerating inward dissolution. At 900 s, increasing the maximum nominal stress from 160 to 240 MPa increased total defect depth by 45.2–51.2%, whereas lateral width changed by no more than 2.2%. At 240 MPa and 900 s, the larger initia…

title: Signal response of bare and moderated cosmic-ray neutron sensors to varying soil and biomass conditions
abstract: Since the first development of hectometre-scale soil moisture estimation using the epithermal(-dominated) neutron intensity from moderated Cosmic-Ray Neutron Sensing (CRNS) detectors, researchers have hypothesised that concurrent lower-energy, thermal(-dominated) neutron measurements with bare (unmoderated) detectors could also be useful for environmental sensing. Early studies in this field have highlighted the potential of neutrons observed with bare detectors for monitoring biomass, plant traits, and snow water equivalent, while others underlined a soil moisture dependence that can adversely affect their usability. Similarly, varying estimates of the radius and depth of the measurement footprint of thermal neutron observations compared to that of the standard epithermal CRNS observations have been proposed. However, a generalised simulation-based assessment of the signal response and of the footprint of bare detectors is currently lacking. Against this background, this study aims to generate an improved understanding of neutron signals recorded by bare and moderated detectors through the simulation of generalised environmental scenarios using a Monte Carlo neutron transport model. The results emphasise the complex and differing response of thermal-dominated, bare and epithermal-dominated, moderated neutron detectors over a range of environmental conditions with respect to th…

title: Clinical effects of third doses of mRNA COVID-19 vaccines among hemodialysis patients: a nationwide retrospective cohort study
abstract: Background: Evidence on the effectiveness of third-dose messenger RNA (mRNA) coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) vaccination during the Omicron-dominant period in Asian hemodialysis (HD) patients remains limited. We evaluated the clinical effectiveness of a third mRNA vaccine dose against severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection, hospitalization, and mortality in Korean HD patients. Methods: Using the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency–National Health Insurance Service database, we conducted a nationwide cohort study of HD patients aged ≥18 years who received two or three doses of BNT162b2 or mRNA-1273 before January 16, 2022. Study outcomes were SARS-CoV-2 infection, hospitalization, and death. Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess the associations between third-dose vaccination and clinical outcomes. Results: Among 66,389 HD patients (mean age, 65.7 ± 12.9 years; 60.5% male), 55,125 (83.0%) received three vaccine doses and 11,264 (17.0%) received two doses. Receipt of three doses was associated with a significantly lower risk of SARS-CoV-2 infection (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 0.58; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.56–0.60). Among 17,886 patients with SARS-CoV-2 infection, third-dose vaccine recipients had a lower risk of hospitalization (aHR, 0.65; 95% CI, 0.62–0.70) and 30-day mortality (aHR, 0.35; 95% CI, 0.30–0.41) com…

Embedding and sustaining quality improvement in hospitals: the CARE model – an expert-informed qualitative study
abstract: Purpose Sustaining quality improvement (QI) in hospitals remains challenging, as many initiatives fail to become embedded in everyday clinical practice. This study explores how QI experts understand the contextual, cultural, organisational and relational conditions shaping the implementation, embedding and sustainability of QI, and translates these insights into practice-oriented guidance. Design/methodology/approach We employed a qualitative design informed by scientific pragmatism. Data were collected in two Danish hospitals through 14 semi-structured interviews with QI experts, followed by a structured focus group. We analysed data using the Gioia approach and abductive reasoning. Analytically derived domains were subsequently refined and translated into the CARE model and practice-oriented recommendations through structured expert involvement. Findings The analysis identified four interdependent domains in experts' accounts of embedding QI in hospital work: Co-creation and Engagement, Adaptive Contextualisation, Relational Leadership, and Enhanced Learning and Progress. These domains were synthesised into the CARE model, an analytical and practice-oriented model for examining how organisational, relational, contextual and learning conditions may be aligned. Healthcare professionals, managers and QI teams may use CARE to structure reflection on where an improvement initiativ…

title: Football Resilience in Crisis-Affected States as Soft Power at the 2026 FIFA World Cup
abstract: This article examines why national football teams from crisis-affected countries can remain competitive and qualify for the 2026 FIFA World Cup. The study focuses on Iran, Iraq, Tunisia, and Egypt as cases that represent different forms of crisis, including geopolitical pressure, post-war recovery, post-uprising political instability, and economic vulnerability. The article argues that football resilience in these countries cannot be explained only by macro-political stability or national wealth. It emerges from the interaction of football culture, institutional continuity, youth development, diaspora networks, elite player pathways, and national identity narratives. Using a qualitative comparative case study method, this research analyzes secondary data from FIFA documents, news reports, international organization reports, and relevant academic literature. The theoretical framework combines soft power, sports diplomacy, social identity theory, and social resilience. The findings show that World Cup qualification works as a symbolic resource that helps crisis-affected countries produce attraction, maintain international visibility, and strengthen collective pride. However, this soft power remains fragile when it is not supported by transparent football governance and long-term development. The article contributes to sports diplomacy studies by shifting the focus from host-count…

title: ДОМ КУПЦА ХЛОПОНИНА. АНАЛИЗ КОНСТРУКТИВНОЙ СИСТЕМЫ ГРАЖДАНСКОГО ЗДАНИЯ XVII ВЕКА
abstract: Дом купца Хлопонина в Курске, известный также как «Палаты бояр Ромодановских», представляет собой один из наиболее выразительных памятников гражданской каменной архитектуры старого города. Несмотря на устойчивую традицию связывать сооружение с XVII веком, современные археологические и историко-архитектурные исследования относят основной объем здания к середине - второй половине XVIII столетия. В статье рассматривается конструктивная система дома, восходящая к традициям палатного зодчества XVII века: массивные кирпичные несущие стены, сводчатые перекрытия, подвальный ярус, арочное крыльцо, внутренняя лестница в толще стены и композиционная роль башенного завершения. Анализ показывает, что дом Хлопонина важен как пример сохранения архаичных строительных принципов в гражданской архитектуре провинциального города переходной эпохи. The house of merchant Khloponin in Kursk, also known as the "Chambers of the Boyars of Romodanovsky", is one of the most expressive monuments of the civil stone architecture of the old city. Despite the steady tradition of associating the building with the 17th century, modern archaeological and historical-architectural studies attribute the main volume of the building to the middle and second half of the 18th century. The article examines the structural system of the house, dating back to the traditions of tent architecture of the XVII century: massive b…

title: Soil-Vegetable Production Nexus: Integrating Soil Health Management with Sustainable Vegetable Crop Systems
abstract: Soil health is a critical pillar of sustainable vegetable production systems worldwide. This narrative review aims to: (1) synthesize the major soil health constraints in intensive vegetable production systems; (2) evaluate the effectiveness of physical, chemical, and biological management interventions; and (3) identify economic and policy pathways for scalable implementation. A comprehensive review of peer-reviewed literature published primarily between 2000 and 2024 was conducted, drawing on evidence from temperate and subtropical systems. Intensive vegetable farming exerts substantial pressure on soil resources through short crop cycles, over-fertilization, repeated tillage, and continuous irrigation, triggering declines in physical structure, chemical balance, and biological function. Key physical constraints include soil compaction, indicated by bulk densities exceeding 1.6 g cm^-3^, while biological degradation manifests as reduced microbial biomass carbon (20–50% lower than extensive systems) and diminished disease suppression. Effective management encompasses organic amendments, integrated soil fertility management (ISFM), diversified crop rotations, and conservation tillage, with soil health recovery typically requiring 2–5 years depending on the severity of degradation. Precision agriculture tools and climate-smart practices offer additional pathways for sustainable …

title: Orkestrasi Sumber Daya dan Kendala Ganda (Dual Constraints):Analisis Peran Moderasi Manajemen Risikoterhadap Kualitas Portofolio Pembiayaan UUS BPD Representatif di Sumatera
abstract: Industri perbankan syariah Indonesia menghadapi paradoks struktural: pertumbuhan aset yang pesat tidak diimbangi oleh kualitas portofolio yang konsisten, khususnya pada Unit Usaha Syariah (UUS) dalam sistem perbankan ganda. Penelitian ini bertujuan menginvestigasi bagaimana manajemen risiko memoderasi hubungan antara kompetensi, kepatuhan syariah, dan strategi penagihan terhadap kualitas portofolio pembiayaan pada Bank Pembangunan Daerah (BPD), dengan mengintegrasikan Resource Orchestration Theory, Enabling Bureaucracy Theory, dan Institutional Logic Theory dalam kerangka Maqasid al-Syariah. Penelitian menerapkan pendekatan kuantitatif eksplanatif dengan teknik sensus terhadap 111 pemegang kewenangan pembiayaan di UUS Bank Sumut, Medan, menggunakan analisis Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) melalui SmartPLS 4.0. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kompetensi karyawan dan kepatuhan syariah secara kolektif memberikan kontribusi sebesar 80,6% (R²=0,806) terhadap peningkatan kualitas portofolio, mengonfirmasi dominasi kontrol preventif (ex-ante) dibandingkan upaya pemulihan (ex-post). Temuan krusial mengungkap fenomena “Kendala Ganda” (Dual Constraints): manajemen risiko efektif sebagai enabling bureaucracy dalam memperkuat kompetensi komersial (β=0,187, p=0,013), namun gagal mengintegrasikan logika religius (kepatuhan syariah) secara organik, sehingga ked…

title: Pathways to High-Level Integrated Innovation Between Large Enterprises and SMEs: Evidence from Wenzhou Under the TOE Framework
abstract: Integrated innovation (in Chinese, rongtong chuangxin), namely the collaborative innovation of large, medium, small, and micro enterprises along and across industrial chains, has become a central instrument of China’s innovation policy. Drawing on the technology–organization–environment (TOE) framework, this study examines how multiple conditions jointly configure to produce high-level integrated innovation among enterprises in Wenzhou, a city emblematic of China’s private economy. Data were collected through a questionnaire survey of enterprises in Wenzhou conducted between May and August 2024, yielding 105 valid responses, supplemented by ten in-depth interviews. Descriptive statistics show that only 41.9% of the 105 surveyed firms—44 firms in total—had engaged in inter-firm innovation cooperation; among these 44 firms, talent shortage (61.4%), lack of cooperation platforms and channels (50.0%), and funding constraints (45.5%) are the most salient barriers. Using fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) on the 44 firms engaged in integrated innovation, the study identifies three equifinal pathways to high-level integrated innovation: an R&D-driven path, a digital-technology-driven path, and an organization–environment composite path. Government policy support emerges as the only core condition common to all three configurations, while top management support and indu…

title: Design and Application of an Experimental System on Multipollutant Catalytic Removal for Undergraduate Teaching: A Case Study of VOCs Oxidation over Mn–Fe Oxide Catalysts
abstract: Abstract In the face of increasingly severe atmospheric pollution, it is crucial to cultivate undergraduates’ environmental awareness and their ability to address complex atmospheric pollution challenges. To this end, a multipollutant catalytic treatment system was developed and integrated into a comprehensive teaching experiment. Taking the catalytic oxidation of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) as the core experiment, students prepared Mn–Fe oxide catalysts in groups via the hydrolysis-driven redox method. Toluene was used as the model pollutant, and the influence of HNO3 dosage on the physicochemical properties and toluene oxidation performance of the catalysts was investigated. The teaching content was further extended through extracurricular experiments on CO oxidation, NH3–SCR, and coupled reactions using the same experimental system, broadening students’ exposure to multipollutant catalytic control. Students’ learning outcomes were evaluated through experimental performance, experimental reports, and oral presentations, while a structured questionnaire was used to collect their feedback on learning gains and the overall teaching experience. Teaching practice indicated that the experiment supported the development of students’ competencies in engineering practice, independent learning, and critical thinking.

title: Improved Colorimetric-Spectroscopic System Combined with Weighted Partial Least Squares for the Rapid Detection of Acephate In Grain
abstract: To enable the rapid detection of acephate residues, an improved colorimetric method was developed using palladium chloride (PdCl₂) as the chromogenic reagent. Sodium chloride was selected to replace hydrochloric acid as the optimized solvent, effectively circumventing the limitations of conventional PdCl₂ formulations. The resulting system yielded a discernible absorbance response for acephate at concentrations as low as 0.05 mg/kg, confirming the high sensitivity of the colorimetric reaction. To improve detection accuracy in the low-concentration range, a weighted partial least squares (wPLS) model coupled with leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) was constructed using a reciprocal concentration weighting strategy. The effects of various combinations of three spectral ranges and five preprocessing methods on model performance were systematically evaluated. Optimal results for the prediction set were obtained within the 370–600 nm wavelength range, yielding a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.9982 and a root mean square error of prediction (RMSEP) of 1.0963. Compared with the conventional PLS model, the proposed wPLS model exhibited distinct advantages in the low-concentration regime. Validation across five low-concentration groups revealed that the mean relative errors of the wPLS model were significantly lower than those of the PLS model. Spiked recovery tests performe…

title: The hidden cost of retention in emerging economies: toxic leadership, employee silence and the dark side of job embeddedness
abstract: Purpose This study aims to develop a differentiated account of employee responses to toxic leadership beyond the conventional emphasis on intended exit. Focusing on Ghanaian informal-sector small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), it explains how toxic leadership may become associated with employee silence through learned helplessness and how job embeddedness (JE) conditions its relationship with turnover intention. Design/methodology/approach Using a quantitative approach, data were collected from 505 employees of SMEs operating within Ghana’s informal sector through a three-wave time-lagged survey design. Partial least squares structural equation modelling was used to test the hypothesised relationships. Findings The findings reveal that toxic leadership is positively associated with learned helplessness and employee silence but does not significantly predict turnover intention. Learned helplessness partially mediates the relationship between toxic leadership and employee silence. The results further show that JE weakens the relationship between toxic leadership and turnover intention, suggesting that employees with stronger organisational and community attachments are less likely to leave despite experiencing workplace toxicity. Originality/value This study advances toxic leadership scholarship by distinguishing its psychological and communicative consequences from its re…

title: Guest editorial: Human-artificial intelligence interactions in knowledge ecosystems
Interpretable machine learning for customer satisfaction optimization
abstract: Purpose Understanding how dining experiences are transformed into customer satisfaction judgments is central to hospitality competitiveness. Using high-dimensional user-generated content on tourism dining experiences, this study aims to examine whether shared three-factor classifications coexist with segment-specific differences in satisfaction relationships. Design/methodology/approach The authors analyze 82,105 Yelp restaurant reviews from nine market segments based on price level, cuisine type and restaurant category. Bidirectional encoder representations from transformers-based aspect mining and clustering extract attribute–sentiment pairs. Ensemble models estimate nonlinear predictive relationships, and SHAP decomposes their predictions to support attribute classification, segment-specific satisfaction functions and diagnostic prioritization. Findings Empirical results reveal a basic-dominant pattern together with segment-level variation in estimated penalty–reward magnitudes, satisfaction-function shapes and diagnostic priorities. This pattern remains largely stable under alternative impact asymmetry thresholds and the procedure based on penalty-reward contrast analysis. Categorical stability can therefore coexist with segment-contingent differences in evaluative weight and relationship form. Practical implications Theoretically, the findings highlight the value of extend…

title: The explanatory power of politeness principle and pragmatic empathy in cross-cultural communication conflicts — An analysis of typical cases in ICT
abstract: The Intercultural Competence Test (ICT) aims to assess an individual's ability to communicate effectively and appropriately in a multicultural context. This paper, drawing on Leech's politeness principle, Brown and Levinson's face theory, and HE Ziran's pragmatic empathy theory as the analytical framework, analyzes typical conflict cases in the ICT, and explains the complementary roles of the three theories. Based on this, a three-step ICT answering strategy is constructed: perception; empathy; action. The research aims to shift ICT tutoring from "memorizing cultural facts" to "understanding pragmatic logic", and provide a path from the perspective of pragmatics for vocational college students to enhance their cross-cultural communication competence.

title: Theoretical and Expert Justification of the Modern Foundations of Organizing Career Guidance Management in Healthcare
abstract: In the context of personnel shortage, the healthcare system is in dire need of effective mechanisms to attract motivated applicants and retain young specialists. However, existing approaches to career guidance fail to account for the continuity of professional self-determination and poorly coordinate the actions of stakeholders. The aim is to substantiate the conceptual framework for building a modern medical career guidance management system drawing on theory and the results of an expert survey. The theoretical basis consists of five concepts: career construction, continuous career guidance support for a person, the Third Mission of the university, stakeholder management, and digital ecosystems, which form a coherent structural base for career guidance. The empirical foundation was implemented by a survey of 240 experts (2024). The identified scientific concepts create an internally consistent methodological framework for organizing career-guidance governance in the healthcare sector. It implies an active role for the optant in career development, systemic support at all stages of professionalization, from school to independent practice, and coordination of stakeholders’ efforts by the medical university through the creation of a regional science-and-education cluster based on a digital platform.

title: Esophageal diverticulum: A clinical framework for patient-tailored endoscopic management
abstract: The management of esophageal diverticula is undergoing a paradigm shift from traditional surgery to minimally invasive endoscopic approaches. However, achieving precise treatment based on individual patient characteristics remains a significant challenge. This paper aims to establish a comprehensive clinical decision-making framework for esophageal diverticulum, encompassing diagnosis, preoperative evaluation, method selection, specific therapeutic techniques, and postoperative assessment, with the goal of facilitating precision treatment. In the preoperative evaluation section, we conduct a detailed analysis of endoscopic approach selection based on diverticulum size, anatomical location, septum length, and patient surgical history, and further discussed recent advances in endoscopic techniques. Additionally, we provide an in-depth comparison of the advantages and disadvantages of different energy modalities, devices, and therapeutic strategies, emphasizing the need for postoperative assessment to account for both technical and clinical success. Lastly, we suggest that the integration of endoscopic techniques with artificial intelligence may represent a future direction for development.

title: LMS Acceptance Factors and Students’ Digital Learning Practices:
abstract: Purpose: This research investigates whether Performance Expectancy, Effort Expectancy, and Facilitating Conditions are associated with Learning Experience and whether they have indirect associations with Digital Engagement and Digital Integration in Daily Life through that experience. Research Method: Survey responses from 114 university students who had used an LMS were examined with Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). Results and Discussion: Students reported better Learning Experience when they perceived stronger performance benefits and more adequate Facilitating Conditions. Effort Expectancy was not significantly associated with Learning Experience. Learning Experience, in turn, was positively related to Digital Engagement and Digital Integration in Daily Life. The indirect associations originating from Performance Expectancy and Facilitating Conditions were significant, whereas those originating from Effort Expectancy were not. Because Learning Experience and Digital Engagement showed only marginal empirical separation, findings involving these constructs require caution. The model did not include direct links from the acceptance factors to either outcome; consequently, the form of mediation cannot be determined. Implications: Universities can improve LMS-based learning by strengthening its educational value, ensuring access to support, and desig…

title: Melampaui Tata Kelola Kolaboratif: Pengelolaan Bersama Simbolis dalam Kemitraan Konservasi Laut di Taman Nasional Wakatobi
abstract: Artikel ini mengkaji dinamika institusional dan implikasi praktis dari konservasi kolaboratif antara Otoritas Taman Nasional Wakatobi dan Forum Posa’asa di Kabupaten Wakatobi Sulawesi Tenggara, Indonesia. Menggunakan metodologi studi kasus kualitatif, penelitian ini menganalisis struktur tata kelola, peran pemangku kepentingan, distribusi manfaat, dan konflik yang muncul dalam kemitraan tersebut. Temuan menunjukkan bahwa meskipun kemitraan ini secara formal didasarkan pada prinsip co-management, operasionalnya berlangsung dalam model tata kelola yang didominasi oleh aktor negara. Struktur ini membatasi kewenangan pengambilan keputusan lokal, memperkuat ketidakseimbangan kekuasaan, dan menghalangi partisipasi inklusif. Ketidakjelasan zonasi, inersia kelembagaan, serta lemahnya penegakan hukum semakin memperdalam kesenjangan antara retorika kolaboratif dan praktik di lapangan. Akibatnya, pengelolaan bersama berlangsung secara simbolis, tanpa pembagian kekuasaan yang setara maupun akuntabilitas mutual antarpemangku kepentingan. Studi ini mengidentifikasi hambatan kritis bagi kolaborasi yang efektif, termasuk ketidakjelasan zonasi, inersia institusional, penegakan hukum yang lemah, kesenjangan kapasitas, dan ketidakhadiran mekanisme penyelesaian konflik. Mengacu pada kerangka kerja kontemporer dalam tata kelola kolaboratif, teori jaringan, dan tata kelola publik baru, artikel ini b…

title: Structural empowerment and psychosocial safety climate in healthcare: a systematic integrative review
abstract: Purpose Psychosocial safety climate (PSC) is associated with nurses' well-being, yet the organisational conditions under which shared PSC perceptions form remain insufficiently understood. Drawing on structural empowerment (SE) theory, PSC theory, and organisational sensemaking, this review derives propositions on the SE–PSC association in healthcare organisations. Design/methodology/approach A systematic integrative review (PRISMA 2020) of five databases identified 30 studies. The synthesis combined deductive framework analysis with abductive theorising; methodological quality was appraised using Joanna Briggs Institute tools. Findings Three propositions emerged. In the resulting framework, leadership and governance are conceptualised as organisational cues in collective sensemaking, resource availability as a signal of management commitment, and role clarity and development opportunities as signals of organisational values. Formal arrangements did not consistently correspond to nurses' experienced authority or access. These patterns support an interpretive account in which leadership coherence, resource provision, and accessible development opportunities may be associated with shared PSC perceptions. Research limitations/implications Cross-sectional designs preclude causal inference. Empirical support was stronger for Propositions 1 and 2 than for Proposition 3. Validated PSC…

title: Electronic theses and dissertations management of agricultural university libraries in Bangladesh: challenges and recommendations
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine electronic theses and dissertations (ETDs) management in Bangladeshi agricultural university libraries, focusing on technological challenges, current practices and actionable recommendations. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research design was employed to collect data from the participating libraries. Four of the seven agricultural university libraries were selected for research sites. Given the limited number of universities maintaining ETD repositories and postgraduate research programs, purposive sampling was adopted. Data were collected through a semi-structured questionnaire administered to library professionals and analyzed using SPSS (version 25.0). Findings The findings reveal that all participating libraries use DSpace and maintain both born-digital and digitized theses. Substantial obstacles – including inadequate ICT infrastructure, limited technical expertise and resistance to technological advancements – continue to hinder effective ETDs management. Long-term digital preservation, repository security and infrastructural reliability emerged as major concerns affecting repository sustainability, accessibility, discoverability and visibility. Variations in digitization practices further indicate the need for improved governance and technological support. Practical implications The findings provide evidence-based guidance f…

title: Caught in ESG trap? Evidence from earnings pressure by examining CEO overconfidence and pay slice
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how firms balance long-term environmental, social and corporate governance (ESG) commitments with more tactical ESG actions aimed at managing capital-market expectations, particularly through dialogues with securities analysts. Drawing on a managerial-cognitive perspective, it investigates how CEO overconfidence and CEO pay slice shape ESG decisions under varying levels of earnings pressure. Design/methodology/approach Using a panel of 14,697 firm-year observations from S&P 1500 firms over 2003–2024, the study estimates OLS regressions of tactical ESG investing on earnings pressure and its interactions with CEO overconfidence and pay slice, and applies time-series clustering to firms’ ESG score trajectories to identify distinct behavioral patterns and industry-driven groupings. Findings The analysis finds that overconfident CEOs are more likely to pursue long-term ESG strategies and resist short-term tactical ESG responses under earnings pressure. In contrast, a high CEO pay slice is associated with increased tactical ESG engagement to meet analyst expectations. Time series clustering reveals industry-driven ESG behavior patterns, reinforcing the need to align governance mechanisms with executive traits and contextual factors in ESG strategy formulation. Practical implications Sustainable development cannot be advanced merely by increasing the…

title: Rethinking resilience: bridging due diligence gaps to mitigate supply chain risks
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to examine the key factors affecting supply chain due diligence (SCDD), evaluating their associated risks and proposing appropriate mitigation strategies that bridge due diligence gaps and strengthen resilience in global supply chains. Design/methodology/approach Key due diligence factors were identified through a comprehensive literature review and expert consultations. The study adopts a multimethod approach that integrates multiple theoretical perspectives, the Fuzzy Evidential Reasoning Algorithm (FERA) and risk profiling analysis. Findings The results identify critical due diligence factors, including regulatory compliance, transparency, supplier evaluation, ethical sourcing, data governance and sustainability practices, that significantly influence governance, operational stability and environmental performance. The study further develops targeted mitigation strategies based on risk intensity and strategic priority. Practical implications The proposed framework supports practitioners and policymakers in making risk-sensitive decisions to strengthen due diligence, improve transparency, enhance compliance and build more resilient and sustainable supply chain operations. Originality/value This study contributes to the SCDD literature by integrating governance, operational and sustainability dimensions within a unified prioritization frame…

title: Digitalisation and sustainable finance in SMEs: unpacking the causal mechanisms through a systematic review and integrative framework
abstract: Purpose Digitalisation has emerged as an important enabler of sustainable finance for small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). While prior studies have examined the roles of digital technologies, financial access and sustainability in SMEs, limited attention has been devoted to understanding the causal mechanisms through which digitalisation facilitates sustainable finance and contributes to sustainability outcomes. This study systematically reviews the literature to develop an integrated understanding of the pathways linking digitalisation, financial capability and sustainable firm performance. Design/methodology/approach A systematic literature review of 63 peer-reviewed articles published in Scopus-indexed journals between 2015 and 2026 was conducted. The review employs the theory-context-characteristics-methodology (TCCM) framework and the antecedents-decisions-outcomes (ADO) approach to synthesise the intellectual structure of the field, identify dominant research themes and develop an integrative conceptual framework. Findings The review demonstrates that digitalisation enables sustainable finance through several interrelated mechanisms, including enhanced information transparency, reduced transaction costs, improved risk assessment, greater financial inclusion and access to alternative financing channels. These mechanisms strengthen SMEs’ financial capability and digi…

title: Urological Manifestations and Management Patterns of Clinically Established Neurogenic Bladder Following Thoracolumbar Spinal Cord Injury: A Hospital-Based Observational Study
abstract: Background: Neurogenic bladder is a frequent and significant complication of thoracolumbar spinal cord injury that can lead to urinary tract infection, upper urinary tract injury, and decreased quality of life. This study aimed to describe the urological manifestations and management pattern of patients with thoracolumbar spine injury who presented with neurogenic bladder at a tertiary care hospital. Methods: This observational study was carried out at Dhaka National Medical College and Hospital from July 2024 to June 2025 on 35 patients. A structured questionnaire was used to gather data on sociodemographic variables, injury characteristics, urinary symptoms, clinical and diagnostic profile, complications and management, which was analyzed using SPSS version 26. Results: Most participants were male (77.1%), rural residents (65.7%), and aged 31-40 years (31.4%). The most common injury mechanisms were falls from height (45.7%) and road traffic accidents (37.1%), with the thoracolumbar junction being the most frequently injured (42.9%). Urinary retention (71.4%) and difficulty initiating urination (62.9%) were the most common symptoms. The most common pattern was an areflexic bladder (51.4%), 42.9% had a post-void residual greater than 300 mL, and 17.1% had hydronephrosis. 51.4% of participants had a urinary tract infection. The most common bladder-emptying method was indwelling …
venue: Journal of Dhaka National Medical College & Hospital

title: Scaling small- and medium-sized enterprise artificial intelligence through governance: A Technology–Organisation–Environment readiness synthesis for information management
abstract: Background: Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) are increasingly experimenting with artificial intelligence (AI), yet many struggle to translate early use into scalable and trusted organisational value. Objectives: This study aimed to identify the conditions that enable or constrain SME AI adoption and assimilation, explain how responsible AI governance shapes progression towards trusted and commercially durable use and interpret the implications for market access and cash-flow-relevant value in Cape Town and the Western Cape. Method: A PRISMA 2020-guided scoping review synthesised global peer-reviewed studies published from January 2021 to December 2025. Database searching and citation chaining identified 486 records, of which 72 met the inclusion criteria. Cape Town and the Western Cape were used as an interpretive application lens rather than as the empirical study setting. Results: Small- and medium-sized enterprise AI adoption and assimilation were shaped by technological readiness, organisational capability, environmental support and governance quality. Trusted data, interoperable systems, leadership commitment, hybrid skills and process discipline supported routinised use. These capabilities enabled service responsiveness, forecasting and customer engagement that may strengthen market access and cash-flow visibility. Fragmented data, skills scarcity, vendor depend…
venue: South African Journal of Information Management

title: A data-driven supervised machine learning study for road-accident prediction in smart transportation operations and planning in smart cities
abstract: Road traffic accidents are still a key public-safety issue that drives the need for intelligent transportation systems to develop data-driven approaches to identifying passengers who are at risk of being involved in an accident. The aim of the current study is to compare machine-learning models on the classification of whether an accident occurs or not from the Transportation and Accident Prediction Dataset (TAPD). There are 5,500 cases and 17 attributes in the data set. The predictors listed were selected without leakage of the target, namely, so that there was no leakage into the target from the following variables: Accident_Severity and Alert_Generated. Accident_Occurred was selected as the binary target and Record_ID was excluded as an identifier. The classifiers that were evaluated and compared were KNearestNeighbors, Adaboost, CN2RuleInducer, SupportVectorMachine, RandomForest and NaiveBayes, with 10-fold cross validation. The accuracy, 95 % Wilson confidence intervals, precision, recall, specificity, F1 and balanced accuracy were used to measure performance. The highest accuracy (97.62%) and specificity (100%) was achieved by RF and NB, with both having a positive-class recall of 77.22%. The highest recall for the positive class was obtained by AdaBoost among the other ones (78.09%). The results show that the overall high accuracy can mask cases of accidents that are not…

title: Physics-Informed Global Model Development via Federated Learning for Indoor Temperature Prediction Toward Advanced Building Control
Risk factors and time-to-event prediction of brain metastasis in patients with lung adenocarcinoma: a retrospective cohort study
abstract: Background Brain metastasis (BM) is a clinically important complication of lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), yet prediction is complicated by variable follow-up, censoring, treatment effects, and competing mortality. This study evaluated time-dependent BM risk and developed an exploratory prediction model in patients with LUAD without BM at baseline. Methods Consecutive patients with pathologically confirmed LUAD treated between 2018 and 2024 were retrospectively screened. Patients entered the cohort at the date of a negative baseline contrast-enhanced brain MRI. Incident BM was analyzed using Cox proportional hazards regression. Candidate predictors were prespecified, collinearity was assessed, and LASSO-penalized Cox regression was used for predictor reduction. Internal validation used 1,000 bootstrap resamples. Competing mortality was evaluated using Fine–Gray analysis, and EGFR-TKI exposure was examined as a time-dependent covariate. Results Of 94 screened patients, 66 were included; 26 developed incident BM during a median follow-up of 27.8 months. LASSO retained T classification, N classification, EGFR mutation status, and serum CEA. In the parsimonious Cox model, T3–4 disease, N1–3 involvement, and EGFR mutation were associated with higher BM hazard, while the CEA estimate was less precise. The apparent C-index was 0.781 and the optimism-corrected C-index was 0.742. Time-depen…

title: LESS-PseU: A Language Model-Enhanced Semistacking Framework for RNA Pseudouridine Site Prediction
abstract: Abstract Accurate prediction of RNA pseudouridine (Ψ) sites remains challenging because existing models often struggle to integrate interpretable handcrafted features with high-dimensional contextual representations from pretrained genomic language models. To address this issue, we propose LESS-PseU, a language model-enhanced semistacking framework that fuses the predicted probability features of primary learners with DNABERT2 embeddings for multiple species Ψ site prediction. Specifically, we first built three primary learners based on three kinds of hand-crafted features, including one-hot, k-mer, and nucleotide chemical property features. Instead of training a primary learner based on the embeddings extracted from DNABERT2, the embeddings were directly concatenated with the predicted probabilities of the three primary learners as the input features for a Logistic Regression meta-learner for final prediction. Under a leakage-aware cross-validation setting, our model was validated on the training sets of three species. Furthermore, on independent test sets from human, mouse, and yeast, LESS-PseU achieved AUC values of 0.9069, 0.8833, and 0.8820, respectively, which were higher than those of the compared models. A Friedman test indicated an overall difference (p = 0.029). Paired DeLong tests further showed that the AUC improvements over Meta-PseU were significant for the human …
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Multi-output Gaussian process regression for uncertainty-aware sound insulation prediction in mass timber floors
abstract: Reliable analysis of sound insulation of mass timber floors requires extensive and time-consuming measurements. Such multi-layer assemblies exhibit a complex insulation behavior under both airborne and structure-borne excitation, governed by the interactions between individual layers. In addition, there are uncertainties associated with timber as a building material, its processing, and measurement of the built assemblies. In order to reduce the measurement effort in the long term, a prediction approach that both accounts for these uncertainties in the model and quantifies them in its predictions is required. This study introduces multi-output Gaussian process regression models for the prediction of airborne and impact sound insulation spectra from 50 Hz to 5 kHz. Single-number quantities are derived from the prediction distributions using a Monte Carlo method. The models are developed on a curated dataset of laboratory measurements of mass timber floor assemblies. To also account for nominal inputs, the models are augmented by embeddings that are trained end-to-end with the remaining model parameters under a common objective, the negative log marginal likelihood. The predictions distinguish aleatoric, i.e. measurement-related uncertainty, from epistemic uncertainty that additional knowledge could reduce. Averaged over the frequency bands, the predictions reach mean absolute er…

title: Antimicrobial Peptide Databases and Prediction Tools: Toward a Standard Evaluation Framework
abstract: Abstract Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) has a profound impact on animal and human health and is associated with substantial morbidity, mortality, and public health costs. There is a clear need to develop novel, effective antibiotic agents, which can overcome the current AMR crisis. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) may offer such a solution and have attracted growing attention for their potential to combat AMR. In parallel, the growing availability of peptide sequences in public databases has stimulated the development of numerous machine learning and deep learning tools to predict antimicrobial activity computationally. However, it remains unclear how reliably these tools can be compared, as existing studies often rely on heterogeneous data sets and inconsistent evaluation protocols that may lead to data leakage and inflated performance estimates. This raises a central question: what evaluation criteria and benchmark resources are needed to enable fair, reproducible, and biologically meaningful assessment of AMP prediction tools? We address this question by focusing specifically on antibacterial peptides (ABPs). We first provide an overview of AMP databases relevant to antibacterial activity and compare their content, redundancy, and experimental metadata. We then critically assess existing computational tools for ABP prediction, highlighting key limitations related to data set co…
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Image-Based Soil Nutrient Prediction Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning Models
abstract: Recent advances in precision agriculture have enabled the use of machine learning and image processing for rapid soil nutrient assessment. This study presents a non-destructive approach for estimating soil nutrient content from digital soil images captured using a camera and analyzed through specialized software. A dataset of 1,500 soil images was processed using color correction, noise reduction, and feature extraction techniques to improve data quality. Five machine learning models, Random Forest, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM), Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM), and a Stacking Regressor, were evaluated for predicting nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium levels. A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) based deep learning model was served as a benchmark. No single model was best for every nutrient and metric. For nitrogen, GBM achieved the lowest test MAE (0.1652), whereas the Stacking Regressor achieved the highest test R² (0.9886). For potassium, Random Forest achieved the lowest test MAE (0.0051), whereas XGBoost achieved the highest test R² (0.9999). For phosphorus, XGBoost achieved both the lowest test MAE (0.1558) and the highest test R² (0.9929). Thus, the best-performing model depends on the nutrient and evaluation metric. Further validation using independent field datasets is required to establish robustness under diverse env…

Psychiatric rehabilitation in Oman: service gaps and a framework for recovery-oriented care
abstract: Psychiatric rehabilitation is a crucial aspect of recovery-oriented mental healthcare, yet it remains underdeveloped in Oman. This paper reviews the current state of rehabilitation services, identifying systemic gaps in in-patient, day care and community-based provisions. Services are fragmented, lacking adequate multidisciplinary integration, sufficient community rehabilitation and supported housing, which leads to prolonged hospital stays. Additionally, broader challenges such as stigma and limited intersectoral collaboration hinder service development. The paper suggests practical strategies to enhance rehabilitation services, including the establishment of multidisciplinary teams, expansion of community programmes, provision of supported accommodation and workforce training, all aligned with Oman Vision 2040 and the principles of recovery-oriented mental health care.

title: Operational efficiency in blood component production: time-driven process mapping study from a national blood service in sub-Saharan Africa
abstract: Abstract Background Efficient blood service operations are critical to safe blood supply in low- and middle-income countries (LMIC). Process mapping provides a systematic approach to understanding operational complexity and identifying inefficiencies. This study aims to map the blood component production cycle at a national blood service. Methods We conducted a detailed process mapping exercise across four stages of blood production: donor recruitment, blood collection, blood processing and testing, and storage and dispatch. We enumerated client pathways and recorded active process times at each stage, guided by a time-driven data collection framework. The e-Delphyn blood donor management system supported data capture at static and mobile collection sites. Results The blood component production cycle comprises four sequential stages, generating 31 distinct client pathways at the donor recruitment stage alone, reflecting substantial operational complexity. Donor recruitment active organization time ranged from 6 to 148 min, depending on the mobilization approach and site. Blood collection followed a consistent patient flow regardless of site, with optimal completion time of ~ 31 min. Under minimum batch conditions, blood processing and testing required a minimum of 113 min. Blood component production times varied substantially from 15 min for packed red blood cells via platelet-…

title: Omnichannel retailing, service quality, brand trust, and customer brand engagement as drivers of brand advocacy in Indonesian health care services: A cross-sectional PLS-SEM study
abstract: Background Indonesian health care providers must now integrate physical and digital channels, yet how patients advocate for a health care brand remains poorly understood. Omnichannel retailing, service quality, brand trust, customer brand engagement, and brand advocacy have been examined in isolation, and their integration within a single stimulus–organism–response (S-O-R) framework is rarely discussed. This study investigates whether channel integration has displaced service quality as the driver of patient trust and advocacy, or whether the two operate through distinct mechanisms. Methods A total of 324 patients were surveyed at a primary clinic, a private hospital, and a regional public hospital in Greater Jakarta. A 49-item, five-point Likert-type questionnaire, adapted from validated English-language scales through back-translation, expert content validation, face validation, and a pretest (n = 50), was digitally administered after the service encounter. Partial least squares structural equation modelling was applied using a disjoint two-stage approach for the higher-order constructs and 5,000 bootstrap subsamples. Results All six hypotheses were supported. Service quality raised trust (β = 0.430) almost twice as strongly as omnichannel retailing (β = 0.259): competence outweighs cross-channel convenience. Trust raised customer brand engagement (β = 0.442), the strongest p…

title: The “Beijing Effect” in AI Regulation
abstract: In this paper, the author analyzes the concept of the “Beijing effect” as an alternative to the concept of “digital authoritarianism”. The relevance of the topic stems from the rapid growth of the artificial intelligence (AI) sector and the emergence of various models of its regulation. The paper also analyzes the concept of the Digital Silk Road as a tool through which investments in the economies of other countries are transformed into China’s political influence. The author concludes that there is a transition from hard “lock-in” to soft influence, facilitated by standards and open AI models. The paper shows how China, by financing the digital infrastructure of developing countries, renders their digital sovereignty illusory. The work is valuable for understanding why AI regulation cannot be reduced to laws when the underlying infrastructure is owned by other countries.

title: Plant Cell-Mimetic Flexible Films for Integrated Solar-Thermal Regulation and Smart Sensing
abstract: Abstract The growing pressures from energy scarcity and climate change are driving the demand for personal thermal management materials that function efficiently at the body scale. However, integrating solar heat harvesting, leakage-free phase-change heat storage, and flexible sensing within a single soft material remains challenging, because these functions impose distinct, often conflicting, requirements on composition, phase distribution, and interfacial structure. Here, we report a plant-cell-inspired, one-step self-segregation strategy to construct a biomimetic Janus heterogeneous flexible film. During film formation, phase-change microcapsules spontaneously sediment to form a vacuole-like energy-storage bottom layer, whereas carbon nanotubes enrich at the upper surface, yielding a chloroplast-like continuous light-harvesting network. This vertical compartmentalization mitigates the filler-dilution trade-off commonly encountered in conventional composites. The resulting film achieves a photothermal conversion efficiency of 95.11% under 808 nm near-infrared irradiation and provides leakage-free latent-heat buffering. Introducing an interfacial regulator endows the film with high stretchability of 637.3% while allowing the film to retain its key functions after moisture exposure. In addition to thermal regulation, the integrated conductive and moisture-responsive pathways en…

title: Evaluating Risk Factors and Frequency of Neonatal Hypoglycemia Admitted in NICU of Bangladesh Shishu Hospital & Institute
abstract: Background: Neonatal hypoglycemia is a common metabolic disturbance during the neonatal period and remains an important cause of neonatal morbidity. Early screening of at-risk neonates and prompt management are essential to prevent adverse outcomes. Objective: To determine the prevalence, clinical presentation, and associated risk factors of neonatal hypoglycemia among neonates admitted to the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) of Bangladesh Shishu Hospital & Institute. Methods: This cross sectional study was conducted in the NICU of Bangladesh Shishu Hospital & Institute from July to December 2024. All admitted neonates were screened for hypoglycemia (blood glucose <2.5 mmol/L). Detailed antenatal, natal, and postnatal histories, clinical features, birth weight, and gestational age were recorded. Neonates with congenital malformations, suspected inborn errors of metabolism, or maternal history of oral hypoglycemic agents or beta-sympathomimetic drug use were excluded. Data were analyzed statistically, and p<0.05 was considered significant. Results: Among 368 admitted neonates, 18 developed hypoglycemia, giving a prevalence of 4.9% (95% CI: 2.9–7.7%). Most admitted neonates were term (76.4%) with normal birth weight (76.1%); mean gestational age was 36.8±2.9 weeks and mean birth weight was 2.64±0.72 kg. Infant of diabetic mother was the most common associated risk factor (22.2…

title: How control allocation in AI-enabled travel planning shapes reuse intention: the roles of user experience, emotion regulation and psychological empowerment
abstract: Purpose This study examines how control allocation between users and artificial intelligence (AI) systems shapes reuse intention in AI-enabled travel planning and whether this effect operates through user experience (UX), cognitive reappraisal, expressive suppression, psychological empowerment and satisfaction. Design/methodology/approach Two scenario-based studies were conducted. A laboratory pilot (n = 92) validated system-dominant, shared-control and user-dominant planning conditions. A main online study (n = 463) tested the proposed serial process using confirmatory factor analysis, structural equation modeling and 5,000-resample bootstrapping. Findings Control allocation significantly affected UX. More favorable UX increased cognitive reappraisal and reduced expressive suppression, and these two regulatory routes had opposite effects on psychological empowerment. Empowerment enhanced satisfaction, which subsequently predicted reuse intention. A supplementary analysis further indicated that AI usage experience conditioned the relationships between UX and emotion regulation. Practical implications AI travel planners should treat control allocation as an interaction-design decision. Modular editing, progressive explanations, reversible changes and adaptive control can preserve user agency while retaining the efficiency benefits of AI assistance. Originality/value This study e…

Correlating structural, optical, dielectric, and antioxidant properties of rare-earth-doped CeO₂ nanoparticles for nanobiosensor and high-frequency device applications
Small caps, large climate data gaps: disclosure shortfalls and investment implications amid regulation retreats
abstract: Purpose This study aims to establish small-cap investment relevance, examine portfolio risk exposures of small-cap stocks screened by environmental data availability, and explore disclosure coverage under three Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) threshold specifications. Design/methodology/approach This study analyses MSCI index returns during 2001–2025 and 2023 Scope 1–3 emissions data availability for 7,895 constituents. We constructs value-weighted portfolios of disclosed and non-disclosed small-cap firms, estimates risk exposure differences using Fama–French six-factor models, and compares climate–data coverage across three CSRD threshold specifications. Findings Small-cap indices recorded higher returns and risk-adjusted performance than mid + large-cap peers, though firm size is not a causal driver. Emissions coverage is lower among small caps, especially for Scope 3 and in Emerging Markets. Non-disclosed-minus-disclosed small-cap portfolios have positive monthly alphas of 1.0–1.5 percentage points and exhibit systematic differences in growth, momentum and, in Developed Markets, profitability exposures. These estimates reflect portfolio-selection effects rather than a causal disclosure effect and may capture omitted firm characteristics or model specification. Applying the original CSRD (the relaxed Omnibus) thresholds leaves 0%–4% (48.5%) of small-cap (E…

title: Mesoscale regulation of ordered membrane electrode assemblies for hydrogen-electric energy interconversion systems
abstract: Hydrogen-electric energy interconversion systems represented by proton exchange membrane fuel cells and PEM water electrolyzers are key technologies for clean energy conversion. However, their widespread commercialization is hindered by challenges such as high cost and limited durability, largely attributed to inefficient catalyst utilization and multiphase transport limitations in conventional membrane electrode assemblies (MEAs). In recent years, ordered MEAs have emerged as a promising strategy to rationally structure the catalyst layer (CL), proton exchange membrane, and gas diffusion layer (GDL) at the mesoscale, thereby enabling ordered pathways for proton, electron, gas, and water transport. This paper reviews the design and regulation strategies of ordered membrane electrodes from the mesoscale perspective, focusing on the ordered structures of the CL, PEM, GDL and their effects on cell performance. The optimization of the reaction interface, the construction of long-range ordered proton transport channels and the design of hierarchical porous GDLs have resulted in significant advancements in the field. The paper concludes with a discussion of the current challenges in research and offers a perspective on future directions, including scale-up preparation, long-term stability assessment and multi-scale coupling mechanism research.

title: Frequency and Risk Factors of Functional Constipation among Children Attending Outpatient Clinics
abstract: Background: Functional constipation is a common pediatric gastrointestinal disorder with multifactorial etiology. Despite its prevalence, many contributing risk factors are under-recognized in clinical settings, especially in limited resource. Objective: To determine the frequency of functional constipation and identify associated risk factors among children. Materials and Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 150 children attending a pediatric outpatient department. Functional constipation was diagnosed based on Rome IV criteria. Data on sociodemographic characteristics, clinical symptoms, bowel habits, dietary patterns, physical activity, and screen time were collected using a structured questionnaire. Statistical analyses included chi-square tests and multivariate logistic regression. Results: Among 150 children, 84 (56%) were diagnosed with functional constipation. The majority of affected children were aged 6–10 years (47.6%), with a slight male predominance (52.4%). Hard stool (75%), large-diameter stool (85.7%), painful bowel movements (69.0%), and abdominal pain (47.6%) were the most common clinical features. More than half of the children had prolonged screen time >2 hours/day (64.3%), inadequate fiber intake (53.6%), inadequate fluid intake (51.2%), and poor school toilet facilities (61.9%). Emotional abuse was reported in 25% of cases, while positive p…
