title: The Role of Self-Regulation in the Formation of Learning Activity Style among Chinese Students
abstract: The number of Chinese students studying in Russia has been steadily increasing over the past decade. Despite the fact that a quantity of studies on the ethnocultural characteristics of Chinese students is growing, there are still many questions about the specifics of the educational activities of Chinese students and their organization in the educational space in Russia. The purpose of this research is to conduct a theoretical analysis of scientific papers on the importance and role of the self-regulation process for a promising investigation of its resource potential in shaping the style of learning activities among Chinese students. The theoretical analysis of the specifics of the activity-based approach and its reconstruction in substantiating the style of educational activity as well as the results of empirical studies conducted with the participation of Chinese students in Russia and abroad allowed us to consider the psychological characteristics of their self-regulation as a fundamental variable between individual and personal characteristics and the style of educational activity. As a result of the analysis, it was determined that self-regulation performs the function of transformation and integration ensuring the transition from personal prerequisites to sustainable forms of learning activity. The novelty of the research consists in the theoretical substantiation of the…

title: Sarcosine-Mediated Interface Regulation of SnO2 Electron Transport Layer toward High-Performance and Durable MAPbI3 Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: Abstract Driven by exceptional light-to-electricity conversion performance alongside inexpensive solution-phase manufacturing, metal halide perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have emerged as a major focus of next-generation photovoltaic research. Nevertheless, further performance enhancements remain constrained by high defect densities at the electron transport layer (ETL) interface, suboptimal band alignment, and pronounced nonradiative carrier recombination. Herein, a direct incorporation strategy was developed by introducing sarcosine (Sar) into the SnO2 colloidal precursor to regulate the surface properties and chemical environment of the SnO2 electron transport layer, which is associated with improved MAPbI3 perovskite film formation. Spectroscopic characterizations indicate that chemical coordination between the amine/carboxylic moieties of Sar and unsaturated Sn centers at the SnO2 boundary contributes to interfacial defect passivation alongside a favorable energy band alignment. Simultaneously, the boosted surface hydrophilicity promotes uniform precursor coverage and regulates grain nucleation, ultimately yielding perovskite thin films with elevated crystalline order and minimized defect density. Consequently, optoelectronic analyses reveal accelerated interfacial charge transfer and suppressed nonradiative recombination pathways, contributing to reduced hysteresis and sign…

title: Protecting the Greater One-Horned Rhinoceros: The Role of Workforce Capacity, Legal Enforcement, and Patrolling in Protected Areas
abstract: This study examines the relationship between anti-poaching management strategies and wild greater one-horned rhinoceros population outcomes in Assam, India. Drawing on archival data from the Assam Forest Department, the study assesses whether key anti-poaching measures, including frontline staffing levels, personnel salary expenditures, poacher arrests, and patrolling efforts, are associated with changes in wild rhino populations. The findings reveal that frontline staffing levels and salary expenditures are significantly associated with rhinoceros population recovery, suggesting that investments in human resources may strengthen deterrence, field monitoring, and habitat protection. Legal enforcement, measured by the number of poachers arrested, also demonstrates a statistically significant association with rhinoceros population outcomes, highlighting the importance of effective law enforcement in anti-poaching strategies. In contrast, patrolling effort alone was not a statistically significant predictor of rhinoceros population changes, suggesting that patrol effectiveness may depend on complementary measures, such as adequate staffing, consistent law enforcement, and systematic monitoring. Overall, the findings highlight the importance of institutional capacity and coordinated enforcement strategies in rhinoceros conservation. The study offers practical policy implications fo…
venue_publisher: Canadian Center of Science and Education

title: Efficacy and Mechanism of Generative AI in Empowering English Writing Instruction
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence technology brings new transformative opportunities to English writing instruction. This paper analyzes the efficacy and mechanism of generative AI in empowering English writing teaching. Drawing on the Technology Acceptance Model and Self-Regulated Learning theory, it summarizes teaching efficacy from three dimensions—the quality of writing output, cognitive support during the writing process, and real-time adaptation of writing feedback—and further reveals the underlying mechanism through three layers: cognitive load reduction, learning motivation activation, and metacognitive strategy activation. Using data from a 12-week quasi-experimental study, it compares the experimental and control groups in terms of writing performance, writing strategy use, and feedback engagement. The results show that generative AI-assisted instruction has a moderately strong facilitative effect on learners' writing performance, achieved mainly by reducing extraneous cognitive load, enhancing writing self-efficacy, and deepening feedback engagement. This study provides theoretical grounding and practical reference for integrating generative AI into the English writing classroom.
venue: International Journal of Social Science Education and Humanities

title: Calcium Alginate/Polyaniline-PSS Core–Shell Particles: Synthesis and Multi-Mechanism Water Vapor Adsorption Behavior
abstract: Abstract Core–shell composite particles combining a calcium alginate (Alg-Ca) hydrogel core with a polyaniline/polystyrene sulfonic acid (PANi/PSS) conductive polymer shell were synthesized and evaluated for water vapor adsorption applications. The resulting particles exhibited a well-defined, phase-separated architecture, comprising a highly hydrated, porous hydrogel core encapsulated by a structurally and chemically distinct shell, consistent with successful incorporation of the sulfonated conductive polymer onto the surface of the alginate network. The core and shell regions displayed markedly different thermal decomposition behavior, confirming their compositional distinction and demonstrating that the composite retains thermal stability within the operating range typical of gas-sensing applications. Kinetic analysis of water vapor adsorption as a function of relative humidity (RH, 50–95%) and temperature (25–45 °C) revealed a systematic transition among pseudo-first-order, pseudo-second-order, and Elovich kinetic models. At moderate RH, adsorption was governed by chemically homogeneous interactions at polar functional groups, while at near-saturation RH, the mechanism shifted toward multilayer adsorption and capillary condensation. Temperature-dependent measurements at fixed RH further revealed an unusual diffusion–reaction–diffusion transition across the studied temperatu…

title: New Insights into the Decoupling Mechanism of Ion Motion from Segmental Relaxation in Glass-Forming Polymers: The Interplay of Cohesive Energy Density
abstract: Abstract Decoupling ion transport from segmental motion offers a promising route for solid polymer electrolytes, yet identifying its governing factor, whether the glass transition temperature (Tg), fragility index (m), or dynamic heterogeneity, remains challenging due to their inherent interdependence. Here, we systematically investigate this decoupling in poly(vinyl acetal)s by varying acetal group length, molecular weight, plasticization, and antiplasticization. It was found that decoupling strength is not dictated simply by Tg, m, or dynamic heterogeneity. Microstructurally, the dynamically heterogeneous “slow” domains are characterized by dense molecular packing and higher cohesive energy density, irrespective of plasticization or antiplasticization. This same characteristic is observed in poly(vinyl acetal) bearing short acetal groups, wherein a weak decoupling effect is also detectable as observed in the “slow” domains. Furthermore, a negative correlation between decoupling exponent and the square of solubility parameter (i.e., cohesive energy density) at room temperature was found, confirming that cohesive energy density plays a key role in governing decoupling. We suppose that the enhanced cohesive energy density impedes ion motion and confines it to proceed only in tandem with segmental relaxation. These findings not only provide new experimental evidence for the decou…

title: Hierarchically Structured Anti-Perovskite Oxynitride-Hydride Enabling Ammonia Synthesis via a Cooperative Mechanism Mediated by (N2)− Ions
abstract: Abstract Ba3AlO4-xNyHz with an antiperovskite structure is employed as a support for transition-metal catalysts for ammonia synthesis. This metastable material is synthesized by employing multiple anions with different valences and ionic radii. The optimized non-noble metal catalyst, Co(5.8 wt %)/Ba3AlO4-xNyHz/Al2O3, exhibits an exceptional ammonia synthesis rate of 15.9 mmol g–1 h–1 at 0.9 MPa and 300 °C, outperforming benchmark Cs–Ru/MgO, industrial Fe catalyst, and recently reported non-noble metal catalysts. Structural analyses show that Ba3AlO4-xNyHz and Co species self-organize on γ-Al2O3 nanorods to form a hierarchically structured catalyst. Combined experimental and density functional theory analyses reveal that the high activity originates from incorporated (N2)− ions at Co–Ba–Al interfacial sites, where the combination of Ba and Al plays distinct roles in N2 activation and NHx formation, respectively. These findings not only provide a strategy for stabilizing metastable crystal structures through the incorporation of diverse anionic species but also demonstrate a unique cooperative mechanism for efficient ammonia synthesis mediated by highly activated molecular (N2)− ions.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Photocatalytic performance of graphitic carbon nitride (g-C 3 N 4 ): tuning factors, mechanisms, challenges, and opportunities
abstract: Abstract Graphitic carbon nitride (g-C3N4) has emerged as the most significant metal-free photocatalyst owing to its suitable band gap, chemical stability, and low-cost synthesis. However, its practical photocatalytic performance is limited by rapid charge recombination, low surface area, and insufficient visible-light absorption. This review provides a comprehensive and critical analysis of the key factors governing the photocatalytic activity of g-C 3 N 4 and the strategies employed to tune its performance. Fundamental properties like electronic structure and photocatalytic mechanisms are first discussed to establish a theoretical foundation. Subsequently, various tuning approaches like morphology control, heteroatom doping, heterojunction engineering, defect creation, co-catalyst loading, and synthesis optimization are systematically analyzed with mechanistic insights. A comparative evaluation highlights the advantages and limitations of each strategy. The review further explores major applications in environmental remediation, hydrogen evolution, CO 2 reduction, and pollutant degradation. Finally, critical challenges like scalability, stability, and mechanistic ambiguity are addressed followed by future research directions. This work aims to provide a clear roadmap for the rational design of high-performance g-C3N4–based photocatalysts.

title: Insight into the Role of Sulfur Confined within the Porous Carbon Structure in 2-Chloroethyl Ethyl Sulfide Adsorption
abstract: Abstract The interactions of 2-chloroethyl ethyl sulfide (CEES), a mustard gas surrogate, with porous carbons, whose surface features were tuned by sulfur insertion, were investigated in this study. The modification process introduced 0%, 5%, 10%, and 50% sulfur relative to the total pore volume of each carbon. Both surface chemistry and porosity were affected, and the extent of changes depended on the initial carbon surface features. CEES adsorption experiments were performed in a closed system, enabling simultaneous analysis of the surrogate adsorbed on the carbon surface and its vapors released into the headspace. The results showed that a gradual decrease in the porosity by sulfur insertion markedly hindered CEES adsorption. The measurement of the heat released upon complete filling of the pores revealed its dependence on accessible pores with the highest adsorption potentials. The analysis of the efficiency of CEES extraction from the pore system combined with DFT calculations suggested that at a low sulfur loading (5% of pore volume), confined sulfur promoted the retention of CEES molecules due to Ssurface–SCEES dispersive interactions, emphasizing the importance of deposited sulfur for separation and extraction processes.

title: Scenario-based land use optimization and carbon storage assessment for regional sustainability: Evidence from the Chengdu–Chongqing Economic Circle
Mechanistic Insights into Chemical-Assisted Steam Injection: Pore-Scale Evidence for More Efficient and Lower-Carbon Heavy Oil Recovery
abstract: Abstract Steam-assisted gravity drainage (SAGD) is the primary method for in situ extraction of heavy oil and bitumen in Canada. However, it (as well as other steam injection methods) suffers from low efficiency, high water and energy consumption, and significant environmental impact. Adding chemicals to steam offers a potential solution by enhancing oil recovery while reducing carbon emissions through lower steam usage. Our previous studies have shown that deep eutectic solvents (DES) and thermally stable nonionic surfactants improve steam chamber sweep efficiency and microscopic displacement efficiency, respectively. However, their mechanisms and effects in porous media, especially at the pore scale, remain unclear. This study explores the microdisplacement mechanisms of these chemical additives. A porous medium model was created by packing glass beads between two plexiglass plates, which was then saturated with heavy oil at a slow injection rate. The research focused on steam chamber growth dynamics, physicochemical changes at the oil-steam-water-rock interface, and their impact on oil drainage. By comparing oil recovery efficiency, energy efficiency, and carbon intensity of SAGD with and without chemical additives, the effects of DES (formulated in our laboratories and named as DES 11) and Novelfroth (a commercial nonionic surfactant) on steam injection efficiency were eval…

title: Microscopic origins of velocity- and temperature-dependent friction in unpassivated amorphous carbon
abstract: Abstract Interfacial friction is an extremely common form of interaction between materials in the field of materials science. It is well known that hydrogenation or environmental passivation can influence the frictional performance of amorphous carbon coatings. However, the atomic-scale friction mechanisms at clean, unpassivated amorphous carbon interfaces remain insufficiently understood. The primary reason is that experimental observations and conventional friction theories have difficulty in describing atomic-scale dynamics in nonperiodic amorphous systems. Here, we employ a machine learning-based deep potential model and quantum thermal bath method to achieve first-principles accuracy in studying the atomic-scale frictional behavior of amorphous carbon interfaces. The simulated friction is qualitatively similar to some experimental findings. By analyzing atomic-scale bond dynamics, we develop a phenomenological friction model that quantitatively describes the microscopic sliding friction at the unpassivated amorphous carbon interface. We further demonstrate that increasing temperature suppresses sliding friction in this system. An ultralow-friction state can be approached at extreme temperatures (~2,000 °C). This work establishes a universal, structure-independent model bridging atomic simulations and friction models, offering insights into designing low-friction materials.

title: Determination of the Muzzle-to-Target Distance in Shooting Cases Using Inductively Coupled Plasma – Optical Emission Analysis of Barium, Lead, and Antimony
abstract: Between 2015 and 2023 firearm-related deaths almost doubled in the U.S., increasing discussions concerning gun control measurements. Gun regulations vary between states. States like Mississippi have not only relaxed gun control laws but also the highest firearm-related deaths. Research involving inorganic gunshot residue (IGSR) typically focuses on the shooter end rather than the target material. This work aimed to create a mathematical relationship between the concentration of metals on target materials and the muzzle-to-target distance for the estimation of shooting distance. Cloth samples containing IGSRs were obtained by shooting a Remington UMC 9mm Luger ammunition from a Smith & Wesson M&P9 Shield semi-automatic pistol in a controlled indoor environment at varying distances. The IGSR was extracted from samples using an acid digestion procedure and analyzed using Inductively Coupled Plasma-Optical Emission Spectroscopy (ICP-OES) to quantify barium, lead, and antimony. A mathematical model was developed for the interpretation of barium, lead, and antimony in both ammunitions analyzed. Polynomial regression was employed as an exploratory tool to visualize the non-linear relationship between IGSR concentration and shooting distance within the experimental range studied. This research provides evidence that the relationship between muzzle-to-target distance and the concentrati…

title: A Review of Benign and Malignant Neoplastic Lesions of the Thorax on Positron Emission Tomography/Computed Tomography
Benchmarking carbon trading adoption in emerging economies through extending the TOE framework
abstract: Purpose This study examines the factors influencing carbon trading system adoption by extending the traditional technology–organisation–environment (TOE) model into the decentralised technology–organisation–environment–technoethics (DT-OET) model. Design/methodology/approach This study used a quantitative research design with a cross-sectional approach and collected data from 384 professionals working in related sectors in Bangladesh. Partial least squares-structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) was used to analyse the data along with unobserved heterogeneity analysis and importance-performance map analysis (IPMA). Findings The structural model shows that organisational readiness, environmental factors and technoethical factors have significant positive effects on carbon trading adoption. Decentralised technology factors do not have a significant direct effect, but their influence is significantly mediated by trust. Interestingly, trust emerges as a strong direct predictor and also significantly mediates the effects of technoethical, environmental and decentralised technology factors on adoption intention. Practical implications The DT-OET instruments of this paper offer organisations a diagnostic framework to assess their readiness for carbon trading. According to the findings, managers need to prioritise top management support, resource allocation and employee training. Polic…

title: Beyond risk mitigation: agricultural insurance enhances crop carbon absorption and delivers environmental co-benefits
abstract: Introduction Agricultural insurance is widely recognized as an economic instrument for dispersing production risk, yet whether it yields environmental co-benefits remains underexplored. This study shifts the focus beyond risk mitigation by examining how agricultural insurance shapes crop carbon absorption. Methods Drawing on a 14-year panel of 333 prefecture-level cities in China, we combine a two-way fixed effects model augmented with province-by-year interaction effects, an instrumental variable approach, and a robust heterogeneous Difference-in-Differences approach to establish causality. Results The results show that agricultural insurance significantly enhances crop carbon absorption. Mechanism analyses trace this effect to the reshaping of farmers’ production decisions: structural adjustment toward staple crop cultivation and scale expansion through a higher multiple cropping index. Heterogeneity analyses corroborate these channels, revealing stronger effects in major grain-producing areas and regions with larger per capita arable land. The carbon benefits are also more pronounced in economically underdeveloped areas and regions where non-agricultural industries are less developed. Discussion Beyond risk mitigation, agricultural insurance thus serves as a policy lever translating micro-level farmer behavior into macro-level ecological gains, and the resulting carbon absor…

title: Adaptability of construction procurement practices to achieve net-zero carbon targets in Sri Lanka
abstract: Purpose Procurement practices play a crucial role in achieving net-zero carbon targets in the construction industry. However, their adaptability in developing countries remains constrained by various contextual barriers. In addition, limited research has systematically mapped procurement practices and strategies for achieving net-zero carbon targets. Therefore, this study aims to investigate the adaptability of construction procurement practices for achieving net-zero carbon targets in Sri Lanka. Design/methodology/approach This study adopted a qualitative Delphi approach involving two rounds of semi-structured expert interviews. Eighteen experts participated in the first round, followed by 12 experts in the second round. Data collected from the experts were analysed using code-based content analysis to identify relevant net-zero carbon strategies, procurement practices and their integration within the construction procurement process. Findings The findings identified seven notable net-zero carbon strategies applicable to the Sri Lankan construction industry and 15 best procurement practices that can facilitate the achievement of these strategies. Furthermore, the study developed a comprehensive integration framework illustrating how procurement practices can be embedded within both pre-contract and post-contract stages to support the implementation of net-zero carbon strategie…
venue: Journal of Engineering, Design and Technology

title: Interfacial Synergistic Engineering of Piezoelectric PVDF/GO/Bi2WO6 Nanofiber Membranes: Coupling Mechanisms of Wetting-Induced Segregation and Electric Field-Assisted Demulsification
abstract: Abstract To address the bottleneck of sudden drops in flux and separation efficiency caused by dispersed water droplets during water-in-oil emulsion separation, this study utilized electrospinning technology to fabricate a PVDF/GO/Bi2WO6 composite nanofiber membrane (PGB 48) that combines thermodynamic selective wetting and sieving with kinetic piezoelectric effects. The synergistic interface effects between GO and Bi2WO6 not only optimize the membrane’s porous network but also efficiently induce the oriented growth of the polar all-trans β crystal phase through interfacial confinement and heterogeneous nucleation, enhancing the membrane’s intrinsic piezoelectric activity. Dynamic fluid shear during continuous separation triggers a subtle strain-induced piezoelectric response in the flexible nanofibers. By utilizing the dynamic changes in local micropiezoelectric potential and the redistribution of interfacial charges, the membrane demonstrates effective in situ demulsification and reduced droplet adhesion. Benefiting from interfacial charge redistribution and in situ piezoelectric field-assisted demulsification, the membrane achieves enhanced separation efficiency and antifouling stability. Owing to its intrinsic hydrophobic-oleophilic properties, the PGB 48 membrane delivers a separation flux up to 19,060 L/(m2·h) and a separation efficiency as high as 99.91% for gravity-driv…

title: Substrate-Controlled Divergent Oxidative Cross-Coupling Reaction via Dual-Chelation-Assisted Strategy: −SMe/–SeMe as Traceless Directing Groups
abstract: Abstract A dual-chelation-assisted oxidative C8–H/C2–H cross-coupling between 1-chalcogen-substituted naphthalenes and benzamides under the Rh/Ag/HFIP catalytic system is disclosed herein, which features excellent regio- and chemoselectivity. When thiomethyl (−SMe) serves as the directing group, only 2-methoxy-substituted thioethers undergo in situ removal of this directing group, whereas other substrates are resistant to C–S bond cleavage. Replacing thiomethyl with selenomethyl (−SeMe) results in smooth C–Se bond cleavage for all selenoether substrates. This strategy enables a substrate-controlled divergent synthesis of biaryls, and represents the first example of utilizing −SMe and −SeMe as traceless directing groups.

title: Coupling coordination of urban–rural integration and county prosperity industries: identifying obstacle factors using empirical data from 135 counties in Hebei Province, China
abstract: Background County prosperity industries and urban–rural integration are two coupled systems that jointly shape high-quality rural development. This paper examines how well these two systems coordinate across Hebei’s 135 counties (cities and districts) from 2014 to 2024. Methods We pair the coupling coordination degree model with Dagum Gini decomposition, obstacle degree diagnosis, and a two-way fixed-effects panel regression with city-level clustered standard errors. Results The coupling coordination degree rose from 0.439 in 2014 to 0.510 in 2024, shifting from the verge of imbalance to barely coordinated, with a clear upward break in 2020. Regional gaps narrowed through latecomer catch-up rather than a slowdown in leading zones. The overall Gini coefficient fell from 0.074 to 0.049, with between-group differences as the main source. The obstacle structure barely changed: vegetable output, agricultural chain extension, fiscal revenue, and road density led the ranking throughout. In the panel regression, all four were positively associated with the coupling coordination degree, vegetable output most strongly, while general public budget revenue had no independent effect once county and year fixed effects were absorbed. Discussion The findings call for zone-specific policies rather than uniform transfers: the coastal zone should deepen processing and cold-chain logistics, the co…

title: Piezo1-mitochondrial calcium uniporter coupling-dependent mechanotransduction basis for acupuncture to drive analgesia
abstract: Abstract Background The mechanosensitive ion channel Piezo1 is a critical sensor of mechanical forces in diverse biological contexts, albeit its role in translating the acupuncture-induced mechanical stimulation into analgesic signaling remains largely unexplored. Acupuncture is a widely used therapy for pain management, with needle manipulation-generated mechanical forces considered central to its therapeutic efficacy. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying this mechanotransduction process remain unknown. Here, we identified myocyte Piezo1 at the ST36 acupoint as a key initiator converting local needling force into peripherally derived analgesic signaling under complete Freund’s adjuvant (CFA)-induced inflammatory pain conditions. Methods In mice with CFA-induced inflammatory pain, we assessed the analgesic efficacy of deep needling at ST36 using paw withdrawal latency tests. The underlying molecular mechanisms were examined through immunohistochemistry, immunofluorescence, western blotting, transmission electron microscopy, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, electromyography, and in vivo two-photon calcium (Ca) imaging. To evaluate the Piezo1-Ca 2 ⁺-calmodulin (CaM)-Ca 2 ⁺/CaM-dependent protein kinase II (CaMKII)-signaling axis and its downstream effects on mitochondrial function and purinergic signaling, we employed muscle-specific adeno-associated virus-mediated knock…

title: Photochemical Cross-Organoboron Coupling of Heteroaryl and Alkyl Boronic Acids and Esters
abstract: Abstract The Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling reaction is a cornerstone of C–C bond formation. However, heteroaryl boronic acids such as pyridyl and quinolyl derivatives remain challenging nucleophiles due to facile protodeboronation. Strategies enabling these substrates are limited to C(sp2)–C(sp2) formation. Efficient and modular C(sp2)–C(sp3) cross-coupling methods that directly employ these substrates remain underdeveloped. Here, we report a cross-organoboron platform that enables direct C(sp2)–C(sp3) bond formation from heteroaryl and alkyl organoboron reagents under visible-light irradiation using Ag2O/TiO2 nanoparticles (NPs). The two organoboron reagents undergo distinct Ag2O NP activations: alkyl boronates undergo single-electron photo-oxidation to generate alkyl radicals while arylboronates undergo transmetalation. Importantly, this method tolerates protodeboronation-prone pyridyl, quinolyl, α-heteroaryl boronic acids, and (hetero)aryl halide-containing substrates, including aryl iodides. High-throughput evaluation across 161 pharmaceutically relevant organoboron substrates identified 113 detectable couplings, and representative examples were validated at preparative scale. This work establishes photochemical cross-organoboron coupling as a complementary approach to classical transition-metal-catalyzed coupling and expands the accessible chemical space of heteroaryl orga…

title: Resonant coupling and refractive-index sensing in planar and vertically stacked terahertz split-ring resonators
Inbound business activities and industrial linkages: insights from Shanghai using a big–small data integration framework
abstract: Abstract Intercity business travel is a critical yet poorly observed channel through which global cities sustain functional linkages. Existing studies often infer ties from firm networks or use purpose-agnostic mobility flows, leaving the behavioral and industrial logic of intercity connectivity underexplained. We develop a transferable big-small data framework to identify intercity business travelers and to examine industrial-structure associations in intercity exchanges. Using Shanghai as a case, behavioral signatures from a travel survey are used to train a purpose-inference model, which is then transferred to large-scale mobile phone data to classify inbound business flows. We then relate inbound business intensity to industrial similarity and characterize nonlinear associations and cross-sector interaction patterns using interpretable machine-learning analysis. Results show that business travelers constitute 36.9% of short-term visitors and their destinations reinforce Shanghai’s polycentric structure. Industrial similarity exhibits a U-shaped statistical association with inbound business flows, with predicted flows reaching their lowest level at intermediate similarity and increasing at both higher and lower observed similarity levels. Cross-industry pairs account for a larger share of the modeled interaction intensity, with advanced producer services frequently appearing…

title: Incommensurate modulations and thickness-dependent energy storage density in (PbLaSrBa)(ZrSnTi)O 3 relaxor antiferroelectric thick-film ceramics
abstract: In this study, (Pb0.92-xLa0.04SrxBa0.02)(Zr0.64Sn0.35Ti0.01)O3 (PLSBZSTi, i = 1 (x=0.04), 2 (0.06), 3 (0.08), and 4 (0.10)) relaxor antiferroelectric thick-film ceramics were prepared using a tape-casting process. An ultrahigh Wrec of 20.09 J/cm3 with an ultrahigh η of 91.34% was obtained for the PLSBZST2 (x = 0.06) ceramic. This outstanding energy storage performance is attributed to the distinct microstructural features of this system. Specifically, transmission electron microscopy revealed the presence of nanosized stripe domains, along with F-spots associated with 1/2{ooo} superlattice diffraction and an incommensurate modulation structure (IMS) related to the 1/n<110> superlattice (n = 4.91). These microstructural characteristics are direct evidence of oxygen octahedral tilting, which promotes the formation of relatively slim hysteresis loops. Moreover, the inverse power-law relationship between the sample thickness and energy storage density was determined. The fitted exponent was -0.43 ± 0.04, which can be quantified by combining the thickness-dependent dielectric breakdown strength (exponent of -0.39) and maximum polarization (exponent of -0.13) with a 20% correction factor accounting for the practical underutilization of the maximum electric field and polarization.

title: Integration philosophy of science and transcendental philosophy in context of philosophical thought: A literature review on phenomenon of ecotourism and preservation of local values
abstract: Background: The interaction between modernization and local wisdom in Indonesia has brought attention to ecotourism as a site where scientific rationality meets cultural and transcendental values. Sade Village in West Nusa Tenggara represents a unique case where traditional values are preserved amid tourism development. Methods: This study employs a descriptive qualitative approach combined with a literature review. Data are collected from philosophical texts, ethnographic studies, cultural research, and relevant academic literature to examine the integration of the Philosophy of Science and Transcendental Philosophy in understanding ecotourism and the preservation of local values. The data are analyzed descriptively and interpretively to identify key concepts and relationships relevant to the research objectives. Findings: The analysis shows that combining the Philosophy of Science and Transcendental Philosophy offers a comprehensive framework for interpreting ecotourism not only as an economic activity but also as a moral and spiritual practice. In Sade Village, traditional values such as harmony with nature, collective identity, and respect for sacred spaces coexist with rational approaches to sustainable tourism management. Conclusion: Integrating these philosophical perspectives provides a conceptual basis for promoting sustainable cultural development, bridging empirical …

title: Residual Finite Group Element Dandelion-Informed Attention Network for Symbolic Knowledge Integration in AI-Driven Educational Intelligence
abstract: Recent advances in intelligent educational systems have emphasized the need for accurate interpretation of Computational Thinking (CT) behaviors. The contextual dependencies and symbolic reasoning necessary to comprehend CT in game-based learning environments are frequently difficult for traditional deep learning techniques to capture. This disparity draws attention to the issue of the current models of educational analytics’ poor generalization and interpretability. The current study presents a novel framework called the Residual Finite Group Element Dandelion Informed Attention Network (Res-FGE-DIAN) under the paradigm of AI in Education with Symbolic Knowledge Integration in order to address this challenge. The proposed framework analyzes CT behaviors using game-based interaction data named “Educational Testing Service (ETS) and Educational Knowledge” dataset, which consists of 427 player records from the AutoThinking learning game. The Masked Attention Mask Transformer (Mask2Former) was used to extract features for improved contextual encoding, and the Cumulative Curve Fitting Approximation (CCFA) algorithm was used for data pre-processing in order to normalize and refine the learning traces. The Res-FGE-DIAN combines a Residual Group Attention Network (ResGANet) and a Finite-Element-Informed Neural Network (FEI-NN), both of which are optimized using the Dandelion Optimizer…

title: A BIM–game engine integration framework for thermal comfort visualization and sustainable building design in sub-Saharan Africa
abstract: Purpose The emergence of building information modeling and virtual reality (BIM–VR) technologies has revolutionized industrial practices. While BIM–VR integration for performance visualization has been demonstrated in other contexts, its application remains largely underexplored in sub-Saharan African (SSA) countries. This study aims to present a proof-of-concept framework integrating BIM and VR to enable visualization of thermal performance. Design/methodology/approach This study used an experimental research strategy centered on software interoperability. Revit was used to develop a digital model of a case building. On-site temperature data were collected and used to calibrate the model. Unreal Engine (UE) 5 was used to develop the virtual environment, into which both the Revit geometry and thermal simulation results were merged. Findings The thermal simulation, calibrated against on-site indoor and outdoor hourly temperature values, was deemed acceptable per ASHRAE Guideline 14. Annual operative temperatures for the sandcrete- and rammed earth-based models ranged from 27.74°C to 27.98°C and 27.83°C to 28.15°C, respectively. The sandcrete-based model recorded an energy use intensity value of 843.50 kWh/m2/year, while 812.75 kWh/m2/year was observed for the rammed earth model. Heat maps were generated from the simulation and merged with the Revit geometry in UE. Originality/va…

title: Multimodal EEG–Wearable Integration for Generalizable Pain Classification
abstract: Objective pain assessment is challenging due to the inherently subjective and multidimensional nature of pain, compounded by intersubject variability and noise in naturalistic settings. These factors limit the development of reliable digital biomarkers for clinical decision support and remote monitoring. In this work, we propose a hybrid deep learning architecture that performs early fusion of single channel EEG band power streams with peripheral biosignals recorded by a wristband (electrodermal activity, photoplethysmography/BVP, triaxial accelerometry, and skin temperature). The model uses residual 1D CNN encoders to learn EEG representations and a multilayer perceptron to encode wearable features; the two embeddings are fused in a unified layer to produce predictions for four classes under a strict subject independent evaluation protocol. On PhysioPain, the proposed approach achieves 86.98% accuracy and 87.46% weighted F1, surpassing widely used machine learning baselines, while maintaining an average inference latency of 0.1495 ms per sample for real time operation. In addition to widely used machine learning baselines, we benchmark contemporary deep 1D CNN baselines for a fair comparison: the proposed model improves over 1D DenseNet by 4.49 percentage points in accuracy and 4.70 percentage points in weighted F1, and over 1D ResNet by 7.90 percentage points in accuracy and …

title: Development and integration of regional markets under digital and investment transformation of the economy
abstract: Research on digital trade, finance, investment, and regional integration remains fragmented, and cross-regional comparisons often rely on broad labels that obscure implementation differences and distributional risks. This conceptual study develops a testable five-pillar framework for regional market integration under digital and investment transformation. A structured narrative review was conducted using 57 full-text candidate documents identified through academic metadata searches and official repositories; 43 sources were retained after relevance and quality appraisal. Evidence was coded for mechanisms, complementarities, moderators, feedback effects, social outcomes, and risks. The European Union, ASEAN, the Eurasian Economic Union, and the African Continental Free Trade Area were then examined as most-different institutional cases using a common four-level implementation scale. The synthesis indicates that digital infrastructure is an enabling rather than sufficient condition. Human capital and institutional interoperability moderate its effects, while financial modernization and productive investment mediate the conversion of connectivity into cross-border exchange. Socially sustainable outcomes additionally depend on affordability, decent-work conditions, data rights, consumer protection, and territorial inclusion. The contribution is a framework that distinguishes ena…

title: Generalized multi-energy model for computing radiation treatment parameters on image domain and automated model-selection framework
abstract: This study developed a general n-energy mathematical model that predicts relative electron density (ρe), effective atomic number (Zef), mean excitation energy (I) and stopping power ratio (SPR) using computed tomography image, and developed an algorithm for best model selection. Mathematical proof is provided. Some numerical examples were carried out and the results were compared. The proposed method includes most of the existing methods as a special case. All the examples of the proposed method considered have modeling error that’s less than or equal to 0.85% and 0.89% for SPR and ρe, respectively, with mean error close to 0.00% and low median absolute error. The method was able to achieve modeling root mean square error of 0.85% and 1.61% for I and Zef, respectively, with some flexibility for improvement. The mathematical model showed to be more general by including most of the other existing models and presents a direction to formulating new ones. It shows little or no bias on prediction since it has mean error that is close to zero in almost all predictions and low median absolute error. The algorithm gives the leverage to select the best model, improve the model and automation.

title: Optimal wind energy site selection in Egypt using a GIS–AHP and remote sensing-based approach
abstract: Abstract Delivering affordable, reliable, and sustainable electricity in lower-middle-income countries requires spatially explicit tools that translate remote-sensing and infrastructure data into decision support for sustainable development planning. Focusing on Egypt, we update the national wind-energy suitability map using a Geographic Information System (GIS) and a multi-criteria decision analysis framework. High-resolution spatial inputs—remote-sensing-derived land use/land cover and updated road and electrical-grid networks—are integrated and weighted across eight criteria using the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP). The results indicate that approximately 1.60% of Egypt's land area (≈ 15,985 km 2 ) is highly suitable for wind development, 6.55% (≈ 65,594 km 2 ) is moderately suitable, and 0.61% (≈ 6,117 km 2 ) is of low suitability, while 91.25% (≈ 914,144 km 2 ) is restricted under the imposed constraints, with priority zones concentrated along the Red Sea corridor. The spatial concentration of wind-suitable land supports a diversified renewable-energy strategy in which wind development is complemented by solar and other renewables aligned to national targets. The resulting suitability surface is a reproducible, national-scale screening layer that can help planners and investors shortlist corridors for pre-feasibility study, anticipate permitting buffers, and align grid r…

title: Enhancing the Performance of All-Solid-State Energy Storage Devices via Interfacial Reaction Analysis of Ion Storage and Ion Conduction Materials
Resilience construction of automated sea–rail intermodal ports against extreme weather: technology integration and collaborative innovation
abstract: Purpose This study aims to explain how a short-lived extreme-weather capacity loss develops into persistent congestion in automated sea–rail intermodal terminals and evaluates how retained operating capacity affects backlog formation and operational recovery. Design/methodology/approach AIS-derived weekly indicators for Ningbo during 2019–2022 are used to calibrate and externally check normal-operation scale. Three seven-day weather paths observed in 2023 drive a nonstationary M/G/25 simulation for a representative container-terminal cluster within Ningbo Zhoushan Port. The weather-driven nonstationary M/G/25 queuing simulation model combines long-run mean arrival rate of 26.429 vessels/day with correlated daily demand variation, lognormal service requirements, 200 common-random-number replications and capacity-retention sensitivity over θ = 0.60–0.80. Findings At θ = 0.70, the event resilience indices are 0.720 for Haikui, 0.744 for Khanun and 0.707 for the convective event. Vessel-level median waiting time (WT) rises from approximately 21.2 h in baseline to 43.3, 43.1 and 44.8 h, respectively, while event peak queues reach 58.5, 56.0 and 60.0 vessels. Khanun and Haikui recover on Days 12 and 13; the convective event does not satisfy the joint WT–time in port recovery rule within 14 days. Raising θ to 0.80 reduces all event medians and restores all three scenarios within five …

title: The terroir paradox: institutional barriers to rural–urban food integration in western Türkiye
abstract: Purpose This study examines how Ödemiş's rural food production connects with İzmir's urban gastronomy market in western Türkiye, primarily from the perspective of rural and locally embedded food-system actors. It focuses on supply-side, institutional, and relational barriers shaping market access and the conversion of production capacity into urban market representation. Design/methodology/approach An interpretivist qualitative case study was conducted with 17 purposively selected stakeholders relevant to the Ödemiş–İzmir food system. Interview data were contextualised with official agricultural statistics and geographical indication (GI)-related documentary sources and analysed using reflexive thematic analysis following Braun and Clarke (2006, 2019). Findings were interpreted through terroir, social capital and collective action theories. Findings Six themes and 24 sub-themes were identified. Despite strong gastronomic capacity, including GI-registered potatoes and olive oil and a strong dairy sector, Ödemiş remains underrepresented in İzmir. Key barriers include rising input costs, logistics deficits and negative assessments of cooperative effectiveness. Integration relies largely on informal personal networks rather than institutionalised channels and is further constrained by weak promotion and intergenerational knowledge erosion. Originality/value The study proposes the “…

title: Ultrahigh-Strength, Fire-Safe, and Passive-Thermal-Regulating Alginate Aerogels Enabled by Dual-Cross-Linked Networks for Energy-Saving Applications
abstract: Abstract Building materials that integrate thermal insulation, fire safety, structural durability, and passive cooling are highly desirable for reducing building energy consumption. Achieving this combination in sustainable biomass-derived materials remains challenging. Here, a multifunctional sodium alginate-based aerogel (SPCA) was fabricated via directional freezing and reinforced by a dual-cross-linked framework formed through PA-mediated hydrogen bonding and Ca2+ coordination. The resulting network produced a denser, more uniform honeycomb-like porous structure, thereby strengthening the aerogel skeleton. SPCA achieved a compressive strength of 4.57 MPa and a compressive modulus of 37.97 MPa, along with improved water stability. Despite moderate structural densification, SPCA retained a low thermal conductivity of 0.044 W m–1 K–1 and outperformed several commercial insulation materials under both hot and cold conditions. The aerogel also exhibited rapid self-extinguishing behavior and enhanced char formation. Furthermore, the combined effects of thermal insulation and radiative cooling enabled effective daytime cooling, resulting in a temperature reduction of 4.2 °C under simulated solar irradiation and a maximum temperature drop of 7.2 °C under outdoor conditions. Model-house experiments demonstrated reductions in roof and indoor temperatures, while EnergyPlus simulations…

title: Design Strategy of T 1-Weighted MRI Contrast Agents for High Relaxivity Based on a Self-Folding Macromolecular Architecture
abstract: Abstract Conjugation of gadolinium chelates to macromolecular nanoplatforms has emerged as a promising strategy for developing high-performance contrast agents for T1-weighted MRI. However, conventional macromolecular gadolinium-based contrast agents (GBCAs) typically achieve limited enhancement of longitudinal relaxivity merely by tethering Gd chelates to macromolecular platforms to slow their global rotational motion. Here, we present a rational design strategy based on a self-folded macromolecular contrast agent (SMCA), formed through intramolecular self-folding of a single amphiphilic polymer chain incorporating a minimized amount of Gd chelate. The SMCA forms a nanosized micellar structure with a hydrophobic core and a hydration shell, while positioning the Gd chelates at the core–shell interface. Experimental results suggest that the rigid architecture of SMCA may contribute to relatively slow global motion, while the PEG shell may restrict segmental dynamics, potentially contributing to the enhanced longitudinal relaxivity. Systematic structural modulation, including control of the degree of polymerization and hydrophilic chain length, enables enhanced relaxivity while ensuring renal clearance. The optimized Gd-DOTA-conjugated SMCA exhibits a longitudinal relaxivity of 31.5 mM–1 s–1 at 0.47 T, representing an 8.5-fold increase over clinically used Gd-DOTA. In a proof-of-…

title: Jagad: Visualizing Wayang Krucil Wiloso through the Damarwulan Narrative in an Illustrated Book for Young Audiences
abstract: Wayang Krucil Wiloso is a traditional performing art from Malang whose visibility among younger generations has declined. This study designs an illustrated book that adapts the Damarwulan narrative as an introductory cultural medium for audiences aged 15–25 years and examines how it is perceived. The Stanford d.school Design Thinking framework guided the process, drawing on interviews with two cultural informants, field observation, research with young participants, and literature study. The resulting 64-page book introduces Arunika, a fictional contemporary protagonist who mediates between Gen-Z visual culture and the historical narrative, and develops Damarwulan and Anjasmara by preserving, modifying, or abandoning specific features of the Wayang Krucil Wiloso puppets. One media expert and one subject-matter expert assessed feasibility, with mean scores of 80.7% and 79.7% (both feasible), and 34 respondents aged 15–25 gave an overall rating of 85.5% in a small-scale trial. These scores indicate perceived feasibility, comprehension, and acceptance; they do not measure learning outcomes. The lowest expert ratings concerned cultural value (73%) and narrative structure (76%), pointing to the need for deeper cultural exposition and pacing. The study contributes a documented logic of cultural translation for wayang-based illustration and a proxy-character strategy for young readers…

title: Extension Design for the Use of a Mobile Application for Oil Palm Harvest Recording in Laut Tador District, Batu Bara Regency
abstract: Harvest recording supports transparent oil palm production reporting for Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) certification. However, smallholders in Laut Tador District, Batu Bara Regency, continue to rely on simple manual systems that may expose harvest data to loss. This study developed an agricultural extension design for a mobile harvest-recording application and assessed its acceptance, behavioural outcomes, and continued application use. A quantitative descriptive approach was employed, with data collected through interviews and questionnaires and analysed using extension planning procedures and Likert-scale scoring. Regional potential identification informed a design specifying objectives, target participants, content, methods, media, session volume, location, timing, and costs. The objectives followed SMART and ABCD principles, with a target achievement level of 60%. Overall acceptance of the extension design reached 86.1%. Evaluation results were 80.9% for knowledge, 78.86% for attitudes, 67% for skills, and 30.4% for continued application use. These findings indicate strong acceptance of the extension design alongside limited sustained use of the application. The study provides an extension design tailored to local conditions and highlights continued assistance as a priority for translating acceptance into routine digital harvest recording and strengthening the …

title: Comparison of Continuous and Pulsed Operation Modes of Terahertz Quantum-Cascade Lasers with Two-Photon Band Design
ELECTION ORGANIZER ETHICS AND A THREE-TIER OVERSIGHT DESIGN FOR SYNTHETIC CAMPAIGN CONTENT
abstract: Indonesia’s 2024 General Election was its first cycle in which generative artificial intelligence (AI) content featured prominently, while campaign law predated widespread public access to the technology. This article reads that void not merely as a gap in norms but as an ethical burden transferred to election organizers: where law is silent, the duty to protect electoral integrity still binds the KPU, Bawaslu, and DKPP without adequate legal instruments. Using normative legal research with statutory, comparative, and conceptual approaches, it analyses Indonesian primary legal materials, five comparator jurisdictions, and one industry initiative. Eight gaps are mapped in four clusters: definition and transparency; enforcement authority and actor coverage; data protection and evidentiary standards; and the structural pacing problem. Each is read twice, as a normative gap and as an ethical burden. Constitutional Court Decision 166/PUU-XXI/2023 provides a foundation whose scope requires careful reading, while comparative materials inform the assessment of instruments against authority, proportionality, capacity, and review. The article proposes a three-tier design of co-regulation, technical regulation within delegated powers, and AI provisions in the Election Law revision, supported by the organizers’ code of ethics as the layer readiest to move. The recommendations are prescript…

title: Design of Traditional Nebulizer for Patients with Coughs
abstract: Cough is a common respiratory disorder that may become chronic in the elderly and reduce quality of life. Limited access to conventional nebulizers necessitates the development of more affordable inhalation therapy alternatives. This study aimed to design a herbal-based traditional nebulizer as an alternative inhalation therapy for patients with productive cough. This study used a Research and Development (R&D) approach with the ADDIE model. It was conducted at Griya Sakinah Nursing Home, Blitar, Indonesia, from January to April 2025. Data were collected using expert validation and field-testing checklists rated on a 1–5 scale, which underwent expert judgment to ensure content validity. Validation involved three experts, followed by a limited trial on two elderly participants. Expert validation yielded a feasibility score of 77.25% (feasible), while participant trials showed 81.17% (very feasible). The device consists of a clay pot heater, plastic tubing, an aluminum sheath, and Piper betle leaves with mucolytic and expectorant properties. No significant adverse effects were observed. This device is potentially beneficial, practical, and cost-effective for use in resource-limited settings. However, the very small sample size limits generalizability.

title: Design and validation of a measurement scale for digital transformation capabilities in agricultural settings
abstract: Digital transformation is essential for strengthening agri-food systems in emerging economies. However, there is a lack of validated tools to assess both the capabilities and levels of digital maturity in agricultural production units. This research validates an instrument to measure Digital Transformation (DT) capabilities and levels of digital maturity in agricultural production units (APU) in an emerging economy. The instrument encompasses six dimensions: sensing, seizing and transforming capabilities, along with the stages of digital maturity, digitization, digitalization, and digital transformation. The validation process was developed in five stages, including theoretical foundation, item development, expert review, and exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, applied to a sample of 68 potato farmers from south-central Chile. The final instrument consists of 32 items with promising psychometric properties; reliability and validity indicators met recommended thresholds across most dimensions, with a small number of exceptions discussed in the study. The results reveal that farmers widely recognize the value of digital technology and demonstrate a willingness to invest, despite being in early stages of digitalization, with widespread use of basic tools such as smartphones and messaging applications, but with limited adoption of more advanced technologies such as precis…

title: Design, Development and Evaluation of a Student-Centred Digital Innovation for Gender-Based Violence Prevention, Reporting and Support in Higher Education: A Mixed-Methods Study Protocol
abstract: Background Gender-based violence (GBV) remains a serious social and public health concern in South Africa and presents particular challenges within higher education. Although universities may have policies, reporting mechanisms and support services, students may face barriers to reporting and accessing assistance, including fear of retaliation, stigma, confidentiality concerns and institutional distrust. Digital technologies may strengthen access to information, reporting pathways, emergency assistance and institutional support. However, digital GBV interventions also raise concerns regarding privacy, safety, trust, accessibility and institutional integration (Lattie et al. 2019). This protocol describes a student-centred, privacy-conscious digital innovation informed by students’ identified needs and linked to existing university support structures. Protocol The study will employ a multi-phase mixed-methods design at the University of Venda. Phase 1 will examine students’ needs, experiences and perceptions regarding GBV prevention, reporting, institutional support and digital help-seeking through an online questionnaire. Phase 2 will use the needs assessment and engagement with relevant users and institutional stakeholders to inform development and refinement of the digital innovation. Phase 3 will evaluate the prototype with intended student users, focusing on usability, acce…

title: Optimalisasi Pemahaman Akademik melalui Implementasi Pendekatan Understanding by Design (UbD): Sebuah Tinjauan Literatur Sistematis
abstract: This study aims to analyze and synthesize the contributions of the Understanding by Design (UbD) approach to optimizing students’ academic understanding. It employs a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) method examining SINTA-accredited articles published between 2016 and 2026. The findings indicate that UbD, through its three stages of backward design, namely identifying learning outcomes, determining assessment evidence, and planning learning experiences, consistently enhances student engagement, the quality of authentic assessment, and the development of six facets of understanding: explanation, interpretation, application, perspective, empathy, and self-knowledge. This approach is also flexible enough to be integrated with other learning strategies, such as Problem-Based Learning (PBL) and Teaching at the Right Level (TaRL), without compromising alignment among learning objectives, assessments, and learning activities. Furthermore, implementing UbD supports instructional design oriented toward achieving deeper understanding rather than merely mastering content. This study concludes that UbD’s main strength lies in shifting the orientation of instructional design from a content-based approach to an understanding-based approach. Therefore, future research should strengthen empirical evidence regarding knowledge transfer and the sustainability of students’ understanding.

title: NSGA-II empowers multispectrum-compatible, polarization-insensitive, and transparent metasurface design
abstract: The increasing demand for modern devices to operate in multiphysics environments presents new challenges for the design of multifunctional materials. Owing to the disparity in wavelengths, multi-field waves are difficult to modulate simultaneously, which hinders the integration of multi-field functionalities. Inspired by characteristic scale analysis, this paper proposes a visible-transparent and multispectrum-compatible metasurface that simultaneously provides broadband microwave absorption and low-frequency acoustic absorption. In the microwave regime, a resistive frequency-selective surface (RFSS) is utilized to achieve broadband absorption. In the visible regime, NSGA-II optimization is employed to generate a Pareto front, from which a trade-off solution is selected to realize optical transparency—maximizing the −10 dB absorption bandwidth while minimizing the indium tin oxide (ITO) coverage area to maximize optical transmittance. In the acoustic regime, after acoustic waves enter the perforated microwave-layer metasurface, four volume-mismatched Helmholtz resonators connected in parallel yield high-efficiency attenuation exceeding 80% over the 204–340 Hz range, and near-perfect sound absorption is attained around 248 Hz. The design methodology is validated through simulations and experimental measurements on a multifunctional sample.

title: Finite element analysis of foot-insole biomechanics for insole design: a systematic review
abstract: Objective To synthesise finite element analysis (FEA) evidence on how insole design features influence foot biomechanics, and to identify implications for insole manufacture and the clinical management of foot disorders. Methods Web of Science, ScienceDirect, and PubMed were searched. Studies meeting the eligibility criteria were reviewed in full text. A best-evidence synthesis was used to determine the strength of evidence. For each included study, we extracted and compared the research objective, insole parameters, finite element model configuration, loading and boundary conditions, model validation and outcome measures to identify common modelling and experimental practices. Results As of December 2025, this review included 45 research articles. The mean methodological quality score was 23.91; 27 studies were classified as high quality and 18 as low quality. Inter-rater reliability was good (ICC[3, 1] = 0.856, 95% confidence interval 0.752–0.918). Conclusion Limited evidence indicates that conforming insoles may reduce plantar pressure, although the optimal conformity index remains unclear. Wedge and arch-support insoles can improve foot alignment, but their parameters require careful tuning to avoid excessive soft-tissue loading. Low-modulus materials and plug-and-hole structures in high-load plantar regions may reduce local pressure. Edge gradients or multiple small plugs …

title: Rationale and design of a nationwide prospective cohort study in type 2 diabetic kidney disease: the Korean Diabetic Kidney Disease (K-DKD) Cohort
abstract: Background: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is the leading cause of end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) worldwide. In South Korea, DKD accounts for nearly half of all ESKD cases, yet prospective data reflecting the clinical characteristics of Korean patients remain limited. This study aims to investigate the clinical and biological features of DKD in Koreans and identify long-term prognostic indicators. Methods: The Korean Diabetic Kidney Disease (K-DKD) Cohort is a nationwide prospective multicenter study investigating the clinical, biochemical, and molecular determinants of DKD progression in Korean adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus. Approximately 1,300 participants will be enrolled from 15 university-affiliated hospitals in South Korea. Demographic, clinical, laboratory data and outcome data are collected using a standardized electronic case report form at baseline and annually for up to 10 years. Blood and urine biospecimens are obtained at baseline and every 2 years thereafter for centralized storage and biospecimen analyses. Clustering analyses will identify the distinct clinical phenotypes of DKD, and long-term prognostic models will be developed on the basis of renal and cardiovascular outcomes using traditional and artificial intelligence-based approaches. Additionally, treatment patterns and management behaviors will be evaluated to understand the real-world clinical pra…

title: Why do hemolysis interference studies produce different results? A proposal for standardized experimental design and reporting
abstract: Abstract Background Hemolysis is a major preanalytical source of laboratory interference, but methods used to experimentally generate hemolyzed specimens are poorly standardized. Content Different lysis procedures, blood sources, cellular compositions, hemolysate volumes, control designs, and time-to-analysis can influence results independently of free hemoglobin concentration. The amount and composition of intracellular material released may also vary with erythrocyte, leukocyte, and platelet characteristics. Therefore, identical hemolysis indices do not necessarily represent equivalent experimental interferents. Summary Hemolysis interference studies should clearly distinguish the interferent, its method of generation, and its measurement. Detailed reporting of specimen preparation and experimental conditions is essential for reproducibility and comparison between studies. Outlook Harmonized hemolysate preparation and reporting, together with assessment at clinically relevant measurand concentrations and, when appropriate, multiple time points, would improve the reliability of hemolysis thresholds and laboratory decision-making.

title: Design and Synthesis of New Combretastatin A-4 Derivatives Containing Naphthothiophene Based on the Structural Rigidification Strategy
abstract: Six new combretastatin A-4 derivatives containing a naphtho[2,3-b]thiophene-4,9-dione core were successfully synthesized via a two-step procedure. This approach involved a multi-component reaction to generate dihydrofuranonaphthoquinone intermediates, followed by a sulfur-mediated oxidative transformation of the dihydrofuran scaffold into the corresponding thiophene derivatives. The structures of all synthesized compounds were characterized using IR, ¹H-NMR, and ¹³C-NMR spectroscopy. In vitro cytotoxicity assays against the A549 lung cancer cell line revealed that five out of the six derivatives exhibited moderate to strong growth inhibitory activity, with IC₅₀ values ranging from 3.40 ± 0.24 to 46.46 ± 1.63 µM. Notably, the fluorinated analogues 4b and 4c demonstrated the most potent cytotoxicity, with IC₅₀ values of 3.40 ± 0.24 and 3.69 ± 0.35 µM, respectively. Molecular docking simulations indicated that compound 4c accommodates effectively within the colchicine-binding site (CBS) of tubulin through a cooperative multi-point interaction mechanism, where polar anchoring and hydrophobic packing work synergistically to stabilize the ligand–protein complex. Despite satisfying standard drug-likeness criteria, computational ADME profiling highlighted that the high hydrophobicity and poor water solubility of 4c remain major physicochemical hurdles. Overall, these combretastatin A-4…

From concept to use: value co-creation in B2B virtual reality environments
abstract: Purpose Virtual reality (VR) is increasingly adopted in business-to-business (B2B) contexts, yet a limited understanding exists of how VR-enabled collaborations generate value over time. This study aims to examine how value coproduction and cocreation unfold in B2B VR environments through resource integration, actor interaction and information flows. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on five dyadic case studies of VR providers and business customers, the authors analyze VR-enabled collaboration across three stages of the value creation trajectory: conceptualization, development and in-use. Findings Using an interactive/network perspective informed by the actors–resources–activities model, the findings identify VR-specific enablers – such as immersive demonstrations, iterative prototyping, real-time feedback and analytics-enabled simulations – that reconfigure resource interfaces and coordination practices. Research limitations/implications From a methodological standpoint, using a case study approach restricts the generalizability of the findings. Future studies could quantitatively test propositions related to the role of customer knowledge or digital experience, examining whether these factors act as mediators or moderators in the relationship between resource integration, interaction quality and the effectiveness of VR-enabled value cocreation. Practical implications The c…

title: Unpacking chromatin accessibility with Fiber-seq: general principles with special considerations for plant systems
abstract: Chromatin accessibility has long been used as a marker for regions of DNA with regulatory potential. Fiber-seq detects chromatin accessibility on individual DNA fibers, enabling analyses beyond the identification of the accessible chromatin regions (ACRs). By providing single molecule level high resolution, Fiber-seq provides unprecedented qualitative descriptions, including potential categorizations of ACRs, identification of internal transcription factor footprints and nucleosome positioning within individual DNA fibers. As with all tools, the power of this technique depends on careful experimental design and data analysis -- incorrect usage will result in incorrect conclusions. Here we offer guidelines and flag potential pitfalls when generating and analyzing Fiber-seq data, such as (1) the optimum levels of adenine methylation per-fiber, (2) the power of per-fiber state inference, (3) the importance of controlling for read depth and methylation rates when comparing across samples, (4) the limitations of long-read sequence mapping, and (5) suggestions for identification of differentially accessible peaks across samples.

title: Green Nanonization Strategies for Plant-Derived Small-Molecule Pesticides: Supramolecular Self-Assembly and Natural Polymer Carriers
abstract: Abstract Plant-derived small-molecule pesticides are renewable and rapidly degradable with low residues, but their poor water solubility, photodegradation, and volatility limit field application. Nanotechnology can improve stability and delivery, yet conventional synthetic or inorganic carriers may increase the costs and ecological risks. Supramolecular self-assembly using active ingredients themselves as building units and biodegradable natural polymer carriers offers two promising green formulation pathways. Aromatic rings, phenolic hydroxyl groups, carbonyl groups, and amino groups in plant metabolites provide a structural basis for the self-assembly. This review summarizes nanonization and self-assembly strategies for phenolics and flavonoids, terpenoids and essential oils, alkaloids, saponins, coumarins, quinones, and sulfur-containing compounds, examining structural features, assembly driving forces, representative examples, and their limitations. The roles of natural polymers are also discussed. Finally, environmental and health benefits, challenges, and future directions are considered, and a structure-guided approach is proposed to integrate green active ingredients with a green delivery.
venue: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry

title: Optionality and Mandatory Nature in the Contractual Circulation of Digital (Virtual) Assets: The Russian Model and the Experience of the Republic of Azerbaijan
abstract: The article examines the extent to which the participants in the circulation of digital (virtual) assets may determine on their own the content of the contractual relationships and where the law justifiably limits their autonomy. The analysis is based on Federal Law No. 282-FZ of August 4, 2026 “On Digital Currencies and Digital Rights”, the civil and electronic commerce legislation of the Republic of Azerbaijan, Resolution No. 2-P of the Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation of January 20, 2026, recent case law and the experience of the regulatory sandbox of the Central Bank of the Republic of Azerbaijan. It is shown that in the digital environment, the will of the parties is expressed not only in the text of the agreement but also in the choice of interface, algorithm, and channel of performance, and that a smart contract is a means of concluding or performing a contract rather than a source of obligations. Four forms of mandatory regulation are distinguished, and a test for the admissibility of mandatory intervention is proposed. The author concludes that a model of “regulated contractual autonomy”, in which the freely determined economic core of the contract surrounded by a minimal mandatory protective perimeter is needed.

title: Pest Invasions: Understanding Risks and Introduction Patterns of Non-Indigenous Plant Pests
abstract: Abstract Non-indigenous plant pests represent an ongoing and growing challenge to agriculture, forestry, biodiversity, and ecosystem functioning worldwide. Over recent decades, hundreds of pests have been introduced beyond their native geographical ranges, often through human-mediated pathways such as international trade and the movement of plants and plant products. The timing and location of these introductions are shaped by a complex interaction of environmental conditions and human activities that facilitate pest entry and establishment. Understanding pest invasions is complicated by limited data, which often rely on historical records of first detections and may be affected by uneven surveillance and reporting across regions. Despite these challenges, introduction records provide valuable insights into where and when pests enter and establish. When combined with environmental and anthropogenic information, these data can be analysed using spatial statistical approaches to identify regions repeatedly affected by new introductions and to assess the factors associated with increased invasion risk. This case explores the drivers of non-indigenous pest introductions and shows how introduction data and spatial analysis can be used to identify introduction hotspots and support risk-based plant health strategies. By improving our understanding of invasion patterns, these approache…

title: Immersive virtual reality in upper secondary history education: the case of the Anne Frank House VR
abstract: Immersive virtual reality opens new learning opportunities across domains. In history education, it can provide intellectually and emotionally meaningful access to environments that no longer exist. Although prior work has catalogued the opportunities and challenges of immersive virtual reality, few studies examine its specific pedagogical implications for developing disciplinary competencies in history education. In this qualitative descriptive study, we address this gap and investigate the experience of using Anne Frank House VR in fostering historical competencies in two upper secondary history classes taught by the same teacher. We analysed open-ended questionnaires from students (n = 49) and a semi-structured teacher interview using a codebook-guided thematic approach. Participants highlighted emotional impact, motivation and support for spatial understanding. However, the experience resulted in limited source analysis and weak critical engagement with reconstruction choices, and students rarely considered the perspectives or situations of other historical actors. The findings show that without explicit pedagogical scaffolding, immersive virtual reality alone is unlikely to cultivate historical competencies that depend on critical reasoning. We suggest that these limitations are related to the cosmopolitan narrative design of Anne Frank House VR, which foregrounds universa…

abstract: Исследуется организация подготовки аспирантов Всесоюзным институтом растениеводства во время пребывания института в Красноуфимске, куда он был эвакуирован из-за блокады Ленинграда. Изучаются факторы, которые затрудняли для института организацию аспирантуры, обстоятельства, из-за которых она была прекращена, и условия, в которых работа по набору аспирантов была восстановлена. За основу методологического исследования был взят системный подход, комплекс использованных методов включал в себя обработку архивных материалов, их анализ и историко-описательный метод для отражения полученной информации. Деятельность ВИР в отношении подготовки аспирантов, ранее не отражённая в историографии, была проанализирована с помощью материалов из архива ВИР, а также документов, относящихся к истории института и находящихся в Центральном государственном архиве научно-технической документации Санкт-Петербурга. Установлены обстоятельства, по которым работа с аспирантами была прервана, включающие в себя эвакуацию института из Ленинграда в Красноуфимск, отсутствие педагогических кадров, неподходящие бытовые условия, а также личное отношение руководства ВИР. За счёт взаимодействия института с Всесоюзной академией сельскохозяйственных наук имени Ленина подготовка аспирантов была восстановлена в заочном формате к 1943 г.
