title: OPTIMAL ECONOMIC DISPATCH OF THERMAL POWER GENERATION CONSIDERING LOSSES USING PARTICLE SWARM OPTIMIZATION (PSO)
abstract: To set the daily schedule for thermal units under rising industrial loads in Vietnam, we calculate the economic dispatch (ED) on a 26-bus grid using a modified version of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). Active power losses are calculated from the B-coefficients of Kron. Instead of scattering initial particles at random across the operating limits, we only modify the starting equation to weight each position by the fuel cost of that unit at half capacity. Early iterations are reduced because the swarm starts near cheaper units. On the 26-bus test grid, we reduce the total fuel cost to $15,689.411per hour, which is lower than the costs from random PSO and from the method of Lagrange multipliers. Transmission losses across the network are cut to 26.091 MW.
venue: Tạp chí Khoa học Đại học Công Thương

title: Contex Virtual Learning Network and the Development of Mathematical and Research Competencies in University Students
abstract: Abstract* Context Este estudio tiene como objetivo analizar la influencia del programa académico conocido como Red de Aprendizaje VirtualContext en el desarrollo de competencias matemáticas y de investigación entre estudiantes universitarios. Este análisis se basa en evidencia y principios científicos relativos a los componentes del programa. Methods The study employed a quantitative approach with a quasi-experimental design and an explanatory scope. The sample consisted of 364 students from academic programs at a private university in the city of Huánuco, located in the central highlands of Peru; 35.4% were female and 64.6% were male, with an age range of 18 to 21. Cognitive, procedural-algorithmic, and attitudinal tests—all validated for use in Peru—were administered to analytically assess the dimensions of mathematical competencies. Results The results indicate a positive influence of the VirtualContext Learning Network on the “knowing” (cognitive), “doing” (procedural), and “being” (attitudinal) dimensions of contextual mathematical and research competencies. Conclusions The study concludes that the VirtualContext Learning Network significantly influences mathematical and research competencies, facilitating meaningful learning.

Dynamic mesh cutting method of deformable garment in immersive virtual reality
abstract: Purpose This study aims to develop a dynamic mesh cutting method for immersive virtual reality (VR) that enables interactive cutting of deformable garment meshes using head-mounted displays (HMDs) and controllers. This study addresses the lack of VR-specific tools for intuitive, real-time, and topology-consistent garment mesh cutting. Design/methodology/approach The proposed system was implemented using Unreal Engine 5 and Meta Quest 2. The method defines cut-points through controller-based ray–mesh intersection and adjusts them according to their topological relationship with the garment mesh. A two-stage cut-point adjustment strategy, projection-based intersection analysis, and doubly connected edge list (DCEL)-based topology processing are used to support localized real-time cutting. The resulting 3D mesh updates are also propagated to the corresponding 2D pattern representation. Findings The mesh cutting cases were classified into six major types and sixteen sub-types according to the topological relationship between cut-points and mesh elements. The results demonstrate that cut-point topology classification, cut-point topology geometric adjustment, and DCEL-based local mesh reconstruction can generate stable real-time cutting results in immersive VR while reducing ambiguous cut-lines, irregular local faces, and unintended cutting of non-target regions. title: Dissection of quality variation and hierarchical quality evaluation of Evodiae Fructus under multidimensional factors
abstract: Introduction Considerable quality fluctuation and heterogeneity are commonly observed in Evodiae Fructus due to multiple confounding factors. Accordingly, this study performed multi-factor analysis to explore potential key factors associated with its chemical quality, aiming to provide scientific evidence and theoretical support for the quality evaluation of this medicinal material. Methods First, for the HPLC-derived multi-component quantitative dataset, the Kruskal-Wallis H test followed by post-hoc Dunn’s tests with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction was performed, and generalized linear models (GLMs) specified with a Gamma distribution and log-link function together with random forest regression were further constructed to quantify the associations of botanical origins, geographical origins, commercial specifications, and maturity stages with the quality of Evodiae Fructus. Second, for the multi-dimensional UPLC-MS/MS metabolomic profiles, principal component analysis (PCA), orthogonal partial least-squares discriminant analysis (OPLS-DA), Kruskal-Wallis H tests, and fold-change analysis were applied to screen differential metabolites across the predefined comparison groups, with metabolites satisfying VIP > 1, |log2FC| > log2(1.5) , and unadjusted p < 0.05 retained as differential metabolites. title: PENGARUH PEER GROUP SUPPORT TERHADAP MOTIVASI PESERTA POSYANDU REMAJA (STUDI DI DESA TERTEK KECAMATAN PARE KABUPATEN KEDIRI)
abstract: Setiap anak usia sekolah dan remaja harus diberikan pelayanan kesehatan, salah satunya dengan pelaksanaan posyandu remaja. Rendahnya tingkat kehadiran remaja di posyandu menjadi hambatan utama dalam meningkatkan kesehatan remaja di komunitas. Remaja yang tidak mengikuti posyandu remaja berisiko mengalami keterbatasan pengetahuan serta perilaku kesehatan yang kurang baik. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh peer group support terhadap motivasi dalam mengikuti kegiatan posyandu remaja. Penelitian kuantitatif dengan desain pre-experimental One Group Pretest-Posttest dilakukan pada 30 remaja di Posyandu Remaja Desa Tertek, Kecamatan Pare, Kabupaten Kediri pada 18 April 2026. Sampel dipilih menggunakan teknik purposive sampling. Intervensi berupa peer group support diberikan kepada responden dan data dianalisis menggunakan uji Wilcoxon Signed Rank Test. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan adanya peningkatan motivasi mengikuti posyandu remaja setelah intervensi peer group support dengan nilai signifikansi 0,004 (p < 0,05). Artinya terdapat pengaruh peer group support terhadap motivasi dalam mengikuti posyandu remaja. Adanya peningkatan nilai motivasi setelah diberikan intervensi menunjukkan bahwa pendekatan berbasis kelompok sebaya mampu menjadi stimulus yang efektif dalam mendorong partisipasi remaja pada kegiatan pelayanan kesehatan. title: Evaluation of a peer mentoring project involving undergraduate psychology students in Greece
abstract: Purpose The mental health needs of university students have increased since COVID-19 and more needs to be done. There is evidence that peer mentoring can facilitate new students’ adjustment to higher education and is associated with well-being and student satisfaction. This study aims to explore lived experiences of peer mentoring further in higher education in Greece, contributing to an under-researched national context and informing the development of accessible mental health support in higher education. Design/methodology/approach Fourteen psychology students undertook 30 h of training in the principles and techniques of peer mentoring. Subsequently, 20 students received mentoring, whilst the peer mentors attended a weekly support group. All participants were invited to take part in a semi-structured interview exploring experiences of mentoring. The interviews were recorded, transcribed and analyzed using thematic analysis. Findings In line with previous research findings, the mentoring relationship was supportive, but it also led to a greater sense of belonging and campus connectedness, an enhanced growth mindset and social inclusion. Social implications Enhancing social inclusion for emerging adults unable to access their usual support network (e.g. international students) or living away from home for the first time. Originality/value The findings indicate that peer mentor…

title: ENHANCING FAMILY WAQF PARTICIPATION THROUGH WAQF LITERACY AND INSTITUTIONAL TRUST AMONG MALAYSIAN MUSLIMS
abstract: This study examines the factors influencing Muslim participation in family waqf in Malaysia, with particular attention to perception, understanding and trust in waqf institutions. Unlike general waqf, which is commonly established for broader public or charitable purposes, family waqf allows the benefits of endowed assets to be directed initially to family members or descendants while preserving the long-term charitable purpose of waqf. This distinctive feature makes family waqf relevant not only as an instrument of Islamic social finance but also as a mechanism for intergenerational wealth preservation and Islamic estate planning. Despite the continued development of waqf institutions in Malaysia, participation in family waqf remains relatively limited. This suggests that participation may depend not only on religious motivation, but also on how well individuals understand family waqf, perceive its benefits and trust the institutions responsible for its management. A quantitative survey was conducted among 400 Muslim respondents selected through purposive sampling. Data were analysed using SPSS through reliability analysis, Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA), regression and mediation analysis. The findings indicate that perception, understanding and institutional trust were significantly associated with participation in family waqf. The results further highlight the importance …

title: Enhancing Student Engagement and Participation in Elementary Science and Social Studies through Teams Games Tournament Cooperative Learning
abstract: Student engagement and participation are essential for interactive elementary science and social studies (IPAS) learning. Limited involvement in questioning, expressing opinions, and teamwork may hinder meaningful learning. This study examined changes in engagement and participation during the implementation of the Teams Games Tournament (TGT) model at SDN Karawang Wetan III. Classroom action research involved 30 students across a pre-cycle and two intervention cycles. Classroom observations assessed seven engagement and seven participation indicators. Descriptive analysis showed improvements in both outcomes. Engagement increased in attention, enthusiasm, active involvement, peer interaction, persistence, and responsibility. Participation improved in questioning, answering, expressing opinions, discussion, cooperation, tournament involvement, and task completion. Reported percentages represent mean indicator-level observation scores rather than proportions of students meeting specific criteria. The findings suggest that structured teamwork, academic games, and individual accountability can provide practical opportunities for collaborative IPAS learning. Teachers should establish clear team roles and encourage individual contributions and questioning. Because the study involved one school and two cycles without a control group, the findings are context-specific and do not estab…

title: Computational exploration of Mg2XH6 (X = Sc, Ti, V) hydrides: insights into their suitability for hydrogen storage
Participation preferences in discharge planning among patients with stroke in China: a cross-sectional study using latent profile analysis
Digitalisasi Arsip dan Dokumen Kependudukan Berbasis Cloud Storage pada Kelurahan Mampang
abstract: A key component in modernizing administrative devices at the village level is transforming the management of digital correspondence archives. At the Mampang village office, issues related to fragmented document management have caused vulnerabilities such as lost files, duplicate records, and slow data access. By integrating cloud storage APIs into the village correspondence program, this community service project addresses these issues and develops a cloud-based storage system that is responsive, secure, and well-organized. This community service is carried out in four detailed stages: Planning and Needs Analysis, Socialization and Participant Recruitment, Cloud Storage Implementation Training, and Technical Assistance and Practical Application. The results show that the new system successfully automates the classification of issued documents by type and date in cloud storage. This action successfully shortened the time needed for filing, eliminated the possibility of lost files or physical damage, and improved daily operational efficiency. With better access restrictions and system integration, cloud storage provides affordable, useful, and durable digital administration options.

title: Battery-logistics-aware operations planning for UAV-based scanning of large built environments
abstract: Purpose This study develops a battery-logistics-aware operations planning framework for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based scanning of large built environments, addressing the gap between geometrically feasible missions and executable field operations under coupled resource, time and cost constraints. Design/methodology/approach The framework converts spatial scanning demand into battery-feasible sorties, coordinates UAVs, reusable batteries, chargers, couriers and personnel, and evaluates UAV-battery-courier configurations through cost-time Pareto optimization. Bounded exact enumeration is benchmarked against five multi-objective methods across 300 cases and applied to the Xuzhou Daguozhuang project through a web prototype. Findings Bounded exact enumeration recovered the complete reference Pareto front across 300 cases with an average runtime of 0.0315 s. In the project application, 36.5% of the recommended makespan arose from nonflight processes. The balanced configuration reduced makespan by 74.2% relative to the lowest-cost plan while reducing cost by 68.1% relative to the fastest plan, demonstrating the importance of battery circulation, logistics and bottleneck migration. Practical implications The framework helps practitioners identify operational bottlenecks, prioritize battery-related resource preparation and select Pareto-efficient configurations according to projec…

title: Improving Indonesian Vehicle License Plate Recognition Using YOLOv8n and Fine-Tuned PaddleOCR
abstract: Automatic License Plate Recognition (ALPR) is an important technology in intelligent transportation systems, enabling automatic vehicle identification through license plate detection and character recognition. However, variations in lighting conditions, image quality, viewing angles, and the design characteristics of Indonesian license plates often reduce recognition accuracy. This study proposes an ALPR system that integrates YOLOv8n for license plate detection and Fine-Tuned PaddleOCR for character recognition. A dataset consisting of 900 vehicle images was utilized to train and evaluate the detection model. The YOLOv8n model was trained using a 640 × 640pixel input size and evaluated using Precision, Recall, mAP50, and mAP50-95 metrics. The detected license plate regions were cropped and processed using image preprocessing techniques, including resizing, grayscale conversion, bilateral filtering, and sharpening. Character recognition performance was evaluated by comparing the default PaddleOCR model and a Fine-Tuned PaddleOCR model trained on Indonesian license plate data. Experimental results showed that YOLOv8n achieved a precision of 0.987, recall of 1.000, mAP50 of 0.989, and mAP50-95 of 0.853. Furthermore, the Fine-Tuned PaddleOCR model improved recognition accuracy from 56% to 81%, demonstrating a 25% increase compared to the default PaddleOCR model. These results indi…

title: DRIVE CYCLE-BASED LOSS EVALUATION OF TWO-LEVEL AND THREE-LEVEL INVERTERS IN 400 V AND 800 V ELECTRIC VEHICLE APPLICATIONS
abstract: In this paper, the driving cycle model tested by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is utilized to analyze power losses in inverter components, aiming to assess the actual performance and energy consumption of electric vehicle drive systems. The primary losses considered include conduction and switching losses that occur under real-world operating conditions. The analyzed conditions cover urban environments, highways, and challenging terrains involving multiple phases of acceleration and deceleration. Two types of semiconductor devices are evaluated: Silicon Insulated Gate Bipolar Transistor (Si IGBT) and Silicon Carbide Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor Field-Effect Transistor (SiC MOSFET), corresponding to battery system voltage levels of 400 V and 800 V, respectively. Three inverter configurations are considered in this study: two-level inverter, T-type three-level inverter, and ANPC three-level inverter. The efficiency and energy losses of each configuration are assessed based on simulation results.

Competency-Based Teacher Education: Insights through the Lens of Policies
abstract: This study examines the diverse policies and frameworks governing Competency-Based Teacher Education (CBTE) through a comprehensive review of the literature, policy documents, and theoretical approaches. Using a descriptive and analytical approach, we explore CBTE's conceptual foundations, its alignment with 21st-century educational demands, and the challenges of implementation. This study aims to contribute to the ongoing discussion on improving CBTE policies to ensure sustainable, high-quality teacher training in a rapidly evolving educational landscape. The research synthesizes global and regional policies, frameworks, and best practices to identify key components essential for effective CBTE integration, including competency frameworks, stakeholder engagement, capacity building, and assessment processes. The study highlights the significance of policy initiatives that promote teachers' holistic development, emphasize performance demonstration, and address technological and assessment barriers. Through this approach, trainees acquire key competencies throughout the curriculum and may demonstrate proficiency after completing a teacher education program. The study revealed a shift from traditional to outcome-based teacher education models, offering strategic insights to help policymakers, educators, and stakeholders effectively develop competent, adaptable teachers.

Turning strategy into employee adaptive performance: why empowering leadership matters in turbulent digital transformation
abstract: Purpose This study examines why formal strategic planning does not always become employee action during digital transformation and environmental turbulence. It proposes that strategic plans are associated with stronger adaptive performance when perceived implementation is translated into empowering leadership and psychological empowerment. Design/methodology/approach Three-wave survey data from 1,000 employees in nine Chinese enterprises are analyzed using employee-level OLS models with organization fixed effects and HC3 standard errors, bootstrap estimates of the conditional indirect associations, and cluster-robust and random-forest sensitivity checks. Findings At the employee level, perceived strategic planning implementation is positively associated with empowering leadership, psychological empowerment and adaptive performance in sequence, and retains no detectable direct association with adaptive performance once the pathway is modeled. Digital transformation intensity strengthens the first two links, whereas environmental turbulence strengthens the final link. Practical implications Managers should convert strategic priorities into bounded decision rights, resources and feedback rather than relying on communication alone: creating room for local experimentation under intensive digital change, and shortening approval chains under turbulence. Originality/value Rather than i…

title: Teaching Practices of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Distance Education: Bibliometric and Knowledge-Base Analysis
abstract: The rapid development of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has created new possibilities for transforming teaching practices in distance education. Although previous studies have discussed artificial intelligence applications in online learning environments, the overall knowledge structure, research development trends, and major teaching practice themes remain insufficiently explored. This study uses bibliometric and knowledge-base analyses to examine the development of research on generative artificial intelligence in distance education from 2000 to 2025. Academic publications were collected from Google Scholar and Scopus during June and July 2026. The analysis examined publication trends, research contributions, keyword relationships, citation patterns, and thematic evolution. The findings indicate that research interest in AI-supported distance education increased significantly after 2020, with particular attention given to personalized learning, automated feedback, intelligent tutoring systems, teacher support, and AI-based assessment. The knowledge structure shows a shift from early studies focused on digital learning technologies to human-centered AI integration and instructional innovation. The results also reveal several challenges, including the need for AI literacy, ethical concerns, academic integrity issues, and effective governance frameworks. This study c…

title: Organizational sensing as strategic infrastructure
abstract: Purpose The paper develops a conceptual architecture for internalizing insight capability as strategic infrastructure. Insight is theorized as an organizational sensing system rather than a procurement category, comprising a data substrate, methodological portfolio, governance spine, sensemaking layer and decision integration. Design/methodology/approach The study uses abductive conceptual triangulation. Contemporary ESOMAR guidance and a 2024 FMCG ethnographic case are read alongside IBM’s 2022 Global AI Adoption Index and the Stanford AI Index 2026. These evidence streams are benchmarked against dynamic capabilities, knowledge integration, behavioral strategy, strategic agility and AI governance. IBM is treated as an historical marker, while Stanford provides contemporary context on organizational AI diffusion. Findings Organizational sensing is increasingly an architecture problem. Historical IBM evidence identifies governance gaps in bias mitigation, explainability and monitoring, while Stanford shows the substantially wider contemporary AI environment. The paper proposes that reusable governance may reduce repeated validation and clearance where assurance constrains decision cadence. This governance-agility mechanism is conceptual and requires empirical testing. Originality/value The paper theorizes insight capability as a higher-order dynamic capability with named microfo…

title: Generation Z in hybrid retail networks: a systematic synthesis
abstract: Purpose This study synthesises research on Generation Z's participation in omnichannel and phygital retail environments. It examines how digitally native consumers navigate hybrid customer journeys and how these behaviours influence retail channel integration and value creation. Design/methodology/approach A Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses-guided systematic literature review was conducted using peer-reviewed journal articles indexed in Scopus and Web of Science. The final sample of 37 studies was analysed using bibliographic coupling to map thematic clusters and the Theory–Context–Characteristics–Methodology (TCCM) framework to examine theories, contexts, constructs and methodological approaches. Findings The review identifies six research streams: phygital journeys, digital engagement, technology adoption, omnichannel decision-making, smart retail and virtual retail well-being. The TCCM analysis shows a technology-centric field dominated by technology acceptance and stimulus–response theories. Research is concentrated in retail-based omnichannel and phygital contexts, with engagement and loyalty emerging as the primary outcomes. The literature relies heavily on cross-sectional survey designs, with limited longitudinal, behavioural and cross-cultural research. Social implications The study highlights the importance of responsible hybrid retail…

title: QRIS Outpaces Cards in Transaction Growth: Changing Dynamics of Indonesia’s Retail Payment Landscape
abstract: Indonesia’s Quick Response Code Indonesian Standard (QRIS) has expanded rapidly, while publicly available statistics do not separately report provincial transactions for Visa and Mastercard. To avoid relying on unverifiable network-specific allocation proxies, this study compares QRIS activity with directly observed debit- and credit-card shopping statistics reported by official institutions. The analysis uses a national annual benchmark for 2021–2024, supplemented by full-year 2025 card data, comparable January–May 2025 and January–May 2026 card-shopping windows, and published QRIS statistics through mid-2026. Between 2021 and 2024, QRIS transaction value increased from Rp27.63 trillion to Rp659.94 trillion, while combined debit- and credit-card shopping value increased from Rp573.86 trillion to Rp959.65 trillion. In H1 2026, QRIS reached 12.55 billion transactions valued at Rp1.12 quadrillion, compared with 6.05 billion transactions valued at Rp579 trillion in H1 2025. Meanwhile, nominal combined card-shopping value increased by 3.8% in January–May 2026 compared with the same period in 2025, while transaction volume declined by 3.4%. The findings indicate that QRIS is expanding substantially faster in transaction frequency, while card payments remain significant in nominal value. Illustrative cross-checks for two regions, East Java and D.I. Yogyakarta, show that card-payment …

title: GenAI-enabled educational game development: the effects of a scripted mystery role-playing game on students’ learning experience and learning outcomes in legal education
abstract: Abstract Although previous studies have shown that GenAI can support learning engagement and motivation, it remains unclear how GenAI-assisted development of offline educational games based on Scripted Mystery Role-Playing Games (SMRPG) influences students’ learning experiences and outcomes. Based on the SMRPG format, this study developed an offline educational game with the assistance of Gemini 3 Pro to explore its potential value for students’ learning outcomes and experiences in higher education contexts. A sequential explanatory mixed-methods design was employed with 84 undergraduate students majoring in law as participants. First, a randomized controlled experiment compared learning outcomes between an experimental group ( N = 42) and a control group ( N = 42). Subsequently, qualitative interviews were conducted with 24 students who participated in the game to examine their learning experiences during the gameplay process. Quantitative results showed that, after controlling for pre-test scores, the experimental group achieved significantly higher post-test scores than the control group (F(1, 81) = 105.61, p <.001, partial η² = 0.566). Qualitative findings indicate that participants described an immersive learning experience involving reasoning scenarios and role interaction in the GenAI-assisted game. This experience was associated with greater willingness to engage in lea…

title: Comparing Students’ Critical Thinking Skills in Arithmetic Sequences: Self-Directed Learning versus Contextual Teaching and Learning
abstract: This study examined differences in students’ mathematical critical thinking skills between self-directed learning and contextual teaching and learning in arithmetic sequences and series. A quantitative approach employing a quasi-experimental design was used. Participants were 60 tenth-grade students at SMA Budi Satrya Medan, Indonesia, divided into two classes. Class XA comprised 30 students who received instruction through self-directed learning, whereas Class XB comprised 30 students who received instruction through contextual teaching and learning. Students’ mathematical critical thinking skills were assessed using posttest scores across four indicators: problem identification, analysis, problem solving, and conclusion drawing. The data were analyzed using a t-test. The results revealed a statistically significant difference between the two groups, with the calculated t-value of 6.33 exceeding the critical value of 2.01. Students taught through contextual teaching and learning achieved higher posttest scores than those taught through self-directed learning. The contextual teaching and learning group also obtained higher aggregate scores across all four critical thinking indicators. These findings indicate that contextual teaching and learning was associated with better mathematical critical thinking performance than self-directed learning in arithmetic sequences and series a…

title: Book Review of Kumar, R., & Eaton, S. E. (Eds., 2026). A Research Agenda for Artificial Intelligence and Academic Integrity. Edward Elgar Publishing.
abstract: A Research Agenda for Artificial Intelligence and Academic Integrity is a 282-page volume in Edward Elgar’s Research Agendas series that sets out what academic integrity research should examine now that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has unsettled long-standing assumptions about authorship and assessment (Kumar & Eaton, 2026). The editors, Rahul Kumar of Brock University and Sarah Elaine Eaton of the University of Calgary, bring together 16 chapters by 27 contributors, 16 of whom are based in Canada or Australia, with others in the United Arab Emirates, Egypt, the United Kingdom, and Türkiye. The volume is framed by postplagiarism, the proposition that inherited definitions of plagiarism break down once human and machine contributions can no longer be separated (Eaton & Kumar, 2026a, p. 1). It opens with a question many teachers now face: “When a student submits work for assessment, can you tell where their thinking ends, and artificial intelligence (AI) begins?” (Eaton & Kumar, 2026a, p. 1). The editors intend it as “a road map for established and emerging scholars” (Kumar & Eaton, 2026, p. xviii).

title: Cultural Constraints and Teacher Agency in SRH Education for Students with Learning Disabilities
abstract: Sexual and Reproductive Health (SRH) education is widely recognised as a fundamental component of inclusive education and a basic human right. However, its implementation remains uneven, particularly for students with learning disabilities who occupy a marginalised position at the intersection of disability, culture, and education. This study examines how teachers mediate SRH education for students with learning disabilities in a culturally complex context in southern Sarawak, Malaysia. Drawing on qualitative data from semi-structured interviews with 12 special education teachers and survey responses from 78 teachers across five districts, the study explores how SRH knowledge is negotiated, adapted, and constrained in classroom practice. Guided by Ecological Systems Theory and Social Cognitive Theory, the findings reveal that SRH education is shaped by multi-layered interactions between institutional limitations, socio-cultural norms, and teacher agency. Four key dynamics are identified: institutional unpreparedness, lack of structured pedagogical resources, cultural and religious regulation of sexuality discourse, and teacher-led adaptive practices. Teachers emerge as cultural mediators who navigate tensions between policy expectations and community sensitivities. The study argues that reliance on individual teacher agency produces fragmented and inequitable access to SRH educ…

title: Prior-informed machine learning for clinically interpretable medical diagnosis
abstract: Traditional machine learning (ML) in medical diagnostics often suffers from limited clinical interpretability and poor generalization, owing to its black-box, data-driven nature. Here, we present Prior-Informed Machine Learning (PIML), a framework that integrates clinically grounded generative reasoning with data-driven, ML-enabled discriminative modeling through Bayesian inference to provide clinically interpretable, patient-specific diagnostic outcomes. By embedding the optimization of sensitivity and specificity in data-driven diagnosis—requirements for subsequent Bayesian inference—directly into the ML model development process, PIML enables a synergistic integration of machine learning and clinical expertise that cannot be achieved through either data-driven or clinically grounded approaches alone. PIML was validated across three clinical domains—cervical neoplasia detection, high-risk oral lesion detection, and preterm birth detection—where Bayesian inference was systematically employed to integrate electrical impedance spectroscopy (EIS)-based machine learning with domain-specific clinical expertise, thereby enabling more comprehensive and enhanced diagnostic decision-making. Our results demonstrate that PIML generally improves diagnostic performance compared with standard ML approaches and provides competitive or superior performance relative to knowledge-based and feat…

title: Beyond Marshmallows: An Update of a Previously Reported Interactive In-Class Activity for Learning VSEPR Theory
abstract: Abstract Using 3D printing technology, the author chose to update an interactive in-class valence-shell electron-pair repulsion (VSEPR) activity (J. Chem. Educ.2023, 100 (8), 2825–2835.) by designing and 3D printing adjustable model kits that could better represent changes in bond angles when lone pairs were present. To assess this update, the author repeated the activity previously reported, conducted an analysis of questionnaire results, and compared the results to those from the previous study. Analysis of the questionnaire results suggests that, although the updates provided no improvement to the quality of the activity, they did not deteriorate the quality of the activity either, still allowing students to learn and understand VSEPR theory, develop their visuospatial skills, and engage in a constructivist activity.

title: Development Of Learning Media Using Adobe Animate And Blooket In Skiing Subjects
abstract: This study aimed to develop learning media using Adobe Animate and Blooket for Islamic Cultural History (SKI) at MA Miftahul Jannah Palangka Raya, assess its feasibility, and examine teachers’ and students’ responses to its use. The study employed a Research and Development (R&D) approach based on the ADDIE model, which consists of five stages: Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation. Data were collected through observations, interviews, documentation, and questionnaires, and analyzed using descriptive quantitative methods with percentage calculations. The findings showed that the learning media was successfully developed by integrating Adobe Animate to present learning materials and Blooket to provide game-based assessments. The main contribution of this study lies in combining these two tools to connect material presentation and assessment within a single learning sequence. The media expert validation score was 88.89%, categorized as highly feasible, while the material expert validation score was 79.17%, categorized as feasible. The teacher response score was 75%, categorized as good, while the responses of 19 students reached 85.53%, categorized as very good. These findings indicate that the developed media met the feasibility criteria and received positive responses from both teachers and students. However, the study did not assess whether the media im…

title: Visualizing Biosynthesis at the Nanoscale: An Immersive Microscopy-Based Learning Experience for Undergraduate Chemistry Education
abstract: Abstract Understanding the relationship between microscopic structures and macroscopic phenomena remains challenging in undergraduate chemistry education, because nanoscale processes are often introduced through abstract models. Here, we present an immersive laboratory module developed in the interdisciplinary general education course Beauty of Microscience at Tongji University, integrating microbial nanoparticle biosynthesis with cryogenic transmission electron microscopy (cryo-TEM) visualization. Implemented across two semesters with 48 undergraduate students, the module emphasizes the interpretation of nanoscale evidence and evidence-based scientific reasoning rather than microscopy operation. Through a learning sequence connecting microbial activity, nanoparticle formation, and microscopic visualization, students explored how biological processes generate nanoscale structures and how microscopic observations reveal the chemical phenomena. Postmodule questionnaire responses revealed a positive student reception of the learning experience, specifically highlighting the perceived value of correlating macroscopic experimental observations with nanoscale structural details and of considering how experimental conditions influence microscopic data. This work provides an implementation model for integrating research-grade cryogenic microscopy with microbial biosynthesis and guided …

title: Traditional Games in Physical Education: Motor Skills, Fitness, Social Learning, and Cultural Sustainability
abstract: Traditional games offer culturally meaningful movement experiences for physical education (PE), yet their use in school lessons remains inconsistent and their outcomes are assessed unevenly. This review synthesised recent evidence on traditional games in relation to fundamental movement skills, physical fitness, participation, social learning, and cultural sustainability. A structured narrative review examined 24 peer-reviewed journal articles published between 2020 and 2026 and one World Health Organization guideline. Searches conducted in October 2026 used English and Indonesian terms across journal publisher portals, DOI-linked records, PubMed, and scholarly web indexing. Evidence was organised thematically without calculating a pooled effect estimate. The reviewed studies generally associated traditional games with opportunities to practise hopping, running, balance, coordination, agility, and object control. Several school-based studies also reported increased participation, motivation, cooperation, and positive peer interaction. Games such as engklek, gobak sodor, bentengan, and bakiak connected movement practice with teamwork, decision-making, and local cultural knowledge. However, small samples, short intervention durations, single-group pretest–posttest designs, and inconsistent outcome measures limited conclusions about causal and long-term effects. The evidence suppo…

How Does Generative AI Support Inquiry-Based Learning? A Systematic Review
abstract: Background Teachers and learners now use generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in inquiry-based learning (IBL), but we know little about which inquiry phases GenAI supports, who uses it and what outcomes studies report across disciplines. Methods Following PRISMA 2020, we searched Scopus on 6 October 2026 for empirical journal articles published in English from 2022 to 2026. Of 267 records screened, we sought 110 reports, assessed 89 in full text and included 66 studies. We coded the studies with a 29-variable codebook and mapped GenAI use onto the five inquiry phases (orientation, conceptualization, investigation, conclusion and discussion). We synthesized the findings descriptively and did not appraise study quality. Results Most studies appeared in 2025–2026 and took place in higher or teacher education; more than half came from fields outside science. Studies used ChatGPT or other OpenAI GPT models in 71.2% of cases, mostly as unmodified chatbots, and GenAI served most often as an information source (60.6%). Studies reported GenAI support most often in the investigation phase (68.2%) and least often in orientation (30.3%); 11 studies covered all five phases, and for most phases about half of the studies did not say whether GenAI was used. Half of the studies reported positive outcomes. Thirteen of the 14 comparisons with instruction without AI were positive, whereas co…

title: SYSTEMATIC REVIEW: THE PEDAGOGICAL ROLE OF AI-BASED ADAPTIVE LEARNING IN DEVELOPING CRITICAL THINKING SKILLS AMONG ONLINE HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS
abstract: AI-powered adaptive learning systems offer significant potential to transform the thinking processes of high school students in online learning environments. This study aims to evaluate the impact of implementing such technology on the critical thinking skills of high school students. A Systematic Literature Review (SLR) approach was adopted, adhering to the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Fifty primary articles were selected from 1,240 identified records (spanning 2021–2026) through the rigorous application of inclusion and exclusion criteria. A synthesis of these articles reveals that analytical skills, evidence evaluation, and problem-solving capabilities can be enhanced by this technology, driven by dynamic learning pathways and real-time Socratic scaffolding. Visual analytics dashboards also support students' self-regulation and metacognitive awareness. However, excessive reliance on AI algorithms was found to diminish students' independent inferential acuity—a phenomenon known as "cognitive offloading." Students' critical thinking skills can only be optimally honed if adaptive AI systems are designed using an inquiry-based pedagogical approach and supported by teachers acting as reflective facilitators.

title: Corrigendum to “Development and external validation of an explainable machine learning model for predicting chronic kidney disease progression in the Korean population” [Kidney Res Clin Pract 2026;45(5):724–742]
Enabling human resource transformation through employee engagement and managerial trust: a learning organization perspective
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate how Work Engagement (WE) and Trust in Management (TM) contribute to Human Resource Transformation (HRT) readiness, with a particular emphasis on their role in fostering a learning-oriented organizational culture. Design/methodology/approach Using a structured quantitative design, data were collected from 424 HR professionals across diverse industries. Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) was used to analyze the relationship between the variables. Measures for WE, TM and HRT readiness were adapted from established scales and validated using Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA). Findings Results indicate that both WE and TM significantly enhance HRT readiness, with TM showing a slightly stronger direct effect. WE was also found to be a strong driver of TM, which in turn partially transmits engagement’s influence onto HRT readiness, highlighting trust as an important mediating mechanism. These findings suggest that organizations with engaged employees and high levels of managerial trust are better positioned to undertake transformational HR initiatives, which are essential for continuous learning and adaptability. Practical implications The findings highlight the importance of embedding employee engagement and trust-building strategies within HR frameworks to cultivate a supportive climate for change and learning. title: Expatriates' dominance and building sustainable learning organizations in the GCC: the process of knowledge creation, transfer, and retention
abstract: Purpose Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries remain heavily dependent on temporary expatriate workforces while pursuing the development of more sustainable and knowledge-based economies. This paper examines the underexplored role of expatriates in creating, transferring, and retaining sustainability-related knowledge within GCC organizations. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on the sustainable learning organization and expatriate management literature, we develop a conceptual framework that explains how expatriates' dominance can support sustainability learning in the GCC. The framework integrates the knowledge management stages of creation, transfer, and retention to reconcile competing views on whether expatriates hinder or advance sustainability learning outcomes. It also illustrates how several factors moderate these relationships. Findings The model shows that expatriates can contribute to sustainable knowledge creation, and this relationship is positively moderated by the fostering of internal dialogue that builds collective sustainability mindsets. It further identifies how macro-, meso-, and micro-level conditions can moderate the relationship between knowledge creation and transfer. Finally, it explains how management processes, human resource management systems, operations, and community engagement can help retain expatriate-led sustainability knowledge within …

title: Container-surface-guided dual-task learning for defect detection in complex port scenes
abstract: Automatic container defect inspection in complex port environments is hindered by substantial scale variation and defect-like interference from non-container regions. This article presents CSG-YOLO, a container-surface-guided dual-task framework that jointly learns five-class defect detection and container-surface segmentation. Its scale-tuned feature fusion module adapts multi-level neck features to defects of different spatial extents, while mask-guided cross-task interaction bidirectionally exchanges the learned surface prior and defect cues between the task heads. Center-to-container consistency and edge-aware mask refinement losses respectively encourage defect-center coverage and surface-boundary consistency. On a single-terminal dataset of 4,000 distinct port images containing 4,480 defect instances, CSG-YOLO-N achieves mean scores of 58.1 average precision (AP), 93.0 AP50, and 65.0 AP75 across three independent training runs, with 16.3 GFLOPs. Compared with YOLOv12-N, it improves these metrics by 2.4, 3.2, and 4.1 points, respectively, while reducing mean overall missed detection rate from 6.4% to 5.7%, false positives per image from 0.19 to 0.11, and outside-region-of-interest (ROI) detection ratio from 1.8% to 0.2%. It also obtains a mean Surface intersection over union of 76.7%. These results support the effectiveness of explicit container-surface modeling for defect…

title: Deep phenotyping of blood cell data reveals novel clinical biomarkers
abstract: Abstract Objectives The complete blood count with differential (CBD) is one of the most common blood tests worldwide. Although modern CBD analyzers generate flow-cytometry based single-cell measurements, the resultant CBD markers are limited to coarse summary features, such as total cell counts and average cell sizes. This means, they cannot detect subtle cell population shifts that may signal early-stage pathogenesis. To test this, we evaluate whether AI-based analysis of the single-cell CBD data can generate novel and clinically prognostic biomarkers. Methods We developed two complementary methods for biomarker discovery using CBD tests from an academic medical center. To create interpretable biomarkers, we clustered cells into known sub-populations and performed statistical summarization. In tandem, self-supervised autoencoders were developed to extract novel non-linear markers. We evaluated the utility of the generated markers for patient prognostication across a range of outcomes (mortality, inpatient admission, and future disease development). Results Our study included 242,584 CBD samples from 127,543 patients. Both clustering and autoencoder biomarkers showed strong prognostic associations for all-cause mortality, inpatient admission, and development of anemia, cancer, or cardiovascular disease, with associations remaining significant after adjustment for demographics a…

title: Navigating currency volatility in West Africa: the role of digital currency uncertainty
abstract: Purpose This study examines the dynamic relationship between digital currency uncertainties and the volatility of West African fiat currencies. This study explores how shocks from cryptocurrency markets and central bank digital currency (CBDC) development are transmitted to regional exchange rate behavior. Design/methodology/approach A time-varying parameter vector autoregressive (TVP-VAR) model is employed to analyze the return and volatility spillovers between eight West African fiat currencies and three global digital uncertainty indices: cryptocurrency price uncertainty (UCRY_Px), cryptocurrency policy uncertainty (UCRY_Po), and CBDC uncertainty (CBDCUI). The sample period spans November 27, 2015, to June 30, 2023. Findings The return and volatility networks exhibit moderate and comparable connectedness. UCRY_Px and UCRY_Po are net transmitters on average, although UCRY_Po is marginal in the volatility network. CBDCUI receives return shocks but episodically transmits volatility shocks. Most currencies are net receivers, with exposure varying over time and intensifying during heightened uncertainty. Originality/value This study is among the first to quantify spillovers from both cryptocurrency-related and CBDC-related uncertainties to African currencies using a time-varying model. These findings provide practical insights for financial regulators and policymakers seeking to …

title: Uncertainty-Aware Single-Channel Surface EMG Classification for Low-Resource Hand Gesture Recognition: A Subject-Independent Evaluation
abstract: Abstract Single-channel surface electromyography (sEMG) could reduce the cost and complexity of hand-gesture interfaces, but performance commonly degrades when models are tested on unseen subjects. We evaluated five-class hand gesture classification using only the Flexor Carpi Radialis (FCR) channel from 83 quality-screened subjects drawn from 113 recordings. Time-domain (TD) features were classified with multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) and three uncertainty quantification (UQ) methods: Monte Carlo (MC) Dropout, Deep Ensembles, and Evidential Deep Learning (EDL). A raw-window one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) and a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) were included as end-to-end comparators. The best within-subject result was obtained by Random Forest at $$73.3\%\pm 13.3\%$$ , while full-coverage leave-one-subject-out cross-validation (LOSOCV) accuracy was $$51.1\%\pm 10.3\%$$ for the MLP baseline; all UQ methods were statistically indistinguishable from this baseline after Holm correction. Confidence-based selective prediction improved per-subject accuracy to $$68.3\%$$ at $$50\%$$ coverage and $$83.9\%$$ at $$30\%$$ coverage, but this gain was achieved equally by plain MLP softmax confidence and by MC Dropout, indicating that the improvement arises from the confidence-ordering property of softmax outputs rather than from stochastic inference. The determinist…

title: TỐI ƯU HÓA QUÁ TRÌNH THU NHẬN VÀ ĐÁNH GIÁ KHẢ NĂNG KHÁNG KHUẨN CỦA SAPONIN TỪ CÂY KIM TIỀN THẢO Desmodium styracifolium
abstract: Desmodium styracifolium is a medicinal plant containing a high level of valuable bioactive compounds, particularly saponins — a class of natural substances with diverse biological activities and wide application potential. This study investigated the influence of key parameters on saponin extraction efficiency using Solid–Liquid Extraction (SLE) and Microwave-Assisted Extraction (MAE). The extraction conditions were then optimized using Response Surface Methodology (RSM), and the antibacterial activity of the saponin-rich extract was evaluated. The MAE method exhibited higher efficiency than SLE; therefore, optimization focused on MAE conditions, including a material-to-solvent ratio of 1:21.47 (w/v), microwave power of 318.92 W, and irradiation time of 65.76 seconds, yielding 79.32 mg OAE/g DW of saponins. The saponin-rich extract from D. styracifolium showed significant antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli, as determined by the agar diffusion method. Increasing the extract concentration from 100 µg/mL to 300 µg/mL resulted in inhibition zones of 20.48 ± 0.39 mm, 22.92 ± 0.06 mm, and 24.36 ± 0.10 mm for S. aureus, and 16.33 ± 0.28 mm, 18.40 ± 0.25 mm, and 19.94 ± 0.32 mm for E. coli. These results indicate the potential application of D. styracifolium saponin extract in the development of functional food and pharmaceutical products.

title: Milstein Mittag-Leffler Integrator for Stochastic Semilinear Subdiffusion with Fractionally Integrated Multiplicative Noise
abstract: This paper investigates the strong convergence of a numerical method for stochastic semilinear subdiffusion equations characterized by a Caputo fractional derivative of order \(\alpha \in (1/2,1)\), driven by fractionally integrated multiplicative noise. A spatio-temporal full discretization scheme, combining the Milstein Mittag-Leffler integrator and the finite element method, is developed and analyzed. The solution operator corresponding to the mild solution does not satisfy the semigroup property due to memory effects induced by the fractional derivative, complicating the proof of well-posedness. The presence of the nonlinear drift term and the high-order temporal discretization using the Milstein scheme make the strong convergence analysis more challenging compared to the case of stochastic linear subdiffusions. We establish the well-posedness of the underlying equation under certain assumptions, using Mainardi’s Wright function and an equivalent norm. The spatio-temporal strong convergence rate of the fully discrete solution is derived using fractional semigroup theory. The time convergence order obtained in this work is twice that of the Maruyama fractional exponential integrator presented by Noupelah et al. [Commun. Nonlinear Sci. 125 (2023)]. Numerical experiments are finally reported to validate the theoretical results.

title: NGHIÊN CỨU CHẾ TẠO VẬT LIỆU HẤP PHỤ TỪ BÃ MÍA TỔ HỢP VỚI NANO TỪ MgFe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub> ĐỂ LOẠI BỎ PHỐT PHÁT TRONG NƯỚC THẢI
abstract: This study investigates the synthesis of a composite material combining biochar derived from sugarcane bagasse with MgFe₂O₄ magnetic nanoparticles as an adsorbent, aiming to optimize adsorption conditions for treating phosphate pollution in wastewater. The sol-gel method was employed to produce MgFe₂O₄ nanoparticles, followed by the integration with biochar using an ultrasonic device. The effects of calcination temperature and the biochar-to-nanoparticle ratio were examined. The resulting materials, both before and after adsorption, were characterized using SEM and EDS-mapping techniques. Results revealed that the MgFe₂O₄ modified biochar (MgFe₂O₄@BC) exhibited superior performance compared to pristine biochar (BC). The study evaluated factors influencing the adsorption efficiency and capacity for PO₄³⁻, including the MgFe₂O₄@BC ratio, solution pH, adsorbent dosage, initial PO₄³⁻ concentration, and contact time. Findings indicate that optimal performance was achieved at a 5% (w/w) MgFe₂O₄@BC modification ratio, alongside optimized pH, adsorbent dosage, initial PO₄³⁻ concentration, and contact time.

Prospects for the Development of Arbitral Proceedings in Light of Court Caseload Optimization in the Courts of Arbitration of the Russian Federation
abstract: The optimization of the caseload of the courts of arbitration is achieved by improving the functioning of existing institutions and developing new mechanisms. Arbitral proceedings are among the tools for optimizing the court caseloads; however, their potential is still not fully realized. The study aims to analyze the prospects for the development of arbitral proceedings as a means of optimizing the caseload in the courts of arbitration of the Russian Federation. The methodology of the study includes the method of dialectical construction, analysis, and synthesis. The paper presents a model of online arbitration without hearings, which involves the asynchronous exchange of written submissions via a secure platform and the application of artificial intelligence for the intelligent analysis of evidence.

title: Unified heuristic optimization (UHO) for scheduling repetitive and nonrepetitive construction and renewal projects
abstract: Purpose Traditional Critical Path Method (CPM) based heuristics are insufficient for managing resource overallocation and meeting deadlines in repetitive projects such as highways and multi-bridge repairs. Despite their inefficiencies, they are still being used due to the lack of simple heuristic scheduling tools that help project managers and stakeholders cater to these projects' needs, such as crew continuity. The study aims to fill this gap and develop a unified framework that extends CPM heuristics to optimize scheduling for both repetitive and nonrepetitive projects. Design/methodology/approach A unified heuristic optimization (UHO) framework was developed, integrating CPM-based cost-resource allocation and time-cost trade-off procedures with the first-come-first-served repetitive scheduling methodology. An Excel-based automated scheduling tool based on the proposed framework was developed as a proof of concept and tested against cases from the literature. Findings This article presented a novel scheduling framework that generalizes CPM procedures to be applicable for repetitive projects, resolving any deadline or resource allocation constraints. Applied to a literature case study, the produced schedule achieved the same overall project deadline while having more efficient resource utilization. Originality/value This study introduces a unified heuristic approach that simpl…

title: High-yield bio-polyols from sugarcane bagasse: process optimization, structural analysis, and application potential
abstract: Abstract This research addresses the management of agricultural waste and the partial substitution of petrochemicals in polyurethanes (PUs) by utilizing renewable resources. The present study evaluates, both quantitatively and qualitatively, the feasibility of producing bio-polyols from sugarcane bagasse by polyethylene glycol (PEG 400) as organic solvent. These polyols can be potentially utilized as substitute for petrochemical polyols in elastic PU formulations. The effects of process conditions (temperature, catalyst content, and sugarcane bagasse: solvent ratio) on the bio-polyol yield were evaluated and optimized using response surface methodology through a Box-Behnken design. In addition, at each experimental point, the qualitative characteristics of the resulting bio-polyols, including functional groups, hydroxyl number ( I OH ), acid number ( A n ), molecular weight ( M W ), functionality, viscosity, and polydispersity index (PDI) were determined. The optimal conditions identified by the model determined the most effective experimental parameters as 2 g of sugarcane bagasse, 3.13% catalyst, and a reaction temperature of 161.1 °C. Under these conditions, a polyol yield of 95.6% was achieved, with a prediction error of 4.4%. For the high‑yield samples, I OH ranged from $$\sim$$ ∼ 195 to 233 mg KOH · g⁻ 1 , M W from 3839.27 to 7582.06 g · mol⁻ 1 , functionality between 3.1…

title: Spatially Heterogeneous Wetting on Stochastic Nanoflake Surfaces
abstract: Abstract While Wenzel and Cassie–Baxter wetting on textured surfaces is well established, their spatial occurrence on stochastic nanotopographies remains less well understood. Here, boehmite nanoflake surfaces with systematically varied morphologies were used to examine local wetting-state occurrence by spatially resolved droplet adhesion measurements. The nanoflake structures were produced by hot-water treatment of atomic-layer-deposited aluminum oxide (Al2O3) films, with the initial film thickness used to vary the resulting nanotopography. The adhesion measurements on the hydrophobized nanoflake surfaces revealed a systematic change in local wetting behavior across the surface series: Wenzel and Cassie–Baxter states coexisted spatially at low and intermediate nanoflake coverage, and Cassie–Baxter wetting was observed at all investigated locations on higher-coverage surfaces under the applied measurement conditions. The occurrence of Cassie–Baxter wetting was quantified by the occurrence fraction, fCB, and its dependence on image-derived nanoflake coverage was described empirically using logistic regression. The results demonstrate that the evolution of stochastic nanoflake morphology is accompanied by a probabilistic change in local wetting-state occurrence and reveal an intermediate regime characterized by spatially heterogeneous Wenzel and Cassie–Baxter wetting.

title: Distributed feedback lasers heterogeneously integrated on a standard 220 nm silicon photonics platform via direct bonding
abstract: Heterogeneous integration of III–V distributed feedback (DFB) lasers on silicon photonics platforms is the key technological step toward fully integrated on-chip photonic systems. However, its implementation on industry-standard 220 nm silicon photonics platforms is hindered by two major factors: weak optical interaction between the guided mode in the III–V gain region and the silicon-based DFB grating, and inefficient power transfer from the III–V active region to the silicon waveguide. Most prior demonstrations have been implemented on non-standard silicon-on-insulator (SOI) platforms featuring 400–500 nm thick silicon device layers, which enhances grating feedback and coupling efficiency. The use of a thick non-standard silicon layer compromises foundry compatibility, increases fabrication complexity, and complicates component design due to the emergence of higher-order vertical modes. Here we develop a heterogeneous integration technology that overcomes these obstacles, culminating in the integration of indium phosphide quantum well (InP QW) DFB lasers on a standard 220 nm silicon photonics platform. An ultrathin bonding interface is used to strengthen optical coupling between the III–V gain region and the silicon DFB grating so that a quarter-wave phase-shifted grating is fabricated with an optimized coupling coefficient that ensures stable single-mode operation. A multi-s…

title: Patient-specific Visualisation of the Cardiac Conduction System to Guide Structural Interventions and Physiological Pacing
abstract: The cardiac conduction system is frequently injured during structural heart disease procedures and it remains difficult to target accurately during conduction system pacing. These current approaches both lead to increased mortality and morbidity. The authors review the anatomical basis, estimated conduction system calibration and subsequent clinical application of a novel CT angiography-based conduction system visualisation platform that enables patient-specific 3D estimation and mapping of the atrioventricular conduction axis for real-time procedural guidance. This breakthrough technology enables clinicians to avoid iatrogenic damage by implanting devices with respect to patient-specific conduction anatomy and to achieve true physiological pacing by targeting precise locations along the conduction system. The authors have applied this visualisation system in more than 2,000 patients undergoing structural heart disease and conduction system pacing procedures, and the results of this early experience are reviewed here. Conduction system-guided intervention provides a framework for a potential shift in cardiac care, with planned prospective trials to further validate these promising outcomes.

title: Localized Crystallization of Ce:YIG Thin Films on Si Using CO2 Laser Annealing for Integrated Nonreciprocal Photonic Device Applications
abstract: Abstract Laser annealing (LA) has emerged as an effective method for localized crystallization of magneto-optical (MO) garnet thin films on semiconductor substrates. However, few studies have explored the crystallization and magneto-optical (MO) properties of cerium-substituted yttrium iron garnet (Ce:YIG, Ce1Y2Fe5O12) thin films for integrated photonic device applications using the LA technique. In this study, we provide a comprehensive investigation into the laser annealing of Ce:YIG films deposited on SiO2 substrates and silicon nitride photonic waveguides for integrated nonreciprocal photonic device applications. Garnet phase was successfully observed in films grown on SiO2/Si substrates and SiN waveguides with laser annealing of sputtered Ce:YIG films on top of a laser annealed Y3Fe5O12 seed layer. The magneto-optical (MO) properties of Ce:YIG films on oxidized Si substrates were found to be comparable to those prepared by rapid thermal annealing (RTA). A Mach–Zehnder Interferometer (MZI) type optical isolator based on Ce:YIG film on SiN was fabricated, exhibiting a saturation Faraday rotation of −2317.7 ± 94.8 deg/cm and propagation loss of 188.2 ± 16.5 dB/cm. Isolation ratio of 27.1 dB and insertion loss of 10.1 dB were achieved at 1552.7 nm wavelength.

Is the health system working for people? Comparison of adolescent and adult perspectives from the people´s voice survey in Germany
abstract: Abstract Background People-centred health system performance assessments rely largely on adults, with limited inclusion of adolescents despite their distinct health needs and rights to participate in decisions concerning their health. The People’s Voice Survey is a multi-country, adult-population-representative survey of health system perceptions, but it includes adolescents in the German survey. Germany’s health system offers financial protection and commits to adolescent participation, yet little is known about adolescents’ views of its performance. We aimed to identify adolescent-specific experiences and perspectives by comparing adolescents’ and adults’ experiences and perceptions of health system performance. Methods Population-representative data were collected through an online panel between December 2024 and January 2025. Respondents could choose to take the survey in either German or English. Because adolescents were intentionally oversampled to enable age-group comparisons, we conducted a weighted cross-sectional analysis comparing adolescents (15–19 years) with adults (≥ 20 years) using descriptive statistics and chi-square tests. Variables included self-reported health status, confidence and autonomy in managing health, experiences during care delivery, and perceptions of the health system. Weighted descriptive analyses and chi-square tests were performed. Results T…

title: Large-scale flood monitoring based on time-series Sentinel-1 images and Z -score
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) satellites have emerged as a crucial technology for real-time flood monitoring in the face of escalating flood disaster hazards. However, existing flood extraction techniques still face challenges in simultaneously achieving accurate urban inundation detection and extensive large-scale monitoring. To address this challenge, this study proposes a time-series Sentinel-1 SAR anomaly-detection approach based on an analysis of backscatter characteristics across different land-cover types and the integration of auxiliary datasets. First, an analysis of scattering behaviour in time-series SAR images revealed that, in natural areas, the consistency of backscatter intensity is strongly influenced by vegetation growth status. In building areas, rainfall and floodwater can intensify or suppress double-bounce scattering depending on building geometry and water depth, thereby disrupting intensity consistency. Based on these findings, a Z -score-based flood classification tree was developed. The method uses reference images and flood-period images to compute standardized anomaly maps with statistical interpretability under approximate normality and establishes operationally transparent flood-detection thresholds. The integration of VV and VH polarizations within the classification tree further improves the reliability of flood identification. Applied to the 202…

title: Considering the Specifics of Chinese Students When Teaching the Prepositional Case System of the Russian Language
abstract: The article explores the issue of teaching the prepositional‑case system of the Russian language to Chinese students at the A1–A2 levels, taking into account four identified stable psycholinguistic profiles of Chinese learners and the typological distance between the inflectional Russian language and the isolating Chinese language. Based on a comparative analysis of grammatical systems, diagnostic testing, analysis of spontaneous speech (monologue), questionnaires, and cluster analysis, four stable psycholinguistic profiles of Chinese learners have been identified. These profiles cannot be reduced to the traditional “strong – average – weak student” gradation. The novelty of the study lies in the fact that, for the first time, a comprehensive set of methodological strategies for educators is proposed for these four distinct stable profiles of Chinese students. This includes the development of varied tasks and teaching techniques tailored to the students’ psycholinguistic profiles, reliance on ready-made speech patterns, systematic practice with a gradual increase in complexity, and the development of self-monitoring and peer-monitoring skills. This approach significantly expands the understanding of the heterogeneity within groups of Chinese students and contributes to the individualization of teaching Russian as a foreign language.

title: Validating Worst-Case System Performance Under Multi-State System Disruptions: Evidence from Supply Chain Networks
abstract: Abstract Reliable performance of large-scale engineered systems is difficult to guarantee when components experience gradual rather than complete failures. Traditional reliability approaches based on binary operational states cannot formally validate performance under such graded disruptions. This study develops an optimization-based framework for validating worst-case system performance under multi-state disruptions with linear or exactly linearizable performance measures, polyhedral adaptive-response structures, and continuous polyhedral or discrete combinatorial disruption sets. The framework models adaptive system responses, such as rerouting and resource reallocation, through a nested optimization that captures the interplay between failures and operational decisions. A dual reformulation combined with the Reformulation–Linearization Technique transforms the resulting nonconvex validation problem into a tractable linear relaxation, providing provable upper bounds on worst-case performance. The methodology is applied to multi-echelon supply chain networks to examine performance degradation under continuous, bounded, and combinatorial disruption scenarios. Numerical analyses demonstrate that the framework efficiently identifies critical vulnerabilities, yields tight performance bounds for the tested instances where the true worst-case values can be certified, and provides co…

Weather extremes and diarrheal disease: findings from a multi-city study in the Asia Pacific Region
abstract: Abstract Background Changes in weather patterns including increasing extreme weather events tied to ongoing climate change is impacting burden of diarrheal disease, yet there is a paucity of data regarding how this risk varies across large urban areas within the high-risk Asia Pacific Region (APR). We investigated the association between weather extremes (temperature, precipitation) and risk of diarrheal disease burden in large metropolitan areas of APR. Method We obtained diarrheal disease records from 17 cities located across the APR, including cities in Nepal, Taiwan, Vietnam, India, Singapore, and Indonesia. We used a distributed lag non-linear model to investigate the association between exposure to weather extremes (high: 95th percentile and low: 5th percentile of temperature and precipitation) and diarrheal disease burden. City-specific risk estimates were subsequently pooled using multivariate random-effects meta-analysis. Results A total of 10,358,987 diarrheal disease cases were included. Considerable heterogeneity was observed in temperature- and precipitation-related associations across cities. At the pooled level, neither extreme low nor extreme high temperature was significantly associated with diarrheal disease, with RRs of 1.02 (95% CI: 0.88–1.19) and 1.09 (95% CI: 0.96–1.24), respectively; pooled associations with extreme precipitation were also not statistical…

INTEGRATIVE MULTI‑MARKER BARCODING AND ITS PHYLOGENY RESOLVE VIETNAMESE STRAIN CCAH013/2 AS Mychonastes rotundus (Sphaeropleales, Chlorophyceae)
abstract: A coccoid green microalga (strain CCAH013/2) isolated from a mangrove edge freshwater site in Can Gio, Viet Nam was identified through an integrative workflow combining morphology with multi marker DNA evidence. Nuclear 18S rRNA and plastid 23S rRNA sequences showed very high similarity to named Mychonastes taxa, supporting placement at the genus level but offering limited interspecific resolution due to locus conservatism. The ITS region (ITS1–5.8S–ITS2) provided species level power: BLAST results reached ≥ 99% identity to Mychonastes rotundus and dropped markedly for other congeners (≤~ 95%). A maximum likelihood tree inferred from ITS recovered CCAH013/2 within the M. rotundus clade with strong bootstrap support, mirroring the pairwise identity pattern. Morphological characters-small, spherical to slightly oval, non motile cells occurring in minute clusters and reproducing by autospores-were congruent with the emended generic concept and the species diagnosis. Together, these data support a robust assignment of CCAH013/2 to Mychonastes rotundus and provide a basis for applied studies under local conditions, including CO₂ enrichment tolerance, lipid and carotenoid productivity, and small scale pilot tests in tropical coastal freshwater niches.

title: Multi-perspective olfactory verbs in English, German, French, and Spanish
abstract: Abstract This paper reports on a corpus-based quantitative study of the central olfactory verbs of four European languages: English ( smell ), German ( riechen ), French ( sentir ), and Spanish ( oler ). The manual annotation of 400 random occurrences of each verb in the TenTen corpora encompassed four aspects of analysis: the three ways of conceptualizing perceptual events (e.g., the wine smells wonderful ; I smell smoke ; she knelt down to smell the daffodil ); axiology (positive, neutral, negative); metaphoricity; and constructions (subjects and complements). Among other intriguing patterns, the examination has shed light upon considerable differences between the frequency of the metaphorical uses of the four verbs, with Spanish oler showing the highest proportion (above 40%). Further, the data on French sentir have revealed a close connection between the ça -construction and metaphoricity: two thirds of the verb’s metaphorical uses are formulated with ça (e.g., ça sent l’arnaque ‘this smells of a scam’).

title: An Effective Wavelet Approach to Solve Nonlinear Sdes Driven by Multi-Fractional Gaussian Noise
abstract: The objective of this research is to develop a novel and efficient approach by using Legendre wavelets to approximate solutions of nonlinear stochastic differential equations (SDEs) driven by multi-fractional Gaussian noise (MFGN). Consequently, based on these wavelets, we derive a stochastic operational matrix of integral (OMI) with respect to the multi-fractional Brownian motion (MFBM) and an exact operational vector of integral (OVI). Then, we employ them to provide approximate solutions for the mentioned problems. Additionally, we analyze the convergence of our approach. Furthermore, we solve four test problems and present comparisons between our results and those of the existing numerical methods to validate the advantages of our method.

title: Endovascular management of acute and chronic arterial mesenteric ischaemia: A narrative review of evidence informing interventional radiology treatment
abstract: Mesenteric ischaemia is a potentially life-threatening vascular disorder caused by impaired intestinal perfusion, with treatment selection requiring consideration of clinical presentation, bowel viability and lesion anatomy. This narrative review examines evidence informing interventional radiology decisions in arterial acute mesenteric ischaemia (AMI) and chronic mesenteric ischaemia (CMI). MEDLINE/PubMed was searched from inception to December 31, 2025, supplemented by reference-list screening and targeted guideline searches. Qualitative evidence synthesis considered patient selection, study design, adjunctive treatments, outcomes and follow-up. In AMI, endovascular techniques can restore perfusion, but predominantly retrospective evidence does not establish superiority over surgery in bowel preservation or survival. For CMI requiring revascularisation, European Society for Vascular Surgery guidelines recommend an initial endovascular approach, supported by Cardiovascular and Interventional Radiological Society of Europe consensus-based guidance. Observational comparisons associate endovascular treatment with lower perioperative morbidity, and surgery with less symptom recurrence. By linking individual treatment decisions to society guidance and supporting studies, this review complements existing comprehensive reviews and guidance documents. It distinguishes formal recommend…
