Green innovative behavior: impact of intrapreneurship and leadership
abstract: Purpose Grounded in the componential theory of creativity (CTC) and extended through the lens of the theory of planned behavior (TPB), this study examines how employee intrapreneurship drives green innovative behavior (GIB) and innovative performance (IP). Specifically, it evaluates the moderating roles of individual moral reflectiveness (MR) and contextual ambidextrous leadership within Pakistan's hotel industry, a context where sustainability initiatives are still nascent and employee-driven green innovation remains largely unexplored. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected via a survey of 300 employees across 3-, 4-, and 5-star hotels in Lahore. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) was conducted using Smart PLS 3.0 to analyze the data. Findings Intrapreneurship positively influences both GIB and IP, with GIB serving as a key mediator. Crucially, moral reflectiveness counterintuitively weakens, rather than strengthens, the positive link between intrapreneurship and GIB, uncovering a novel boundary condition. Ambidextrous leadership exhibits no significant moderating effect. Practical implications The findings offer hotel managers a clear route to unlocking employees' green innovative potential. By identifying individual factors (intrapreneurship, moral reflectiveness) and contextual factors (ambidextrous leadership) that jointly shape GIB and …

title: Irreversibility analysis and thermosolutal transport in baffled cavities for advanced thermal management applications
abstract: Purpose Efficient thermal management is critical for enhancing the performance and reliability of modern energy storage systems while minimizing energy losses. This study aims to investigate thermosolutal convection and entropy generation in a partially heated baffled cavity filled with a Casson ternary hybrid nanofluid. Design/methodology/approach A two-dimensional numerical model is developed by incorporating non-Newtonian Casson fluid behavior and buoyancy-driven flow. The governing equations are solved using a higher-order compact finite difference scheme to ensure high computational accuracy. The physical configuration includes a T-shaped baffle and a localized heat source along the bottom wall to promote flow mixing and regulate thermal distribution. Findings The results indicate that the combined effects of geometric baffling and partial heating significantly enhance convective circulation and improve temperature uniformity within the cavity. Entropy generation increases by 42.2% with heater length and by 53% with increasing Lewis number, highlighting stronger irreversibility due to coupled heat and mass transfer. Additionally, kinetic energy rises by approximately 65% with increasing Rayleigh number, indicating intensified convection. Internal heat generation and heater location further increase entropy generation by 15.3% and 38%, respectively. Originality/value This s…

title: Self-Identified Effective Strategies for the Management of Adverse Drug Reactions to First-Line Anti-Tuberculosis Drugs
abstract: Objective: Adverse drug reactions are important factors in patients’ discontinuation of antituberculosis drugs. Therefore, managing adverse drug reactions is vital to reducing the risk of tuberculosis transmission due to premature discontinuation of medications and increasing the chances of treatment success. We sought to explore self-identified, effective strategies for managing adverse drug reactions among newly diagnosed pulmonary tuberculosis patients.Material and Methods: This was a cross-sectional survey investigating the symptom management of adverse drug reactions among newly diagnosed pulmonary tuberculosis patients using first-line antituberculosis drugs.Results: Participants (n=394) reported the three highest-rated, self-identified, and effective strategies based on mean scores, enabling them to continue taking antituberculosis drugs, were: 1) Applying cold powder to manage itching (mean±S.D.=3.58±0.79), 2) Eating sour fruit to manage nausea (mean±S.D.=3.11±0.87), and 3) Eating small, frequent meals to manage decreased appetite (mean±S.D.=3.15±0.69).Conclusion: Self-identified effective strategies for adverse antituberculosis drug reactions can help patients continue taking antituberculosis drugs, decreasing disease severity.

The 2026 PAYE Tax Reforms and Financial Resilience of Individual Taxpayers in Uganda
abstract: This study examined the potential implications of Uganda's 2026 Pay As You Earn (PAYE) tax reforms for the financial resilience of individual taxpayers. The study responded to a limitation in the existing tax-policy literatures, which has predominantly evaluated personal income tax reforms through domestic revenue mobilisation, taxpayer compliance, taxable-income responses and redistribution, while giving comparatively limited attention to the financial capacity of individual taxpayers to absorb and recover from economic shocks. The study adopted a policy-oriented conceptual and evidence-synthesis approach. It integrated Uganda-specific evidence on personal income taxation with recent international literatures on financial resilience, financial literacy, saving, debt management and household risk management. The analysis developed a conceptual pathway linking PAYE reform to tax liability, disposable income and financial resilience. The 2026 reform raises Uganda's resident PAYE tax-free threshold from UGX 235,000 to UGX 335,000 per month and restructures the intermediate tax bands while retaining the additional 10% surcharge on monthly chargeable income above UGX 10 million. The immediate effect was therefore heterogeneous across taxpayers rather than uniformly expansionary or contractionary. Previous Ugandan evidence indicated that personal income tax reforms increased revenue …

title: Digital Transformation of the Financial Model of a Global Technology Corporation: The Case of Microsoft
abstract: The article is devoted to the analysis of the digital transformation of Microsoft's financial model under the company shifting from a licence- and product-centred logic towards a cloud-platform and AI-oriented architecture. The purpose of the study is to identify the mechanisms, through which cloud services, subscription monetisation, ecosystem integration, and artificial intelligence reshape the company’s revenue structure, operating leverage, capital intensity, and cash flows. The methodological basis is formed of the case method, systemic and comparative analysis, content analysis of corporate reporting and dynamic analysis of indicators for the fiscal years 2024–2026. It is established that revenue and operating income growth is accompanied by a sharp increase in capital inclusion of data processing and computing infrastructure. The research substantiates that the financial effect of Microsoft's digital transformation is awash with duplicity: recurring revenues and AI monetisation strengthen revenue resilience, while they increase capital intensity of the model. The practical significance of the research results may be used to assess digital strategies of large technology companies.

title: 10-mode PM-QPSK transmission over 2320 km enabled by optimized mode permutation strategies
abstract: In order to overcome the capacity limits of long-haul communication systems in single-mode fibers, mode-division multiplexing based on few-mode fibers (FMFs) is expected to greatly increase the per-fiber capacity. However, the signal pulse spread, induced by differential mode delay (DMD), and mode-dependent loss (MDL) are limiting factors in long-haul transmission, especially for a high mode count. Here, we develop the guidelines for identifying superior mode permutation strategies (MPSs) among a huge number of MPSs; 25 MPSs are found by taking DMD distribution of the FMFs into account and verified in experiments to greatly mitigate the DMD and MDL. For the first time, to our knowledge, we demonstrate a 15-Gbaud PM-QPSK 10-mode transmission over 2320 km, with a reach extension by 1000 km and a three times larger system capacity-distance product than those of previously reported works.

title: Institutional Adaptation in the Digital Transformation of Local Government Financial Governance: A Case Study of Balangan Regency
abstract: Digital transformation in local government financial governance involves more than changes in technology and administrative mechanisms; it also requires institutional adjustments to ensure that such changes can be implemented and sustained over time. This study aims to analyze institutional adaptation in the digital transformation of local government financial governance in Balangan Regency, Indonesia. The study used a descriptive qualitative approach and collected data through interviews, observations, and document analysis. The study analyzed data interactively through data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification. The analysis draws on institutional change and Problem-Driven Iterative Adaptation (PDIA), developed by Andrews, Pritchett, and Woolcock (2017), to examine institutional change and the development of adaptive capacity. The findings show that implementing SIPD/SIPD-RI, SIPANDA, the Cash Management System (CMS), SP2D Online, and non-cash transactions has prompted adjustments to regulations and work procedures, staff capacity, interorganizational coordination, infrastructure, and oversight mechanisms. Adaptation has occurred through a gradual, iterative process in which implementation challenges serve as learning opportunities that inform subsequent institutional adjustments. The findings indicate that institutional adaptation links digital …

title: Determinants of Personal Financial Management Behavior in MSME Actors in North Semarang District
abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of financial literacy, financial attitude, and financial knowledge on personal financial management behavior (PFMB), as well as examine the mediating role of locus of control among MSME actors in North Semarang District. This research employs a quantitative approach with 96 respondents selected through a purposive sampling technique. The analytical method used is Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with the assistance of SmartPLS 4.0. The results indicate that financial literacy, financial attitude, and financial knowledge have a positive and significant effect on PFMB. In addition, locus of control significantly mediates the relationship between financial literacy and PFMB, financial attitude and PFMB, as well as financial knowledge and PFMB. These findings suggest that individuals' belief in their ability to control financial decisions strengthens the influence of financial literacy, financial attitude, and financial knowledge on financial management behavior. Overall, this study highlights the importance of enhancing financial literacy, financial attitude, financial knowledge, and locus of control in supporting better financial management behavior among MSME actors

A comparative study on the financial performance of hospitals by establishment type
abstract: Purpose This study examines whether hospital establishment type conditions the relationship between strategic priorities and financial performance. It compares public hospitals, university hospitals, medical corporations and foundation hospitals and identifies which strategic priority is most closely associated with profitability, stability and growth within each type. Design/methodology/approach Financial data for Korean hospitals from 2016–2022 are combined with text-mined 2022 director messages. TF-IDF identifies the salience of four Balanced Scorecard-based priorities – public orientation, patient focus, internal processes, and learning and growth – and establishment-type-specific regressions relate these priorities to return on assets (ROA), leverage (LEV) and sales growth (GRW). Findings No single priority is financially effective across all hospital types. In public hospitals, public orientation and patient focus are positively associated with profitability, while patient focus and learning and growth are positively associated with growth. University hospitals show patient focus for profitability, internal processes for stability, and learning and growth for growth; medical corporations show patient focus for profitability, public orientation for lower leverage and learning and growth for growth; and foundations show internal processes for profitability, public orientati…

title: Individual and State-Protective Principles of the Institution of Cultural Rights after the 2020 Constitutional Reform
abstract: The article argues that after the 2020 constitutional reform, the institution of cultural rights combines two principles. Article 44 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation confirms them as individual freedoms and claims. The introduced Article 67.1 and Articles 68 and 69 as amended entrust the State with protecting cultural heritage, historical truth, and the originality of peoples, which presupposes defining the value content of culture. Formal legal, systemic, and comparative legal methods are used. The conclusions are tested against judicial practice of 2016–2025. It is demonstrated that the inconsistency between the two groups of norms has a conceptual cause. They apply the concept of culture in different meanings – narrow, a sphere of individual activity, and broad, a value characteristic of the people. And their dividing line runs along the subject entitled to judge the content of culture. Their relationship is assessed as a collision of constitutional values added by a gap in the criteria for its resolution, which predetermines the way of overcoming – the values balancing establishment. The scientific novelty of the study lies in substantiating that the 2020 amendments consolidated not collective rights of communities but a State function capable to serve as a ground for limitations of individual rights, which is not noted in the doctrine of collective rights. The…

title: A Study on the Reform of College English Teaching in Higher Vocational Institutions from the Perspective of Curriculum-Based Ideological and Political Education
abstract: The college English courses in higher vocational colleges are an important carrier for implementing the basic task of “cultivating morality through education” and promoting the integration of ideological and political education with the curriculum. These courses possess dimensions of instrumentality, humanism and ideology, and have inherent advantages in promoting collaborative education. However, the current practice of integrating ideological and political education into the university English teaching in higher vocational colleges still faces many challenges in terms of educational concepts, textbook content, teaching methods, assessment mechanisms and teachers’ professional qualities. These problems hinder the full realization of the potential of language teaching education. Based on the theoretical connotation of curriculum-based ideological and political education and the educational mission of university English in higher vocational colleges, this paper systematically explores the practical challenges involved and proposes corresponding reform strategies from five dimensions: integrating educational goals, reconstructing teaching content, innovating teaching methods, diversifying assessment mechanisms and enhancing teachers’ professional qualities. This document aims to provide practical insights for higher vocational education institutions that wish to strengthen ideolo…
venue: English Language Teaching and Linguistics Studies

title: Biological activity of seven fungicides on Cladosporium paeoniae and their field control efficacy against red spot of oil peony
abstract: Red spot of oil peony, caused by Cladosporium paeoniae, severely affects the ornamental value of oil peony and threatens the oil yield of its seeds, significantly reducing its economic value. Currently, only azoxystrobin has been registered for the control of this disease, resulting in limited fungicide options. This study evaluated the inhibitory activities of seven fungicides—pydiflumetofen, fluopyram, prochloraz, fluazinam, iprodione, prothioconazole, and tebuconazole—against four key developmental stages of C. paeoniae (spore germination, germ tube elongation, mycelial growth, and sporulation) via in vitro toxicity assays, using azoxystrobin as a control. In addition, field efficacy trials were conducted during the growing season of oil peony using spray applications. The results showed that all seven fungicides inhibited different developmental stages of C. paeoniae, but with distinct activity spectra. Prochloraz and pydiflumetofen demonstrated strong, broad-spectrum inhibition across all four stages, with EC 50 values of 0.0083-0.0756 μg/mL and 0.0047-0.6990 μg/mL, respectively. Fluazinam and tebuconazole were particularly effective against germ tube elongation (EC 50 = 0.0106 μg/mL) and mycelial growth (EC 50 = 0.3166 μg/mL), respectively. Fluopyram and prothioconazole showed moderate effects on germ tube elongation and sporulation but weak activity on spore germination …

title: JUUL’s ‘smoking switching’ initiative in Ghana: market expansion through global health
The Blind Spot of GeneXpert MTB / RIF : Isoniazid‐Resistant, Rifampicin‐Susceptible Tuberculosis Detected on Phenotypic Drug Susceptibility Testing
abstract: ABSTRACT GeneXpert MTB/RIF detects only rifampicin resistance. A 19‐year‐old man with cough and haemoptysis had rifampicin‐susceptible tuberculosis on bronchoalveolar lavage Xpert. Phenotypic drug susceptibility testing later revealed isolated isoniazid resistance, and isoniazid was replaced with levofloxacin. Additional susceptibility testing is essential to detect isoniazid‐resistant, rifampicin‐susceptible tuberculosis.

title: Unyielding Resilience of the Schengen Area: Adapting to Crises in a Transforming World
abstract: Abstract The Schengen area has recently experienced many crises. Despite occasional references to its potential end, it has proven its resilience. Whilst researchers explore Schengen's borders and databases, few studies have focused on the discourse on Schengen per se. This article fills this gap by examining discursive shifts in the perception of Schengen's resilience during recent crises, especially since 2015 (refugee crisis, COVID‐19, Russian invasion of Ukraine). Employing the theoretical concept of crisis and the methodological framework of the discourse‐historical approach and conceptual history, this analysis interprets how the European Union (EU) institutions and their representatives managed to adapt to these recent crises, which initiatives they adopted and how they discursively constructed Schengen's resilience. The findings show that although the conceptualisation of Schengen vis‐á‐vis the selected crises has shifted from ‘saving Schengen by applying Schengen’ to ‘saving Schengen by amending Schengen’, gradual amendments towards more EU authority ( vertical deepening ) and more member states' control ( horizontal broadening ) continue.
venue: JCMS: Journal of Common Market Studies

title: Hedonic Analysis of Cassava Product Attributes' Influence on Observed Market Prices. A Case Study of Smallholder Farmers in Kilifi County, Kenya
abstract: Cassava commercialisation is increasing in Kenya, mainly due to recent emphasis on its role in enhancing food security and income generation. However, smallholder cassava farmers still receive low prices for their products, constraining their ability to maximise returns. There is limited empirical evidence on how cassava product attributes influence market prices. Understanding the product attribute-price relationship will enable farmers to orient their production, marketing and value addition to attract better prices. This study aimed to analyse the influence of cassava product attributes on observed market prices among smallholder cassava farmers using a hedonic pricing model. A multi-stage sampling technique was applied to select smallholder cassava farmers. Both qualitative and quantitative data were collected using a semi-structured questionnaire. STATA software was employed to analyse data. Hedonic pricing model results revealed that cassava flour, well-shaped raw cassava, selling in bundles, and selling through consumer and farm-gate market outlets commanded a price premium, while selling in kilograms had a decrease in price. This underscores the importance of promoting cassava value addition, improving product appearance, and facilitating access to high-value markets to enhance smallholder cassava farmers’ incomes. Market policies should be put in place to ensure transp…

title: Beyond electricity and computers: How institutional information and communication infrastructure shapes teachers’ digital technology use in public junior secondary schools in Kakamega County, Kenya
abstract: Access to functional digital infrastructure is a prerequisite for teachers to convert information and communication Technology (ICT) competence into classroom practice, yet the quality and distribution of infrastructure remain uneven in many developing education systems. This paper examined the effect of the status of institutional ICT infrastructure and digital tools on teacher use of digital technologies in public junior schools (JS) in Kakamega County, Kenya. Relying on the Theory of Organizational Information Processing, the study used a convergent parallel mixed-methods design involving 332 responding JSS teachers, 11 Sub-County Directors of Education and observations from 78 schools. Factor analysis of 12 infrastructure indicators produced a factor-based index of 3.500, interpreted as good, although important differences were evident across infrastructure components. Electricity, computer rooms, broadband connectivity, and technical support were relatively strong, whereas specialized digital tools, suitable educational software and security mechanisms were weaker. Teachers most frequently identified inadequate computers/devices (26.8%) and unstable or absent internet connectivity (22.9%) as the leading infrastructure challenges. Pearson correlation showed a significant positive moderate relationship between infrastructure status and technology use (r = .417, p < .001). In…

Effects of climate change on residential electricity consumption in Guangzhou: evidence, forecasting, and warming scenarios
abstract: Introduction: Climate change, rising living standards, and increasing household electrification are expected to make residential electricity demand an important source of future energy growth in emerging economies. Focusing on Guangzhou, a humid subtropical megacity in southern China, this study examines how temperature affects daily residential electricity consumption, evaluates short-term forecasting performance, and assesses demand pressure under counterfactual warming scenarios. Materials and methods: Using daily weather and electricity data from 2019 to 2025, the analysis combines nonlinear econometric models with Ridge Regression, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting. Results: The results reveal a pronounced U-shaped temperature response, with electricity consumption reaching its minimum at approximately 19 °C and increasing sharply under hotter conditions. Relative to days with mean temperatures of 20–24 °C, consumption is about 62.4% higher when the mean temperature reaches 30 °C or above. Extreme hot days, hot nights, and prolonged heat also generate additional demand, while no statistically significant difference is found between urban and rural temperature-response patterns. Gradient Boosting performs best, reducing mean absolute error (MAE) and root mean squared error (RMSE) by around 77% compared with the weekly naïve benchmark. Under warming of 1 °C, 2 °C, and 3 °…

title: Pathway to low-carbon arctic shipping: carbon tax thresholds and market equilibrium under climate change
abstract: Global maritime trade faces the dual challenges of climate change and the low-carbon transition. The melting of Arctic sea ice is enabling the Northeast Passage to emerge as a potential alternative to the Suez Canal Route, while carbon pricing policies continue to reshape the relative competitive advantages of these two shipping routes. Addressing the limitations of existing research—which overlooks the multi-agent game-theoretic allocation of carbon emissions, lacks dynamic policy–market feedback loops in static comparisons of heterogeneous shipping routes, and fails to adequately assess the cascading effects of carbon taxes under single-scenario analyses—this paper constructs a two-level Stackelberg game model that integrates sea ice melt scenarios with voyage-level carbon emissions accounting. It systematically characterises the ‘carbon tax–voyage speed–cost–route share–emissions’ transmission mechanism and explores the heterogeneous dynamic competition between the two shipping routes, as well as the bidirectional policy–market feedback loops, in a China–Europe scenario. The results indicate that global warming and fuel price volatility significantly influence route competitiveness through dual channels, while a differentiated carbon tax can guide the orderly reallocation of freight traffic towards the low-carbon Arctic route. The emissions reduction effect of the carbon tax…

title: Union Membership and Native-Immigrant Labour Market Gaps
abstract: Abstract We estimate the causal effects of union membership on labour market outcomes for natives and immigrants, exploiting quasi-experimental variation from large increases in Norway’s tax deduction for union dues. Union membership raises earnings and improves employment protection for native workers, while the private returns for non-Western immigrants are substantially smaller and often close to zero. Complementary survey evidence suggests that this gap is not explained by differences in information, preferences, or engagement with unions: immigrants receive similar information when joining, report similar preferences over job amenities, and are more likely than natives to seek union assistance. Instead, the combined administrative and survey evidence is consistent with differences in union-side behaviour. Immigrants report lower satisfaction after contacting unions for support and are more likely to believe that native workers and those with strong local networks receive greater benefits from membership. The impact is most pronounced in concentrated labour markets, indicating that relying on unions to address monopsony-based market failures may unintentionally amplify group inequalities.

title: Behavior Uncertainty Aware Operational Planning for Multi‐Resource Virtual Power Plant in Balancing Market
abstract: ABSTRACT Aggregators in balancing markets operate Virtual Power Plants (VPPs) by integrating distributed energy resources like batteries, electric vehicles (EVs), and heat pump water heaters (HPs) installed in low‐voltage households. A key challenge is managing user behavior uncertainty both in day‐ahead bidding and real‐time operation. This paper proposes a hierarchical planning framework using probabilistic scenario forecasting, two‐stage stochastic programming, and model predictive control (MPC). Day‐ahead bidding optimizes demand response (DR) capacity and resource schedules using two‐stage stochastic programming under behavior uncertainty, while real‐time MPC ensures commitment fulfillment. By explicitly linking scenario‐based bidding with receding‐horizon control, the framework increases bidding aggressiveness without compromising EV charging and hot‐water availability. Evaluation with 30 households over 150 days shows the proposed method reduces net electricity cost by 14.1% and increases offered down‐DR volume by 1.6 times compared to the robust method, while achieving a 98.69% DR fulfillment rate and limiting EV energy shortage and HP hot water shortage to 1.0% and 0.61%, respectively.

title: The Concept of Electricity and Magnetism in Central Europe in the Eighteenth Century as Presented in Physics by Martin Krúzi
Benchmarking Copula-Based Scenario Models and Risk Criteria for Multi-Market BESS Scheduling in the Greek Electricity Market
abstract: This study presents an observed-day-ahead computational benchmark comparing Gaussian, Student-t, first-tree-truncated Gaussian D-vine, and single-parameter Clayton scenarios under expected-value (EV), lower-tail conditional value-at-risk (CVaR), and finite-scenario maximin scheduling of a 20 MWh/10 MW battery in the Greek electricity market. The day-ahead trajectory is fixed, and recourse decisions use complete daily scenarios. An 84-day experiment provides descriptive economic comparisons at finite solver gaps. An additional twelve-date assessment yields 67 accepted solutions out of 144, without a common accepted date across all four copulas under EV or CVaR. Independent recalculation verifies seven accepted EV–CVaR pairs with sampled lower-tail mean increases of EUR 0.17–10.40/day. These changes are interpreted descriptively in view of their magnitude relative to the objective gaps. Full-training D-vine ordering reproduces the historical chain for the supplied input. Source reconciliation identifies first-quarter-hour selection and a one-hour balancing-series offset across 5040 nominal rows in the exact workbook used by the additional experiment. The comparisons are conditional on this representation and assumed balancing-opportunity bounds; the retained records leave uncertainty about the source units and battery-specific interpretation. The study integrates dependence diagn…

title: The Mediating Role of AI Readiness in the Relationship Between the Knowledge Economy and Labour Market Resilience
abstract: Advances in artificial intelligence technologies have made countries’ capacity to develop, adopt and effectively utilise these technologies increasingly important. This study examines the relationships between the Knowledge Economy, Artificial Intelligence Readiness and Labour Market Resilience, with a particular focus on the indirect role of Artificial Intelligence Readiness. The analysis combines data from the Global Knowledge Index (GKI) 2025, the Government Artificial Intelligence Readiness Index 2025 and the Global Labour Resilience Index (GLRI) 2025 for a cross-sectional sample comprising 112 countries. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) was used to evaluate the proposed relationships. The findings indicate that the Knowledge Economy is positively related to Artificial Intelligence Readiness (β = 0.789, p < 0.001) and Labour Market Resilience (β = 0.533, p < 0.001); and that Artificial Intelligence Readiness is also positively related to Labour Market Resilience (β = 0.453, p < 0.001). The indirect relationship between the Knowledge Economy and Labour Market Resilience, mediated by Artificial Intelligence Readiness, is positive and statistically significant (β = 0.357, p < 0.001; 95% bootstrap CI [0.191; 0.484]) and the VAF value is 40.1 per cent. The model explains 62.2 per cent of the variance in AI Readiness and 87.1 per cent of t…

title: Market dynamics before and after a recession announcement: Evidence from the banking sector
abstract: This study examines the reaction of the Indonesian capital market, with a particular focus on the banking sector, to the official announcement of Indonesia’s economic recession on November 5, 2020, which followed the economic downturn triggered by the COVID-19 pandemic. The research investigates whether this macroeconomic announcement contained informational value that influenced investor behavior as reflected in abnormal returns and trading volume activity. Using an event study methodology, the analysis applies a market model with a 30-day estimation period and a 15-day event window to banking companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX). The empirical results indicate no statistically significant differences in either abnormal returns or trading volume activity before and after the recession announcement. These findings suggest that the recession announcement did not generate a strong market reaction, implying that the information had been largely anticipated by investors and already incorporated into stock prices. This outcome is consistent with the semi-strong form of market efficiency (Jogiyanto, 2008; Yulianti et al., 2022). The study contributes to the literature on market efficiency and crisis-related event studies by providing empirical evidence from an emerging market, specifically Indonesia’s banking sector.
venue: Risk Governance and Control Financial Markets & Institutions

title: On-Premises Question Answering for Turkish IT Service Management Tickets: Synthetic Data Generation, QLoRA Fine-Tuning, and NPU-Accelerated Inference—A Preliminary Feasibility Study
abstract: Enterprise information technology (IT) service management (ITSM) requires accurate Turkish-language responses while limiting exposure of sensitive support records. This preliminary feasibility study presents a local, on-premises question-answering workflow that integrates synthetic data generation, quantized low-rank adaptation (QLoRA), multi-method evaluation, and neural processing unit (NPU) inference. From 149,674 IT support records, a local qwen2.5-coder:32b teacher model generated 48,876 question–answer pairs passing automated filters; 48,757 were retained after formatting. The v2 corpus contained more numbered steps (88.7% versus 6.7%) and specific commands (62.5% versus 0.5%) than v1; these descriptive comparisons did not control for experimental generation conditions. Qwen2.5-7B and Qwen2.5-3B were fine-tuned using ticket-grouped training and validation splits to prevent source-ticket overlap. On a ten-scenario benchmark under greedy decoding (without sampling), ROUGE-1 rose from 0.2603 to 0.3763 for the 7B model and from 0.2048 to 0.4010 for the 3B model after fine-tuning. On a 30-question evaluation set (10 benchmark scenarios and 20 validation records), mean G-Eval scores under a shared local judge were 3.78 and 3.76, and pairwise Arena comparisons favored 7B in 15 cases and 3B in 10, with five ties. Following conversion to OpenVINO INT4, single post-warm-up measurem…

title: Self-supervised learning for inflammatory response pattern recognition in physical education and exercise interventions
abstract: This study proposes PhysicalForwardPersistent, a self-supervised learning framework for recognizing inflammatory-response patterns associated with physical education and exercise interventions. The method operates on structured multivariate physiological sequences containing inflammation-related biomarkers, physiological measurements, and exercise descriptors, separating label-free representation learning from labeled downstream evaluation. PhysicalForwardPersistent integrates three components: a Physical Consistency Encoder that learns stable representations under physiologically admissible perturbations, a Forward Consistency Projector that models temporal latent-state evolution, and a Persistent Relation Extractor that preserves stable relationships among physiological profiles. The framework was evaluated on four datasets: the Physical Activity Inflammation Response Dataset, Exercise Induced Cytokine Patterns Dataset, Self-Supervised Learning Inflammation Dataset, and Physical Education Intervention Biomarker Dataset. These datasets include approximately 1,000 participants and 8,000 physiological samples, with 14–24 input variables and 2–5 temporal observations per sequence. Using participant-level separation and repeated runs, PhysicalForwardPersistent achieved accuracies of 89.23%-90.23% and macro-F1 scores of 88.34%-89.34%. Compared with the strongest baseline, it improv…

title: A tumor stemness-based prognostic model derived from single-cell and bulk transcriptomics predicts survival and therapeutic response in hepatocellular carcinoma
abstract: Abstract Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is characterized by marked intratumoral heterogeneity, therapeutic resistance, and poor prognosis, in which cancer stemness plays an important role. This study aimed to develop and validate a stemness-related prognostic model and to investigate its biological and therapeutic relevance in HCC. Single-cell RNA sequencing and bulk transcriptomic data were integrated to characterize stemness-associated tumor heterogeneity. CytoTRACE analysis identified a stemness-enriched epithelial subpopulation, and a seven-gene tumor stemness-related signature (TSCMS) was subsequently constructed using LASSO-Cox regression. The model was validated across four independent external cohorts and showed favorable prognostic discrimination. High-risk tumors were characterized by activation of oncogenic and stemness-associated pathways, a higher frequency of TP53 mutations, and an immunosuppressive microenvironment. CellChat analysis further revealed extensive predicted bidirectional communication between the stemness-enriched Epi1 subpopulation and immune cells, prominently involving MIF signaling from Epi1 and VISFATIN/NAMPT signaling from immune populations. TSCMS was also associated with differential anti-PD-1 response and predicted oxaliplatin sensitivity. Further functional validation confirmed that ENO1 knockdown reduced colony formation, migration, sphere…

title: Dose-response effects of sonified movement instability on perceptual-motor regulation in ballet dancers with body image vulnerability
abstract: Abstract Human sensorimotor control relies on detecting and regulating subtle movement fluctuations. Sonification, mapping these fluctuations into sound, makes normally imperceptible micro-instabilities accessible and supports real-time perceptual–motor regulation. However, it remains unclear how much feedback is beneficial, for whom, and under what conditions. In particular, body-image-related vulnerability may influence responses to such feedback. This study examined how different rates of auditory feedback on movement instability, treated as doses of sonification, affect perceptual–motor regulation in young adult ballet dancers classified into exploratory Low- and High-Vulnerability profiles. Twenty-two participants performed a standardized ballet sequence under three conditions: Active Control (ambience-only), Low-rate sonification (+2 SD threshold in changes in jerk), and High-rate sonification (+1 SD threshold). Micro-instabilities were detected in real time. Outcomes combined subjective measures of body experience (awareness, control, flexibility, and lightness) with objective measures of elbow-level movement instability (Instability Frequency and Cumulative Instability Duration). Results showed systematic differences across the tested feedback-density conditions. Low-rate sonification was generally associated with more favorable subjective body-experience ratings and lo…

title: Cementation-Controlled Mechanical Response and Failure Evolution of Naturally Fractured Dolomite
abstract: Reservoirs containing cemented natural fractures are widely developed in deep subsalt formations and play an important role in controlling rock mechanical behavior and failure evolution. However, the influence of fracture cementation on strength degradation, deformation response, and failure mode remains insufficiently understood, limiting the mechanical basis for evaluating hydraulic fracturing behavior in fractured dolomite reservoirs. A laboratory experimental framework is established to investigate the mechanical effects of cemented natural fractures in Cambrian subsalt dolomite from the Tarim Basin. CT scanning is used to characterize pore structure, fracture distribution, and cementation features of the samples. Based on these observations, Brazilian splitting tests and triaxial compression tests under a confining pressure of 40 MPa are conducted to analyze tensile strength, compressive strength, deformation characteristics, pore structure evolution, and failure modes under different cementation conditions. The results show that cemented natural fractures significantly weaken the tensile resistance of dolomite, and failure during Brazilian splitting mainly occurs along pre-existing fracture interfaces. Under triaxial compression, well-cemented samples exhibit limited porosity increase and relatively stable mechanical responses, whereas poorly cemented or heterogeneously c…

title: FORAGE YIELD AND SILAGE NUTRITIONAL QUALITY IN NATIVE AND HYBRID MAIZE (Zea mays L.): RESPONSE TO A SEEDING DENSITY GRADIENT
abstract: The livestock sector can utilize native maize (Zea mays L.) varieties as an alternative source of feed for livestock during the dry season. However, their capacity to withstand high planting densities has not been fully evaluated. The objective of this study was to evaluate the agronomic and forage performance, as well as the nutritional quality of silage produced from the native maize varieties Crema Carrillo Puerto and Criollo Tezonapa, compared with the hybrids HV-570, H-518, and Imparable, at planting densities of 15 625, 50 000, and 90 000 plants ha-1. Planting was established in a completely randomized block design with a split-plot arrangement and four replications. The variables evaluated included days to male (MF) and female (FF) flowering; leaf width (LW), length (LL), and number of leaves (NL); plant height (PH), stem diameter (SD), and green forage yield (GFY). In addition, the dry matter, moisture, ash, fat, fiber, protein, and nitrogen-free extract contents of the corn silage were calculated. Data were analyzed using the GLIMMIX procedure of SAS, and treatment means were compared using the least significant difference (LSD) test at α = 0.05. The native maize variety Crema Carrillo Puerto reached female flowering (FF) 76 d after sowing (DAS), whereas the hybrids reached FF at 64 DAS, 12 d earlier than the native maize varieties. At a density of 90 000 plants ha-1, …

title: Effectiveness of Minimum Support Price Policy for Oilseed Crops in Maharashtra, India
abstract: Minimum Support Price (MSP) is an agricultural price policy instrument intended to support farmers' price realisation and agricultural production. This study assessed the effectiveness of MSP for soybean, groundnut and sunflower in Maharashtra over 2014–15 to 2024–25. Using secondary data, compound annual growth rates and exponential trends were estimated for market arrivals and prices. Differences between market prices (MPs) and MSPs were examined, and multiple regression models were used to assess associations between production, MSP, MP and cultivated area. Soybean arrivals increased significantly by 7.76% annually, whereas groundnut arrivals declined by 4.75% and sunflower arrivals remained nearly unchanged, with growth of 0.03%. Market prices increased significantly for soybean (5.20%), groundnut (3.51%) and sunflower (5.72%) during the study period. Soybean market prices exceeded MSP in seven of the eleven years, compared with three years for groundnut. Sunflower market prices remained below MSP throughout the study period. Regression estimates indicated positive associations between MSP and production for soybean and groundnut at the 10% significance level, while the corresponding association was not statistically significant for sunflower. Cultivated area was positively associated with groundnut production at the 1% significance level and with sunflower production at th…

title: Cuando el bazo paga el precio: Infarto esplénico agudo, en la colitis ulcerosa aguda grave. (ASUC)
abstract: La enfermedad inflamatoria intestinal (EII) es un factor de riesgo independiente de tromboembolismo venoso y arterial, particularmente durante los brotes graves y la hospitalización. El infarto esplénico aislado, a diferencia de la trombosis venosa esplénica, es una manifestación excepcionalmente rara, reportada casi exclusivamente como casos aislados. En este contexto describimos el caso de una mujer de 29 años quien consulta en su debut de EII, con un episodio de colitis ulcerosa aguda grave (ASUC) que desarrolló infartos esplénicos múltiples a pesar de una profilaxis antitrombótica adecuada con HBPM, sin fuente cardioembólica, trombosis arterial o venosa demostrable, trombofilia hereditaria ni síndrome antifosfolípido. A partir de este caso, realizamos una revisión focalizada de la literatura sobre infarto esplénico y trombosis en la EII, y aplicamos el marco emergente de la trombo inflamación para explicar por qué la profilaxis estándar puede resultar insuficiente durante la actividad inflamatoria grave, junto con las recomendaciones vigentes de profilaxis antitrombótica con HBPM y anticoagulación terapéutica en pacientes hospitalizados con EII.

Assessing the Effects of Fuel Price Fluctuations on the Sustainability of Public Transport Operators in Lusaka, Zambia
abstract: The purpose of this study was to assess the effect of fuel price fluctuations on the sustainability of public transport operators in Lusaka. The study examined the impact of fuel price fluctuations on operational costs, revenue streams, and their influence on the sustainable growth of public transport services. The study worked with a sample size of 75 public transport operators, and the collected data were analyzed in Megastat software. The findings revealed that fuel price fluctuations caused an increase in operational costs, with 42.7% of the respondents reporting that fuel accounted for 20 – 40% of operational costs, while 29.3% indicated 41–60%. A statistically significant association between route type and fuel-related operating costs was confirmed by the chi-square analysis (X2 = 15.03, df = 3, p = 0.0018). Additionally, the study found that 43% reported a moderately high effect of fuel changes on revenue and 37% reported a significantly high effect. Regression analysis found a type of business statistically significant effect on revenue (β = 0.3331, p = .0172). The study further found that 36% of respondents reported a significant impact of fuel fluctuations on business strategy and 21.3% a very significant impact. The chi-square analysis shows a highly significant relationship between fuel price fluctuations and sustainable business growth (χ² = 62.20, df = 9, p < 0.00…

title: Dynamical Solar Wind Forecasting Using In Situ Solar Wind Speed Observations
abstract: Abstract Accurate prediction of the ambient solar wind at Earth is a key requirement for space‐weather forecasting but is limited by uncertainties in coronal boundary conditions and, to a lesser extent, heliospheric transport. We present a quantitative assessment of a solar wind forecast that uses near‐Earth in situ solar wind observations to estimate the inner boundary condition for the Heliospheric Upwind eXtrapolation with Time dependence (HUXt) model. In terms of the accuracy at Earth, this method is very similar to 27‐day recurrence forecasting. However, unlike 27‐day recurrence, it produces a solution throughout the heliosphere that can potentially be used to improve CME propagation estimates and forecasting at a range of near‐ecliptic heliospheric locations. To test this forecast method, daily hindcasts are generated over a 15‐year interval spanning 2008–2022. Performance is directly compared with forecasts generated by the standard operational forecast approach, namely Global Oscillations Network Group (GONG) magnetogram‐based estimates using the Wang–Sheeley–Arge (WSA) coronal model. The InSitu‐HUXt hindcasts achieve mean absolute error (MAE) in solar wind speed of 65 km for lead times up to 27 days. WSA‐HUXt hindcasts are most accurate around 4‐day lead time, with an MAE of around 85 km . More diagnostic metrics show that this is partly because InSitu‐HUXt naturally p…

title: Forecasting LLM‐Enabled Biorisk and the Efficacy of Safeguards
abstract: ABSTRACT Capabilities of large language models (LLMs) on several biological benchmarks have prompted not only excitement about their usefulness for research but also concern about biosecurity risks. We recruited 46 subject‐matter experts in biology and biosecurity, and 22 generalist forecasters to estimate the risks of growing LLM capabilities. Most respondents expected some hypothetical LLM capabilities to increase their estimates of risk and dramatically underestimated the rate of LLM progress in those capabilities. When these capabilities arose, the median forecast did update as anticipated. The median expert initially predicted a 0.3% annual risk of a human‐caused epidemic that causes 100,000 deaths. This estimate then rose to 1.5% conditional on several hypothetical LLM capabilities, including matching the performance of a top‐performing team of virologists on a virology troubleshooting test, which the median expert did not expect to occur until 2030. Given this finding, we conducted a baselining study and found that LLMs already crossed this performance threshold in April 2025. A follow‐up survey conducted after these results were available found that forecasters significantly updated their median unconditional risk estimates upward, with the new median expert forecast of annual risk rising to 1.5% (as anticipated by the earlier conditional forecasts). More encouragingly,…

title: AI-Based Demand Forecasting and an Intelligent Sustainable Inventory Model for Green Deteriorating Products
abstract: The increasing need for green products and the unpredictable nature of the market demands have posed serious challenges in dealing with deteriorating green products. Traditional inventory theories may not consider AI demand prediction, especially where demand varies. To solve this problem, this study formulates an intelligent sustainable inventory model using AI-based demand prediction for deteriorating green products. The model aims to determine optimal inventory policies by evaluating relevant inventory costs, including ordering, holding, and deterioration costs. AI-based forecasting predicts the demand needed for making inventory decisions. The effect of important variables on the efficiency of the model is investigated through numerical experiments and sensitivity analysis. The study also investigates the impact of demand forecasting, inventory, and deterioration losses. The proposed framework establishes an integrated approach to intelligent inventory planning by connecting AI-based demand prediction with sustainable inventory optimization. This is because it allows analysis of how better forecasts can help with replenishment, waste reduction, and efficiency. The current study makes a valuable contribution to green inventory management through integration of artificial intelligence-based forecasting into the optimal design of inventory for deteriorating items.

title: A Hybrid Mamba–GNN Framework For Spatio-Temporal Solar Irradiance Forecasting Using Sky Camera And Satellite Data Fusion
abstract: Solar irradiance forecasting is known to be one of the crucial issues in integrating the use of renewable energy sources into power grids. Solar energy is intermittent, and precise forecasts are crucial for grid stability and efficiency. At present, however, the methods used to forecast such events are often at odds with being able to capture the high-resolution local cloud dynamics and the synoptic scale atmospheric patterns that are present at the time of prediction, especially if computational efficiency is also important. To tackle these challenges, the proposed novel hybrid deep learning framework Mamba-GNN is introduced.For this purpose, a novel hybrid deep learning framework, named Mamba-GNN, is introduced to address these challenges. In this framework, a Vision State Space Model (Mamba) is used for processing high-frequency temporal sequences while a Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Network (ST-GNN) is used for modeling cloud propagation over the region using the sky camera images from the ground. A dynamic cross-attention mechanism is embedded, which is able to adaptively fuse these heterogeneous features. As illustrated in this paper, the Mamba-GNN is consistently better than ConvLSTM for different forecasting horizons, achieving a forecast skill of 0.85 for 10 min forecast and 0.55 for 3 hrs forecast. Both RMSE and MAE values are significantly decreased in particular in …

title: Comparative Benchmark of Metaheuristic and Model-Based Hyperparameter Optimization for Deep Learning Models in Global Solar Irradiance Forecasting
abstract: Deep learning solar forecasters depend strongly on their hyperparameters, yet comparisons of hyperparameter optimization methods usually rely on few runs per optimizer, confounding the optimizer with the random seed. A protocol is proposed that tests whether optimizers are practically equivalent and how reliable published comparison designs are. Seven methods (four metaheuristics, two model-based methods, one of them multi-fidelity, and Random Search) tuned three deep networks for one-hour-ahead forecasting of global horizontal irradiance in Querétaro, Mexico, with public reanalysis data, a shared search space, one hundred evaluations, and thirty paired seeds, in nine hundred and thirty runs across all experiments. The tuned models improved on smart persistence by 4–11% in mean absolute error. With the 10-epoch search objective, no pair of optimizers differed after Holm correction, 62 of 63 pairs were equivalent within 1 W/m2, and the optimizer explained 0.8% of the error variance, compared with 7.9% for the seed. In a higher-fidelity check with 50 epochs, two guided methods improved on Random Search by 0.74 W/m2, significantly for one of them, while remaining equivalent to each other, suggesting that, in this setting, objective fidelity mattered more than the choice among guided optimizers. In emulations of published designs, even with 30 runs, 2 studies agreed on the winner i…

title: Structure-Aware Reformulation of Physics-Informed Bayesian Inference for Wildfire Aerosol Forecasting on an Embedded GPU
abstract: The GOES-16 and GOES-17 satellites retrieve AOD every five minutes, so a smoke forecasting system must complete each cycle before the next observation arrives. We previously accelerated a Physics-Informed Bayesian State-Space model using datacenter GPUs to meet this requirement. However, datacenter hardware is impractical for remote field deployments, which require compact, low-power embedded modules. We therefore ported the GPU implementation to the NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano, where the initial implementation took 256 s to execute, leaving little operational margin within the 300 s cycle. A fully single-precision implementation failed because the covariance matrices lost positive definiteness, so double precision was retained. Therefore, additional performance gains must come from optimizing the underlying computations. The baseline implementation executes the statistical recursions directly, resulting in significant computational overhead from not exploiting the available mathematical structure. We optimize these operations by exploiting matrix sparsity, symmetry, and reusable intermediate terms, reducing the Jetson runtime from 256 to 110 s and achieving a 2.33× speedup. All modifications are exact mathematical reformulations rather than approximations, so the reported inferential and forecast quantities agree at the precision at which they are reported, with small floating-poi…

Multi-Step Load Forecasting with State-Guided Expert Routing for Energy Management Systems
abstract: Accurate load forecasting is crucial for operational planning and rolling decision-making in energy management systems (EMSs). However, the dynamic nature of temporal patterns and the inconsistent availability of covariates across the forecasting horizon complicate this task. While covariate-aware Transformer models distinguish between endogenous and exogenous inputs, their feed-forward modules typically employ homogeneous transformations across different operating conditions, and traditional Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) routing mechanisms usually rely solely on implicit token representations for decision-making. To address these limitations, we propose SA-TimeXer-MoHE, a scenario-aware TimeXer model with heterogeneous experts. First, the model partitions its inputs by forecast-time availability into the load target, historical-only measurements, deterministic future calendar variables, and operating-scenario covariates. Then, it replaces the homogeneous feed-forward module with MLP, depthwise-convolution, drift, and residual experts and conditions sparse Top-K routing jointly on token representations and nine EMS scenario variables. On a real EMS dataset, the full model achieves reported mean MAE, RMSE, P95_AE, and Ramp_MAE values that are 7.4%, 5.7%, 4.0%, and 6.0% lower, respectively, than those of TimeXer across 1, 2, 4, and 8 h forecasting horizons. These results highlight the…

title: Global prevalence of Salmonella spp. and Escherichia coli in reptile taxa: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Background Reservoirs of zoonotic agents have been well-described in reptiles; however, global consensus across reptile taxa is lacking. In this systematic review and meta-analysis, the global prevalence of Salmonella spp. and Escherichia coli were estimated in reptiles to provide an overview of their occurrence and potential public health relevance. Methods The Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines were adhered to. Five online databases PubMed, Scopus, ScienceDirect, Google Scholar, and Medline were thoroughly searched to conduct meta-analyses. Data on prevalence were pooled using the random-effects model and heterogeneity was quantified using I 2 statistics to ensure robustness of the data. Further, the publication bias was carefully assessed by Egger’s linear regression and Begg’s rank correlation tests. Results The pooled prevalence of Salmonella spp. and Escherichia coli was examined using Comprehensive Meta-Analyses software v4.0. A total of 189 studies met the criteria for inclusion in this meta-analysis. Across these studies, a combined total of 24,152 specimens were assessed, resulting in the evaluation of 5,046 E. coli and Salmonella spp. isolates. The overall pooled prevalence of E. coli and Salmonella spp. was 25.1% (95% CI: 18.9–32.5%) and 33.3% (95% CI: 29.3–37.5%), respectively. Lizards exhibited the highest pooled…

title: Physicochemically Motivated Decomposition for Long-Sequence Urban O<sub>3</sub> Forecasting: A Cross-Method Comparison
abstract: Surface ozone (O3) forms via nonlinear chemistry and is highly non-stationary, complicating 168-h forecasts. Many models omit key physical drivers, mix time scales, and degrade quickly with lead time. We propose a decomposition-ensemble framework that fuses surface observations with NWP predictors (e.g., solar radiation, PBL height). To prevent data leakage, decomposition (STL, GAM, CEEMDAN, VMD) was performed exclusively on the training and validation data to isolate the annual, diurnal, and residual components. We then train LSTM and Transformer models on each component using both direct and incremental (ΔY) learning. Across Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, and Chengdu, decomposition lowers the error bound and curbs horizon-wise error growth. Among the tested strategies, VMD (K = 2) and period-based merging (for CEEMDAN) robustly isolate the 24-h diurnal mode, limit cross-scale leakage, and provide the best balance of separability, interpretability, and forecast skill. The results further reveal pronounced heterogeneity in optimal model architectures across temporal scales and city-specific regimes, indicating that a single universal model is insufficient to jointly optimize short-term accuracy and long-term stability. Overall, this study provides a scenario-adaptive forecasting paradigm that offers practical guidance for O3 pollution early wa…

An AI-Assisted Workflow for Tea Product Discrimination and Moisture Prediction Using Portable NIR Spectroscopy
abstract: Portable near-infrared (NIR) spectrometers enable rapid tea analysis, but the heterogeneity of tea leaves can reduce spectral representativeness and modelling reliability. This study evaluated the influence of sampling configurations on tea product discrimination and moisture prediction using two portable NIR spectrometers and developed a domain-specific NIR-analysis skill to support the analytical workflow. Ten tea products were analysed in ground and unground states using the NIR-R210 and NeoSpectra Scanner. Sixteen preprocessing methods were evaluated with partial least squares and support vector machine models. Classification and regression models were selected using stratified four-fold and leave-one-product-out cross-validation, respectively. Within the investigated product and batch range, the NeoSpectra Scanner achieved 100% classification accuracy for both sample states in validation, whereas the NIR-R210 achieved 100% and 92.5%, respectively. Support vector regression achieved the best moisture-prediction validation performance for unground NeoSpectra Scanner samples (R2 = 0.95; RMSEP = 0.330%). External validation showed decreased performance, particularly for unground NIR-R210 samples (classification accuracy, 80.0%; R2 = 0.68; RMSEP = 0.797%). Grinding reduced spectral variability, particularly for the NIR-R210, while the NeoSpectra Scanner’s rotating sampling conf…

title: In Silico Prediction of a Divergent Candidate FII-Related Replicon Among the Serratia Plasmid Lineage
abstract: The replication region, replicon, is the most important module of plasmids that controls their replication and consequently their existence. Currently, a large number of replicon types with different architectures have been characterized, serving as a basis for plasmid classification and replicon typing. Despite ongoing research to characterize the replicative apparatus of plasmids, they remain unidentified by the replication system. Fifty replicons were studied in Serratia bacterial plasmids that were untypable or showed contradictory identification results by the replication system. These replicons shared a possibly new gene for the replication initiation protein repA. But a varying arrangement of the copA and copB genes typical of the FII and FIC replicons was observed. Comparative genomic and phylogenetic analysis revealed new insights into their possible evolution from the FII type. Based on these results, we propose a divergent candidate FII-related replicon type among Serratia plasmids. The obtained findings are discussed through the prism of the two phases of evolution’s general model. The results provide new insights into plasmid classification by replication system, plasmid replicons evolution, and bacterial plasmid typing.

title: PERFORMANCE EVALUATION AND MACHINE LEARNING-ASSISTED PREDICTION OF A HYBRID BIOCHAR–ZEOLITE COLUMN REACTOR FOR TURBIDITY AND IRON REMOVAL FROM TROPICAL RIVER WATER
abstract: High turbidity and elevated dissolved iron are the two most persistent water quality problems facing tropical river communities in Kalimantan, Indonesia, where both parameters regularly exceed the limits set by the WHO. We investigated how well a continuous-flow hybrid biochar–zeolite column reactor could remove turbidity and dissolved iron at the same time, working through 100 controlled experimental runs using synthetic river water. Three operating variables were tested—influent turbidity (50, 150, and 300 NTU), hydraulic loading rate (0.3, 0.5, and 0.8 L min⁻¹)—and biochar-to-zeolite ratio (0.5:1, 1:1, and 2:1)—arranged in a factorial design. Iron adsorption equilibrium was described by Langmuir (qmax = 18.5 mg g⁻¹; KL = 0.62 L mg⁻¹; R² = 0.961) and Freundlich (Kf = 6.2 mg g⁻¹; n = 2.1; R² = 0.943) isotherms, and breakthrough dynamics were described by the Thomas kinetic model. Mean turbidity removal efficiency was 83.93 ± 5.10% (range: 74.52–93.18%) and mean iron removal efficiency was 72.06 ± 7.05% (range: 55.83–85.71%). Among all variables tested, hydraulic loading rate had by far the greatest influence, showing a strong inverse relationship with turbidity removal (r = −0.919) and iron removal (r = −0.848; both p < 0.001). Data-driven prediction of compressive strength in rice husk ash concrete using machine learning for sustainable construction
abstract: Abstract Rice husk ash (RHA) has the potential to partially replace ordinary Portland cement and increase the sustainability of concrete production, but optimizing the compressive strength of RHA concrete is challenging due to the complexity of interplay between mix-design and curing variables in the conventional laboratory approach which consumes a significant amount of time and resources. The present study is an attempt to propose an interpretable machine-learning model for predicting the compressive strength based on 9 input variables obtained from published experimental studies, such as RHA replacement, water-to-cement (W/C) ratio, curing time, aggregate size, superplasticizer dosage, cement content, fine aggregate content, coarse aggregate content and water content. The target variable is taken as the compressive strength. The four increasingly challenging validation scenarios included five regression algorithms: Linear Regression (LR), Decision Tree (DT), Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM) and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN). GridSearchCV using 5 fold cross validation was used to optimize Hyperparameters. SVM had the best performance in the final optimized comparison with R² = 0.875641, RMSE = 5.919637 MPa and MAE = 4.813035 MPa, whereas RF showed almost similar performance with R 2 = 0.860683 and also lower MAPE value. Curing time and W/C ratio were found to be i…

title: Revealing nonlinear and interaction mechanisms of resource and environmental carrying capacity through explainable machine learning
abstract: Existing studies on resource and environmental carrying capacity (RECC) have primarily focused on comprehensive evaluation and linear identification. But the quantification of driving effect on RECC have not been fully explored, especially the interaction and nonlinear effects. Therefore, this paper constructs an explainable machine learning framework, to comprehensively assess the RECC index of 31 provincial regions in China and to reveal nonlinear and interaction mechanisms of influence factors. Firstly, the XGBoost model is utilized to surrogate the evaluation results, which demonstrates outstanding predictive performance (R 2 = 0.95, RMSE = 0.08) and stability. The results shows that the average RECC index in China dropping from 1.18 to 0.39, marking a transition from a high-risk state to a safe and sustainable state. Then, the SHAP model quantifies the nonlinear and threshold effects of key influence factors. The results indicate that the total emissions of pollutants in wastewater ( X 2 ) and industrial sulfur dioxide emissions ( X 3 ) are the two most critical factors, with a cumulative contribution rate of 49%. 50000 tons is a threshold for X 2 , beyond which the RECC index significantly increases with the increase of X 2 . 10 billion cubic meters is the marginal contribution of X 3 , with the greatest impact on RECC index. Pharmacist-led redesign of chemotherapy delivery and supportive care: effects on infusion capacity, aseptic workload, costs and resource stewardship in oncology practice
abstract: Introduction Medication-related processes in oncology are complex and resource intensive, creating opportunities for treatment delays, preparation burden, medication errors, and inefficient resource utilization. Pharmacist-led interventions have been associated with improvements in medication safety, efficiency, and costs, yet evidence evaluating their system-wide impact remains limited. This study evaluated an integrated pharmacist-led, multidisciplinary redesign of medication-use processes encompassing supportive medications, infusion administration, and drug preparation in a tertiary oncology center. Materials and methods We performed a retrospective analysis of routinely collected administration data from January to June 2023. Baseline practice (3,750 administrations) was compared with a modelled full-implementation scenario. Scheduled administration time (SAT) was used as an operational measure of infusion-unit resource use. Aseptic workload, direct acquisition costs, and assessed single-use consumable waste were estimated using prespecified model rules, measured unit weights, and 2023 institutional acquisition prices. A pragmatic February 2026 substudy compared current SAT with real administration time, reconstructed baseline equivalent SAT, and modelled full-implementation SAT. title: Top-Down Electron Detachment Dissociation at ∼15–92 eV and 9.4 T with High Space Charge Capacity FT-ICR Cells
abstract: Abstract Top-down mass spectrometry (TD-MS) allows detailed characterization of biomolecular heterogeneity, e.g., sequence variants, chemical and biological modifications, and mutations. While relatively established in positive-ion mode, negative-ion-mode TD-MS of intact proteins has been less explored, in part due to a lack of suitable activation approaches for tandem mass spectrometry. Here, we show that electron detachment dissociation (EDD) can yield analytically useful sequence coverage up to ∼60% for β-casein (24 kDa), with relatively straightforward spectral interpretation due to favored formation of a• and x-type fragments with limited neutral loss. This leap in EDD performance from previously reported 5% sequence coverage was enabled by use of a custom wide-bore 9.4 T FT-ICR instrument with a solid dispenser cathode for optimal anion-electron overlap. In addition, a prototype─now commercially available─instrument with a dynamically harmonized ICR cell and a hollow cathode yielded 51% sequence coverage for β-casein, more than an order of magnitude higher than previous reports. EDD of phosphorylated α- and β-casein proteins showed phosphate retention in fragment ions and allowed phosphorylation site determination. title: Feeling the body politic: Interoception as a mechanism of political stress resilience
abstract: Abstract Politics can substantially harm physical and mental health, especially in polarized contexts, making political polarization a major non‐medical cause of disease and suffering. We examined whether citizens can protect their health without undermining civic engagement. Across three studies with over 2000 participants during the 2022 U.S. midterms and 2024 presidential election, we show that interoceptive sensibility, that is, the ability to perceive and trust one's internal bodily signals, protects against politics' adverse health effects. Higher interoceptive sensibility consistently predicted lower emotional, physical, behavioral, and social health costs, controlling for political identity, demographics, and emotion regulation. During the charged 2024 election, it further predicted fewer negative emotions, more hope for the future, and less fear, particularly when their candidate lost. Interoceptive sensibility also correlated with political engagement and efficacy, suggesting it enhances rather than inhibits participation. Our findings highlight it as a promising trait for mitigating political stress without reducing civic involvement.

Efficacy and Mechanism of Transcutaneous Auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation in Patients With Poststroke Dysphagia: Protocol for a Randomized, Sham-Controlled Clinical Trial
abstract: Abstract Background Dysphagia is a common complication following stroke. While current management strategies for poststroke dysphagia (PSD) range from nutritional support to neurostimulation techniques, an optimal treatment regimen remains elusive. As a promising noninvasive neuromodulation approach, transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) requires further validation in rigorously designed trials to establish robust evidence of its efficacy and mechanisms of action. Objective This study aims to validate the efficacy of taVNS in treating PSD and to elucidate its underlying mechanisms, thereby supporting the development of a novel, noninvasive therapeutic strategy for improving swallowing function in stroke survivors. Methods This study will use a prospective, randomized, double-blind, controlled trial design. A total of 40 patients with PSD will be enrolled and randomly allocated to either a taVNS group or a sham taVNS group. Both groups will receive conventional swallowing rehabilitation therapy as the baseline intervention. The taVNS group will receive bilateral electrical stimulation at the cymba conchae and cavum conchae of the auricle. These sites correspond to the “Heart” and “Kidney” auricular acupoints, selected in accordance with traditional Chinese medicine theory. title: Study on synthesis, growth mechanism, and optoelectronic properties of SnZrS3 semiconductor
abstract: Abstract SnZrS3 is a promising but underexplored chalcogenide semiconductor for optoelectronic applications. Herein, we report a two-step solid-state route in which a highly crystalline ZrS2 intermediate, pre-formed in the first step, reacts with SnS at 600 °C in the second step. Systematic optimization identifies 600 °C, 6 h, and a 1:1 precursor ratio as the optimal conditions. The growth mechanism is elucidated as a template-induced topological transformation in which the morphology of the final SnZrS3 product is inherited from the ZrS2 precursor. DFT calculations reveal an indirect band gap of 1.08 eV, with the valence band edge dominated by S 3p states and the conduction band edge contributed by Zr 4d and Sn 5p states. UV–Vis spectroscopy gives an experimental optical band gap of 1.15 eV, in excellent agreement with the calculated optical band gap 1.14 eV. Raman spectroscopy combined with DFPT calculations identifies the characteristic Ag modes at 158.6 and 330.8 cm-1, assigned to in-plane Sn–S and Zr–S stretching vibrations. These results establish a controllable synthesis route and provide a combined experimental and theoretical understanding of SnZrS3 for photovoltaic and optoelectronic applications.

title: Microcosm evaluation of saturation and labile carbon controls on nitrate persistence in vadose zone soils
abstract: Groundwater table recovery increases water saturation in the lower vadose zone, altering nitrate persistence. To clarify how soil properties and substrate availability modulate these dynamics, two microcosm experiments compared static water-filled pore space levels (50%, 80%, and 100%) and various nutrient additions in a Beijing soil profile. Between days 1 and 45, nitrate remained stable at 50% WFPS but declined by 39.15%~53.52% at 100% WFPS, with the largest reduction in the deepest soil due to higher initial organic carbon. Glucose addition enhanced the 45-day decline to 85.30% by inducing reducing conditions (-89 mV) within the first 15 days. In contrast, ammonium inputs persisted as the dominant dissolved form, while glycine triggered a sequential cascade marked by organic nitrogen decrease and transient ammonium, nitrite, and nitrate peaks. Day 45 sequencing confirmed that glucose and glycine shifted bacterial structures and gene profiles. Although gaseous measurements or isotope tracing are required to resolve specific pathways, these findings demonstrate that labile carbon governs the extent of nitrate decline under high saturation, while substrate composition shapes inorganic nitrogen accumulation timing.

title: Long-Term Trends and Nonlinear PM2.5–O3 Coupling in a Typical Oilfield City of the “2 + 26” Region
abstract: Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) and ozone (O3) are the two dominant air pollutants in China, yet their coupling relationship at the daily urban scale remains debated because observational correlations are often confounded by meteorology. This study investigates the nonlinear PM2.5–O3 relationship in Puyang, a typical oil and gas industrial city in the “2 + 26” region, using daily observations from 2015 to 2025. A set of progressively nested generalized additive models were constructed, adding meteorological factors and NO2 sequentially, followed by humidity and season interaction terms. Stratified correlation analyses revealed a concentration-stratified reversal: positive in the low-concentration segment (<35 μg·m−3; r = 0.271) and negative in the mid (35–75 μg·m−3; r = −0.208) and high (>75 μg·m−3; r = −0.313) segments. After controlling for meteorology and NO2, however, the conditional partial effect increased over most of the PM2.5 range, indicating that the uncontrolled negative correlation largely disappeared after controlling for meteorology. Humidity exerted a significant conditional modulating effect (p < 0.001), whereas seasonal modulation was concentrated in autumn (p < 0.001).
