title: Electrocatalytic oxidation and determination of hydrazine at the surface of dioxo-molybdenum(VI) complex-NiFe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub> nanoparticle-modified carbon paste electrode
abstract: NiFe2O4 nanoparticles and a dioxo-molybdenum(VI) complex were used to create a modified carbon paste electrode (Mo/NFO/CPE) and investigate the electrocatalytic oxidation of hydrazine (HZN) on its surface. By catalytically reducing the anodic overpotential, the Mo/NFO/CPE significantly improved the kinetics of HZN electrooxidation. Using a variety of electrochemical techniques, the mechanism of HZN electrochemical behaviour at Mo/NFO/CPE surface was examined. The developed modified electrode demonstrated highly sensitive voltammetric responses for HZN, which makes it ideal for detecting HZN at trace levels. In pH 7.0 buffered solution, a linear dynamic range of 0.1 to 350.0 µM and a detection limit of 0.07 µM were found for HZN.
venue: Journal of Electrochemical Science and Engineering

title: Impact of fault aperture variation on induced seismicity at the VITO geothermal site
abstract: Abstract Mitigating induced seismicity remains a major challenge for geothermal reservoir stimulation. At the VITO geothermal site in Belgium, operations have induced seismic events with moment magnitudes up to M W 2.0 within the fractured Dinantian limestone reservoir. Numerical models are commonly used to forecast and reassess seismic hazard during fluid injection, supporting operational strategies to reduce the likelihood of larger seismic events. In modeling studies, fault behavior is often simplified by assuming a constant aperture to reduce computational costs. This study investigates the influence of different stress- and slip-dependent fault aperture variation laws on the simulated seismic response and examines the mechanisms driving the resulting differences in seismicity by comparing three aperture formulations: (1) constant aperture, (2) aperture dependent on effective normal stress, and (3) aperture dependent on both effective normal stress and slip displacement. Our results show that the effective normal stress dependent aperture law best reproduces the observed b -value at the VITO geothermal site. However, the model with fracture stiffness characteristics including dependencies on effective normal stress and slip displacement provides a more conservative estimate of the maximum moment magnitude and is less likely to underestimate the occurrence of larger seismic …

title: Dual Effects of Water on CO2 Adsorption in Silica Mesopores: Interfacial Promotion versus Volume-Limited Inhibition
abstract: Abstract Water is ubiquitous in natural and engineered porous media and plays a critical role in regulating CO2 adsorption in carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) systems. Previous studies report contradictory effects of water, ranging from suppression to enhancement of CO2 uptake, indicating that the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we investigate CO2 adsorption in silica mesopores with varying water contents using molecular simulations under thermodynamic conditions relevant to three typical CCUS scenarios. The results suggest two distinct adsorption regimes controlled by the thermodynamic state of CO2. Under gaseous conditions, CO2 uptake is governed by an interfacial-area-controlled regime and exhibits a pronounced nonmonotonic response to water content, with enhancement arising from abundant water interfacial area within low-density regions. In contrast, under supercritical conditions, CO2 uptake is governed by an accessible-volume-controlled regime and decreases monotonically with increasing water content. Similar trends are observed in both hydrophilic and hydrophobic pores, although the spatial distribution of water differs substantially between them. These findings provide molecular-scale insights into the contrasting effects of water on CO2 adsorption and may inform future investigations of water management in CO2 capture, mineral carbonation, an…

title: Performance optimization of an IoT ‐enabled vibratory double‐slope solar still with carbon aerogel‐impregnated carbon fiber felt and phase change material
abstract: Abstract Freshwater scarcity and the low productivity of conventional solar stills create a need for improved desalination systems that enhance freshwater production while enabling continuous monitoring. To address this limitation, an IoT‐enabled vibratory double‐slope solar still integrating carbon aerogel‐impregnated carbon fiber felt (CA‐CFF), phase change material (PCM), and vibration‐assisted heat transfer was developed and experimentally investigated. The IoT system enables real‐time monitoring of key thermal and operating parameters during desalination. The novelty lies in the combined integration of CA‐CFF for photothermal evaporation, PCM for thermal energy storage, vibration for enhanced water mixing and heat transfer, and IoT‐based monitoring within a single double‐slope solar still, together with systematic multi‐parameter optimization. Four operating parameters, namely vibration amplitude (0.25–1.00 mm), vibration frequency (10–25 Hz), PCM mass (0.5–2.0 kg), and basin water depth (10–40 mm), were optimized using a Taguchi L16 orthogonal array. ANOVA and multiple linear regression were used to evaluate parameter significance and predict performance. The optimum combination was A 4 –B 3 –C 4 –D 1 : 1.00 mm amplitude, 20 Hz frequency, 2.0 kg PCM, and 10 mm water depth. The experimental freshwater productivity reached 5600 mL/m 2 /day, compared with 5647.7 mL/m 2 /day …

title: Efficacy of guanidinoacetic acid supplementation in diets with various energy contents on growth performance, intestinal morphology, serum biochemical parameters and antioxidant status of broilers under dexamethasone-induced oxidative stress
Beyond the Energy Vector: Siting Green Methanol and Ammonia Through Social Multi-Criteria Evaluation—The Spanish Case
abstract: Renewable hydrogen derivatives—green methanol and green ammonia—are central to European industrial decarbonization, energy sovereignty and low-carbon transport, shipping in particular, yet decisions on where to site their production are driven by techno-economic criteria alone, sidelining social and territorial impacts. We ask where in Spain these derivatives should be produced when social need is placed at the centre of the decision. Using Social Multi-Criteria Evaluation, operationalized through the European Commission’s SOCRATES tool, we rank the 50 Spanish provinces across four dimensions—technical, economic, social and human capital—from 17–19 public criteria aggregated with a non-compensatory Kemeny rule, and compare two scenarios (methanol and ammonia) tested by local and global weight-sensitivity analyses. Giving the social dimension an explicit, high weight shifts the geography obtained under the adopted weighting toward the south and interior. A weight-robust core—Murcia, Zaragoza, Asturias and an Andalusian arc—ranks highly for both derivatives, whereas the scenario leaders (Huelva for methanol, Sevilla for ammonia) are weight-dependent; within the present analytical framework, capturable CO2 is the factor that differentiates the two geographies. The ranking should be read as just-transition priority under the adopted weighting—distinct from engineering feasibility a…

title: AI-Driven Secure Channel Estimation and Energy-Efficient Power Allocation for Cell-Free Massive MIMO
abstract: Cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) improves user fairness by allowing many distributed access points (APs) to cooperatively serve users without fixed cell boundaries. Its practical reliability, however, is limited by pilot contamination, pilot spoofing, channel state-information (CSI) uncertainty, inter-user interference, and inefficient power consumption. This paper proposes an AI-driven secure channel estimation and energy-efficient power allocation (AI-SCE-EEPA) framework for uplink cell-free massive MIMO. The AI component is a lightweight supervised anomaly classifier trained on synthetically generated pilot observations representing clean and spoofed contaminated CSI conditions. Its output is used as a soft reliability gate before minimum mean-square error (MMSE) channel refinement. The refined secure CSI is then used by an adaptive regularized MMSE receiver and an energy-efficient power allocation rule. A reproducible Monte Carlo simulation is conducted under distributed APs, Rayleigh fading, large-scale path loss, log-normal shadowing, QPSK transmission, pilot contamination, and active pilot spoofing/eavesdropping stress. The proposed framework is compared with MR, conventional LMMSE, and adaptive R-MMSE baselines using bit error rate (BER), normalized mean-square error (NMSE), spectral efficiency (SE), energy efficiency (EE), secrecy rate, and power…

title: Mitigation of aflatoxin contamination in raw and roasted cashew nuts using gamma irradiation and storage conditions
In Situ Dense Interfacial Barrier via Tailored CA 6 Gradation and Si Doping for Durable Li‐Ion Battery Saggars
abstract: ABSTRACT Severe saggar corrosion by cathode materials hinders the sustainable production of lithium‐ion batteries. Herein, high‐performance refractory saggars were fabricated via high‐temperature reconstruction using waste high‐voltage porcelain insulators as the main raw material, combined with other solid wastes and mineral additives to form a dense mullite–corundum matrix. A physical–chemical synergistic strategy was adopted by optimizing calcium hexa‐aluminate (CA 6 ) particle‐size gradation and Si powder addition. At an optimal coarse‐to‐fine CA 6 ratio of 5:15, a stable interlocking skeleton was formed, reducing open pores and enhancing matrix packing density. Meanwhile, 2 wt% Si enabled in situ modification through oxidation‐derived liquid SiO 2 filling and mullitization‐induced micro‐expansion, effectively sealing residual micro‐ and nanoscale pores. Consequently, the apparent porosity decreased below 1% while maintaining high mechanical strength and thermal shock resistance. During service, the refined matrix forms a liquid–solid double interfacial barrier: high‐viscosity lithium silicate glass immobilizes Li + , while a compact β‐eucryptite layer blocks Li 2 O inward diffusion. This work offers a low‐cost route for long‐life refractory saggars and high‐value solid‐waste utilization.
venue: Journal of the American Ceramic Society

title: Enhancing Performance of SrCO₃-Based Materials for High-Temperature Thermochemical Energy Storage With Advanced Additives
abstract: Thermochemical energy storage (TCES) is an emerging technology that aims to improve efficiency of high-temperature Concentrated Solar Power (CSP) systems. At the same time, the pool of materials for TCES at T = 900-1200oC remains very limited mainly due to poor cyclic stability. This work addresses the performance and cyclic stability of new SrCO3-based composites with CaCO3, Li2CO3, SnO2, MgAl2O4, and SnAl2O5. The composites were prepared by mechanical mixing and sol-gel methods, characterized by XRD analysis and tested under cycling at 1200 °C (decarbonation) and 900 °C (carbonation) by using TGA and DSC. The incorporation of additives generally improved cycling stability compared to pure SrCO3, although the effect on effective conversion depended on the additive composition. The SrSnO15 composite, consisting of SrCO3 and 15 wt. % of SnO2, achieved the highest performance, reaching an effective conversion 5.36 times greater than pure SrCO3 after nine cycles. In contrast, the SrSnAl20 and SrMgAl20 composites exhibited lower effective conversion rates but maintained stable cycling with asymptotic conversion trends, suggesting that further optimization of synthesis conditions may enhance their performance. X-ray diffraction analysis revealed the formation of secondary phases after cycling, including Sr3Al2O6, SrSnO3, and Sr2SnO4, indicating chemical interactions and phase evolut…

title: Unsafe firearm storage among family caregivers of older persons living with dementia
abstract: Purpose Firearm access in dementia caregiving households poses safety risks. This study examines household firearm ownership and storage practices among dementia caregivers, identifying factors associated with unsafe firearm storage. Methods We analyzed pooled data from 2017, 2021, 2022, and 2023 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS). Weighted logistic regression assessed associations between caregiver characteristics and firearm storage behaviors (unloaded vs. loaded, locked vs. unlocked). Results Dementia caregivers were more likely to live in firearm-owning households than non-caregivers (40.57% vs. 35.12%). Among caregivers in firearm-owning households, 35.8% reported loaded storage, and 50.8% of those also reported unlocked storage. Older caregivers are more likely to report unlocked firearm storage (50–64 years: OR=3.74, 95%CI: 1.75–8.01; 65 + years: OR=5.39, 95%CI: 2.02–14.40; reference: < 50 years). Male caregivers had higher odds of reporting a loaded firearm in the household (OR=1.98, 95% CI: 1.32–2.96). In contrast, longer caregiving duration (>5 years: OR=0.36, 95%CI: 0.16–0.78) and assisting with household tasks (OR=0.27, 95%CI: 0.11–0.63) were associated with safer storage, though this protective effect was only observed among younger caregivers. Conclusion Household firearm storage patterns among dementia caregivers varied by caregiver age, sex, and …

title: Harnessing Interhalogen and Polyinterhalogen Compounds: Novel Strategies for Advancing Halogen Battery Performance
abstract: Abstract Interhalogen and polyinterhalogen compounds (IAPCs) have long represented a focal point in halogen chemistry. Recently, with the growing application of interhalogen chemistry in halogen ion battery (HIB) systems, increased attention has been drawn to their unique electrochemical merits and potential to advance battery design. This article discusses the correlation between the electrochemical mechanisms and properties of IAPCs, as well as their current applications in halogen batteries. We first elucidate the fundamental electrochemical mechanisms underlying IAPCs. We then categorize and discuss the applications of various types of IAPCs in halogen batteries. Finally, we offer perspectives on the existing challenges in integrating interhalogen chemistry into battery design and highlight promising prospects for the practical use of novel IAPC materials.

title: Deep-Learning-Decoded Spatial Electrochemiluminescence from Potentiostat-Free, Button-Battery-Driven Microneedle Arrays for Multiplexed microRNA Imaging
abstract: Abstract Electrochemiluminescence (ECL) bioassays are essential for rapid intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) diagnosis, while conventional approaches require bulky instrumentation and complex readout electronics that hinder point-of-care (POC) use. To address this limitation, we developed a battery-driven catalysis-initiated ECL imaging platform for multiplexed detection of ICH-associated microRNAs. The device integrated a gold film-modified copper microneedle array (Au film/Cu MNA), polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) dual-chamber microcells, and button-battery excitation. Heterogeneous catalysis at the Au film/Cu MNA generated reactive oxygen species (ROS) that amplified ECL and sustained luminescence propagation across 168 μm. A competitive hybridization assay using ferrocene-modified linker DNA (Fc-LDNA) on microneedle tips enabled simultaneous miRNA-126 and miRNA-21 detection with detection limits of 4.6 and 0.8 pM, respectively. A hybrid convolutional neural network (CNN) model decoded spatial emission patterns, extending the linear ranges to 1.28 ∼ 32 fM and 0.59 ∼ 32 fM, beyond those achieved by pixel averaging. Preliminary clinical validation (n = 35 ICH, n = 25 healthy controls) revealed an inverse miRNA expression correlation and dual-target diagnostic accuracy (AUC = 0.993), exceeding single-biomarker performance (miRNA-126: AUC = 0.945; miRNA-21: AUC = 0.964). This strategy ad…

title: A Practical SUMO-TraCI Framework for Single-Vehicle Maneuver Execution and Traffic Performance Monitoring
abstract: This study presents a practical framework combining Simulation of Urban MObility (SUMO) with its Traffic Control Interface (TraCI) to evaluate how predefined longitudinal and lateral maneuvers imposed on a single vehicle affect target-vehicle performance and aggregate traffic conditions in a simplified signalized urban network. A baseline scenario was compared with a controlled scenario in which one existing vehicle performed distance-triggered speed changes, sub-lane displacements, and a temporary stop. Both scenarios used the same network, traffic demand, routes, departure schedule, simulation settings, and random seed. External control increased the target vehicle’s travel duration from 101.05 to 107.20 s, waiting time from 8.20 to 10.05 s, and time loss from 16.82 to 22.97 s. Network-level differences were substantially smaller: mean network speed decreased from 10.759 to 10.751 m/s, mean completed-trip duration increased from 89.185 to 89.253 s, and 268 vehicles completed their routes in both scenarios. One emergency-braking event was recorded in each scenario, while no collisions or teleportations occurred. The results demonstrate a measurable direct effect on the controlled vehicle, while aggregate network responses remained small and mixed in direction.

title: Ultrahigh strain in BF–BT ceramics via synergistic optimization of defect dipoles and electric field gradient
abstract: Abstract The development of high-performance lead-free piezoelectric ceramics is critical for advancing precision actuation equipment while mitigating the environmental toxicity associated with lead-based materials. Herein, a synergistic strategy combining defect dipoles with electric field gradient was proposed to improve the strain characteristics of BiFeO3–BaTiO3 (BF–BT) ceramics. Through introducing the component KTaO3 (KT), it is found that defect dipoles [(Fe' Ti–V •• O)• and (Mn'' Ti–V •• O)×] and relaxor characteristics are mediated, and that a unique domain structure is also created in BF–BT–0.015KT ceramic, in which island domains are surrounded by stripe domains, showing fast response to external field. Moreover, reducing the sample thickness enables a significant increase in the electric field gradient at electrode edges, thereby enhancing the macroscopic strain induced by bending deformation. Finite element analysis results indicate that the electric field gradient at the electrode edge in thin samples is greater than that in thick samples by approximately one order of magnitude. Accordingly, an ultrahigh strain of 1.13%, a high Curie temperature of 374 ℃, excellent cyclic stability (4×105 cycles, degrades by 7.9%), and good thermostability (25–150 ℃, varies by 8.3%) are simultaneously achieved in the BF–BT–0.015KT ceramic with a thickness of 0.15 mm and an electro…

title: Recreating cellular dedifferentiation processes using weak electric fields
abstract: Bioelectrical signals play a crucial role in controlling the behaviour and physiological processes of various types of cells, including the differentiation of stem cells into more specialised cell types. The potential for reversing the differentiation process through the application of bioelectrical signals could potentially allow the induction of pluripotent stem cells from differentiated cells. In hopes of expanding the existing body of research, the primary objective of this study was to replicate the in-vitro experiment conducted by Becker and Murray in 1967. The experiment focused on investigating the induction of cellular dedifferentiation in nucleated amphibian red blood cells through the application of small electrical currents. The results obtained substantiated Becker and Murray’s findings and offer further insights into the factors that potentially contribute to the process of cell dedifferentiation. This study highlights the need for further research to refine the mechanisms and technical aspects of electrically inducing dedifferentiation as well as explore the possibility of using small electric fields as a means to guide the redifferentiation process.

title: Side-impact protection of floor-mounted battery packs in electric vehicles: a review of load-path design, energy absorption, and lightweight optimisation
abstract: Floor-mounted battery packs improve packaging efficiency and lower the centre of gravity of battery electric vehicles, but the limited lateral crush space leaves the cells vulnerable to localised lateral intrusion. Side-pole and low-height obstacle impacts are therefore particularly demanding crash scenarios because localised deformation can propagate from the rocker or sill into the pack perimeter, compress cells, damage separators, initiate internal short circuits, and potentially trigger thermal runaway. This review synthesises recent work on side-impact protection from a structural mechanics perspective and organises the literature into three sequential protection functions: redirecting concentrated loads through the body-in-white, absorbing residual energy at the pack perimeter, and redistributing the remaining load before it becomes localised in vulnerable cells. Particular emphasis is placed on linking conventional crash metrics — including intrusion, peak force, residual deformation, acceleration, and energy absorption — to battery-relevant failure indicators rather than treating these metrics as interchangeable proxies. Lightweight optimisation and cell-to-body integration are discussed as cross-cutting design problems with trade-offs in mass, occupant loading, repairability, and life-cycle cost. The synthesis indicates that effective battery protection depends on coor…

title: Relational Ethics and Community Education: Navigating Power, Reciprocity, and the Self‐in‐Relation
abstract: ABSTRACT Drawing on thirty years of community‐based education practices, this chapter highlights the relational and participatory dimensions of engaging with learners in diverse settings as an antidote to an extractive era, where ethics emerges through practices of care, reciprocity, and accountability to learners and communities. Utilizing autoethnography to underscore the embodiment of relationality, the chapter examines challenges such as power, reciprocity, and the “self‐in‐relation”, across place, interest, and function‐based communities, emphasizing the importance of ongoing reflexivity and collaboration in sustaining equitable relationships. Using critical autoethnographic reflection across different types of communities, the chapter illustrates how relational ethics can guide ethical decision making in community education and concludes by offering six principles for relationally ethical practice.
venue: New Directions for Adult and Continuing Education

title: Beyond economic bargaining power? Work-related internal migration and subjective well-being in couples
abstract: Abstract Bargaining theory posits that both partners’ utility shapes couples’ migration decisions. Yet, most empirical tests focus on individual incomes, thus overlooking non-economic factors in couples’ deliberations about spatial mobility. We argue that considering holistic indicators of utility, such as subjective well-being, can advance our understanding of couples’ decision-making. Using data from the German Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP, 1991–2021) and fixed effects panel regressions, we analyze changes in life satisfaction following work-related internal migration on both individual and dyadic levels. Moreover, we examine whether these changes depend on shifts in partners’ economic bargaining power (EBP, defined as female partners’ share of total household labor income), thereby evaluating the common assumption that couples’ bargaining centers around income. Our results show that, on average, both partners experience increases in their life satisfaction following migration. Distinguishing whether women’s EBP remains unchanged, decreases, or increases with migration, we find that women’s life satisfaction gains are only weakly related to changes in their EBP. In contrast, men’s life satisfaction only increases if their partner’s EBP decreases or remains unchanged, but not if it increases—a pattern consistent with the notion of gendered expectations about the within-couple in…

title: A Human-Stiffness-Based Simulator for Ergonomic Evaluation of Pistol-Grip Power Tool Reaction
abstract: Powered pistol-grip fastening tools can produce substantial handle rotation during torque build-up, which may contribute to operator overuse injuries. This study developed and evaluated a human-stiffness-based physical simulator for a controlled relative comparison of fastening variables affecting peak handle rotation. The simulator used a DC-powered pistol-grip tool, which was constrained to rotate about its spindle axis, with a double-acting pneumatic cylinder providing resistance set according to a specified human-derived stiffness. The evaluation used stiffness data from 10 operators at 5 and 7.5 N·m, with simulator peak displacement compared to in vivo measurements using paired analyses. The simulator was then used as a screening platform to examine the effect of target torque and, at 7.5 N·m, the effects of fastener material, drive style, head type, and spindle speed. The simulator overpredicted human peak displacement, with mean biases of 14.72° at 5 N·m and 10.29° at 7.5 N·m. The peak rotation increased by 15.0% when torque was increased from 5 to 7.5 N·m (p = 0.022). Torx Plus style fasteners produced 11.5% less rotation than Hex drive fasteners; fastener material significantly affected rotation; head type did not; and rotation was substantially lower at 160 rpm. Although the simulator did not reproduce absolute human displacement without bias, the results support its …

title: A Study of Retail Availability and Point-of-Sale Visibility of Classic Balanced Taste Longs and Gold Flake Blue Longs in Akola, Maharashtra
abstract: In India, cigarette marketing is tightly restricted by law, so retail execution at the counter carries unusual weight for manufacturers. This study examines two aspects of retail execution, product availability and point-of-sale (POS) visibility, for two cigarette variants of ITC Limited, Classic Balanced Taste Longs and Gold Flake Blue Longs, in Akola, Maharashtra. It uses a descriptive, observational field design. During an internship from 18 May to 18 July 2026, outlet visits were recorded as binary availability and display observations. After data cleaning, 123 valid outlet-visit observations were analysed from a convenience sample; the sample cannot be treated as representative of Akola. Classic Balanced Taste Longs was available in 87 of 123 observations (70.7%) and Gold Flake Blue Longs in 72 (58.5%). Among observations where each variant was available, it was displayed in 49 of 87 (56.3%) and 36 of 72 (50.0%) cases respectively. Neither variant was available in 30 observations (24.4%) and both in 66 (53.7%). Reported outlet-type differences should be read cautiously because outlet type was inferred from names. No causal or sales conclusions can be drawn. The study illustrates how a simple, repeatable outlet audit can reveal availability and display gaps, and it proposes compliance-aligned monitoring practices consistent with tobacco-control law. Mobile-Assisted Listening Use and Perceived Listening Improvement and Confidence Among EFL Learners: The Roles of Listening Strategy Use and Listening Engagement
abstract: Despite the growing use of mobile technologies for English listening practice, the relationships linking mobile-assisted listening use with perceived listening improvement and confidence remain insufficiently understood. This study employed a quantitative cross-sectional survey design to examine the relationships among mobile-assisted listening use, listening strategy use, listening engagement, and perceived listening improvement and confidence among EFL learners. Following instrument validation, data were collected from a convenience sample of 715 Saudi undergraduate EFL learners and analysed using structural equation modelling. The findings revealed that mobile-assisted listening use was positively associated with listening strategy use and listening engagement. Listening strategy use was positively associated with both listening engagement and perceived listening improvement and confidence, whereas listening engagement showed the largest standardised coefficient in relation to perceived listening improvement and confidence (β = 0.427). The direct relationship between mobile-assisted listening use and perceived listening improvement and confidence was not statistically significant (β = 0.013, p = 0.770). In contrast, the sequential indirect effect through listening strategy use and listening engagement was positive and statistically significant (β = 0.069, 95% BCa CI [0.045, …

title: El juego terapéutico en la hospitalización pediátrica: una estrategia de atención integral más allá del manejo del dolor
abstract: Durante la hospitalización pediátrica se realizan procedimientos invasivos y dolorosos que pueden generar ansiedad y miedo, especialmente en niños que, debido a su edad, pueden no comprender completamente la situación. Si el dolor no se gestiona adecuadamente, puede asociarse con consecuencias negativas, como alteraciones del sueño, fobia a las agujas y rechazo o reticencia a recibir atención sanitaria. Por ello, el alivio del dolor pediátrico constituye tanto un derecho como una responsabilidad de los centros sanitarios, que deben implementar estrategias eficaces para su manejo. Entre estas estrategias, la distracción no farmacológica constituye una intervención utilizada para disminuir el dolor y el malestar asociados a determinados procedimientos. Puede incluir estímulos sensoriales adaptados a la edad y al nivel de desarrollo del niño. En este contexto, el juego ha adquirido relevancia como herramienta terapéutica, aunque sus efectos deben interpretarse teniendo en cuenta el tipo de intervención, el contexto clínico y la calidad de la evidencia disponible. El juego favorece el desarrollo emocional, cognitivo y social del niño, y puede mejorar la relación con el personal sanitario y favorecer la cooperación durante los tratamientos. Por ello, se ha propuesto su incorporación desde el ingreso hospitalario, acompañada de políticas institucionales específicas y programas de for…

title: Income Diversification as a Coping Strategy for Economic and Climate Shock: A Scientific Mapping on Global Research from 2000 to 2025
abstract: Households in climate exposed and economically volatile environments are increasingly faced with multiple shocks, and income diversification has become a key way that households deal with this multiple shock exposure. Scholarly work on this relationship has now grown quickly and no research has systematically charted its intellectual geography, development or productivity foundation. This paper fills this gap by conducting a bibliometric study of 379 documents obtained from the Scopus database from 2000 to 2025 and analyzed using the Bibliometrix R package and its Biblioshiny interface. Until 2018, annual production was less than 20 documents annually, and, when implementing a logistic growth curve on the cumulative publication trend, the saturation point is estimated to be close to 3,790 documents; the logistic model predicts the peak annual production to be around 436 documents in approximately 2030–2031, suggesting that the field is not nearing maturity. Output is focussed on Environmental Science (25.2% of subject area classifications) and Social Sciences (23.3%), with Economics, econometrics and finance having a comparatively low proportion with 8.0% of the classification, and 84.2% of output is in the form of research articles, nearly sixty per cent of which is published via an open access route. At the author level an analysis of the distribution of productivity shows a …

title: Drivers of Sustainability Strategy Adoption in European SMEs : The Role of Digitalisation, Innovation and Organisational Barriers
abstract: ABSTRACT Sustainability has become a core concern to be embedded in firms' strategic orientations. This study investigates how digitalisation, innovation, and internal organisational barriers contribute to or constrain the development of formal sustainability‐oriented strategies in SMEs. In addition, it examines whether internal barriers to innovation moderate the relationship between different innovation types and the adoption of formal sustainability strategies. The paper applies a binary logistic regression model to microdata from Flash Eurobarometer 486, using a final analytical sample of 11,861 SMEs across 35 European countries. The research reveals that product, organisational, and marketing innovation, as well as factors associated with digitalisation, are positively and significantly associated with the probability of SMEs adopting a formal sustainability strategy. Previous participation in sustainability practices shows a positive and statistically significant relationship as well. Although the coefficient for internal barriers is not statistically significant among firms reporting none of the three innovation types, barriers weaken the positive association between marketing innovation and sustainability strategy adoption. This finding is supported by both the log‐odds and probability‐scale analyses. These findings highlight how innovation, digitalisation, and organisa…

title: Islamic Banking Innovation: Addressing Fintech Challenges Through Blue Ocean Strategy
abstract: Purpose— This study examines Islamic banking innovations to address fintech challenges through a blue ocean strategy. Therefore, the main focus of the discussion is on: External business environment factors of Islamic banking; Internal business environment factors; SWOT analysis; and Blue Ocean Strategy. Design/methodology/approach— This descriptive qualitative research used primary data collected through interviews and secondary data. Five Islamic commercial banks were selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected, reduced, and then triangulated using literature and documentation studies to strengthen arguments and analysis, leading to strategic and innovative recommendations. Findings— The strategy of Islamic banks in responding to fintech challenges focuses on holistic digital transformation to achieve operational efficiency, increased security, Sharia compliance, and the creation of a holistic digital service ecosystem, such as: integrating various financial services, ZISWAF platforms and disaster mitigation, cardless withdrawals, investment services, legacy management, and halal supply chain financing in one holistic ecosystem supported by partnerships with industry and government. Research implication/limitation— This study develops an integrated digital ecosystem model for Islamic banking based on Blue Ocean Strategy, emphasizing value innovation amidst fintec…

title: Green Innovation Through Artificial Intelligence: Sectoral and Regional Perspectives of China
abstract: ABSTRACT The rapid adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed manufacturing and promotes firms' green innovation. Concurrently, the significance of green innovation plays an important role in supporting firms' environmental transformation. Against this backdrop, the present study investigates the dynamic relationship between AI and firms' green innovation (FGI), with a specific focus on Chinese manufacturing firms. The results show that manufacturing companies with extensive AI adoption demonstrate heightened levels of green innovation. Furthermore, the study explores the heterogeneous impact of AI on FGI across different types of firms and regions. Notably, AI has a stronger effect on FGI within the eastern region and significantly drives green innovation in non‐SOE, high‐tech, and non‐labor‐intensive firms compared to their counterparts in SOE, labor‐intensive, and non‐tech industries. Additionally, AI contributes to the enhancement of FGI by stimulating investments in green research and development (R&D), reducing operational costs, and facilitating digital transformation initiatives. The study also illuminates the influence of environmental regulations in amplifying AI's promotion of FGI in manufacturing firms. Finally, based on the pragmatic assessments, valuable policy implications are discussed.

title: Optimization of a deformable mirror using covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy.
Fecal Microbiota Transplantation: A Promising Therapeutic Strategy Targeting the Microbiota–Gut–Brain Axis in Anorexia Nervosa
abstract: Abstract Purpose Anorexia nervosa (AN) is a complex psychiatric disorder characterized by self‐starvation, body‐image disturbance, and serious medical complications. Because current treatments have variable outcomes and relapse is common, the microbiota–gut–brain axis has been investigated as a possible contributor to disease persistence. This review evaluates fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) as an experimental microbiota‐directed strategy for AN. Methods PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched for relevant studies published from January 1990 to October 2025. Eligible evidence included human reports, animal studies, and mechanistic studies examining FMT or gut–microbiota alterations in AN and related pathways. Findings Individuals with AN have been reported to show altered microbial diversity and changes in taxa associated with short‐chain fatty acid production and inflammation. These findings are heterogeneous and may reflect starvation, diet, medication exposure, or illness‐related physiology. Human evidence for FMT in AN is limited to small, uncontrolled studies and case reports, while most mechanistic support comes from animal models or indirect evidence from other conditions. Conclusion Evidence for FMT in AN remains preliminary and is largely based on uncontrolled human observations and preclinical studies. FMT may alter gut microbial composition an…

title: SURT-DETR: Sea–Sky Line Context-aware and Uncertainty-Guided Small Object Detection for Unmanned Surface Vehicles
abstract: Detecting small objects within complex maritime environments presents a persistent challenge for unmanned surface vehicle (USV) perception. Extreme scale variations often render distant targets as indistinct visual features, while background interference from waves and sea–sky boundaries further obscures object delineation. Consequently, state-of-the-art detectors frequently suffer from inaccurate localization and limited generalization capabilities. To address these limitations, we propose SURT-DETR, a robust Transformer-based framework tailored for USV perception. Constructed upon the RT-DETR architecture, SURT-DETR integrates three innovations: (1) the sea–sky line context-aware feature enhancement module (SLCAM) to model geometric priors and suppress background noise; (2) the uncertainty-guided small object decoder branch (UGSD) to enhance tiny target detection; and (3) an uncertainty-regularized NWD loss to mitigate scale sensitivity and localization uncertainty. Experimental results on the Pohang Canal dataset verify the effectiveness of our method. The SURT-DETR achieves an overall mAP of 79.5% and small-object [Formula: see text] of 69.2%. Compared with the RT-DETR baseline, our model obtains clear accuracy gains on overall and small-target detection metrics with a modest parameter increment of 1.2 M. Ablation experiments further confirm the complementarity and efficacy…

title: CP-BayesNE: Uncertainty-Aware Personalized Nutrient-Density Estimation from Food Images Using Conformal Prediction and Prior-Corrected Dietary Adaptation
abstract: Background/Objectives: Reliable longitudinal dietary assessment is a prerequisite for precision nutrition, important for studying nutrition-related changes in health and physical function, but conventional dietary recording can impose substantial user burden. AI-driven, food-image-based assessment can reduce this burden, although uncertainty in food recognition and inter-individual dietary differences may propagate to nutrient estimation. Methods:We developed CP-BayesNE, an uncertainty-aware framework that combines temperature-scaled food classification, conformal candidate sets, training-prior-corrected dietary-history personalization, and posterior-weighted nutrient estimation to support AI-driven personalized nutrition. Results: EfficientNetV2-S achieved 78.01% Top-1 and 93.67% Top-5 accuracy, while temperature scaling reduced expected calibration error from 0.11238 to 0.04345. At α=0.10, regularized adaptive prediction sets reduced the average candidate-set size from 80.78 to 5.77 while maintaining 94.32% empirical category coverage. In FoodLogAthl-218, prior-corrected personalization reduced nutrient density mean absolute error (MAE) by 4.0–6.6% across energy and macronutrients over 51 users. A single-participant 92-meal personal dataset provided preliminary end-to-end feasibility evidence, while also revealing limitations, including slightly worse fat MAE and conservative…

title: Heavy metal contamination and risk assessment with uncertainty analysis in agricultural soils at a rural–urban interface
abstract: Abstract As traditional pollution risk assessments fail to comprehensively consider the conbined effects of individual element toxicity and pollutant species, a modified geoaccumulation index ( I geo ) was proposed to identify priority trace metals and assess pollution risk characteristics in agricultural soils at a rural–urban interface area. Seventy agricultural soil samples were collected and analyzed for 6 heavy metals (Cr, Ni, Cu, Zn, Cd, Pb). To account for uncertainty from spatial heterogeneity in soil heavy metals and model parameters in the risk assessment model, a health risk model coupled with probabilistic triangular fuzzy numbers (TFN) was utilized to evaluate human health risks from three primary exposure pathways. The average concentrations of Cr, Ni, Cu, Zn, Cd, and Pb (mg kg −1 ) were 75.3, 22.6, 44.0, 189, 0.63, and 106, respectively, indicating elevated accumulation of Cd and Pb. The proposed I geo index determined elevated pollution risk levels comparable to the conventional index. Notably, Cd was identified as a priority trace metal to control due to its severe contamination risk ( I m = 3.3). The health risk model revealed no significant non-carcinogenic or cancer risk for adults. However, health risk for children were determined to be unacceptable, with a hazard index (HI) value > 1.0 and a total carcinogenic risk (TCR) > 1.0E−04. Ingestion was identified…

title: From Pendulums to Smartphones: Instructional Approaches for Measuring Local G and Developing Uncertainty Reasoning in Preservice Teachers
FedEdgeHealth: an uncertainty-aware federated edge intelligence framework for real-time multi-modal health monitoring
abstract: Abstract This study introduces a sustainability-focused, uncertainty-aware federated edge intelligence framework for multimodal healthcare monitoring within simulated AIoT-edge environments. Unlike conventional healthcare AI systems that optimize predictive accuracy or latency in isolation, the proposed framework integrates probabilistic multi-task learning with adaptive federated coordination to enable selective client participation and risk-aware resource management across distributed edge nodes. The framework captures predictive uncertainty while learning from heterogeneous, multimodal healthcare data distributed across non-IID clients. Furthermore, an energy-aware workload management strategy is incorporated to minimize computational and communication overhead, thereby supporting sustainable edge-cloud healthcare infrastructures. Experimental evaluations using diverse public healthcare datasets in a simulated federated edge environment demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves superior predictive performance (AUC-ROC = 0.956), enhanced calibration reliability, and reduced estimated latency and modeled energy consumption compared to centralized and conventional federated learning baselines. These findings highlight the effectiveness, robustness, and resource efficiency of the proposed approach under controlled simulation conditions, establishing a reproducible methodo…

title: On a competition problem under uncertainty and risks
abstract: A hierarchical model of the problem of competition between two firms under the influence of uncertain factors is considered. Two companies produce and supply the same type of products to the market. In addition, products of the same type produced by the importing company enter the market. Moreover, only possible limits are known about the amount of imported goods, which plays the role of uncertainty. The following principles are used: the Wald principle, according to which the player uses a strategy that guarantees him the best outcome in the worst situation, and the Savage principle, according to which the player minimizes his regret, i.e. the difference between what he could get in the game if the outcome was favorable for him, and what he actually got. The optimal strategies of the second player within each approach are indicated. The optimal strategies of the first player are determined depending on the behavior of the second player and his own optimality criterion. The article analyzes the methods of formalizing the optimal solution for the upper-level conflict participant (center), as well as the individual attitude of the second lower-level player (agent) to risk. Sufficient conditions of existence have been found for the presented solutions of the game and their explicit form has been found.

title: Geometrical waveguide design for stray-light suppression in augmented reality displays
abstract: A geometrical waveguide design for stray-light suppression in augmented reality displays is presented. The mechanism responsible for stray-light formation is analyzed by tracing the propagation paths and reflection sequences leading to unintended extraction. By reconfiguring the waveguide geometry, these paths reach the outer waveguide boundary before their required reflection sequences are completed. Ray-tracing and image simulations validate the proposed design. Compared with a traditional geometrical waveguide, the proposed design reduces the average and maximum stray-light percentages from 4.92% and 12.81% to below 0.001% and 0.01%, respectively. This suppression is accompanied by a decrease in optical efficiency from 11.53% to 7.99%. The proposed waveguide provides a 30° FOV, a 15mm×15mm eye-box, and a 20 mm eye relief.

title: System-Level Assessment Methodology for PV–AEL–H2–PEMFC Power-to-Power Systems: Constant-Efficiency Versus Quasi-Dynamic Modeling
abstract: Hydrogen-based power-to-power (PTP) systems complement batteries for long-duration storage, but their assessment often assumes fixed electrolyzer and fuel-cell efficiencies. The main innovation of this work is developing a system-level methodology to quantify how component-model fidelity affects the annual assessment of photovoltaic-alkaline electrolyzer-hydrogen-proton exchange membrane fuel cell systems. To highlight parameter and operational differences, two approaches are compared for the Santa Cruz–Baltra case study. Case A relies on simplified parameter assumptions, using fixed AEL and PEMFC efficiencies of 0.65 and 0.52. In contrast, Case B resolves operational differences by capturing operating-point-dependent electrochemical behavior, part-load variations, and AEL thermal-state propagation. Both cases use identical system boundaries and supervisory control, allowing model-fidelity effects on hydrogen production, storage utilization, and electricity recovery to be quantified. Annual simulations show that Case A predicts higher recovered electricity than Case B. For a representative configuration, global efficiency decreases from 0.529 to 0.440 (a 17% relative difference). The largest relative difference in recovered electricity (~91%) occurs in constrained configurations. Component-level experimental validation does not constitute full system-level validation. Overall, …

title: Behavior Uncertainty Aware Operational Planning for Multi‐Resource Virtual Power Plant in Balancing Market
abstract: Aggregators in balancing markets operate Virtual Power Plants (VPPs) by integrating distributed energy resources like batteries, electric vehicles (EVs), and heat pump water heaters (HPs) installed in low‐voltage households. A key challenge is managing user behavior uncertainty both in day‐ahead bidding and real‐time operation. This paper proposes a hierarchical planning framework using probabilistic scenario forecasting, two‐stage stochastic programming, and model predictive control (MPC). Day‐ahead bidding optimizes demand response (DR) capacity and resource schedules using two‐stage stochastic programming under behavior uncertainty, while real‐time MPC ensures commitment fulfillment. By explicitly linking scenario‐based bidding with receding‐horizon control, the framework increases bidding aggressiveness without compromising EV charging and hot‐water availability. Evaluation with 30 households over 150 days shows the proposed method reduces net electricity cost by 14.1% and increases offered down‐DR volume by 1.6 times compared to the robust method, while achieving a 98.69% DR fulfillment rate and limiting EV energy shortage and HP hot water shortage to 1.0% and 0.61%, respectively.

title: A hybrid statistical–machine learning framework for day-ahead electricity price forecasting in smart city environments
abstract: Accurate day-ahead electricity price forecasting, particularly in the context of customer-centric services and emerging smart city infrastructures, is a cornerstone of efficient power market operations, supporting bidding strategies, hedging, and grid reliability. This paper proposes SSXLR, a fault-tolerant hybrid forecasting framework that combines Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average with Exogenous variables (SARIMAX), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) within a 2-out-of-3 voting architecture to capture both linear seasonal trends and nonlinear temporal dynamics while reducing dependence on a single forecasting branch. The proposed method was evaluated using one year of historical data (July 1, 2024–July 1, 2025) from Duke Energy Ohio and Kentucky (DEO&K) within the PJM interconnection. The dataset integrates day-ahead market prices ($/MWh), corresponding load consumption (MW), eleven weather variables, and population growth indicators. The target is the day-ahead price profile for July 2, 2025, consisting of 24-hourly points. Results show that SSXLR achieves more than 30% reduction in Root Mean Squared Error over SARIMAX and XGBoost, respectively. The Mean Absolute Error (MAE) reached 1.196, demonstrating the ability of SSXLR to account effectively for external market drivers and temporal dependencies. These findings highlight…

title: Energy and reserve markets-based energy management system in smart grid including integrated system of flexible resources and distributed generations
abstract: By coordinating generation units, storage systems, and responsive loads within a unified framework, virtual power plants (VPPs) can function as both energy producers and storage entities. This operational model enables the constituent components to generate favorable revenue when aggregated as a VPP. Furthermore, applying advanced energy management schemes to grid-connected VPPs can significantly improve both the economic viability and the technical operation of power systems. In line with this objective, this study introduces a comprehensive energy management structure for flexible renewable VPPs functioning within an active distribution network (ADN), while explicitly considering their involvement in day-ahead energy and reserve markets. The proposed approach is formulated as a bi-level optimization problem. At the upper level, the operational strategy of the ADN is determined by minimizing a weighted objective function that incorporates both the expected operational cost and the voltage deviation index, subject to AC optimal power flow constraints. At the lower level, a risk-aware framework is adopted to model the participation of renewable and flexible VPPs in both energy and reserve markets. The objective at this stage is to simultaneously maximize the VPP’s expected profit and its conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) in the respective markets. The associated constraints inclu…

title: PROJECT FINANCE AS A TOOL FOR MOBILIZING PRIVATE CAPITAL INTO UNITED STATES POWER INFRASTRUCTURE FOR ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE DATA CENTERS
abstract: Artificial intelligence is changing the scale, speed, and location of electricity demand in the United States.Large data centers can seek hundreds of megawatts, require high reliability, and arrive faster than conventional utility planning and construction cycles.This review examines whether project finance can mobilize the private capital required for generation, energy storage, transmission, and interconnection assets that serve this emerging load.It synthesizes scholarship on project finance, infrastructure contracts, renewable-energy investment, cost of capital, power-purchase agreements, electricity-market design, transmission expansion, and data-center energy use, supplemented by authoritative U.S. institutional evidence.The literature shows that project finance creates value chiefly through risk isolation, contractual coordination, lender monitoring, and matching long-lived assets with longdated capital.For AI-related power infrastructure, creditworthy corporate offtakers can strengthen revenue certainty and permit nonrecourse debt, but conventional contracts must be adapted to uncertain load ramps, short data-center development timelines, interconnection delays, and the possibility that computing efficiency or geographic migration changes demand.

title: Clinical prediction models: from foundational concepts to practical application
abstract: Abstract Objectives Clinical prediction requires formalizing uncertainty into a statistical model. However, persistent confusion between prediction and inference, and between traditional (stepwise) and modern (penalized) development strategies, leads to unstable, poorly calibrated, and overfit models. A structured statistical framework is essential. Methods This article is a structured, didactic tutorial that explains the core concepts of clinical prediction models. It covers the definition of a prediction model, the fundamental strategies for its construction, and the essential framework for its evaluation, illustrated through an applied example using real-world clinical data. Results The tutorial illustrates model development using the GUSTO-I dataset (n=40,830). Penalized methods (LASSO [Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator] and Elastic Net) retained established clinical predictors and shrank the two independently generated synthetic noise variables to zero in this worked example. The LASSO model (λ1SE) achieved strong discrimination (AUC 0.818; 95 % CI: 0.803–0.832), with a Brier score of 0.058. Calibration analysis revealed a slope of 1.28, indicating underdispersion of predicted risks consistent with the stronger shrinkage applied at λ1SE in this worked example. Calibration-in-the-large was 0.011 on the logit scale, indicating negligible average-level miscalibr…

title: A General Framework for Gradient-Based Optimization of Superconducting Quantum Circuits using Qubit Discovery as a Case Study
abstract: Engineering the Hamiltonian of a quantum system is fundamental to the design of quantum systems. Automating Hamiltonian design through gradient-based optimization can dramatically accelerate this process. However, computing the gradients of eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a Hamiltonian–a large, sparse matrix–relative to system properties poses a significant challenge, especially for arbitrary systems. Superconducting quantum circuits offer substantial flexibility in Hamiltonian design, making them an ideal platform for this task. In this work, we present a comprehensive framework for the gradient-based optimization of superconducting quantum circuits, leveraging the SQcircuit software package. By addressing the challenge of calculating the gradient of the eigensystem for large, sparse Hamiltonians and integrating automatic differentiation within SQcircuit, our framework enables efficient and precise computation of gradients for various circuit properties or custom-defined metrics, streamlining the optimization process. We apply this framework to the qubit discovery problem, demonstrating its effectiveness in identifying qubit designs with superior performance metrics. The optimized circuits show improvements in a heuristic measure of gate count, upper bounds on gate speed, decoherence time, and resilience to noise and fabrication errors compared to existing qubits. While this m…

title: Rapid symptomatic and radiological response to pembrolizumab–lenvatinib in a 30-year-old man with metastatic sarcomatoid renal cell carcinoma not otherwise specified and extensive osteolytic bone disease
abstract: Sarcomatoid dedifferentiation and bone metastases characterize an aggressive subset of metastatic renal cell carcinoma (mRCC) with a poor prognosis. Immune- checkpoint inhibitor combinations are the standard first-line therapy, whilst the role of deferred cytoreductive nephrectomy (dCN) remains debated. We report on the case of a 30-year-old man with International mRCC Database Consortium (IMDC)-classified poor-risk mRCC featuring sarcomatoid dedifferentiation and symptomatic osteolytic bone lesions. First-line pembrolizumab–lenvatinib and bone-targeted agents were initiated. Treatment was well tolerated, achieving rapid symptomatic relief and durable disease control. Following durable disease control, the patient underwent dCN. Histopathological analysis confirmed sarcomatoid RCC, not otherwise specified (ypT1b) with extensive necrosis. Pembrolizumab–lenvatinib was resumed 4 weeks postoperatively. Subsequent restaging demonstrated substantial disease stability. This case highlights the efficacy of pembrolizumab–lenvatinib in achieving rapid clinical benefit in sarcomatoid mRCC with symptomatic bone involvement and the opportunity to perform dCN for carefully selected patients after a caseby- case multidisciplinary discussion. title: Shared Genetics of Hypertension and Preeclampsia Converges on Immune Regulation
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypertension and preeclampsia are clinically distinct, yet biologically related conditions characterized by vascular dysfunction and elevated cardiovascular risk. Although genome-wide association studies have identified loci associated with blood pressure traits and preeclampsia, the functional mechanisms linking shared variants to gene regulation and clinical phenotypes remain unclear. METHODS: We integrated genome-wide association study summary statistics for hypertension, systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, and preeclampsia to identify shared variants ( P ≤1×10 −4 ). Cis -expression quantitative trait loci analyses were performed in whole blood using RNA sequencing data from 180 Black women. Significant associations (false discovery rate ≤0.05) were evaluated for replication across vascular, metabolic, and endocrine tissues in the Genotype-Tissue Expression project. Associations between gene expression and blood pressure traits were also assessed. RESULTS: We identified 4792 shared genome-wide association study variants, of which 4663 were tested in expression quantitative trait loci analyses, yielding 1837 significant variant-gene associations across 78 genes. Replication in the Genotype-Tissue Expression project confirmed 645 associations involving 24 genes, many showing cross-tissue regulatory effects. Three genes ( C4B , HLA-C , and HLA-DQB1 ) …

title: Диспропорции рынка труда в стратегии обеспечения экономической безопасности региона
abstract: Усиление пространственного неравенства регионов угрожает их экономической безопасности. Исследованы территориально-отраслевые диспропорции рынка труда Республики Башкортостан. Цель – формирование регуляторных подходов к сглаживанию дифференциации занятости. Методология базируется на статистическом, сравнительном анализе и SWOT-моделировании данных Росстата. Установлено, что отток трудового потенциала оголяет периферию, формируя межмуниципальный зарплатный спред до 1,9 раза. Сформулированы механизмы преодоления демографических и финансовых диспропорций через налоговое стимулирование, гранты малому бизнесу и платформы удаленной занятости. Growing spatial inequality in regions threatens their economic security. This study examines territorial and sectoral imbalances in the labor market of the Republic of Bashkortostan. The objective is to develop regulatory approaches to mitigate employment differentiation. The methodology relies on statistical, comparative analysis, and SWOT modeling of Rosstat data. The research reveals that labor potential outflows deplete the periphery, driving an inter-municipal wage spread of up to 1.9 times. Mechanisms to overcome demographic and financial imbalances are proposed, including tax incentives, small business grants, and remote employment platforms.

title: Do limits to arbitrage and mispricing explain belief heterogeneity? Evidence from an emerging market
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine whether mispricing and limits to arbitrage explain belief heterogeneity in the Tunisian stock market, while accounting for investor sentiment in an emerging market context. Design/methodology/approach Using portfolio sorting and Fama–MacBeth regressions, this study analyzes stock returns from July 2007 to July 2018. It proposes a new trading–volume-based measure of belief heterogeneity and uses multiple proxies for limits to arbitrage and investor sentiment. Findings The results show that stocks with high belief heterogeneity earn lower expected returns. Limits to arbitrage and investor sentiment do not significantly moderate this relationship. However, belief heterogeneity has a stronger effect on undervalued stocks than on overvalued stocks, providing new evidence beyond traditional overvaluation-based explanations. Research limitations/implications The study is limited by its focus on the Tunisian stock market, and the findings may not be generalizable to markets with different institutional structures and investor behaviors. Practical implications The findings provide useful insights for investors and regulators seeking to better understand how belief heterogeneity and market frictions affect stock returns in emerging markets. title: Микрофинансовый рынок России: угрозы и возможности
abstract: В статье исследована динамика отечественного рынка микрозаймов, рассмотрены актуальные тенденции и угрозы в деятельности микрофинансовых организаций (МФО), особое внимание уделено развитию данного рынка и расширению регуляторных требований Банка России; сформулирован вывод о приспособлении сектора МФО к изменяющимся условиям. The article analyzes the dynamics of the Russian microloan market, current trends and threats in the activities of microfinance organizations, pays special attention to the development of this market and the expansion of regulatory requirements by the Bank of Russia, and concludes that the MFO market is adapting to changing conditions.

title: Targeted demand-side stimulus and the equity market: evidence from China's mortgage interest-subsidy for first-time homebuyers
abstract: On 29 September 2026 China's Ministry of Finance, the People's Bank of China and the National Financial Regulatory Administration issued the Notice on Implementing the Residential Home-Purchase Mortgage Interest-Subsidy Policy (Caijin [2026] No. 95). From 1 October 2026 the central government subsidizes, for up to five years, one percentage point of the annual interest on newly issued commercial mortgages used by first-time buyers to purchase homes of at most 120 square metres and no more than RMB 1.5 million, on subsidized principal of up to RMB 1 million. This paper studies the stock-market response of the A-share real-estate sector to this sharply dated, narrowly targeted demand-side intervention. Using a single-factor market model on the 69 constituents of the CSI All-Share Real Estate Index, the estimated average abnormal return is +3.81% on the event day (29 September 2026), significant at the 1% level under the cross-sectional t (10.67), Patell (12.90) and Boehmer–Masumeci–Poulsen (10.48) tests. An equal-weighted portfolio gives an identical estimate, 94.2% of firms recorded positive abnormal returns, and the aggregate change in market value is about RMB 32.6 billion. The sector had already risen about 4.2% over the prior five sessions and gave back about 1.8% over the five sessions after the National Day holiday. The pattern is consistent with anticipatory pricing of a …

title: Working for fame or fees? Tensions in exhibition work
abstract: Purpose The paper explores the job marketisation of exhibition work by examining the coexistence of traditional and new market norms and the tensions these conflicting norms generate. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on qualitative fieldwork, the paper examines this marketisation through the case of the Swedish MU agreement, introduced to regulate artists' work and income when exhibiting at publicly funded institutions. Findings Conflicting norms contribute to artists pursuing both symbolic and monetary income simultaneously, creating four dimensions of tension. When facing these tensions, artists employ practices of prioritisation, negotiation and guessing. Research limitations/implications The study suggests that marketisation often entails the coexistence of competing norms rather than straightforward change. This coexistence generates tensions, requiring actors to develop coping practices. By examining exhibition work as a case of job marketisation, the study calls for greater attention to how market reforms are experienced and enacted in everyday work practices, and how competing remuneration principles shape professional identities, exchanges and labour market participation. Practical implications The paper offers insights into how a specific marketisation process in the art world unfolds in practice. Open discussion about the tensions generated by this job marketisati…

title: The relationships between geopolitical risk, the value relevance of accounting information and auditor opinion: evidence from a developing market
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the relationship between geopolitical risk (GPR) and the value relevance (VR) of accounting information (AI) under different types of auditor opinion (AO). Design/methodology/approach This study uses a sample of nonfinancial firms listed on EGX100 during the period 2014–2023. Whereas GPR and AO data have been collected manually from annual reports and governance reports, stock prices are collected from EGX Archives available at the Egyptian Company for Information Dissemination. The study depends on the t-test, Pearson correlation, and OLS, 2SLS and GMM regressions to examine the authors’ hypotheses. Findings The results revealed a negative effect of GPR on the VR of AI. However, this negative effect may vary across accounting measures, depending on the auditor’s opinion. The VR of book value (BVS) declined during higher GPR periods, which was clearly visible with qualified auditor opinion. However, GPR increased the value relevance of EPS, which was clearly visible with unqualified auditor opinion, indicating that EPS might be perceived as a more reliable measure in uncertain environments, especially with the existence of a supportive auditor opinion. Originality/value This study contributes to literature by examining relationships between geopolitical risk, the VR of AI and auditor opinion, especially in developing markets, such as the Egypt…

Talking or typing? How GenAI modality, product type, and multitasking shape recommendation response behaviour
abstract: Purpose This research aims to explore how generative AI (GenAI) recommendation modality (text vs voice) influences consumer recommendation adoption and how this effect further interacts with product type (search vs experience), processing fluency and multitasking to shape consumers’ behavioural responses to recommendations. Given that GenAI recommendation systems increasingly support interactive consumer decision-making, the authors examine modality as a key design feature shaping how GenAI-generated recommendations are delivered to consumers. Design/methodology/approach Across five studies, the authors examine how GenAI recommendation modality influences consumers’ recommendation adoption. The preliminary field study uses actual customer interactions in a natural commercial environment to establish the practical relevance of the phenomenon. Study 1 replicates the core modality effect in a controlled Chinese experiment. Study 2 examines the moderating role of product type. Studies 3 and 4 investigate processing fluency and multitasking as the underlying mechanism and boundary condition, using behavioural measures across all studies. Findings The findings demonstrate that GenAI recommendation modality affects consumers’ recommendation adoption, with text-based recommendations outperforming voice-based recommendations. Correlation between pathological response to neoadjuvant immunotherapy and long-term survival in locally advanced rectal cancer: A real-world study
abstract: BACKGROUND Conventional treatment for locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) is associated with several limitations, and neoadjuvant immunotherapy has been proposed to address these current clinical dilemmas. However, the correlation between pathological response and long-term survival remains unclear. Most existing studies are derived from clinical trials, with a lack of real-world evidence. Therefore, this real-world study was conducted to analyze the correlation between the two indicators. AIM To investigate the correlation between pathological response to neoadjuvant immunotherapy and long-term survival in patients with LARC using real-world data. METHODS Clinical data of 130 LARC patients who received neoadjuvant immunotherapy combined with radical surgery in our hospital from March 2022 to March 2025 were retrospectively collected. All patients were administered neoadjuvant immunotherapy regimens based on anti-programmed cell death protein 1/programmed death-ligand 1 inhibitors, and laparoscopic or open radical resection of rectal cancer was performed 4-6 weeks after the end of treatment. Tumor regression grade (TRG) was used to evaluate the degree of pathological response, which was classified into pathological complete response (pCR; TRG grade 0), major pathological response (MPR; TRG grade 1), and non-MPR (TRG grades 2-3). The Kaplan-Meier method was adopted for surviva…

Recent advances in critical care nutrition: from dose escalation to phase-guided and response-guided care
abstract: Purpose of review To critically appraise recent advances that are shifting critical care nutrition from uniform nutrient targets towards phase-guided, phenotype-guided and response-guided care, with particular emphasis on major studies published in 2025–2026. Recent findings Recent large trials do not support routine early full-dose energy or high-dose protein delivery in unselected critically ill patients, and some higher dose strategies have generated safety signals. Indirect calorimetry improves measurement of energy expenditure, but measured expenditure is not synonymous with the dose that should be delivered. Emerging data suggest that dynamic responses, including early phosphate trajectories, may help identify metabolic readiness for feeding, although no validated bedside marker exists. Pharmacological intravenous vitamin C has shown no benefit and recurring harm signals in shocked patients, whereas micronutrient care should distinguish physiological requirements and deficiency correction from megadosing. After ICU discharge, intake frequently falls during the transition from enteral to oral nutrition, and intake-guided protocols have achieved high nutritional adequacy in proof-of-concept studies. Summary Critical care nutrition is moving from universal targets towards phase-guided, phenotype-guided and response-guided treatment. Acute-phase caution should not become prol…

Combination of Serum Leucine-rich Alpha-2-Glycoprotein 1 and Citrulline as Biomarkers of Graft Monitoring and Response to Antirejection Treatment in Intestinal Transplantation
abstract: Background. Intestinal transplantation (ITx) has the highest rejection rate among solid organ transplantations. Nevertheless, convenient, reliable, and noninvasive biomarkers for rejection surveillance are lacking. Leucine-rich alpha-2-glycoprotein 1 (LRG-1) has been developed as a new serum biomarker of disease activity in numerous gastrointestinal inflammatory pathologies. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the utility of serum LRG-1 as a biomarker for predicting post-ITx rejection, using citrulline as a known marker. Methods. Serum LRG-1 (n = 77) and citrulline (n = 64) samples were obtained from 5 post-ITx patients. We analyzed the correlation between these serum levels and the “villi appearance, erythema, capillary network, crypt widening, and heterogeneity (VENCH)” score according to the endoscopic findings of the intestinal graft evaluated on the same day as serum sample collection, as well as histopathological diagnosis. Results. We observed a negative correlation between serum LRG-1 and citrulline levels. LRG-1 values in the VENCH score ≥4 group were significantly higher than those in the VENCH <4 group ( P < 0.0001). The area under the curve of the citrulline/LRG-1 (C/L) ratio for detecting endoscopic abnormalities was 0.896 (sensitivity: 0.87; specificity: 0.89). In addition, LRG-1 values in the pathological rejection group were significantly higher than those i…

title: Expert recommendations and investor psychology: a qualitative study of behavioural biases in investors’ response
abstract: Purpose The popularity of expert recommendations is increasing, as investors seek assistance in making investment decisions. However, such advice may be risky, as it can affect perceptions and induce biases, leading to uncertainty and risky investment behaviour. Building on signalling and prospect theory, the study aims to explore several expert-induced biases that affect investors’ intentions and behaviour regarding investment in the stock market. Design/methodology/approach The study uses a qualitative research approach, with open-ended survey questionnaires, to collect the viewpoints of 55 Indian investors on the importance and concerns associated with expert recommendations or financial advisors. Data is evaluated using Gioia’s thematic coding process to identify various biases influencing investors’ intentions. Findings The findings identified four main categories of biases among investors: cognitive biases, emotional biases, social biases and informational biases when following expert recommendations or other similar financial advice sources when making investment decisions. The study indicated that expert advice may induce uncertainty or biased judgement among investors, thereby directly affecting their decision-making. Originality/value The present study extends the signalling and prospect theory literature in the domain of investors’ psychology by discussing the inform…

title: Discordance between proptosis response and other clinical improvements at week 12 during teprotumumab N01 therapy for thyroid eye disease: a multicenter prospective registry study
Treatment response in pediatric metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: Noninvasive endpoints and body composition
abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease is the most common chronic liver disease in youth, yet treatment response remains difficult to define as lifestyle therapy, anti-obesity pharmacotherapy, and metabolic and bariatric surgery produce changes across different biological domains. This narrative review examines histology, alanine aminotransferase, magnetic resonance imaging proton density fat fraction, elastography, serum biomarkers, body composition, cardiometabolic health, and patient-centered outcomes as candidate response endpoints. Diagnostic accuracy, cross-sectional severity, prognostic validity, longitudinal responsiveness, association with histological response, and validated thresholds for meaningful change are considered separately. Pediatric evidence remains strongest for repeated aminotransferases, growth-adjusted adiposity measures, and selected imaging approaches, but no single test defines response and normal aminotransferases do not exclude persistent steatohepatitis or fibrosis. Adult magnetic resonance imaging and drug-trial thresholds are informative but cannot be adopted uncritically in children. Loss of lean mass should also not be equated with sarcopenia without evidence of low muscle quantity and impaired strength or function. A practical three-tier framework is proposed: Minimum clinical assessment, specialist-center assessment, and re…

title: Anti-PF4 antibodies trigger a faster and stronger platelet procoagulant response than anti-heparin/PF4 antibodies
abstract: Abstract Vaccine-induced immune thrombocytopenia and thrombosis (VITT) and VITT-like syndromes are emerging causes of severe thrombocytopenia and thrombosis associated with immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibodies targeting platelet factor 4 (PF4). These syndromes are characterized by more frequent and severe thrombosis than heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT), which is typically caused by antibodies targeting heparin-modified PF4 (anti-PF4/H). In this study, we compared the intrinsic prothrombotic properties of IgG anti-PF4 and anti-PF4/H to identify mechanisms that may contribute to the severity of VITT and VITT-like syndromes. Using the monoclonal IgG1 antibodies 1E12 (anti-PF4) and 5B9 (anti-PF4/H), we showed that IgG anti-PF4 exhibited an increased propensity to induce the formation of fibrin-rich platelet–leukocytes aggregates in a microfluidic model of whole-blood (WB) thrombosis. This phenomenon was related to a strong potentiation of thrombin generation in plasma by 1E12, but not by 5B9, and occurred only in the presence of platelets and coagulation factors V and XI. We also demonstrated a substantially faster and stronger ability of 1E12, compared with 5B9, to activate platelets using the serotonin release assay and confirmed these findings using human VITT and HIT samples. Furthermore, 1E12 was more likely than 5B9 to induce procoagulant platelets (CD62P+/phosphatidylser…
