Developing Conflict-Ready Managers: an integrative framework linking leadership discernment and conflict capability
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this paper is to develop the Conflict-Ready Manager Framework as an integrated explanation of how managers move from complex conflict toward constructive action. The framework conceptualizes conflict readiness as a higher-order, developable managerial capability. Design/methodology/approach A theory-informed conceptual approach integrates research on conflict, cognitive load, sensemaking, ethical decision-making and conflict capability. Sources addressed three analytic questions; concepts were compared for overlap and distinction, then organized into a developmental framework and four propositions. Findings The framework explains how cognitive regulation, contextual and ethical interpretation and adaptive action are coordinated within conflict readiness. Cognitive load management helps preserve leadership discernment under pressure; leadership discernment determines what response a situation warrants; and conflict capability enables managers to select, adapt and enact that response. It distinguishes dynamic response within conflict episodes from longer-term capability development. Research limitations/implications As a conceptual paper, the study develops rather than empirically tests the framework. Future research can develop measures, test the propositions across contexts, examine boundary conditions and evaluate targeted development. Practical implicat…

title: Leveraging digital capabilities for supply chain recovery and renewal: the mediating roles of spontaneous and creative improvisation
abstract: Purpose Building on the dynamic capability view (DCV) and supply chain (SC) literature on digitalization, improvisation and resilience, we examined how different digital capabilities influence different post-disruption SC resilience outcomes (recovery and renewal) through distinct forms of improvisation in cross-border SCs. Design/methodology/approach Our sample comprises 217 matched Chinese supplier–buyer dyads, with buyers located in 66 countries. Confirmatory factor analysis and multiple regression were used to test the measurement model and hypothesized relationships, respectively. Robustness and endogeneity tests were also performed. Findings We find that digital market orientation is positively associated with creative improvisation, while its relationship with spontaneous improvisation is non-significant. In contrast, digital process innovation is positively associated with spontaneous improvisation, while its relationship with creative improvisation is non-significant. Furthermore, spontaneous improvisation is positively associated with SC recovery, while creative improvisation is positively associated with SC renewal. Creative improvisation mediates the relationship between digital market orientation and SC renewal, while spontaneous improvisation mediates the relationship between digital process innovation and SC recovery. Originality/value This study reveals distinct…
venue: International Journal of Operations & Production Management

title: Dynamical evolution and surface accretion of DART impact ejecta in the (65803) Didymos system
abstract: The DART spacecraft impacted Dimorphos, the small moonlet of the Didymos binary system, on 26 September 2022. The impact ejected dust, fragments, and boulders into the near-binary environment. In November 2026, ESA's Hera mission is expected to arrive at the binary system to characterise both asteroids and investigate the post-impact consequences in detail. We investigated the dynamical evolution of DART-generated impact ejecta and quantified their surface accretion patterns within the Didymos binary system. We constructed high-fidelity ejecta dynamics, including polyhedron asteroid gravity and solar radiation pressure with combined occultations. The initial conditions of the ejecta were generated from the observation-constrained velocity--size distribution and ejecta-cone geometry. In total, 20 million trajectories were integrated to characterise the ejecta evolution and surface accretion. More than 93.5% of DART-generated ejecta particles escape from the system within two years, while only approximately 0.002% remain in the near-binary environment. The deposited layer on Dimorphos reaches the order of 1.5 mm at mid-to-low latitudes. On Didymos, the accreted layer is mostly thinner than 0.3 mm, but it may reach 3--11.5 mm in a localised high-density region. Most DART-generated ejecta are removed from the binary system, while a small but dynamically meaningful subset remains ne…

title: When robots take the initiative: how robotic service proactivity shapes customer experience of hospitableness
abstract: Purpose Drawing on social response theory, this research aims to examine whether, how and when robotic service proactivity fosters customer experience of hospitableness. Design/methodology/approach A multistudy design consisting of three scenario-based experiments and one field validation survey was used to test the proposed conceptual model. Findings Customers reported a more intense experience of hospitableness when service robots displayed higher levels of proactivity. Automated social presence accounted for this effect, and the effect was amplified when robots possessed a more human-like appearance. Practical implications This research presents actionable insights for optimizing the coordinated management of robotic behaviors and appearances to enhance customer-robot interaction experiences. Originality/value This research extends research on service robots from static design to dynamic behavior, positioning robotic service proactivity as a key driver of customer experience of hospitableness. From the perspective of customer social responses, this study reveals automated social presence as the socio-emotional mechanism. It further establishes humanoid appearance as a moderating factor, demonstrating that proactive behavior yields greater benefits when robot form and behavior are aligned. These findings advance research on service robot form–behavior consistency and offer no…
venue: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management

title: Pola Manajemen Bisnis Rumah Makan Dirgahayu Sepapan
abstract: Several factors underpin the scope of the food and beverage service business: the substantial and ever-growing market potential, and the availability of the necessary equipment for serving food and beverages which constitutes an essential asset for an eatery. This study aims to examine the business management practices employed. Both qualitative and quantitative data were utilized in the research. The findings reveal a lack of clear role delineation among the various functional areas namely production, finance, marketing, and human resource management in the execution of business activities. This situation stems from the owner's tendency to dominate operations, thereby leaving employees with no opportunity to develop their skills.

title: Evaluation of Coasting Resistance in Heavy-Duty Vehicles Based on the Coasting Momentum Method and Coasting Equal Power Method
Imbalance of the coagulation-anticoagulation-fibrinolytic system: Pathogenesis and therapeutic approaches in progressive liver injury
abstract: The coagulation-anticoagulation-fibrinolysis system is essential for normal hemostasis, and its key components are predominantly synthesized in the liver. During the progression of liver injury, reduced synthesis and increased consumption of coagulation factors occur concurrently, leading to an imbalance between coagulation and anticoagulation, and the establishment of an unstable rebalanced state. At the systemic level, these derangements tend to manifest as a relative hypocoagulable phenotype with elevated bleeding tendency. In contrast, the intrahepatic microcirculation, characterized by tissue factor exposure and sluggish portal perfusion, preferentially promotes local prothrombotic changes and accumulation of coagulation factors, particularly during advanced cirrhotic stages, resulting in a regionally hypercoagulable milieu despite systemic coagulation instability. Combined with the reduced synthesis of anticoagulant factors, these changes may create a prothrombotic, low-flow microenvironment within the intrahepatic and portal venous compartments, which is closely associated with intrahepatic microcirculatory disturbances and portal vein thrombosis. Given the bidirectional interplay between this dynamic imbalance and liver injury progression, a thorough understanding of the underlying regulatory mechanisms and the development of targeted interventions are paramount for mit…

title: Barriers, biases, and the path to belonging: addressing the underrepresentation of women in the Australian property valuation profession
abstract: Purpose Strong evidence shows gender-diverse workforces bring real benefits to organisational performance, innovation, and stakeholder engagement. Despite this, women remain underrepresented in Australia's property valuation profession. This study explores the experiences and views of female valuers to understand the structural, cultural, and social factors keeping this imbalance in place, and to propose practical strategies for change. Design/methodology/approach This study used a qualitative approach, based on a focus group discussion with twelve female valuers from private and government valuation firms in Melbourne, Australia. Participants were purposively selected to include senior practitioners across different valuation specialisations. The data were analysed using Braun and Clarke (2006) six-phase thematic analysis approach. Findings The findings clearly reveal a profession still deeply characterised by male dominance, with gender inequality operating with particular intensity in the commercial valuation subsector. Persistent social and cultural biases, discriminatory recruitment and promotion practices, the grey ceiling, inflexible project structures, and unpaid caregiving burdens collectively limit the entry, advancement, and retention of female valuers industry-wide. Diversity efforts are widely seen as performative rather than substantive. A notable counter-narrativ…

title: Examination of personal data protection regimes in developing countries: comparative study of Malaysia, Pakistan and Bangladesh with reference to GDPR
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine and compare the personal data protection regimes of Malaysia, Pakistan and Bangladesh with the aim of identifying regulatory strengths, weaknesses and emerging trends in developing country approaches to privacy governance with reference to global data protection standards, particularly the European Union’s General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). Design/methodology/approach This paper adopts a doctrinal and comparative legal methodology, analyzing statutory frameworks, draft legislation and regulatory structures in the three jurisdictions. The comparison focuses on scope, individual rights, regulatory independence and enforcement mechanisms. Findings The analysis demonstrates that while all three jurisdictions reflect increasing convergence with international data protection principles, significant structural deficiencies remain. Malaysia’s regime is limited in scope to commercial transactions and excludes state actors. Pakistan’s framework is more expansive but remains unimplemented and institutionally uncertain. Bangladesh’s proposed legislation suffers from definitional ambiguity and extensive executive control. Compared with the GDPR, all three regimes exhibit weaknesses in accountability, regulatory independence and enforceability. Research limitations/implications This study focuses on three selected developing jurisdictions and relies…
venue: International Journal of Law and Management

title: Exploring the digital shift: an analytical study on the implementation of Construction 4.0 enabling technologies
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the evolving landscape of digital transformation in the construction industry, with a specific focus on the implementation and impact of Construction 4.0 enabling technologies. In addition, the study formulates a strategic framework aimed at facilitating the systematic and effective adoption of the Construction 4.0 concept across various segments of the construction sector. Design/methodology/approach A dual research methodology was used in this study, integrating both quantitative and qualitative approaches to ensure comprehensive data collection and analysis. A total of 256 respondents from 64 construction companies participated in the questionnaire survey, while expert interviews were conducted with 20 industry professionals who have been actively engaged in the implementation of Construction 4.0 technologies over the past three years. Findings The study revealed that building information modeling is the most extensively adopted Construction 4.0 technology across the surveyed construction firms. By contrast, cloud computing, big data analytics and cybersecurity were not reported as being used by the surveyed firms, indicating areas requiring further technological development and adoption. Research limitations/implications This study is subject to certain limitations. As it is based on self-reported data, there is a possibility of respon…
venue: Journal of Science and Technology Policy Management

title: BPJS Claim Receivables, Working Capital, and Operating Cash Flow at PKU Muhammadiyah Wonosobo
abstract: BPJS Kesehatan claim receivables represent a significant source of liquidity pressure for hospitals, as delays in reimbursement collection may constrain working capital and operating cash flow. This study examined the performance of BPJS Kesehatan claim receivables and their statistical associations with working capital and operating cash flow at PKU Muhammadiyah Wonosobo Hospital. A quantitative descriptive-associative research design was employed using 36 consecutive monthly financial statements covering January 2023 through December 2025. Receivables management performance was measured using receivables turnover (RTO) and days sales outstanding (DSO), while financial performance was assessed using working capital, the current ratio, and the operating cash flow ratio. Data were analyzed using descriptive trend analysis, Pearson correlation analysis, and separate simple linear regression models with IBM SPSS Statistics. RTO decreased from 6.35 times in 2023 to 5.89 times in 2025, while DSO increased from 57.52 to 61.96 days. Working capital declined from IDR 4.17 billion to IDR 4.00 billion, the current ratio decreased from 1.73 to 1.57, and the operating cash flow ratio fell from 0.38 to 0.22. RTO exhibited positive associations, whereas DSO demonstrated negative associations, with all three financial indicators. However, because DSO is mathematically related to RTO, the repo…
venue: Journal Research of Social Science, Economics, and Management

title: Substance versus symbolism: how ESG dimensions relate to financial performance in family firms
abstract: Purpose This study examines how ESG performance, environmental innovation, exposure to ESG controversies, and internal governance mechanisms are associated with the financial performance of listed family firms. Socioemotional wealth (SEW) is used as an interpretive lens rather than measured as a moderator. Design/methodology/approach A near-balanced panel of 83 firms from the Global 500 Family Business Index over 2016–2023 (662 firm-year observations) is analysed using two-way fixed effects models with Driscoll-Kraay standard errors. Robustness checks include clustered and bootstrap inference, lagged specifications and an alternative measure of controversy. Regional differences are examined in an exploratory pooled interaction model. Findings ESG performance is positively associated with Tobin's Q but not with accounting metrics. Environmental innovation is associated with higher ROE, although this association does not survive conservative inference. Controversy exposure is associated with lower ROA and ROE. The only result robust to every inference procedure concerns governance: where boards reach a critical mass of female directors, the market valuation of ESG is reversed rather than amplified. Practical implications ESG score optimisation should not be treated as a route to accounting value in family firms. Boards should not assume that formal gender diversity reinforces the…

title: Contextualizing consumer shyness in apparel retailing: scale validation and implications for decision-making styles
abstract: Purpose This study investigates the role of consumer shyness in apparel retailing by validating and contextualizing an existing consumer shyness scale within a setting characterized by high levels of social visibility and interpersonal interaction. It further examines how consumer shyness and extroversion influence consumer decision-making styles. Design/methodology/approach A multi-phase research design was employed. The consumer shyness construct was examined within the apparel retail context using qualitative and quantitative procedures. Established scales measuring consumer shyness, extroversion and decision-making styles were applied to two independent samples (NA = 928 and NB = 827). Structural equation modelling was used to compare models based on general shyness and context-specific consumer shyness. Findings Consumers with higher levels of consumer shyness tend to exhibit stronger brand and price consciousness, as well as greater confusion from overchoice, while showing lower tendencies toward hedonic shopping. A significant negative relationship between extroversion and consumer shyness was also confirmed. The findings indicate that context-specific consumer shyness provides stronger explanatory power for consumer decision-making styles than general shyness constructs. Research limitations/implications The study was conducted in Turkey, which may limit generalizabilit…
venue: Journal of Fashion Marketing and Management: An International Journal

title: Критерии оценки организационных структур управления нефтегазовых предприятий
abstract: Основная задача исследования, результаты которого приведены в статье, заключается в обосновании набора критериев оценки рациональности организационных структур управления (ОСУ) нефтегазовых предприятий. Критерии увязаны автором с четырьмя этапами управленческого цикла: планированием, организацией, мотивацией и контролем. Предложены девять критериев, характеризующих соответствие структуры стратегическим целям, факторам создания ценности, ресурсам, нормам управляемости, принципам взаимодействия подразделений, миссии предприятия, вовлеченности сотрудников, разделению операционной и развивающей деятельности, а также отсутствию дублирования контроля. Рассмотрены примеры применения критериев и типовые организационные несоответствия. Определены направления дальнейшей работы, в частности, по созданию методики количественной оценки рациональности ОСУ нефтегазовых предприятий. The main objective of the study, the results of which are presented in the article, is to substantiate a set of criteria for assessing the rationality of the organizational management structures (OMS) of oil and gas enterprises. The authors link the criteria to the four stages of the management cycle: planning, organization, motivation, and control. Nine criteria are proposed, characterizing the соответствие of the structure to strategic goals, value creation factors, resources, manageability standards, principles …
venue_publisher: Bashkir Presidential Academy of Public Administration and Management

title: Establishing a good practices repository to support health system learning in South Africa: methods, implementation processes and lessons learnt
abstract: Aim Health systems generate substantial knowledge through routine service delivery and local problem-solving, but effective practices are often poorly documented and shared. A mechanism for systematically identifying, documenting and disseminating such practices may strengthen health system learning. This paper describes the processes used to identify, assess and document good practices across South Africa’s health system, and the establishment of a national digital repository. Method A descriptive implementation study was undertaken from September 2024 to October 2025. A multi-source approach was used to identify and document good practices through: (1) a national call for submissions; (2) stakeholder engagement meetings in seven of the nine provinces; and (3) analysis of 20 routine district health indicators over six years (2018/19 to 2023/24) to identify districts demonstrating sustained improvement. Submitted practices were assessed against adapted World Health Organization good practice criteria. Districts whose indicators showed sustained improvement were contacted for follow-up interviews to identify activities contributing to improved performance. Validated practices were documented using standardised templates and uploaded to an open-access digital repository hosted on Scholastica. Results Overall, 58 good practices met the core assessment criteria. Of these, 16 met al…

title: Exploring what drives Finland’s journey toward sustainable and low-carbon growth
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the dynamic link between urbanization, economic expansion, renewable energy consumption, forest area and CO2 emissions in Finland from 1990 to 2022. Grounded in environmental economics and sustainability transition frameworks, it aims to address how these factors interact in the context of Finland’s carbon-neutral agenda and to identify key drivers influencing environmental sustainability. Design/methodology/approach The study uses time-series data to investigate long-term correlations between the variables, using specialized econometric approaches such as Canonical Cointegrating Regression, Fully Modified Ordinary Least Squares, as well as Dynamic Ordinary Least Squares. Findings The results show that urbanization, economic growth and forest area expansion contribute to increased CO2 emissions, while renewable energy consumption significantly reduces emissions. These outcomes highlight the critical mitigating role of renewable energy in achieving environmental sustainability and suggest that structural and policy factors must be carefully balanced to meet climate goals. Research limitations/implications The results imply that Finland should further strengthen renewable energy expansion as the most effective strategy for reducing CO2 emissions, supported by continued investment in clean energy technologies and improved energy efficiency sy…
venue: International Journal of Energy Sector Management

title: Collaborative Governance in Strengthening the Early Warning System (EWS) and the Impact of Floods on Communities in Special Areas of Jakarta
abstract: Background: Flooding remains a recurring hydrometeorological disaster in Jakarta, causing significant social, economic, and environmental impacts. Strengthening flood early warning systems (EWS) requires technological infrastructure and effective stakeholder collaboration. Objective: This study examines collaborative governance in strengthening flood EWS and proposes a collaborative model to mitigate flood impacts on communities. Methods: A descriptive qualitative approach was employed through in-depth interviews, observations, and document analysis. Data were analyzed using an interactive model supported by NVivo 15. Informants represented government agencies, BPBD, BMKG, the Water Resources Agency, communities, volunteers, the private sector, and academia. Results: Institutional Design emerged as the strongest dimension, supported by regulations, standard operating procedures, task allocation, coordination mechanisms, memoranda of understanding, command structures, and information dissemination. Conversely, Starting Conditions represented the weakest dimension due to resource disparities, capacity limitations, misaligned incentives, and insufficient operational trust among stakeholders. Although Jakarta possesses EWS infrastructure, including sensors, geospatial dashboards, command centers, and flood information applications, data integration and utilization remain suboptimal…

title: Rethinking physician–patient communication: exploring physicians’ use of AI in healthcare: a dual-factor perspective
abstract: Purpose This study aims to identify the physicians’ intentions to use artificial intelligence (AI) in order to provide digital information to physicians about their patients by the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology 2 and QSB theories. Design/methodology/approach To collect the necessary data, an electronic questionnaire was designed to survey 789 physicians working in Iraqi clinics and healthcare institutions. To analyze these data, a structural equation model was used using the AMOS.26 program. Findings The results revealed the importance of the study model in using AI technology in communication between physicians and patients. Research limitations/implications It is concluded that communication between physicians and their patients should be based on the use of AI technology, as the vast majority of physicians surveyed supported this. This indicates the need to use AI technology and its digital tools in physicians’ performance of their healthcare tasks (consultations, examinations) and, consequently, in providing treatment to patients. Furthermore, this study is not without its limitations, namely its focus on AI. Thus, it should focus on other digital technologies. Originality/value This research provides innovative value by bridging the digital transformation gap in digital healthcare systems for patients. It is the first study in Iraq to re-establish comm…

title: Cultural mediation of the impact of professional identity and social influence on clinical decision support system adoption: a study of European general practitioners
abstract: Purpose Clinical decision support systems (CDSS) are digital systems that enhance patient care by integrating established clinical knowledge with real-time patient information. Yet, CDSS face persistent challenges in achieving widespread adoption by physicians. This study seeks to deepen the understanding of general practitioners' (GPs) adoption behaviour by integrating micro-level determinants, namely the perceived support of GPs' professional identity and social influence with macro-level determinants of national culture. Design/methodology/approach This quantitative study used repeated cross-sectional data from 27 European countries. Structural equation modelling (SEM) was used to examine the effects of perceived support of professional identity, social influence and national culture on CDSS adoption by European GPs. Findings The findings from SEM suggest that GPs' perceptions of the support of their professional identity and of social influence as well as the values and beliefs of their national culture affect their adoption of CDSS, and that the effects of perceived support of professional identity and social influence are mediated by values and beliefs of national culture. Originality/value This study contributes to cross-cultural and information systems (IS) adoption research by addressing gaps in institutional theory and health IS (HIS) adoption. It examines both micro-…

title: Investigational drug services operations: Defining core and supplemental workload metrics
abstract: Abstract Purpose Investigational drug services (IDS) support highly complex and regulated aspects of clinical research, yet the absence of defined workload metrics limits clear and consistent understanding of IDS workload across pharmacy, research, and executive leadership. Staffing and resource requests, as well as being responsible for acceptance of new studies, require defensible, numerical workload data to secure leadership approval for additional resources. We developed a structured approach to IDS workload measurement that includes broadly applicable core metrics and site-specific supplemental metrics to support staffing justification, resource allocation, and operational planning. Summary A modified Delphi process informed by literature-identified metrics was used to achieve expert consensus on IDS workload definitions and metrics. Subject matter experts in IDS pharmacy practice and clinical research operations participated in iterative rounds of review. Metrics were categorized into core workload elements and supplemental metrics. Core metrics broadly describe site characteristics and day-to-day operations. Supplemental metrics capture study-specific, expanded services or site-derived time-based measures. Conclusion Organizing IDS workload into core and supplemental components provides a structured method to account for both routine operations and expanded study- or sit…

title: Health and related indicators: assessing the data foundation of a learning health system
abstract: Aim South Africa produces extensive routine, survey, surveillance and financial health data, but their value depends on translation into decisions that improve health and service delivery. This paper assesses whether available indicators support system learning across a continuum from data availability and signal identification, to interpretation, documented response, and demonstrated improvement. It describes key South African health and related indicators, assesses what they reveal about progress, inequity and system responsiveness, identifies data constraints, and examines where learning cycles are completed or break down. Method Secondary data were synthesised from routine health information systems, Statistics South Africa, disease registers, surveillance platforms, the National Treasury and international estimation series. Indicators were selected for continuity, policy relevance, currency and provincial disaggregation, with attention to source divergence, denominator effects, timeliness, completeness and disaggregation. Divergent estimates were presented side-by-side, and implausible values interrogated and flagged. Fourteen domains were assessed across three learning arcs: practice into data, data into knowledge, and knowledge into changed practice. Results Indicators show simultaneous progress and persistent strain. Life expectancy continues to recover; HIV diagnosis a…

title: Artificial intelligence in marketing: a knowledge management perspective on decision-making
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how artificial intelligence (AI) is implemented across marketing functions and analyses how the knowledge associated with AI is managed. It also explores how AI-related knowledge supports marketing decision-making and organizational learning while identifying future research lines for strengthening knowledge management (KM) practices in marketing contexts. Design/methodology/approach This study follows a two-stage research design. First, a systematic literature review is developed to identify and classify the main variables linking AI, marketing and KM. These variables are coded into a binary matrix and analyzed through multiple correspondence analysis under a homogeneity analysis by alternating least squares, implemented in R and Visual Studio Code. Findings AI adoption in marketing is primarily associated with four interconnected areas: customer-oriented personalization and behavioral response, KM foundations, strategic knowledge-based decision support and AI-enabled operational marketing applications. The analysis shows meaningful associations between AI use and customer knowledge, market knowledge, predictive analytics, personalization and strategic marketing capabilities. Originality/value This study contributes to the intersection of AI, marketing and KM by conceptualizing AI in marketing as a knowledge-based organizational mechanism rat…

title: Risk factors analysis and management strategy optimization for postoperative complications in neonatal necrotizing enterocolitis: A single-center retrospective study
abstract: BACKGROUND Neonatal necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is severe with high morbidity and mortality, and postoperative complications seriously affect prognosis. AIM To investigate the risk factors for postoperative complications in neonates with necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) and provide evidence for optimizing perioperative management. METHODS Clinical data of 62 NEC infants undergoing exploratory laparotomy at the Children’s Hospital of Soochow University from August 2022 to September 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. The patients were divided into complication and non-complication groups based on the occurrence of major postoperative complications. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent risk factors for postoperative complications. RESULTS Among the 62 infants, 28 (45.16%) developed major postoperative complications, with septic shock being the most common (25.81%). Combined univariate and multivariate logistic regression analysis showed that preoperative hemodynamic instability [odds ratio (OR) = 5.32, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.84-15.39], intestinal resection length > 30 cm (OR = 4.18, 95%CI: 1.51-11.56), albumin < 30 g/L on postoperative day 3 (OR = 3.77, 95%CI: 1.42-10.00), and postoperative mechanical ventilation duration > 7 days (OR = 3.25, 95%CI: 1.21-8.74) were independent risk factors for postoperative co…

title: Hidden nonlinearity in VAIC research: a meta-analytic specification audit of intellectual capital and firm performance in emerging economies
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to reassess evidence on value added intellectual coefficient (VAIC) and firm performance in emerging economies by examining the algebraic dependence between human capital efficiency (HCE) and structural capital efficiency (SCE). Design/methodology/approach The study combines analytical derivation with a systematic review and model-level meta-analytic specification audit of 94 articles, published through 31 December 2025, and 644 regression models. The 16-case coefficient-sign audit covers 357 models from 77 articles. A source-validated random-effects synthesis covers 159 paired effects from 32 articles, with article-level dependence adjustments and sensitivity analyses. Findings Because SCE = 1–1/HCE, regressions jointly including original HCE and SCE are nonlinear HCE models, not linear models of independent components. SCE is significant in 201 of 357 classifiable models (56.3%; article-weighted prevalence: 54.8%). At the HCE mean, 22 of 208 comparisons (10.6%) reverse the sign implied by the published HCE coefficient. Dependence-adjusted pooled associations are r = 0.223 for the linear HCE term and r = −0.133 for the hidden reciprocal term, with substantial heterogeneity. Research limitations/implications The evidence base is limited to published articles whose full texts could be retrieved, and incomplete reporting restricts effect-size conversion an…
venue: VINE Journal of Information and Knowledge Management Systems

title: Optimising resource use in audiology and speech therapy practice in South Africa: sectoral challenges, adaptive strategies and system-level implications
abstract: Purpose Efficient and contextually responsive resource utilisation is central to sustainable healthcare delivery, particularly in resource-constrained settings. Within South Africa's dual healthcare system, characterised by structural inequities, there is limited evidence on how practitioners operationalise resource use in practice. This study explored challenges associated with productive resource utilisation among audiology and speech therapy practitioners and identified strategies to enhance efficiency and sustainability across sectors. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative design was employed using semi-structured interviews with 92 practitioners across public and private sectors and urban, peri-urban, and rural contexts in four South African provinces (Gauteng, KwaZulu-Natal, Western Cape, and Limpopo). Data were analysed thematically using Braun and Clarke's framework, with exploratory inferential analyses examining sectoral differences. Qualitative codes were quantified at participant level to allow descriptive and exploratory statistical comparison across sectors. Findings Four themes emerged. First, public sector resource constraints included equipment shortages (80%), staffing limitations (75%) and budgetary constraints (85%), particularly in rural areas (χ2 = 17.89, p < 0.01). Second, private sector optimisation strategies emphasised efficiency through technol…
venue: International Journal of Health Care Quality Assurance

title: Pink Tax Perception, Price Accountability, and Purchase Intention Among Personal Care Consumers
abstract: Pink tax is not treated as a formal tax, but as consumers’ perception of possible gender-based price differences in products marketed to women compared with comparable products marketed to men or gender-neutral consumers. This study examines the relationship between Pink Tax Perception, Price Accountability, and Purchase Intention among personal care consumers. This study uses a quantitative survey approach involving 201 valid respondents in Indonesia who had purchased and compared personal care products. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling. The results show that Pink Tax Perception has a positive and significant effect on Price Accountability, and Price Accountability has a positive and significant effect on Purchase Intention. However, Pink Tax Perception does not have a significant direct effect on Purchase Intention. The mediation test shows that Price Accountability significantly mediates the relationship between Pink Tax Perception and Purchase Intention. These findings indicate that consumers’ purchase intention is shaped not directly by pink tax perception, but through their evaluation of whether pricing practices are fair, transparent, and accountable.

title: Between-hospital variation in prices for robot-assisted surgery: a multilevel analysis of Korea’s 2026 non-covered price disclosure data
Price under pressure: BayanMart’s pricing dilemma in a volatile economy
abstract: Learning outcomes The key learning objectives are as follows: Case overview/synopsis In May 2026, Miguel Santos, Chief Executive Officer of BayanMart Retail Corporation, faced a critical pricing dilemma as the economic fallout from the 2026 Iran war intensified across the Philippines. Rising fuel prices, inflation, peso depreciation and supplier price increases significantly raised procurement and logistics costs, while weakening consumer purchasing power resulted in smaller basket sizes, downtrading, lower store traffic and growing demand for private-label products. In April 2026, BayanMart’s revenues and gross margins had declined sharply, raising concerns about the sustainability of its low-margin, high-volume business model. At the same time, competitors adopted divergent pricing strategies, creating further uncertainty in the market. As Santos prepared for an important board meeting, he had to evaluate whether BayanMart should pass rising costs on to consumers, absorb them to protect customer loyalty or adopt a hybrid approach. The case explores the trade-offs between profitability, customer retention, competitive positioning and long-term resilience in a volatile retail environment. Complexity academic level This case is suited for MBA and undergraduate courses (including online courses) in Marketing, Strategy and Retail Management. It can be used to discuss pricing under…

title: Evaluating image embeddings and metadata for NFT price prediction using temporal validation
abstract: Abstract Images and categorical traits provide closely related descriptions of profile picture non-fungible tokens (NFTs), making the incremental predictive value of image embeddings uncertain. We compare metadata-only, image-only, early-fusion and weighted late-fusion models for Bored Ape Yacht Club (BAYC) and Mutant Ape Yacht Club (MAYC) using eight regression families and seven visual encoders. Models are selected on pre-2025 data and retrospectively evaluated from January 2025 to April 2026. Selected models in all four groups outperform a zero log-relative-price benchmark. Relative to metadata, early fusion reduces root mean squared error (RMSE) by 0.09% in BAYC and 0.95% in MAYC; late fusion increases BAYC RMSE by 0.07% and reduces MAYC RMSE by 0.70%. Sensitivity analyses assess unseen tokens, matched regression families, transaction-row versus count-weighted fitting, and full reselection under stricter cleaning. For unseen tokens, exploratory 95% fusion-versus-metadata intervals include zero in both collections. Metadata-only partial least squares (PLS) outperforms CLIP–PLS early fusion in MAYC. Across two stricter cleaning variants, 13 of 16 representative configurations change relative to a common base-clean control; fusion improvements are not consistently supported after reselection. Some tree-based comparisons are implementation-sensitive. The results do not establis…

title: Zero price or token price? The impact of bundle promotional format on promotional attractiveness and value discounting
abstract: Purpose This study aims to explore the relative attractiveness of freebie (e.g. “buy one, get one free”) and token-price (e.g. “buy one, get the second one for only 1¢”) promotions in the short run and value discounting effect for the separate items in the long run. Design/methodology/approach Two imaginary-scenario and two incentive-compatible experiments test the hypotheses. Findings Token-price promotions are more attractive than freebie promotions no matter if the supplemental item is identical to the focal item or not. Moreover, when the two items are identical, consumers who encounter a token-price (vs freebie) promotion express stronger value discounting for the focal item. This effect reverses when the items are nonidentical. Research limitations/implications Future research should examine whether the bundle promotional format effect differs with the amount of the token price and the complementarity of the focal and supplemental items. Practical implications Practitioners can draw on the findings to determine when to use freebie or token-price promotions and how to adjust bundle promotional strategies according to the type of the supplemental item. Originality/value This study improves understanding of the effects of freebie and token-price promotions, especially over the long-term. Based on mental accounting theory, the authors build a comprehensive framework that expl…

title: Standardized Preprocedure Protocolling of Stereotactic Breast Biopsies Enables Device-Level Supply Chain Forecasting: A Multisite Quality Improvement Analysis
abstract: Background: Breast imaging depends on single-use, vendor-proprietary consumables produced by a concentrated set of manufacturers. During supply shortages in 2026, healthcare organizations faced urgent pressure to shift from reactive to proactive inventory management. Stereotactic breast biopsy needle shortages revealed that traditional forecasting based on procedure volume lacks the granularity needed for device-specific demand. We aimed to enable device-level forecasting through standardized preprocedure protocolling. Methods: In a retrospective analysis of 1,456 stereotactic biopsies across 4 breast imaging sites (June 2025 to June 2026), compliance with a standardized electronic protocolling tool that captured lesion count and needle size (standard vs. petite) was assessed. Compliance rates across sites were compared using chi-square analysis, monthly trends were tracked using run charts, and root cause analysis was conducted to identify barriers at the lowest performing site. Epic reports operationalized protocolled data into historical use tracking and 30-day forward demand forecasts. Results: The overall protocolling compliance rate was 62.7% (913 of 1,456 cases), with striking variation across sites. Specifically, sites A-C achieved 97.3-99.2% compliance, whereas site D (the highest volume site, with 57 cases per month) achieved only 23.4% compliance (c² = 865.7, p < 0.0…

Stacking ensemble-based predictive maintenance framework on AI4I datasets in IIoT systems for forecasting machine failures
abstract: Purpose The current study proposes building a strong predictive maintenance (PdM) model for industrial systems through the use of ensemble machine learning models to forecast equipment failures before they happen. The research emphasizes enhancing the reliability during operation, minimizing downtime and offering a scalable solution to fill the gap between theoretical studies and real-world industrial applications in the Industry 5.0 era. Design/methodology/approach Two benchmark datasets: AI4I 2020 and its extended variant AI4I Predictive Maintenance Dataset with Irregularities (PMDI) are employed to verify the proposed approach. The research undertakes thorough data pre-processing, such as label encoding, feature scaling and Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique for handling class imbalance and data quality problems. Three heavy-hitting gradient boosting algorithms: XGBoost, LightGBM and CatBoost are employed as base learners in a stacking ensemble, with logistic regression as the meta-learner. The performance of the model is tested rigorously by Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-score and Receiver Operating Characteristic-Area Under the Curve (ROC-AUC). Findings Experimental results indicate that stacking ensemble outperforms standalone base models consistently and attains 99.16% accuracy for the AI4I 2020 dataset and 99.60% accuracy for the AI4I PMDI dataset with ROC-AUC…
venue: Journal of Quality in Maintenance Engineering

title: Clinical prediction model for inguinal hernia recurrence risk after transabdominal preperitoneal hernia repair surgery in elderly patients
abstract: BACKGROUND Inguinal hernia is a common surgical condition in elderly individuals. Postoperative recurrence after laparoscopic transabdominal preperitoneal hernia repair (TAPP) remains an important clinical challenge. However, reliable predictive tools to assess the risk of recurrence are limited. AIM To establish and validate a clinical prediction model for the risk of recurrence after TAPP in elderly patients with inguinal hernia. METHODS Data from 300 elderly patients with inguinal hernia admitted to the Affiliated Hospital of Jiujiang University between January 2023 and January 2025 were retrospectively collected. All patients underwent TAPP in the hospital and were followed up for 24-72 months postoperatively. Inguinal hernia recurrence was observed; patients were subsequently divided into recurrence and non-recurrence groups. Differences in the general data between the two groups were compared. Logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with postoperative recurrence, and these multivariate factors were incorporated into R software to establish a visualized nomogram model. The patients were randomly divided into training and validation sets at a ratio of 7:3. Receiver operating characteristic curve, clinical calibration curve, and decision curve analysis were used to evaluate the diagnostic efficacy and clinical net benefit of the prediction model. RESULTS …

title: A physics-informed surrogate model for rapid prediction and source inference of pollutant dispersion in complex urban environments
Survey-based uncertainty assessment and FEINN prediction in Indian construction projects
abstract: The Indian construction industry plays an important role in economic growth but faces delays, cost overruns, and performance inefficiencies due to uncertainties in material availability, labour, regulations, and environmental conditions. This manuscript presents a survey-based assessment of key uncertainty factors affecting construction project performance in India and develops a predictive model based on the identified factors. A structured questionnaire, developed from an extensive literature review, was administered to 50 engineers at a leading Indian construction firm, achieving a 90% response rate. Exploratory factor analysis (EFA), Kaiser–Meyer–Olkin, and Bartlett’s test were employed to identify and validate the major uncertainty dimensions. The novelty lies in integrating statistically validated uncertainty dimensions extracted through EFA with a finite element interpolated neural network (FEINN)-based predictive framework, combining interpretable survey analytics with non-linear project performance prediction. The research uncovers major uncertainty dimensions including financial instability, labour shortages, material availability, and regulatory delays. The FEINN model achieved a lower prediction error with a root mean squared error of 0.12 and mean absolute error of 0.07, and a mean absolute percentage error of 2.7%, outperforming benchmarks. This approach offers va…

title: Recurrence risk prediction of small-molecule drugs plus chemo in postoperative gastric cancer: Retrospective analysis via molecular markers
abstract: BACKGROUND Gastric cancer (GC) exhibits high postoperative recurrence rates even after adjuvant small-molecule and chemotherapy therapy. Reliable molecular markers are urgently needed to accurately predict recurrence risk and guide precise clinical treatment. AIM To investigate the clinical value of molecular markers in predicting recurrence risk in patients with postoperative GC receiving small-molecule drugs combined with chemotherapy. METHODS The clinical data of 136 patients with postoperative GC who received adjuvant therapy with small-molecule drugs combined with chemotherapy at our hospital between September 2023 and January 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. Based on the follow-up outcomes, the patients were divided into a recurrence group (38 cases) and a non-recurrence group (98 cases). Baseline data and molecular marker test results were compared between the groups. Factors influencing recurrence after treatment and the predictive value of molecular markers for recurrence risk were analyzed. RESULTS There were no significant differences in baseline data, including sex, body mass index, primary tumor location, The Cancer Genome Atlas subtype, or serum levels of carcinoembryonic antigen, alpha-fetoprotein, and CA125, between the two groups (P > 0.05). The recurrence group showed significantly higher proportions of age ≥ 60 years, poorly differentiated tumors, TNM stag…

title: Optical imaging framework for melt pool monitoring and bead geometry prediction in blown powder directed energy deposition
abstract: Abstract Blown powder laser directed energy deposition (DED-LP) is an emerging additive manufacturing process with applications in both new part manufacture and repair of high-value components. However, the deposition of consistent bead geometry requires precise control of melt pool dynamics. While in-situ monitoring methods have been developed, linking melt pool optical signals to solidified geometry remains an open challenge. Monocular imaging offers a low-cost, minimally invasive sensing approach, yet is inherently indirect due to projection effects and process-induced optical variability. This work presents a monitoring framework to interpret melt pool images by analytical and data-driven means. Contours detected from intensity-based image segmentation are translated to world coordinates using affine projection to provide calibration-based geometric proxies for comparison with solidified bead geometry. At nominal printing conditions, the analytical approach yielded mean absolute percentage errors of 2.5 % for bead width and 16.2 % for bead height. The affine projection method captured trends in solidified bead geometry across the traverse speed and laser power ranges investigated within the material-specific operating envelope. To refine estimates, a Gaussian process regression model (GPR) was trained on image-derived features and process conditions. GPR achieved a mean abs…

title: Mortality prediction in immune TTP remains challenging despite artificial intelligence advances
Adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference systems with improved optimisation for fibre-reinforced polymer-confined concrete strength prediction
abstract: Fibre-reinforced polymer (FRP)-confined concrete is often applied in engineering practice where structures are damaged. However, research on the behaviour of FRP-confined damaged concrete remains relatively limited. In this study, a machine learning approach was adopted to develop a unified model for the ultimate strength of damaged concrete, and a practical formula was derived for rapid strength estimation in engineering applications. To enhance the optimisation capability, the arithmetic optimisation algorithm (AOA) was first improved (IAOA) by incorporating the optimal neighbourhood learning strategy and a crisscross search mechanism. Then the algorithm is hybridised with adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference systems (ANFIS) for predicting the strength of FRP-confined damaged and undamaged concrete. The performance of the ANFIS-IAOA was compared with that of four other traditional ANFIS algorithms, namely ANFIS-particle swarm optimisation, ANFIS-grey wolf optimisation, ANFIS-genetic algorithm and ANFIS-AOA. 736 existing experimental data of FRP-confined damaged and undamaged concrete were collected to train and test the algorithms. Metrics including convergence speed and error evaluation factors were used to assess the performance of the algorithms. The results showed that the ANFIS-IAOA was applicable to predict the FRP-confined concrete strength and outperformed the other four hy…
