Comparison of five commonly used survival prediction tools (KPS, PPS, ECOG, PPI, and PaP) for 7‑day, 14‑day, and 30‑day mortality risk in children with advanced cancer receiving palliative care: a single‑center retrospective cohort study
abstract: Abstract Background Survival prediction is a core issue in pediatric palliative care, yet no specific tool has been developed for this population. The predictive value of five adult‑derived tools—KPS(Karnofsky Performance Scale), PPS(Palliative Performance Scale), ECOG(Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group Performance Status), PPI(Palliative Prognostic Index), and PaP (Palliative Prognostic Score), have not been adequately validated in pediatric end‑of‑life populations. Objective To systematically compare the predictive value of these five tools for 7-day, 14-day, and 30-day mortality risk in children with advanced cancer receiving palliative care, and to explore the independent prognostic value of clinician-predicted survival (CPS), a core component of PaP. Methods This single-center retrospective cohort study included children with stage IV malignant tumors admitted to the palliative care unit of West China Fourth Hospital, Sichuan University, between January 2020 and March 2026. Survival differences were analyzed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards regression, with the proportional hazards assumption verified by Schoenfeld residuals and time-dependent interaction terms. ROC curves were constructed for 7-, 14-, and 30-day mortality as binary outcomes; AUCs were compared using DeLong’s test. Precision-recall (PR) curves and AUPRCs were additionally used to address out…

title: Genome-wide association studies and genomic prediction for key ornamental traits in tetraploid pot carnation
abstract: Abstract Background Carnation ( Dianthus caryophyllus L.) is one of the most commercially important ornamental crops worldwide. Similar to many ornamental species, genomic selection has yet to be widely adopted as a breeding tool in carnation. Moreover, the widespread development and commercialization of polyploid carnation cultivars makes their genomic study particularly relevant. In this study, we investigate the genetic architecture of key ornamental traits in a tetraploid pot carnation diversity panel using genome-wide association studies (GWAS), and evaluate the potential of genomic prediction for ornamental trait improvement in this panel. For genomic prediction, we assessed three SNP marker encodings capturing different allele dosage information, a pseudo-diploid encoding, a tetraploid additive dosage encoding, and an encoding accounting for both additive and non-additive genetic effects. In addition, we carried out a GWAS-assisted genomic prediction by fitting top-scoring GWAS markers as fixed effects to the genomic prediction model. Results Through GWAS, we identified potential genomic regions of interest associated with seven of the eight traits studied. Genomic prediction achieved moderate to high prediction accuracy across traits and encodings, ranging on average from 0.54 to 0.82 for flowering-related traits (earliness, flower filling, flower count, and flower size…

title: BREST-AI: Three-year breast cancer risk prediction from screening mammograms
abstract: Abstract Accurate assessment of breast cancer risk is essential for risk-stratified screening strategies. We developed BREST-AI, a deep-learning model that predicts three-year breast cancer risk from negative screening mammograms. Model development used a curriculum-learning strategy and data from 65,419 women; the model was trained on 58,591 women (9020 cancer, 1633 benign, and 47,938 three-year cancer-free). In the external UK case–control validation (1899 cases and 5697 matched controls), BREST-AI achieved an AUC of 0.751 (95% CI 0.738–0.764), outperforming Mirai (0.700, 95% CI 0.687–0.714; p < 0.001). In a US external cohort (97 cases and 291 matched controls), AUCs were 0.670 (95% CI 0.609–0.731) for BREST-AI and 0.633 (95% CI 0.570–0.696) for Mirai ( p = 0.199); this analysis is underpowered to detect modest differences and should be interpreted as exploratory. In a UK cross-vendor external cohort acquired on Siemens systems (400 cases and 1200 matched controls), cross-vendor domain shift modestly reduced discrimination, but BREST-AI still exceeded Mirai (AUC 0.719 versus 0.685; p = 0.019). When projecting case–control results to the English screening prevalence (8 cancers per 1000 examinations), BREST-AI yielded an estimated positive predictive value of 8.0% and a relative risk of 10.1 at a high-risk operating point defined by 99% specificity. These prevalence-adjusted e…

title: Real-World Patterns of Immune-Related Toxicity in Gastrointestinal Cancer Patients Treated with Immunotherapy: A service evaluation
abstract: Introduction: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed cancer treatment and are now the standard therapy for several gastrointestinal (GI) malignancies. Although they can improve survival, ICIs are associated with immune-related adverse events (irAEs) that may affect multiple organ systems, potentially impacting treatment continuity and quality of life. Gastrointestinal toxicities, including diarrhoea and colitis, are among the most frequently reported adverse effects. As the use of ICIs expands, understanding the incidence and management of irAEs in routine clinical practice is essential. This service evaluation aimed to quantify ICI use in GI cancers at a tertiary cancer centre, determine the proportion of patients who developed irAEs, and describe referral and management patterns. Methodology: A retrospective observational evaluation was conducted at a London-based hospital. Electronic health records were reviewed to identify patients with GI cancers treated with ICIs between October 2023 and October 2025. A subsequent subgroup analysis was performed for patients who developed irAEs. Data collected included irAE presentation, affected organ system, CTCAE grade, referral source, specialist involvement, and management, including hospital admission, treatment, follow-up, and ICI rechallenge. Findings were summarised using descriptive statistics. Results: Fifty patie…

title: Belief, forgiveness and karma: unpacking customer incivility following service failures
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the association between religious belief and customer incivility following a service failure. It examines lower situational interpersonal forgiveness toward frontline employees as an indirect pathway and investigates belief in karma as a boundary condition for this relationship. Design/methodology/approach Three studies examined the proposed model in service-failure contexts. Studies 1 (n = 202) and 2 (n = 279) used restaurant and hotel scenarios, respectively, to examine the indirect association involving religious belief and customer incivility intentions and the moderating role of belief in karma. Study 3 (n = 297) used a Prolific experiment that made karma-related action–consequence considerations salient. Mediation and moderated-mediation effects were tested using PROCESS with 5,000 bootstrap samples. Findings Across three studies, stronger religious belief was associated with intentions to engage in customer incivility, indirectly through lower situational interpersonal forgiveness toward the frontline employee. In Study 2, this indirect association was weaker among customers reporting stronger belief in karma. In Study 3, it was weaker when karma-related considerations were made situationally salient. Practical implications Following a service failure, organizations can state openly and for all customers, the standard of respectful cond…

title: Public visibility of digital user-service entry points on Chinese academic library websites
abstract: Purpose Academic library websites increasingly operate as first-contact points for digital reference and user services. This study examines how selected user-service entry points are made publicly visible on the official library websites of Chinese second-round Double First-Class universities. Design/methodology/approach A structured, codebook-guided, non-login website audit was conducted across the full 147-university policy-defined sample frame. The final analytic set contained 141 fully codable library web presences. A two-author coding-and-verification workflow was used: one author completed first-pass coding, while the other independently checked coded values for all 147 institutions, evidence URLs, evidence summaries and case notes against official public pages. Ambiguous cases were resolved through codebook clarification and consensus. Findings The results show a support-oriented but uneven public service layer. Consult or contact links and off-campus access guidance were the most consistently visible features, followed by FAQ/help and account-related access. Search and reservation services were less consistently exposed. English-language entry was limited, no visible accessibility or disability statement was observed and visible AI-supported service entry remained uncommon. Practical implications The findings offer a practical benchmark for academic libraries to examine…

title: Knowledge flows and service encounters in digital retail: a bibliometric mapping of cross-buying and customer relationship expansion research (2000–2026)
abstract: Purpose This study aims to map the intellectual structure, knowledge flows and thematic evolution of cross-buying and customer relationship expansion research in digital retail and service encounter contexts from 2000 to 2026. Design/methodology/approach A bibliometric science-mapping design guided by the SPAR-4-SLR protocol was adopted. Data were retrieved from Scopus using a TITLE-ABS-KEY search. After applying year, subject area, document type, language and source type filters and removing one duplicate DOI record, the final data set comprised 567 Scopus-indexed journal documents. “Bibliometrix” and “VOSviewer” were used for performance analysis, co-citation analysis, bibliographic coupling, keyword co-occurrence, temporal overlay, thematic mapping and thematic evolution. Findings The field is rooted in customer lifetime value, customer equity, CRM, service quality, satisfaction, loyalty and relationship marketing. Recent research fronts increasingly emphasise digital service quality, customer engagement, e-commerce, omnichannel service encounters, artificial intelligence, machine learning and predictive analytics. Thematic evolution shows a shift from firm-centric customer valuation and retention models toward digitally mediated, experience-driven and analytics-enabled relationship expansion. Practical implications Managers should treat cross-buying as a relationship-expans…

title: Intelligent workspaces: how AI tools are changing service models and workforce skills in academic libraries
abstract: Purpose This study investigates how artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming service models, workflows, and workforce roles in academic libraries in Saudi Arabia. It examines the extent to which AI adoption influences service delivery, professional responsibilities, staff competencies, organizational readiness, and the development of intelligent library workspaces. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts a qualitative descriptive design based on twenty semi-structured interviews with librarians, information technology staff, and administrative personnel working in academic libraries in Saudi Arabia. Participants were purposively selected based on their direct experience with AI-supported tools and technology-enabled library services. The interview data were analyzed thematically following Braun and Clarke's framework to identify patterns relating to AI-tool adoption, service transformation, workforce competencies, staff readiness, and implementation challenges. Findings The findings reveal four interrelated dimensions of AI-driven transformation in academic libraries. First, AI tools such as chatbots, intelligent discovery systems, automated search applications, and plagiarism-detection tools are increasingly embedded in routine library operations. Second, AI is contributing to more automated, personalized, responsive, and digitally mediated service models. Third, work…

title: Advancing phygital service research (PSR): key streams and future research directions
abstract: Purpose This editorial article aims to establish phygital service research (PSR) as a distinct and integrative academic discipline. It synthesizes the contributions of the special issue to consolidate scattered knowledge, organize emerging themes and set a comprehensive agenda to guide future scholarship across blended physical-digital service ecosystems. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on the 18 contributions published in the special issue “Phygital Service Research (PSR) for Positive Marketplace Experiences: Integrating Physical and Digital Realms with Human-Centric Approaches,” this article develops an integrative synthesis of the emerging PSR literature. The papers are classified into core thematic areas and used to identify future research trajectories for deepening theoretical foundations, broadening ecosystem-level analysis and strengthening understanding of societal and cross-contextual implications. Findings The editorial identifies five primary research streams shaping current PSR: the intellectual architecture of phygital service ecosystems; human-first experience design; frontline employee experience and phygital organizational governance; transformative phygital service research; and phygital well-being paradoxes alongside dark-side tensions. It shows a paradigm shift in PSR toward long-term human flourishing, actor agency and systemic equilibrium. Research lim…

title: Molecular Structure Modification and Performance Regulation of Highly Flexible Poly(ester-imide)s with Low Dielectric Constant and Low Dissipation Factor
abstract: Abstract Inspired by the excellent dielectric properties and low moisture uptake of liquid-crystalline polymers (LCPs), ester units are introduced into polyimide (PI) backbones to develop poly(ester-imide)s (PEIs) for high-frequency communication dielectrics. Though PEIs show reduced dissipation factor (Df) and hygroscopicity relative to traditional PIs, the intrinsic rigidity and polarity of ester groups lead to relatively high dielectric constant (Dk) and low ductility, restricting their practical use in 5G/6G complex service environments. Herein, three dual-ester-functionalized diamine monomers are rationally designed and synthesized, which are polymerized with terephthaloyl bis(trimellitate) dianhydride (TAHQ) to yield four structurally modified MPEI films: ABHQ-TAHQ, Me-ABHQ-TAHQ, 6H-ABHQ-TAHQ, and 6F-ABHQ-TAHQ. XRD, POM, and AFM demonstrate that molecular-structure regulation can tailor the condensed-state and aggregation structures of polymer chains and improve overall performances synergistically. At 10 GHz, 6F-ABHQ-TAHQ exhibits ultralow Dk (2.93), ultralow Df (0.001 56), and excellent humidity resistance. Me-ABHQ-TAHQ and 6H-ABHQ-TAHQ achieve moderate Dk reduction with slightly elevated dissipation factors. All substituents greatly enhance the low elongation at break of pristine PEI in the order 6F (28%) > 6H (20%) > Me (11%) > PEI (6%). Meanwhile, all modifi…

title: Time of day metabolism and endocrine regulation of immune health
abstract: The immune system is a dynamic, energy-dependent network regulated by temporal biology. Advances in circadian biology have enabled the synchronizing of critical immune parameters such as metabolism, endocrine secretions, surveillance, tissue repair, and adaptation to environmental cycles. Here, we propose a metabolomic, and endocrine, chromodynamic model of immune health, based on time-of-day rhythms. Immune resilience is defined by synchronization among three groups of oscillators i) the central circadian clocks, ii) food-entrainable metabolic oscillators, iii) peripheral cellular clocks. The model provides a framework to optimize these interconnected systems to maintain metabolic efficiency, minimize unnecessary inflammation, and enable precise immune responses through temporal gating. External factors of modern lifestyle disruptions, including irregular feeding patterns, sleep deprivation, and chronic stress, induce internal circadian desynchrony, contributing to persistent low-grade inflammation, metabolic dysfunction, immune aging, and chronic non-communicable diseases. We propose that immune health is characterized not merely by the absence of disease, but by stable circadian phase coherence, low inflammatory noise, and adaptive immune resilience. We have listed some chrono-biomarkers of metabolomic and endocrine parameters that may provide a functional assessment of immu…

title: The VariableTNG project: Mass-dependent regulation of galaxy morphology by baryonic feedback
abstract: Galaxy morphology is shaped by both assembly history and baryonic processes, but their relative roles remain uncertain. We used the VariableTNG (VTNG) simulation suite to quantify how systematic variations in baryonic feedback regulate the morphological diversity of galaxies, while keeping the initial conditions fixed. VTNG is a suite of cosmological magnetohydrodynamic simulations performed with the moving-mesh code AREPO , in which eight parameters governing stellar and active galactic nucleus (AGN) feedback are varied. At z=1, we quantified galaxy morphology using the kinematic indicators κ_̊m co and v/σ, together with the structural indicator c/a. We find that baryonic feedback produces substantial morphological diversity even among galaxies with identical large-scale initial conditions. The dominant regulating mechanism depends strongly on stellar mass. For M_* łesssim 10^ 11 ̊m M_⊙ , morphology is primarily controlled by the supernova temperature T_̊m SN: higher T_̊m SN delays early star formation, promotes the build-up of a denser and more rotationally supported gas reservoir, and favours the subsequent growth of stellar discs through in situ star formation. At higher masses, morphology becomes increasingly sensitive to AGN feedback, especially the quasar-mode coupling efficiency ε_̊m f,high. A higher ε_̊m f,high suppresses early black hole growth and thus weakens the la…

title: Parallel Spatial–Frequency Diffractive Neural Networks for Autonomous-Driving Visual Understanding
abstract: Abstract Diffractive neural networks (DNNs) offer a promising route toward high-throughput, low-power optical computing; however, their application to autonomous-driving perception remains limited by insufficient representational capacity for complex scenes, owing to their relatively simple architectures and reliance on spatial-domain information alone. Here, we propose a spatial–frequency diffractive neural network (SFDNN) architecture that jointly exploits spatial- and frequency-domain information through two parallel sub-DNN branches. By leveraging the complementarity of these two domains, the proposed architecture improves feature separability and enhances perception performance, thereby outperforming conventional DNNs in the autonomous-driving segmentation task. Numerical results show that, under the same modulation-layer constraint, the SFDNN consistently surpasses single-domain models in segmentation tasks, improving reconstruction fidelity and spatial overlap over the best single-domain baseline by 10.9% and 23.2%, respectively. The framework further demonstrates strong generalization to traffic sign classification, achieving accuracies of up to 93.67%. Experimentally, we validate the proposed framework using a hybrid optical–digital system and demonstrate reliable target-region segmentation in a physical optical setup. Furthermore, a micrometer-scale SFDNN chip fabrica…

title: Communicative strategy selection in language anxiety: eye-tracking evidence of EFL learners’ multimodal pragmatic regulation
Other side of the coin: intrapersonal effects of managerial interpersonal emotion regulation
abstract: Purpose Research on the favorable impacts of leader interpersonal emotion regulation on employee and organizational outcomes has increased recently. However, an important question often goes unasked: What does this emotional work cost the managers themselves? We know little about the intrapersonal impact and intervening explanation of such effects on leaders who engage in emotion regulation in leading employees. We present new evidence showing how regulation strategies affect managers themselves and what this means for leadership. Design/methodology/approach Using the managers as sample (n = 81) of three business units of a financial company, we conducted a diary study (experience sampling, five daily surveys) and used multilevel analysis to examine the intrapersonal effects of managerial deep and surface acting on the two impaired well-being constructs – emotional dissonance and emotional exhaustion. Findings While our hypotheses about the positive relationship between surface acting and impaired emotional well-being were supported, as predicted, we did not find a significant negative relationship between deep acting with emotional dissonance and emotional exhaustion. Nonetheless, our study provides important empirical evidence suggesting that, while managerial surface acting can be bad for their well-being, deep acting is not emotionally taxing at the least. Originality/value…

title: Comparative efficacy of low- vs. high‐frequency endovaginal electrostimulation combined with pelvic floor muscle training on pelvic floor bioelectrical activity in young, healthy women: a preliminary, single-center, randomized controlled trial
abstract: Abstract Background Pelvic floor dysfunctions can significantly affect women’s quality of life. Endovaginal electrostimulation is a well-established conservative therapy; however, the optimal stimulation frequency remains uncertain, particularly as a preventive measure in healthy populations. This study aimed to compare the effects of 10 Hz versus 50 Hz endovaginal electrostimulation, when combined with pelvic floor muscle (PFM) training, on the bioelectrical activity of PFM in young women without urinary–genital dysfunction. Methods In this prospective, single-blinded, randomized controlled trial, 45 healthy women aged 18–28 were randomized into three groups of n = 15 each: Study group I, receiving 10 Hz endovaginal electrostimulation plus pelvic floor exercises; Study group II, receiving 50 Hz endovaginal electrostimulation plus pelvic floor exercises; and the Control group, performing pelvic floor exercises only. All 45 women completed the intervention and follow-up and were analyzed: Study group I, n = 15; Study group II, n = 15; Control group, n = 15. Interventions were administered thrice weekly over eight weeks. Surface electromyography (sEMG) measured resting and functional bioelectrical activity in supine and standing positions at baseline (M1), immediately post-intervention (M2), and at one- (M3) and three-months follow-up (M4). Results Resting sEMG activity decreased…

title: MOF-303-Functionalized Glass Fiber Separator Enabling Synergistic Ion Flux Regulation and Desolvation Modulation for Durable Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries
abstract: Abstract Aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) have emerged as promising candidates for stationary energy storage owing to their intrinsic safety, low cost, and environmental benignity. However, their practical deployment remains hindered by interfacial instability of the Zn anode, including dendritic growth, hydrogen evolution, and parasitic byproduct formation. Here, an aluminum-based metal–organic framework-functionalized glass fiber separator (MOF-303-GF) is developed to regulate Zn2+ transport and deposition chemistry in AZIBs. With the porous framework and abundant zincophilic binding sites of MOF-303, the modified separator reconstructs the local ion transport environment, improves electrolyte wettability, and delivers a high ionic conductivity of 22.6 mS cm–1 together with a Zn2+ transference number of 0.46. More importantly, MOF-303-GF homogenizes the interfacial electric field and Zn2+ concentration distribution, facilitates desolvation-coupled charge transfer, and induces preferential Zn deposition along the Zn(002) plane, thereby effectively suppressing dendrite growth and side reactions. As a result, the Zn symmetric cell achieves highly reversible Zn plating/stripping for over 3700 h at 2.0 mA cm–2, while the Zn∥Cu cell exhibits a Coulombic efficiency of 99.0%. When paired with a sodium vanadate (NaV3O8, NVO) cathode, the Zn||NVO full cell delivers improved cycling s…

title: Prognostic value of measuring LSC frequency in AML: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Abstract Leukemia stem cells (LSC) are thought to be responsible for relapse in patient with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). LSC can be quantified at diagnosis to improve risk stratification and during follow-up to monitor residual disease. To systematically evaluate the prognostic relevance of measuring LSC at diagnosis and in remission in patients with AML, we conducted a systematic and reconstructed individual patient data meta-analysis. We performed a comprehensive search for studies that reported overall survival (OS) and/or event-free survival (EFS) in relation to LSC measurements at diagnosis or in remission. We reconstructed individual patient data based on Kaplan-Meier curves. Fifty-six studies were included, including a total of 44 cohorts (n = 7781) for OS and 37 cohorts (n = 5032) for EFS at diagnosis; and 19 cohorts (n = 2006) for OS and 22 cohorts (n = 1342) for EFS in remission. Positive LSC status was significantly associated with inferior OS and EFS at diagnosis (OS: hazard ratio [HR], 1.96; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.85-2.08; EFS: HR, 2.32; 95% CI, 2.15-2.49) and in remission (OS: HR, 2.59; 95% CI, 2.23-3.03; EFS: HR, 2.53; 95% CI, 2.18-2.94). To conclude, we found that measuring LSC has prognostic relevance both at diagnosis and in remission. This supports LSC frequency as a key prognostic factor that warrants implementation into clinical practice.

Why employee silence persists: unequal capacity to bear the consequences of speaking up
abstract: Purpose This study aims to develop capacity to bear voice consequences to explain why employees anticipating comparable repercussions from speaking up may make different communication choices. It examines how unequal protection shapes silence within a voice episode and how experience can alter later choices. Design/methodology/approach The conceptual argument integrates employee voice and silence research with conservation of resources theory, career scholarship and employment relations to develop propositions linking anticipated exposure, available capacity and perceived capacity. Findings The model proposes that anticipated consequence exposure is more strongly associated with silence when perceived capacity is low. Available capacity comprises resources that employees can access and mobilise to absorb, contain or recover from specified losses. Perceived capacity concerns their assessment of that protection. Appraisals may underestimate or exceed the protection available at the decision point. Communication arrangements and experiences of harm or protection may alter exposure, capacity and subsequent choices. Originality/value The contribution specifies how resources become protective through their fit with anticipated consequences. By distinguishing available protection from its appraisal, the model explains why comparable anticipated events can exert unequal behavioural inf…

title: Digital state capacity in fragile and conflict-affected contexts: cross-national evidence from the World Bank GovTech Maturity Index
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine the association between World Bank Fragile and Conflict-affected Situations (FCS) status and GovTech maturity, including differences across four functional pillars. Design/methodology/approach The analysis uses 2025 GovTech Maturity Index (GTMI) data for 197 economies, including 39 FCS economies. Ordinary least squares models adjust for income, population and region. Covariance-aware coefficient contrasts, matching, bounded-response estimation, restricted samples (including survey-based records only), a regional cluster bootstrap and comparison with the UN E-Government Development Index provide complementary checks. Findings The adjusted composite association is −0.187 index points. All four pillar associations are negative, but covariance-aware comparisons do not establish differences between pillars or FCS categories, and matching reverses the ordering of two pillar estimates. The associations hold in the survey-based subsample. Exploratory quantile contrasts are inconclusive. Research limitations/implications Cross-sectional associations do not identify causal effects, investment returns or mechanisms. Index measurement, limited overlap and small FCS subgroups constrain interpretation. Practical implications The findings support examining multiple GovTech functions in country diagnostics. They do not establish an investment ranking or a mat…

title: Generative AI as an external knowledge source: digital literacy, individual absorptive capacity and sports communication knowledge creation intention
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how knowledge-oriented generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tool use (GAIU) is associated with sports communication knowledge creation intention (SCKCI), with digital literacy (DL) and individual absorptive capacity (IAC) as sequential capability pathways. Design/methodology/approach A cross-sectional survey of 616 university students in Yunnan Province, China, with sport-related academic backgrounds or sports communication experience was analysed using confirmatory factor analysis, latent-variable structural equation modelling and 5,000 resample bootstrap mediation. Composite-score mediation served as a robustness check. Findings Both specific indirect paths and the sequential GAIU–DL–IAC–SCKCI path were significant, while the direct association remained significant, yielding a pattern consistent with partial sequential mediation. Research limitations/implications The cross-sectional, self-reported and region-specific design does not establish causal or temporal ordering and limits generalisability. SCKCI reflects intention rather than observed behaviour. Practical implications GenAI-supported knowledge work should incorporate source verification, human review and traceability. Social implications Responsible GenAI use in public-facing sports communication requires attention to misinformation, accountability and public trust. Originalit…

title: Clinical trials in Lusophone Africa – results from a capacity building training initiative
abstract: Abstract Background Portuguese-speaking African countries (PSACs) face structural barriers in conducting biomedical research and clinical trials, including limited ethical and regulatory capacity-building opportunities. Most international capacity-building initiatives are conducted in either English or French, thus often excluding PSACs due to language barriers. The CT-Luso project (2024–2027), building on the BERC-Luso Project (2018–2022), was designed to address this gap, through providing comprehensive training in Portuguese on the ethical and regulatory requirements of clinical trials in Africa. Methods This study is a descriptive evaluation of the first level of CT-Luso training “Ethical and Legal Requirements for the Development of Scientific and Clinical Research” , focusing on programme outputs and self-reported perceptions without a pre-training baseline or control group. The programme, coordinated jointly by Portuguese and African partners, ran online from December 2024 to June 2025, and comprised 111 training hours (including evaluation) across 6 modules. It targeted a broad range of professionals in regulatory authorities, ethics committees, research institutions, and universities. Evaluation included module-specific multiple-choice tests, recovery assignments, and oral assessments, complemented by continuous quality assurance surveys. Successful completion granted …

title: Adsorption behavior and mechanism of malachite green dye onto natural bentonite from Sa Bot district, Lopburi province, Thailand
abstract: Dye-laden wastewater poses a persistent environmental challenge due to its toxicity and resistance to degradation. This study reports the novel application of natural bentonite sourced from Sa Bot district, Lopburi province, Thailand, for the adsorption of cationic malachite green (MG) dye. The distinct geological origin of this bentonite, which has not been previously investigated for MG dye removal, underscores its unique physicochemical properties and local relevance. Comprehensive characterization was performed using BET surface area analysis, FTIR spectroscopy, SEM-EDXS, and determination of the point of zero charge (pHpzc). Batch adsorption experiments systematically examined the effects of pH, adsorbent dose, contact time, initial dye concentration, and temperature. Optimal adsorption occurred at pH 9, with equilibrium being reached within 180 minutes, yielding a maximum adsorption capacity of 35.97mg/g at 30°C. Equilibrium data were well fitted to both Langmuir and Freundlich models, while the Redlich–Peterson model indicated surface heterogeneity. Kinetic analysis confirmed pseudo-second-order behavior, with intraparticle diffusion contributing alongside surface adsorption. Thermodynamic evaluation revealed that the process was endothermic and spontaneous across 20-40°C, as evidenced by negative ∆G values throughout this temperature range. Mechanistic insights highligh…

title: Enhanced medical image segmentation using mixer-block integration with channel attention mechanism
Reaction Mechanism and Chemoselectivity of an Enzymatic PAS Domain: A Combined MD and QM/MM Study
abstract: Abstract A Per-ARNT-Sim (PAS) domain exhibits oxidative N-demethylation activity toward dimethylamine (DMA); however, the detailed reaction mechanism remains elusive, thus hindering the rational engineering of the enzyme. In this work, we conducted molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and quantum mechanical/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) calculations to investigate the PAS domain-catalyzed DMA N-demethylation reaction. Our results indicate that the protonated substrate DMA is the most plausible proton donor during the formation of compound I (Cpd I, iron(IV)-oxo porphyrin cation radical). The calculated energy barrier for Cpd I generation is 14.4 kcal/mol, which is the rate-determining step of the reaction. Following its generation, Cpd I can rapidly oxidize the substrate via an electron-transfer-initiated hydrogen atom abstraction. The chemoselectivity favoring methyl hydroxylation over amine oxidation is mainly determined by the protein environment. Our computations provide mechanistic insights into the heme-dependent oxidative N-demethylase (HODM)-catalyzed reaction and offer information for the rational design of new PAS enzymes.

Механизм софинансирования инициативных проектов в старо-промышленных регионах Приволжского федерального округа
abstract: В статье исследован механизм софинансирования проектов инициативного бюджетирования (ИБ) в контексте финансовой безопасности. На примере субъектов Приволжского федерального округа (ПФО), включая старопромышленные регионы (СПР), дана оценка состоянию механизма софинансирования с точки зрения экономического и социального эффектов от реализованных проектов ИБ. Оценка экономической эффективности механизма софинансирования свидетельствует о более высоком экономическом и социальном эффектах, полученных от проектов, в ПФО и СПР, чем в целом по стране. Значительная доля внебюджетных средств в рамках проектов означает расширение самостоятельности муниципалитетов и укрепление их финансовой безопасности. The article examines the co-financing mechanism for participatory budgeting (PB) projects in the context of financial security. Using the regions of the Volga Federal District (VFD), including old industrial regions, as a case study, it assesses the co-financing mechanism in terms of the economic and social effects of implemented PB projects. The assessment of the economic efficiency of the co-financing mechanism indicates that projects in the VFD and old industrial regions have generated greater economic and social effects than those observed nationwide. A substantial share of extra-budgetary funding in these projects implies greater municipal autonomy and stronger financial security.

title: How natural disaster cues trigger interest in capability-oriented self-improvement products: the mediating mechanism of self-protection motivation
abstract: Purpose This research investigates how natural disaster cues influence consumer preferences for capability-oriented self-improvement products. Specifically, it examines the mediating role of self-protection motivation and the moderating effect of self-mastery in this relationship. Design/methodology/approach Three experimental studies were conducted with different manipulations of natural disaster cues (i.e. guided recall tasks, news articles paired with photographs and image stimuli) and diverse capability-oriented self-improvement products (i.e. a wealth management app, a learning website and an e-book titled communication skills). Findings Results across three studies demonstrate that exposure to natural disaster cues significantly increases preferences for capability-oriented self-improvement products. This effect is mediated by self-protection motivation. Furthermore, self-mastery moderates this mediating pathway: the indirect effect is stronger among consumers with high self-mastery than those with low self-mastery. Originality/value First, we extend disaster research by examining the impact of disaster cues on capability-oriented self-improvement product preferences. Second, we identify natural disaster cues as a new precursor of self-improvement product preferences. Third, beyond its established role in harm avoidance, we show self-protection motivation also drives proa…

Ethical leadership as an informal HR governance mechanism: linking ethical leadership to organizational citizenship behavior via trust and affective commitment
abstract: Purpose This study examines how ethical leadership activates organizational citizenship behavior through trust and affective commitment, and how these relational processes are shaped within the context of ethical climate. Design/methodology/approach This study uses a cross-sectional survey design with data from 1,096 technical employees in 42 Turkish manufacturing and technology firms. Ethical leadership, trust, affective commitment, ethical climate, and organizational citizenship behavior were measured with validated Likert scales. Hypotheses were tested using structural equation modeling (DWLS) and conditional process analyses (Hayes PROCESS), estimating direct, indirect, and moderated effects and assessing measurement quality (reliability/validity) and potential common method bias. Findings The findings show that ethical leadership has both direct and indirect effects on organizational citizenship behavior. Trust and affective commitment function as complementary psychosocial mechanisms in the transformation of ethical leadership into behavioral outcomes, while ethical climate reshapes the strength of these mechanisms depending on the context. Originality/value The study conceptualizes ethical leadership as an informal ethical governance mechanism and tests a context-sensitive model in which trust and affective commitment transmit ethical signals to citizenship behavior unde…

title: Carbon footprint and energy-related performance indicators of Mediterranean and Black Sea trawl fisheries
abstract: Abstract Spatially explicit information on fuel consumption and energy efficiency is essential for evaluating the climate-related and economic performance of trawl fisheries, yet such data are rarely available at regional scales. This Data Descriptor presents four harmonised spatial datasets describing fuel consumption, fuel costs, and energy-related performance indicators for Mediterranean and Black Sea trawl fisheries during 2013 to 2022. The datasets integrate fleet-segment economic data from the EU Annual Economic Report with spatially resolved fishing effort and landings from the Fisheries Dependent Information database, using a reproducible framework that allocates fleet-segment fuel consumption and costs to spatial fishing grounds according to the distribution of fishing effort and landings. Indicators include Energy Consumption, Energy Costs, Fuel Use Intensity, Energy Use Intensity, and Fuel Efficiency, reported on a 0.5° c-square grid. The four products provide energy indicators at increasing levels of aggregation, ranging from datasets disaggregated by fishing technique, gear type, and vessel length to datasets summarised across all trawl fleet segments within each c-square grid. Spatial patterns of energy consumption were independently validated using Automatic Identification System data combined with empirically derived fuel-consumption relationships to reconstruct…

title: Highly Conductive Carbon Nanosheets Derived from Rhodanine Pyrolysis-Modified Graphite Felt for Viologen-Based Redox Flow Batteries
abstract: Abstract Viologen-based aqueous organic redox flow batteries (AORFBs) are characterized by outstanding electrochemical reactivity. Simultaneously improving the electrical conductivity of electrode materials while maintaining sufficient active surface area is recognized as a viable strategy to enhance the energy conversion efficiency of AORFBs. In this study, graphite felt (GF) was selected as the electrode substrate, and ultrathin carbon nanosheets were synthesized via in situ growth on the surface of graphite felt fibers through in situ pyrolysis of rhodanine, which enables synergistic improvement of the electrical conductivity and electrochemically active area of the resulting electrode. The loading mass of rhodanine was systematically optimized, and the surface chemical composition, microstructure, physicochemical properties, and electrochemical performance of the as-prepared materials were comprehensively characterized. Experimental results demonstrated that the RGF-0.75%-T10 composite electrode exhibits the optimal electrochemical activity toward viologen molecules. A BTMAP-vi/Nme-TEMPO flow cell was assembled to evaluate the practical application potential of the prepared electrodes. In comparison with the battery assembled with pristine graphite felt electrodes, the device constructed with RGF-0.75%-T10 electrodes delivers a substantially reduced charge–discharge overpot…

title: Retarding Energy Transfer Kinetics to Suppress Auger Recombination for Low-Threshold Amplified Spontaneous Emission in Perovskite Heterostructures
abstract: Abstract Quasi-2D perovskites offer efficient energy funneling for lasing applications, yet ultrafast carrier injection into the gain centers triggers severe Auger recombination, while poor environmental stability further hinders their practical use. Here, we construct a 0D/quasi-2D multiphase heterostructure via mFPEA+ and TmPA+ incorporation, wherein the 0D Cs4PbBr6 phase acts as an energy reservoir and physical barrier. Transient absorption spectroscopy reveals that the stepwise cascade retards energy-transfer time from 9.38 to 19.03 ps, suppresses Auger recombination (Auger lifetime prolonged from 76.29 to 130.52 ps), and extends the carrier lifetime in the gain phase from 192.4 to 351.6 ps. Meanwhile, the 0D phase passivates uncoordinated defects and blocks moisture/oxygen. Consequently, the amplified spontaneous emission (ASE) threshold is reduced from 120.1 μJ cm–2 for the control film to 13.5 μJ cm–2, with excellent ASE stability under continuous pumping and 15-day ambient-air exposure. This work establishes kinetic modulation of energy transfer as a powerful strategy for suppressing Auger recombination in perovskite laser.

title: Controlled Surface Ga Treatment to Suppress the Ostwald Ripening Process for InP Quantum Dots with Narrow-Bandwidth Emission
abstract: Abstract Environmentally friendly indium phosphide (InP) quantum dots (QDs) offer tunable emission from visible to infrared wavelengths, while synthesizing InP QDs with high brightness and narrow-bandwidth emission remains challenging. In this work, controlled surface Ga treatment was used to suppress the Ostwald ripening process during the synthesis of InP QDs with an enhanced optical performance. The tunable interaction of Ga with the QD surface was systematically investigated, and Ga treatment narrowed the full width at half-maximum (fwhm) of InP/ZnSeS QDs from 52 to 44 nm. Subsequent optimization of ZnS shell growth suppressed spectral broadening, while further increasing the ZnSeS interlayer thickness ultimately yielded a narrow fwhm of 46 nm and a high photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of 96.15%. Improvement in color rendering index and correlated color temperature using InP-based quantum dots for white light-emitting diodes (LEDs) was demonstrated, and prototype devices exhibit an ultrahigh color rendering index of 95.6, a low correlated color temperature of 4414 K, and CIE coordinates of (0.36, 0.36). This work provides a promising way to obtain InP QDs with narrow-bandwidth emission and high brightness for future research and applications.

title: The physical and chemical structure of TMC-1: The spatial distribution and excitation conditions of carbon, oxygen, and sulfur bearing species -- Depletion of CO and CS
abstract: We present a detailed study of the physical and chemical structure of TMC-1 from the observed spatial distribution of HC_3N, NNH+, CN, and their isotopologues; the O-bearing species C 18 O, C^17O, CH_3OH, CH_3CHO, and H_2CO; and the S-bearing species CS, HCS+$, H_2CS, and H$_2CCS. The well-known filamentary structure of TMC-1 can be interpreted as a single cloud with a velocity gradient perpendicular to the filament or less likely as being due to the alignment of three independent clouds in the line sight with velocities of 5.3-5.7, 5.7-5.9, and 5.9-6.3 ̨ms. The main contribution to the emission of all studied C-bearing species is at 5.83 ̨ms. We conclude that the three velocity components are dynamically connected and that the abundances of C-bearing molecules show a different behavior compared to O-bearing species, which have emission peaks at 5.7 and 6.25 ̨ms, and appear at different spatial locations than cyanopolyynes and C_nH and C_nN radicals. The detection of 13 C^ 18 O, with exactly the same line profile than that of C 18 O and C^ 17 O, excludes the possibility that the decrease of their emission at 5.83 ̨ms, could be due to self-absorption or absorption by a foreground cloud component. Hence, as indicated by the spatial distribution of C 18 O and C^ 17 O, CO is significantly depleted at the velocities and positions where the emission of the carbon chains and radicals …

title: Soil and plant carbon affected by topographic differentiation at coal mine waste dump sites
Observation-Based Emission Estimates of the Potent Greenhouse Gas HFC-23 for Article 5 and Non-Article 5 Country Groups under the Montreal Protocol
abstract: Abstract The Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol requires parties to destroy, to the extent practicable, HFC-23 generated as a byproduct during the production of controlled hydrochlorofluorocarbons and hydrofluorocarbons. Global total HFC-23 emissions estimated from reported abatement and known sources (bottom-up) agreed with those inferred from atmospheric observations (top-down) before 2015, but have been substantially lower since then. Here, we show that during 2011–2013, bottom-up estimates of global total HFC-23 emissions were right for the wrong reasons: bottom-up estimates for the non-Article 5 (mainly developed) country group were lower than top-down estimates (1.7 ± 0.2 vs 3.1 ± 0.5 Gg yr–1 on average), while those for the Article 5 (mainly developing) country group were higher (11.8 ± 0.4 vs 9.7 ± 1.0 Gg yr–1), resulting in a cancellation at the global scale. We further show that during 2015–2023, while the underestimation of global bottom-up emissions was dominated by the Article 5 country group, the non-Article 5 country group also contributed in 2023 [bottom-up (byproduct emissions reported to UNEP plus other known sources) vs top-down: 0.5 ± 0.2 vs 1.3 ± 0.6 Gg yr–1]. Our results underscore improvement of emission accounting and mitigation for both country groups under the Kigali Amendment.

title: Bridging the knowledge gap: assessing Nigerian construction professionals' awareness and readiness for zero-carbon initiatives
abstract: Purpose The built environment is a major contributor to global carbon emissions, making the transition to zero-carbon buildings essential. Achieving this transition depends on construction professionals' awareness and readiness to implement zero-carbon initiatives (ZCIs). However, empirical evidence on their preparedness in the Nigerian construction industry remains limited. This study assesses Nigerian construction professionals' knowledge and awareness of ZCIs supporting the zero-carbon transition. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research design was adopted using a structured questionnaire administered to 225 Nigerian construction professionals. The questionnaire was validated through expert review and pilot testing. Purposive sampling was used to ensure representation of key industry stakeholders, and data were subsequently analyzed using descriptive statistical techniques. Findings The results reveal substantial awareness and capacity gaps among Nigerian construction professionals. Awareness of international climate agreements, national climate policies, and industry-led ZCIs was generally low. Familiarity, experience, and training in carbon assessment, building performance assessment, life cycle assessment, and energy modelling were also limited. These deficiencies indicate inadequate sectoral preparedness for the effective implementation of ZCIs in Nigeria's co…

title: Surface engineering of diamond and diamond-like carbon for quantum technologies: interface chemistry, near-surface defects, and device-level performance
abstract: Abstract Diamond is an established solid-state platform for quantum sensing, integrated photonics, and spin-based quantum technologies. Still, the performance of shallow color centers is strongly affected by surface-induced band bending, charge-state instability, interface traps, spectral diffusion, and near-surface defects. This review critically examines how hydrogen-, oxygen-, fluorine-, nitrogen-, and mixed-surface terminations, molecular functionalization, dielectric passivation, plasma and electrochemical treatments, defect-engineering routes, and emerging diamond-like carbon interfaces modify the local electronic and spin environment. Particular attention is given to the relationships among interface chemistry, defect depth, charge-state stability, spin coherence, optically detected magnetic resonance response, optical linewidth, spectral diffusion, and device-level reliability. Evidence from wide-field sensing, scanning-probe, nanophotonic, and hybrid architectures is compared while accounting for differences in processing and measurement conditions. Persistent limitations include inter-study variability, incomplete chemical–quantum correlation, inconsistent performance reporting, and limited long-term stability data. Standardized surface characterization, matched-condition performance measurements, and device-specific interface design are therefore required to improve …

title: A Review of Carbon Nanoparticles-Enhanced Salt-Based Phase Change Materials for Thermal Energy Storage Applications
abstract: ABSTRACT Thermal energy storage (TES) is critical to improving energy efficiency and integrating intermittent renewable energy systems. Among various TES technologies, latent heat TES systems employing phase change materials (PCMs) offer high energy storage density but suffer from inherently low thermal conductivity, which limits charging and discharging rates. Carbon nanostructures have emerged as promising thermal conductivity enhancers because of their exceptional intrinsic thermal properties and large surface area. This review critically examines the incorporation of carbon nanostructures, including carbon nanotubes, graphene, expanded graphite, and carbon nanofibers, into salt-based PCMs. The review emphasizes their influence on thermal conductivity, specific heat capacity, phase transition behavior, cyclic stability, and overall energy storage performance. The mechanisms responsible for thermal enhancement, including percolation network formation, phonon transport facilitation, and interfacial thermal resistance reduction, are discussed in detail. A comparative analysis of reported literature highlights the trade-offs between conductivity enhancement and latent heat reduction, dispersion challenges, and long-term reliability concerns. Finally, key research gaps and future directions for optimizing nano-enhanced PCMs (NePCMs) for large-scale TES applications are identified…

title: Beyond Morphology: Revealing Support-Active Phase Coupling in Spherical SiO2 and TiO2 Nanoreactors for Cu- and Co-Oxide-Catalyzed Toluene Combustion
abstract: Abstract Disentangling the intrinsic contribution of support-active phase interactions remains a major challenge in heterogeneous catalysis, as conventional supported catalysts often combine variations in morphology, particle size, dispersion, and support chemistry. Herein, we introduce hollow SiO2 and TiO2 nanoreactors containing encapsulated transition metal oxide particles as model platforms for systematically investigating how chemically distinct oxide environments influence transition metal oxide catalysts during volatile organic compounds (VOCs) oxidation. Mesoporous amorphous SiO2 and anatase TiO2 shells with comparable diameters (500–600 nm) and similar textural properties were synthesized using polymeric spherical templates. Subsequent impregnation with 5–15 wt % Cu or Co, followed by calcination, yielded nanoreactors containing predominantly crystalline CuO or Co3O4 particles within the internal cavities. The CuO- or Co3O4-based systems exhibited fundamentally different support-active phase coupling. Strong interactions between CuO and TiO2 modified the Cu coordination environment without significant incorporation of Cu2+ into the TiO2 lattice, while ex situ XPS/XAS measurements indicated Cu+ as the dominant surface Cu species after air exposure. In contrast, Co3O4 interacted only weakly with the surrounding oxides, and its catalytic behavior was influenced primarily …

title: Multifunctional Integration in Aerogels: Recent Progress and Prospects in Simultaneous Thermal Insulation and Microwave Absorption
abstract: Abstract The rapid development of science has led to an increasing demand for lightweight and high-performance composite materials. Aiming at the dual requirements of thermal insulation and microwave absorption in the field of aerospace, this paper first clarifies the mechanism of heat insulation and microwave absorption. Secondly, five representative bifunctional aerogel systems are introduced. This paper mainly focuses on the recent research progress of the thermal insulation and microwave absorption bifunctional composite aerogels. Finally, challenges and future perspectives of the current thermal insulation and microwave absorption composite integrated aerogels are discussed.

title: From openness to integration: the role of vulnerability in consent-based decision-making
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to explore how to maintain participatory practice in organizations by understanding the role of vulnerability in consent-based decision-making. Design/methodology/approach This research adopts a reflexive and interpretive methodology. It builds on ethnographic fieldwork in a Swiss social organization that uses consent-based decision-making in meetings as part of a transformation toward a self-managing organization. Findings The study highlights the crucial role of vulnerability in integrating divergent perspectives through processes of sharing, becoming open, allowing unknowingness, and integrating difficult emotions. Originality/value The research demonstrates the value of vulnerability in consent-based decision-making as a process of integrating differences. It introduces the notion of a pedagogy of participation to capture how participatory capacities are learned in everyday practice.

title: Sources and Energy of Even Harmonics of a Femtosecond Pulse in Air Plasma
Metal-organic framework/MXene composites: design strategies and applications for energy storage, catalysis, and sensing
abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), as crystalline porous materials with tunable chemical compositions, have attracted widespread interest for energy-related applications. However, their low electrical conductivity and limited structural stability under electrochemical conditions restrict practical deployment. Integrating MOFs with two-dimensional transition metal carbides/nitrides (MXenes) creates composite materials that combine the high surface area and active sites of MOFs with the metallic conductivity and mechanical flexibility of MXenes. This review summarizes recent progress on MOF/MXene composites. The major synthetic routes are classified into four categories: in situ growth with interfacial chemical bonding, electrostatic self-assembly, post-synthetic transformation into metal oxides, sulfides, and phosphides, and interface engineering. Their applications are discussed across electrochemical energy storage (lithium, sodium, potassium, and zinc-ion batteries, and supercapacitors), energy conversion (electrocatalytic hydrogen/oxygen evolution, oxygen reduction, and photocatalysis), and sensing. Despite research advances, challenges remain for practical application, including MXene oxidation during processing and operation, difficulties in large-scale fabrication with batch-to-batch consistency, and the need for precise interfacial regulation. Finally, future research dire…

title: Interface-engineered CZTS solar cells with Cd-free buffers and MoS2 back contacts: a TCAD route toward enhanced photovoltaic performance
abstract: Abstract This work presents a comprehensive numerical investigation of Cu 2 ZnSnS 4 (CZTS) thin-film solar cells in conventional substrate and tandem configurations, with particular emphasis on absorber optimization, buffer layer engineering, and MoS 2 interfacial effects. Device simulations were carried out using AMPS-1D and Silvaco-Atlas TCAD to systematically analyze the influence of absorber thickness, acceptor concentration, buffer layer properties, and MoS 2 back-contact layers on photovoltaic performance. For the substrate configuration, an optimal efficiency of 13.86% was achieved with a CZTS thickness of 3 μm and acceptor concentration of 3 × 10 16 cm −3 , yielding Voc = 0.98 V, Jsc = 17.13 mA/cm 2 , and FF = 82.4%. Covered interest rate parity in the presence of time-varying transaction costs: an application of the fractional integration approach
abstract: Purpose We demonstrate that fractional integration offers an improved framework for assessing the reliability of the covered interest rate parity condition compared with traditional unit root tests. Specifically, in the presence of transaction costs, the parity condition will tend towards one of the arbitrage bounds, making the process fractionally integrated at that bound which renders traditional unit root tests unsuitable. Given the widespread adoption of parity conditions in practice, in areas such as risk management and foreign exchange rate forecasting, an approach which permits an assessment of the reliability of these models, particularly for volatile markets such as emerging markets, is crucial. Design/methodology/approach We propose a threshold autoregression framework that more effectively identifies near-unit-root behaviour and improves market classification relative to conventional approaches. The analysis uses data from the industrialized markets of Australia, Hong Kong, Japan, New Zealand and Singapore, as well as the emerging markets of India, Indonesia, Korea, Malaysia, the Philippines and Thailand, with the USA serving as the reference market. Findings Our results show that shocks to covered interest rate parity are asymmetric and that the parity conditions tend towards one of the arbitrage bounds. title: Mating history reveals within-individual integration of multimodal signaling effort in a pseudophylline katydid
abstract: Abstract Sexual advertisement often involves multimodal signals whose expression may be integrated differently among and within individuals. When signals overlap in function, patterns of covariation in signaling effort can indicate whether they operate as coordinated components of a complex display, alternative tactics, or independently evolving traits. However, these patterns can be obscured by plasticity in signaling effort in response to fluctuations in environments and individuals’ internal states. Using a katydid species ( Docidocercus gigliotosi ) that produces both airborne and substrate-borne sexual advertisement signals, we tested whether multimodel signaling efforts were more strongly influenced by persistent individual differences or short-term intra-individual plasticity. We recorded wild-caught males for repeated 24-hour periods over multiple weeks and examined how individual identity, experimentally manipulated mating history, and other factors affected signaling effort in each modality. We found that plasticity during a transient refractory period after mating accounted for most of the overall variation in signal production. Over six weeks, unmated males increased stridulation effort more than males that had mated immediately before the first week of recording, suggesting a more persistent effect of mating history on sexual advertisement behavior. title: Dry electrode binders: from fluoropolymer fibrillation toward multifunctional architectures for next-generation energy storage
Recent Advances in Sensing Materials for Monitoring Thermal Runaway in Lithium-Ion Batteries
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) play a critical role in modern energy technologies, powering portable electronics, electric vehicles, and renewable energy storage systems due to their high energy density, long cycle life, and lightweight properties. However, their high energy storage capacity presents intrinsic safety challenges posed by thermal runaway, a potentially catastrophic failure mode. Recent advances in safety monitoring leverage detectable thermal runaway precursors, including temperature fluctuations, pressure variations, and gas evolution. Although significant efforts have focused on developing smart materials for early-stage thermal runaway detection, limited reviews have systematically addressed these material innovations. This review seeks to fill this gap by providing a concise overview of the mechanisms underlying thermal runaway in LIBs and the corresponding smart monitoring strategies. It also examines recent progress in smart materials tailored for temperature, pressure, and gas sensing applications. The primary objective of this survey is to offer valuable insights and guidance for enhancing thermal runaway safety management in battery systems.

title: Exploring sustainable finance and ESG integration in commercial bank
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how senior executives in Nepalese commercial banks conceptualize and implement sustainable finance, with a focus on integrating environmental, social and governance (ESG) practices. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative phenomenological approach was adopted. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with eight purposively selected executives, and data were analyzed using Colaizzi’s seven-step thematic framework using axial coding. Findings The study reveals varied understandings of sustainable finance, ranging from corporate social responsibility initiatives to ESG risk integration. Leadership commitment and personal values drive progress, while regulatory uncertainty, limited ESG tools and profitability pressures hinder implementation. A fragmented approach emerges, reflecting the tension between short-term financial goals and long-term sustainability. Research limitations/implications The focus on commercial banks limits generalizability across other financial institutions, but the findings highlight important directions for future research on ESG integration in frontier markets. Practical implications The study provides actionable insights for banks to strengthen leadership engagement, build internal ESG capacity and design policies that integrate sustainability into financial decisions. Social implications By highlighting the role of b…

title: Cultivating strength inside and out: green credit interest subsidy policies and corporate energy efficiency – new evidence from China
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the effect of green credit interest subsidy policies on corporate energy efficiency, examine their potential complementarity with government environmental regulation and explore the internal capability-building channels that may underlie firms’ responses to the coordination of fiscal and financial policies. Design/methodology/approach Using panel data on Chinese A-share listed firms from 2009 to 2022, this study employs a machine learning-enhanced difference-in-differences approach to estimate the effect of exposure to green credit interest subsidy policies on corporate energy efficiency. It further conducts policy-interaction, potential-channel and heterogeneity analyses to examine possible policy complementarities, firms’ internal responses and differences in the estimated policy effect across firms. A series of robustness checks is also performed to assess the sensitivity of the main findings. Findings The findings indicate that exposure to green credit interest subsidy policies is associated with a significant improvement in corporate energy efficiency. The estimated interaction terms provide evidence of potential complementarity between these policies and both government administrative environmental penalties and R&D subsidies. Formal coefficient-difference tests suggest that the estimated complementarity is stronger for administrativ…

abstract: Abstract Background Restoration of shoulder function after resection for primary bone tumors of the scapula is a challenge, according to the sacrifice of rotator cuff muscles and glenoid. This study aims to define the advantages of a prosthetic design over the others in different clinical situations, comparing the functional outcomes and complication rate of patients treated for a primary tumor of the scapula or surrounding soft tissue with resection and reconstruction with custom-made prostheses. Materials and methods Eight patients were retrospectively reviewed; seven underwent total scapulectomy, while one underwent partial. A humeral prosthesis was placed in five patients (four with constrained and one with anatomical design), and in one patient, a transposition of the latissimus dorsi was performed, in order to replace the deltoid muscle. Results At a median follow-up of 55 months (24–97), two complications requiring further surgeries (a local recurrence and a wound dehiscence) were assessed in two patients, all managed without scapular prosthesis removal. The median MSTS score was 24 (14–30); in the group of constrained prosthesis, the median MSTS score was 24 (19–26), while in the group of nonconstrained prosthesis it was 19 (14–26). The patient with partial scapular reconstruction scored 30 points. Conclusions After resection of the scapula, custom-made prostheses repre…

title: How and to what extent does training transfer climate and training design shape transfer of training: evidence from a meta-analysis study
abstract: Purpose This study examines the relationship between training transfer climate and training design on transfer of training (TOT). It synthesizes findings from previous empirical studies using a meta-analytic framework. Additionally, subgroup moderation and meta-regression were performed to analyze the plausible reasons for equivocal findings across studies. Design/methodology/approach The study adopted a meta-analysis technique to present the findings reported by 51 prior empirical studies on TOT, incorporating bivariate and moderation analyses. Findings The findings reveal that training transfer climate (peer support, supervisory support, organizational support, opportunity to use, and rewards) and training design (transfer design and perceived content validity) positively influence TOT. The study also examined the moderating effects of types of training (hard vs. soft skills), culture (high vs. low power distance and collectivism vs. individualism), and gender (male vs. female). The results show that these moderators explain inconsistent findings in the TOT literature. The study offers insightful recommendations for human resource development managers and practitioners to maximize the likelihood of TOT. Practical implications The study offers insightful recommendations for human resource development managers and practitioners to maximize the likelihood of TOT. Originality/val…

abstract: تهدف هذه الدراسة إلى تقييم تطبيق التصميم المرن في مشروع تاغ فيلا (٢٠٢٢)، وهو مشروع معاصر يسعى إلى تحقيق تصميم مرن، مع الأخذ في الحسبان البنية الاجتماعية والثقافية للمجتمع السعودي. بعد أن فقدت المساكن في المملكة العربية السعودية مفهوم المرونة الذي كان موجوداً في العمارة التقليدية مع إدخال الأنماط المعمارية الأجنبية، نُفِّذت عدة مشاريع تهدف إلى استعادة هذا المفهوم. في هذه الدراسة يتم فحص ممارسات التصميم المرن المطبقة في مشروع تاغ فيلا ومستويات تحقيقها، وفقاً لتصنيف المرونة الذي وضعه المعماري السعودي رائد محمد الدخيل، مع مراعاة القيم الاجتماعية والثقافية للمملكة العربية السعودية. تركِّز الدراسة على تحديد مدى تكييف الجوانب المرنة للتصميم التقليدي للمساكن السعودية مع التصاميم السكنية المعاصرة، وتقييم الجوانب الإرشادية للقيم الاجتماعية والثقافية للمجتمع السعودي؛ لتحقيق التصميم المرن. بناءً على ذلك حُلِّلت الرسوم المعمارية لمشروع تاغ فيلا، وأُجريت مقابلة مع المهندس المعماري الذي صمم المشروع. تشير نتائج الدراسة إلى أن الأساليب التي نُفِّذت في هذا المشروع لتحقيق المرونة تحتوي على كثير من الجوانب الإرشادية التي يمكن أن تفيد دراسات أخرى تسعى لتحقيق المرونة مع مراعاة القيم الاجتماعية والثقافية.

title: Design and Development of Adventures of Pixel Using a User-Centered Approach
abstract: The growing demand for more interactive and immersive computer games has led developers to adopt user-centered methods that emphasize game experience over pure aesthetic design only. While there has been a technological advancement in interactive technology, the majority of games still overlook usability and emotional engagement, thereby leading to inconsistent user satisfaction. This project aims to create Adventures of Pixel, a prototype of an iterative 2D platformer game that combines old-school pixel-art graphics with User-Centered Design (UCD) to maximize playability and enjoyment. An iterative design-based approach was utilized in this research, embracing requirement analysis, prototyping, and user evaluation phases. Thirty users participated in usability testing, and data were collected using the User Experience Questionnaire (UEQ) and the System Usability Scale (SUS). The result demonstrates significant improvement of overall user satisfaction, with the mean UX score improved from 3.4 to 4.6 and SUS score improved from 71.2 to 89.5 after iterative redesigns. Participants reported greater clarity, coherence, and aesthetic enjoyment, all testifying to the success of integrating UCD with retro-art visual aesthetics. These findings demonstrate that user input in early phases of design enhances functional performance as well as emotional engagement. The main contribution of …

Architectural Design of a Deep Learning Framework for Real-Time Urban Air Quality Anomaly Detection
abstract: The background of this research addresses the escalating environmental crisis caused by rapid urbanization and the urgent need for advanced technological interventions to monitor atmospheric conditions. Rapid industrial growth has led to severe air pollution which directly threatens public health and sustainable development across the globe. Therefore the primary object of this study is the architectural design of a highly efficient predictive framework capable of identifying sudden spikes in air pollution levels across smart city infrastructures. To achieve this the proposed method utilizes a novel deep learning architecture that synergizes one dimensional Convolutional Neural Networks and Long Short Term Memory networks. This combination is specifically designed to extract spatial features from environmental sensors and analyze temporal sequences without relying on extensive empirical datasets or physical surveys. Through the formulation of the algorithm and the presentation of the core source code the theoretical result demonstrates a lightweight yet robust processing pipeline. This architectural blueprint significantly reduces computational overhead while maintaining high precision in anomaly identification during continuous data streaming. Ultimately the conclusion emphasizes that implementing this conceptual design will profoundly impact modern environmental technology. B…

title: Design and analysis of polyester/cotton sirofil yarn warp–knitted suit fabric
abstract: Purpose Warp-knitted suit fabrics have become a topic of interest in recent years because of the growing need for casual wear as a symbol of mainstream lifestyle. To design a comfortable warp-knitted fabric with adequate bending rigidity and elastic recovery for suits, two types of warp-knitted suit fabrics with polyester/cotton sirofil yarn (CVC) were developed. Design/methodology/approach Two types of CVC warp-knitted suit fabrics were designed and fabricated using 100D/30D 40s C/T sirofil yarn on a Karl Mayer HKS-3M high-speed warp-knitting machine, following a warp plain weave padding structure. The fabricated samples underwent a series of performance tests, including air permeability, moisture permeability, bending rigidity, crease recovery and pilling resistance. Based on the experimental results, a comprehensive evaluation model was established to assess the overall performance of the fabrics. The findings demonstrate that CVC warp-knitted suit fabrics exhibit superior comprehensive properties. An H-shaped silhouette warp-knitted suit was developed, balancing structural formality and enhanced comfort, validated by sensory evaluation to outperform woven suits due to the fabric’s superior bending resilience and elastic recovery. Findings It was found that CVC warp-knitted fabric had good thermal and humidity comfort, bending rigidity and dimensional stability. Based on the…

title: Copywriting Strategy in the Plastic Waste Management Campaign Message for Early Childhood at Bunda Ganesa Kindergarten Bandung
abstract: This study extends a design research project on a plastic-waste-management infographic campaign for early childhood at Bunda Ganesa Kindergarten, Bandung, by examining its copywriting dimension. It analyzes how the campaign's verbal message the tagline “Aku Selamatkan Bumi” (“I Save the Earth”), infographic captions, and supporting text was constructed for children aged 4–6, mediated by teachers, even though the parent project focused on visual design. Using a qualitative descriptive case-study method, campaign documentation, interview transcripts, and pre/post-campaign evaluation data were reanalyzed through the Attention-Interest-Desire-Action (AIDA) framework and early-childhood readability principles. The campaign content uses short declarative phrases, a first-person point of view, concrete action verbs, and repetition that align conceptually with the AIDA stages and readability principles. Evaluation data reported in the earlier study showed improvement in children's knowledge, attitude, and skills after the campaign; because copywriting, visual elements, and teacher mediation were delivered as a single medium, this improvement cannot be attributed to copywriting alone, and the findings should be read as evidence of message suitability rather than isolated copywriting effectiveness. The study contributes a copywriting-specific perspective to visual-design research on earl…

title: Adjuvant selection and optimization in the design of an epstein–barr virus–based multi-epitope vaccine against Burkitt lymphoma
abstract: Abstract Background This study aimed to identify and optimize a multi-epitope vaccine construct against Epstein–Barr virus (EBV)-associated Burkitt lymphoma, with particular emphasis on adjuvant selection, using an immunoinformatics approach. Methods CTL, HTL, and B-cell epitopes derived from gp350, EBNA1, LMP2A, and BZLF1 were screened based on their predicted immunological properties. We assembled candidate epitopes into multi-epitope vaccine constructs with different configurations and evaluated them using immunoinformatics analyses. Results A total of 39 CTL, 21 HTL, and 10 B-cell epitopes met the predefined selection criteria. Five multi-epitope vaccine constructs (R1–R5) were generated and compared. The 50 S ribosomal protein L7/L12 was selected as the adjuvant, and R5 was selected as the final construct based on its comparatively favorable predicted tertiary structure and molecular interactions with TLR2 and TLR4. R5 consisted of 790 amino acids and showed favorable predicted antigenicity (0.6479), solubility, non-allergenicity, and non-toxicity. The predicted population coverage was 98.46% worldwide.
