title: Waste plant‑derived cellulose hydrogels from orange peel and hemp stems as tailored porous platforms for mesenchymal stem cell culture
abstract: Abstract Plant‑derived cellulose hydrogels were prepared from orange peel and hemp stem agroindustrial wastes and compared with microcrystalline cellulose (MCC) hydrogels as a control system. The materials were systematically characterized in terms of morphology, crystallinity, 3D porosity, swelling and degradation behavior, thermal stability, protein adsorption and in vitro biocompatibility. SEM and micro‑CT revealed a fibrous, interconnected porous architecture with overall porosities of approximately 92% and 78% for orange‑ and hemp‑derived hydrogels, respectively, while X‑ray diffraction, FTIR and Raman spectroscopy confirmed the typical structure of cellulosic networks. The hydrogels showed a three‑stage thermal degradation profile and high swelling capacity, reaching about 1000% (orange) and 600% (hemp) after 3 h of immersion. All formulations showed evidence of protein adsorption, together with antibacterial effects and mesenchymal stem cell viabilities above 80%, with increasing metabolic activity over time, indicating non‑cytotoxic behavior and supporting cell proliferation. Overall, orange-derived cellulose hydrogels provided a more favorable substrate for mesenchymal stem cell adhesion and growth than hemp-based and MCC hydrogels. Their high porosity and swelling capacity support their potential use as wound dressings by facilitating fluid uptake and retention, while…

title: Literature Review: The Role of Plant Growth Regulators in Embryogenic Callus Induction in Curcuma sp.
abstract: Embryogenic callus development in Curcuma species depends on the type, concentration, and proportion of plant growth regulators (PGRs), particularly the interaction between auxins and cytokinins. These hormones regulate tissue dedifferentiation and influence subsequent regeneration. Although tissue culture is widely used for Curcuma propagation and conservation, callus induction efficiency varies according to species, explant type, and hormonal composition. This review discusses the effects of auxins, such as 2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid (2,4-D) and naphthaleneacetic acid (NAA), alongside cytokinins, including benzylaminopurine (BAP), thidiazuron (TDZ), and kinetin, on embryogenic callus formation. Previous studies have reported promising PGR combinations, including 2,4-D at 2.0 mg/L combined with TDZ at 0.5 mg/L, although their effectiveness may differ among species. Appropriate hormonal balance is essential for improving the regenerative capacity of cultured tissues and supporting embryogenic or organogenic development. By comparing findings across Curcuma species, this review examines hormone-mediated physiological responses and challenges in protocol standardization. Further research is needed to clarify species-specific PGR requirements, the mechanisms underlying embryogenic competence, and the long-term stability of regenerated plants. Future efforts should prioritize h…

title: A review of virtual onboarding programs and experiences
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how virtual onboarding programs have both developed and been experienced by newcomers since the 2020 pandemic. This literature review of 24 articles published between 2020 and 2025 highlights prevalent issues and challenges with virtual onboarding in training organizations. Design/methodology/approach A systematic literature review of peer-reviewed journal articles published since 2020 was conducted using the following search terms: virtual onboarding, remote onboarding, remote work socialization and virtual employee orientation. A total of 24 articles were included in the literature review. Data analysis consisted of establishing a coding dictionary and repeated scrutinization of data until three key themes emerged. Findings Three overarching themes were identified through coding the articles that fit the search criteria. First, the structure of virtual onboarding programs plays a significant role in shaping newcomers’ experience. Second, socialization, while an essential component of any onboarding program, is more difficult to facilitate in virtual environments and requires formal and informal opportunities to be successful. Finally, the use of technology in virtual onboarding can be both an aid to and an impairment of newcomer experiences. Originality/value The dramatic rise in remote workers since the COVID-19 pandemic challenges scholars…

Investigating statistical and spatial loss functions for geometry-aware unsupervised virtual microphone estimation in multi-source environments
abstract: Purpose Small-scale devices often provide too few microphones for effective array processing. This study investigates geometry-aware unsupervised loss functions for a neural network-based virtual microphone estimator (NN-VME), aiming to generate virtual microphone (VM) signals without ground-truth recordings at VM positions. Design/methodology/approach Known array geometry is used to construct training constraints. Alongside a previously proposed loss that maximizes linear correlation between estimated VM signals and recordings from other channels, a new loss based on the time difference of arrival (TDOA) of each source is introduced. The losses are compared on simulated multi-source LibriSpeech data, and the generated VM signals are evaluated with multiple beamformers. Findings The correlation-based method generates high-quality VM signals and improves beamforming performance on CHiME-4. The LibriSpeech experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of geometry-aware unsupervised NN-VME under multi-source conditions and show that the generated VM signals can support different beamforming methods. Research limitations/implications The framework assumes known array geometry, and correlation- and TDOA-based constraints may become less reliable under highly reverberant conditions. Future work should improve robustness in diverse real-world environments. Originality/value This study sys…

title: From One Hell to Another: Exploring the Continuities of Violence against Migrant Women
abstract: Abstract This article examines the violence experienced by migrant women on their migration journeys and in their destination countries, aiming to identify analogies and similarities. It first analyses the inhuman treatment migrant women are subject to on the central Mediterranean route between sub-Saharan countries, Libya and Italy, and on the route between Central America, Mexico, the United States and Canada. Sexual violence is used as a systematic practice of dehumanisation aimed at the submission, control and commodification of women. It then examines the working and living conditions of female migrant workers in Italy’s and Canada’s agricultural sectors. Various characteristics of this sector reinforce these women’s vulnerability, exposing them to different forms of violence. Using a social production of violence lens, the article shows there are various continuities, primarily of gender-based violence against migrant women, which are an integral part of the political economy of violence now characteristic of global migration.

Impact of Virtual Property Tours and Technology on Home-Buying Decisions
abstract: Purpose – This paper examines the impact of virtual property tours and allied digital technologies — including 3D/360-degree walkthroughs, augmented reality (AR), virtual reality (VR), artificial intelligence (AI)-based recommendation engines and digital mortgage integration — on home-buying decisions. It explores how these technologies are reshaping buyer search behaviour, trust formation, engagement and speed of decision-making, with specific reference to an internship undertaken at House of Real Estate. Design/methodology/approach – The study adopts an exploratory-descriptive design carried out in two phases, a structure informed by the bibliometric-cum-qualitative approach used in prior beauty-influencer marketing research (Shukla and Jha, 2026). Phase I consists of a secondary literature and industry-data review covering global and Indian PropTech adoption trends. title: Travel without movement: understanding the impact of immersive technologies on virtual tourism experiences
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how immersive digital technologies shape virtual tourism by investigating the mediating role of user engagement in the relationships among digital technology adoption, accessibility, content quality, interactivity and the effectiveness of virtual tourism experiences. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research design was adopted using a structured online survey of 235 respondents with prior virtual tourism experience, selected through purposive and snowball sampling. Data were analyzed using SPSS and AMOS using confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modeling. Findings User engagement significantly mediates the relationships between technological attributes and virtual tourism effectiveness. Content quality and digital technology adoption demonstrate strong direct and indirect effects, accessibility and interactivity operate only through engagement, suggesting that experiential immersion depends more on cognitive and emotional engagement than on functional interaction alone. Practical implications The findings provide guidance for platform developers, destination marketers and policymakers on designing immersive, accessible and user-centered virtual tourism environments that enhance engagement and broaden access to tourism experiences. title: Exploring red fox (Vulpes vulpes) occupancy, detectability and statistical power to inform monitoring decisions at Booderee National Park
abstract: Context The difficulties of invasive predator management can be exacerbated by suboptimal monitoring data. Developing a cost-effective, operationally achievable and statistically robust monitoring program is therefore a key component of biodiversity conservation and management. Aims To explore options to better balance the survey effort, cost and statistical power of the red fox (Vulpes vulpes) monitoring program at Booderee National Park (BNP), south-eastern Australia. Methods We analysed existing camera-trap data over an 8-year period to estimate fox occupancy and detectability. We then conducted a power analysis to assess our ability to detect reductions in fox occupancy of varying magnitudes under six hypothetical monitoring scenarios with varying survey effort. We compared how statistical power varied among scenarios between seasons of high and low fox detectability (i.e. summer and spring respectively), and across three levels of initial occupancy (Ψ = 0.75, 0.50, 0.25). Annual costs were estimated for each hypothetical scenario as well as the current fox monitoring approach at BNP. Key results Fox occupancy at BNP increased between 2017 and 2022, while recent monitoring demonstrated seasonal variation in fox detectability. Additional monitoring sites could help maintain statistical power to detect a change in the fox population at BNP when fox occupancy is low. For a giv…

title: Supplementary and complementary fit in peer evaluations: evidence from cross-cultural collaboration
abstract: Purpose Peer evaluations are widely used to assess individual contributions in teamwork, yet they are often shaped by biases rather than objective performance alone. Drawing on person–person fit theory, we examine both supplementary fit and complementary fit between evaluators and evaluatees in cross-cultural collaboration. Design/methodology/approach Using 7,513 dyad–time observations from 488 cross-cultural teams, we develop a dynamic multilevel model to examine how supplementary fit and complementary fit influence peer evaluations over time. Findings Greater supplementary fit in English proficiency, managerial experience, enjoyment and gender-equality orientation is associated with higher peer evaluations. In contrast, lower fit in international experience is associated with higher evaluations, consistent with complementary fit. We find no interaction between supplementary and complementary fit. The positive effects of supplementary fit weaken in larger teams but strengthen over time, whereas the positive effect of complementary fit becomes stronger in larger teams and remains stable over time. Originality/value This study extends the person-person fit theory literature by applying it to peer evaluations in cross-cultural collaboration. We contextualize supplementary fit and complementary fit variables within a single framework and demonstrate how their effects vary across t…

title: Peer assessment, student engagement and academic performance: a study of international students in business education
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine whether the learning benefits attributed to peer assessment are primarily associated with receiving feedback or providing feedback to others. The study explores this in the context of international postgraduate students enrolled in a business school. Design/methodology/approach Performance data from 140 international postgraduate business students enrolled in a corporate finance course are empirically analysed by comparing receiving-side and providing-side variables generated through three rounds of peer assessment. Findings The findings highlight that the cognitive benefits of providing peer feedback may be greater than those of receiving feedback in the context of international business students. Practical implications The findings suggest that instructors need to carefully design their peer assessment activities given this context. Maximising the learning benefits of feedback received from peers may require various scaffolding mechanisms. Originality/value To the best of the author’s knowledge, this study provides more robust evidence than has previously been available on the pedagogical relevance of peer assessment and feedback mechanisms. It contributes to the ongoing debate on the purpose and effectiveness of peer assessment. Unlike previous studies, the study design simultaneously investigates the learning gains from receiving and provi…

title: A solid-state all-PbSe platform for thermoelectric cooling

Fe-Incorporated MoO3 Nanorods as Efficient Anodic Electrocatalysts for Urea-Assisted Alkaline and Seawater Oxidation Reactions: Unraveling OER and UOR Interfacial Kinetics via Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy and Distribution of Relaxation Times Analysis
abstract: Abstract Oxygen evolution reaction (OER), characterized by sluggish kinetics and high energy demand, remains a major bottleneck for large-scale hydrogen production, particularly under the challenging conditions of seawater electrolysis. Herein, Fe-incorporated MoO3 nanorods are successfully synthesized via a facile one-pot hydrothermal route, where the Fe content is systematically optimized to enhance electrocatalytic activity. Among the prepared catalysts, FeM15 exhibits superior performance toward both the OER and the urea oxidation reaction (UOR) in alkaline and natural seawater electrolytes. FeM15 achieves low OER overpotentials of 264 and 306 mV at 10 mA cm–2 in 1 M KOH and seawater electrolytes, respectively, along with excellent long-term stability. Replacing OER with UOR significantly reduces the anodic energy requirement, lowering the operating potential by 148 mV in alkaline electrolyte and 184 mV in alkaline seawater. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) and distribution of relaxation times (DRT) analyses reveal that OER is governed by sluggish multistep interfacial processes, whereas UOR proceeds through accelerated charge-transfer kinetics with lower polarization resistance and relaxation time. Despite the complex ionic environment of seawater, urea-assisted electrolysis effectively mitigates kinetic limitations and substantially enhances anodic reaction ef…

title: Understanding the implications of global value chain participation on ecological sustainability in emerging economies
abstract: Abstract The environmental economics literature has documented several factors influencing ecological sustainability, albeit with divergent findings. However, the literature has largely overlooked the effects of global value chain (GVC) participation on the load capacity factor (LCF), which captures both the supply and demand dimensions of ecological sustainability. This study provides an updated perspective using estimates from quantile-on-quantile kernel regularized least-squares and wavelet KRLS within the context of the emerging economies. These novel estimators account for time, quantile, and frequency dimensions in the analyzed relationship, thereby enhancing policy options. Using a quarterly dataset (1990Q1–2018Q4), the estimators reveal heterogeneous implications of GVC participation on LCF across countries. The observed heterogeneity underscores country-specific nuances essential for policy formulation. Specifically, GVC–LCF relationships are predominantly positive in Brazil, China, India, South Africa, and Nigeria. Conversely, in Russia, Mexico, and Turkey, the associations remain largely neutral, with isolated adverse and weakly positive correlations. Additionally, these relationships vary across the short, medium, and long terms, reflecting the scale, composition, and technique effects in most countries. The varying nature of these associations highlights the need f…

title: Participation thresholds and recruitment milestones for HIV cure-related trials: a modified Delphi study
abstract: Abstract Background Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) cure-related trials remain insufficiently representative of populations most affected by HIV. Whether participation thresholds and recruitment milestones should be used to improve representativeness remains unresolved. We examined stakeholder views on whether, when, and how these approaches should be used. Methods We conducted a focused analysis of the participation-threshold domain from a larger modified Delphi study conducted in the USA. The continuing panel comprised 56 community, scientific, clinical, industry, ethics, regulatory, and community-engagement stakeholders. Across four rounds, the domain progressed from an open-ended question to structured statements, reassessment after summarized feedback, and follow-up with hesitant respondents. We used framework analysis for Round 1 responses, descriptive analyses for Round 2 and Round 3 items, and thematic analysis for Round 4 responses. We examined levels of support and disagreement across rounds; the protocol did not specify a numerical cutoff for declaring consensus. Results Stakeholders generally supported participation thresholds and recruitment milestones as tools for representation and accountability, but support was conditional. In Round 2 ( n = 46), the most frequently selected statements emphasized representation and equity because findings otherwise have limit…

title: Creating a Culture of Well-Being By Removing Barriers to Participation in a Multi-Campus Cancer Center
abstract: Background: Healthcare professionals in geographically distributed cancer care settings may face barriers to accessing workforce well-being resources due to geographic distance, staffing constraints, and operational demands. Disconnect & Refresh was developed to improve access to restorative wellness opportunities across community-based cancer care sites. Methods: Disconnect & Refresh was implemented at The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center across 4 Houston area locations. The initiative included BeWell Paws, virtual reality meditation, chair yoga, and creative wellness activities delivered during the workday. Participation was voluntary and tracked through employee badge scans. Participants were invited to complete an anonymous post-event survey, and open-ended responses were analyzed thematically. Results: A total of 257 employees participated, with 69 completing post-event surveys. Activities received consistently high value ratings, with 86.7% to 100% of participants rating offerings as very or extremely valuable. BeWell Paws received the highest endorsement (97%). The overall composite program score was 4.62 on a 5-point scale, reflecting positive perceptions of restoration practices, well-being awareness, and organizational support. Findings were consistent across locations, job roles, and work arrangements. Qualitative themes included mental reset, stress rel…
venue: Advances in Cancer Education and Quality Improvement

title: An In Situ-Formed Mg3AlNi2/Mg3AlNi2H x Ternary Hydrogen Pump for Rapid and Reversible Hydrogen Storage in Mg–Al–Ni Alloys
abstract: Abstract Mg90–xAl10Nix (x = 5, 10, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, and 20) ternary alloys were synthesized by hydriding combustion synthesis (HCS) to improve the de-/hydrogenation performance of MgH2. Among these alloys, Mg71Al10Ni19 shows rapid hydrogen uptake, reaching approximately 97% of its practical capacity within 500 s at 225 °C, and nearly complete dehydrogenation within 600 s at 300 °C. The hydrogenation and dehydrogenation enthalpies of the Mg/MgH2 are reduced from –76.24 and 80.86 kJ/mol to –74.40 and 76.91 kJ/mol, respectively. The pronounced kinetic enhancement is mainly attributed to in situ-formed Mg3AlNi2, which reversibly accommodates and releases hydrogen while retaining structural stability during cycling. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations and deep potential molecular dynamics (DPMD) simulations reveal the favorable formation of Mg3AlNi2Hx, faster H diffusion in Mg3AlNi2 than in Mg2Ni, and weaker H-related electron localization in Mg3AlNi2Hx than in Mg2NiH4. These results support the Mg3AlNi2/Mg3AlNi2Hx couple as a ternary hydrogen pump. Al3Ni2 may further serve as an electron-transfer mediator between Mg3AlNi2 and MgH2, whereas Mg2Ni/Mg2NiH4 provides an additional hydrogen-transfer pathway. These findings provide a rational strategy for designing high-performance Mg-based hydrogen storage materials through the in situ generation of synergistic intermetallic …

title: Analisis Perlakuan Akuntansi Pendapatan Serta Pengaruhnya terhadap Penyajian Laporan Laba Rugi pada PDAM Kabupaten Lombok Timur
abstract: This study aims to determine the revenue accounting treatment method applied by the Regional Drinking Water Company (PDAM) of East Lombok Regency and its effect on the fairness of the presentation of the Income Statement based on applicable accounting standards. This study employed a descriptive research method. The data collection techniques used included observation, interviews, and documentation. The data consisted of quantitative and qualitative data, while the sources of data included primary and secondary data. Based on the analysis conducted, operating revenue is recognized using the accrual basis method, including revenue derived from water charges, administrative services, and other water sales, even though the cash receipts may occur at a later date. The results of the analysis indicate that the revenue accounting treatment applied by the Regional Drinking Water Company (PDAM) of East Lombok Regency and its effect on the fairness of the presentation of the Income Statement are reasonable and in accordance with generally accepted Financial Accounting Standards. Therefore, the researcher recommends that the company maintain and improve the application of appropriate accounting standards to enable users of financial statements to obtain a clear overview of the company's financial performance and financial condition.

A Bench-Stable Reagent for Divergent Synthesis and Storage of SF5X
abstract: Abstract Herein, we report a novel concept to promote the formation of mixed sulfur fluorides SF5Br and SF5Cl, pentafluoronitrosulfane SF5NO2, and disulfur decafluoride S2F10, divergently from a single, bench-stable, liquid, and commercially available organic reagent. Upon photoreaction with elemental bromine, liberation of SF5Br is observed in up to 87% yield. Consequently, after applying a chromoselectivity approach to purify the sulfur fluoride in the reaction mixture, SF5Br could be trapped by alkynes, affording access to SF5Br adducts in good to excellent yields of up to 81% over two steps. Furthermore, this concept could be extended to the release of SF5Cl by reaction with BrCl, affording SF5Cl in up to 82% yield. This reaction features an unprecedented halogenide-catalyzed halogen-methathesis reaction converting SF5Br into SF5Cl. At the same time, the reagent can act as a storage for SF5X with an improved safety profile and can release the molecule on demand. The storage of SF5X on industrial scale is a critical safety hazard that can be addressed by the reported method. Furthermore, the experimental findings are supported by in silico studies that reveal a critical stabilizing effect of the Si substituent.

title: Thermally Transformed ZnC8H4O4 Nanocrystals for Enhanced Sodium-Ion Storage
abstract: Abstract Metal-organic terephthalates composed of earth-abundant elements are promising low-cost and structurally tuneable anodes for sodium-ion batteries, yet their electrochemical behavior, particularly in newly developed compounds, remains insufficiently understood. We report monoclinic nanocrystalline ZnC8H4O4 (ZnTP-2), prepared through the controlled thermal transformation of a hydrated zinc terephthalate precursor, ZnC8H6O5 (ZnTP-1), containing residual terephthalic acid (ZnTP-1@TPA). This transformation involves TPA sublimation and framework dehydration, producing ZnTP-2 with fine crystals of approximately 50–150 nm, increased surface area, and a higher concentration of oxygen-related defect sites compared with ZnTP-1@TPA. ZnTP-2 delivers a reversible Na-ion storage capacity of 222.7 mAh g–1 after 80 cycles at 50 mA g–1, approaching its theoretical capacity and indicating highly efficient utilization of the terephthalate redox framework. It also retains 110 mAh g–1 after 500 cycles at 1000 mA g–1, with a relatively low charge-transfer resistance of 11.5 Ω, demonstrating improved electrochemical stability and rate performance compared with conventional metal-organic terephthalate anodes. Electrochemical kinetic analyses reveal Na-ion diffusion coefficients between 10–14 and 10–12 cm2 s–1, with the differences discussed in terms of apparent, Warburg-related and bulk/chemic…

title: Numerical Simulation and Field Validation of Airflow Field and CO Dispersion Characteristics during Tunnel Construction under Dynamic Vehicle Movement
abstract: Abstract During tunnel construction, a substantial amount of pollutants, such as carbon monoxide, are generated. Compared with the blasting phase, the CO produced by internal combustion engines during the mucking phase exhibited continuity owing to temporal accumulation and had a wider range of influence. Therefore, it is necessary to investigate CO dispersion characteristics under different ventilation modes at various construction stages. In this study, to reveal the influence mechanism of the coupled effect of traffic-induced wind and mechanical ventilation on the airflow field and pollutant migration under dynamic vehicle movement during the tunnel mucking phase, a construction ventilation model was established based on the overset grid method. The effects of mucking truck speed, mechanical wind velocity, and truck travel direction on CO dispersion patterns under different ventilation modes were systematically analyzed. The results show that under forced ventilation conditions, a stable traffic-induced wake was generated by the dynamic movement of the vehicle in the mechanically ventilated stable zone, whereas airflow field fluctuations and multiple turbulent structures were induced in the recirculation zone near the tunnel face, where the peak airflow velocity was reduced by 47.33%. The CO concentration exhibited an annular spatial distribution pattern, characterized by hi…

title: Performance optimized electric vehicle powertrain converters in hybrid AC/DC grids for enhanced synchronization and control
Fatigue Analysis of Vehicle Chassis for Three-Axle Truck Using Ansys Software
abstract: The fatigue performance of a three-axle truck chassis is an important consideration for ensuring structural reliability under variable road-induced loading. This study presents a numerical investigation of the fatigue behavior of a three-axle truck chassis using finite element analysis in ANSYS. A three-dimensional chassis model was developed in SolidWorks and evaluated under static loading, modal analysis, and dynamic road excitation corresponding to ISO 8608 Class D and Class E road profiles at a vehicle speed of 20 km/h. The fatigue life and fatigue damage were predicted using the Goodman, Gerber, and Soderberg mean-stress correction criteria under identical material and loading conditions. The static analysis identified the rear suspension mounting region as the critical structural area, with a maximum von Mises stress of 382.39 MPa, while the minimum predicted fatigue lives under Class D were 8338.5, 8290.4, and 8338.5 cycles for the Goodman, Gerber, and Soderberg criteria, respectively. Under the more severe Class E road profile, the corresponding minimum predicted fatigue lives were 6349.9, 6306.2, and 6349.9 cycles, indicating that road excitation severity has a greater influence on the predicted fatigue life than the selection of the mean-stress correction criterion under the present loading conditions.

title: Transformational leadership and sustainable performance of local government
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the role of transformational leadership in the sustainable performance of local public administration by examining how transformational leaders influence the achievement of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) objectives within Portuguese local government entities. Design/methodology/approach The sample includes a panel of 211 respondents who work in government entities in Portugal through the application of structural equation modelling (SEM). This approach enables the simultaneous examination of both the direct effects of transformational leadership on sustainable performance and the indirect effects mediated by corporate social responsibility and organizational politics. Findings The results demonstrate that transformational leadership positively influences both corporate social responsibility (CSR) and sustainable performance, but the hypothesized indirect/mediating effect of CSR was not statistically supported. Conversely, organizational politics neither significantly affects sustainable performance nor mediates the relationship between transformational leadership and sustainable performance. Originality/value The empirical insights provided by this study offer important insights for public managers and policymakers interested in promoting sustainable governance practices in local governments Beyond their practical implications…

title: Concretizing the abstract: embodied learning as a pedagogical strategy for teaching measurement and evaluation
From teachable moment to national strategy: Acting on readiness to quit smoking
abstract: In this issue of the Annals, Fong et al. note that Singapore’s daily smoking prevalence has continued its long-term decline, reaching 8.4% among residents in 2024.1 This progress reflects decades of sustained investment across Singapore’s tobacco control ecosystem, spanning legislation, taxation, smoke-free public spaces, and public education.2 Yet as prevalence falls, the remaining smokers may be harder to reach, and further gains are unlikely to come from conventional measures alone.

title: When does profitability translate into credible sustainability reporting? The role of board governance
abstract: Purpose This study aims to address a strategic leadership dilemma by asking when profitability translates into credible sustainability reporting. It examines whether board governance conditions the relationship between financial capacity and higher levels of sustainability-reporting credibility among manufacturing firms in Africa. Design/methodology/approach The study uses a balanced panel of 201 firms observed from 2014 to 2023, yielding 2,010 firm-year observations. Sustainability reporting credibility (SRC) is hand-coded as an ordinal ladder ranging from no identifiable disclosure to board-governed and externally assured reporting. Correlated random-effects ordered-logit models with firm-clustered standard errors are used, supplemented by linear-panel and measurement sensitivity tests. Findings Board size and average director tenure are positively associated with higher credibility stages, whereas female board representation and the non-executive director ratio are not statistically significant. Return on equity is not independently significant in the direct-effects ordinal model, whereas its association with SRC becomes more positive at higher levels of board size and average director tenure. Practical implications Senior leaders should treat sustainability-reporting credibility as a strategic governance and control architecture rather than merely as a communication exercis…

title: Development of gemcitabine-modified miR-15a as a novel, multimodal treatment strategy to overcome 5-FU and oxaliplatin resistance in colorectal cancer
abstract: Abstract Background Resistance to 5-fluorouracil (5-FU)-based chemotherapy is a major clinical obstacle in colorectal cancer (CRC), highlighting the urgent need to overcome established resistance mechanisms. MicroRNA-based therapeutics have emerged as compelling candidates in this context, given their inherently pleiotropic mode of action; however, their clinical translation remains hindered by poor stability and suboptimal delivery. Methods To address these limitations, Gem-miR-15a, a unique gemcitabine-modified tumor-suppressor microRNA-15a was designed to synergistically integrate the tumor-suppressive activity of miR-15a with the chemotherapeutic potency of gemcitabine into a single molecular entity. Therapeutic efficacy of Gem-miR-15a was evaluated across a spectrum of preclinical models, including parental and drug-resistant CRC cell lines, 3D tumor spheroids, patient-derived organoids and in vivo metastatic models. Cell viability, apoptosis and cell cycle analyses were performed, along with RNA sequencing and protein validation. Statistical analyses were conducted using Student’s t-test or two-way ANOVA with mixed effects, and data were presented as mean ± SD. Results Gem-miR-15a exhibited potent anti-proliferative activity with IC 50 values in the low nanomolar range, achieving ~ 100-5000-fold greater potency relative to 5-FU and oxaliplatin. Importantly, it retained ef…

title: Стратегия государственной национальной политики РФ: результаты достижения целевых показателей и методологические проблемы (2012–2025 гг.)
abstract: Актуальность: Стратегия государственной национальной политики РФ (2012–2025 гг.) – первый документ с измеримыми показателями межнациональных отношений. Проблема: позитивная динамика в докладах сочетается с методологическими проблемами, снижающими точность оценки. Цель: оценить достижение целевых показателей и выявить методологические проблемы системы измерения. Методы: анализ нормативных актов, докладов, отчётов Счётной палаты РФ, данных социологического мониторинга. Результаты: по трём из пяти показателей – выполнение планов (один – после корректировки), один не достигнут, пятый несопоставим. Выводы: программно-целевой метод эффективен, результаты достигнуты; необходимы унификация методологии, включение показателей в статистическое наблюдение. Relevance: The Strategy of the State National Policy of the Russian Federation (2012–2025) is the first document to introduce measurable indicators for interethnic relations. Problem: While official reports demonstrate positive dynamics, they coexist with methodological issues that reduce the accuracy of assessments. Objective: To evaluate the achievement of target indicators and identify methodological problems in the measurement system. Methods: Analysis of regulatory acts, reports, reports of the Accounts Chamber of the Russian Federation, and sociological monitoring data. Results: Three out of five indicators met the targets (one aft…

title: Optimizing Water Addition to Balance Tenderness and Freeze–Thaw Stability: Processing Strategy for Tender Fish Balls
Smart cart use, empowerment and loyalty in cross-cultural DIY retail
abstract: Purpose This study examines how smart-retail technologies shape shopping experience and loyalty in the do-it-yourself (DIY) sector, focusing on the mediating roles of empowerment, trust and flow across cultural contexts. Design/methodology/approach A multi-method, three-study design was employed. Study 1 used a Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) survey of 309 Chinese DIY customers, Study 2 replicated the survey with 273 Australian consumers and conducted multi-group analysis and Study 3 implemented a 2 × 2 experimental vignette to test empowerment and trust cues across both countries. Findings Results extend the technology acceptance model (TAM) by indicating that empowerment, trust and flow mediate the pathway from adoption perceptions to satisfaction and loyalty. Empowerment was found to be culturally contingent: attenuated in China and prone to decision fatigue in Australia. Trust appeared to substitute for empowerment in collectivist contexts, while flow emerged as a culturally stable mechanism. These counterintuitive findings suggest boundary conditions for empowerment theory; as evidence from a single study, they warrant replication before firm generalisation. Originality/value By integrating psychological mediators and cross-cultural comparisons, this study advances understanding of how smart technologies influence experiential and relational ou…
venue: International Journal of Retail & Distribution Management

title: The branch is strong when the tree is healthy: symbolic reassurance in retail banking in a post-trust economy
abstract: Purpose This study clarifies the strategic role of physical bank branches in a post-trust economy by theorizing and testing Symbolic Reassurance and identifying which customer experience dimensions translate reassurance signals into loyalty and word-of-mouth. Design/methodology/approach Using a three-study mixed-method design, Study 1 focus groups (n = 20) identify symbolic reassurance signals and their customer experience mappings; Study 2 scenario-based experiments (n = 298) test how these customer experience dimensions translate into loyalty and word-of-mouth across conventional versus technology-enhanced branch scenarios; and Study 3 uses topic modeling and machine learning on 363,184 Google reviews to assess whether these same dimensions emerge in naturally occurring consumer discourse. Findings Branches function as costly, visible and enduring signals that consumers interpret through customer experience dimensions. Across the studies, SURROUND, SOCIALIZE and SITUATE emerge as the most consequential dimensions. Innovation-heavy experiences add little beyond a functional floor, while THINK and FEEL exhibit weak relationships with the examined outcomes. In consumer reviews, SOCIALIZE is the strongest predictor of ratings. A cross-study synthesis maps ten symbolic signals to their most relevant customer experience dimensions. Practical implications Banks should prioritize sta…

title: Развитие логистики и управления цепями поставок в сетевой розничной торговле в современных условиях
abstract: Статья посвящена вопросам развития сетевой розничной торговли в современных условиях, характеризующихся неопределенностью логистики и проблемами управления цепями поставок на региональном уровне. Анализ оборота розничной торговли показал, что сетевые торговые компании усиливают свои позиции в сегменте продовольственных товаров, тогда как в общей рознице их доля несколько снижается. Выделены несколько ключевых векторов трансформации российского ритейла, которые формируют новую конкурентную реальность. Предложены технологии управления цепями поставок в условиях цифровой трансформации, которые дадут решающее конкурентное преимущество, предлагая клиентам принципиально новый уровень персонализированного и качественного обслуживания. The article is devoted to the development of online retail in modern conditions characterized by logistics uncertainty and supply chain management problems at the regional level. An analysis of retail trade turnover has shown that network trading companies are strengthening their positions in the food segment, while their share in general retail is slightly decreasing. Several key vectors of transformation of Russian retail have been identified, which form a new competitive reality. Supply chain management technologies in the context of digital transformation are proposed, which will give a decisive competitive advantage, offering customers a fundamental…

title: The role of robots in the retail industry
abstract: Purpose The aim of this study is to illustrate how the global retail industry is adopting and benefiting from robotic technology. Design/methodology/approach Following an introduction, this first discusses the role of robots in inventory management. It then provides details of in-store customer assistance robots. This is followed by a discussion of robot applications in the e-commerce sector, including the role of humanoids. Finally, conclusions are drawn. Findings Due to labour shortages and in the interest of improved efficiency, the global retail industry is increasingly making use of automation in both the conventional and e-commerce sectors. Robots are playing a vital role in this process. The traditional retail sector presently makes limited use of robots, but inventory management applications are growing and significantly improve efficiency. An emerging application is the customer assistance robot. Several trials with humanoids are being conducted in retail environments, most notably in the Far East. The fast-growing e-commerce sector makes extensive use of robotic technology in highly automated warehouses and fulfilment centres. The main classes of robots are autonomous mobile robots and articulated arm designs. Trials are being conducted with the latest generation of humanoids, which have the potential to replace single-task robots and automate a facility’s full workfl…

title: Impact of interface modality and product type on Gen Z E-retail purchases
abstract: Purpose The research examines how interface modality (text versus voice) influences Generation Z consumers' online shopping experiences and purchase intentions in low-involvement product categories. Drawing on the stimulus-organism-response-behaviour (SOBC) framework, it investigates the role of convenience, enjoyment and perceived value in Gen Z search satisfaction and purchase intentions, and the moderating role of product type (utilitarian versus hedonic). Design/methodology/approach Two laboratory experiments were conducted with Gen Z consumers and were analysed using Smart PLS4. Study 1 examined differences in perceived convenience, enjoyment and value across voice and text interfaces. Study 2 validates these findings and extends the model by testing the moderating effect of product type on the relationships among perceived value, search satisfaction and purchase intention. Findings Voice interfaces deliver significantly greater convenience and enjoyment, leading to greater perceived value than text-based interfaces for shopping, especially among Gen Z consumers. Perceived value subsequently positively influences search satisfaction and purchase intention. Product type significantly moderated the relationships between perceived value and satisfaction, with stronger effects for hedonic than utilitarian products in voice-enabled shopping. Originality/value The research advan…
venue: International Journal of Retail & Distribution Management

title: Beyond freemium: how ad-supported subscriptions reshape platform pricing and innovation dynamics
abstract: Purpose Streaming and other subscription platforms increasingly add an ad-supported plan to their free and premium tiers, attracting price-sensitive users but possibly cannibalizing premium subscriptions. This study examines how such a plan affects innovation investment, long-term profitability and welfare and how the reference price effect changes the platform's preference for it. Design/methodology/approach A differential game model captures how the platform sets subscription prices and development effort over time as innovation accumulates. Four scenarios are compared: a freemium model with free and premium plans, a model that adds an ad-supported plan and their extensions with a reference price effect from users comparing current and past prices. Equilibria are derived analytically for the first two scenarios and numerically for the extensions. Findings The platform first sets lower prices and invests heavily in development, then raises prices and reduces development effort as innovation accumulates. Introducing an ad-supported plan stimulates innovation investment. With the reference price effect, the plan raises cumulative profit and user surplus in all numerical experiments and can enhance societal welfare. Without the effect, the platform generally avoids the plan but can still prefer it when it is short-sighted and users are less sensitive to innovation. The innovation…

title: Retailer Engagement, Stock Projection and Loyalty Programme Promotion in FMCG General Trade: A Field-Based Study of ITC Limited’s Personal Care Products Business
abstract: Retail execution in fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) depends on the coordination of product availability, outlet coverage, retailer communication and channel relationships. This field-based study examines retailer engagement, stock projection and loyalty-programme promotion in ITC Limited’s Personal Care Products business, drawing on the activities and records described in the researcher’s On-the-Job Training (OJT) report. The purpose is to interpret how regular retailer contact can support market information collection, stock planning, programme communication and sales-team coordination. The study follows a descriptive, exploratory approach based on internship fieldwork, retailer interactions, discussions with sales personnel and the outlet-coverage and activity figures recorded in the report. The OJT document records 1,200 outlets visited, an average of 25 outlets covered per day, five products/brands covered, 12 retailers providing stock projections, 10 retailers engaged with the PACE programme, four recorded stock-related issues and 20 instances of major retailer feedback. These figures describe reported field activity; the report does not provide a sufficiently detailed outlet-level dataset to calculate conversion rates, sales revenue, product-wise performance or the effect of loyalty-programme participation on sales. The findings indicate the practical value of systemati…
venue: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management

title: Predicting crowdfunding success through gender dynamics and social validation: a comparative analysis using econometrics and machine learning models
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examines the influence of gender and social validation – proxied by the number of campaign supporters – on the success of reward-based crowdfunding campaigns. It explores whether female entrepreneurs experience disparities in funding outcomes and assesses the extent to which social endorsement mitigates or amplifies these effects. Design/methodology/approach This study uses a dual-method approach, combining traditional logistic regression with supervised machine learning (ML) models to examine the effects of gender and supporter count on crowdfunding success (1 = successful, 0 = unsuccessful). Using data from 561 campaigns (188 female-led, 373 male-led), eight ML models – Bagging, Decision Tree, Logistic Regression, Random Forest, SVM, XGBoost, Deep Learning (MLP) and Adaptive Tree Induction (ATI) – were trained and evaluated using accuracy-based metrics. This comparative analysis assesses the relative effectiveness of logistic regression versus ML models in predicting crowdfunding success. Findings Supporter count consistently emerges as the strongest associational predictor of crowdfunding success, with early social backing particularly benefiting female-led projects. Gender alone does not drive crowdfunding success, but its interaction with supporters highlights the role of social validation in overcoming credibility barriers. Across classification…

title: From marked scripts to diagnostic insight: a viewpoint on AI-assisted assessment in paper-based primary classrooms
abstract: Purpose This Viewpoint examines how AI-assisted dashboards might support teachers' diagnostic interpretation of paper-based primary assessment evidence, particularly in Caribbean and other low-resource contexts. It argues that AI's value in classroom assessment lies less in automating judgment than in strengthening teachers' responsible interpretation of evidence. Design/methodology/approach The article uses a conceptual AI-assisted assessment dashboard, developed using simulated data from 22 fictional students, as an illustrative case. The prototype combined optical character recognition (OCR), structured data extraction, and teacher-facing visualizations to illustrate how marked paper scripts may be transformed into diagnostic outputs. Findings The prototype illustrates that traditional summative marking can be reorganized into descriptive information that supports formative interpretation. It also highlights the importance of human oversight, transparent descriptive outputs, privacy-by-design and contextual fit when applying AI and OCR to classroom assessment. Research limitations/implications As the prototype used simulated data, future research should validate the workflow with authentic scripts under a fixed, fully reported technical configuration, with error rates, timed comparisons against manual entry, teacher and student perspectives and classroom implementation. An AI/generative AI-assisted blended learning intervention for nursing undergraduates: a quasi-experimental study of attitudes toward AI, AI literacy, and autonomous learning competency
abstract: Abstract Background Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly shaping healthcare, highlighting the need for nursing graduates to develop relevant competencies. However, structured AI education remains limited in nursing programs, and evidence on the effects of AI-focused teaching interventions remains scarce. Methods A quasi-experimental pretest–posttest study was conducted among 142 undergraduate nursing students at a university in southwestern Zhejiang, China. Seventy-two students participated in a 10-week AI/generative AI (GenAI)-assisted blended learning course comprising 12 h of self-paced online learning and 6 h of hands-on workshops, while 70 students received standard instruction. Attitudes toward AI, AI literacy, and autonomous learning competency were assessed before and immediately after the intervention using validated instruments. Post-test outcomes were compared using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), adjusting for the corresponding baseline score, previous AI training experience, frequency of AI use, and digital literacy. Results In the intervention group, AI literacy increased significantly from 55.67 ± 9.84 to 65.01 ± 8.81 ( P < 0.001), as did attitudes toward AI, which increased from 48.07 ± 6.77 to 51.72 ± 9.90 ( P = 0.049). Neither outcome changed significantly in the control group. After adjustment for covariates, the intervention group had significantly …

This research employed a quasi-experimental method. The research sample consisted of 54 students selected using the cluster random sampling technique, with Class VIII B serving as the experimental class and Class VIII A as the control class. The research instrument was a learning outcome test, whose validity was tested using the Product Moment correlation formula, while its reliability was tested using the KR-21 formula. title: Competency certification and institutional signals in the higher education-to-work transition: psychological wellbeing and future-ready work-based learning
abstract: Purpose This study examines university-linked competency certification as a competence signal in the higher education-to-work transition. It asks how students' interpretations of institutional signals are associated with registration intention and whether psychological wellbeing is associated with a selective indirect pathway in that decision. Design/methodology/approach The study used a quantitative explanatory design with cross-sectional survey data from 337 undergraduate students in Indonesia. Partial least squares structural equation modelling tested the direct and indirect associations of brand awareness, perceived value, trust and perceived usefulness, with psychological wellbeing specified as mediator. Findings Trust and perceived value were positively associated with intention to register, and psychological wellbeing was also linked to intention. Brand awareness and perceived usefulness did not show significant direct associations with intention. Only the indirect association from trust through psychological wellbeing reached statistical significance, whereas perceived value was associated with intention mainly through the direct path. Originality/value The article identifies certification registration as a distinct pre-employment transition point, separates the institutional signal from students' receiver-side evaluations, and shows that wellbeing is associated with a …

title: Active Learning Enables Discovery of Asymmetric Dual-Atom Catalysts for Nitrate-to-Ammonia Electrocatalysis
abstract: Abstract Electrochemical nitrate reduction to ammonia requires a delicate balance between nitrate activation, hydrogen delivery, suppression of competing hydrogen evolution, and stabilization of the catalytic metal centers. Such coupled requirements make the rational design of dual-atom catalysts challenging, particularly when the two metal sites and their coordination environments contribute differently to the reaction. Here, we establish an interpretable active-learning framework to navigate the chemical space of asymmetric dual-atom catalysts and uncover the physicochemical origins of their performance. Rather than learning an empirical activity score, the framework predicts individual DFT-derived properties from readily accessible elemental and structural descriptors and uses uncertainty-aware sampling to iteratively explore previously uncharted metal-pair and coordination environments. Model interpretation reveals distinct roles of the two metal sites in regulating nitrate activation and hydrogen adsorption, and identifies moderate electronic asymmetry coupled with mixed N/O coordination as a favorable design regime. Guided by these principles, active learning efficiently explores an expanded library of 1050 structures and progressively identifies candidates beyond the initial chemical space. Prospective DFT validation highlights Mo–Ta/N3O3–C, Mo–Nb/N3O3–C, and Mo–Nb/N5O1–…

title: A Thematic Synthesis of Social-Emotional Learning, Learning Climate, and Student Achievement in Elementary Education
abstract: Social and emotional learning (SEL) is increasingly recognized as an important component of elementary education, supporting students’ social-emotional development, engagement, well-being, and academic learning. However, the relationships among teacher social-emotional competence, learning climate, implementation quality, and student outcomes remain insufficiently integrated, particularly in the Indonesian context. This study aims to synthesize literature on these relationships and examine their implications for SEL implementation in Indonesian elementary schools. A narrative literature review was conducted using an existing source corpus supplemented by relevant peer-reviewed literature. The synthesis examined major themes concerning teacher competence, classroom practices, learning climate, student outcomes, implementation conditions, and contextual adaptation. The findings suggest that teacher competence is associated with the quality of SEL enactment, while a supportive learning climate provides a context for student participation and social-emotional learning. Implementation quality and cultural context also shape how SEL is adapted and sustained. These relationships should not be interpreted as a universally established causal pathway. The review highlights the need for context-responsive teacher development, school-level support, and rigorous evaluation of SEL practices.…

title: Risk factors for pediatric acute chest syndrome using machine learning techniques
abstract: Abstract Acute chest syndrome (ACS) causes significant morbidity and mortality in both adult and pediatric patients with sickle cell disease. Despite known risk factors for developing ACS, this complication is often unexpected. We hypothesized that a machine learning model could predict progression to ACS in children. A random forest model was used using the Scikit-Learn Python library. Prediction performance was assessed using the C-statistic, sensitivity, and specificity. The features included are demographics, vital signs, laboratory values, medication orders, and additional comorbidities. The positive cohort developed ACS on diagnosis or during admission, and the negative cohort did not. A total of 3223 encounters were included in the model for training and testing. Up to 65% of the positive cohort developed ACS 24 hours after admission. The model had a sensitivity of 65.1% and specificity of 77.4% at the cutoff point of 0.6. For diagnosing ACS, the negative predictive value was 89.8%, and the positive predictive value was 42.3%. For the correct positive cases, the model predicted ACS a median of 18 hours before the diagnosis was determined in the electronic health record. The features that were important included pulse, respiratory rate, presence of hypoxia, temperature, neutrophil count, and use of pain medications. Despite the model’s limitations, it is, to our knowledge…

title: Impact of digital technology-supported learning on learners’ motivation towards Quranic memorization: contextual insights
abstract: Purpose In today’s era of digital technology, the process of learning is mainly reliant on information and communication technology. Moreover, the rapid advancements in information and communication technology have significantly impacted the learning performance of students. Hence, due to the significance of digital technology-supported learning in education, the current study aimed to analyze the effect of digital technology integration on Quranic memorization among madrasa students and examine the influence of digital technology integration for Quranic memorization on madrasa student motivation. Design/methodology/approach The study used a quantitative, correlational research design. The data were collected through random sampling techniques from 500 madrasa students from the Larkana, Sindh region, associated with the Sunni Deobandi sect, with the help of a survey questionnaire. Descriptive and inferential statistics were used to determine the relationship between Quranic memorization through digital devices and students’ motivation. Findings The study’s findings revealed that the motivation level of Madrasa students was in the high mean range and the students are highly motivated to use digital technology for Quranic memorization. Furthermore, results indicate that the impact of digital technology integration on Quranic memorization was at a high level of the mean range amon…

title: Understanding student satisfaction with generative AI learning tools in Vietnamese business education: a TAM- and SDT-informed framework
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the determinants of student satisfaction with their experience of using artificial intelligence (AI) tools for learning-related activities in Vietnamese higher education, addressing a gap in research that has focused primarily on AI adoption and usage, with limited evidence on students’ post-use satisfaction in an emerging-market higher education context. Design/methodology/approach A construct-level framework informed by selected insights from the technology acceptance model (TAM) and self-determination theory (SDT) was used to organise perceived credibility, content quality, perceived utility, cognitive absorption and emotional wellbeing within one explanatory model. Survey data from 380 undergraduate business students were analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM). Findings All five factors were positively associated with satisfaction. The findings indicate that students’ satisfaction depends not only on the functional value of generative AI tools but also on the credibility of their outputs and the cognitive and emotional quality of the learning experience. Originality/value This study shifts attention from AI adoption to satisfaction as a post-use evaluative outcome. Rather than testing TAM or SDT in their entirety, it uses selected insights from both theories to organise complementary technology-related…

title: Identification and evaluation of diagnostic signatures for VTE based on bioinformatics analysis and machine learning
abstract: Abstract Background Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a common life-threatening vascular disorder for which reliable diagnostic biomarkers remain limited. This study aimed to identify potential diagnostic signatures by integrating bioinformatics and machine learning, followed by model evaluation. Methods Both GSE19151 and GSE48000 were adopted to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in VTE patients. Functional enrichment analyses were performed using GO and KEGG databases. Five machine learning algorithms (LASSO, RF, XGBoost, GBM, and KNN) were applied to screen diagnostic biomarkers. The expression levels and diagnostic performance of the candidate biomarkers were both evaluated in GSE19151, GSE48000 datasets and examined in a clinical cohort by ELISA. The models were evaluated using AUC, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA), and DeLong’s test was used to compare AUCs between models. Results Venn analysis identified 76 common DEGs in VTE, primarily enriched in erythrocyte homeostasis and oxidative stress pathways. Four candidate biomarkers (BFAR, CXorf21, PIP5K1A, and UBFD1) were identified. BFAR (535.7 ± 84.3 vs. 451.4 ± 24.2 pg/mL, p < 0.001) and CXorf21 (688.5 ± 89.8 vs. 598.8 ± 31.9 pg/mL, p = 0.006) protein levels were significantly higher in VTE patients than in controls. The GSE19151-derived four-molecule nomogram had an apparent AUC of 0.979 (9…

title: Evaluating Drug–Drug Interactions by Constructing Advanced Machine Learning Models of ABC Transporter Inhibitors
abstract: Abstract ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporters play a critical role in transmembrane transport, and the inhibition of ABC transporter-mediated efflux can lead to unintended drug–drug interactions (DDIs). The identification of new drug candidates as perpetrators of transporter-mediated DDIs requires synthesis of significant drug products and costly experimental evaluation. Alternatively, computational approaches can rapidly and accurately screen the DDI liability of new drug candidates in silico. Here, we developed a novel DDI risk assessment protocol incorporating classic and graph-based quantitative structure–activity relationship (QSAR) models. These models were trained on publicly available, large-scale, structurally diverse in vitro chemical inhibition data for P-gp, BCRP, and MRP1. The resultant models yielded promising R2 scores (0.58 to 0.82). External predictions successfully identified inhibitors, verified by experimental validation or literature review, and detected drugs with the potential to perpetrate clinically relevant DDIs. In summary, we developed a large, diverse database of ABC transporter inhibitors and present an applicable alternative protocol that incorporates model predictions to evaluate transporter-mediated DDIs for new drug candidates to prevent potentially harmful clinical outcomes.

title: How do learning facilitation competency and self-leadership relate to learning outcomes?
abstract: Purpose This study aims to empirically examine how instructors’ learning facilitation competency and learners’ self-leadership are associated with engagement, satisfaction and transfer in corporate training contexts. It further investigates whether learning engagement mediates the relationships among these key variables. Design/methodology/approach The research was conducted with a sample of 537 adult learners who had prior experience in corporate training programs and was grounded in facilitation learning theory and self-directed learning theory. Findings The findings show that instructors’ facilitation competency is significantly associated with learning engagement and satisfaction but does not show a significant direct relationship with learning transfer. Learners’ self-leadership is positively associated with all three outcomes: engagement, satisfaction and transfer. Learning engagement functions as a key mediator, especially between facilitation competency and transfer. Overall, facilitation competency shows stronger associations with engagement and satisfaction than self-leadership. Research limitations/implications This study has several limitations. First, cross-sectional self-report data limits causal inference and common method bias may inflate associations, particularly for learning transfer. Second, the sample is limited to Korean adult learners, which may affect ge…

title: Perspectives of adaptation to new technologies: qualitative study on the use of educational robots in industrial engineering education
abstract: Purpose The continuous advancement of digital technologies and the increasing complexity of industrial production require industrial engineers to possess both theoretical knowledge and practical skills relevant to real-world environments. Educational robots provide an effective and accessible means to bridge the gap between academia and industry. The main objective is to demonstrate how the use of educational robots improves understanding of automation, robotization and human-technology interaction, which are key aspects of Industry 4.0. Design/methodology/approach This research adopts a qualitative, exploratory approach to capture users' perspectives based on their experience with educational robotics, supported by inductive code quantification. The study introduces an educational robotics kit designed to simulate manufacturing and logistics processes in a laboratory setting. Through guided exercises and team-based problem-solving, students engage in practical tasks that mirror real industrial scenarios. Findings Practice-oriented learning enhances both technical and managerial competencies. Students analyze differences between manual and automated production, evaluate advantages and limitations of robotization and suggest process improvements. Collaborative activities also strengthen communication, teamwork, and decision-making skills. Integrating educational robots increases…

title: Machine Learning and Homopolymer-Based Calibration for Enhanced Composition Analysis by Infrared Detection in Polyolefin Chromatography
abstract: Abstract Polyolefins, the most widely produced class of synthetic polymers, play a pivotal role in modern society. Their performances are inherently controlled by key molecular parameters such as molecular weight distribution (MWD) and comonomer content—also referred to as short-chain branching (SCB)—and its distribution (chemical composition distribution, CCD, or SCBD). State-of-the-art techniques employ chromatographic methods, e.g., high-temperature gel permeation chromatography (HT-GPC/SEC), crystallization elution fractionation (CEF), and Crystallization+Extractables (CRYSTEX) in 1,2,4-trichlorobenzene (TCB) coupled with filter-based infrared (IR) detectors, providing MWD and CCD quantification. However, this approach heavily relies on labor- and resource-intensive comonomer compositional calibration workflows, requiring bespoke well-defined copolymer references/standards, narrow fractions derived from preparative molecular weight fractionation (PMMF), and 13C nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) validation. These limitations hinder cross-laboratory consistency in data comparison and industry-wide efforts to precisely correlate molecular structures with material performance and to accelerate the development of cost-effective upcycling of plastic wastes. This study introduces a calibration strategy using commercially available α-olefin homopolymers, e.g., homopolymer polyethyle…

title: Artificial intelligence in higher education (AIHE): implications for personalized learning and institutional practices
abstract: Purpose This study addresses the following research question: What are the implications of artificial intelligence (AI) for Personalized Learning and Online Higher Education (OHE)? Design/methodology/approach A qualitative study was conducted using semi-structured interviews including faculty members and higher education administrators. The data were analyzed to identify the adoption factors, challenges, opportunities, and ethical considerations. An Integrative Model of Adopting AI in Online Higher Education (IMAOHE) was developed based on the empirical findings. Findings AI supports personalized learning through adaptive assessment, real-time feedback, learning analytics, and tailored content. The reported challenges include ethical dilemmas, institutional barriers, and the need to preserve teacher autonomy. Research limitations/implications Limited respondents and lack of student perspectives suggest future research with larger, more diverse samples and mixed-methods or longitudinal designs. Practical implications The model guides institutions, educators, and developers to integrate AI ethically and strategically, ensuring meaningful, context-aware learning. Social implications AI can enhance equity, inclusion, and student-centered learning while maintaining human mediation and cultural sensitivity. Originality/value This study provides an empirically grounded model linking A…

title: Natural Missplicing Events Amplified by an Elusive Deep-Intronic MYBPC3 Variant Cause Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
abstract: BACKGROUND: Disruption of MYBPC3 precursor mRNA splicing is a frequent genetic cause of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM). Most often, it reflects changes at canonical sites or the creation of novel splice sites. Prediction tools usually prioritize splice variants with lower efficiency when they are distant from canonical sites. These elusive variants may explain HCM in patients considered genotype-negative after DNA testing. METHODS: Massively parallel sequencing identified the previously unreported deep-intronic variant MYBPC3 c.2308+227G>A in a cohort of genotype-negative patients with HCM from Salamanca, Spain. SpliceAI predicted a benign effect (Δ score, 0.03). However, its recurrent detection prompted us to conduct extensive analyses to investigate its pathogenicity, including genetic testing, clinical assessment, family studies, splicing assays, and haplotype reconstruction. RESULTS: We identified 35 unrelated HCM probands carrying c.2308+227G>A, plus 46 relatives from 27 families, yielding 81 confirmed carriers. Of these, 56 (69%) met diagnostic criteria for HCM (66% male; mean age, 53±15 years). By age 60 years, cumulative penetrance was estimated to be 81% in women and 96% in men. The combined logarithm of the odds score of 5.51 across 20 informative families provided strong evidence of cosegregation. During follow-up of probands, no significant differences were obser…

title: Supply chain coordination in contract farming under yield uncertainty and alternative agricultural subsidy policies
abstract: Food grain subsidies and contract farming are two important institutional arrangements for stabilizing agricultural production and improving farmers' incomes. However, the effectiveness of these policies and organizational arrangements depends critically on the interaction between subsidy mechanisms and supply chain contracts. To examine this interaction, we develop a Stackelberg game model of the operational decisions and coordination of a contract farming supply chain under two major agricultural subsidy programs: the Target Price (TP) program and the Producer Direct (PD) program. Our analysis yields several important insights. First, both subsidy schemes increase the company's profit relative to the no-subsidy benchmark. For farmers, however, the TP scheme does not always yield higher profits than the no-subsidy case. When the farmer's production cost coefficient is relatively low, the subsidy induces substantial expansion of planted acreage. As the Stackelberg leader, the company responds by substantially reducing the wholesale price. This adjustment redistributes part of the benefits generated by the target-price subsidy from farmers to the company. Second, the traditional wholesale-price contract fails to coordinate the contract farming supply chain in the presence of government subsidies. To address this issue, we propose a “wholesale price + fixed transfer” contract tha…

title: Acceptance, adaptation and interaction: how entrepreneurs navigate institutional uncertainty in Iran’s emerging fintech industry?
abstract: Purpose Entrepreneurs in developing economies often face uncertainty due to weak or absent formal institutions, prompting them to rely on a combination of practices to mitigate this uncertainty and successfully create and develop their ventures. This study examines how entrepreneurs in Iran’s emerging Fintech industry navigate and respond to institutional uncertainty. This study aims to bridge the gap in understanding the intersection between institutional uncertainty and entrepreneurial action. Design/methodology/approach An inductive exploratory investigation was conducted using a multiple case study approach to examine how entrepreneurs navigate and manage institutional uncertainty. Findings Entrepreneurs adopt three primary modes of action in response to institutional uncertainty: acceptance, where entrepreneurs acknowledge the existing institutional status quo and overcome uncertainty arising from institutional constraints by managing their attention to what is controllable; adaptation, where they devise strategies to circumvent institutional challenges; and interaction, where they actively engage in communications to change harmful institutions through institutional entrepreneurship or bypass them by leveraging rent-seeking behaviors. Practical implications This research offers valuable guidance for existing and potential entrepreneurs on navigating institutional uncertai…

title: Acceptance-threshold and remanufacturing decisions under returned-core quality uncertainty
abstract: Purpose This paper investigates how a manufacturer should set the acceptance threshold for returned cores under quality uncertainty when returned-core supply is limited. It examines whether stricter quality screening necessarily improves profitability and whether remanufacturing always enhances environmental performance. Design/methodology/approach We develop a supplier–manufacturer Stackelberg game in which the supplier sets the wholesale price of new cores and the manufacturer endogenously determines the acceptance threshold for returned cores, together with the production quantities of new and remanufactured products. The model captures the trade-off between accepted-core quality and accepted-core availability and incorporates carbon-emission accounting. Findings A stricter acceptance threshold improves the average quality of accepted cores and lowers the average remanufacturing cost, but it also reduces accepted-core availability. Therefore, the optimal threshold depends critically on returned-core market size. When accepted-core supply is sufficiently abundant, new-core procurement is relatively costly, and consumers sufficiently value remanufactured products, the manufacturer may shift from mixed production to exclusive remanufacturing. However, relaxing the threshold to expand remanufacturing does not always improve environmental performance, because the induced output e…
