Interpreting participation in sharia-compliant fintech markets: User narratives of engagement, uncertainty, and socio-economic meaning
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how users interpret and sustain participation in Sharia-compliant fintech markets within digitally mediated financial environments and how governance signals, conditional acceptance and socio-economic meaning shape engagement, risk negotiation and trust. Design/methodology/approach Adopting an interpretivist qualitative design, this study analyses 43,994 user-generated reviews from seven Sharia-compliant fintech platforms in Indonesia. Data were collected from the Google Play Store and analysed using reflexive thematic analysis supported by ATLAS.ti through iterative coding, pattern development and thematic abstraction. Findings Participation is constructed through an evolving process of sensemaking rather than discrete behavioural decisions. Governance signals enable users to infer institutional credibility through platform interactions, while conditional acceptance explains how continued participation is sustained despite recognised uncertainty. Socio-economic meaning reinforces engagement by embedding financial participation within broader contexts of financial inclusion, ethical legitimacy and household well-being. Originality/value This study advances behavioural finance and fintech research by conceptualising governance signals and conditional acceptance as interpretive mechanisms through which users construct institutional credibility a…

title: RSM-based multi-objective optimization of process parameters for aluminum alloy pipe stir welding: mechanical and microstructural evaluation
abstract: Purpose This study aims to optimize the friction stir welding (FSW) process parameters for AA1100 aluminum alloy pipe joints and evaluate their effects on tensile strength, microhardness, and microstructural characteristics. The objective is to identify the optimal combination of tool rotational speed, welding speed, and axial load for achieving superior joint performance suitable for industrial piping applications. Design/methodology/approach AA1100 aluminum alloy pipe joints were fabricated using friction stir welding. Response Surface Methodology (RSM) based on a Box-Behnken Design (BBD) was employed to investigate the influence of tool rotational speed, welding speed, and axial load on the mechanical properties of the welded joints. Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) was used to evaluate the significance of process parameters and their interactions. Multi-response optimization was performed using the desirability function approach to simultaneously maximize tensile strength and microhardness. Microstructural characterization was conducted to examine grain refinement and weld quality in the stir zone. Findings The ANOVA results indicated that tool rotational speed was the most influential process parameter for both tensile strength and microhardness. The quadratic models exhibited high coefficients of determination (Rˆ2 = 0.99 for tensile strength and Rˆ2 = 0.98 for microhardness)…

title: Critical Daily Dose Warning Optimization in an Electronic Health Record at a Tertiary Cancer Center
abstract: Objectives: Clinical decision support (CDS) is a form of health information technology utilized by electronic health records (EHR) to reduce prescribing errors. The challenge of incorporating CDS into medication workflows is balancing alert fatigue with clinical appropriateness. At a tertiary cancer center, one form of interruptive CDS is critical dose warnings that appear when the ordered dose deviates by a defined threshold from the maximum dose. A tertiary cancer center relies on a third-party data vendor to provide maximum dose limits that are integrated into the EHR medication ordering process. At the time of project initiation, only critical single dose warnings were visible, with a deviation threshold of 500%, therefore end users did not see critical daily dose warnings. Materials and Methods: At this 777-bed tertiary cancer center, critical daily dose warnings with deviation thresholds ≥500% were evaluated for clinical appropriateness from October 31, 2024, to March 31, 2025. A clinically appropriate warning was defined as one that identified a dose unsupported by published literature after considering patient-specific and clinical factors. The project aim was to reduce clinically inappropriate critical daily dose warnings by 10% by June 2026. During the pre-intervention period, there were 1,926 critical daily dose warnings ≥500% deviation threshold. The top 10 medicati…

title: Dynamic Programming Principle for Stochastic Control Problems on Riemannian Manifolds
abstract: In this paper, we first establish the dynamic programming principle for stochastic optimal control problems defined on compact Riemannian manifolds without boundary. Subsequently, we derive the associated Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation for the value function. We then prove the existence, uniqueness of viscosity solutions to the HJB equation, along with their continuous dependence on initial data and model parameters. Finally, under appropriate regularity conditions on the value function, we establish a verification theorem that characterizes optimal controls.

Evolving landscape of biomarkers in colorectal cancer: From interleukin-8 to integrated multi-marker strategies
abstract: Interleukin-8 (IL-8) is a pro-inflammatory protein implicated in blood vessel formation, tumor growth, and cancer spread, making it a candidate biomarker in colorectal cancer (CRC). Recent prospective data confirm that serum IL-8 levels are significantly elevated in patients with CRC compared with healthy controls, with moderate diagnostic accuracy (area under the curve, 0.68) and independent predictive value. However, these findings must be interpreted within the contemporary multi-pillar biomarker framework for CRC, where mismatch repair status, RAS /BRAF mutations, tumor laterality, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 amplification, neurotrophic tyrosine receptor kinase fusions, phosphoinositide 3-kinase pathway alterations, perioperative carcinoembryonic antigen, and postoperative circulating tumor DNA have emerged as key clinically relevant biomarkers with growing levels of evidence. This opinion review critically examines the potential role of Interleukin-8 (IL-8) within this evolving landscape and provides a comprehensive overview of the current biomarker spectrum in CRC. Although IL-8 is consistently overexpressed in CRC and shows promise in multivariable models, substantial heterogeneity in study design, assay platforms, and patient populations limits the generalizability of existing data. IL-8 may represent an investigational complementary biomarker with potentia…

title: Strain-Resilient Integrated Conductive Elastomer with Stable Conductivity via Grafting and Blending for Flexible Sensing and Self-Adhesive Dry Electrocardiogram Monitoring Electrode
abstract: Abstract Integrated conductive elastomers have attracted significant attention for their potential in flexible wearable electronics, electrocardiogram (ECG) monitoring, and other fields due to their unique combination of elasticity and electrical functionality. Conventional flexible conductors often suffer from environmental instability, such as solvent leakage in gels, or conductivity degradation under mechanical deformation in filler-based elastomers. To realize practical applications in flexible electronics, conductive elastomers must possess stable conductivity under stretching, as well as superior deformability and resilience. Moreover, addressing the trade-off between electrical performance and mechanical properties of conductive elastomers is still challenging. In this study, the solid polymer electrolyte (SPE) polyethylene glycol (PEG) was incorporated into a butyl acrylate (BA) elastomer via grafting and blending to fabricate integrated conductive elastomers. Furthermore, based on the multi-bond network (MBN) concept, 1-vinylimidazole (VI) was copolymerized into the butyl acrylate elastomer backbone to form Zn2+-VI coordination, which further enhanced the mechanical properties of the conductive elastomer. The PEGMA chains grafted onto the BA ensure excellent compatibility between P(BA-co-VI)-g-PEGMA/Zn2+ and the blended free PEG chains, thereby inhibiting phase separat…

A study on experimental demonstration of CMOS–MEMS PiezoMOS force sensors integrated with current-mirror readout circuitry
abstract: Purpose This study aims to experimentally validate and characterize PMOS and NMOS current-mirror-integrated cantilever-and bridge-based force sensors. Design/methodology/approach Four sensor configurations were fabricated and characterized, consisting of PMOS- and NMOS-based current-mirror readouts integrated on both cantilever and bridge structures on 2-inch <100> silicon wafers. In each device, the reference MOSFET is placed on the substrate and remains unaffected by applied load, while the output MOSFET, embedded at the fixed edge, converts mechanically induced stress into drain voltage variations via the piezoresistive effect of the MOSFET. Device characterization was performed under controlled and repeatable loading conditions using a nanoindenter. Findings All four sensors showed reproducible voltage responses to the applied force. The sensor sensitivities ranged from 0.010 to 0.95 mV/mN, with the NMOS cantilever sensor showing the highest sensitivity. The NMOS sensors showed approximately an order of magnitude higher sensitivity than PMOS sensors, consistent with the larger piezoresistive coefficients of N-type silicon for the <100> orientation. Furthermore, cantilever sensors showed higher sensitivity than bridge sensors due to their greater mechanical deflection under equivalent loading conditions. Repeated trials and measurements performed on multiple devi…

title: Развитие института социальных координаторов в системе поддержки участников специальной военной операции
abstract: В статье рассматривается процесс институционализации новой для российской системы социальной защиты населения профессиональной группы – социальных координаторов. Проанализированы нормативно-правовые основы их деятельности, специфика и отличия в требованиях к социальным координаторам и риски в разрезе претендентов на должность из числа работников социальных служб и ветеранов боевых действий. Выявлены ключевые проблемы деятельности социальных координаторов в системе комплексной поддержки участников специальной военной операции (СВО) и членов их семей при длительной работе в помогающих профессиях. This article examines the institutionalization of a new professional group within the Russian social welfare system: social coordinators. It analyzes the regulatory framework for their activities, the specifics and differences in requirements for social coordinators, and the risks associated with job applicants from among social service workers and combat veterans. Key problems in the activities of social coordinators in the system of comprehensive support for participants in special military operations (SMO) and their family members during long-term work in helping professions were identified.

title: Corruption, institutions and economic growth in South America: evidence from multi-dimensional governance indicators
abstract: Purpose This study examines how corruption and institutional quality interact to influence long-run economic growth in nine South American economies over the period 1980–2019. It explores whether the economic effects of corruption are uniform or conditional on institutional strength, with particular emphasis on judicial and legislative integrity as moderating factors. Design/methodology/approach The study develops an extended Solow-type framework where corruption affects total factor productivity and institutions moderate this effect. Using V-Dem corruption indicators, the analysis applies Common Correlated Effects Mean Group (CCE-MG), Dynamic CCE, Dynamic Ordinary Least Squares and panel threshold estimators to account for heterogeneity and cross-sectional dependence. Findings Corruption has a persistent negative effect on economic growth, while stronger judicial and legislative integrity improves productivity. Threshold results show that corruption is more damaging under weak institutional conditions and less harmful once institutional quality passes a critical level. Research limitations/implications The study focuses on South America and uses governance indicators that may not fully capture informal corruption. Future research could extend the framework to other regions and include additional institutional or financial channels. Practical implications The findings suggest t…

title: Multi-objective, multi-type, continuous space maximal covering problem: an application to points- and areas-of interest
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this work is to identify optimal air-defense locations in a multi-objective (MO) setting considering multiple and sometimes competing objectives within a large search space at the national scale. Design/methodology/approach First, a mathematical MO maximal covering location problem is formulated. This formulation includes the following three objectives: (1) providing coverage to densely populated areas, (2) providing coverage to areas having high residential and commercial property value and (3) providing coverage to infrastructure of national or regional significance. Three algorithms are applied to solve the problem, and their performance compared (1) Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II), (2) an augmented NSGA-II-A and (3) Strength Pareto Evolutationary Algorithm II (SPEA-II). Findings Within the context of our computing environment, specific parameter settings, implementations and case instances, our results indicate that the NSGA-II-A algorithm outperforms both the NSGA-II and SPEA-II algorithms in that the NSGA-II-A algorithm concentrates solutions toward the estimated Pareto front within reasonable computational effort. Originality/value The originality of this study lies in its integrated approach to defense location planning, combining multiple defense-resource types, point- and area-based coverage priorities and an application-spe…

title: Predictive value of multi-slice spiral computed tomography tumor diameter and necrotic ratio for very high-risk gastrointestinal stromal tumors
abstract: BACKGROUND Accurate preoperative risk stratification of gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GISTs) is essential for individualized treatment planning and prognostic evaluation. However, reliable non-invasive imaging biomarkers for identifying very high-risk GISTs remain limited. AIM To evaluate multi-slice spiral computed tomography (MSCT)-derived maximum tumor diameter and necrotic area ratio (NAR) for predicting very high-risk GISTs. METHODS We enrolled 158 patients with primary GIST treated at Binhai County People’s Hospital (January2025 to October 2025). The patients underwent preoperative plain abdominal MSCT and triple-phase enhanced scanning. Based on postoperative pathology, the patients were categorized as very high-risk or non-very high-risk. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses identified independent predictors of very high-risk GISTs. The diagnostic efficacy of the combined predictive model was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. RESULTS Among 158 patients with primary GIST, 35 (22.2%) were classified as very high-risk. Multivariate logistic regression identified maximum tumor diameter and NAR as independent predictors of very high-risk GISTs (both P < 0.01). The combined predictive model demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance [area under the ROC curve (AUC) = 0.968], yielding a significantly higher AUC than that o…

title: EK Cha b: Multi-tracer detection of a protoplanet candidate in a gas-rich environment
abstract: Despite sustained community efforts and advances in instrumentation and high-contrast imaging, the search for protoplanets remains difficult, with only two widely accepted systems to date in Class II systems (PDS 70 and WISPIT 2). Here we present the detection of EK Cha b, a new protoplanet candidate, identified through CO emission, millimeter continuum, and 0.82 μm broadband photometry, linked to EK Cha, a young late-type M star. The detection of a new protoplanet candidate offers an additional opportunity to advance our understanding of planet formation. By exploiting the wealth of archival data available for nearby star-forming regions, we aim to place EK Cha b in context, characterize its properties, and motivate future campaigns targeting similar systems. We analyzed high-spatial-resolution archival observations of EK Cha from HST, VLT/NACO, VLT/MUSE, and ALMA. We searched for EK Cha b in broadband continuum and gas tracers, reporting the measured flux with uncertainties, and upper limits for non-detections. EK Cha b shows a spectrally resolved footprint that matches the CO J=2--1 emission, together with 0.82 μm and millimeter continuum emission. EK Cha b is spectrally resolved in CO J=2--1 emission, kinematically consistent with a circumplanetary disk. Best fits from evolutionary models place EK Cha b as a planetary-mass companion, although deeper observations are require…

title: Network positions and project-based innovation in cross-regional construction projects: a role embeddedness perspective
abstract: Purpose This study aims to explore the heterogeneous effects of network embeddedness on project-based innovation performance (PIP) within cross-regional construction collaboration networks, focusing on differences in network effects between project owners (POs) and cross-regional project teams (CPTs). Design/methodology/approach Using 153 cross-regional construction projects completed in the Greater Bay Area between 2013 and 2023, this study applies social network analysis to construct lagged cumulative collaboration networks and measure five dimensions of network embeddedness. Hierarchical negative binomial regression models examine the linear and nonlinear effects of PO and CPT network positions on PIP. Findings The network analysis shows that CPTs have broader connections, stronger bridging positions, and greater local cohesion, whereas POs are more concentrated within particular network communities. For POs, degree centrality shows a monotonically decreasing relationship with PIP, betweenness centrality has a negative effect, structural holes have a positive effect, clustering coefficient has an inverted U-shaped effect, and closeness centrality shows no stable effect. For CPTs, degree centrality and structural holes show inverted U-shaped relationships; closeness centrality and clustering coefficient have positive effects, whereas betweenness centrality has a negative effe…

title: Breaking the vicious cycle of health management: how compensatory strategies increase consumers' persistence after experiencing failure
abstract: Purpose Consumers pursuing health goals often experience two types of failures: health-management behavioral failure and outcome failure. Both can undermine intentions to persist in health behaviors. This research examines how these failures influence persistence intentions and proposes two intervention strategies (i.e. conservative and breakthrough) based on compensatory control theory to restore sense of control and encourage persistence in health behaviors. Design/methodology/approach Four studies are developed to test these hypotheses. Specifically, in the context of keeping exercise, Study 1A examined whether familiarity and novelty strategies could effectively alleviate the negative consequences of behavioral failure and outcome failure, respectively, which demonstrates H1a and H1b. Study 1B further investigated the differentiated compensatory effects of self-production and non-self-production strategies across the two types of failure, which demonstrates H2a and H2b. To further enhance the robustness of the findings, Studies 2A and 2B replicated the above investigations in the context of dietary control, providing additional evidence for H1 and H2, respectively. Findings The findings of four experiments are convergent and indicate the effectiveness of two types of intervention strategies, namely, the adoption of conservative strategies (i.e. familiarity and non-self-prod…

title: Effect of Filtration Time on the Performance of PVDF Membrane for Palm Oil Mill Effluent Treatment
abstract: Palm oil mill effluent (POME) is a high-viscosity wastewater generated during palm oil processing. Its high content of oil and grease, suspended solids, and colloidal organic matter contribute to elevated turbidity and pollutant loads. Therefore, effective treatment is necessary before POME can be discharged into the environment. Membrane filtration is a potential treatment method for reducing turbidity by retaining suspended and colloidal particles. This study investigated the effect of filtration time on the performance of a polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) hollow-fiber ultrafiltration membrane for POME treatment, with particular emphasis on pure water flux, permeate flux, and permeate turbidity. Before filtration, POME was pretreated with alum at a concentration of 1 g/L. The feed characteristics were assessed by measuring turbidity. Filtration was performed using a dead-end system at a constant pressure of 1 bar for 60 minutes, with measurements taken at 15-min intervals. Pure water flux was measured before POME filtration to establish a baseline for evaluating membrane performance. The results showed that pure water flux decreased from 345.5 to 247.4 L/m²·h, while permeate flux decreased from 56.6 to 10.7 L/m²·h over the filtration period. Meanwhile, pretreatment reduced feed turbidity from 5,060 to 405 NTU, corresponding to a 92% reduction. Subsequent membrane filtration pr…

Andragogical principles as predictors of employee motivation to transfer soft skills training
abstract: Purpose The relationship between andragogical principles and employee motivation to transfer training was examined in this study. The research problem is whether the six principles of andragogy, need to know, self-concept, experience, readiness to learn, orientation to learning and motivation to learn, predict motivation to transfer training among individuals who completed postsecondary soft skill courses in Alberta, Canada. Despite growing organizational investment in workplace training, the challenge of low transfer rates persists: estimates suggest that only 10%–15% of training content is applied on the job (Ford et al., 2018). This study aims to explore the predictive relationship between andragogical principles and transfer motivation to better understand how training programs can be made more effective. Grounded in Malcolm Knowles’ Theory of Andragogy and Baldwin and Ford’s Transfer of Training model, the research investigates two primary questions: whether the combined principles of andragogy predict motivation to transfer training and whether these principles individually predict this motivation. Design/methodology/approach The study uses a quantitative correlational predictive design with data collected from n = 134 participants via online surveys administered through the centiment platform, resulting in a final sample of n = 122 after data cleaning and outlier removal…

title: Beyond moonlighting: side-gigs and employee performance
abstract: Purpose We examine how types of secondary activities relate to primary job performance under bounded rationality and when managers should permit, encourage, or restrict them. Design/methodology/approach Using an archival dataset from professional baseball (1945–2018), we classify secondary activities as unrelated, teaching-related, or learning-related. We estimate Ordinary Least Squares and difference-in-differences models around the 1965 Major League Baseball (MLB) draft and measure performance with Wins Above Replacement Findings Unrelated and teaching-related secondary activities are associated with lower performance, whereas learning-related secondary activities are associated with higher performance than teaching-related secondary activities. When the job becomes more salient, these negative associations intensify, while the performance advantage of learning-related secondary activities widens. Research limitations/implications Evidence derives from a single industry and an observational setting. The cognitively aligned typology and boundary-condition logic refine Behavioral Theory of the Firm accounts of attention allocation and offer testable extensions. Practical implications Rather than adopting blanket rules, managers should evaluate secondary activities according to their cognitive demands, intensity, alignment with the focal role, and demonstrated performance conseq…

title: The right to exogamy: Muslim-born women in partnership with Italian men
From the P2SK Law to its amendment
abstract: This study examines the legal politics of financial-services supervision in Indonesia across Law No. 21 of 2011 on the Financial Services Authority (OJK), Law No. 4 of 2023 on Financial Sector Development and Strengthening, and its 2026 amendment. Using normative legal research with statutory, conceptual, and case approaches, it analyzes Constitutional Court Decisions No. 59/PUU-XXI/2023 and No. 85/PUU-XXII/2024, legislative materials, and official supervisory reports. The analysis identifies three phases: institution-building in 2011; expansion of regulatory and enforcement powers in 2023; and recalibration in 2026 through shared investigative authority, sector-specific restorative justice, an expanded supervisory perimeter, and parliamentary performance evaluation. The article develops an accountable-independence framework drawing on international standards for financial supervisors. It argues that accountability is legitimate when it concerns transparent reporting, aggregate performance, governance, and use of resources, but becomes problematic when binding recommendations or prior legislative approval can influence technical supervisory decisions or individual enforcement cases. The constitutional position of Bank Indonesia requires separate consideration under Article 23D of the 1945 Constitution, while OJK’s institutional design must be read alongside its statutory mandat…

title: Right Brain: Language Without Speech
Analysis of financial fraud at oil and gas holding company: fraud triangle theory perspective
abstract: Purpose This research aims to examine the influence of fraud triangle theory on financial fraud. Variables such as financial target, internal audit and core values were used to explain fraud triangle theory. Financial target was measured through the profit growth ratio, while internal audit was assessed based on the number of auditors. The core values were measured by the understanding score of corporate governance. Design/methodology/approach The quantitative research method was used and secondary data were collected from the company’s annual report. The amount of data observed was 323 from 2018 to 2022 and analysis was carried out using the regression method. Findings The results showed that internal auditors and core value had a positive and negative effect on financial fraud, respectively. On the other hand, financial target did not affect financial fraud. Research limitations/implications This research has limitations. First, the measurement of the dependent variable only showed the existence of sanctions in the company. Second, the internal audit section only showed the number, without describing the profile and competency of auditors. Practical implications This research has practical implication such as company should adopt new policies, internal control procedures or employee training to strengthen an ethical culture and reduce the risk of fraud. title: Discretion, rotational programs and reported corruption in public procurement: an analysis of Italian municipalities
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to assess whether municipalities that increased their reliance on direct award procedures (DAP) after the 2020 Italian procurement reform, which more than tripled the monetary threshold for DAP, were more likely to report corruption cases and whether staff rotation moderates this association. Design/methodology/approach The analysis focuses on Italian municipalities with more than 15,000 inhabitants over the period 2016–2023. It uses difference-in-differences and triple-difference designs to analyze, respectively, whether municipalities that increased their reliance on DAP after the reform experienced a higher likelihood of reported corruption and whether staff rotation moderated this relationship. Findings Municipalities that increased their reliance on DAP after the reform are more likely to report at least one corruption case. The results also indicate that staff rotation mitigates this association. Originality/value This paper offers novel evidence on the association between municipalities’ increased reliance on discretionary procurement procedures and reported corruption at the municipal level, complementing contract-level analyses by focusing on a nationwide regulatory change. It further extends prior experimental evidence on staff rotation by providing longitudinal, real-world evidence on how staff rotation moderates the association between increa…

title: The allocation channel of monetary policy: reserve parking, liquidity regimes and transmission effectiveness in the euro area
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine whether the allocation of central-bank reserves between the European Central Bank (ECB) deposit facility and current accounts influences monetary-policy transmission independently of the aggregate quantity of liquidity. The study addresses an empirical puzzle: abundant-reserve frameworks are expected to provide tight control of overnight rates, yet small but persistent deviations between market and administered rates remain. The dependent variable is the transmission gap, measured as the absolute deviation between the euro short-term rate (€STR) and the ECB deposit facility rate. Reserve allocation is measured by both the share of reserve liquidity parked in the deposit facility and the levels of parked and circulating balances. Design/methodology/approach The study uses monthly euro-area data. The main estimations use a modern transmission sample beginning with the introduction of €STR, while a complementary historical liquidity sample supports longer-run analyses of liquidity regimes, thresholds and structural stability. The empirical framework combines heteroskedasticity- and autocorrelation-consistent baseline regressions with interaction, dynamic, threshold, quantile, structural-break and rolling-window specifications, together with multi-collinearity diagnostics and alternative dependent-variable checks. Findings Reserve allocation does …

title: Perlindungan Hak Atas Lingkungan Hidup yang Baik dan Sehat Sebagai Hak Konstitusional: Analisis Kasus Polusi Udara di Surabaya
abstract: Although the right to a good and healthy environment has been constitutionally guaranteed under Article 28H paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution and Law Number 32 of 2009, its implementation in Surabaya remains far from substantive fulfillment, particularly in the context of increasingly alarming air pollution; therefore, this study aims to analyze the implementation of such rights protection and identify the factors affecting its effectiveness. This study employs an empirical legal method with a qualitative approach, combining statutory and case approaches. Informants were selected through purposive sampling, encompassing local government officials, affected communities, and other relevant stakeholders. Data were collected through literature review, interviews, and observation, while data analysis was conducted through the stages of data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing, with data validity verified through source and method triangulation as well as member checking. The findings indicate that air quality in Surabaya remains under pressure due to motor vehicle emissions contributing approximately 60–70% of total pollutant loads and industrial activities, while implemented policies such as emission testing, industrial supervision, and green open space development have not effectively reduced pollution levels significantly. The effectiveness of rights protection i…

title: Natural resource rents and financial development in Sub-Saharan African countries: is there an inverted U-shaped curve?
abstract: Purpose This paper examines the impact of natural resources on financial development using data from 32 Sub-Saharan African (SSA) countries from 1992 to 2021. The study also examines the existence of an inverted U-shaped relationship between natural resource rents and financial development in these countries. Design/methodology/approach The study uses quantile regression analysis and Driscoll–Kraay estimators within a quadratic setting to examine this linkage. The study also divides SSA into three groups: All SSA, low-income SSA and middle-income SSA. In addition, the study uses five proxies of financial development in a stepwise fashion, thereby estimating multiple model specifications for each technique and each SSA income group. Findings Overall, the study found a distinct inverted U-shaped relationship between natural resource rents and financial development to exist only in middle-income countries and only when financial development is measured by the Financial Development Index (FINDI). In the remaining specifications, the results indicate a predominantly U-shaped rather than inverted U-shaped relationship in all instances where a non-linear pattern is observed. This suggests that natural resource rents may hinder financial development (i.e. act as a curse) in some SSA countries, particularly low-income countries, during the early stages of development. However, once a ce…

title: Microfinance sustainability amid gender inequalities in G20 emerging economies: the role of female board representation and voice and accountability
abstract: Purpose The role of microfinance institutions (MFIs) in fostering economic development in emerging markets cannot be denied. Nevertheless, concerns regarding their financial sustainability persist. This study examines the relationship between social performance and state-level governance indicators, specifically voice and accountability, in shaping the financial sustainability of MFIs. In addition, the research examines how social performance, amid prevailing gender inequalities, shapes the financial sustainability of MFIs. Design/methodology/approach We analyse panel data from MFIs across the emerging economies of the G20, sourced from the MIX Market database of the World Bank. Gender inequality index (GII) data were obtained from the United Nations Development Programme website. Using dynamic panel data analysis, specifically the generalised method of moments (GMM), we estimate robust standard errors. Additionally, we employ moderated hierarchical regression to assess the interaction effects of social performance with voice and accountability, under conditions of gender inequality. Findings The results indicate that financial sustainability in the previous period significantly predicts current performance, suggesting persistence over time. Female representation on boards enhances operational self-sufficiency (OSS), though it does not have a direct effect on return on assets (…

title: Forty years on: revisiting the bridge
OmniVira: a knowledgebase of source-linked evidence on viral spillover and cross-species transmission
abstract: Abstract Zoonotic viral emergence poses persistent challenges to global health, yet evidence relevant to spillover and cross-species transmission is dispersed across surveillance, epidemiological, experimental, mechanistic, and genomic studies. Here, we present OmniVira (https://omnivira.org/), a curated knowledgebase that transforms literature-derived findings into structured, traceable, and reusable OmniVira Evidence (OVE) records. OmniVira implements an auditable article–evidence framework linking individual findings and supporting text to normalized virus, host, and geographic entities, and relevant biological context. A domain-specific ontology organizes 14 evidence types into five categories: Zoonotic Surveillance, Transmission Evidence, Experimental Infection, Functional Mechanism, and Genomic Evolution. The platform integrates ontology-guided curation, large language model-assisted literature screening and candidate extraction, automated consistency checks, and curator review of flagged or ambiguous records, enabling daily updates. As of 4 August 2026, OmniVira contained 8072 publicly retrievable OVE records derived from 2623 source articles, spanning 60 ICTV virus families, 55 host orders, and 121 countries. Its responsive interface supports evidence-centred retrieval, source-text verification, and exploration of linked virus–host–literature relationships across deskto…

title: Digital financial inclusion in Europe: the roles of digital infrastructure, socioeconomic structure and institutional quality
abstract: Purpose This study investigates how digital infrastructure, socioeconomic structure and institutional quality are associated with digital financial inclusion (DFI) across Europe. Design/methodology/approach Using World Bank Global Findex and World Development Indicators data for 24 European countries across the 2014, 2017 and 2021 survey waves, the study estimates fixed-effects panel regressions with country-clustered standard errors separately for developed and emerging and frontier economies. Random-effects comparisons are also conducted for the latter group. Robustness analyses examine the influence of Kazakhstan, population sub-grouping, economic classification and survey-wave effects, while wild-cluster-bootstrap tests assess sensitivity to the small number of country clusters. Findings Digital infrastructure, particularly Internet connectivity, exhibits the most recurring positive associations with DFI, especially for payment activity. These relationships are more consistent in developed economies, whereas the emerging and frontier results are broader but more sensitive to estimator choice, survey-wave controls and small-cluster inference. Population sub-grouping and economic classification reveal patterns concealed by aggregate and pooled estimates. Excluding Kazakhstan preserves the principal Internet-related payment findings and selected Gross Domestic Product (GDP) pe…

title: Annals Graphic Medicine - Right Back Where We Started
Islamic finance adoption among entrepreneurs in Kyrgyzstan’s dual banking system: a qualitative study
abstract: Purpose This study aims to explain why Islamic finance adoption remains limited among entrepreneurs in Kyrgyzstan despite strong ethical and religious appeal. It shows that adoption depends on financial knowledge and institutional capacity rather than values alone. It argues that ethical preference does not become market uptake without these foundations. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative design was adopted using semi-structured interviews with 25 entrepreneurs and senior managers across key regions of Kyrgyzstan. Data were analyzed through thematic analysis, which identified four interrelated themes. Findings Participants generally perceive Islamic finance as ethically legitimate and religiously compatible. However, actual adoption is contingent on price competitiveness, accessibility, transaction speed and institutional reliability. Knowledge gaps and limited product diversity reduce perceived distinctiveness relative to conventional banking. Structural barriers include limited staff expertise, operational complexity and inconsistent religious guidance, which together weaken trust and increase decision uncertainty. Entrepreneurs express cautious optimism about future growth, conditional on measurable improvements in institutional capacity, service quality and financial literacy. Practical implications The findings indicate clear managerial priorities, including improve…

title: «Стеклянный потолок счастья»: проблемы финансовой устойчивости нижнего среднего класса в Башкортостане
abstract: Цель исследования – оценить степень финансовой уязвимости домохозяйств Республики Башкортостан в условиях зависимости от текущих трудовых доходов. Фактическая база исследования собрана методом социологического исследования – опроса населения на территории региона (n = 2216 респондентов), проведенного ИСЭИ УФИЦ РАН в 2025 г. Исследование позволило подтвердить гипотезу о формировании пограничного статуса нижнего среднего класса в регионе, чье потребление поддерживается за счет кредитного плеча, а финансовая стабильность находится в прямой зависимости от непрерывности текущих доходов основного кормильца. The aim of the study is to assess the degree of financial vulnerability among households in the Republic of Bashkortostan that rely on current labor income. The empirical data were gathered through a sociological survey of the regional population (n = 2,216 respondents) conducted by the ISER UFRC RAS ​​in 2025. The study confirmed the hypothesis regarding the emergence of a "borderline" status for the lower-middle class in the region – a group whose consumption is sustained through credit leverage and whose financial stability depends directly on the continuity of the primary breadwinner's current income.

title: Novel Interactive Visual Heuristics for Evaluating Audience Perception of Ethical TikTok Campaigns
abstract: The rapid evolution of social media, particularly short-form video platforms like TikTok, has fundamentally transformed the dissemination of ethical and sustainability messages to global audiences. This paradigm shift presents a profound challenge for contemporary design researchers and communication practitioners, who must navigate the complexities of audience perception within an intensely competitive and fast-paced digital ecosystem. The core objective of this study is to develop and demonstrate a novel interactive visual heuristics framework that enables the simulated evaluation of audience response to ethical campaign content prior to public deployment. Our methodological approach involves the systematic construction of a prototype interactive environment that applies defined visual heuristic principles to synthetic eco-influencer campaign material, analyzed using rigorously generated dummy engagement data. Key findings from this simulation reveal that specific interactive heuristics, particularly those emphasizing procedural transparency and authentic source relatability, serve as the most significant drivers for positive ethical perception and intended behavioral engagement. The primary contribution of this work is a rigorous, reusable design research tool that provides graphic designers and digital strategists with an evidence-based, low-risk methodology for optimizing …

EDA-AGENT: A MULTI-AGENT AI SYSTEM FOR RTL VERIFICATION, CIRCUIT DEBUGGING, AND SEMICONDUCTOR DESIGN AUTOMATION
abstract: Hardware verification and debugging consume over 70% of digital Integrated Circuit (IC) design cycles. Hardware engineers spend thousands of hours manually parsing static timing reports, inspecting Value Change Dump (VCD) waveform traces in GTKWave, and writing SystemVerilog assertions (SVA). In this paper, we introduce EDA-Agent — an open-source, multi-agent artificial intelligence platform designed to automate Register-Transfer Level (RTL) code analysis, functional testbench generation, waveform failure debugging, synthesis area estimation, and timing slack optimization. EDA-Agent combines Large Language Models (LLMs) with deterministically bounded Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) static analysis, VCD waveform time-tick tracing, and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) over IEEE specifications. Our empirical evaluation demonstrates 100% unit test accuracy, 94.2% bug localization accuracy on VCD signal traces, a 37.5x acceleration in testbench generation compared to human engineers, and 89.5% functional coverage reachability.

title: Enhancing Intellectual Property Protection in Digital Graphic Design: A Conceptual Framework for Integrating Blockchain and Digital Rights Management Systems
abstract: This study addresses the increasing risk of intellectual property (IP) violations in the digital graphic design industry, driven by the ease of copying, modifying, and distributing digital content across online platforms. Traditional protection methods are no longer sufficient in the rapidly evolving digital environment. Therefore, the study aims to develop a conceptual framework integrating blockchain, digital watermarking, encryption, and Digital Rights Management (DRM) to enhance intellectual property protection in digital graphic design. The research adopts a descriptive–analytical approach supported by multiple case studies and a comparative analysis of recent academic literature and documented industrial applications. Selected case studies, including Adobe Content Authenticity and blockchain-based protection systems, were analyzed using predefined evaluation criteria to compare the capabilities of contemporary protection technologies within digital graphic design workflows. The comparative analysis indicates that multi-layered protection systems can enhance the security, authenticity, and traceability of digital design assets. Blockchain supports ownership verification through immutable records, while encryption, digital watermarking, and DRM provide complementary mechanisms for protecting digital content, improving transparency, and strengthening digital trust. The revie…

title: Synthesis-by-design of ferroelectric Dion–Jacobson two-dimensional hybrid organic–inorganic perovskites
abstract: Abstract Dion–Jacobson two-dimensional hybrid organic–inorganic perovskites are promising ferroelectric materials, combining chemically tunable polarity enabled by their organic spacers with enhanced environmental stability. However, rational discovery remains difficult owing to uncertain phase formability and scarce, biased ferroelectric data. Here we show a staged, physically guided synthesis-by-design workflow that integrates learning from scarce ferroelectric data with structure-aware screening. Starting from 11 known ferroelectric compounds in this family, symbolic regression defines a descriptor-bounded ferroelectric-consistent region. Similarity-guided expansion and chemical filtering reduce 83,924 molecules to 1012 candidate divalent spacers, while machine-learned interatomic-potential relaxation and connectivity analysis identify 338 candidates retaining Dion–Jacobson connectivity. Sequential prioritization by connectivity retention, chemical similarity, energetic refinement and synthetic accessibility selects s −2-fluorobutane-1,4-diamine, leading to the synthesis of a PbI 4 -based Dion–Jacobson perovskite with experimentally confirmed ferroelectric switching. This prospective proof of concept shows how sparse property knowledge can be coupled with structural screening to prioritize organic spacer candidates for experimental synthesis.

title: Context-aware intelligent colour design via multi-objective optimisation and vision–language models
Pharmacophore-Conditioned Diffusion Model for Ligand-Based De Novo Drug Design
abstract: Abstract Developing bioactive molecules remains a central, time- and cost-heavy challenge in drug discovery, particularly for novel targets lacking structural or functional data. Pharmacophore modeling presents an alternative for capturing the key features required for molecular bioactivity against a biological target. In this work, we present PharmaDiff, a pharmacophore-conditioned diffusion model for 3D molecular generation. PharmaDiff employs a transformer-based architecture to integrate an atom-based representation of the 3D pharmacophore into the generative process, enabling the precise generation of 3D molecular graphs that align with predefined pharmacophore hypotheses. Through comprehensive testing, PharmaDiff demonstrates superior performance in matching 3D pharmacophore constraints compared to ligand-based drug design methods. Additionally, it achieves higher docking scores across a range of proteins in structure-based drug design, without the need for target protein structures. By integrating pharmacophore modeling with 3D generative techniques, PharmaDiff offers a powerful and flexible framework for rational drug design.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Harmonizing Family Law with International Human Rights Standards: Comparative and Legislative Reform Perspectives
abstract: Family law is a critical site where Islamic legal traditions, state regulation, social practice, and international human-rights standards intersect. In Muslim-majority jurisdictions, tensions surrounding gender equality, marriage, polygamy, divorce, child marriage, custody, maintenance, and marital property raise a broader question of how legal reform can protect human dignity without treating Islamic law as inherently incompatible with contemporary rights. This article employs normative legal research using statutory, conceptual, comparative, and case-oriented approaches. It examines international human-rights instruments, Indonesian constitutional and statutory law, the Compilation of Islamic Law, and comparative reform experiences in Morocco, Tunisia, Malaysia, and India, supplemented by recent scholarship on Indonesia. The analysis finds that sustainable harmonization is best understood as dialogical normative translation rather than one-sided legal transplantation. Five mutually reinforcing pathways are emphasized: contextual ijtihad and maqāṣid al-sharīʿah reasoning; rights-based legislative reform; gender- and child-sensitive adjudication; comparative legal learning; and participatory accountability through civil society and international monitoring. The Indonesian experience demonstrates that formal legislative progress, including the 2019 marriage-law reform, may be we…
venue: JISRev: Journal of Islamic Studies Review

title: Reform on paper, change in practice: mapping connections between organizational practices
abstract: Purpose This study examines how structural reforms unfold through the reconfiguration of interrelated organizational practices. It investigates how changes in these practices – whether or not formally mandated – are enabled or constrained through changes in the material-spatial, temporal, jurisdictional and communicational–cultural connections that link them. Design/methodology/approach The study uses qualitative interview and documentary material from two structural reforms in the Estonian Ministry of Education and Research to demonstrate how practice connections can be analysed empirically. During the analysis, a distinction emerged between practices targeted by reform and instrumental practices through which reform implementation unfolded, providing the analytical basis for identifying how ties between practices were maintained, disrupted or reconfigured. Findings The findings show that organizational change gains traction through changes in how everyday practices are connected. Reforms reshaped work when authority and responsibility were redistributed, when task sequencing and timing changed or when spatial arrangements altered opportunities for coordination. Where reforms did not alter these connections, or addressed them only weakly, particularly through communication, formal changes remained largely nominal. Originality/value This study introduces the distinction between…

title: Translating organizational learning mechanisms into organizational development in schools: the roles of reform sensemaking and organizational literacy orientation
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how organizational learning mechanisms relate to organizational development in schools, whether reform sensemaking mediates this relationship, and whether these relationships vary across organizational literacy orientations. Design/methodology/approach Survey data were collected from 1,261 respondents in 97 Taiwanese junior high schools. Of these, 767 were classified into one of four dominant organizational literacy orientations and formed the common analytic sample. Structural equation modeling was used to test direct and indirect relationships, followed by multi-group comparisons across orientations. Findings Organizational learning mechanisms were positively related to organizational development both directly and indirectly through reform sensemaking, supporting partial mediation. Neither of the two paths constituting the indirect relationship differed significantly across orientations. The indirect relationship as a whole, however, differed across orientations and was statistically significant only in the bureaucratic group. Research limitations/implications The cross-sectional, individual-level design limits causal and school-level inference. Longitudinal and multilevel research is needed to establish temporal ordering, examine reciprocal relationships and determine whether these patterns hold across schools and reform contexts. Surrogate-Assisted Robust Multi-Objective Optimization of a Fluidized-Bed Methane Pyrolysis Reactor Under Technical and Market Uncertainty
abstract: Conventional multi-objective optimisation (MOO) of methane pyrolysis reactors assumes model parameters as precisely known, while many crucial factors are highly unknown. This research uses NSGA-II and Monte Carlo sampling to produce and analyse robust Pareto fronts under uncertainty using a surrogate-assisted robust multi-objective optimisation framework. Kriging surrogates trained on 300 Latin hypercube designs with 500 Monte Carlo samples compare mean–variance, worst-case, and chance-constrained formulations.
venue: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology

title: Combined application of Pseudomonas chlororaphis strains and zinc suppresses Alternaria alternata leaf spot in chili pepper
abstract: ABSTRACT Chili pepper ( Capsicum annuum L.) is a vital vegetable crop susceptible to yield loss from Alternaria alternata (Fr.), Keissl., which causes leaf spot/blight and fruit rot. Harnessing beneficial rhizobacteria offers an eco-friendly strategy to enhance plant resilience to biotic stressors. In vitro screening identified Pseudomonas chlororaphis strains viz., P. chlororaphis subsp. aurantiaca (ARS-38) and P. chlororaphis subsp. chlororaphis (RP-4) as potent antifungal strains, inhibiting A. alternata growth by 62% and 64%, respectively. In a zinc (Zn)-amended medium, their antifungal activity increased further, reducing fungal growth by 70% with individual strains and 93% when combined. Microscopy revealed fungal growth inhibition linked to conidia and conidiophore disintegration. In planta under open-field pot conditions, A. alternata infection resulted in 100% disease incidence (DI) and altered histochemical, photosynthetic, and enzyme responses. Treatment with ARS-38 + RP-4 in Zn-amended soil enhanced plant resistance by increasing lignin and phenolic accumulation and reducing enzyme activities, resulting in a 96% reduction in DI. Zinc supplementation improved plant health and enhanced disease suppression when combined with the bacterial strains. Combining rhizobacteria with Zn (2 mg/kg) emerges as a promising strategy to mitigate Alternaria leaf spot disease and enha…

title: Corporate Governance, ESG Disclosure and Firm Value in an Emerging Market
abstract: Purpose: This paper examines how corporate governance and the disclosure of environmental, social and governance (ESG) information have co-evolved in Vietnam between 2015 and 2024, and through which channels the two are expected to bear on firm value in an emerging market where the state remains a dominant owner. Design/methodology/approach: The study adopts a qualitative design that combines systematic document analysis of 18 regulatory and soft-law instruments issued between 2012 and 2024 with an integrative review of published empirical evidence on Vietnamese listed companies and secondary benchmark data from the ASEAN Corporate Governance Scorecard and a ten-year census of disclosure practices. Material was coded deductively against agency, stakeholder, legitimacy, signalling and institutional theory, and inductively for emergent themes. Findings: Vietnam’s regime moved through three phases: Mandated entry (2015 to 2017), soft-law consolidation (2017 to 2020) and statutory upgrading with climate alignment (2021 to 2024). Disclosure spread rapidly in breadth, yet depth lagged. Standalone reports rose only from about 1 percent to 7 percent of listed firms, GRI referencing stayed near 22 percent throughout the decade, and third-party assurance remained rare. Vietnam’s mean governance score in the 2024 regional assessment (60.15 points) sat 31 points below the ASEAN mean. The e…
venue: International Journal of Advanced Multidisciplinary Research and Studies

title: Analysis of the Impact of E-Commerce on the Labor Market: A Case Study of the Clothing Market
abstract: The rapid development of e-commerce and technology has changed the labor market across the whole economy in different fields. Meanwhile, more complaints have emerged on social media, similar to those regarding layoffs and poor employment conditions. This study aims to explore the impact of e-commerce on the labor market, especially on the unemployment rate, and uses the case study of the clothing market to help investigate this thesis. The clothing market is characterized by long-tail structure and short product life cycles. This study looks into factors in the labor market such as job creation and displacement, among other factors that affect the labor market on a global scale. This essay applies different types of e-commerce to discuss and support the impacts in order to use examples to explore. This research helps to establish a link between e-commerce and the labor market and the effects of the labor market on the environment in the development of e-commerce.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: The Economics of Scarcity and Ecosystem Lock-in: NVIDIA's Premium Pricing, Market Power and Consumer Willingness to Pay in the AI Accelerator Market
abstract: This study analyzes NVIDIA's high pricing model in the AI chip market by combining the concepts of product differentiation, market power, and consumer behavior. It suggests that NVIDIA has established very high switching costs with the CUDA ecosystem, making the price elasticity of demand very low, if not approaching zero, allowing them to charge a price well above the marginal cost. While this approach is based on using excess profits to invest in technological progress, it has also brought about demand-side issues such as distortions in the allocation of resources resulting from the "computing capacity tax" and consumer surplus reductions due to hardware-and-software bundling. At the industry level, it has exacerbated the excessive concentration of the market and created systemic risks. To address this, this study recommends steps to optimize these measures, like setting up interoperable technical standards, moving towards transparent tiered-pricing regulations, and enhancing the resilience of the supply chain. These measures are designed to maintain a balance between the corporate incentives for innovation, market fairness, and efficiency, and to offer a theoretical reference for the healthy development of the AI industry ecosystem and inclusive growth in the global digital economy.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Industry Dynamics and Strategic Business Analysis: An Applied Case Study of Data Bridge Market Research
abstract: Market research supports strategic decision-making by helping organizations interpret customer needs, competitive conditions, regulatory developments, technological change, and emerging sources of risk. Yet the availability of information does not automatically produce reliable market intelligence. Researchers must define the market precisely, assess the credibility and comparability of evidence, and connect observations to the business question being examined. This paper presents an applied case study of secondary market research and strategic analysis conducted in the professional research environment of Data Bridge Market Research Private Limited (DBMR), Pune. The analysis is based on a documented research project undertaken between 12 May and 11 August 2026 and uses a descriptive, single-organization case-study design. It covers healthcare, packaging, advanced materials, chemicals, food and agriculture, and technology and services. Eight markets received detailed attention: global sleep apnea devices, European aesthetic dermatology, global paper and paperboard packaging, Brazilian corrugated board packaging, global soft magnetic materials, European vegetable oil-based esters, global custom pulses, and U.K. restaurant point-of-sale systems. Approximately 30–40 market report descriptions were also prepared, according to the project record. The analytical process drew on PESTE…
venue: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management

title: The customer is always king! Exploring how service experiences, identity fit, and social media shape customer satisfaction and loyalty in the café sector
abstract: Abstract China’s café sector has moved from excellent coffees to address experience, ambiance, exposure, and brand exclusivity. Stimulus-organism-response (SOR) theory furthers the social, emotional, and behavioural endeavours on customer loyalty in this evolutionary industry. This study investigated the influences of service innovation, store environment, staff behaviour, identity cues, and self-congruence cues including lifestyle congruence, brand identification, and ideal self-congruence on brand loyalty by internalizing satisfaction, brand trust, and brand love. Social media marketing activities (SMMA) was further examined on the internalized factors and brand loyalty. Using AMOS and SPSS, obtained findings from 351 café consumers in China clarified the collective influences of operational excellence and identity alignment on satisfaction. The insignificant influence of ideal self-congruence specifies matching brand identity through actual self-congruence. Satisfaction then influences brand loyalty through brand trust and brand love, with SMMA moderates the relationship between satisfaction and brand loyalty. This study highlighted the importance of external and self-congruence stimuli on satisfaction, brand trust, and brand love. To improve brand loyalty, meaningful social media engagement is strategically needed by café practitioners for higher satisfaction.

title: The Impact of Insurance Market Regulation on Companies' Financial Growth Prospects: The Case of Georgia
abstract: This paper examines the impact of regulations on the financial performance of Georgian insurance companies. The research period covers 2016-2024. The research employs deductive reasoning and multiple linear regression using a constructed Regulatory Stringency Index (RSI) and secondary data. The findings indicate that Georgia's insurance market experienced rapid growth alongside a substantial strengthening of capital adequacy and solvency measures following regulatory reforms, confirming that enhanced oversight has bolstered financial stability. However, the results also reveal a trade-off: stricter regulations are associated with lower return on equity and profit margins, suggesting that compliance costs and higher capital buffers modestly constrain profitability.

title: Beyond Age: Market Context, Perceived Value, Social Influence, and Product Category in Young Consumers' Brand Choice
abstract: This review examines how young consumers choose brands by moving beyond explanations that rely mainly on age. Existing studies treat young consumers as an important market segment, but age alone does not explain why the effect of loyalty is stronger in some product categories than in others. This paper argues that young consumers' brand choice is shaped by three main mechanisms: market and information context, perceived value, and social influence. Market and information context influences what brands consumers notice and encounter. Perceived value explains how consumers judge price, quality, usefulness, and risk. Social influence explains how family, peers, online reviews, and user-generated content shape brand meaning and purchase decisions. The review also argues that product category acts as a boundary condition: routine products, visible identity products, and high-risk information-intensive products activate different decision mechanisms. The paper ends with a framework and future research directions that link consumer behavior to business analytics, including segmentation, prediction, and recommendation systems.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Digital Accounting Disclosure and Market Valuation of Listed Non-Financial Companies in Nigeria
abstract: The increasing use of digital technologies in accounting has changed not only how financial information is generated but also how companies communicate the quality and reliability of their reporting processes to capital-market participants. This study examines the relationship between digital accounting disclosure and market valuation of listed non-financial companies in Nigeria, focusing on real-time financial reporting disclosure, automated tax reporting disclosure and automated internal control disclosure. The study adopts an ex-post facto design and uses archival information from annual reports and corporate disclosures of 66 listed non-financial companies over 2016–2025. Market valuation is proxied by market capitalization growth, while firm size, measured as the natural logarithm of total assets, is included as a control variable. Disclosure indices are constructed from corporate reports. The reduced model was re-estimated from the underlying firm-year observations rather than transferring coefficients from the original seven variable model. Robust ordinary least squares estimates based on 538 complete observations show positive but statistically insignificant coefficients for real-time financial reporting disclosure (β = 0.515; p = .333), automated tax reporting disclosure (β = 0.889; p = .264), and automated internal control disclosure (β = 1.216; p = .492). The finding…

title: Investigating Consumer Preferences and Behavior in the Digital Coffee Market on the Tmall Platform in China
abstract: China’s coffee market has expanded alongside the rapid development of digital retail platforms, yet the mechanisms through which online platform-related product perceptions shape coffee purchasing frequency remain insufficiently specified. This study examines consumer preferences and behavior in the digital coffee market on Tmall, a major Chinese business-to-consumer online retail platform [citation needed]. Drawing on consumer behavior theory, digital platform marketing, and a cautious Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) logic, the study investigates how coffee product customer preference (CP), coffee product portfolio design (PD), coffee product customer feedback (CF), and offline experience of coffee products (OE) relate to the average monthly frequency of purchasing coffee products through Tmall. Primary survey data were collected from 270 consumers through online channels, yielding 265 valid responses and a valid response rate of 98.1%. The data were analyzed using reliability analysis, validity assessment, exploratory factor analysis, confirmatory factor analysis, and structural equation modeling (SEM). The results show that CP has a significant positive effect on purchasing frequency, whereas PD and OE have significant negative effects. CF is not statistically significant. The study contributes by focusing specifically on China’s Tmall coffee market and by identifying how…
