Orientación al mercado y desempeño económico en empresas textiles de los Valles Centrales de Oaxaca
abstract: El objetivo de este artículo es analizar los fundamentos teóricos y la evidencia empírica sobre la relación entre la orientación al mercado y el desempeño económico, con el propósito de construir un marco conceptual aplicable al estudio de las empresas textiles de los Valles Centrales de Oaxaca. Se desarrolla una revisión teórica integrativa basada en literatura clásica y contemporánea de marketing estratégico, pequeñas empresas y contextos artesanales, complementada con fuentes académicas e institucionales sobre la producción textil oaxaqueña. El análisis distingue dos tradiciones principales: el enfoque cultural de Narver y Slater, centrado en orientación al cliente, orientación a la competencia y coordinación interfuncional, y el enfoque conductual de Kohli y Jaworski, que conceptualiza la orientación al mercado como generación, difusión y respuesta a inteligencia de mercado. La evidencia acumulada muestra una asociación generalmente positiva entre orientación al mercado y desempeño, aunque su magnitud depende de la medición, el tamaño de la empresa, el sector y el entorno competitivo. Para el contexto textil de los Valles Centrales se propone privilegiar el enfoque conductual, debido a que permite estudiar procesos de información y respuesta sin presuponer estructuras departamentales formales. El modelo resultante plantea que la generación de inteligencia de mercado, su int…

title: Left Anterior Descending Artery Also Lives at the Apex: A Cardiac Point-of-Care Ultrasound Blind Spot and the Risk of False Reassurance
Building a Sustainable Governance Pattern Based on Constructive-Spontaneous Theory: Evidence from the Chinese Tourism Market
abstract: Research on market governance has emphasized top-down strategies, often neglecting the demand-side dynamics. To address this limitation, this research constructs an analytical framework grounded in constructive-spontaneous theory. Utilizing Fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis on a large-scale online review dataset, we examine how diverse governance configurations shape sustainable tourism experiences. The results show that the efficacy of governance models is contingent upon the level of external risks. In low-risk scenarios, both government-led constructive governance and platform-led spontaneous governance can effectively enhance the tourism experience. However, high-risk environments demand a synergistic governance model. This study highlights a paradigmatic shift from unidimensional governance towards polycentric coordination and explains the influence of risk events on market governance through a demand-oriented perspective.

title: Multi-Objective Optimization of Spot-Welding Robot Trajectories Using an Improved NSGA-II Algorithm
abstract: To address the inherent drawbacks of conventional spot-welding path-planning methods, which cannot simultaneously consider welding efficiency, energy consumption and trajectory motion stability, this paper proposes an intelligent path-planning approach for spot-welding robots based on the improved NSGA-II multi-objective optimization algorithm. First, the NSGA-II algorithm is optimized with improved targeting to the spot-welding process. An integer-permutation encoding scheme together with a random initialization strategy is adopted to guarantee the feasibility of solutions for welding-point sequences. Meanwhile, the original genetic operators are replaced. Ordered crossover and Swap mutation are employed to enhance the algorithm’s adaptability to combinatorial optimization problems. Second, focusing on the core evaluation indicators for robot paths, including path length, energy consumption and motion stability, this paper constructs a quantitative characterization model for each indicator and integrates these models into the multi-objective optimization framework. On this basis, path-simulation experiments are carried out on the JAKA-A5 robotic platform. The experimental results show that the proposed method can realize the collaborative optimization of the above-mentioned objectives. Compared with the unoptimized random sequence, the path length is reduced by 36.67%, the ene…

title: AI Pilot Zones and Labor Market Demand: Evidence from China
abstract: Whether artificial intelligence policy can expand labor demand, and how the additional demand is distributed across different types of jobs, is an important question in evaluating the economic consequences of technological development. This paper matches city-level annual online job posting data and city statistical yearbook data with policy information on the National New-Generation Artificial Intelligence Pilot Zones, and employs a difference-in-differences model to examine the labor market effects of pilot zone construction. The results show that the policy significantly increases overall local hiring demand. The growth in recruitment covers workers at different levels of education, skills, and experience, and is reflected in high-skill, low-technology, technology- and knowledge-intensive, and labor-intensive positions. At the same time, the posted wage gap between high-skill and low-skill positions widens. These findings indicate that the construction of AI pilot zones may bring about both a multi-tiered expansion of job demand and a divergence in skill-based wages, providing empirical evidence for coordinating technological development, worker skill upgrading, and employment policy.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Calibrated agents as market makers: automated liquidity provision for long-tail prediction markets
Impact of Non-Technical Losses on The Electricity Grid in Smart Grids: The Case of Dicle Electric Ditribution Company
abstract: Non-technical losses (NTL) in electricity distribution networks are not only a economic and commercial issue but also a critical engineering problem that shortens the life of network equipment, degrades power quality, and threatens system reliability. In cases where individual subscriber consumption data is inaccessible or privacy constraints exist, detecting illegal usage poses a significant challenge. The main objective of this study is to empirically prove that macro-level electrical anomalies carry the characteristics of non-technical losses by using the Automated Meter Reading System (AMR) secondary data belonging to a specific distribution transformer located in the responsibility area of Dicle Electricity Distribution Corporation. Within the scope of the study; load profiles, power factor collapses, net reactive power asymmetry, inter-phase current-voltage unbalances, and voltage sags were analyzed in depth. As a result of the analyses, it was determined that uncompensated and single-phase loaded illegal usages reduce the power factor of the transformer to dangerous levels, create severe phase asymmetry causing overloads on the neutral line, and push voltage profiles out of standards. The findings demonstrate that without direct household-based data, non-technical losses can be detected with high accuracy by processing macro anomalies solely in transformer output paramet…
venue: Turkish Journal of Electrical Power and Energy Systems

title: Beyond relationship investments: leveraging market access equity and AI-enabled intelligence for superior market performance
Cross market consumer behavior intelligence through corporate multimodal financial sentiment computing and predictive recommendation systems
A Reverse QFD Framework Integrating Interval Type-2 Fuzzy Sets and Regret Theory for Seasonal Demand Analysis in Smart Farmland Abandonment Monitoring Platforms
abstract: The abandonment of farmland necessitates the implementation of intelligent monitoring platforms that are tailored to the specific requirements of relevant stakeholders. However, the prevailing solutions in this domain tend to prioritize technical performance over considerations of seasonality. The present study proposes a Reverse Quality Function Deployment (R-QFD) framework integrating interval type-2 fuzzy sets, Regret theory, and grey-entropy TOPSIS to analyze and prioritize user requirements for smart farmland abandonment governance. To address these challenges, the model incorporates interval type-2 fuzzy sets to manage linguistic uncertainty, regret theory to capture behavioral biases, and a feedback-driven R-QFD mechanism for adaptive design. Using data from 204 stakeholders in Jiangxi Province, China, this model revealed distinct seasonal demand fluctuations: land abandonment warnings predominate in spring; online customer service reaches its zenith in summer; land transfer information becomes paramount in autumn; and online service experiences a resurgence in winter. The recommendations made in this study include prioritizing seasonal features, incorporating behavioral feedback loops, and using modular architectures. The present study proposes a replicable, behavior-aware demand analysis model for smart agriculture and associated technology governance.

title: Interpersonal Violence Victimization and Attributions Among Black LGBTQ+ Young People: Associations with Behavioral Health Indicators
KAN-GRU: A Lightweight Temporal Kolmogorov-Arnold Network for Cloud Resource Utilization Forecasting
abstract: Accurate forecasting of cloud resource utilization is essential for proactive provisioning, autoscaling, and energy-aware scheduling in modern data centers. Temporal Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (TKANs) provide a promising alternative to MLP-based models by combining Kolmogorov- Arnold representations with recurrent sequential modeling. However, prior TKAN formulation typically relies on LSTM-style recurrence, which increases parameter count and computational cost. This work introduces KAN–GRU, a lightweight TKAN-based architecture that substitutes the LSTM cell in the TKAN temporal component with a GRU, reducing parameters while preserving temporal modeling capacity. The evaluation benchmarks KAN–GRU for data-center resource-utilization forecasting under univariate and multivariate configurations and across single-step and multi-step prediction horizons. The results indicate that KAN-GRU improves computational efficiency while maintaining competitive predictive performance, making it suitable for scalable deployment in monitoring and control operations in cloud environments.
venue: Sakarya University Journal of Computer and Information Sciences

title: Boundary Conditions of Institutional Investors' Impact on Stock Price Crash Risk
abstract: Institutional investors are central participants in the capital market, and stock price crash risk is directly tied to the stability of that market. Existing studies mainly focus on how investors from institutions influence stock price crash risk, yet few studies summarize the boundary conditions under which this influence operates. This paper systematically reviews these boundary conditions from three dimensions: institutional investors' own heterogeneity, firms' own characteristics, and the external market and institutional environment. The literature review results indicate that under different boundary conditions, there are pronounced differences in the direction of institutional investors' impact on stock price crash risk (inhibition or exacerbation), as well as the strength of various mechanisms of influence. Finally, this paper identifies future research directions related to multi-boundary interaction effects and the ongoing reform of China's capital markets, providing a literature basis for deeply understanding the heterogeneous role of institutional investors and improving capital market regulation.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Beyond Price: Unfair Trading Conditions and Data Collection by Dominant Digital Platforms in the EU
abstract: Abstract This paper examines whether data collection by dominant digital platforms can constitute an abuse of dominance under Article 102(a) TFEU. Drawing on the Facebook Germany case, culminating in the CJEU’s ruling in Meta Platforms v Bundeskartellamt, and the Commission’s findings against Meta under Article 5(2) of the Digital Markets Act, it argues that unfair trading conditions offers a more suitable framework than unfair pricing. The paper proposes a three-step methodology of joint application. In this methodology, the GDPR’s data minimisation and purpose limitation principles and the economic value concept from unfair pricing jurisprudence serve as sequential inputs into a single proportionality inquiry, rather than as separate or cumulative theories of harm. This enables holistic enforcement alongside the GDPR and consumer protection law. The paper further argues that ex ante regulation under the DMA and ex post enforcement under Article 102(a) TFEU are complementary rather than substitutable. Article 5(2) DMA, as interpreted in the Commission’s April 2025 decision fining Meta EUR 200 million, is the appropriate forward-looking framework for preventing excessive data collection by designated gatekeepers. Article 102(a) TFEU nonetheless remains an indispensable safety net for conduct outside the DMA’s targeted scope, conduct pre-dating designation, and undertakings belo…

title: ‘Forced’ Opportunism: Purchasing for the Lowest Price in Slovakia
abstract: Public procurement accounts for a significant part of global public expenditure. Procurement legislation usually allows authorities to choose the lowest bid or the most economically advantageous offer. Many argue that the lowest price is suitable only when all contract parameters are precisely specified, whereas European procurement directives favor complex criteria. However, Slovakia and some other European countries still rely heavily on the lowest price even for complex contracts. This article explores why Slovak authorities resist multicriteria evaluation. Bureaucracy theory highlights bureaucrats’ risk-averse behavior, driven by a desire to reduce personal and institutional risk. This opportunistic behavior seems to be a critical factor behind Slovakia’s continued use of lowest-price selection, contrasting with the dominant Western EU practices. Understanding these dynamics reveals barriers to more strategic procurement in Slovakia.

title: A Comparative Investigation of Linear and Non-Linear Methods for Stock Price Prediction
abstract: Predicting stock prices is a common topic in finance and data science. Investors and companies are interested in possible future price movements, but making accurate predictions is difficult. Stock prices can be affected by trading activity, company information, economic conditions, investor decisions, news, and unexpected events. This paper reviews several approaches for stock price prediction, with a focus on both linear and non-linear methods. The methods discussed are Linear Regression, ARIMA, Support Vector Regression (SVR), Decision Trees, Random Forest, Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM). Previous studies are compared based on their datasets, prediction targets, evaluation measures, and main findings. In general, simpler models are easier to understand and use, while non-linear models can deal with more complicated patterns. However, complex models may require more data, computing power, and careful training. The paper also considers problems related to external information, model interpretability, overfitting, and changes in financial markets. Future studies could combine market data with news and sentiment, improve the explainability of AI models, and allow prediction systems to update as market conditions change.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Cross-Validated Adaptive Grey–ARIMA Hybrid forecasting of annual municipal water consumption under structural change: a case study of Suez City, Egypt
A Threshold‐Price Approach to Oligopolistic Competition: A Resolution to the Bertrand Paradox
abstract: ABSTRACT In homogeneous‐product markets, changing a price does more than alter a firm's profit margin: it may also determine which competitors can profitably remain active. This paper develops a new static theory of price competition based on this observation. We first establish that, under homogeneous products, unlimited production capacity, and consumer indifference across firms charging the same price, matching a profitable rival price weakly dominates remaining above it (Matching Dominance). Consequently, firms recognize that every feasible price simultaneously determines the corresponding market structure and solve a single optimization problem in which prices and market structure are jointly determined. The solution yields firm‐specific threshold prices that balance operating margins against the profitability of alternative market structures. We then show that competition selects the lowest threshold price as the Nash equilibrium of the game (Competitive Selection). Unlike the classical Bertrand model, equilibrium prices may exceed the relevant competitive benchmark—the common marginal cost under cost symmetry, or the marginal cost of the next most efficient rival under cost asymmetry—without relying on product differentiation, capacity constraints, repeated interaction, or collusion. The conventional Bertrand outcome nevertheless arises as a special case when the exclusi…

title: Analysis and Forecasting of FTSE 100 Return Volatility Using an ARMA-GARCH Model
abstract: This paper investigates whether a relatively simple ARMA-GARCH specification is useful for modelling and forecasting daily FTSE 100 returns. Closing prices from 31 May 2023 to 28 August 2026 generate 823 percentage log returns. Of these, 758 observations are used for estimation and the final 65 trading days are kept aside as an out-of-sample test. Several low-order ARMA and GARCH specifications, under normal and Student-t errors, are compared using only the estimation sample. BIC selects ARMA(0,0) for the mean equation. For volatility, Student-t GARCH(1,1) is retained because it is parsimonious and its parameters are statistically significant. Out of sample, the mean forecast gives an RMSE of 0.5760 and an MAE of 0.4190, only slightly better than a zero-return benchmark. The reported directional accuracy of 56.9% is largely explained by the positive constant mean, which produces a positive sign forecast on every test day. For conditional variance, GARCH performs better under MAE, whereas the 20-day rolling variance has lower MSE and QLIKE. Overall, the model is more useful for tracking changes in risk than for forecasting the short-run direction of FTSE 100 returns.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Wind Power Forecasting Architectures in Complex Terrain and Coastal Environments: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Comparative Performance
abstract: Wind forecasting in complex coastal terrain, such as the Colombian Caribbean, is hindered by air–sea heat fluxes and nonlinear atmospheric dynamics. This pre-registered systematic review and meta-analysis tests whether advanced architectures (artificial intelligence, hybrid, ensemble) outperform classical ones (physical, statistical). Scopus and Web of Science (last query: 22 September 2026) yielded 100 studies with extractable effect sizes; 76 compared a proposed model with an explicit comparator (primary analysis). Hedges’ g (negative values favor the proposed model) was pooled with REML random effects and Knapp–Hartung inference. The pooled effect was g=−1.07 (95% CI [−1.38,−0.75]; 95% prediction interval [−2.77,0.64]; I2=69.5%), robust to the estimator and to influential studies, although 59 comparisons were against a baseline of the same family. The estimates favored advanced over classical architectures, but not significantly (β=−0.30, 95% CI [−0.99,0.38]); only 10 studies compared them directly, and 9 favored the advanced model (g=−0.78, 95% CI [−1.93,0.36]). Only AI (g=−1.08, k=48) and physical (g=−0.93, k=19) models had intervals excluding zero. Egger and Begg tests indicated funnel-plot asymmetry, but the Pustejovsky–Rodgers test, robust to the dependence of the standard error on the effect, did not. Proposed models outperform their baselines; the superiority of any a…

title: Characterizing statistical association patterns and local forecasting of PM2.5-bound polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon concentrations in Nagoya, Japan
Price Transparency’s Impact on Hospital Prices: An Analysis of the 2021 Hospital TransparencyFinal Rule
abstract: Health care expenditures in the United States have risen steadily for decades, imposing a growing financial burden on patients. In response, President Trump signed an executive order in 2019 requiring hospitals to publicly post the prices of 300 common procedures on their websites that was implemented in 2021. Prior research suggests that price transparency can either increase or decrease prices. This study employs ordinary least squares (OLS) and a difference-in-difference (DiD) framework to evaluate whether the executive order reduced service prices between 2018 and 2022. I hypothesize that prices decline in highly competitive hospital markets but rise in less competitive markets following the transparency mandate. Results indicate no statistically significant change in prices across varying levels of market competition as hospitals became more transparent. The results may be attributed to low compliance rates with the price transparency executive order between 2021-2022.

title: GridMind: Issue-Time-Safe Cross-Country Load Forecasting with Conformal Uncertainty and Operator-Aware Model Selection
abstract: Operational electricity forecasting must be accurate, uncertainty-aware, and protected against future-information leakage. This study presents GridMind, an operator-oriented champion-challenger framework combining a forecast-origin feature ledger, Light Gradient Boosting Machine point forecasts, rolling split-conformal intervals, reproducible feature evidence, and an explicit retain-or-replace decision. The framework was evaluated on complementary national datasets from Panama and Spain. For Panama, the exact 14 published 168-hour test weeks and the prescribed 72-hour unseen gap were reproduced. Target-week realized weather was excluded, and only completed-week load lags and known calendar variables were used. The model achieved 4.193% pooled MAPE, 63.796 MWh RMSE, and a 28.26% reduction in mean weekly MAPE relative to a safe 336-hour seasonal-naive benchmark. It improved 11 of 14 weeks; the mean paired improvement was 1.652 percentage points (bootstrap 95% CI 0.670-2.903; one-sided Wilcoxon p=0.002625). Nominal 90% split-conformal intervals attained 89.97% pooled coverage. For Spain, the public operator forecast remained the champion: H2-2018 MAPE was 0.8855%, compared with 0.8947% after forecast-origin-safe residual correction. GridMind therefore provides an auditable pattern for feature availability, accuracy, calibrated uncertainty, and operational model governance without …

title: Food-level nutrient-to-price analysis and modelled costs of Thai dietary guideline baskets using prices from selected retail outlets in Bangkok, Thailand
Regional Multi-Sector Water-Demand Forecasting with Cross-Sector Historical Information
Subsidiary Cash Holdings and Stock Price Crash Risk —Evidence from Cash Distribution Within Business Groups
abstract: Where a business group keeps its liquidity—within operating subsidiaries or at the parent— shapes how quickly business units obtain funds and the risks investors face. Using consolidated and subsidiary-level disclosures for Chinese A-share firms from 2012 to 2022, this paper finds that the share of group cash retained by subsidiaries forecasts stock price crash risk one year ahead: firms whose subsidiaries control more group cash suffer significantly less severe crashes, a pattern that survives specification checks and matching-based corrections. Two channels underpin the result: subsidiary-level cash enhances financing capacity and resilience, and it restrains idle cash at the group level. The relation is stronger for recently listed and financially constrained firms.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Correction: Enhancing Arabica and Robusta coffee prices forecasting through machine learning approaches
Demand Forecasting Strategies in Fast Fashion Retail
abstract: The fast fashion industry is characterized by short product life cycles, rapid style turnover, and highly volatile demand. Forecast accuracy is therefore a critical determinant of inventory performance, profit margins, and sustainability outcomes. This study systematically reviews the distinctive challenges of demand forecasting in fast fashion, traces the evolution from conventional statistical methods to artificial intelligence-driven approaches, and adopts a comparative case-study design involving Zara and H&M to compare the implementation paths and operational implications of alternative forecasting strategies. The findings suggest an ongoing paradigm shift from forecast-driven production toward demand-driven operations. Rather than pursuing a single high-precision forecast, leading firms are building a dynamic sensing system centered on small-batch testing, real-time data feedback, and agile replenishment. The paper further discusses the implications of this transformation for inventory management, supply chain design, and sustainable development, and proposes differentiated demand forecasting strategies for fast fashion firms.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Mortality Prediction in Imbalanced Pediatric Oncology Data: A Cost-Sensitive Hybrid Resampling Framework Using Recurrent Deep Learning
abstract: Background: Severe class imbalance hampers mortality prediction in pediatric oncology, where clinical-improvement discharges greatly outnumber deaths and bias standard models toward the majority class. Objectives: We aimed to develop and evaluate a Cost-Sensitive Hybrid Resampling Framework (CSHRF) across recurrent deep-learning architectures to mitigate this bias and improve discharge-outcome classification. Methods: A retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted using electronic health record data from a National Institute of Health in Mexico City during 2023. We analyzed 1607 hospital-discharge records, comprising 1554 clinical improvements and 53 deaths. The CSHRF combines cost-sensitive learning, which amplified the mortality class by a factor of 2.5, with a fixed-seed hybrid resampling protocol embedded in a regularized funnel-shaped architecture (N → N/2 → N/4) trained with gradient clipping (clipnorm = 1.0). Simple Recurrent Neural Network (SimpleRNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) models were compared with a naïve recurrent baseline and standard tabular classifiers (Weighted Logistic Regression, Balanced Random Forest, and XGBoost) using stratified cross-validation. Performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), G-mean, sensitivity, specificity, precision, F1-score, mean absolute er…

title: Theoretical Study on Main Parameter Prediction for Full-Face Rock Tunnel Boring Machines
Prediction of time-to-collision for autonomous ground vehicles: An evaluation of supervised and reinforcement learning approaches
abstract: Time-to-collision (TTC) prediction is an essential factor for autonomous ground vehicle (AGV) safety frameworks and decision-making. This research focuses on establishing an efficient benchmark evaluation of supervised machine learning, Neural Networks (NN) and deep reinforcement learning approaches with diverse operational datasets. The investigation utilises a diverse feature set and validation protocol to evaluate three major machine learning (ML) families, namely supervised learning, neural network-based learning, and reinforcement learning. The categorisation includes linear ML regressors (such as Ordinary Least Squares (OLS), lasso, ridge, and ElasticNet), composite ensemble regressors (gradient boosting, random forest, and AdaBoost), Neural network-based (multi-layer perceptron, deep neural network), a meta-learner (MLP-Hybrid) and deep RL algorithms (Deep Q Network, Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient). Key performance indicators (regression scores) indicate that reinforcement learning models significantly outperform classical approaches. The Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) achieved the highest predictive accuracy ( R 2 = 0.986), followed by MLP-Hybrid and Deep Q Network (DQN) with R 2 of 0.891 and 0.878, respectively. Neural network models yield an average of 0.857, while linear and ensemble models delivered average results of 0.752 and 0.727, respectively. Th…

title: Pixel-Wise Prediction of Glioblastoma Recurrence Using Mid-Treatment MRI and Deep Learning
abstract: Introduction: Glioblastoma (GBM) commonly recurs close to the original gross tumor volume (GTV), suggesting treatment-resistant subregions may be present before radiologically visible progression. This study investigated whether deep learning on apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) maps could generate pixel-wise probability maps of treatment-resistant regions within the GTV. Methods: The training/validation set included images of 64 in-house patients after radiation fraction 10 (Fx10) and 40 external patients before treatment used as an auxiliary cross-domain training cohort; the held-out test set included 16 in-house Fx10 patients. Resistant regions were defined as the overlap between the GTV from scans acquired at radiation fraction 10 and subsequent recurrence after finishing treatment. Models were trained on 2D GTV-cropped slices with patient-level separation to prevent data leakage. Single- and multimodal MRI inputs were compared, and ADC-based models (including baseline UNet, pretrained ResNet34, BiomedCLIP-assisted UNet, and a BLIP image-text UNet) were later evaluated. Performance was evaluated using conventional metrics, including ROC AUC, PR AUC, F1-score, recall, specificity, and precision. Results: ADC was the most informative single modality, achieving 69% and 80% for Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC)- and Precision-Recall (PR)-Area Under the Curve (AUC), res…

title: A hybrid physics–data decision-support framework for real-time prediction and season-adaptive optimization of a natural evaporative water cooler
abstract: Abstract This study presents a hybrid physics–data decision-support framework for a natural evaporative water cooler that unifies real-time temperature-drop prediction with season-adaptive operational optimization and delivers both as a deployable tool. A one-dimensional resistance-network heat-transfer model of the cooler forms the physics layer, and machine-learning surrogates trained on 81 balanced experimental runs spanning summer, monsoon and winter (dry-bulb temperature (DBT) 19.3 °C–42 °C, relative humidity 24.6%–80.5%, temperature drop 1.8 °C–9.8 °C) form the data layer. Under ten-fold cross-validation a Gaussian-process regressor is the most accurate model ( R 2 = 0.973), while a tuned artificial neural network ( R 2 = 0.941) is selected as the deployed surrogate because it compiles to a compact, dependency-free model of 241 parameters suited to low-cost field hardware. The neural network is coupled with a differential-evolution search that, for any ambient DBT and relative humidity, returns the operational settings (fan speed, sprinkled-water flow rate and coil-water velocity) that maximize the temperature drop at a fixed, design-selected viscose-fibre pad, generalizing three discrete seasonal optima to a continuous envelope. The global optimality of the search was verified against an exhaustive grid in 1500 independent runs, and the best of five runs came within 0.01…

title: Interpretable machine learning-based prediction of tensile and flexural strength of nanoparticle modified basalt fiber reinforced epoxy composites
Development of conditional cores via supersaturated designs for genetic diversity–based prediction models
abstract: Abstract Genetic diversity is fundamental to sustainable crop improvement. This study uses 1755 soybean [Glycine max (L.) Merr.] recombinant inbred lines from the soybean nested association mapping population, phenotyped for yield across nine environments to optimize the composition of the training set for a given testing set. Using supersaturated designs, we generated conditionally optimized training sets by iteratively selecting candidate genotypes according to a metric that quantifies diversity as the trace of the cross‐product of the genomic matrix containing both a candidate training set and the fixed testing set. Two strategies were considered: (i) maximizing and (ii) minimizing genetic distances to the testing set. Our results show that maximizing genetic distance relative to the testing set improves prediction accuracy over random training sets under standard genomic best linear unbiased prediction. However, this advantage disappeared when models incorporated family structure or genotype‐by‐environment interactions, which consistently yielded superior overall accuracy regardless of training set selection. This result highlights the complexity of considering multi‐omics integration for interpretability: determining whether an increase in accuracy comes from a better model specification or from capturing confounding factors. Finally, we also found that maximizing the gene…

title: Overall survival prediction and risk stratification for advanced EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma patients treated with first-line tyrosine kinase inhibitors
abstract: Abstract Background Lung adenocarcinoma (LAD) is the most common non-small cell lung cancer subtype, with frequent epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutations in Asians. First-line tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) improves survival but resistance is inevitable, leading to disease progression and even death. We aimed to develop a predictive model for overall survival (OS) and prognostic risk stratification. Methods In this retrospective study, patients with stage IIIB-IV EGFR-mutant LAD who received first-line TKIs and underwent pretreatment contrast-enhanced thoracic CT between January 2015 and April 2024 were enrolled. Clinicoradiological findings associated with OS were evaluated using multivariate Cox regression. The performance of the Cox regression model was assessed using the time-dependent area under the curve (AUC) and Harrell’s concordance index (C-index). Nonparametric bootstrapping with 1000 resamples was performed as internal validation to evaluate the robustness and discriminative ability of the model. Results A total of 250 patients (105 males and 145 females) with a mean age of 61 ± 11 years were included. The median OS was 33 (95% CI 25–37) months in patients with advanced EGFR-mutant LAD receiving TKIs. Among the EGFR subtypes, the exon 21-L858R mutation was associated with greater mortality than the exon 19- deletion mutation (HR = 1.541, P = 0.030). Ag…

title: Hybrid Modeling-Based Personalized Prediction for University Dropouts
Probabilistic Prediction of Rock Strength: Physics-Featured Gaussian Process Regression
abstract: Laboratory determination of uniaxial compressive strength (UCS) after in situ sampling is costly and slow. Coupling measurement while drilling (MWD) with machine learning can recover UCS in place. Most such models, however, return point estimates and quantify uncertainty only weakly. This study compiled 161 records from seven sources. Records that recur across sources were removed, leaving 111 unique records, 93 of them soft rock with torque below 100 kN·m. PG-GPR was fitted to these 93 records and checked by five-fold cross-validation with ten random seeds. Against a baseline that used the same kernel on the four raw drilling channels, R2 rose from 0.925 ± 0.011 to 0.964 ± 0.006 and mean absolute error fell from 3.19 ± 0.22 MPa to 2.25 ± 0.15 MPa. At comparable empirical coverage, mean interval width fell from 14.45 ± 0.43 MPa to 8.60 ± 0.25 MPa, and CRPS fell from 2.37 ± 0.12 to 1.65 ± 0.12. Leave-one-source-out scoring of all 93 held-out records together gives R2 = 0.463 and RMSE = 12.11 MPa.

title: Cross‐Ancestry Polygenic Prediction of Bipolar Disorder and Obsessive‐Compulsive Disorder in India
abstract: ABSTRACT Most genetic studies of psychiatric disorders have been conducted predominantly in populations of European ancestry, limiting evidence for the transferability of polygenic scores (PGS) to other populations. This cross‐sectional study evaluated the predictive performance of European‐derived PGS for bipolar disorder (BD) and obsessive‐compulsive disorder (OCD) in an Indian sample. Participants ( N = 2531) included individuals with BD ( N = 463), OCD ( N = 554), and controls ( N = 1514) recruited from hospital‐ and community‐based samples. Genotyping was performed using the Illumina Global Screening Array. PGS were derived from the summary statistics of European‐ancestry genome‐wide association studies using two Bayesian methods, PRS‐CS‐auto and SBayesRC. Principal component analyses demonstrated genetic overlap of the study population with other South Asian populations. BD PGS showed significant predictive performance, explaining approximately 6%–7% of liability‐scale variance with PGS‐only AUCs of ~0.71. OCD PGS showed lower but significant predictive performance, explaining ~2%–3% of variance with AUCs of approximately 0.59. Bayesian approaches showed better predictive performance than conventional clumping‐and‐thresholding. These findings demonstrate that European‐derived psychiatric PGS can retain predictive information in an Indian population, although performance d…

title: The impact of AI hallucination on the chatbot service quality in e-commerce: the moderating role of human agent based service recovery
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence has been widely adopted in e-commerce, demonstrating significant advantages in enhancing information processing efficiency and human-computer interaction. However, its inherent hallucination characteristic often results in the generation of false or misleading content that does not align with reality. In e-commerce, such AI hallucination is likely to trigger a crisis of trust among users and lead to negative evaluations of service quality. Clarifying the mechanisms through which AI hallucination affects chatbot service quality and exploring effective strategies to mitigate its negative effects have become critical issues. The study conducted two scenario-based experiments using a scripted chatbot with pre-written responses. No large language model (LLM) generated the experimental responses. Both experiments employed a 2 × 2 between-subjects design to examine the effects of simulated hallucination level and human agent-based service recovery on perceived service quality. Study 1 included 236 participants (129 female and 107 male, mean age = 30.10, SD = 6.76), and Study 2 included 364 participants (172 female and 192 male, mean age = 33.98, SD = 9.81). Mediation effect analysis supported indirect associations between higher perceived AI hallucination and lower perceived chatbot service quality through cognitive dissonance and technical frustrati…

title: Wheel-Flat Identification from Axle-Box Acceleration: Cross-Track Generalisation and In-Service Validation
abstract: The objective of this study is to assess cross-track generalisation and direct controlled-to-service transfer of wheel-flat classifiers based on three revolution-wise axle-box acceleration indicators: Root Mean Square (RMS), Crest Factor (CF), and Wheel-Flat Index (WFI). Full-scale controlled measurements were analysed across distinct track sections, and cross-track transferability was assessed through nested leave-one-track-out validation of speed-dependent k-nearest neighbour classifiers. Final all-track models were applied without retraining or field-specific adaptation to 403 acquisitions collected during commercial freight operation with a wireless axle-box sensor. The controlled measurements showed that the dynamic manifestation of a fixed wheel-flat is not spatially invariant, while the combined RMS–CF–WFI representation retained useful discrimination across track sections. Cross-track balanced accuracy ranged from 0.841 to 0.980; all-track models achieved mean balanced accuracies of 0.967, 0.937, and 0.931 at 30, 45, and 60 km/h. In service, balanced accuracy was 0.878, specificity 0.984, and binary-decision coverage 0.978 against a manually reviewed signal-based reference. Applicability analysis of the exploratory high-speed extension indicated that speed extrapolation does not necessarily imply feature-space extrapolation, although false-positive acquisitions showed s…

title: ARMENIANS' PARTICIPATION IN THE AFGHAN WAR: SERVICE AND COMBAT EXPERIENCE
abstract: The Afghan War and its impact on Soviet society brought about decisive transformations. This article examines the quantitative picture of military servicemen from Soviet Armenia who participated in the Afghan War, aiming to demonstrate the transfer and application of combat experience of Armenian servicemen who went through the Afghan War in the Artsakh War and their contribution to the process of formation of the Armed Forces of the Republic of Armenia. Through a combination of archival files, veterans' organizations, and online information, it has been established that around 4,000 servicemen (400 officers) from Soviet Armenia participated in the war, 86 compatriots were killed, and around 300 were wounded. The author reveals that the combat experience of veterans and the formation of organizational and combat brotherhood networks contributed to the formation of military detachments and the organization of combat operations in the Artsakh War and the defense of the homeland. Particularly emphasized is the circumstance that veteran officers made a decisive contribution not only to the formation of volunteer detachments but also to the formation and establishment of the national army. It is concluded that the use of combat experience of the Afghan War in the Artsakh War was not coincidental but a natural result of the transformation of "combat capital," under conditions when de…

title: Embolization of the middle meningeal artery for non-acute subdural hematoma
Reservation Policy and Policy Dialogue in the Civil Service of Nepal
abstract: Reservation in Nepal's civil service remains a subject of ongoing debate regarding its effectiveness in promoting inclusion while maintaining administrative efficiency. This study examines the perceptions of senior bureaucrats, social activists, and political representatives towards the reservation policy. Using a qualitative research method, data were collected through 12 key informant interviews (KIIs) involving six senior bureaucrats, three social activists, and three political leaders representing Dalit, Indigenous Nationalities, Madheshi, and Khas- Arya communities. The participants included four women and eight men. The data has been analyzed using thematic analysis method. The findings indicate broad support for reservation as a mechanism for advancing social justice, improving the representation of historically marginalized groups, and strengthening inclusiveness in public administration. At the same time, respondents expressed concerns about policy implementation, particularly the absence of transparent eligibility criteria, inadequate monitoring mechanisms, and the potential capture of benefits by the relatively advantaged ("creamy layer") within target groups. The study concludes that the effectiveness and legitimacy of the reservation policy depend on strengthening its implementation through clear beneficiary identification, transparent indicators, and periodic poli…

title: Realizing Molecular Excited-State Regulation through Donor Molecular Engineering: The Intrinsic Relationship between TADF and HLCT Mechanisms
abstract: Abstract For developing high-performance pure organic light-emitting diode (OLED) emitters, thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) and hybrid local and charge-transfer (HLCT) mechanisms are two pivotal strategies by harvesting triplet excitons via reverse intersystem crossing. The intrinsic relationship between the two in molecular design is revealed in this study: the switching between TADF and HLCT mechanisms can be achieved by adjusting the strength of the donor groups. In this work, five D-π-A-π-D type blue and green OLED emitters with acridine/phenoxazine/phenothiazine groups as donors were designed and synthesized. Compared to reported HLCT molecules adopting carbazole/diphenylamine groups as donors, the excited states of the molecules in this work were successfully regulated to TADF. The solution-processed blue/green OLED device based on FIP-DPAC/FIP-PXZ achieved the maximum external quantum efficiency (EQEmax) of 10.01%/17.45%. A strategy for regulating HLCT and TADF mechanisms of OLED emitters through donor molecular engineering was elucidated in this study.

title: Coupling Ligand Tuning With Polymer‐Induced Aperture Regulation for Molecular Sieving in Flexible MOFs
abstract: ABSTRACT Framework flexibility fundamentally limits molecular sieving in many metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) by enlarging their effective pore apertures beyond crystallographic constraints. This challenge is pronounced in zeolitic imidazolate framework‐8 (ZIF‐8), where dynamic aperture expansion prevents CO 2 /N 2 size‐sieving despite an ideally positioned nominal aperture size. Here, we show that polymer infiltration enables in situ regulation of dynamic apertures, converting ZIF‐8 from a nonselective adsorbent into a CO 2 /N 2 molecular sieve. During mixed‐matrix membrane (MMM) formation, poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA) partially infiltrates ZIF cavities and suppresses framework dynamics, as supported by solid‐state NMR ( 1 H‐ 13 C HetCor) and spin–lattice relaxation. Consequently, the CO 2 /N 2 diffusion selectivity of ZIF‐8‐NH 2 with 6 mol% 2‐aminobenzimidazole increased from 0.58 (polymer‐free) to 26.6 within the polymer environment, enabling CO 2 /N 2 size sieving. Membranes with 20 wt% filler achieved a CO 2 permeability of 261.7 Barrer and a CO 2 /N 2 selectivity of 73.9. This strategy is generalizable to other flexible ZIFs, such as ZIF‐7 and ZIF‐67, establishing polymer infiltration as a simple and versatile route for controlling dynamic MOF apertures for effective gas separation.

title: Optical Calibration of a Frequency-Domain-Multiplexed X-Ray TES Microcalorimeter Array via Photon-Number-Resolved Statistics
abstract: Transition-edge sensor (TES) microcalorimeters for future X-ray space observatories require accurate low-energy calibration, a regime where conventional X-ray sources are limited by intrinsic linewidth, count rate, or experimental complexity. In this work, we investigate fiber-coupled optical photons as a compact calibration tool for an Athena-like TES array. Optical pulses at 405 nm were generated with an acousto-optic modulator and delivered through an optical fiber onto a selected TES pixel inside a dilution refrigerator, via a dedicated cryogenic alignment interface. Externally triggered pulses were processed with an optimal-filter pipeline, including baseline subtraction, drift correction, and multi-Gaussian reconstruction of the pulse-height spectrum. The reconstructed spectra show resolved photon-number peaks consistent with the Poissonian statistics expected from an attenuated coherent source, reaching equivalent energies above 400 eV with a mean photon number exceeding 100 per pulse. The detector response was further tested for linearity by comparing the measured photon-number distributions against those predicted from the independently calibrated number of photons sent to the detector and a single, globally estimated detection efficiency, confirming Poissonian, linear behaviour across nearly two orders of magnitude in photon number. These results demonstrate that fibe…

title: Examining commissioners for oaths, governance in advance, and upper-middle economics: Digital revolution, regulatory supervision, and professional standards
abstract: Commissioners for oaths perform an important verification function within judicial and administrative systems, yet this role has attracted far less institutional governance scholarship than the evidentiary validity of affidavits and statutory declarations (Commissioner for Oaths Rules, 2018). Drawing on legal instruments, governance incidents, and scholarship from 2018 to 2026, this conceptual article uses a comparative case study of Malaysia, Singapore, and the United Kingdom (UK) to examine how regulatory governance, professional standards, and technological adaptation shape institutional effectiveness, individually and in combination. Drawing on institutional theory, agency theory, and professional regulation theory, commissioners are reframed as institutional governance actors rather than procedural certifiers, and the study identifies a dual-monitoring problem in which verifiers must themselves be subject to credible oversight. The framework develops four propositions: three address the individual contribution of each governance dimension, and the fourth proposes institutional complementarity, supported by governance alignment, as the main integrative mechanism. Recent Malaysian governance incidents show that formal appointment alone does not ensure process integrity. The study provides a basis for future empirical work and institutional reform, particularly given Malaysia…

title: Dietary Antioxidant Capacity and Serum Antioxidant Status in Men with Coronary Artery Disease: An Exploratory Case–Control Study
abstract: Background: Oxidative stress, dietary antioxidant intake, and body fat distribution have been implicated in the development and progression of coronary artery disease (CAD). However, studies simultaneously evaluating serum oxidative status, dietary total antioxidant capacity (DTAC), nutritional status, and angiographically determined CAD severity remain scarce. Therefore, this study aimed to comprehensively investigate these parameters and their associations in men with angiographically confirmed CAD. Methods: This hospital-based case–control study included 80 men aged 25–65 years, comprising 40 patients with angiographically confirmed CAD and 40 angiographically normal controls. Dietary intake was recorded using three-day dietary records, and an antioxidant food frequency questionnaire (FFQ) was also administered. Dietary total antioxidant capacity (DTAC) was calculated separately from the three-day dietary records and the FFQ using ferric reducing antioxidant power (FRAP) values. Anthropometric and body composition measurements, routine biochemical parameters, serum total antioxidant status (TAS), and total oxidant status (TOS) were assessed. CAD severity was quantified using the Gensini score. Multivariable binary logistic regression was performed to examine factors associated with CAD status. Results: Compared with controls, participants with CAD had significantly higher fa…

title: Fractional-Order Model-Based State-of-Charge and State-of-Power Estimation with Available-Capacity Feedback for Lithium-ion Batteries
abstract: Abstract Accurate state-of-charge (SOC) and state-of-power (SOP) estimation requires consistent treatment of voltage dynamics and available-capacity uncertainty. This study couples a fractional-order equivalent circuit model, a fast multi-innovation unscented Kalman filter SOC observer, and a slow capacity estimator. Self-adaptive learning particle swarm optimization (SLPSO) identifies the model parameters. Capacity feedback links SOC correction to voltage prediction and multi-constraint SOP calculation, with constant-power discharge verification. Compared with a second-order resistor-capacitor model, the fractional-order model reduces voltage root-mean-square error (RMSE) and mean absolute error by 3.45% and 5.82%, respectively. SLPSO reduces the mean final voltage RMSE from 2.215 to 1.561 mV. Across two dynamic profiles and initial SOC values of 0.90 to 1.05, the proposed method yields SOC RMSE values of 0.844% to 0.966%. The fixed-capacity baseline yields 4.9% to 9.8% under initial-SOC mismatch. The maximum capacity-related state-of-health indicator deviation remains below 0.279 percentage points. The maximum discharge-power error is 2.20% for 10 s and below 5% for all 30 s cases. It reaches 8.34% at 30% SOC for 60 s, indicating the need for caution under low-SOC, long-duration operation. These results are limited to fresh-cell tests at 25 °C.

title: Breaking the Theoretical Capacity Limit of Fullerene Anode in Alkali‐Ion Batteries Through Two‐Dimensional Covalent Network Engineering
abstract: ABSTRACT Carbon‐based anode materials offer compelling advantages for rechargeable ion batteries, and particularly fullerene C 60 has a higher theoretical capacity of 446 mAh g −1 than the traditional graphite anode in lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs). However, its zero‐dimensional cage structure tends to spontaneously aggregate, and its alkali‐metal intercalated intermediate (fulleride) facilely dissolves in organic electrolytes, severely limiting its practical anode capacity and deteriorating recyclability. Herein, for the first time, we apply metal‐free two‐dimensional C 60 covalent network (2D‐C 60 ) with distinct bonding patterns, including tetragonal phase (TP‐2D‐C 60 ) and hexagonal phase (HP‐2D‐C 60 ) nanosheets, as novel anode materials for LIBs, achieving high anode capacity, breaking the theoretical limit of C 60 molecule. TP‐2D‐C 60 delivers a specific capacity of 522.0 mAh g −1 at 0.1 A g −1 , outperforming HP‐2D‐C 60 (408.6 mAh g −1 ) and pristine C 60 (3.4 mAh g −1 ). This phenomenon is rationalized by DFT calculations, revealing that TP‐2D‐C 60 exhibits a higher density of Li‐ion binding sites and a lower Li‐ion migration barrier than HP‐2D‐C 60 . To assess its universality across ion‐battery chemistries, we further demonstrate the application of TP‐2D‐C 60 as an anode for sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs), achieving a high discharge capacity of 309.9 mAh g −1 at 0.1 A g …

title: Electric Vehicle Hosting Capacity in Distribution Systems: A Critical Review of Distributed Generation Foundations, Unified Assessment, and Emerging Research Directions
abstract: Electric vehicle hosting capacity (EV-HC) is increasingly important for distribution-system planning, yet existing reviews provide limited guidance on how mature distributed-generation hosting-capacity (DG-HC) concepts should be transferred to mobility-dependent and potentially bidirectional EV operation. This review uses a transfer–adaptation–reformulation taxonomy to examine how DG-HC foundations can be transferred to EV-HC. It distinguishes connected charger capacity from coincident charging demand, feasible from safe multi-resource regions, and firm from flexibility-dependent HC. Assessment approaches are compared across six non-exclusive dimensions: uncertainty treatment, temporal representation, solution mechanism, model fidelity, control treatment, and computational acceleration. The evidence shows that no single constraint universally governs EV-HC; voltage, thermal loading, unbalance, or power quality may become binding depending on feeder characteristics and charging conditions. Operational measures can release network headroom, but HC enhancement is established only after recalculating the feasible boundary under consistent assumptions. Direct evidence for risk-calibrated and AI-assisted EV-HC remains limited, motivating consequence-aware risk treatment, standardized reporting, and real-network validation.

title: Percolation-Based Optimization of Zn–MnO₂ Battery Cathodes Balancing Capacity Density and Electrical Conductivity
abstract: Abstract This study introduces a novel, systematic approach to maximize electrode-side capacity density in ZMBs without significantly reducing power density. A percolation-based model was developed to evaluate how usable capacity and electrical conductivity vary with the volume fractions of MnO₂, carbon black (CB), and porosity, overcoming the system's dual non-linear scaling behaviour. The model identifies an optimal composition range for any given porosity and was extensively parameterized and validated through a comprehensive set of targeted electrochemical and structural measurements. Applying this optimal composition to a 75 % porosity cathode increased capacity by 25 mAh cm⁻² (290 mAh g⁻¹) compared to conventional cathodes without preloaded active material, while maintaining a high electrical conductivity of 150 S m⁻¹. This work establishes a novel, general framework for designing high-energy-density composite cathodes.

Nonlinear evolution and influencing mechanism of rutting in asphalt pavement under coupled high-temperature and heavy-load conditions
abstract: To investigate the nonlinear evolution and mechanism of rutting in asphalt pavement incorporating steel slag under coupled high-temperature and heavy-load conditions, a three-dimensional finite element model was established in ABAQUS based on a typical semi-rigid base asphalt pavement structure. Steel slag was used to replace 30% of the natural coarse aggregate by mass. The Bailey–Norton creep model was adopted to characterize the high-temperature mechanical behavior of the asphalt mixtures, and the model was validated using laboratory rutting tests. On this basis, coupled working conditions involving multiple temperatures and load levels were established. The rut depth at 60 min was used as the primary evaluation index, and a coupling influence coefficient was introduced to quantitatively characterize the interaction between temperature and contact pressure. The results show that rut depth increased nonlinearly with increasing temperature and contact pressure. The coupling influence coefficient remained close to unity under a contact pressure of 1.0 MPa, whereas it increased to 1.09 and 1.15 at 65 °C and 70 °C, respectively, under 1.2 MPa, indicating an evident synergistic amplification under severe high-temperature and heavy-load conditions. title: Mechanism Research Progress of Acupuncture Regulating Vagus Nerve-Cholinergic Anti-inflammatory Pathway in the Prevention and Treatment of Endometriosis-Related Pain
abstract: Endometriosis (EM)-related pain involves multiple links including local inflammatory microenvironment, neurogenic inflammation, peripheral and central sensitization, and autonomic nervous imbalance. Current hormone therapy and surgical treatment cannot achieve sufficient pain relief and are prone to recurrence. This paper reviews the role of the vagus nerve-mediated cholinergic anti-inflammatory pathway (CAIP) in EM pain and the mechanistic evidence that acupuncture regulates this pathway. It proposes that CAIP impairment in EM may exist at two levels simultaneously: reduced central vagal efferent tone and downregulated expression of local α7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (α7nAChR) in peripheral lesions. Patients with EM have decreased vagal tone which correlates with pain severity. Vagus nerve stimulation can slow lesion progression and improve hyperalgesia in animal models, and α7nAChR agonists can inhibit lesion formation and fibrosis. Electroacupuncture activates the vagus-adrenal axis or spleen-dependent CAIP via acupoints such as Zusanli to exert anti-inflammatory effects, with selectivity for acupoints and stimulation parameters. It is thus inferred that simply enhancing upstream vagal input may be inadequate. Combined strategies that raise vagal efferent tone while improving local receptor reactivity in lesions deserve exploration. Future work shall optimize acupunct…

title: Effect of electrode structure on pumping performance of electrohydrodynamic pumps based on the dissociation-injection mechanism
abstract: Abstract Electrohydrodynamic (EHD) pumps are promising for microfluidic actuation because of the absence of mechanical moving parts and their ease of integration. In this study, a multiphysics numerical model of an EHD pump considering the coupled dissociation–injection mechanism is developed based on the finite volume method. The effects of electrode polarity connection, injection intensity C, conduction number C0, electric Rayleigh number T, and electrode configuration on pumping performance are systematically investigated. For the mirror-symmetric arrangement of asymmetric electrode pairs, the steady-state outlet velocity is 36.7% higher when the narrow electrode is connected to the positive potential than when the wide electrode is connected to the positive potential. This enhancement arises from the synergistic effect between injected-charge migration and the net Coulomb force generated by charge dissociation. With the other parameters fixed, increasing C from 0.1 to 10 increases the steady-state velocity by 48%, indicating the dominant contribution of charge injection under strong-injection conditions. The conduction number exhibits a non-monotonic effect on pumping performance: a moderate increase enhances the flow, whereas an excessively large C0 weakens the effective driving force. Among the electrode configurations examined, the mirror-symmetric arrangement of asymmet…

title: ACTA: A Verifiable Accountable Decryption Mechanism for Secure and Auditable Blockchain-Based Data Sharing
abstract: The implementation of the secure credential management systems requires the exchange and sharing of sensitive records along with the strict access control, confidentiality, and accountability requirements. However, the sharing of the credentials is associated with security and privacy concerns. While there are many blockchain solutions that enable immutable audit trails and decentralized trust, the existing approaches provide limited support for verifiable accountability and controlled decryption mechanisms that are needed for the secure handling of sensitive data. This paper proposes a novel framework called Accountable Confidential Trusted Access (ACTA) that offers verifiable accountable decryption and combines the use of blockchain and trusted execution environments (TEEs). In addition, ACTA incorporates Interplanetary File System (IPFS) for off-chain encrypted record storage and maintains its integrity validation with on-chain content identity identifier (CID) and cryptographic hash values. ACTA is based on the three-phase secure process, which includes the linkage of the access authorization, encrypted data, and enclave-execution of the decryption while storing the immutable audit records on the blockchain. Following a successful decryption operation, ACTA records verifiable evidence that an authenticated requester obtained the encrypted record bound to their authorization…

title: Mechanism and Progress of Stimulus-Responsive Nanoparticles in Targeted Cancer Therapy
abstract: Cancer, a disease characterized by uncontrolled cell proliferation, poses significant challenges to traditional treatments. Surgery, chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and immunotherapy, while commonly used, are limited by issues such as difficulty in eliminating micro-metastasis, poor specificity with severe side effects, radiation damage to healthy tissues, and low patient response rates. Stimulus-responsive nanoparticles have emerged as a promising precision drug delivery strategy to address these limitations. They achieve targeted drug accumulation and controlled release by leveraging unique features of the tumor microenvironment (e.g., acidic pH, overexpressed enzymes like MMPs, and elevated ROS levels) and exogenous stimuli (e.g., light). Key types include pH-responsive nanoparticles, which rely on pH differences between tumor and normal tissues; enzyme-responsive nanoparticles, activated by specific overexpressed enzymes in tumors; and ROS-responsive nanoparticles, triggered by high ROS concentrations in the tumor microenvironment, each with distinct mechanisms and applications. However, their clinical translation faces challenges such as tumor microenvironment heterogeneity, biocompatibility concerns, insufficient drug release control, and limited tumor penetration. Future prospects lie in multi-stimulus synergistic therapy, intelligent and personalized design, combination wit…

title: Missing-Modality Robustness in Clinical Multimodal Prediction: A Mechanism-Level Review
abstract: Multimodal medical artificial intelligence (AI) aggregates complementary evidence from imaging, omics, pathology, and clinical records, yet hospital deployment routinely confronts structurally incomplete inputs. This review synthesizes 77 algorithmic studies on missing-modality robustness in clinical prediction, selected through a Scopus search (16 May 2026) and a Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) study-selection pathway, and organizes them in a three-family taxonomy: imputation and generative reconstruction (Family A), representation learning and robust fusion (Family B), and knowledge transfer and distillation (Family C). Cross-tabulating families against segmentation (Seg), diagnosis (Dx), and survival prognosis (Surv) endpoints yields 107 family–task assignments, within which Family B is most frequently represented (51 assignments), while reconstruction and relational transfer provide complementary approaches where spatial fidelity matters. Missingness is characterized along data dimensionality, temporal stage, and selection mechanism, and each study is mapped onto this joint space. At least 23 of the 77 studies (29.9%) test robustness by artificially withholding clinical inputs at test time, and 6 (7.8%) evaluate three or more missingness levels. The formation of silicon-carbon chain molecules in IRC+10216
abstract: Abstract Linear silicon-carbon chain molecules, SiCn (n = 3–6), have been detected in the circumstellar envelope of the carbon-rich AGB star IRC+10216. Here, we discuss the mechanisms likely to be at work in the synthesis of chains up to SiC8 and present for the first time a detailed comparison between observations and model calculations. Using a combination of measured and postulated rate coefficients, we show that the column densities of the silicon carbide molecules observed in IRC+10216 can be reproduced to with a factor of four. Furthermore, our model calculations suggest that the column densities of SiC7 and SiC8 are a factor of 2–4 less than that of SiC6. We discuss the influence of neutral-neutral reactions involving parent SiC2 on chain growth and show that their neglect leads to a reduction in column densities of carbides up to a maximum of about six for SiC6 and SiC7. Our results suggest that the detection of SiC7 and SiC8 in IRC+10216 will be challenging but that astronomical searches should be undertaken.

Modelling plant stem cells: evolution, development and regeneration
abstract: ABSTRACT In June 2025, The Company of Biologists Workshop ‘Modelling Plant Stem Cells: Evolution, Development and Regeneration’ brought together a diverse group of plant researchers to discuss open questions in plant developmental biology. Expertise ranged from computational modelling, cell biology and developmental genetics to paleontology. All participants shared an interest in understanding the establishment, maintenance and regeneration of plant stem cell niches, how these dictate plant growth and how stem cell niches arose through evolution. This led to fruitful discussions identifying necessary steps to further integrate experimental and computational approaches to speed up the transfer of knowledge from current model species to emerging model species. The discussion covered the evolutionary and practical aspects in the selection of plant model systems, the importance of both generalities and specificities of model systems and methodologies, and the use of computational models as tools to infer developmental mechanisms in emerging research species. The diversity in career stages of participants, the plant species used, and experimental versus computational approaches, created an environment for establishing cross-system and cross-disciplinary collaborations. Here, we present distinct ways to connect experimental and computational approaches, and discuss what is needed to …

Genome-wide comparative analysis of homeobox transcription factors in rice and expression profiles of selected genes reveal potential tissue and developmental stage specificity as well as abiotic stress responsiveness
abstract: Introduction Homeobox (HB) transcription factors are essential for plant development and can participate in regulating plant responses to diverse biotic and abiotic stresses. Methods In this study, we performed an in-silico analysis of the different HB gene and protein subfamilies in rice, including Oryza sativa subsp. indica and O. sativa subsp. japonica . Results A total of 112 and 156 sequences annotated as HB transcription factors were retrieved from PlantTFDB for O. sativa subsp. indica and subsp. japonica , respectively, which showed 94% sequence identity. The homeobox–plant homeodomain finger (HB-PHD) subfamily showed 100% identity, whereas the three-amino-acid-loop-extension (TALE), WUSCHEL-related homeobox (WOX), and zinc-finger-homeodomain (ZF-HD) subfamilies displayed values equal to or higher than 95%; in contrast, HB-OTHERS showed the lowest identity (82%). Phylogenetic analysis grouped the proteins into six major subfamilies: HB-PHD, HD-ZIP, TALE, WOX, ZF-HD, and HB-OTHERS. In the promoter regions of HB genes of O. sativa subsp. japonica , 688 cis -regulatory motifs were retrieved as potentially associated with hormonal and stress responses such as drought, salinity, and cold; among the most frequent were ABRE, CGTCA-motif, TGACG-motif, and ARE. In addition, de novo motif analysis retrieved regulatory patterns specific to HB genes with significant similarity to tr…

title: Tropical peatland microbiomes as a One Health nexus: linking soil, plant, and climate health across land-use transitions
abstract: The One Health framework recognizes the intrinsic connections among environmental, plant, animal and human health. While soils and soil microbes have received substantial attention in the recent years, tropical peatlands still remain largely overlooked despite representing globally important reservoirs of carbon, biodiversity, freshwater. Microorganisms are central regulators of peat accumulation, nutrient cycling, greenhouse gas exchange and ecosystem resilience, yet their role as mediators of One Health outcomes has received limited attention. Emerging evidence from tropical peatlands demonstrates that land-use change, drainage, fire and agricultural conversion substantially alter microbial community composition and function, with cascading effects on ecosystem processes. In this Perspective, peatland microbiomes are proposed as critical but neglected One Health nexus linking soil health, vegetation dynamics, wildlife habitat quality, climate regulation and human wellbeing. Considering, oil palm plantations that produce the most consumed vegetable oil in the world, cover substantial portion of tropical peatlands, tropical peat also plays a crucial role in food security and safety. The perspective argues that microbial communities should move from being considered ecological indicators to becoming policy-relevant components of peatland governance. Furthermore, incorporation of…

title: Don’t say it’s green! How green framing can depress support for renewable energy
abstract: Abstract The green transition implies a shift towards renewable energies. However, their deployment has faced some backlash. This article assesses whether (a) the type of renewables and (b) framing can affect support for deployment. Through a survey experiment, three types of renewables (hydropower, onshore wind, offshore wind) and three types of frames (energy sovereignty, economic competitiveness, green transition) are evaluated, in general and for two typically skeptical groups (the least climate-worried and the less-educated ruralites). Using the case of Norway, we find strong effects for the type of renewables but little evidence for general framing effects. There are two exceptions: green framing has a negative effect on support for renewables where citizens have more fluid preferences (offshore wind) and depresses support among the least climate-worried and the less-educated ruralites. For these citizens, remaining silent about the climate benefits of renewable energy will actually boost support for its deployment.

title: A PQC-Based Cyber Resilient and Energy Efficient Framework for Secure Blockchain-Enabled Decentralized Transactions in the BFSI Sector
abstract: Elliptic curve cryptography (ECC) serves as the security foundation for decentralized ledger systems that enables transaction authorization and user account control through compact signatures. However, this architectural reliance poses an existential threat due to Shor’s algorithm, which allows a cryptographically relevant quantum computer (CRQC) to reconstruct private keys from publicly recorded transactions. Simply replacing ECDSA with post-quantum signature schemes introduces severe system bottlenecks, as schemes like ML-DSA require signature payloads up to 70 times larger than ECDSA. This leads to transaction bloats, increased propagation delays, high archival storage costs, and heavy CPU/energy consumption on resource-constrained mobile nodes. This paper presents the Quantum Resistant Digital Wallet (QRDW), a full-stack post-quantum blockchain wallet, and ledger architecture. QRDW features the Deterministic Adaptive Post-Quantum Policy Engine (DAPPE), which dynamically selects signing profiles (ML-DSA-44, ML-DSA-65, or ML-DSA-87) based on real-time transaction amounts and a consensus-derived sliding window. DAPPE utilizes a consensus-verified sliding window threshold derived from the ledger’s public state, ensuring that validators independently recompute the required profile deterministically. This research contributes a demonstrable end-to-end PQC wallet architecture that…

title: Direct Imaging of Energy Dissipation in Surface Acoustic Waves
abstract: Abstract Unraveling the spatial distribution and energy dissipation of high-frequency surface acoustic waves (SAWs) is essential for advancing nanoacoustic architectures and probing low-dimensional wave–matter interactions. However, visualizing these dynamics at the subwavelength scale remains challenging due to the optical diffraction limit and severe topographic artifacts, such as surface defects and roughness, in scanning probe measurements. Here, we establish scanning thermal microscopy (SThM) as a robust metrological paradigm to map nanoscale energy dissipation and resolve complex acoustic wavefields through their localized thermal signatures. Leveraging this platform, we demonstrate how microgeometries sculpt the acoustic energy landscape and enable quantitative extraction of wave scattering parameters. Furthermore, by interrogating the h-BN/LiNbO3 van der Waals (vdW) interface, we capture localized temperature signatures of interfacial energy exchange. We observe anomalous nonlinear thermal scaling at the 2D heterointerface, consistent with the intrinsic nonlinear damping of the 2D heterostructure. This work highlights the capability of SThM to probe acoustic energy dissipation, establishing a diagnostic framework for subwavelength acoustic wavefields and heterogeneously integrated devices.

title: Governing Generative AI in Peer Review: An Author-Authorised, Version-Synchronised Preprint Pathway
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) in peer review raises questions of permission, human judgment, and fair participation. This normative and conceptual analysis proposes an author-authorised, journal-authorised, version-synchronised public-preprint pathway for bounded external-AI assistance. It aims to broaden opportunities for defensible criticism while maintaining rigorous evaluation and limiting governance to necessary safeguards. Eight cumulative conditions connect voluntary, unanimous author opt-in, journal permission, a rights-cleared public package, round-specific synchronisation, service eligibility, disclosure, human accountability and redress, and exclusion of non-public editorial information. Synchronisation supplies complete, same-version context for checking consequential criticisms without requiring full-manuscript input for every task. An optional open pre-review pilot permits contributions before formal reviewer appointment while preserving invited review. Comparisons separate public access, participation, and AI provision across confidentiality, retention and training, model change, auditability, burden, equity, and complementary questioning. Approved external assistance may support contributors without journal-provided internal-AI accounts; its value depends on voluntary uptake, usable support, contribution quality, and total burdens relative to feasible …
