title: Dinuclear Cu(II) metal complexes as room-temperature energy storage quantum devices: review and outlooks
abstract: Abstract {The urgent demand for sustainable energy storage devices necessitates the development of novel conceptual and technological paradigms that extend beyond the constraints imposed by classical thermodynamic limits. in order to present the material innovations required to enable viable room-temperature quantum technologies, this Review outlines the potential of dinuclear Cu(II) complexes as promising model platforms for the development of room-temperature quantum batteries.} We address how the quantum properties of these dinuclear materials can be harnessed to store and extract energy, and how they can be handled and engineered by the management of the intra-molecular magnetic coupling and external thermodynamic conditions.{Through macroscopic magnetometric mappings, we present how the maximum extractable work (ergotropy) can be directly quantified without invasive quantum tomography. Furthermore, we review the operational simulation of these materials using quantum computing approaches using the Variational Quantum Thermalizer (VQT) algorithm on Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) devices. Finally, we provide an outlook on future research directions, highlighting the critical material engineering and quantum error mitigation strategies required to transition these coordination compounds from theoretical models to functional macroscopic solid-state quantum energy…

title: A New Class of Decoupled and Energy-Stable Numerical Schemes for the Binary Phase-Field Crystal Model
Evolution of the High-energy Excess in Swift J1727.8-1613 during Its 2023 Flare State
abstract: Abstract We investigate the evolution of the high-energy excess in Swift J1727.8-1613 during its 2023 flare state using joint Insight-HXMT and INTEGRAL/ISGRI observations covering 2–500 keV. Fits to the broadband spectra with a model including thermal Comptonization and disk reflection leave systematic positive residuals above ∼150 keV. Adding a power-law component improves the fits and yields photon indices of Γ PL = 2.08–2.61, demonstrating that the high-energy excess beyond the thermal Comptonization continuum is present throughout the flare state. We also show that all spectra can be well described by the hybrid Comptonization model eqpair without requiring any additional high-energy component. The fitting results indicate that the energy supply to the electrons transitions from predominantly thermal heating to nonthermal acceleration, and that the electron injection spectrum steepens abruptly near the onset of the flare state. During this evolution, the radio spectral index changes from approximately zero to negative values, accompanied by the ejection of three transient jet knots. Based on this temporal association, we discuss a possible connection between the increase in nonthermal power indicated by our spectral analysis and the ejection of the transient jet.

title: Enhanced dual-converter resonance control coordinated with gate- controlled series capacitor for sub-synchronous resonance mitigation in series-compensated DFIG-based wind energy systems
abstract: Fixed series capacitors are effective in increasing transmission line capacity in grid-connected Doubly Fed Induction Generator (DFIG)-based wind farms. Sub-Synchronous Resonance (SSR) phenomena occur when the series capacitors are in operation. The Gate-Controlled Series Capacitor (GCSC) model is used to eliminate the SSR effect. However, while the GCSC can control low series capacitance conditions, it is insufficient in high series capacitance conditions. To address this problem, this study aims to enhance a resonance control model for the Rotor-Side Converter (RSC) and Grid-Side Converter (GSC) circuits to reduce the SSR effect and improve the system's efficiency under different operating conditions in the DFIG. By enhancing the resonance control models for the GCSC and converter circuits, comparisons are made on some parameters in the DFIG at different wind speeds and different fixed series compensation ratios. In these comparisons, evaluations were made using the traditional model, the GCSC model, and the enhanced resonance control model in multiple applications in the RSC and RSC-GSC circuits. In addition, eigenvalue analyses were examined in detail in the comparisons. The results showed that the resonance control models enhanced for the GCSC and RSC-GSC circuits stabilized the system in a short time, and the resulting oscillations were quickly damped.

title: Self-powered neural intervention via piezoelectric nanogenerators
abstract: Piezoelectric nanogenerators (PENGs) are electromechanical energy-conversion devices constructed from piezoelectric materials. They convert physiological motion, local tissue deformation, or externally applied mechanical stimuli into localized electrical signals and have attracted considerable interest in self-powered neural interventions. Despite the rapid expansion of research in this field, the systematic understanding needed to guide translational optimization remains limited. This review delineates the current research landscape by organizing the discussion around mechanical inputs, piezoelectric transduction, neural responses, and functional restoration, thereby linking fundamental principles with representative application studies. This review discusses neural-interface-compatible materials, device architectures, and powering strategies for PENGs; the underlying neurobiological mechanisms; and recent advances in their applications across the peripheral, central, and autonomic nervous systems, neurodegenerative diseases, and neural interfaces. It further examines key barriers related to the precision of deep-tissue targeting, the long-term safety of implanted devices, and the lack of standardized frameworks for clinical translation. To this end, PENGs are systematically compared with other self-powered and wirelessly powered transduction technologies, and a standardized r…

title: Modeling and Simulation of Reactive Power Compensation Using a Synchronous Motor with Excitation Control in MATLAB/Simulink
abstract: This study investigates reactive power compensation using a synchronous motor in a three-phase electrical power system without conventional capacitor banks through MATLAB/Simulink-based modeling and simulation. The proposed system consists of inductive loads and a 15 kVA synchronous motor operating as a dynamic reactive power compensator via excitation current control. Different operating conditions were analyzed by varying the excitation voltage and current parameters. The simulation results demonstrated that the proposed compensation method significantly reduced reactive power demand and improved the overall system power factor to nearly unity (PF ≈ 1.00). In addition, the apparent power demand decreased from 24 kVA to 21.63 kVA under optimized operating conditions, resulting in lower transmission line current, reduced power losses, improved voltage stability, and enhanced overall system efficiency. The findings confirm that synchronous motor-based reactive power compensation provides a flexible, reliable, and dynamically controllable alternative to conventional capacitor bank systems under varying load conditions.
venue: Turkish Journal of Electrical Power and Energy Systems

title: Optimal Allocation of Battery Energy Storage Systems in Solar Integrated Distribution Networks Using Particle Swarm Optimization Technique
abstract: This study presents an efficient methodology for the optimal sizing and placement of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) in distribution networks with pre-installed solar PV Distributed Generators (DGs). High solar photovoltaic (PV) penetration in distribution networks often leads to challenges such as voltage rise, reverse power flow, and increased daytime losses, thereby motivating the integration of BESS to effectively mitigate these issues. However, some of these issues can be exacerbated when the capacity and placement of BESS are not correctly optimized. The proposed approach employs Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) to determine optimal BESS locations and capacities, aiming at minimizing energy losses while adhering to technical constraints such as feeder voltage and current limits, power balance, and BESS state of charge (SOC) boundaries. The methodology is validated through two case studies: a modified IEEE 33-bus network with integrated solar PV DGs and a practical feeder located in Kurunegala, Sri Lanka. The convergence statistics of this study confirm the effectiveness of the developed PSO algorithm in identifying optimal results, justifying its computational efficiency and robustness. Results of two case studies demonstrate that the optimal BESS placement significantly reduces daily energy losses while improving the voltage profile of the network. Therefore, the …

title: Suppressing Photooxidation and Iodine Migration in HTL‐Free Carbon‐Based Perovskite Solar Cells via a Tailor‐Made Redox Guard
abstract: ABSTRACT Hole transport layer‐free carbon‐based perovskite solar cells (HTL‐free C‐PSCs) suffer rapid performance decay under operational stressors, driven by iodine migration and photogenerated superoxide radicals (O 2 •− ). To break this photo‐oxidation‐iodine migration vicious cycle, we design a multifunctional molecular stabilizer, tetrakis(4‐carboxyphenyl)tetrathiafulvalene (4B‐TTF). This tailor‐made “molecular guard” works via two synergistic mechanisms: its reversible TTF core acts as a charge‐transfer mediator, reducing I 2 to I − and scavenging O 2 •− , while four peripheral benzoic acid groups anchor to undercoordinated Pb 2+ sites, passivating grain‐boundary defects. Incorporating 4B‐TTF into MAPbI 3 ‐based devices yields a champion power‐conversion efficiency (PCE) of 19.96%, vs. 17.58% for the control, by suppressing non‐radiative recombination. Unencapsulated devices retain 96.4% of their initial efficiency after 1200 h under ambient storage and 93.5% after 120 h under harsh UV‐oxygen exposure; encapsulated devices retain 90.32% after 700 h of continuous maximum power point (MPP) tracking under 1‐sun illumination at 55°C in nitrogen. The strategy is further validated in Cs 0.17 FA 0.83 PbI 3 systems, delivering a state‐of‐the‐art PCE of 20.70%. This work provides a unified molecular‐level strategy to concurrently address ionic, radical, and defect‐related degradat…

title: The Effect of Storage Conditions on the Properties of Sourdough Starters, Mature Sourdoughs and Quality of the Bread
abstract: Sourdough production is an important technological process in bakeries. An increasing number of artisan bakeries choose to store their sourdough starters under refrigerated conditions. This study aimed to evaluate changes in the properties of bakery sourdoughs produced from rye sourdough starters stored at 4 °C for 48, 96, and 144 h, and to determine the effect of sourdough starter storage on the quality of the resulting bread. Refrigerated storage of sourdough starter for 48, 96 and 144 h affected the pH and acidity of the sourdough starters but did not influence these parameters in the mature sourdoughs. The concentrations of fermentation products, such as acetic acid, ethanol, glycerol, and lactic acid, changed during storage, and it was found that ethanol increased with longer storage time in sourdough starters. Refrigerated storage did not affect key bread quality characteristics, including crumb moisture, bread yield, baking loss, or loaf volume. Sensory evaluation showed that bread made from a starter stored for 144 h was the least acceptable in terms of taste. Overall, these findings establish a clear operational guideline, demonstrating that rye sourdough starters can be safely stored under refrigerated conditions for up to 96 h without compromising bread quality.

title: Direct Reuse of Uncured CFRP Prepreg Scraps for Structural Applications: Experimental Qualification and Numerical Validation of an Automotive Battery Case
abstract: ABSTRACT The high demand for fiber‐reinforced composite materials generates large quantities of uncured prepreg waste, still in pristine condition, usually landfilled or incinerated. Among the various established recycling routes, direct reuse of these scraps represents an attractive strategy to reduce both raw material consumption and manufacturing waste, while preserving the original constituents' properties, and avoiding energy‐intensive recovery processes or the use of hazardous chemicals, thus moving an energy demanding industry toward sustainability. This work aims to demonstrate that when properly processed, prepreg scraps can be converted into a recycled material with high potential also for structural applications. A full‐scale Electric Vehicle (EV) battery pack has been manufactured from uncured prepreg scraps and tested according to UN 38.3 vibration test T.3 with frequency sweep cycles to assess vibration response, mechanical robustness, and post‐test structural integrity. The battery enclosure successfully completed the test with no structural failure, debonding, or functional degradation. A limited reduction of approximately 3% in the first resonance frequency was observed throughout the test campaign, suggesting only minor stiffness degradation while preserving the structural integrity of the component. A numerical model of the battery pack was also developed and…

title: Performance evaluation of sodium-ion batteries for microgrid and off-grid energy storage applications
abstract: Introduction Sodium-ion batteries are increasingly considered for stationary energy storage; however, their application-level performance depends on how experimentally measured electrochemical behavior translates into realistic grid-connected and standalone operating conditions. Methods This study evaluated 24 5.0-Ah sodium-ion pouch cells through baseline electrochemical characterization, identification of a second-order Thevenin electrochemical-thermal model, annual system simulation, and application-specific aging tests. Discharge behavior was characterized at rates of 0.20–2.00 C and temperatures of 10–40 °C. Pulse and impedance measurements were used to parameterize the model across 10%–90% state of charge. The calibrated model was scaled to a 504-kWh grid-connected microgrid and a 120.96-kWh standalone off-grid system, both simulated over 365 days at 15-min resolution. Results Increasing discharge rate reduced usable capacity and energy efficiency, whereas Coulombic efficiency remained above approximately 99%. The model reproduced measured voltage responses with millivolt-scale prediction errors and captured state-of-charge- and temperature-dependent resistance trends. The grid-connected microgrid achieved 91.6% round-trip efficiency, an 18.7-kW tracking root-mean-square error, and 4.3% renewable curtailment. title: Research on Skeletal Muscle Glycogen Storage Kinetics, Supercompensation Mechanisms, and Periodized Nutritional Supplementation Strategies in Endurance Exercise
abstract: In endurance exercise, skeletal muscle glycogen serves as a principal carbohydrate source, especially during high-intensity exercise. The storage, utilization, and replenishment of glycogen in muscles after exercise affect the quality of training, the recovery process, and endurance performance. This paper reviews the dynamic changes in the glycogen status of skeletal muscle and its related regulatory mechanisms, and clarifies how different glycogen levels and carbohydrate availability affect athletes' adaptation to endurance training and their performance. Moreover, it also examines how carbohydrate periodization regulates glycogen availability, influences training adaptation, and preserves exercise performance. In this context, low muscle glycogen may limit high-intensity, high-volume training, while adequate post-exercise carbohydrate intake promotes glycogen resynthesis and may induce glycogen supercompensation. Meanwhile, although low-glycogen training may upregulate signaling proteins involved in cellular adaptation, lipid oxidation, and mitochondrial biogenesis, these metabolic adaptations have not consistently improved competitive performance. Thus, during endurance training, carbohydrate intake should be periodized according to exercise intensity and duration, recovery demands, and individual needs rather than maintained at consistently high or low levels, to balance t…

title: Alliance Entry Decision of Autonomous Vehicle Manufacturers from a Cost Perspective
abstract: The rapid development of autonomous driving technology has promoted the rise of cross-industry innovation alliances. From the perspective of cost, this study discusses the decision-making problem of autonomous driving manufacturers participating in the alliance under the static, single-period market and acquisition and sales mode. We construct a game theory model and compare two scenarios : independent operation and participation in the alliance. Enterprise costs include manufacturing, battery and software / hardware expenses, while consumer costs include variable energy costs and fixed costs, which are embedded in the utility function to derive demand. By solving the profit function in two scenarios and calculating the profit difference ∆ π > 0, we get the decision rule : if ∆ π > 0, we should join the alliance. Sensitivity analysis reveals key thresholds for manufacturing and battery costs. The results show that higher manufacturing or battery costs are conducive to alliance membership, and the impact of profit sharing ratio on participation in decision-making is non-monotonic. This paper provides a quantitative framework for evaluating alliance participation and provides management insights for manufacturers and alliance leaders.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Impact of different on-road vehicle emissions inventories on downstream air quality, exposure, health, and equity assessments
abstract: Abstract Emissions from on-road vehicles are a pervasive source of air pollution, contributing to inequitable pollutant exposure and adverse health outcomes. Numerical air quality models are used to characterize traffic-related pollutant concentrations and impacts. However, model outputs rely on underlying emissions inventories whose formulations can differ substantially. Here, we leverage the widely used Intervention Model for Air Pollution (InMAP) to examine how four different on-road emissions inventories used at three different spatial resolutions (1, 1.3, and 4 km) influence simulated fine particulate matter (PM2.5) population exposure, health impacts, and equity outcomes in a freight-heavy urban setting – the Greater Chicago Region. We find that population-weighted exposure and attributable mortality differ up to 72% and 69% across inventories, compared to only 15–17% across resolutions. While all inventories result in higher estimated PM2.5 exposure and mortality among Black, Hispanic, and Asian populations compared to non-Hispanic White populations, the magnitude and relative ordering of disparities across racial groups vary with both inventory choice and spatial resolution. Furthermore, we demonstrate that characterizing exposure inequities using emissions colocation can yield substantially different disparity estimates (up to 20%) from pollutant concentration-based es…

title: Element Partitioning and Fe-V-Ti Recovery During Electric-Furnace Smelting of Vanadium Titanomagnetite with Various SiO2/Al2O3 Ratios
Museums as Digital Media: A Literature Review of Cultural Heritage Promotion Strategy Through the Case of Dunhuang Academy
abstract: Digital media has transformed how cultural heritage reaches people by extending museums' reach beyond physical spaces and enabling audiences to interact with cultural content. However, relatively little is known about how varying digital structures shape audience engagement. This review examines how museums use digital media to communicate cultural value by distinguishing among database, narrative, interactive, and produsage logics. Using Dunhuang Academy as a case study, the review synthesizes museum communication and new media theories with research on its digital initiatives, including the Digital Dunhuang Open Material Library, virtual tours, interactive experiences, and digital cultural products. The analysis suggests that these forms serve complementary functions. Database structures expand access and provide multiple pathways for exploration, while narrative structures provide contextual interpretation. Interactive experiences connect learning with user action. Produsage extends cultural circulation through audience participation. Together, these findings suggest that digital media does not simply replace traditional museum communication but reshapes how cultural heritage is accessed, interpreted, and circulated.

title: The Materials of Design Strategy
Phthalide-to-Phthalane Strategy for the Synthesis of Citalopram and its Analogues
abstract: Citalopram is a widely prescribed racemic selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) and a privileged scaffold for the design analogues. We report new synthetic approaches to citalopram based on 3-arylphthalide. The first route, starting from an easily accessible 6-methoxyphthalide, was successfully elaborated up to a mesylate-citalopram precursor. The second, bromide-based route proved fully productive, delivering citalopram in six steps and 23% overall yield. This strategy was applied to prepare three original citalopram amino-analogues, highlighting the versatility of this synthetic pathway.

title: Robin Hood or rogue? Leadership dynamics and legitimate power in the donmanship of Christopher “Dudus” Coke
abstract: Abstract This paper examines the concept of legitimate power through the leadership dynamics between Christopher “Dudus” Coke, a drug cartel leader, and the Tivoli Gardens community in Jamaica. Drawing on French and Raven’s framework of social power, it examines how legitimate power was constructed and sustained within the Coke-Tivoli context. The analysis identifies a necessity-driven legitimacy, whereby Coke addressed “wicked problems” of poverty, unemployment, and insecurity through service provision, reciprocal trust, and a survival-based social contract that fostered loyalty and a level of voluntary compliance. His shared identity with Tivoli Gardens further generated representational-symbolic legitimacy, reinforcing mutuality and extending his influence beyond material provision. The paper also explores the moral and operational dimensions of his authority as both protector and enforcer. Situating the Coke–Tivoli relationship within broader debates on transnational criminal organisations, communities, and the state, the analysis conceptualises legitimate power as relational and contextual, calling for a rethinking of legitimacy as a fluid, co-constructed process in contexts where state functions are challenge.

title: Dual-Channel Thermal-Drift Modeling and Analytical Inverse Compensation for Tractor Hydraulic Output Power Measurement
abstract: During tractor hydraulic output power testing, the temperature rise induced by throttling loading causes simultaneous drift in the output characteristics of pressure sensors and turbine flowmeters, resulting in coupled errors during pressure–flow product calculation and reducing the reliability of test-bench measurements. To address the limitation of conventional single-channel temperature compensation in suppressing the coupled effects of dual-sensor thermal drift, an analytical inverse compensation method for pressure–flow dual channels based on a second-order thermal-drift parameterized model is proposed. First, a mathematical model describing the parameter drift of pressure and flow channels under temperature variations and its error propagation to hydraulic power is established. Then, temperature-dependent offsets and sensitivities of the pressure and flow channels are identified using full-temperature-range static calibration data, and the actual pressure and flow rate are analytically reconstructed based on the sensor measurement equations to achieve online hydraulic power compensation. Dynamic loading experiments with continuous temperature increase were conducted within a temperature range of 34.87~80.72 °C. Using the first test (lowest initial oil temperature 34.87 °C) as the reference baseline, the proposed method reduced the maximum relative error of hydraulic power…

title: MODELAGEM MATEMÁTICA NO ENSINO DE CÁLCULO DIFERENCIAL: UMA PROPOSTA DIDÁTICA DE OTIMIZAÇÃO DA POTÊNCIA EM SISTEMAS DE PROPULSÃO HÍBRIDA
abstract: Este artigo tem por objetivo analisar as potencialidades didático-matemáticas de uma proposta de Modelagem Matemática para o ensino de derivadas e otimização em cursos de Engenharia, tomando como situação problematizadora a relação entre torque, rotação e potência em sistemas de propulsão híbrida. A investigação é teórico-dedutiva, fundamentada em literatura de Modelagem Matemática na Educação Matemática e em resultados clássicos do Cálculo e da Análise. A partir de , estabelecem-se condições diferenciais para extremos e demonstra-se que um máximo interior positivo do torque não coincide com um máximo local da potência. Para um modelo aditivo simplificado, demonstra-se que , com igualdade precisamente quando há um maximizador comum. Um exemplo quadrático permite investigar a não simultaneidade dos máximos. Como contribuição educacional, apresenta-se um percurso de problematização, matematização, investigação de conjecturas e interpretação dos resultados, distinguindo resultados matemáticos demonstrados de possibilidades de aprendizagem ainda não verificadas empiricamente.

title: An Improved Residual Power Series Method for Radiative MHD CuO-Water Nanofluid Convection in a Semi-Porous Stretching Channel
abstract: This study considers radiative magnetohydrodynamic forced convection of a CuO–water nanofluid in asemi-porous channel with a stretching wall, with Joule heating included in the energy equation. By applyingsuitable similarity transformations, the governing continuity, momentum, and energy equations are reducedto a coupled system of nonlinear ordinary differential equations. The resulting boundary value problem issolved using the Improved Residual Power Series Method (IRPSM). The validity of the proposed approachis confirmed through comparison with available benchmark results, showing close agreement. The effectsof the Reynolds number, Hartmann number, suction parameter, and nanoparticle shape on the velocity andtemperature distributions are examined. The results indicate that the magnetic field suppresses the flow,suction significantly alters the thermal and momentum boundary layers, and platelet-shaped nanoparticlesyield the highest local Nusselt number among the considered shapes. The study demonstrates that IRPSM isan effective and accurate semi-analytical tool for this class of nonlinear transport problems.

Brassica spp. and Antimicrobial Power: A Review of MICs of Their Plant Extracts
abstract: Background/Objectives: Brassica spp. constitute an important group of edible plants. Over the last century, the important power of these plants as bioactive producers with anticancer, anti-inflammatory, antioxidant or cardioprotective properties has clearly been established. There are many species of this genus, with more than 34 species, as well as several subspecies. Brassica species also have antimicrobial properties, and this is an important aspect of this group. Therefore, the objective of this study was to explore the antimicrobial properties of extracts of different Brassica species. These aspects are important to consider in actual antimicrobial resistance crises and in terms of the possible modulation of the gut microbiota by these foods. Methods: A search of the scientific literature was carried out using the Scopus, Web of Science and Google Scholar databases. The search was carried out regarding antimicrobials as well as Brassica as the main initial term. From the great number of papers found, those with minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) data and aspects such as the extraction procedure, as well as the proven microorganisms, were selected. Results: A total of 41 papers were selected from the literature. Most of them were from Brassica oleracea, with a total of 14 papers. There are differences between different species, as well as among the different parts of th…

title: Latent Profiles of Codex-Mapped Additive Functional Classes and Their Association with Nutri-Score in a Sampled Turkish Retail Food Inventory
abstract: Food additives recur in combinations across packaged foods, but their association with nutritional quality is uncertain. We identified latent profiles of Codex-mapped functional classes from label-declared additives in a sampled Turkish retail inventory and related them to Nutri-Score grade. Of the 6515 products, 3383 with a retained functional-class indicator entered latent class analysis. Five profiles were retained using a prespecified multi-criterion procedure without numerical cutoffs; the fifth, gas-related profile was mapping-sensitive and not interpreted. Investigator-computed grades (2023 algorithm) were analyzed in 2942 products across 56 food subgroups with two-step ordinal models. The raising and texture profile was associated with poorer grades across the scale (odds ratio, 1.99; 95% confidence interval, 1.51–2.63); the oxidation and color-retention profile was inversely associated at the grade-E boundary (0.49, 0.37–0.63); and the coating and structure profile was displaced from the favorable end (imprecise estimate). In profile-only models, these directions held under a structurally reduced specification and after restoring nonsweetener classes of excluded sweeteners and polyols; magnitudes and cutpoint-specific forms, particularly for the raising and texture profile, were specification-sensitive. The associations are subgroup-conditional descriptive contrasts in…

title: Boards of Directors and Voluntary Carbon Disclosure: Evidence From Italy
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines whether Italy's concentrated ownership environment alters the effectiveness of board‐level governance mechanisms as drivers of voluntary carbon disclosure quality, in line with the institutional theory, challenging the assumptions of standard agency and stakeholder theories. Using a sample of 60 Italian listed non‐financial companies over 2015–2023, we employ the Carbon Disclosure Project scores as a measure of disclosure quality. The presence of a corporate social responsibility committee is the only governance mechanism consistently associated with the disclosure quality across all specifications. Board independence exhibits a significant negative effect, consistent with the symbolic compliance hypothesis, according to which independent directors in blockholder‐dominated firms may function as compliance figures rather than effective monitors. Board size, gender diversity, and CEO duality are not significantly associated with disclosure quality. Further analysis shows that the CSR committee effect is stronger in carbon‐intensive industries and weaker in family‐controlled firms. Family ownership also attenuates the negative effect of board independence, suggesting that concentrated ownership selectively conditions, rather than uniformly suppresses, governance effectiveness. Results are robust to alternative estimators, lag structures, and endogeneit…

title: Multimodal lifestyle intervention during neoadjuvant chemotherapy in patients with early breast cancer as a strategy to improve treatment response: Protocol of the DIANA randomized clinical trial
abstract: Breast cancer (BC) represents a major global health concern. Lifestyle factors influence both prevention and prognosis, but evidence on their impact on oncological response to BC treatment remains limited. We present the protocol of a randomized clinical trial designed to assess whether a multimodal intervention—combining physical exercise, psychological support, and nutritional counseling during neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC)—could improve pathological response, measured by the Residual Cancer Burden (RCB) index, in women with early BC. A total of 216 women will be randomized (1:1) to control (standard of care, n = 108) or intervention (n = 108). The intervention consists of a supervised, individualized multimodal prehabilitation program that combines physical exercise, psychotherapy, and nutritional support delivered throughout NAC (4–6 months). Tumor pathology, including microenvironment analysis, will be assessed before NAC and after surgery. Data will be collected at baseline, preoperatively, and at 1 and 12 months postoperatively. Long-term oncological outcomes will be reported annually for a minimum of 5 years, with the intention to extend to 10 years. We hypothesize that the intervention group will show higher pathological response rates than controls, with a targeted 20-percentage point improvement in the rate of favorable RCB response (fRCB, defined as RCB class 0 or …

Brand Strategy in Transition: From Traditional Marketing to Social Media Precision Marketing
abstract: This paper researches the strategic transition from traditional mass marketing to algorithm-driven precision marketing and why it has become essential in modern society. Traditional frameworks such as the 4Ps and STP models are based on one-way communication and demographic segmentation, being less effective in today's world. As consumer behavior shifts to focus more on user-generated content (UGC) and electronic word-of-mouth (e-WOM), brands have started losing their narrative control. In order to adapt to these changes, companies could make use of big data and algorithms to deliver personalized content directly to individuals, predicting potential consumers and making the marketing process more efficient. By a case study of Nike's digital strategy, this study shows how using social media and brand apps can help the company share a better connection with consumers, while also having challenges around internet privacy. Overall, this paper offers insights about how brands can promote their marketing strategies in the digital age.

title: A SWOT Analysis of the U.S. National Artificial Intelligence Strategy And Its Implications for Smart Mobility
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is a cutting-edge technology that enhances efficiency across multiple sectors through the effective analysis of diverse data sources. Governments are continuously publishing strategic AI plans to adapt to AI-centric digital transformation. These plans address various concepts, including infrastructure investments, ethical and human values, innovation speed, political barriers, inclusiveness, and transparency. These efforts are critical for establishing the necessary infrastructure for the development of smart cities that integrate innovative systems and improve citizens’ quality of life. Smart mobility constitutes a key pillar of smart cities and is directly linked to the efficiency of these systems. Experience in AI governance underscores the importance of evaluating how national strategies affect such critical sectors. This study first evaluates the United States Artificial Intelligence Action Plan, published by The White House on July 10, 2025, using the SWOT analysis method. Subsequently, recommended policy actions and their potential impacts on smart mobility are examined in the light of literature findings. The SWOT analysis highlights advantages such as accelerated innovation and increased inter-institutional collaboration, as well as some disadvantages such as environmental and ethical concerns. Accordingly, this study presents recommendatio…

title: Redescription of Uranoscopus bicinctus Temminck and Schlegel 1843 (Teleostei: Uranoscopidae): an integrative approach resolves taxonomic uncertainty related to variation in body colouration and oral luring organ
abstract: Abstract The highest diversity of the family Uranoscopidae (commonly known as stargazers) is in the Indo-Pacific. Many guidebooks and studies from the region have found the number and identification of species to be difficult to determine, especially in the genus Uranoscopus . Herein we redescribe Uranoscopus bicinctus Temminck and Schlegel 1843 to address new information on the morphological variation across the species’ range that has contributed to taxonomic confusion. We use museum specimens and genetic data from across their distribution from Japan to Australia to explain differences in the body colouration (e.g., presence/absence of black spots) and the oral luring organ (e.g., complexity of cirri, tendrils). We then discuss taxonomic confusion in Uranoscopus bicinctus and compare to other uranoscopids to aid in future identification of this species.

title: Strategic Alliances and Competitive Advantage in a Predominantly Family-Owned SME Context: The Mediating Role of Resource Acquisition and the Moderating Effect of Environmental Uncertainty
abstract: This study investigates the relationship between Effective Strategic Alliances (ESA) and Competitive Advantage among small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in resource-constrained environments. Situated in the West Bank, Palestine, where family ownership is highly prevalent among SMEs and political and economic conditions are uncertain, the study examines whether strategic alliances facilitate external resource acquisition and whether these resources contribute to competitive advantage. ESA is conceptualized as a formative higher-order construct comprising Relational Quality, Resource Complementarity, and Agility. Using a quantitative, deductive approach, we analyzed data from 262 Palestinian SMEs using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results demonstrate that ESA is significantly associated with Resource Acquisition and Competitive Advantage. Resource Acquisition mediates the relationship between ESA and Competitive Advantage, while Environmental Uncertainty moderates the link between ESA and Resource Acquisition, highlighting the importance of alliances under high uncertainty. These findings provide an integrated framework for SME managers, particularly in family-business contexts, and policymakers to leverage collaborative strategies for economic resilience and performance in challenging environments.

title: Need-Conditioned Uncertainty and Perceived Non-Provision of Community Services: Social Participation and Functional Status Among Older Adults in Urban China
abstract: Older adults who need community services may remain uncertain whether those services are locally provided or judge that they are not. Research on perceived unmet need often combines these positions. Using a cross-sectional survey of 929 adults aged 60 or older in urban Jiangsu, China, we paired reported need with perceived provision across 20 services and distinguished awareness gaps, perceived non-provision, and comparison uncertainty for services not reported as needed. Fractional logit models examined associations with social participation and functional status. Greater social participation was associated with fewer awareness gaps, concentrated among adults with ADL disability (−8.75 percentage points per SD). A weaker, less stable association with perceived non-provision appeared among functionally independent adults, and no counterpart appeared for comparison uncertainty. Unresolved uncertainty and negative provision judgments may call for different responses, and outreach may be especially relevant for older adults with ADL disability.

title: On the Singular Control of a Diffusion and Its Running Infimum or Supremum
abstract: Abstract. We study a class of singular stochastic control problems for a one-dimensional diffusion [Formula: see text] in which the performance criterion to be optimized depends explicitly on the running infimum [Formula: see text] (or supremum [Formula: see text]) of the controlled process. We introduce two novel integral operators that are consistent with the Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman equation for the resulting two-dimensional singular control problems. The first operator involves integrals where the integrator is the control process of the two-dimensional process [Formula: see text] or [Formula: see text]; the second operator concerns integrals where the integrator is the running infimum or supremum process itself. Using these definitions, we prove a general verification theorem for problems involving two-dimensional state-dependent running costs, costs of controlling the process, costs of increasing the running infimum (or supremum) and exit times. Finally, we apply our results to explicitly solve an optimal dividend problem in which the manager’s time-preferences depend on the company’s historical worst performance.

title: Law Audit on Violation of Fundamental Right in Context of Water Shortage in Bengaluru
abstract: This research paper presents a comprehensive legal audit investigating the systemic water shortage in Bengaluru and its direct implications on fundamental rights, particularly the right to life, dignity, and livelihood under the Constitution of India. With a population exceeding 13 million heavily reliant on distant river supplies and rapidly depleting groundwater, Bengaluru faces a recurring structural deficit, marked by a documented official shortfall of over 500 million liters per day and widespread drying of borewells. Employing a doctrinal and vulnerability-focused approach, the audit evaluates the roles, statutory powers, and accountability mechanisms of key municipal and state institutions. While Indian jurisprudence ties the right to clean water and livelihood to Article 21, alongside supporting directive principles and fundamental duties, the study identifies a critical legislative lacuna: the complete absence of a statutory right to water or enforceable minimum service standards in state law. Furthermore, the paper highlights pervasive governance gaps, including fragmented institutional responsibilities, weak enforcement of groundwater and tanker regulations, high distribution losses, and inadequate protections for vulnerable communities, informal workers, and peripheral urban areas. To bridge these gaps, the author proposes practical legal and structural reforms, inc…

A Review of Monte Carlo Simulation in the Field of Financial Credit Risk Prediction
abstract: In recent years, global economic volatility has intensified, and rising market uncertainties have continuously exacerbated, the international situation has shifted, and the uncertainty of the market environment continues to rise. So the operating pressure on small and medium-sized enterprises is constantly increasing. Consequently, the transmissibility and complexity of credit risk have significantly increased. The complexity of credit risk renders traditional static financial risk prediction methods incapable of coping with the complex scenarios involving multiple factors interacting with each other. As a numerical analysis method based on random sampling, Monte Carlo simulation, with its core advantages of being capable of handling multiple variables and supporting dynamic simulation, is increasingly widely applied in the field of financial risk assessment. This essay takes credit risk prediction as the starting point, outlining the core principles of Monte Carlo simulation and the implementation process for risk analysis, and elaborate on their application pathways and modeling logic in three specialized financial fields: real estate investment appraisal, insurance actuarial risk control, and financial derivatives pricing, compare and analyse the adaptability advantages and inherent limitations of this method in different situations. The findings indicate that Monte Carlo si…

title: A Cognitive Hybrid Cryptosystem for the Secure and Resilient Transmission of Election Results: Homomorphic Aggregation, Quantum Key Distribution and Constrained Reinforcement Learning
abstract: The electronic transmission of polling-station reports must keep results confidential during processing, protect them in transit against present and quantum adversaries, and remain available when the network degrades or is attacked. Existing architectures address these requirements separately and statically. This paper proposes the Cognitive Hybrid Cryptosystem (CHC), which combines Ring-LWE-based BFV homomorphic encryption for blind aggregation and threshold decryption, BB84 quantum key distribution with a hybrid post-quantum fallback (ML-KEM-768 + X25519), and a MAPE-K cognitive engine formalised as a constrained Markov decision process. We mathematically model the electoral workflow and the threat model, prove the correctness of the tally, prove with a sub-Gaussian concentration bound that the aggregation noise grows as √n — which makes bootstrapping unnecessary — and derive from a smudging lemma the admissibility condition of secure threshold decryption: 42 bits of noise budget for a statistical distance of 2-40 per coefficient, and about 58–59 bits for a global distance of 2-40over all coefficients and decryptions. The reproducible prototype CHC-Vote, whose ML-KEM-768 module passes the official NIST ACVP test vectors, was evaluated on synthetic electoral data with a simulated quantum channel and a simulated network: 50,000 actually encrypted reports, 12,700 active attacks …

title: Selection into Financial Education and Effects on Portfolio Choice
abstract: We study the impact of a financial education program on portfolio choices in a setting that allows us to examine both participation decisions and differences in program benefits across individuals. We directly elicit willingness to pay for financial education and show that individuals with higher financial literacy, greater confidence in applying new knowledge, and higher expected returns are willing to pay more. Using incentivized portfolio allocation tasks, we develop outcome measures tailored to individual risk preferences and show that financial education improves decision quality along these dimensions. The program increases the share of participants who experience an improvement by 20 percentage points, corresponding to average gains of 3.2 percentage points of initial wealth. Individuals with the highest willingness to participate benefit disproportionately from the program, with important implications for the design and evaluation of financial education initiatives. By isolating a specific investment skill in a setting with voluntary participation, our design sheds light on how selection into financial education shapes measured program effects and informs the assessment of broader workplace and public training programs. Neuroinflammation in levodopa-induced dyskinesia in Parkinson’s disease: current state of the art
abstract: Abstract Levodopa-induced dyskinesia (LID) remains a major limitation of long-term dopaminergic therapy in Parkinson’s disease (PD). Although LID is classically attributed to maladaptive corticostriatal plasticity driven by pulsatile dopaminergic stimulation in the dopamine-denervated striatum, accumulating evidence indicates that chronic neuroinflammation may lower the threshold for LID development and expression. Here, we synthesize preclinical, human biomarkers, neuroimaging, and genetic findings that support neuroinflammation as a mechanistic bridge between cellular stress and circuit-level maladaptation. In animal models, pharmacological modulation of inflammation-linked pathways, particularly nitrergic signaling, antibiotic repurposing, and cannabinoid-based strategies, attenuates abnormal involuntary movements and reduces striatal glial reactivity, implicating an inflammation–plasticity coupling in LID. In humans, post-mortem studies implicate regionally constrained mitochondrial DNA abnormalities and lipid dysregulation in the striatum, while biofluid metabolomics supports altered nitric oxide generation and lipid pathways associated with LID severity. Neuroimaging studies reveal markers consistent with oxidative stress and neurovascular dysfunction, and genetic studies link LID risk to variants in genes involved in lysosomal function, mitochondrial homeostasis, and inf…

title: Peak-Weighted Calibration of Implemented Integer-Order, Caputo, and Atangana–Baleanu–Caputo Schemes for Simultaneous COVID-19 and Influenza Transmission
abstract: COVID-19 and influenza may produce overlapping waves, yet an overall least-squares fit need not represent their high-activity weeks well. We compare implemented integer-order, Caputo, and Atangana–Baleanu–Caputo (ABC) discrete schemes for a common ten-compartment transition structure with seasonal transmission and external influenza input. The schemes are calibrated with ordinary mean-normalized weighted least squares (J1) and a peak-weighted objective (J2). We fit the first 66 of 83 weekly observation pairs and assess the remaining 17 weeks. ABC gives the smallest training peak root-mean-square error for both series under either objective. Within ABC, J2 reduces COVID-19 and influenza training peak errors by 9.50% and 42.98%, respectively, relative to its J1 fit. Integer order achieves the smallest ordinary loss and lower temporal validation error. The autonomous disease-free and conditional invasion thresholds characterize the underlying unforced vector field, not the fitted seasonal system. These findings support peak-weighted calibration for retrospective high-activity reconstruction in these data, but they do not establish superior future-peak prediction.

title: Artificial Intelligence Application in Financial Customer Fraud Detection
abstract: With the rapid digitization of financial services, the online transactions have become prevalent, accompanied by a growing number of financial fraud incidents that cause substantial losses to financial institutions and individual users. Traditional rule-based fraud detection methods suffer from low efficiency, poor timeliness and limited adaptability to hidden and emerging fraud behaviors. Benefiting from the powerful self-learning capability, high-dimensional data processing performance and dynamic feature mining advantages of artificial intelligence algorithms, intelligent detection technologies have become the mainstream solution for modern financial fraud risk control. This paper systematically investigates the application of typical machine learning and deep learning algorithms in customer financial fraud detection. It summarizes the practical advantages of different models, analyzes the core application challenges including the data imbalance and poor model interpretability, and proposes targeted future development directions. The research aims to provide the theoretical references for the optimization and industrial application of intelligent financial fraud detection systems.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Seconds-scale renewable AGC security control considering multi-level transmission section constraints
abstract: With the increasing penetration of renewable energy, fluctuations of non-AGC renewable stations and load disturbances may cause security-boundary violations in multi-level transmission sections. This paper proposes a seconds-scale renewable AGC security-control method that integrates DNN-based fast state estimation, PTDF-based section-to-station sensitivity analysis, and quadratic-programming-based command optimization. The method redistributes AGC commands within a 4-s rolling cycle while coordinating transmission-section security, 15-min dispatch tracking, and renewable energy accommodation. Tests on the IEEE 118-bus system show that the active- and reactive-power relative estimation errors remain below 3% when the measurement-noise level is increased to three times its baseline value. In the baseline renewable energy export scenario, the proposed method reduces the control-boundary violation duration from 448 s to 0 s and the maximum boundary exceedance from 52.754 MW to 0 MW, while maintaining a renewable energy accommodation rate of 92.596%. Across ten operating scenarios, the method prevents physical overload in all cases and achieves accommodation rates of 90.447%–98.388%. These results demonstrate its effectiveness and computational feasibility for seconds-scale coordinated security control of multi-level renewable energy export sections.

title: Economic Dispatch in Hybrid Microgrids Considering Time-Varying Voltage-Dependent Load Models
abstract: Renewable energy intermittency, network congestion, voltage fluctuations, and time-varying electricity demand provide operational issues as renewable energy supplies become more prevalent in microgrids. Therefore, coordinated scheduling of conventional production, renewable resources, and battery energy storage is necessary for accurate economic dispatch while specifically taking voltage-dependent demand and network operational restrictions into account. For a hybrid microgrid consisting of diesel generators, photovoltaic (PV) production, wind turbines, and battery energy storage systems (BESS) under time-varying voltage-dependent load conditions, this study creates an economic dispatch framework based on AC optimal power flow (AC-OPF). The cost of diesel generation, curtailment of renewable energy, load shedding, and voltage deviation are all taken into account concurrently by the objective function. A modified IEEE 24-bus test system is used to assess the suggested formulation over a 24-hour operational horizon under various loading and renewable energy availability scenarios. The findings demonstrate that the integration of renewable energy significantly lowers reliance on diesel, operating costs, and locational marginal prices. Additionally, the incorporation of BESS increases operational flexibility, decreases load shedding, and improves voltage control. With a stated tota…

title: Distributed optimization for transactive energy management in interconnected multi-microgrid systems
abstract: The rapid proliferation of renewable energy resources, battery energy storage systems (BESSs), and flexible loads has increased the operational complexity of interconnected multi-microgrid systems, creating the urgent need for effective and decentralized energy management strategies. In this context, this paper proposes a framework for Distributed Transactive Energy Management (DTEM), leveraging the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM), aimed at transactive energy transfer to achieve coordinated operation of interconnected microgrids. The proposed framework simultaneously schedules dispatchable generators, battery energy storage systems, flexible loads, and peer-to-peer energy exchange, aiming to minimize the overall operating cost while preserving the operational privacy of individual microgrids through information exchange between neighboring grids. The convex optimization problem is formulated by incorporating generation costs, battery degradation costs, energy trading costs, and the utility associated with flexible loads, together with operational and grid constraints. This optimization problem is decomposed into independent local sub-problems, enabling each microgrid to determine its operating schedule without the need for a centralized coordinator. Furthermore, the convergence of the distributed algorithm to the optimal solution is demonstrated under standar…

title: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces with liquid crystal technology: a hardware design and communication perspective
abstract: Abstract With the surge of theoretical work investigating Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RISs) for wireless communication and sensing, there exists an urgent need of hardware solutions for the evaluation of these theoretical results and further advancing the field. The most common solutions proposed in the literature are based on varactors, Positive-Intrinsic-Negative (PIN) diodes, and Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems (MEMS). This paper presents the use of Liquid Crystal (LC) technology for the realization of continuously-tunable extremely large millimeter-wave RISs. We review the basic physical principles of LC theory, introduce two different realizations of LC-RISs, namely resonant versus delay-line architectures, and highlight their key properties that have an impact on the system design and RIS reconfiguration strategy. Moreover, the LC technology is compared with the competing technologies in terms of feasibility, cost, power consumption, reconfiguration speed, and bandwidth. Furthermore, several important open problems for both theoretical and experimental research on LC-RISs are presented.

title: Visual Search Strategies in Dense Virtual Reality Scenes Depend on Inter-Object Spacing
abstract: Visual search in virtual reality (VR) relies on the coordination of peripheral vision, eye movements, and head movements. In dense immersive scenes, inter-object spacing is expected to influence search behavior by modulating local visual interference, while also changing the angular extent of the explored scene. In this article, we investigate how inter-object spacing shapes visual search strategies in VR using ecologically valid textured 3D objects. We conducted a user study in which participants searched for target objects among distractors under three spacing conditions, while keeping the number of objects constant and recording both eye and head movements. Conventional visual search measures, such as search time, fixation count, and mean fixation duration, are typically expected to vary consistently with task difficulty. However, our results reveal a mixed pattern: search time and fixation count increase with spacing, whereas mean fixation duration decreases. This apparent paradox highlights the limitations of standard metrics in VR, where performance is strongly influenced by scene extent and head contribution. To address this, we complement traditional measures with detailed scanpath analyses. We show that dense layouts induce more refixations, more frequent direction changes, and less stable exploration patterns. Although absolute scanpath length increases with spacing, …

title: Ensemble quantile-based deep learning framework for streamflow and flood prediction in Australian catchments
abstract: Abstract In recent years, climate extremes such as floods have created significant environmental and economic hazards for Australia. Deep learning methods have been promising for predicting extreme climate events; however, large flooding events present a critical challenge due to factors such as model calibration and missing data. We present an ensemble quantile-based deep learning framework that addresses large-scale streamflow forecasts using quantile regression for uncertainty projections in prediction. We evaluate selected univariate and multivariate deep learning models and catchment strategies. We implement a multistep time-series prediction model using the CAMELS dataset for selected catchments across Australia. The ensemble model employs a set of quantile deep learning models for streamflow determined by historical streamflow data. We utilise the streamflow prediction and obtain flood probability using flood frequency analysis and compare it with historical flooding events for selected catchments. Our results demonstrate notable efficacy and uncertainties in streamflow forecasts with varied catchment properties. Our flood probability estimates show good accuracy in capturing the historical floods from the selected catchments. This underscores the potential for our deep learning framework to revolutionise flood forecasting across diverse regions and be implemented as an …
venue: Stochastic Environmental Research and Risk Assessment

title: Optimizing cross-border CCS policy: an integrated energy–carbon–cost framework for source–host credit allocation
abstract: Cross-border carbon capture and storage (CCS) can support industrial decarbonisation where emissions and storage resources are unevenly distributed. Existing optimisation studies mainly minimise techno-economic cost and rarely integrate energy penalties, country-level emissions accounting, domestic-versus-export allocation, and source–host credit sharing. This study develops a mixed-integer linear programming framework that selects domestic or export storage, shipping routes, offshore pipelines, and sinks while tracking operational emissions, costs, and source–host credit allocation. An anonymised Japan–Malaysia case includes two Japanese sources, two Malaysian sinks, and a domestic screening pathway. Domestic Japanese storage costs USD 0.327 billion/year, compared with USD 0.484 billion/year for full export. Under the Combined Competitiveness scenario, a combination of a lower Malaysian service fee, equal source–host credit sharing, and an upper-end published domestic-storage cost selects full export to MY-Sink 1 at USD 0.426 billion/year, with the capability of storing 2.674 MtCO<sub>2</sub>/year after shipping loss. Credit ownership changes economic and national accounting outcomes without changing routing. Malaysian storage and injection, shipping, and credit values give the largest local sensitivity responses. In summary, the framework provides a transparent method for ass…

title: Observation operator and detection limits for MODIS and VIIRS Fire Radiative Power products
abstract: We analyze the MODIS and VIIRS active-fire Fire Radiative Power (FRP) products, suggest an approximation for the FRP detection limit as a linear function of a pixel area, and develop analytical observation operators for both pixel-level and gridded FRP products. We have shown that the collection-6.1 of MODIS has the FRP detection limit at 3.7 MW in case of a nadir retrieval at a clear-sky night. For a daytime sideview, it reaches as high as 40 MW. For VIIRS, the smallest fire reliably detected at night is 0.5 MW. Application of the developed operators for the cross-mapping the MODIS and VIIRS datasets at the pixel/granule level confirmed their consistency. Applying the grid-level operators alongside satellite overpass and weather data, we generated global maps of fire detection probabilities, revealing regional variations. As a global average, probability of detection of powerful fires is 78 % for MODIS (88 % for VIIRS). Variations between regions are large: in some equatorial areas this probability is less than 30 % for MODIS (40 % for VIIRS).

title: The moderating role of financial constraints on the relationship between supply chain finance efficiency and firm market value: Evidence from Egypt
abstract: Background: Supply chain finance efficiency (SCFE) is increasingly recognised as an important determinant of firms’ financial performance and market value. However, limited evidence exists on how financial constraints influence the relationship between SCFE and firm market value, particularly in emerging markets. Aim: This study examines the relationship between SCFE and firm market value and investigates the moderating effect of financial constraints. Setting: The study focuses on 34 non-financial firms listed on the Egyptian Stock Exchange during 2016–2023, yielding 268 firm-year observations. Method: Supply chain finance efficiency is measured using the cash conversion cycle (CCC) and variable returns to scale data envelopment analysis (DEA). Firm market value is measured using the market-to-book ratio (MB) and market capitalisation. Results: Supply chain finance efficiency has a significant positive relationship with firm market value. Financial constraints significantly negatively moderate this relationship when market value is measured by MB. The positive effect of SCFE is stronger for unconstrained firms, while it weakens and becomes statistically insignificant under financial constraints. Conclusion: Improving SCFE can enhance firm market value, but financial constraints may limit its effectiveness. Contribution: The study contributes by introducing a DEA-based relative…

title: The fishery biology of the three-spot seahorse (Hippocampus trimaculatus) in the Con Dao Archipelago, Vietnam
abstract: The three-spot seahorse (Hippocampus trimaculatus Leach) is among the most heavily harvested seahorse species in Vietnam. Due to overexploitation and habitat degradation, H. trimaculatus is listed in Appendix II of CITES (2014), the IUCN Red List (IUCN, 2025), and the Vietnam Red List of Threatened Species (Vietnam Academy of Science and Technology, 2024). Although H. trimaculatus is harvested throughout Vietnamese waters, its fishery biology data remain limited, particularly for the Con Dao Archipelago, a biodiversity hotspot of high conservation importance. This study investigated the fishery biology of H. trimaculatus in the Con Dao Archipelago and proposes conservation measures. A total of 499 H. trimaculatus specimens were collected from local fishers in April and October 2024 in the Con Dao Archipelago and identified on the basis of molecular analysis and morphology. Interviews were conducted with 16 fishers and seven seafood shops to gather information on exploitation and trade. The results indicated that H. trimaculatus is being exploited unsustainably, as evidenced by the fishing gear used, the male-to-female sex ratio of 1:1.1, the portion of brooding males (21.04%) in the total catch, the capture of immature individuals, and the scarcity of mega-spawners. Sexual dimorphism, allometric growth, and differences in the length-weight relationships of the H. trimaculatus p…

title: Formal policy decisions and housing-market divergence under second-home taxation in Wales
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine local housing-market paths after formal decisions to impose recurring council-tax premiums on second homes in Wales. Design/methodology/approach The study links 485,767 sales in 22 local authorities, 2015–2025, to verified decisions and administrative exposure. Group-time differences use not-yet-determined and never-determined controls. Inference uses 9,999 wild cluster multiplier replications and simultaneous bands. Census 2011, UK House Price Index (UK HPI) and office for national statistics boundaries support sensitivity checks. Findings Relative prices are near zero through month 23, then 4.1% lower in months 24–47, 6.8% lower in months 48–71 and 9.7% lower in months 72–84. The last estimate uses four cohorts and ten treated authorities. UK HPI and border exclusions preserve a negative late difference, although the strictest rule is not simultaneously significant. Transactions do not respond jointly. With 2.8% of dwellings charged in positive-return cells, direct tax capitalisation alone cannot explain the market-wide magnitude. Research limitations/implications Voluntary adoption, one never-determined authority and policy-responsive classification preclude definitive causal or affordability claims. Practical implications Evaluation should report the share of dwellings actually charged alongside the headline premium rate and track classifi…
venue: International Journal of Housing Markets and Analysis

title: Is China still considered an emerging market? Divergent viewpoints
abstract: Purpose China is an indispensable and dynamic member of the global community. The purpose of this viewpoint is to consider whether China still exhibits the characteristics of an emerging market first introduced in the literature in 1981. Design/methodology/approach Two international business scholars approach China's categorization as an emerging market through the lens of the traditional emerging market definition. The method employed is a back-and-forth debate grounded in international business theory. Findings Our contrasting findings indicate that China adheres to some traditional characteristics of an emerging market but not all of them, resulting in definitional ambiguity. The decades-old definition of emerging markets may no longer adequately describe China today. Originality/value Our original discussion moves beyond the traditional emerging market framework and considers other parameters that may better reflect China’s rise on the global stage.

title: Vision Based Robotic Autonomous Refueling System for Highway Service Areas
abstract: Highway service-area fueling stations face recurring challenges in labor cost, centralized management, and operational safety. This paper presents a prototype autonomous visual unmanned gas-station system that combines YOLOv5s object detection, a Raspberry Pi-controlled two-degree-of-freedom manipulator, and an ESP32-based Internet-of-Things (IoT) interface. A camera detects the fuel-inlet proxy target, and its image coordinates are transmitted through a serial link to an incremental PI controller that aligns the nozzle. Users select a fueling amount through a mobile interface connected to the Bafa Cloud platform. A 900-image dataset was collected under varied viewpoints and backgrounds; the model was trained for 400 epochs with an 80/20 train–validation split. The prototype achieved detection accuracies above 80% on the tested target shapes, while nozzle positioning errors remained below 3 cm. The results demonstrate the feasibility of integrating lightweight deep learning, embedded control, and cloud interaction for unattended fueling, while also revealing the need for larger real-vehicle datasets and additional safety sensing.
venue: Journal of Computer Science and Frontier Technologies

title: Family-focused suicide risk management service on reducing suicide behavior repetitions among adolescents: protocol for a randomized controlled trial
abstract: Abstract Background Suicidal behavior in adolescents is a major global public health challenge, yet evidence-based, scalable interventions remain limited, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Methods This is a single-center, randomized, parallel-group controlled trial with a 1:1 allocation ratio. A total of 824 adolescents with suicide behavior and their family caregivers will be randomly allocated to either a brief family-based cognitive behavioral therapy intervention (three sessions) or an enhanced usual care control condition (supportive contact and psychoeducation). The primary outcome is time from randomization to first suicidal behavior within 90 days, assessed using the Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale. Secondary outcomes include suicide attempt occurrence, self-harm frequency, self-efficacy to coping self-harm, perceived family function, retention rate and adherence to medical treatment. Follow-up assessments are conducted at day 30, day 60, day 90, and month 6. Data analysis will follow the intention-to-treat principle using Cox proportional hazards models. Discussion This trial will provide evidence on the effectiveness of a brief family-based intervention for adolescent in suicide crisis. If successful, the intervention has the potential to be scaled in resource-limited settings. Protocol version 2024-12-27, 1.0. Trial registration This study was …

title: Code-Switching in English Curriculum Delivery in Rural South African Universities: Pedagogical Roles, Benefits, and Challenges for Pre-Service Teachers
abstract: This systematic literature review examines how code-switching (CS) functions in English instruction at rural South African universities for preservice teachers, highlighting its advantages and challenges. Although English is the primary language of instruction in higher education, most students in these settings speak African home languages, which pose major challenges to understanding and academic success. The review combines research from peer-reviewed journals, book chapters, and policy documents published between 2010 and 2025, drawing on Vygotsky's Sociocultural Theory and Cummins' Linguistic Interdependence Hypothesis. The researchers started with 1281 documents collected from Google Scholar, Web of Science, and Scopus and identified 186 studies that met their research requirements, which they analysed using reflexive thematic analysis (Braun & Clarke, 2006). The study identified five themes: CS as strategic pedagogical scaffolding; the promotion of inclusivity and affective security; the policy–practice disconnect; meta-pedagogical modelling for pre-service teacher socialisation; and systemic resource, stigma, and training deficits. The findings show that CS is an effective teaching method when grounded in theory, connecting students' native language skills with academic English. The system faces major limitations due to its English-only teaching rules, the absence of fo…

title: Visitor Attraction Model of Trade and Service Facilities at the Business Unit Level in the Planned Government Centre Area of Serang Regency
abstract: Estimating the traffic impact of the planned Serang Regency Government Centre requires attraction models for every constituent land use, including the trade and service facilities that dominate the Serang-Jakarta arterial corridor. This study develops a visitor attraction model from 138 business units across nine activity types in Ciruas and Kragilan Districts, using daily visitor counts as the dependent variable and three independent variables: parking area, building area, and number of employees. The analysis works at the business unit level, unlike the common practice of aggregating to village level, which reduces the sample to 27 observations. All three independent variables correlate positively and significantly with the dependent variable, at 0.875 for parking area, 0.730 for building area, and 0.552 for employees. Multiple regression yields a coefficient of determination of 0.836, yet the employee coefficient turns negative and significant (B = -28.182; p < 0.001). Adding business type controls raises the coefficient of determination to 0.862 without restoring the sign, and logarithmic transformation of all three predictors merely relocates the reversal. The linear specification also fails the Breusch-Pagan test (LM = 847.2; p < 0.001) and is dominated by 14 market units whose removal lowers the slope by 78 percent. The elasticity model ln Y = 2.068 + 0.501 ln X, with X …
