Co-designing a frailty care pathway in the emergency department: integrating patient, carer and multidisciplinary perspectives through mixed-method service evaluation
abstract: Purpose Emergency departments (EDs) increasingly operate at the interface between acute care, Hospital at Home (H@H) and community services for frail older adults. Despite this, frailty care in EDs often remains fragmented, time-pressured and insufficiently aligned with patient and carer priorities. This study aimed to co-design an integrated frailty care pathway for the ED that supports continuity across the ED, H@H and community services, incorporating patient, carer and multidisciplinary staff perspectives. Design/methodology/approach A mixed-methods service evaluation was conducted in a large UK tertiary hospital ED with established H@H services. Quantitative patient and carer surveys (n = 52) explored experiences of ED care, including communication, involvement, kindness and respect. Qualitative data were generated through staff co-design workshops and patient and carer engagement activities. Appreciative inquiry and co-design principles guided data analysis and pathway development. Findings Survey findings demonstrated consistently positive experiences overall, with kindness and involvement strongly associated with patient experience and kindness the strongest independent correlate in the multivariable model. Qualitative analysis identified four themes: challenges in current frailty care, what matters to patients and carers, co-designing a responsive frailty pathway and o…

title: The impact of perceived service quality in customs services on customer satisfaction and customer loyalty: an analysis with structural equation modeling
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the relationships between the perceived quality of services received by foreign trade companies from customs brokerage firms and customer satisfaction and loyalty. In addition, the research re-evaluated the dimensional structure of the service quality scale in a sector-specific manner. Design/methodology/approach In this research, which was conducted with data collected through a survey method from 404 participants working in foreign trade companies in Türkiye, the service quality (SERVQUAL) model was used to evaluate service quality, and the structural equation modeling (SEM) method was used to examine the links between customer satisfaction and loyalty. Findings The findings indicate that perceived service quality is positively associated with customer satisfaction and customer loyalty, with customer satisfaction representing a significant mediating pathway. Furthermore, the analysis results yielded a three-component representation consisting of Reliability, Interaction Quality, and Tangibles. Research limitations/implications During the adaptation process of the SERVQUAL scale, some items were found to not provide sufficient decomposition within the factor structure and were therefore removed from the analysis. This limits the extent to which conclusions can be drawn regarding the dimensional structure of SERVQUAL and highlights the need fo…

title: Understanding the spillover effect of personal AI use on service innovation: the role of psychological capital and conscientiousness
abstract: Purpose As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly embedded in everyday life and workplace operations, research has begun to document numerous organizational benefits, including enhanced efficiency and productivity. However, employees’ personal experiences with AI and how these experiences spill over into the work domain remain underexplored. Using sociomateriality as a sensitizing lens, we propose and test a sequential process in which personal AI use increases work-related AI use, further enhancing employees’ psychological capital, ultimately improving their service innovation performance. We further examine conscientiousness as an important boundary condition that moderates this pathway. Design/methodology/approach Study 1 uses a three-wave survey of 438 service employees and employs structural equation modeling to test the hypothesized serial mediation. Study 2 extends this investigation by examining within-person dynamics using a daily experience sampling design with 121 participants and testing the moderating role of conscientiousness. Findings Across both studies, personal AI use positively predicts employees’ work-related AI use, which in turn increases their psychological capital and subsequently service innovation performance. Moreover, employees lower in conscientiousness benefit more from AI use. Originality/value This paper contributes to our understandin…

title: Designing phygital tourism experiencescapes for tourist well-being: a transformative service framework
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to develop a Transformative Service Research (TSR)-informed framework explaining how phygital tourism experiencescapes can be designed to foster tourist well-being. It addresses limited understanding of how hybrid physical–digital service environments can operate as well-being-oriented transformative systems beyond technological enhancement and engagement. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts an integrative conceptual approach because phygital transformative tourism experiencescapes constitute an emergent, multidisciplinary and theoretically fragmented domain. It synthesizes customer experience, tourist well-being and service research through thematic clustering to clarify relationships among service environments, tourists’ interpretive processes and well-being-oriented transformation. This synthesis generates six framework elements: experiencescape stimuli, decoding mechanisms, experience types, transformative mechanisms, well-being outcomes and experiential marketing as a design layer. Findings The paper proposes a Stimulus–Experience–Well-being framework. Phygital experiencescape stimuli are interpreted through sensoriality, cognition, affectivity, sociability, conativity, pragmatism and lifestyle alignment mechanisms, producing experience types such as immersion, refreshment, reflection, volunteering, challenge, education, entertainment, soci…

title: The Importance of Supply Chain Strategy in Logistics Service Delivery: An Exploratory Study from the Libyan Perspective
abstract: This study examines how supply chain management can enhance logistics service delivery in Libya. Drawing on recent literature and comparative evidence from the MENA region and Africa, it explores how supply chain strategies influence logistics performance in developing countries facing infrastructure, regulatory, and operational challenges. A qualitative approach is adopted, synthesizing academic studies, case examples, and regional analyses to demonstrate how supply chains can improve logistics services. The results show that Libya faces significant infrastructure deficiencies, fragmented regulatory frameworks, and conflict-related disruptions, which hinder effective strategic integration. However, adopting supply chain management practices, effective leadership, and partnerships can help develop competitive advantages. The study identifies significant gaps in logistics infrastructure, especially in ports and supply chain systems, while noting Libya’s strategically important geographic location. Recommendations focus on strengthening institutions, investing in digital technology, developing a skilled workforce, and improving regulatory and policy frameworks to enhance supply chain resilience and effectiveness. This research contributes to the limited work on supply chain management in conflict-affected developing countries. It provides practical insights for policymakers, logi…

title: Ionic Potential Regulation Coupled with Multiphase Sodium Storage Engineering for Advanced Cathode Materials
abstract: Abstract Currently, the intercalated MoSe2 acts as a heterogeneous engineering regulator to modulate the electronic structure of Na3V2(PO4)3 (NVP). By regulating the amount of MoO2 added, we effectively control the coating morphology of MoSe2 on the NVP surface, successfully preparing the flocculent NVP@MoSe2-2 sample. Ex situ XRD/XPS analysis elucidate that the decomposition of MoSe2 under high-voltage stimulation generates Mo4+ and Se2–. With the higher ionic potential of Mo4+ (6.15 Å–1 vs. 4.69 Å–1 of V3+), trace Mo4+ substitution for V3+ results in charge rearrangement, suggesting an increase in the electron-cloud density around Mo4+ and therefore the emergence of electronic delocalization effects of V3+. The modified V reveals stronger coordination properties and electrochemical activity, as confirmed by XAFS. Partial V4+ oxidizes Mo4+ to activate the extra redox couple of Mo4+/Mo5+, forming the second reversible discharge plateau at 3.9 V, further increasing the capacity and energy density. Meanwhile, the intercalated MoSe2 could provide rich reactive sites for Na+ to produce the intermediate solid-solution phase of NaxMoSe2, elevating reversible capacity. Furthermore, DFT calculations demonstrate that the NVP/MoSe2 heterostructure exhibits a zero-band-gap electronic structure and modified charge rearrangement, indicating its superior electronic structure. Finally, the mo…

title: P2RY11–SIRT1–PGC-1α–dependent mitochondrial redox and bioenergetic regulation of macrophages drives fin regeneration in zebrafish
abstract: Abstract Background Tissue regeneration is an energy-intensive process that requires coordinated mitochondrial bioenergetics and redox homeostasis. Extracellular ATP is rapidly released after tissue injury, but how ATP-derived signals support regenerative repair remains incompletely understood. Here, we investigated whether the purinergic receptor P2RY11 regulates macrophage mitochondrial metabolism and thereby promotes tissue regeneration. Methods Using zebrafish caudal fin regeneration as an in vivo model, we examined regenerative outgrowth, cell proliferation, macrophage accumulation and migration, mitochondrial function, redox status, and metabolic gene expression in p2ry11 -deficient larvae. Genetic ablation and pharmacological inhibition of P2RY11 were combined with macrophage depletion and pathway rescue experiments targeting the SIRT1–PGC-1α axis and PPARγ signaling. Results Loss or inhibition of p2ry11 markedly impaired caudal fin regeneration, reduced injury-induced cell proliferation, and decreased macrophage migratory capacity and accumulation at the wound site. Mechanistically, p2ry11 deficiency disrupted systemic mitochondrial metabolic and redox homeostasis, as evidenced by a reduced NAD⁺/NADH ratio and decreased PGC-1α expression. Importantly, cell-resolved analyses further revealed mitochondrial depolarization, increased mtROS accumulation, and reduced ATP leve…

title: Delineation of hazardous regions in the unit hypercube: A copula-based approximation for the identification of low-frequency compound occurrences
abstract: Abstract The probabilistic characterization of compound extreme events, defined as those arising from the joint action of several (generally dependent) drivers, is a central problem in engineering hydrology and water resources. The copula-based scenarios customarily used in the literature (i.e., OR, AND, Kendall, and survival Kendall) summarize multivariate risk by tracing a single boundary in the unit hypercube and assigning to it a target probability, or equivalently a return period. Except for the rectangular OR and AND cases, the prescribed probability attaches to the bounding layer rather than to the hazardous region itself, which is then determined only implicitly. Moreover, the marginal exceedance rates of the drivers are fixed by the level of the critical layer and cannot be set independently. Here we introduce a copula-based approximation that characterizes the hazardous region directly as a full-dimensional set to which the target exceedance frequency is attached. The boundary of this set consists of linear segments meeting at a vertex at the point of maximum curvature of an equiprobability surface of the copula. Crucially, the per-variable exceedance rates are predefined by the user, so that application-specific marginal rates are reconciled with the joint target within a single region, allowing asymmetric compound occurrences (e.g., high discharge under moderate coa…

title: Histone lactylation mediates the regulation of dental follicle cells' senescence driven by RUNX2 during the process of tooth eruption
abstract: Abstract Cleidocranial dysplasia (CCD), an autosomal dominant disorder caused by RUNX2 mutation, is characterized by delayed or failed eruption of the permanent teeth; however, the pathogenesis of tooth impaction remains unclear. Tooth eruption is a complex developmental process in which the dental follicle plays a crucial role. Although the dental follicle is known to coordinate osteoclastogenesis and osteogenesis, the precise cellular mechanisms that initiate eruption are still not fully defined. Moreover, how dental follicles activate the signals of tooth eruption and whether the other biological alterations occur in CCD dental follicles have not been reported. Previous work from our group demonstrated that RUNX2 mutations inhibit dental follicle cell senescence in CCD patients. Cellular senescence participates in diverse physiological and pathological processes and is increasingly implicated as a dynamic regulator of morphogenesis and tissue remodeling. This study investigates whether the senescence of dental follicle cells (DFCs) critically mediates tooth eruption and elucidates its underlying regulatory mechanism. Analysis of dental follicle tissues showed a significant reduction in SA-β-gal-positive and P16 INK4a -positive cells in CCD patients compared with healthy controls. Animal studies revealed a progressive accumulation of senescent cells in the dental follicle dur…

title: Applied Voltage Regulation of Pollutant Removal and Electrochemical Response in a Microbial Electrolysis Cell–microbial Fuel Cell Coupled Constructed Wetland
Yap1 mediates miR-143 regulation of ovarian estrogen synthesis in Larimichthys crocea‌
Drought, thermal response, and climate-patterning in cuticular conductance of the widespread C4 grass Themeda triandra
abstract: Grasslands underpin global biodiversity, carbon storage, and ecosystem resilience. However, grasslands are increasingly threatened by rising temperatures and water scarcity, making it essential to understand physiological responses to drought and heat to sustain their function under future climates. We investigated intraspecific variation in minimum cuticular conductance after stomatal closure (gmin) and its thermal response (phase transition temperature; Tp) in six Australian accessions of Themeda triandra spanning a broad climatic gradient. We also tested whether gmin and its response to drought reflected climate-at-origin. Plants were grown under well-watered glasshouse conditions and then exposed to a short-term drought. We measured gmin of control and droughted plants and assessed gmin responses to increasing temperature (30–55°C) using fresh, fully hydrated leaves (well-watered). Climatic data from accession origin were used to examine trait−environment relationships. Under well-watered conditions, gmin was unrelated to climate-at-origin. However, under drought, gmin was lower in accessions from cooler and wetter regions, contrary to expectations, with drought effects varying strongly among accessions. gmin generally decreased with temperature, and no accession showed a distinct Tp, indicating thermally stable leaf cuticles in this species. These findings reveal intraspec…

title: Preliminary Impact and Injury Response of Varied Anthropometry Postmortem Human Surrogates in Frontal Sled Tests
abstract: <div>Robust restraint system design requires effectiveness across varied anthropometries. Biofidelity reference datasets of postmortem human surrogates (PMHS), a necessary component of informing and assessing restraint system design, exist for the midsize males and small females, but there is limited research for other anthropometries such as the midsize female and obese populations. The goal of this study was to evaluate the kinematic and injury response of midsize female, elderly midsize female, obese female, and obese male PMHS in upright frontal impacts in a simplified restraint environment. The test condition in this study was a full-frontal 30 km/h impact. The test fixture consisted of a rigid seat, knee bolster, footpan, a custom 3 kN shoulder belt force limiter, and separate shoulder and lap belts. Twelve tests were performed with PMHS of varied anthropometries: three per occupant type (midsize female, elderly midsize female, obese female, and obese male). The restraint environment limited the movement of the lower extremities, isolating the thoracic response. Shoulder belt lengths and positioning varied by occupant type. Peak shoulder belt force values ranged between 2.8 and 4.4 kN. Differences in soft tissue distribution (including the hips, abdomen, and breasts) affected both the pre-test path of the shoulder belt on the thorax and the belt’s subsequent motion relati…

title: Reservoir stress sensitivity and its influence on pressure response characteristics in deep fractured-vuggy reservoirs: a case study of the X deep fractured-vuggy reservoir
Koopman-enhanced offline reinforcement learning for robust multi-echelon inventory control under demand distribution shift
abstract: Purpose Multi-echelon inventory optimization (MEIO) under demand distribution shift remains an open challenge in supply chain management. Classical rule-based policies are effective when calibrated online but cannot exploit historical data structure. This paper investigates whether a Koopman operator world model, applied as a structured latent dynamics model within an offline reinforcement learning (RL) framework, can improve the out-of-distribution (OOD) robustness of learned inventory policies and reduce temporal difference (TD)-target variance during training. Design/methodology/approach We propose Koopman-enhanced Multi-Echelon Inventory Optimization (K-MEIO), a two-stage framework combining a Deep Koopman World Model (DKWM) with Implicit Q-Learning (IQL). The DKWM learns a finite-dimensional linear embedding of the multi-echelon inventory dynamics, enabling analytically tractable TD targets with 12.4% lower variance than direct next-state encoding. The Koopman-enhanced Implicit Q-Learning policy is trained entirely on simulated offline transitions calibrated from University of California, Irvine Online Retail and Rossmann Store Sales demand statistics. Ablation experiments across five expectile values, three training seeds, and three OOD stress scenarios are reported, together with full cost breakdowns. Findings Under standard evaluation, K-MEIO achieves service level 0.99…

title: Management, Survivorship, and Supportive Care in Early-Onset Colorectal Cancer
Riskiyani System Dynamics-Based Assessment of Climate Resilience among Milkfish Aquaculture Households in Sibulue District, Bone Regency
abstract: Climate change increasingly threatens aquaculture livelihoods through extreme weather events, seasonal variability, and production uncertainty, potentially undermining household resilience and enterprise sustainability. This study aimed to assess aquaculture household resilience to climate change and evaluate alternative adaptation policies using a System Dynamics approach in Sibulue District, Bone Regency, Indonesia. A mixed-methods approach was employed involving 30 aquaculture households. Quantitative data were analyzed descriptively to construct resilience indicators, while qualitative findings were used to identify key factors and relationships influencing household resilience. These findings were integrated into a System Dynamics simulation model developed using Vensim to evaluate alternative policy scenarios. The overall household resilience index was 53.87, indicating a moderately resilient condition. The resilience perception index was 54.38, while the dependency resilience index reached 60.25 and was classified as resilient. The climate change adaptation and recovery adaptation indices were 47.08 and 53.75, respectively, both indicating moderately resilient conditions. Simulation results indicated that alternative policy scenarios generated different projected trajectories of household resilience and aquaculture enterprise sustainability under changing climatic condit…

title: Influence of Growth Mindset, Time Management, and Academic Self-Efficacy on Academic Achievement
abstract: This study examines the influence of growth mindset, time management, and academic self-efficacy on students’ academic achievement. Grounded in the theoretical perspectives of Carol Dweck’s mindset theory and Albert Bandura’s social cognitive theory, the research aims to explore how cognitive beliefs, behavioral strategies, and motivational factors contribute to academic performance. A quantitative research design was employed, utilizing a structured survey questionnaire administered to a sample of students. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and multiple regression techniques. The findings reveal that all three independent variables significantly and positively predict academic achievement, with academic self-efficacy emerging as the strongest predictor, followed by time management and growth mindset. The model explains a substantial proportion of variance in academic performance, highlighting the combined importance of psychological and behavioral factors in educational success. The study contributes to the existing literature by integrating multiple theoretical frameworks into a single model and providing empirical evidence of their combined effects. The findings suggest that educational interventions aimed at enhancing students’ self-efficacy, fostering a growth mindset, and improving time management skills can significantly improve acade…

title: Design of an adaptive lower limb rehabilitation system with virtual reality and multimodal biosignals
abstract: Abstract Objectives To develop and evaluate a virtual-reality-enhanced lower-limb rehabilitation framework that combines EEG-based motor-intention detection, robotic gait assistance, trunk-motion assessment, and lumbar surface electromyography to support multimodal assessment, interactive training, and therapist-oriented performance monitoring. Methods Nine healthy participants completed VR-enhanced EEG motor-imagery training, open-loop calibration, closed-loop exoskeleton-triggering, trunk-attitude assessment, and lumbar-sEMG evaluation in separate experimental sessions. A four-degree-of-freedom hip–knee exoskeleton was integrated with participant-specific CDF threshold calibration, treadmill synchronization, VR rehabilitation tasks, attitude sensing, and RMS/MPF analysis. Participant identity was consistent across modalities, although the signals were not acquired simultaneously. Results The seated VR motor-imagery condition produced the highest open-loop command accuracy of 75.35 ± 4.21 %. Mean closed-loop gait-triggering accuracy was 76.7 ± 10.0 %, ranging from 60 % to 90 %. Mean trunk-movement magnitudes were 30.8°, 30.7°, 91.3°, and 31.0° for left lateral flexion, right lateral flexion, forward flexion, and backward extension, respectively. System prompting increased mean RMS from 0.094759 to 0.103330 mV and reduced mean MPF from 111.2023 to 103.0729 Hz. Conclusions The f…

title: Exploring Reform in a Progressive, Project-Driven Deep Learning Practical Course: A Case Study of an Intelligent Image Classification System
abstract: Addressing issues such as fragmented laboratory sessions, a disconnect between theory and practice, and one-dimensional assessment methods in deep learning practical courses, this paper explores a progressive, project-driven teaching reform centered on the iterative development of an “intelligent image classification system.” The course restructured scattered experiments into four progressive projects focused on modeling from scratch, transfer learning, few-shot fine-tuning, and competition practice. By aligning with the competency requirements of the Lanqiao Cup competition, it promoted the integration of competition and coursework. The implementation incorporated AI programming assistants and large language models, while the evaluation established a five-dimensional formative assessment system covering the project process, use of AI tools, technical competence, final defense, and personal growth portfolios. Pilot results show that all four projects met the predetermined requirements. Students’ engineering practice skills and technical decision-making abilities have significantly improved, and the competition pass rate exceeded historical levels, providing a valuable reference for reforming similar practical courses.

title: Social media engagement and participation intention in humanitarian logistics contexts: the mediating role of trust
abstract: Purpose As humanitarian organizations increasingly rely on digital platforms to engage and mobilize the public, this study aims to draw on the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S–O–R) framework to examine how social media engagement and perceived logistics efficiency are associated with participation intention, with trust as the internal evaluative mechanism. Design/methodology/approach A cross-sectional survey of 574 social media users in Egypt with prior exposure to humanitarian organizations’ online content was analyzed using confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modeling in IBM AMOS. Indirect associations were estimated using 5,000 bootstrap resamples with bias-corrected and percentile 95% confidence intervals. Findings Trust was positively associated with participation intention. Social media engagement was associated with intention mainly through the direct pathway; its small indirect effect through trust was significant under bias-corrected but not percentile bootstrap intervals. Perceived logistics efficiency had a significant total association with intention but no significant direct association; approximately 94% of its total association ran through trust, although this indirect effect was not statistically significant at the 95% level. Practical implications Humanitarian organizations should manage social media as a participation pathway, combining interacti…
venue: Journal of Humanitarian Logistics and Supply Chain Management

title: Caught in the crossfire: Geopolitical risk and firm performance, and the lifeline of risk management and sustainability strategies
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to test the adverse impact of geopolitical risk (GP_RISK) on firm performance and to examine whether risk management and sustainability strategies mitigate this relationship in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries. Design/methodology/approach The study sample comprises 6140 firm-year observations from non-financial listed firms from 2013 to 2024. Consistent with prior studies, the study uses a system GMM estimator to address endogeneity and heterogeneity issues in panel data, ensuring consistent and efficient estimates. Findings The study shows that heightened GP_RISK significantly reduces firm performance in the GCC, negatively affecting both return on assets (ROA) and Tobin’s Q. The adverse effect is stronger for ROA, indicating that geopolitical shocks transmit more immediately through operational channels, including higher adjustment costs, supply-chain disruptions and operational inefficiencies. The negative impact on Tobin’s Q reflects investors’ concerns regarding future performance and risk exposure. The findings further show that geographical diversification (GEO_DIV) intensifies the adverse effect of GP_RISK, while hedging does not significantly mitigate it. In contrast, environmental, social and governance performance reduces the negative impact of GP_RISK, driven primarily by the governance dimension. Originality/value This study cont…

title: Creative Math Preneurship Learning Model to Enhance Students' Creative Thinking and Educational Innovation Management
abstract: Mathematics education in higher education requires learning that integrates mathematical creative thinking skills with the capacity to develop and manage innovation. An initial diagnostic study indicated that most students still experience difficulties in solving non-routine problems, particularly in the originality aspect. The importance of equipping prospective mathematics educators with applied reasoning and innovation management in the digital socio-economic era, along with the fact that students' creative cognitive abilities remain low, forms the background of this research. This study aims to develop the Math-Preneurship Creative learning model and to evaluate its validity, practicality, and changes in mathematical creative thinking ability after its implementation. This research employed the Research and Development (R&D) method with the Plomp development model, and the product quality criteria referred to validity, practicality, and effectiveness. Validation involved four experts, while the field trial was conducted with 38 fourth-semester students of the Mathematics Education Study Program at Universitas PGRI Semarang using a One-Group Pretest-Posttest Design. Data were collected through validation sheets, a mathematical creative thinking test (α = 0.86; ICC = 0.88), an innovation management rubric based on the nine elements of the Business Model Canvas (α = 0.89), and…

title: Foreign Exchange Risk Management for Chinese Portable Energy Storage Exporters: The Huabao New Energy Case
abstract: Chinese portable energy storage exporters face foreign exchange risk arising from differences between the currencies of production costs and overseas revenues, together with uncertainty in transaction timing and cash collection. This study examines foreign exchange risk management at Huabao New Energy through a qualitative case analysis of publicly disclosed financial information and relevant literature. Drawing on enterprise risk management and principal–agent perspectives, alongside hedge accounting requirements, the analysis considers how exposure measurement, hedging decisions, accounting treatment, and governance support interact. It highlights the importance of distinguishing year-end foreign-currency monetary exposure from forecast cash-flow exposure, annual derivative transactions from outstanding contracts, and economic hedging from the application of hedge accounting. A proposed management framework integrates currency- and maturity-specific exposure measurement, exposure-matched hedging, appropriate accounting treatment, and continuous monitoring, supported by internal controls, managerial incentives, and integrated treasury information. The study provides a practical framework for evaluating foreign exchange risk management in export-oriented manufacturers. However, public disclosures alone cannot establish deficiencies in internal procedures or managerial motivatio…
venue: Journal of Economics and Management Sciences

title: Sustainable Thermoplastic Thermal Interface Adhesive Derived from Poly(lipoic acid) and Boron Nitride for Efficient Electronic Thermal Management
abstract: Abstract The escalating power density of electronics demands thermal interface materials (TIMs) that simultaneously offer high thermal conductivity, strong adhesion, and environmental sustainability. Conventional thermally conductive adhesives (TCAs) face inherent trade-offs among these properties, often relying on non-recyclable thermosets. Here, we present a sustainable thermoplastic TCA composed of a poly(lipoic acid) (polyLA)-based dynamic polymer matrix integrated with polyvinylpyrrolidone-modified hexagonal boron nitride (BN@PVP). The polyLA matrix incorporates catechol moieties and reversible Fe3+-carboxyl/catechol coordination bonds, creating a dynamically reconfigurable network. This design yields an adhesive (LD50Fe100) with high toughness (1.52 MJ m–3), and strong lap shear adhesion (884 kPa on PMMA and 1210 kPa on steel). The dynamic bonds enable room-temperature self-healing (93.1% efficiency) and robust recyclability. At a BN@PVP loading of 40 wt %, the composite (BN@LD50Fe100) achieves a thermal conductivity of 1.2 W m–1 K–1 while maintaining enhanced mechanical properties. LED chip heat dissipation experiments demonstrate a 4 °C lower operating temperature compared to devices without a TIM, with stable thermal performance over multiple cycles. This work provides a promising material strategy to overcome the traditional trade-offs in TCAs, offering a path toward …

title: De minimis at scale: legal thresholds and the political visibility of programmed compliance
abstract: Purpose This paper examines how legal thresholds generate field-level coordination among organization-specific decision premises and how programmed compliance becomes politically consequential at industrial scale. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on Luhmann's systems theory, we analyse the US de minimis customs exemption ($800 threshold, 2016–2025) using aggregated public shipment data (1.36 billion packages by 2024), systematic patent searches across logistics firms and regulatory documents. We show how a legal rule operating within the conditional programming of customs determinations produces an exemption status that participating organizations reconstruct as linked, system-specific decision premises. These premises connect with purposive programmes through shared governmental and commercial infrastructure rather than firm-specific innovation. Findings Customs authorities processed the statutory criterion through Automated Commercial Environment and communicated an exempt or dutiable status; carriers, brokers and e-commerce platforms reconstructed that status within organizational programmes of the form IF exempt, THEN select routine n. No Section 321-specific patent was identified, corroborating parametric absorption into existing governmental and commercial systems. Entry Type 86 provides affirmative evidence of continual administrative and organizational adaptation. Pa…

title: Sustainable water resource management in Ghana: evidence on the determinants of renewable freshwater resources
abstract: Purpose Although Ghana is not classified as a water-scarce economy, its renewable freshwater resources per capita have declined over the years, raising concerns about long-term water security. This study examines the climatic-, technological-, economic- and urbanization-related determinants of renewable internal freshwater resources in Ghana. Design/methodology/approach Annual World Bank data spanning 1971–2023 were analysed using Fully Modified Ordinary Least Squares (FMOLS) and Canonical Cointegrating Regression (CCR) techniques to estimate long-run determinants of renewable freshwater resources. Findings Precipitation, water productivity, natural resources and manufacturing growth are positively associated with renewable freshwater resources, while agricultural growth and temperature have negative effects. A 1% increase in these variables is associated with changes of 0.001%, 0.457%, 0.015%, 0.016%, −0.011% and −0.088%, respectively. Economic growth and urbanization exhibit positive coefficients, while their squared terms are negative, indicating non-linear relationships with renewable freshwater resources. However, their estimated turning points are below the observed sample range. Furthermore, marginal effects evaluated at the minimum, mean and maximum levels are negative, indicating that economic growth and urbanization reduce renewable freshwater resources across the obs…

title: Broken production system, strong community: disaster management experiences of livestock farmers after the 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquakes
abstract: Purpose Livestock systems are fundamental to food security, yet post-disaster recovery research frequently overlooks agriculture. On 6 February 2023, two earthquakes struck south-eastern Türkiye and northern Syria, devastating a region central to national livestock production. This study examines how farmers experienced the disaster, managed disruptions and navigated recovery. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative descriptive design captured the experiences of 21 affected livestock farmers through semi-structured interviews in May 2024. Data were analysed via reflexive thematic analysis with data triangulation, and interpreted through global disaster frameworks including the Livestock Emergency Guidelines and Standards and the Five Domains Model. Findings The central concept “Broken Production System, Strong Community” captures failures participants described across shelter, water, feed, labour and market access, alongside production decline, distress sales and compromised animal welfare. Participants reported that formal aid meaningfully supported registered farmers, that uneven distribution and bureaucratic hurdles limited access for others, and that informal social networks substantially compensated for these limitations; the small insured subset linked coverage to deeper recovery. Originality/value Addressing an empirical gap on livestock recovery after a mega-earthquak…

title: Impact Of Tiktok Review Overclaim On Consumer Trust and Repurchase Intention Of Generation Z
abstract: This paper provides an empirical investigation intothe impact of promotional overclaims in TikTokvideo reviews on consumer trust and repurchaseintention among Generation Z undergraduatestudents. Grounded in Source Credibility Theory andExpectancy Disconfirmation Theory, a quantitative causal research design was implemented. Primarydata were gathered through a structured onlinequestionnaire administered to 100 activeundergraduate students in the Digital Business study program at Universitas Kristen Satya Wacana who had experienced product discrepancies following purchases driven by TikTok reviews. Data analysiswas executed using simple linear regressionmodeling in IBM SPSS Statistics. The empirical findings demonstrated that promotional overclaimsin TikTok video reviews exerted a statisticallysignificant negative influence on consumer trust (B =0.868, t = 16.406, p = 0.000), accounting for 73.3 percent of the variance in consumer trust erosion. Furthermore, review overclaims exerted a statistically significant negative impact on repurchase intention (B = 0.918, t = 17.765, p =0.000), explaining 76.3 percent of the variance inrepurchase reluctance. Descriptive statisticalanalyses revealed high mean scores for perceivedoverclaim (4.196), consumer skepticism (4.056), andrepurchase reluctance (4.178). These findings confirm that deceptive promotional exaggerations severely damage cr…

title: HD 152384: A 5-megayear-old debris disk system showing a gaseous ring of refractory elements at the dust sublimation radius
abstract: Circumstellar gas around young stars provides key insights into planet formation and disk evolution. HD,152384, a young (5 Myr) A0,V star in Sco-Cen, exhibits hybrid disk characteristics with a modest infrared excess due to small dust grains and atomic emission lines dominated by refractory elements, but the disk's structure and origin remain unclear. We aim to characterise the kinematics and excitation of the circumstellar gas around HD,152384, and to constrain the physical properties of the emitting region. We used new optical and near-infrared high spectral resolution data from the Ultraviolet and Visual Echelle Spectrograph (UVES) and CRyogenic high-resolution InfraRed Echelle Spectrograph (CRIRES) instruments at the Very Large Telescope to revisit the circumstellar environment of HD,152384. Earlier studies suggested the presence of a broad, gas-rich circumstellar disk; here, we re-examine this scenario. -1 $ peak separation. Modelling of gas in Keplerian rotation indicates that the gas is confined to a geometrically thin ring at a radial distance of 0.09--0.12 au from the central star, close to the dust sublimation radius (0.10--0.14 au, assuming a dust sublimation temperature of ∼1500 K). title: Challenges faced by librarians in private universities in Malawi
abstract: Purpose University libraries serve as vital hubs for knowledge dissemination, research support, and academic excellence. However, librarians in private universities in Malawi face significant challenges that hinder their effectiveness in fulfilling these roles. Despite the mushrooming of private universities in recent years, little research has been conducted on the specific challenges faced by librarians working in these institutions. This study investigated these challenges, explored librarians' perceptions of their work environment, and identified possible solutions. Design/methodology/approach Guided by a pragmatic worldview, the study employed a mixed-methods approach, utilising in-depth interviews and structured questionnaires to collect data from 15 librarians drawn from 15 private universities in Malawi. Purposive sampling was used, and findings were analysed using thematic and descriptive analysis. Institutional Theory and Herzberg's Two-Factor Theory framed the study, highlighting both structural and motivational aspects affecting librarianship. Findings The findings revealed that financial constraints, lack of institutional support, low salaries, and limited professional development opportunities were the primary challenges. Librarians perceived private universities as offering a more personalised and creativity-enhancing environment, yet such institutions often prov…

title: Thoracic Biomechanical Responses of Small Female Postmortem Human Subjects in a Simplified Side-Impact Condition
abstract: <div>Biomechanical response targets for the thorax have largely focused on the 50th percentile male, limiting their relevance for smaller females. Previous studies have provided side-impact female postmortem human subjects (PMHS) data from either oversimplified or realistic boundary conditions. This study aimed to generate thoracic biomechanical responses of small female PMHS in a simplified side-impact condition with realistic components and compare responses between two input energy levels. Twelve small female PMHS were seated on a simplified seat with FMVSS No. 213a seat foam and fabric and impacted once on the left thorax with either a 14.0 kg (low energy) or 23.7 kg (high energy) pneumatic impactor at 4.5 m/s. A rectangular impactor face (22.9 × 25.4 cm) covered with FMVSS No. 213a armrest foam simulated an intruding door panel. Thoracic deflection was measured using a chestband. Inertially compensated force was recorded via a load cell. Spinal kinematics were captured using six-degree-of-freedom motion blocks. Biomechanical responses were compared between groups using two-sample t-tests. The high-energy group exhibited significantly higher peak forces (2.5 vs. 1.9 kN, p = 0.0001), greater thoracic deflections (41.0 vs. 33.9 mm, p = 0.016), and increased deformation energy (91.6 vs. 61.0 J, p = 0.0001). Effective stiffness did not differ significantly between groups (p = 0…

Workplace benign envy and employee outcomes: the mediating role of a leader’s knowledge-sharing behaviour on innovative work behaviour and workplace well-being among nurses
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the effect of benign envy in the workplace on innovative work behaviour and well-being among nurses, and to test the mediating role of leaders' knowledge-sharing behaviour in these relationships. Design/methodology/approach A cross-sectional survey was used to collect data from 518 nurses working at a public hospital in Turkey. The mediation model was examined using SPSS, AMOS and PROCESS Macro (Model 4). Findings The results suggest that workplace benign envy is positively and significantly associated with innovative work behaviour and workplace well-being (r = 0.508 and r = 0.382, respectively). Furthermore, it was observed that benign envy significantly influences the leader’s information-sharing behaviour. Mediation analyses revealed that the leader’s knowledge-sharing behaviour plays a significant role in these relationships. It is therefore concluded that the indirect effect of benign envy on innovative work behaviour is significant (β = 0.059), although this effect remains relatively limited. Conversely, the indirect effect on workplace well-being was found to be stronger (β = 0.109), indicating a moderate mediating effect. Originality/value The findings indicate that a leader’s support for knowledge sharing is a crucial variable in determining the impact of envy on employees. Furthermore, it is observed that in a supportive environment…

title: Comparison of Pelvis Injury Patterns and Loading Mechanisms in Postmortem Human Subject Tests and Real-World Side-Impact Collisions
abstract: <div>Pelvis fractures can be complex and occur in many different regions of the bone. Loading due to side impact can transfer anteriorly through the pubic symphysis and posteriorly through the sacroiliac joint. Virtual testing with human body models (HBMs) has the potential to capture the complex loading mechanisms that contribute to pelvis fractures, but injury prediction with HBMs must be refined and validated using physical test data. Most postmortem human subject (PMHS) studies testing side-impact and pelvic injuries use simplified test modes rather than simulating realistic boundary conditions. It is important to understand the differences between pelvis fractures resulting from in-lab tests and those sustained in real-world collisions, particularly for when these PMHS tests are used in injury risk function development to predict injuries caused by collisions in the real world. This study seeks to compare injury types and loading mechanisms from existing PMHS tests to those observed in real-world side-impact collisions from Crash Injury Research and Engineering Network (CIREN) to examine their suitability for refining HBM injury prediction for the pelvis. Seventy-seven percent of PMHS tests with injuries had fractures in the anterior region of the pelvis, 23% in the iliac wing, 30% in the sacroiliac region, and 16% in the acetabulum, where a PMHS test could have fractures …

Price conflicts and housing price volatility in the United States
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine whether the newly constructed price conflict index (PCI) has predictive value for housing price volatility across the 50 US states and Washington D.C. This study would determine whether price conflict significantly predicts volatility after controlling for market momentum and state-level economic conditions, to test whether a PCI-augmented model improves out-of-sample forecasting accuracy relative to standard benchmarks and to identify the transmission channels driving this relationship, and inform investors, policymakers and other stakeholders about housing market risk. Design/methodology/approach This study uses quarterly panel data from 1976 to 2023 across all 50 US states and Washington D.C. A newly constructed PCI is used as a predictor of housing price volatility, with models controlling for historical market momentum and state-level economic conditions. Predictive performance is evaluated using out-of-sample forecasting tests across semiannual, annual and biennial horizons, benchmarked against baseline models. Panel regression analysis is then applied to confirm the nationwide significance of the PCI–volatility relationship and to identify the primary transmission channels linking price conflict to housing volatility. Findings PCI significantly and positively predicts housing price volatility across most US states, even after controllin…

title: Systematic framework for ARIMA and SARIMA model selection using multiple error metrics: An application to export forecasting
abstract: This study proposes a systematic and practical framework for selecting autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) and seasonal autoregressive integrated moving average (SARIMA) forecasting models based on multiple error evaluation metrics, including root mean square error (RMSE), mean absolute percentage error (MAPE), and mean absolute error (MAE). In practical forecasting applications, different error metrics often produce conflicting model selection outcomes, resulting in uncertainty in decision-making. Accordingly, this study introduces a percentage-based consistency evaluation approach to identify the most reliable forecasting model across multiple datasets. This study proposes a systematic framework for ARIMA and SARIMA model selection that integrates multiple forecasting error metrics to address conflicting model rankings and improve the consistency of model-selection decisions. This framework is applied to Thailand’s export value data, consisting of 69 monthly observations across 12 datasets derived from major industrial product groups (HS-84, HS-85, and HS-87) and key trading partners, including China, Japan, and South Korea. Results indicate that ARIMA(1,2,1) achieves the highest level of consistency across error metrics, with 83.33% under RMSE and 75% under MAPE and MAE. In terms of seasonal models, SARIMA (2,2,2)(2,0,0)₁₂ demonstrates the best overall performan…

title: Choosing Cardiovascular Assessment and Risk-Prediction Tools Across the Care Pathway
abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, making accurate and efficient risk stratification essential across the care pathway. Numerous tools support emergency triage, disease assessment, procedural decision-making, long-term prevention, atrial fibrillation management, and evaluation of functional status, but no single model is applicable across all clinical settings or populations. This clinician-oriented review categorizes and critically compares commonly used cardiovascular assessment and risk-prediction tools, including History, Electrocardiogram, Age, Risk factors, Troponin, Global Registry of Acute Coronary Events, and Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction for emergency triage; Agatston, Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis, and Synergy Between Percutaneous Coronary Intervention with Taxus and Cardiac Surgery for anatomical and clinical assessment; European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation, Society of Thoracic Surgeons, and Revised Cardiac Risk Index, for procedural risk; and Framingham, the pooled cohort equations implemented in the Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease, Risk Estimator, Systematic Coronary Risk Evaluation 2, QResearch Cardiovascular Risk Algorithm 3, and Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease EVENTs for long-term prediction. Congestive heart failure, hypertension, age ≥75, diabetes, stroke/trans…

title: Regression-based prediction of JCAPL transport parameters and sound absorption in microslit architected porous absorbers
abstract: Microscale numerical approaches can predict the acoustic properties of periodic porous absorbers from unit-cell geometries. However, evaluating the transport parameters typically requires microscale computations, limiting their straightforward use in rapid absorber design. In this study, a regression-based framework was developed to predict sound absorption in a microslit architected porous absorber (Microslit-APA) consisting of simple-cubic unit cells with embedded microslits. The eight transport parameters required in the Johnson–Champoux–Allard–Pride–Lafarge (JCAPL) model were obtained for systematically varied slit configurations by solving local viscous and thermal problems within the unit cell. Five parameters showing systematic dependence on the slit geometry were represented by nonlinear regression models using two geometric descriptors: the aperture ratio and a composite index combining slit number and height. The remaining three parameters were determined directly from the unit-cell geometry or assigned representative values within the investigated domain. This framework enables all eight JCAPL parameters and the normal-incidence sound absorption coefficient to be determined without repeated microscale calculations for each new configuration. Predictions were validated against direct numerical calculations and impedance-tube measurements of 3D-printed specimens, showi…

Water-Balance Physics-Informed Neural Network for Daily Streamflow Prediction: A Single-Catchment Comparative Study Using CAMELS-GB v2
abstract: Accurate daily streamflow prediction remains challenging because rainfall–runoff dynamics are nonlinear, temporally dependent, and subject to water-mass conservation. This study examines whether a simplified catchment water-balance constraint improves the internal consistency of a physics-informed neural network (WB-PINN) without compromising predictive accuracy. Using 18,993 daily observations (1970–2022) from Catchment 31010 in CAMELS-GB v2, the WB-PINN jointly estimates discharge, latent storage, and an evapotranspiration scaling factor. Its loss function combines prediction error with a water-balance residual weighted by λ. We evaluated performance on a chronological independent test period (2012–2022) against Ridge regression, support vector regression, XGBoost, a multilayer perceptron, and an LSTM. We tested five physics-loss weights and additional regularization controls to distinguish physical constraints from generic regularization effects. At λ = 0.001, mean validation water-balance loss decreased from 13.69 to 8.22, with nearly unchanged accuracy (NSE 0.8419 versus 0.8433 without the constraint). On the test set, LSTM performed best (NSE 0.8673; RMSE 0.3772 mm/day), while WB-PINN ranked second numerically (NSE 0.8209; RMSE 0.4381 mm/day). Paired bootstrap analysis found no statistically significant differences between WB-PINN and XGBoost or support vector regression,…

The Mechanism of Digital Economy Development on Energy Intensity under the “Dual Carbon” Goals
abstract: Reducing energy intensity has became important in the context of the “dual carbon” goals. Panel data were collected from 30 provinces in China during the period of 2011-2020 to investigate how the digital economy affects energy intensity and the mechanisms underlies. The empirical findings indicate that digital economy development significantly lowers energy intensity. A series of robustness checks confirm that this result is not coincidental. Heterogeneity analysis shows that the energy-reduction effect is more pronounced in non-resource-based provinces and the western region, while varying degrees of heterogeneity are observed in resource‑based provinces and the eastern and central regions. This paper elucidates the intrinsic mechanisms through which the digital economy enhances energy efficiency at the provincial level, providing empirical support and practical insights for promoting coordinated development of digitalization and greening under the “dual carbon” goals, as well as for formulating region‑specific energy transition policies.

title: The “Speed Paradox” of Capability Building: A Study on the Chain Mediation Mechanism of Innovation Capability Affecting the Speed of Enterprise Internationalization
abstract: To explore the impact mechanism of innovation capability on the speed of enterprise internationalization, this study takes China A-share listed companies in manufacturing and software and information technology services from 2012 to 2016 as samples. Based on dynamic capability and organizational learning theory, a chain mediating model of “innovation capability—absorption capability—adaptability—internationalization speed” is constructed, and empirical tests are conducted through regression analysis, Bootstrap testing, and endogeneity treatment. The results show that innovation capability significantly enhances absorption capability, which in turn significantly promotes adaptability, while adaptability has a significant negative impact on internationalization speed. Innovation capability does not have a direct effect on internationalization speed. The chain mediating path is significantly established. This study breaks through the limitation of a single cause, verifies the chain transmission mechanism of absorption capability and adaptability for the first time, fills the gap in the research on the timing of capability transformation, integrates interdisciplinary theories, and provides practical guidance for enterprises to improve their capability systems and differentiate their responses to environmental distance to optimize their internationalization strategies.

title: A gauge theory of turbulence: Higgs mechanism for the Gribov parameter, intermittency and the anomalous dimension of the scalar field
abstract: Abstract We formalize the gauge structure of the Navier–Stokes equation for incompressible fluids, interpreting ∇ ⋅ v = 0 as a gauge fixing analogous to the Coulomb gauge in electromagnetism. We construct the Martin–Siggia–Rose action and its full BRST symmetry, introducing BRST doublets for the Gribov parameter γ and the monodromy phase θ . Through a Higgs mechanism, γ acquires a vacuum expectation value γ 0 , generating a mass scale for the vorticity and the ghosts; we compute the one-loop effective potential and analyze vacuum stability. Intermittency – measured by the exponents ζ n – is described by fluctuations of the Higgs field σ around the condensate, via a Gribov-inspired log-Poisson hierarchy that satisfies exactly ζ 3 = 1 (Kolmogorov’s four-fifths law). A one-parameter fit to the DNS exponents of Gotoh et al. favors filamentary vorticity structures, D f = 1.10 ± 0.15, while a two-parameter fit shows no significant improvement, the ( D f , Δ) plane being degenerate. The one-loop anomalous dimension in d = 3, Δ σ ≈ 0.50, supports the identification D f = 2Δ σ within the fit uncertainty. The formalism unifies classical hydrodynamics with gauge theory and spontaneous symmetry breaking, opening the study of turbulence and intermittency to quantum field theory methods.

title: Phosphate-Modulated Heterojunction to Trigger the Lattice Oxygen Mechanism for Industrial-Scale Water Electrolysis
abstract: Abstract To address the issue of slow kinetics in the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) during industrial hydrogen evolution, phosphate adsorption or intercalation is commonly employed to modulate the electronic structure of electrocatalysts. However, these binding modes suffer from weak interfacial attachment and limited electronic coupling, leading to gradual phosphate leaching under operating potentials and a loss of structural stability in the material. Here we report a surface chemical anchoring strategy that grafts phosphate groups directly onto a Ni–Mo-based heterojunction catalyst (Pi-NiO/Ni/MoO3) via P–O–Ni bonds. The chemically bonded phosphate, synergizing with interfacial charge transfer across the heterojunction, raises the Ni valence state and strengthens metal–oxygen covalency, enhancing stability and lowering the potential required for dynamic surface reconstruction into highly active NiOOH. A series of in situ spectroscopic measurements, differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (DEMS), and density functional theory (DFT) reveal that phosphate modulation shifts the dominant OER pathway from the adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) to the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM), with the 18O/16O ratio establishing a marked increase of 2.03 times. Consequently, Pi-NiO/Ni/MoO3 achieves an industrial-level current density of 500 mA·cm–2 at an overpotential of 359 mV in 1 …

title: Hierarchical porous N/S-Co-doped carbon from coal tar pitch for durable supercapacitors
Failure Tolerance of Male and Female Lower Extremities under Pure Bending and Combined Loading Modes
abstract: Lower extremity injuries remain common in frontal motor vehicle crashes, with evidence suggesting increased vulnerability among female occupants. While prior research has established failure tolerances of midsize male lower extremities under bending and combined loading conditions, limited data exist for small female specimens. This study aimed to characterize and compare the failure tolerance of small female and midsize male postmortem human subject lower leg specimens under combined axial compression and posterior–anterior (PA) bending using consistent boundary conditions. Twenty-four lower leg specimens, including the tibia, fibula, and surrounding soft tissue, were obtained from 50th percentile male (n = 12) and 5th percentile female (n = 12) donors. Dynamic tests to failure were conducted at 1.5 m/s using a test apparatus designed to apply three-point bending in the PA direction with varying levels of superimposed axial compression (0, 2, 4, and 6 kN). When paired left and right legs from the same donor were available, they were assigned to different loading conditions to assess the influence of axial compression magnitude. Fracture timing was determined using force, strain, acoustic emission data, high-speed video, and post-test CT imaging. Results indicated that 18 specimens fractured at the tibial shaft, 5 near the potting interface, and 1 did not fra…

title: Cavity-Filling Calcite in the Deccan Traps as a Natural Analogue for Mineral Carbon Sequestration and Low-Temperature Deformation
abstract: Cavity-filling calcite is among the most widespread secondary phases in the Deccan Traps, and its position late in the amygdale paragenesis, after zeolites and silica phases, is long established. Two questions that remain open are addressed here: whether this calcite retains a mechanical record of deformation imposed after the cavities were sealed, and what a naturally carbonated flood-basalt pile can tell us about the durability of engineered mineral carbon storage. Calcite from three closely spaced amygdaloidal basalt exposures in the district of Maharashtra, Ane Ghat in Junnar taluka, Pune, Shindewadi 1 and Shindewadi 2 in Parner taluka, Ahilyanagar was examined by transmitted-light petrography, scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive X-ray spectrometry (SEM–EDS) and micro-Raman spectroscopy, with growth features deliberately separated from post-growth strain features. All three occurrences comprise coarse, optically continuous calcite grown into open voids: rhombohedral cleavage is perfect, birefringence is extreme, planar crystal faces survive in secondary-electron images, and no replacement front is developed against the basalt wall. Superimposed on this growth fabric are closely spaced polysynthetic e-twin lamellae, undulose extinction, cleavage-controlled intracrystalline microfractures, and healed fractures carrying trails of secondary inclusions. title: Beyond conventional imaging – a full-waveform inversion application with 2D land seismic for Carbon Storage
Synergistic Cu–Zn Dual-Atom Sites in Hierarchically N-Doped Porous Carbon Enable Efficient Rechargeable Zn–Air Batteries
abstract: Abstract Herein, we report an atomically well-defined Cu–Zn dual-atom catalyst featuring isolated Cu–N4 and Zn–N4 moieties embedded in a hierarchical N-doped carbon framework. Through controlled precursor chemistry and defect engineering, the spatial proximity and electronic coupling between the two metal centers are precisely regulated, enabling the construction of stable dual-atom catalytic sites with distinct electronic characteristics. Electrochemical measurements reveal that the optimized CuZn-NC catalyst exhibits enhanced oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) activity, characterized by a positive onset potential (0.99 V) and a half-wave potential (0.88 V), together with excellent durability and methanol tolerance. Combined spectroscopic analyses and density functional theory calculations demonstrate that the cooperative interaction between adjacent Cu–N4 and Zn–N4 sites effectively modulates the adsorption energetics of oxygenated intermediates, thereby lowering the reaction energy barriers and accelerating ORR kinetics. When evaluated as an air cathode, the catalyst further delivers an impressive peak power density of 331.8 mW cm–2 and stable discharge operation over 333 h. This work provides mechanistic insights into dual-metal single-atom cooperation and offers a rational strategy for designing advanced oxygen electrocatalysts.

title: Application of Coconut Shell Activated Carbon for the Adsorption of Toxic Heavy Metals from Wastewater
abstract: Copper and lead are poisonous, non-biodegradable heavy metals that persist in the environment and can cause severe health challenges in the human body. This study investigates the effectiveness of coconut shell activated carbon (CSAC) as an adsorbent for the removal of copper and lead ions from wastewater in a batch mode. The effects of varying operating parameters in the adsorption process namely, initial concentration (10–200 mg/L), pH (2–12), adsorbent dosage (1–5 g) and particle size (75–300 µm) using the central composite design (CCD). The adsorbent was characterised prior to and after adsorption to determine the functional groups, morphological structure and the elemental composition with the aid of Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR), Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) and Energy Dispersive Spectroscopy (EDS) analytical instruments respectively. The analysis of variance (ANOVA) indicated a strong coefficient of determination (R2) for Cu2+ and Pb2+, measuring 0.9761 and 0.9689, respectively. Adsorption of Pb2+ showed higher capacity and stronger affinity than Cu2⁺. Isotherm studies showed that the Langmuir, Temkin, and Dubinin–Radushkevich (D–R) models provided a strong fit for Pb2+ but were significantly less suitable for describing the Cu2+ adsorption data. while kinetics followed pseudo-second order, confirming chemisorption. title: Potential evaluation of low-carbon growing soil synthesized via multi-source solid waste synergy
Estimation of agricultural carbon abatement costs using a marginal-productivity-based production-input model: evidence from Fujian Province, China
abstract: The shadow price of agricultural carbon emissions serves as a key indicator for quantifying the cost of carbon reduction in agriculture and for reflecting the associated opportunity costs. It has substantial theoretical and practical relevance for the green development and low-carbon transformation of agriculture under the dual-carbon goals. It holds significant theoretical and practical value for advancing green development and low-carbon transformation in agriculture under the dual-carbon goals. Drawing on marginal productivity theory, this study classifies agricultural carbon emissions as a production factor, builds a translog production function model, and employs ridge regression to address multicollinearity. Using panel data from nine prefecture-level cities in Fujian Province (2010–2023), we measure the shadow prices of agricultural carbon emissions across cities and conduct robustness tests via stochastic frontier analysis (SFA), exploring spatiotemporal evolutionary patterns and the drivers of regional disparities. The key findings are as follows: (1) Fujian’s agricultural carbon emission shadow prices show an overall sustained upward trend, with the economic opportunity cost of per-unit carbon reduction rising consistently across cities. (2) Significant regional disparities exist—the average shadow prices in eastern and northern Fujian remain among the highest in the …

title: Effect of boron nitride nanoplatelet loading on the thermomechanical performance, thermal stability and X-band electromagnetic interference shielding of carbon-fiber/epoxy laminates
abstract: Abstract Woven carbon-fiber/epoxy laminates containing 0, 0.5, and 2 wt.% boron nitride nanoplatelets (BNNPs), relative to the epoxy resin mass, were fabricated using the same processing route. Their thermomechanical behavior, thermal stability, and X-band electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding were evaluated using dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA), thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), and shielding effectiveness (SE) measurements over 8–12 GHz. At 0.5 wt.% BNNP, the glassy storage modulus ( E ′) increased from 9.3 to 11.2 GPa, and the rubbery plateau modulus increased from 0.33 to 2.1 GPa. The loss factor (tan δ) peak temperature shifted from 95.84 to 105.23 °C, while the temperature at 5 % mass loss (Td5) increased from 305.95 to 314.04 °C. The residual mass at 900 °C increased from 68.53 % for the neat laminate to 72.38–72.93 % for the BNNP-containing laminates. The band-averaged total SE values were approximately 50, 46, and 43 dB for the laminates containing 0, 0.5, and 2 wt.% BNNP, respectively. Although the SE curves crossed at several frequencies, the band-averaged values decreased with increasing BNNP content. Among the formulations tested, the 0.5 wt.% BNNP laminate showed the most favorable thermomechanical response, with a reduction in band-averaged EMI shielding relative to the neat laminate.

title: PENGARUH FILLER BIOKARBON DAN CARBON BLACK TIPE N990 TERHADAP SIFAT DINAMIK KOMPOSIT KARET ALAM
abstract: Abstrak Material viskoelastik berbasis karet alam (NR) sering digunakan dalam aplikasi peredaman getaran, sehingga membutuhkan sifat dinamis dan peredaman yang memadai. Perilaku dinamis dan peredaman getaran komposit NR yang diisi dengan biokarbon turunan biomassa dan karbon hitam N990 diteliti dalam studi ini sebagai respons terhadap pengaruh jenis dan kadar pengisi. Pengisi biokarbon disintesis dari pati singkong dan kayu asam jawa melalui pirolisis, diikuti dengan penggilingan bola. Pengisi ini kemudian dimasukkan ke dalam NR dengan kadar 15, 30, dan 50 phr. Pengujian geser dinamis dan Analisis Proses Karet (RPA) diimplementasikan untuk menilai sifat dinamis komposit. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kinerja dinamis komposit NR sangat dipengaruhi oleh jenis dan kadar pengisi. Kekakuan geser, modulus geser efektif, dan kapasitas peredaman getaran semuanya meningkat dengan peningkatan kadar pengisi. Dibandingkan dengan senyawa NR kosong, biokarbon pati singkong meningkatkan modulus geser kompleks sebesar 159% pada pemuatan 50 phr, sedangkan biokarbon kayu asam jawa meningkatkannya sebesar 109%. Karbon hitam N990 hanya menghasilkan peningkatan sebesar 62,5%. Rasio redaman yang sesuai pada 50 phr meningkat dari sekitar 0,35% untuk karbon hitam N990 menjadi 0,85% dan 1,35% untuk biokarbon pati singkong dan kayu asam jawa, masing-masing, menunjukkan peningkatan kemampuan komposi…

title: Photochemically Mediated Oxidative Cross-coupling of Aminopyrazoles with 1-Thiosugars for the Synthesis of Thioglycosides
abstract: Abstract By harnessing visible-light excitation of a photocatalyst to initiate a single-electron transfer (SET) process, thereby activating glycosyl thiols to generate thiyl radicals and promote their coupling with aminopyrazoles, this work establishes an efficient photocatalytic strategy for C–S bond construction. This process involves radical addition for thioglycosyl incorporation, followed by oxidative deprotonation to furnish the target products in yields of up to 90%. Consequently, this method enables the efficient synthesis of diverse thioglycosylated pyrazole derivatives under mild conditions, exhibiting a broad substrate scope, excellent functional-group tolerance, and promising scalability, thus providing a green and sustainable synthetic approach.

title: Integrated equilibrium model for electrified logistics and power systems
abstract: This paper proposes an integrated equilibrium model to characterize the complex interactions between electrified logistics systems and electric power delivery systems. The model consists of two major players: an electrified logistics operator (ELO) and a power system operator (PSO). The ELO aims to maximize its profit by strategically scheduling and routing its electric delivery vehicles (e-trucks) for deliveries and charging, in response to the locational marginal price (LMP) set by the PSO. The routing, delivery, and charging behaviors of e-trucks are modeled by a perturbed utility Markov decision process (PU-MDP) while their collective operations are optimized to achieve the ELO's objective by designing rewards in the PU-MDP. On the other hand, PSO optimizes the energy price by considering both the spatiotemporal e-truck charging demand and the base electricity load. The equilibrium of the integrated system is formulated as a fixed point, proved to exist under mild assumptions, and solved for a case study on the Hawaii network via Anderson's fixed-point acceleration algorithm. Along with these numerical results, this paper provides both theoretical insights and practical guidelines to achieve sustainable and efficient operations in modern electrified logistics and power systems.

title: Strategic bidding model of integrated power-to-hydrogen systems in electricity-hydrogen coupling market
Multi-agent deep reinforcement learning based demand response and energy management for heavy industries with discrete manufacturing systems
abstract: Energy-centric decarbonization of heavy industries, such as steel and cement, necessitates their participation in integrating Renewable Energy Sources (RES) and effective Demand Response (DR) programs. This situation has created the opportunities to research control algorithms in diverse DR scenarios. Further, the industrial sector’s unique challenges, including the diversity of operations and the need for uninterrupted production, bring unique challenges in designing and implementing control algorithms. Reinforcement learning (RL) methods are practical solutions to the unique challenges faced by the industrial sector. Nevertheless, research in RL for industrial demand response has not yet achieved the level of standardization seen in other areas of RL research, hindering broader progress. To propel the research progress, we propose a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL)-based energy management system designed to optimize energy consumption in energy-intensive industrial settings by leveraging dynamic pricing DR schemes. The study highlights the creation of a MARL environment and addresses these challenges by designing a general framework that allows researchers to replicate and implement MARL environments for industrial sectors. The proposed framework incorporates a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP) to model energy consumption and production processes w…

title: Energy poverty and children’s subjective well-being: evidence from young lives data
abstract: This study examines the impact of energy poverty on the subjective well-being of children in four developing countries: Ethiopia, India, Peru, and Vietnam. We assess energy poverty using a multidimensional approach, leveraging data from the Young Lives study, which conducted surveys in 2006, 2009, 2013, and 2016 (Rounds 2 to 5). Our analysis focuses on the young cohort (Rounds 3 to 5) and the older cohort (Rounds 2 to 5), as these rounds include questions on children’s subjective well-being. To mitigate potential endogeneity concerns and establish causal relationships, we employ a two-stage least squares regression, using residential electricity prices at the country level as an instrumental variable. Our findings reveal that energy poverty significantly reduces children’s subjective well-being, with boys and older children more affected. Robustness checks confirm the validity of these results. Additionally, we find that health status mediates the impact of energy poverty on children’s well-being, highlighting the importance of targeted policy interventions.

title: Market-oriented operational strategy for biomass-geothermal combined power generation and hydrogen production plant
Capacity remuneration mechanisms for decarbonized power systems
abstract: Motivated by generation system adequacy concerns, many European countries have introduced capacity remuneration mechanisms (CRMs) to ensure sufficient investments in power generation . However, it is uncertain whether the existing CRMs will promote sufficient adequacy and flexibility in a decarbonized power system , where supply and demand will become more weather-dependent. We assess the effectiveness of a centralized capacity market, a strategic reserve , and a decentralized capacity market via capacity subscriptions in a climate-neutral, weather-driven power system. We develop a co-simulation of two agent-based models simulating myopia in both operational and investment decisions. We simulate weather uncertainty by running the model with 40 different weather years. Our results from a case study based on the Netherlands indicate that a strategic reserve may increase electricity price volatility in the long-term. A centralized capacity market is more cost-effective than a strategic reserve, but administratively setting its parameters is prone to over- or underprocurement. Capacity subscription allows consumers to select their desired level of reliability. Results indicate that these decentralized capacity markets may yield a clearer signal for the needed dispatchable capacity and promote demand-side response, but it may be challenging to provide long-term certainty for investo…

title: Local energy monitoring to support smart energy management and decarbonized town development
abstract: Introduction With the increase in variable renewable energy and liberalization of the electricity retail market, the integrated energy management of demand and supply has become crucial, complementing traditional energy-saving efforts. Therefore, high-resolution energy demand-side information, accounting for household attributes and owned equipment, is essential. However, previous studies have identified energy consumption based on surveys of utility bill payments; this approach does not provide detailed, hourly data on electricity demand, which changes over time owing to lifestyle patterns and weather conditions. Therefore, we aimed to investigate the actual electricity consumption in residential buildings in Shinchi Town using the developed electricity monitoring system.Material and Method In support of regional disaster recovery initiatives, we developed a regional information and communication technology (ICT) system as a network interface for residents. As part of a social experiment, network terminals of the local ICT system were distributed to approximately 100 households in the town. Power monitoring data were collected via equipment installed in home distribution boards and centrally managed by a cloud server.Results and Conclusion We analyzed electric power consumption patterns, focusing on household attributes, seasonal variations in hot-water-supply device usage, an…
